title: Block malformed-Host authentication bypass in ECM MCP
description: User value: an unauthenticated network client cannot obtain administrator-equivalent MCP access. Starlette 1.0.0 plus the request.url.path health exemption lets a request routed to /mcp appear as /health to authentication when Host is malformed. Evidence: mcp-server/requirements.txt:98; mcp-server/server.py:96-101,247-259; docker-compose.mcp.yml:8-9. Confirmed CVE-2026-48710/PYSEC-2026-161 behavior, CVSS 9.8.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade to a non-vulnerable compatible Starlette release; make auth exemption decisions from trusted raw ASGI path; reject malformed/untrusted Host values; re-enable or replace DNS-rebinding protection with a tier-appropriate allowlist; rotate the MCP key; end-to-end Uvicorn/h11 tests prove poisoned Host requests to /mcp return 401 and never dispatch tools while /health remains public.
notes:
CODE REMEDIATION READY in PR #879 (commit 62d7fcc8, build 0.18.1-0116). Independent code review, security review, and QA approved. Verification: 29 focused tests, 672 full MCP tests, real Uvicorn/h11 boundary, and dangerous-mutant regression proof. Starlette 1.6.0 is clear; 23 unrelated pre-existing MCP dependency advisories remain tracked by 04c0u.5/04c0u.11. DO NOT CLOSE YET: acceptance still requires operational rotation after the fixed build is deployed—regenerate the live MCP key, update all clients, and verify the old key is rejected. No production access, deployment, or live rotation occurred in this session.
CODE REMEDIATION MERGED to dev in PR #879 at merge commit edf77e6d. Required tests/security/docs/version checks passed; ECM and MCP AMD64/ARM64 image builds also completed successfully. BEAD REMAINS IN_PROGRESS: deploy the fixed build, regenerate the live MCP key, update every client, and verify the old key is rejected before closure.
PO RISK ACCEPTANCE 2026-08-17: live MCP key rotation is waived. The MCP service is local-only; the PO accepts the possibility that the existing key may have leaked and does not want rotation pursued. This acceptance removes key rotation as a closure blocker. REMAINING BLOCKER: the running ecm-ecm-mcp-1 container still uses Starlette 1.0.0 from image revision 33042bfd; deploy merged build 0.18.1-0116 and verify the live container uses the patched dependency and Host policy before closing.
close_reason: Verified deployed remediation on 2026-08-17. Running ecm-ecm-mcp-1 uses merged revision edf77e6d and Starlette 1.6.0 with allowed hosts localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], and ecm-mcp. Live container-local HTTP probes: valid-host /health returned 200; poisoned unauthenticated /mcp returned 401; authenticated untrusted and malformed Host values returned 400; valid authenticated Host reached MCP routing (406 due only to intentionally omitted MCP Accept negotiation). No key value was printed or rotated; PO accepted local-key rotation risk.

title: Security hardening: ECM and ECM MCP
description: User value: ECM operators can safely run ECM and its AI-facing MCP sidecar without unauthenticated administrative access, credential theft, account takeover, unsafe recovery behavior, or known vulnerable releases. This epic dispositions the confirmed 2026-08-15 full-team security review at commit a2beab75. Scope is tier-proportionate remediation for ecm-core, mcp-server, data-store, dbas-backup, ci-release, docs, and dev-tooling; it does not introduce enterprise security theater.

title: DBAS backup does not archive the bytes of logos uploaded through ECM, although Dispatcharr serves them on request
description:
P0. Found on backup/restore round-trip drill run 2026-08-04-run2 (ECM 0.18.1-0023, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable stack, NOT production). Raised by the PO on review of that run: 'we should be able to back up the logo if it has been uploaded.' Correct - and the drill's own evidence proves it is achievable today.

SYMPTOM

A logo uploaded through ECM's own Logo Manager is NOT carried in the backup
artifact. binary/metadata.json reads:

    {"logo_count": 0, "logos": []}

even when the instance has an uploaded logo assigned to a channel. Only the logo
INVENTORY (id + name + url) is archived, in categories/logos.yaml. On restore the
record is re-created for remote http(s) URLs but a Dispatcharr-local logo has no
retrievable source, so it is counted as a permanent miss (logo_misses).

WHY THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG (not merely incomplete)

The shipped design assumes those bytes are unreachable. dbas/importers/logos.py
and routers/backup.py both state the premise explicitly - that the binary subtree
'only ever carried ECM's OWN /config/uploads/logos/', that a Logo-Manager upload
lands in DISPATCHARR's /data/logos/ instead, and that therefore 'their URLs are
the only thing that CAN round-trip'.

THAT PREMISE IS FALSE, and the drill demonstrated it by accident.

The drill's inventory script fetched every logo's bytes over plain HTTP from
Dispatcharr's own cache endpoint (the cache_url on each logo row,
/api/channels/logos/<id>/..., header X-API-Key) purely to compute a SHA-256 for
comparison. For the uploaded logo it retrieved a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy:

    original file on disk : sha256 09b1732a1defcde737b981fd53f1167696183da6ef43ee08d5c265695db32b01
    fetched via Dispatcharr: sha256 09b1732a1defcde737b981fd53f1167696183da6ef43ee08d5c265695db32b01

using nothing but the API key ECM already holds and already uses for every other
category. The bytes are not lost at backup time. They are available, over an
endpoint ECM is already authenticated against, and the backup simply does not
ask for them.

They are only unrecoverable AFTER the source volume is destroyed - which is
precisely the event a backup exists to survive.

IMPACT

* Any operator who has uploaded channel logos through ECM cannot get them back
  from a DBAS backup, on ANY artifact variant. Confirmed on both standard and
  encrypted+credentials.
* It also converts a recoverable situation into the P0 in
  enhancedchannelmanager-d0agi: because the logo cannot be re-created, the
  restore records a per-row failure, and a logo failure is currently fatal, so
  the ENTIRE restore aborts and compensating-rolls-back. Fixing THIS bead
  removes the trigger for that one in the common case.

SUGGESTED FIX

At gather time, for each archived logo whose url is NOT an absolute http(s)
remote URL (i.e. a Dispatcharr-local /data/logos/... path), fetch the image from
Dispatcharr's logo cache endpoint and store it in the artifact's binary/ subtree
with its filename + content, exactly as the uploaded-file path already expects on
the restore side. dbas/importers/logos.py ALREADY has the upload path
(_validate_logo -> filename/size/magic-byte checks -> upload) and already
declares hydratable_bytes()/content_b64 - it is the producer side that never
populates it for this case.

Note the restore-side validator requires a 'filename' key that these records do
not currently carry (see enhancedchannelmanager-dgnms), so the gather must emit
filename alongside the bytes.

Keep the existing URL re-create path for genuinely remote CDN logos - those
round-trip correctly today (verified: 10 of 10 restored sha256-identical) and
should not be turned into archived bytes unnecessarily.

SECONDARY / ARGUABLY THE DEEPER ISSUE

ECM's Logo Manager writes uploads into DISPATCHARR's /data/logos/ rather than
ECM's own /config/uploads/logos/, which is the directory BACKUP_DIRS already
collects (verified again this run: ECM's own directory is EMPTY, the file is in
Dispatcharr's volume). Had the upload landed in ECM's own config volume it would
have been backed up all along. Worth deciding whether to also change where
Logo-Manager uploads are written; fetching from Dispatcharr at gather time fixes
existing instances either way, and changing the write location alone would not
help any logo already uploaded.

REPRODUCTION (1/1)

1. Upload a logo via ECM Logo Manager, assign it to a channel.
2. Confirm it landed in Dispatcharr: docker exec <dispatcharr> ls /data/logos/
   and that ECM's /config/uploads/logos/ is empty.
3. Take a DBAS backup. Unzip it: binary/metadata.json is {"logo_count": 0}.
4. Confirm the bytes were fetchable all along:
   curl -H 'X-API-Key: <key>' '<dispatcharr>/api/channels/logos/<id>/...' | sha256sum
   matches the original file.

RELATED
enhancedchannelmanager-d0agi - the restore-side consequence (fatal rollback).
enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn - its fix enshrined the false 'URLs are the only
thing that CAN round-trip' premise; commented there, not reopened.
enhancedchannelmanager-dgnms - the missing 'filename' key on logo records.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-04-run2/ (inventory/before.json,
inventory/DIFF-encrypted.md, REPORT.md).
close_reason:
FIXED — verified live THREE times on a disposable drill stack, and the code is present.

SYMPTOM: a DBAS backup did not archive the bytes of logos uploaded through ECM's Logo Manager, so an uploaded logo could not survive a round trip.

CODE: backend/routers/backup.py gathers uploaded-logo payloads via _gather_dispatcharr_logo_payloads() and writes them to the artifact's binary/ subtree with a logo_count in binary/metadata.json.

LIVE EVIDENCE — drill run 4 (2026-08-05-run4), artifact opened BEFORE destroying anything:
  binary/metadata.json -> {"logo_count": 1, "logos": [{"filename": "drill-uploaded-logo.png", "size_bytes": 4898, ...}]}
  binary/logos/drill-uploaded-logo.png -> 4898 bytes,
    sha256 f1222f2f8b4d749c7aed756d88f97161ff39ac1707a4768572e3e39323f6b086
    -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to the source PNG uploaded through ECM's Logo Manager.
  Remote CDN logos are correctly NOT pulled into the binary subtree (1 of 11 logos), as designed.

RESTORE SIDE, measured on the destination's own disk after a wipe-and-restore:
  run 4: docker exec bkr-dispatcharr sha256sum /data/logos/drill-uploaded-logo.png
         -> f1222f2f...f6b086  == source. PASS.
  run 5: same hash, PASS, on both artifact variants.
  run 7: 11 logos restored, logo_misses 0.

Also established and worth recording: an ECM-uploaded logo lands in DISPATCHARR's /data/logos/, not ECM's /config/uploads/logos/ (which stays empty). That is now documented in docs/user_guide/backup-restore/backup-overview.md.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DOCS — being fixed separately: three user-guide articles still carry a P0 warning telling operators to DELETE their ECM-uploaded logo records before taking a backup they intend to restore, accepting permanent loss of those logos. With this bead fixed that advice destroys operator data for no reason. It is stale in the operator's DISFAVOUR, which is the dangerous direction, and is being corrected.

Closed on the strength of three independent live measurements across two artifact variants, plus the code.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECISION (2026-08-04), answering this bead's 'SECONDARY / ARGUABLY THE DEEPER ISSUE' section. Recorded so no future run re-raises it.

QUESTION ASKED: should ECM's Logo Manager write uploads into ECM's own
/config/uploads/logos/ (which BACKUP_DIRS already collects) instead of
Dispatcharr's /data/logos/?

ANSWER: NO. Writing uploads to Dispatcharr is INTENTIONAL and correct.

PO, verbatim: 'that's intentional because our source of truth on logos is
Dispatcharr, not ECM. We pull all data from Dispatcharr, we're really a frontend
with extra tools.'

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS BEAD - it makes the proposed fix the architecturally
correct one rather than a workaround:

* Do NOT change where Logo Manager writes. Do not add a second copy in ECM's
  config volume. Do not treat ECM as a competing store of logo bytes.
* Dispatcharr being the source of truth is exactly WHY the backup must fetch the
  bytes FROM Dispatcharr at gather time. ECM already reads every other backup
  category from Dispatcharr over the same API with the same key; logos are the
  one category where it reads the metadata and not the payload. Closing that gap
  makes logos consistent with everything else, it does not make ECM a store.
* It also retires the premise recorded in dbas/importers/logos.py and
  routers/backup.py that the binary subtree can only ever carry ECM's OWN
  /config/uploads/logos/. Under this decision that subtree's job is 'the bytes
  ECM fetched from the source of truth at backup time', which is a coherent
  contract and is what makes an uploaded logo restorable.

Scope of this bead is therefore unchanged and now unambiguous: fetch at gather
time from Dispatcharr's logo cache endpoint for any logo whose url is not an
absolute http(s) remote URL, store bytes + filename in binary/, leave genuinely
remote CDN logos on the existing URL re-create path.

title: DBAS restore: a single ECM-uploaded logo aborts the whole restore and rolls it back
description:
P0. Found on the backup/restore round-trip drill (run 2026-08-04-run2), disposable stack bkr-ecm/bkr-dispatcharr, NOT production.

ECM 0.18.1-0023 (digest sha256:787bf82f...), Dispatcharr 0.28.2 (sha256:3eb0ec77...). Artifact variant: ENCRYPTED + include_credentials (also present in the standard redacted artifact - same logo record).

SYMPTOM
A DBAS restore that is otherwise completely successful is aborted and compensating-rolled-back because ONE logo could not be re-created. Restore report verbatim:

  outcome: partial_failed_rolled_back
  logo   created=10 updated=0 skipped=0 failed=1
    reason=validation_error label='Drill Uploaded Logo'
    message=unsafe or empty logo filename
  logo_misses: 1
  notes:
    - restore failed at category logo; compensating rollback ran.
    - rollback completed: 44 entity/entities removed.
    - NOTE: 7 applied setting(s) were NOT rolled back - settings changes are not compensatable and remain applied.

Everything else had already succeeded: m3u_account created=1, epg_source created=1, channel_group created=2, channel_profile created=1, user_agent created=1, stream_profile created=1, user created=1, channel created=12, stream created=14, logo created=10. All 44 were then destroyed by the rollback.

ROOT CAUSE (read from the pinned image's own source, not inferred)
Two designs in the shipped build contradict each other:

1. dbas/importers/logos.py - for a logo whose archived url is a Dispatcharr-LOCAL path (/data/logos/x.png), the bytes died with the source volume. The code's own comment says such a logo must be 'an honest miss ... reported instead of silent'. It implements that as cat.failed += 1 plus report.record_logo_miss(...).

2. dbas/restore_orchestrator.py:188 - NON_FATAL_FAILURE_CATEGORIES = frozenset({EntityType.USER}). LOGO is NOT in it, so ANY failure in the logo category is fatal and triggers the compensating rollback.

So the very outcome the logo importer is designed to produce (a counted, reported miss) is classified by the orchestrator as a fatal abort.

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NORMAL, NOT AN EDGE CASE
A logo uploaded through ECM's OWN Logo Manager is written to Dispatcharr's /data/logos/, not ECM's /config/uploads/logos/ (confirmed again this run: ECM's dir is empty, drill-logo.png is in Dispatcharr's). So every operator who has ever uploaded a channel logo through ECM has an artifact that CANNOT be restored. The seed here had exactly one such logo out of 11.

The RestoreOutcome enum already has COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES for precisely this shape ('the restore ran to completion and NOTHING was rolled back'). It is not reachable for logos.

SUGGESTED FIX
Add EntityType.LOGO to NON_FATAL_FAILURE_CATEGORIES, so a logo that cannot be re-created is counted in logo_misses and surfaced in the report while the restore completes - which is what the logos importer's comment already says the behaviour should be.

REPRODUCTION
1. Seed an instance and upload ONE logo through ECM Logo Manager (it lands in Dispatcharr /data/logos/), assign it to a channel. Add remote-CDN-URL logos too.
2. Take a DBAS backup. categories/logos.yaml carries {id,name,url} with url='/data/logos/<file>.png' for the uploaded one.
3. down -v both containers, roll out fresh, connect ECM.
4. Restore the artifact. Reproduced 1/1.

RELATED
Distinct from enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn: dfkbn was 'logos silently lost, logo_misses wrongly 0'. The dfkbn fix added the logos category and correct miss-counting; this bead is that the correctly-counted miss is misclassified as fatal. Without this, dfkbn cannot be verified end-to-end because the restore never completes.

Screenshot: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-04-run2/shots/ ; full report ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-04-run2/notes/restore-encrypted-raw.json
close_reason:
FIXED — code present and the failure path IS unit-tested. Stating precisely what was and was not verified live.

SYMPTOM (drill run 2026-08-04-run2): a restore that had already created 44 entities reported partial_failed_rolled_back and compensated ALL 44 away because ONE logo failed. Logos run last in the hard ordering, so everything the rollback destroyed had already succeeded.

CODE: backend/dbas/restore_orchestrator.py
  NON_FATAL_FAILURE_CATEGORIES: frozenset[EntityType] = frozenset({EntityType.USER, EntityType.LOGO})
A failure in a non-fatal category no longer triggers the compensating rollback.

TEST COVERAGE — this is the part I want on the record, because my own drill could NOT reach it:
  backend/tests/dbas/test_restore_orchestrator.py:1112
    test_logo_category_failure_does_not_roll_back_the_restore
  It INJECTS a genuine logo-failure step after successful M3U_ACCOUNT and CHANNEL
  creations and asserts the failure is visible, counted and named while nothing is
  rolled back. Its docstring cites this bead and the run-2 measurement directly.
  Also: test_non_fatal_set_is_exactly_users_and_logos pins the set itself.
  Both PASS (verified by the orchestrator, 2 passed).

WHAT WAS *NOT* VERIFIED LIVE, stated plainly: across drill runs 4, 5, 6 and 7 the genuine logo-failure path was never reached — logo_misses was 0 in every run, because with bead xb58a fixed the uploaded logo always restored successfully. Run 4 recorded this honestly as NOT EXERCISED rather than claiming a pass. So the live evidence here is negative-space evidence: the SYMPTOM (an uploaded logo aborting and rolling back an entire restore) demonstrably does not occur — uploaded logos restored cleanly with no rollback in three separate runs — but I did not manufacture a failing logo to watch the non-fatal path execute on a real stack.

Closed on: the policy is implemented, the set is pinned by test, the failure path is exercised by an injecting unit test that cites this bead, and the reported symptom does not reproduce across four live drill runs. If someone wants the live failure-path proof specifically, that is a small, well-defined follow-up and worth doing on the next drill.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DOCS: the P0 warnings in three user-guide articles advise deleting ECM-uploaded logos before a backup and cite this bead plus xb58a as unshipped. Both are shipped. Being corrected separately.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION after PO review of run 2026-08-04-run2.

This bead proposed making a logo failure non-fatal (add EntityType.LOGO to
NON_FATAL_FAILURE_CATEGORIES). That is still worth doing as defence in depth, but
it is NOT the primary fix and this bead should not be closed by it alone.

The PO's position, which the drill's own evidence supports: an uploaded logo
should be BACKED UP, so that it can be restored rather than 'honestly reported as
lost'. Filed as enhancedchannelmanager-xb58a (P0).

The premise this bead accepted - that a Dispatcharr-volume-local logo's bytes
cannot round-trip - is false. The drill's inventory script retrieved that exact
logo's bytes over HTTP from Dispatcharr's own cache endpoint using only the API
key ECM already holds, byte-identical to the original
(sha256 09b1732a1defcde737b981fd53f1167696183da6ef43ee08d5c265695db32b01 on both
sides). The backup simply never asks for them.

Revised relationship:

* xb58a (backup archives the bytes) removes the TRIGGER in the common case: an
  uploaded logo restores instead of failing, so nothing fatal happens.
* d0agi (this bead) remains the SAFETY NET for the residual cases that can still
  fail per-row - an upstream 5xx on upload, a logo whose source is genuinely gone,
  a byte payload that fails the magic-byte validator. A restore should not
  destroy 44 successfully-restored entities because one image could not be
  written. RestoreOutcome.COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES already exists for exactly this
  shape and is currently unreachable for logos.

Both should land. Fixing only d0agi would leave operators with a restore that
completes and silently has no logos, which is close to what run 1 complained
about. Fixing only xb58a would leave the fatal-rollback landmine armed for every
other logo failure mode.

title: Restored channels stay bound to URL-less placeholder streams and are never re-matched to the real provider streams, so no channel plays
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK, NOT production. ECM v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Affects BOTH artifact variants. Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n.

SYMPTOM
A DBAS restore that reports 'success' produces a structurally perfect but entirely non-functional lineup. All 12 channels come back with correct number, name, group and ORDERED stream list, and not one of them can play.

The restore creates a synthetic M3U account 'ECM Custom Streams (DBAS restore)' and materialises each archived stream under it as a placeholder with NO URL:

  GET /api/channels/streams/1/  ->  name='US: FOX News Channel FHD', url=None, m3u_account=3
  channel 201 streams = [1, 2, 3]  (all three url=None)

The synthetic account itself sits permanently in ERROR: 'No M3U source available (missing URL and file)'.

THE REFRESH DOES NOT FIX IT
The runbook's post-restore step is an M3U refresh. Performed on the encrypted variant (where credentials restored correctly):
- The real provider streams DID materialise: stream count went 14 -> 124 (110 real + the 14 placeholders), in under 10 seconds.
- Every channel REMAINED bound to its URL-less placeholder. No re-match occurred.
So after the documented recovery step, the operator has 110 working streams sitting next to 12 channels that still cannot play. 'Verify one channel plays' -- the runbook's own Phase 6 acceptance check -- FAILS.

COMPOUNDING: the enabled-group selection is not restored
The source M3U account had exactly one of 375 groups enabled ('USA | News'). After restore the account shows '0 / 375 groups' and status PENDING SETUP. A refresh at that point ingests nothing and the account flips to:
  ERROR | 'No streams returned from Xtream Codes provider'
which blames the provider for what is actually 'you have no groups enabled'. Re-selecting the group by hand and using Save & Refresh materialised the streams in under 10 seconds -- but, again, without re-binding any channel.

So the true post-restore recovery sequence is: re-select the enabled groups -> Save & Refresh -> re-attach every channel's streams by hand. Only the middle step is documented.

REPRODUCED: yes, on both variants, each on its own clean rollout.

RELATED EVIDENCE FOR bead enhancedchannelmanager-1zwmr
This drill is the seeded instance 1zwmr has been waiting for. Stream ORDER survives perfectly: the multi-stream channel was seeded as [US: FOX News Channel FHD, US: FOX News Channel HD, US: FOX News Talk FHD] and restored in exactly that order, in both variants. The 4-tier matcher's ordering behaviour is CONFIRMED GOOD. The problem is not the order -- it is that the things being ordered are empty placeholders.

SUGGESTED FIX
After the M3U accounts have refreshed and real streams exist, re-run the stream matcher to rebind channels from the placeholder rows onto the real provider streams, then drop the placeholders and the synthetic account. Failing that, restore the M3U account's enabled-group selection and state plainly in the restore report that every channel needs its streams reattached -- the report currently says 'success' with 0 failures for an instance that cannot play anything.
notes:
RUN-3 LIVE EVIDENCE (drill 2026-08-05-run3, published :dev 0.18.1-0024, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable stack).

FIXED / CONFIRMED GOOD:
- Enabled-group selection round-trips: '1 / 375' with USA | Local PBS, not '0 / N'.
- ENCRYPTED + credentials artifact: channels bind to REAL streams with URLs and PLAY on the first restore. Verified by FETCHING media bytes, not inferred: HTTP 200, video/mp2t, 262144 bytes on 2 channels. streams_rebound: 11.
- Stream ORDER survives on the multi-stream channel on both variants.

RESIDUAL CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT (redacted path, one-shot rebind). Measured as three explicit states rather than assumed:
  step 1  straight after restore                : 14 streams, 0 with url, 0/12 channels on real streams, playback 0/2, password state 'absent'
  step 2  + credential re-entry + M3U refresh   : 110 streams, 96 with url, STILL 0/12 on real streams, playback STILL 0/2
  step 3  + RE-RUN the restore                  : 110 streams, 96 with url, 11/12 on real streams, playback 2/3
Step 2 is the recovery an operator reaches for first and it changes nothing they can see: 96 real playable streams exist and not one channel is bound to any of them. Re-running the restore is mandatory. Behaviour unchanged from run 2.

Cosmetic residual: the 3-step path leaves 11 orphaned URL-less placeholder streams and the synthetic 'ECM Custom Streams (DBAS restore)' account behind (without_url 14), whereas the encrypted path cleans them up (without_url 3).

NEW, SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND ON TOP OF THIS -> enhancedchannelmanager-ixdaw: a channel whose streams normalize to the same name (e.g. 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA' + 'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA') has both slots matched to the SAME destination stream; the rebind PATCHes a duplicate id, Dispatcharr 500s on unique_channel_stream, and the WHOLE channel reverts to placeholders. That channel stays unplayable even after the 3-step recovery.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run3/inventory/DIFF-standard.md, DIFF-encrypted.md, playback-after-standard-step{1,2,3}.json
close_reason:
RESIDUAL FIXED and proven end-to-end. Shipped in PR #785, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0033.

THE RESIDUAL: restoring a STANDARD (redacted) backup — the default, and the one most operators hold — took THREE steps to reach a working instance. Measured identically in drill runs 4, 5 and 7:
  1. after the restore              -> every channel on a URL-less placeholder, 0/n playback
  2. + re-enter the credential and refresh -> 96 real streams materialize BESIDE the placeholders; NOT ONE channel rebound; still 0/n playback
  3. + re-run the ENTIRE restore     -> channels finally rebind
Step 2 is the recovery an operator reaches for first and it changed nothing they could see. Step 3 was non-obvious and nothing in the product said to do it.

CAUSE: rebind_placeholder_streams() had exactly one caller (restore_orchestrator.py:937). It is a restore-completion step that runs once, immediately after the restore's own deferred M3U refresh. On a redacted artifact the account has no credential at that instant, so there is nothing real to match against, and the pass never ran again.

FIX: a COMPLETED M3U refresh now rebinds any channel still holding a synthetic placeholder. The enabling fact, verified in code rather than assumed: the placeholder is created carrying the ARCHIVED STREAM'S OWN NAME (custom_stream_fallback._build_stream_payload forwards 'name' verbatim), so a post-restore rebind needs neither the archive, the ledger nor the id remap — all gone once the restore ends. It matches the placeholder's own name through the existing 4-tier matcher, landing on Tier 3, which carries the ixdaw raw-name preference.

No second implementation: _rebind_one_channel holds the whole loop verbatim (claimed_ids seeding, demote-to-MISS on a claimed id, in-place ordered_ids[index] rewrite, PATCH-failure revert). Both entry points differ only in one callable. Only ECM's own placeholders are touched — on the synthetic account, URL-less; an operator's own custom stream is never rebound or deleted.

PROVEN LIVE (run 8, 2026-08-06-run8-2o0cz, disposable drill stack). STEP 2 ONLY, no second restore:
  [DBAS-REBIND] M3U refresh of 'Infinity': rebind complete — 14 slot(s) rebound across 12 channel(s);
                14 orphaned placeholder(s) swept; 0 channel(s) still hold a slot that cannot play
  Read off Dispatcharr: channels holding a URL-less slot = NONE; URL-less streams anywhere = 0;
  accounts back to ['custom','Infinity'] (synthetic account deleted);
  multi-stream channel [102 'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA', 98 'TX | Austin | PBS KLRU', 101 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA'] — exact archived order.
  PLAYBACK FETCHED: 4/4, HTTP 200, video/mp2t, 262144 bytes each.

THE REDACTED PATH IS NOW TWO STEPS: restore -> re-enter credential and refresh.

COVERAGE, stated precisely rather than overclaimed:

  NOT COVERED, heals on the next scheduled refresh: POST /api/m3u/refresh (refresh-all) exposes no completion signal; direct DispatcharrClient.refresh_all_m3u_accounts callers; a refresh done in Dispatcharr's own UI.

DOUBLE-RUN SAFETY: (1) structural — the restore's deferred phase calls client.refresh_m3u_account() directly, never ECM's route and never the task, pinned by a source-grep tripwire test; (2) explicit — a module-level asyncio.Lock, archive-driven pass waits, refresh-driven pass stands down. The orchestrator verified the lock's SCOPE independently: the entrypoint runs 'uvicorn main:app' with NO --workers, so ECM is single-process and a module-level lock covers the whole app. That assumption would break if --workers were ever added.

title: Redacted DBAS restore writes the literal string ***REDACTED*** into the M3U password, so the account looks configured and cannot authenticate
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK, NOT production. ECM v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Artifact variant: STANDARD (redacted). Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n.

SYMPTOM
Restoring a standard (non-encrypted, credentials-redacted) DBAS artifact restores the XC M3U account with password set to the LITERAL STRING '***REDACTED***' rather than leaving it empty.

  GET /api/m3u/accounts/  ->  name='Infinity', username='mot2', password='***REDACTED***'

Compare the encrypted + include_credentials artifact restored onto an identical fresh target: password='63832936' (the real value, correct).

CONSEQUENCE
The account presents as fully configured -- username AND password both populated -- and then fails at the provider:

  ERROR | Infinity | XtreamCodes | Failed to authenticate with XC server:
  512 Server Error: <none> for url: https://<provider>/player_api.php?use...

Zero streams materialise. No manual refresh was even required to trigger it; the restore's own post-import refresh failed immediately.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN EMPTY PASSWORD
An empty password is visibly incomplete: the UI shows a blank field and any 'is a credential present' check returns false, so the operator is prompted to act. A literal placeholder defeats every such check:
- The UI shows a filled password field.
- Any boolean 'has_credential' probe returns True. The drill's own inventory script reduces credentials to exactly such a boolean (deliberately -- it must never emit a secret), so its before/after diff reported the M3U account as BYTE-IDENTICAL while the instance was non-functional. The defect was caught only by reading the raw field by hand.
An operator following 'preview, apply, check the counts' has no signal at all. The counts are perfect.

Also note the restore PREVIEW is byte-identical between the encrypted and redacted artifacts -- same 11 categories, same create/update/skip numbers. Nothing in the preview tells the operator which variant they are about to apply or that credentials will be placeholders.

REPRODUCED: yes, on a clean rollout, both variants restored onto their own fresh stack.

SUGGESTED FIX
Do not write the redaction sentinel into the target field. Either leave the credential empty on restore, or restore it as empty AND surface it in the restore report as an explicit post-restore action item ('N accounts need credentials re-entered before they will refresh'). The report already has a natural place for this next to logo_misses. Whichever is chosen, a 'credential present' check must not return true for a value the product itself wrote as a placeholder.

title: DBAS restore aborts at the user category: Dispatcharr returns 500 (KeyError: 'password') when ECM creates an archived user
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK (bkr-ecm / bkr-dispatcharr, project ecmbkr), NOT production. ECM v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2 (digest sha256:3eb0ec77...). Artifact variant: encrypted + include_credentials. Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n. Second blocking defect of the round-trip drill; found only after working around enhancedchannelmanager-lvfwd. SYMPTOM Restoring a DBAS artifact onto a fresh Dispatcharr whose superuser has a DIFFERENT username than the source's fails the whole restore at the 'user' category: outcome: partial_failed_rolled_back message: 'Restore partial_failed_rolled_back: created 6, failed 1 across 8 categories' user created=0 updated=0 skipped=0 failed=1 reason: upstream_api_error label: 'drilladmin' message: 'User creation failed: 500 -

Server Error (500)

' Dispatcharr's log gives the real cause: ERROR django.request Internal Server Error: /api/accounts/users/ Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../rest_framework/views.py", line 486, in raise_uncaught_exception KeyError: 'password' INFO uwsgi.requests Worker ID: 3 POST 500 /api/accounts/users/ 34ms ECM POSTs the archived user with no 'password' key. Dispatcharr's user-create serializer reads validated_data['password'] unconditionally, so the KeyError escapes as an uncaught 500 rather than a 400 validation error. ECM then treats the 500 as a fatal category failure and rolls the restore back. WHY THIS IS NOT A CORNER CASE Every DBAS artifact contains at least one Dispatcharr user (the admin). The category only SKIPS when the archived username matches the target's current admin -- the preview against the source instance showed 'Users 1 WILL SKIP / Current admin preserved'. On a genuine disaster-recovery rebuild the operator names the new superuser whatever they like, so the archived user does not match, ECM tries to CREATE it, and the restore dies. Restoring onto a rebuilt Dispatcharr is the primary use case for this feature. WORKAROUND (confirmed working) Name the rebuilt Dispatcharr superuser EXACTLY the same as the source's. The user category then skips with 'Current admin preserved' and the restore proceeds. Nothing in the documentation tells an operator this, and it must be decided at Dispatcharr's first-run wizard -- BEFORE ECM is involved and long before the restore is attempted. ALSO EXPOSED HERE -- the rollback is not a rollback The same report carries: notes: ['restore failed at category user; compensating rollback ran.', 'rollback completed: 6 entity/entities removed.', 'NOTE: 7 applied setting(s) were NOT rolled back -- settings changes are not compensatable and remain applied.'] So a failed restore leaves ECM settings mutated. Separately, the restored M3U account had already triggered a Dispatcharr playlist ingest, creating 375 channel groups that the rollback ledger does not own; those survive too. Net effect: a failed restore leaves a THIRD state that is neither the pre-restore instance nor the backed-up one, and the operator is told only 'Restore failed'. Fallout observed as the rollback raced Dispatcharr's async tasks: IntegrityError: insert or update on table "epg_epgsourceindex" violates foreign key constraint ... Key (source_id)=(1) is not present in table "epg_epgsource" ERROR apps.epg.tasks [build_programme_index] EPGSource 1 not found i.e. the rollback deleted the EPG source while a celery indexing task was mid-flight. REPRODUCED: yes, deterministically, on a clean rollout. SUGGESTED FIX (ECM side, since the upstream 500 is not ours to land) Send a password on user create -- a generated random one is fine and is safer than carrying the source hash -- so the upstream serializer's required key is present. Failing that, treat a user-category failure as NON-FATAL: users are opt-in and are the least load-bearing category in the artifact, and losing one should not cost the operator their channels, groups, profiles and settings. Worth reporting the upstream KeyError to Dispatcharr as well, since a 400 would have made this diagnosable from ECM's own report instead of requiring the Dispatcharr container log.

title: DBAS restore aborts and rolls back the whole instance when a stream profile references a custom user agent
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK (bkr-ecm / bkr-dispatcharr, project ecmbkr), NOT production. ECM v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2 (digest sha256:3eb0ec77...). Artifact variant: encrypted + include_credentials (also affects the standard redacted artifact -- the failing category is identical in both). Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n. This is the headline result of the round-trip drill: the restore did NOT reproduce the instance.

SYMPTOM
Restoring a DBAS artifact onto a genuinely fresh ECM + Dispatcharr pair fails outright. The UI shows only 'Restore failed' with no reason. The task report says:

  outcome: partial_failed_rolled_back
  message: 'Restore partial_failed_rolled_back: created 5, failed 1 across 5 categories'
  notes:  ['restore failed at category stream_profile; compensating rollback ran.',
           'rollback completed: 5 entity/entities removed.']

  stream_profile  created=0 updated=0 skipped=5 failed=1
    reason:  upstream_api_error
    label:   'Drill Profile'
    message: "Client error '400 Bad Request' for url 'http://bkr-dispatcharr:9191/api/core/streamprofiles/'"

Dispatcharr's actual rejection, reproduced by hand against the same target:
  POST /api/core/streamprofiles/ {..., "user_agent": 4}
  -> 400  {"user_agent":["Invalid pk \"4\" - object does not exist."]}

The net effect is total: everything already created (M3U account, EPG source, 2 channel groups, channel profile) is rolled back, no channels are restored, and the operator is left with an empty instance and a one-line 'Restore failed'.

ROOT CAUSE -- one wrong assumption, two defects
/app/dbas/importers/groups_profiles.py documents its own model:
  'remappable_fk_fields maps an archive payload field name to the EntityType whose
   IdRemapTable namespace rewrites it; it is EMPTY for the three real leaf categories
   (they carry no outbound FK).'
Stream profiles are classed as a leaf category with no outbound FK. That is false -- a Dispatcharr stream profile has a user_agent FK. Hence:

1. ORDERING. /app/dbas/restore_orchestrator.py calls import_stream_profiles (line 934) BEFORE import_user_agents (line 946). A stream profile bound to a custom user agent therefore references a row the restore has not created yet.
2. RAW ID PASSTHROUGH. Because remappable_fk_fields is empty for stream_profiles, the archived user_agent value is sent through UNREMAPPED -- the SOURCE instance's id (4) is POSTed at the target. A restore reassigns ids by design, so this is wrong even when the object exists.

Defect 2 is the more dangerous of the two: it currently fails loudly only because id 4 happens to be absent on a fresh target. If the target already has some unrelated user agent at the source's id, the create SUCCEEDS and silently binds the WRONG user agent -- no error, no report entry.

REPRODUCED: yes, deterministically, on a clean rollout.

STEPS
1. On the source: create a custom user agent ('Drill UA') and a custom stream profile ('Drill Profile') whose user_agent points at it. Assign the profile to a channel.
2. Take a DBAS backup (either variant). It completes successfully -- the artifact is NOT degraded, no warning-level result.
3. Destroy both stacks and their volumes; roll out clean; complete both first-run wizards; connect ECM to the fresh Dispatcharr.
4. Restore the artifact. Preview is clean and reconciles exactly with the source inventory (stream_profiles 1 create + 5 skip = 6). Apply.
5. Apply fails at stream_profile and rolls the whole restore back.

Note the preview does NOT predict this: the dry run reported 'stream_profiles 1 WILL CREATE, 0 FAILED'. The preview cannot see the FK problem, so 'preview first, always' does not protect an operator here.

SUGGESTED FIX
Move import_user_agents ahead of import_stream_profiles in restore_orchestrator.py, AND give stream_profiles a remappable_fk_fields entry mapping 'user_agent' -> EntityType.USER_AGENT so the id is rewritten through the IdRemapTable like every other cross-category reference. Fixing only the ordering leaves the silent wrong-binding case live. A regression test should restore an artifact containing a stream profile bound to a custom user agent onto a target whose id space does not line up, and assert the profile resolves to the correctly-NAMED user agent.
close_reason:
VERIFIED FIXED on drill run 2026-08-04-run2 (ECM 0.18.1-0023, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable stack, not production).

Tested under the HOSTILE conditions the bead demands, not run 1's workaround:
  * the custom user agent 'Drill UA' was NOT pre-created on the target;
  * three DECOY user agents were created on the fresh target FIRST, so the
    source's user-agent id 4 was occupied by a DIFFERENT object ('Decoy One').
    Target id space before restore: 1 TiviMate, 2 VLC, 3 Chrome, 4 Decoy One,
    5 Decoy Two, 6 Decoy Three.

Result, on BOTH artifact variants (encrypted+credentials and standard redacted),
each on its own clean rollout:

  stream_profile created=1 skipped=5 failed=0
  user_agent     created=1 skipped=3 failed=0
  'Drill Profile' -> user_agent id=7 NAME='Drill UA'

The id was correctly REMAPPED (source 4 -> destination 7) rather than passed
through raw. The assertion is on the NAME, not merely a 2xx: had the raw source
id been passed through, the profile would have bound to 'Decoy One' at id 4 and
still returned 2xx. It did not. No 400 'Invalid pk "4"', no abort, no rollback.

Both halves of the bead (ordering and raw-id passthrough) are closed.

title: Pre-Alembic install bootstrap stamps at HEAD instead of baseline — skips all post-baseline migrations
description:
User reports 'no such column: auto_creation_rules.match_scope_target_group' breaking Auto Creation with 500s.

Root cause: backend/database.py:_bootstrap_alembic lines 144-151. When ECM detects a pre-Alembic install (user_tables exist, alembic_version table missing), it stamps at HEAD and returns before running upgrade head. The intent was to avoid duplicate-DDL on existing schemas — but stamping at HEAD means Alembic believes ALL post-baseline migrations are already applied, even though the schema is physically at the baseline.

Affected: any user whose journal.db was created before the Alembic baseline (revision 0001, ~2026-04-20) and who has since pulled an image with new columns/indexes added by migrations 0002, 0003, 0004.

Migrations skipped:
- 0002: auto_creation_rules.match_scope_target_group (the column the user is hitting — a SELECT * fails because SQLAlchemy includes it in queries)
- 0003: rule_lint_findings
- 0004: journal batch_id + entity composite indexes

Fix: change line 150 from command.stamp(alembic_cfg, 'head') to command.stamp(alembic_cfg, '0001'), drop the return, so upgrade head runs after stamping at baseline. The baseline IS the pre-Alembic schema by design.

Recovery for already-affected users (no code change required):
docker exec ecm-ecm-1 sqlite3 /config/journal.db "UPDATE alembic_version SET version_num='0001';"
docker restart ecm-ecm-1

This re-stamps the user at baseline; bootstrap then upgrades to head (0004), applying the 3 missing migrations.

Considerations:
- The fix MUST also include a self-heal: detect any schema/version mismatch on startup and recover. Otherwise users already stamped-at-head are stuck without the manual SQL.
- Alternatively, file as separate bead: ship the bootstrap fix now (prevents future cases), follow up with self-heal logic.

Priority: P0 — production users hitting 500s, blocks Auto Creation entirely for affected DBs.
close_reason: Merged via PR #201 (commit b7d69c40). Pre-Alembic stamping bug fixed + self-heal for stamped-at-head DBs shipped to dev as 0.16.0-0063. Affected users pull the new container image and the bug auto-recovers on first restart.

title: security: validate tenant_id/drive_id in OneDrive adapter (CodeQL 1361, 1362)
description:
CodeQL alerts 1361 and 1362 flag SSRF risk in the OneDrive adapter via unvalidated tenant_id/drive_id interpolation into Microsoft Graph URLs.

Root cause: user-supplied tenant_id and drive_id flow from CloudTargetCreateRequest/UpdateRequest into Microsoft Graph URL construction without shape validation. Although admin-only, credentials are admin-authored; a malformed or maliciously-crafted identifier could redirect Graph calls to an attacker-controlled endpoint, leaking the client_secret during OAuth token exchange.

Exploitability:
- Admin-only write path, but admin credentials are themselves the secret being protected
- client_secret leak possible if URL is redirected to attacker origin
- Graph URL composition pattern: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/... and https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{drive_id}/...

Fix direction (from triage):
- Add _TENANT_ID_RE: GUID-or-domain validator (36-char GUID or verified-domain form like contoso.onmicrosoft.com)
- Add _DRIVE_ID_RE: base64url validator for drive IDs
- Apply at Pydantic CloudTargetCreateRequest and CloudTargetUpdateRequest layer (primary gate)
- Apply again at adapter __init__ as defense-in-depth
- Reject with HTTP 422 at API boundary; raise ValueError at adapter construction

Acceptance criteria:
- CodeQL alerts 1361 and 1362 auto-close on next scan after merge
- New tests pass:
  - test_rejects_invalid_tenant_id_shape (reject javascript:, attacker.com, traversal, null-byte, overlong)
  - test_rejects_invalid_drive_id_shape (reject non-b64url characters, path separators, URL schemes)
- Existing OneDrive happy-path tests still pass
- No breaking change for legitimate Azure AD tenants or existing drive IDs

References:
- CodeQL alerts 1361, 1362 (both py/full-server-side-request-forgery or similar)
- Tracked under Bead C audit entry (separate)

description:
# Rollback v0.16.0 Release (Hard)

Owner: Project Engineer (same persona that executed bd-mghjm).
Authorized by PO 2026-04-20: user has bugs they want cleared before v0.16.0 ships.
Confirmed no consumers have pulled `:latest` or `:0.16.0` yet, so a destructive hard rollback is safe.

## Rollback Targets

- **main** → reset to `v0.15.2` @ `b277a383b4084b5025c85a8519cd385a046ecd26` (current tip `d2843d54` — the merge commit)
- **dev** → reset to `36108f35` (the [bd-0lvkk] ErrorBoundary #70 merge; package.json was `0.16.0-0040` at this point)
  - Strips these two commits from dev: `e3298a9d` (counter open to 0.17.0-0000) and `42e8c46b` (0.16.0 version bump)
- **GitHub Release** `v0.16.0` → delete (published 2026-04-20T16:00:45Z, currently non-draft/non-prerelease)
- **Git tag** `v0.16.0` → delete local + remote
- **GHCR tags** `0.16.0` and `0.16` → delete
- **GHCR `:latest`** → retag to the v0.15.2 image digest (find via `gh api` or docker registry API — the v0.15.2 release workflow produced a multi-arch manifest; point `:latest` back at it)

## Branch Protection Concern

`main` protection: `allow_force_pushes: false`, `enforce_admins: false`. Force-push needed to reset main. Options:
1. Admin bypass (since enforce_admins is false) — try first
2. If that fails, temporarily flip `allow_force_pushes: true`, do the reset, flip back

Prefer option 1. If option 2, restore protection exactly to the current config (required_status_checks: Backend Tests + Frontend Tests, strict; required_conversation_resolution: true; everything else as-is).

## Execution Order

1. Delete GitHub Release: `gh release delete v0.16.0 --yes --cleanup-tag` (cleanup-tag also removes the v0.16.0 ref)
2. Confirm v0.16.0 git tag is gone locally + on remote. If not, `git push origin :refs/tags/v0.16.0`.
3. Reset `main` to `b277a383b4084b5025c85a8519cd385a046ecd26` via worktree (root stays on dev). If force-push is blocked, follow the branch-protection-toggle approach above.
4. Reset `dev` to `36108f35`. Force-push. (No branch protection on dev per current state — verify.)
5. GHCR cleanup:
   - Find the v0.15.2 image manifest digest (look up via `gh release view v0.15.2` asset metadata, or the build.yml run for v0.15.2, or `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:0.15.2`)
   - Retag `:latest` → v0.15.2 digest (use `docker buildx imagetools create -t ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:latest <v0.15.2-digest>` or equivalent)
   - Delete tags `:0.16.0` and `:0.16` via the GHCR API or `gh api` DELETE on the version IDs. These are the package-version API endpoints; scope may require a PAT with `delete:packages` if `gh auth token` doesn't carry it. If it doesn't, report back — don't improvise.
6. Verify:
   - `git log --oneline origin/main -n 3` tip = `b277a383`
   - `git log --oneline origin/dev -n 3` tip = `36108f35`
   - `gh release list` does NOT include v0.16.0
   - `gh api repos/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/git/refs/tags` does NOT include v0.16.0
   - `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:latest` → points at the v0.15.2 manifest (compare to `:0.15.2`)
   - `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:0.16.0` → Not Found
   - `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:0.16` → Not Found
   - Branch protection on main still at the documented config

## Follow-up After Rollback

- Reopen bd-mghjm or file a new release bead once bugs are cleared. Don't reopen automatically — PO will decide when.
- Root local checkout is on dev; after dev is reset, the root checkout will be ahead of origin/dev (by e3298a9d + 42e8c46b). PE should leave instructions for the user to `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/dev` in the root checkout (not do it from a worktree).
- PR #72 (ESLint, cr/zjge5-eslint-logger-api-any) was based on dev @ e3298a9d. After dev resets, PR #72's base vanishes. PE should comment on PR #72 explaining the rollback and that the branch needs rebase onto new dev tip. Don't close the PR.

## Hard Constraints

- Root checkout MUST stay on dev (use worktrees for any main work)
- No force push to main WITHOUT first trying admin bypass
- If branch protection toggle is needed, it MUST be restored before the task is considered done
- Destructive GHCR deletes are permanent — verify the v0.15.2 digest retagging BEFORE deleting 0.16.0/0.16/latest's current pointers
- If any step fails (e.g., missing scope on gh token), STOP and report — do NOT leave a partial rollback

description: Onboarding finding (RED, security). The fix applied under ppe28.1 was scoped to ffmpeg_builder/probe.py and routers/stream_preview.py — it missed the scheduled probing path. backend/stream_prober.py:903-923 (_run_ffprobe) and :1030-1060 (black-screen ffmpeg scan) invoke ffprobe/ffmpeg against user-controlled URLs without -protocol_whitelist. description:

- Two parallel top-level jobs: backend, frontend
- backend job: pytest on the existing suite. Uses existing backend/tests/conftest.py — no new ci_seed.sql required (pytest fixtures handle test data already)
- frontend job: SEQUENTIAL steps — npm ci → npm run lint (changed-files-only in PR mode; see Lint strategy) → npm run typecheck → npm test (no --coverage)

Lint strategy (Decision 1b):
- Remove the ajv override first (required — lint is currently broken on dev).
- PR mode: lint CHANGED FILES ONLY with --max-warnings 0. Engineer chooses mechanism (simplest: git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD filtered to TS/JS files piped to npx eslint).
- Push mode (dev/main): full lint as NON-BLOCKING informational step (continue-on-error: true). Visibility without blocking.
- Existing 71 errors + 98 warnings are grandfathered; cleanup is bead zjge5.

Coverage strategy (Decision 2f):
- Gate: 'npm test' (no --coverage). DO NOT use 'npm run test:ci' — it fails today because actual coverage (~15%) < 20% threshold in vitest.config.ts.
- DO NOT modify vitest.config.ts. Companion bead nmlxi handles threshold setting from measured data.
- Optionally add non-blocking coverage-report step uploading coverage artifact.

Triggers:
- backend + frontend: push to dev/main AND all PRs

E2E — EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE:
- Engineer discovered that running E2E on GitHub-hosted runners cannot produce a meaningful gate — ECM proxies Dispatcharr; ~15 of 21 modals.spec.ts skips need Dispatcharr-owned entities that don't exist in CI. - The prior engineer's work on e2e job YAML (on ci/test-t8xw3 scratch branch) should be REMOVED before this bead closes.

- admin user seeding for E2E
- E2E seed email fix

- Branch protection (→ 8w33i, update to reflect only backend + frontend as required checks)

- PR with failing backend test → red backend check

- MTTR (mean time to recovery)
- MTBF (mean time between failures)

title: Spec: Service Alerting
description:
Write tests defining service alerting:

**Alert Triggers:**
- Service goes from healthy to unhealthy
- Service goes from unhealthy to healthy (recovery)
- Service degraded for > threshold duration
- Consecutive failures exceed threshold

**Alert Configuration:**
- Per-service alert enable/disable
- Failure threshold (default: 3 consecutive)
- Degraded threshold duration (default: 5 min)
- Alert cooldown period (default: 15 min)

**Alert Integration:**
- Uses existing AlertMethod system
- Service alerts are a notification category
- Configurable alert methods per category

**Alert Content:**
- Service name and status change
- Timestamp of state change
- Error message if applicable
- Link to status page

**Recovery Alerts:**
- Optional recovery notifications
- Include downtime duration
- Sent to same methods as down alert

title: Spec: Service Control Actions
description:
Write tests defining service control:

**Control Endpoints:**
- POST /api/services/{name}/restart - restart service
- POST /api/services/{name}/enable - enable service
- POST /api/services/{name}/disable - disable service
- GET /api/services/{name}/logs - get service logs

**Restart Behavior:**
- Returns immediately with job_id
- Polls for restart completion
- Timeout after configurable duration
- Returns new status after restart

**Enable/Disable:**
- Disabled services skip health checks
- Disabled services don't trigger alerts
- State persisted across ECM restarts
- Cannot disable critical services (backend, database)

**Controllable Services:**
- ecm_scheduler: can disable/restart
- ecm_prober: can disable/restart
- dispatcharr_sync: can disable (prevents auto-sync)

**Non-Controllable:**
- ecm_backend: restart requires container restart
- ecm_database: cannot disable
- external services: control via their own interfaces

**Permissions:**
- Service control requires admin role
- Non-admin gets 403 on control endpoints
- Read-only status available to all users

title: Spec: Service Status API
description:
Write tests defining status API endpoints:

- GET /api/status - overall system status summary
- GET /api/status/services - all service statuses
- GET /api/status/services/{name} - specific service status
- GET /api/status/history - historical status data
- GET /api/status/uptime - uptime statistics

**Response Format:**
- status: healthy/degraded/unhealthy
- services: array of service statuses
- uptime_percent: 99.9 format
- last_incident: timestamp or null
- check_interval: seconds

**Individual Service Status:**
- name, status, message
- last_check: timestamp
- response_time_ms: number
- consecutive_failures: count
- last_success: timestamp

**History Endpoint:**
- Returns time-series data
- Configurable time range (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d)
- Aggregated by minute/hour/day based on range

title: Spec: Service Registry & Discovery
description:

**Discovery API:**

title: Spec: Dispatcharr Connectivity Checks
description:

**Status States:**
- connected: API reachable, authenticated

title: Spec: ECM Backend Health Checks
description:

**Status Levels:**
- healthy: all components operational
- degraded: some components have warnings
- unhealthy: critical component failed

**Historical Data:**
- Health checks run on configurable interval (default 30s)
- Last N check results stored (default 100)
- Uptime percentage calculated from history

title: Spec: Frontend Builder UI

title: Spec: Command Execution

title: Spec: Command Preview & Validation
description:
Write tests defining command preview behavior:

title: Spec: Preset Templates
description:
Write tests defining preset behavior:

**Built-in Presets:**

title: Spec: Stream Mapping
description:

- Simple: -map 0
- Selective: -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0 -map 0:a:1

title: Spec: Audio Filters
description:
Write tests defining audio filter behavior:

**Volume Filter:**
- Volume multiplier (0.5x, 1x, 2x) or dB
- Generated: -af volume=1.5

**Normalization:**
- Loudnorm filter for broadcast normalization
- Generated: -af loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11

**Channel Manipulation:**
- Downmix to stereo: -af 'pan=stereo|...'
- Extract channel: -af 'channelsplit'
- Mono: -af 'pan=mono|c0=c0+c1'

**Tempo/Speed:**
- Atempo for speed change (0.5x-2x)
- Generated: -af atempo=1.25

**Noise Reduction:**
- Highpass/lowpass filters
- Generated: -af 'highpass=f=200,lowpass=f=3000'

**Filter Chaining:**
- Multiple filters: -af 'volume=1.5,loudnorm,atempo=1.1'
- Validate chain compatibility

title: Spec: Video Filters
description:
Write tests defining video filter behavior:

**Scale Filter:**
- Width/height inputs with aspect ratio lock

- Generated: -vf scale=1280:720

**Crop Filter:**
- Visual crop area selector (future)

- Generated: -vf crop=640:480:100:50

**FPS Filter:**
- Target framerate input
- Generated: -vf fps=30

**Deinterlace:**
- Method: yadif, bwdif
- Generated: -vf yadif

**Other Filters:**
- Rotate: transpose=1 (90°CW)
- Flip: hflip, vflip
- Pad: pad=1920:1080:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2
- Overlay: overlay=10:10 (for watermarks)

**Filter Chaining:**
- Multiple filters: -vf 'scale=1280:720,fps=30,yadif'
- Order matters - validate chain

title: Spec: Audio Codec Settings
description:

title: Spec: Video Codec Settings

title: Test Spec: Frontend Permission UI
description:

title: Test Spec: Frontend Auth Flow
description:

title: Test Spec: Group Management
description:
Write pytest tests for groups:

**Group CRUD:**
- POST /api/admin/groups creates group

- PATCH /api/admin/groups/{id} updates group
- DELETE /api/admin/groups/{id} removes group

- DELETE /api/admin/groups/{id}/roles/{role_id} removes role

title: Test Spec: RBAC Permissions
description:

**System Roles:**

- 'viewer' role has read-only access
- System roles cannot be deleted

**Permission Checking:**
- has_permission(user, 'channels', 'read') returns True for viewer
- has_permission(user, 'channels', 'write') returns False for viewer
- has_permission(user, 'users', 'write') returns True only for admin
- Permissions are inherited from groups

**Endpoint Protection:**
- GET endpoints require 'read' permission
- POST/PATCH/DELETE require 'write' permission
- /api/admin/* requires admin role
- 403 returned with clear error message

**Role Management:**
- Admin can create custom roles
- Custom roles can be assigned subset of permissions
- Roles can be assigned to users
- Roles can be assigned to groups

title: Test Spec: LDAP Authentication
description:

- Connection timeout returns clear error
- Invalid server returns clear error

**Bind Authentication:**

**User Search:**

- Search finds user by uid (OpenLDAP)

title: Test Spec: SAML Authentication
description:

- Importing IdP metadata file parses XML
- Required fields extracted: entityID, SSO URL, certificate
- Invalid metadata returns clear error

**Authentication Flow:**
- GET /api/auth/saml/{provider}/login redirects to IdP SSO URL
- Redirect includes AuthnRequest in SAMLRequest param
- AuthnRequest is signed with SP key

**Assertion Handling:**
- POST /api/auth/saml/{provider}/acs validates Response signature
- Invalid signature returns 401
- Expired assertion returns 401
- Assertion InResponseTo matches request ID
- Successful assertion creates/updates user
- Attributes mapped per configuration

title: Test Spec: OIDC Authentication
description:
Write pytest tests for OIDC (mock OIDC provider):

**Discovery:**

- Missing required fields in discovery raises error
- Discovery results are cached

**Authorization Flow:**
- GET /api/auth/oidc/{provider}/login redirects to authorization_endpoint
- Redirect includes client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce, code_challenge
- State and nonce are stored in session

**Callback:**
- GET /api/auth/oidc/{provider}/callback exchanges code for tokens
- Invalid state returns 400
- Token exchange failure returns 401
- id_token signature is validated against JWKS
- id_token claims (iss, aud, exp, nonce) are validated
- Successful callback creates/updates user, returns JWT

**User Provisioning:**
- User created with auth_provider='oidc', external_id=sub claim
- Email extracted from email claim
- Username from preferred_username or email
- Groups claim mapped to roles if configured

**Configuration:**

- GET /api/auth/providers includes dispatcharr when enabled

title: Test Spec: First-Run Setup

title: Test Spec: JWT Tokens
description:
Write pytest tests for JWT handling:

**Token Creation:**

title: Test Spec: Password Security
description:
Write pytest tests for password handling:

**Hashing:**
- hash_password() returns bcrypt hash (starts with $2b$)
- hash_password() with same input returns different hashes (salt)
- verify_password() returns True for correct password
- verify_password() returns False for incorrect password

- Password must be >= 8 characters
- Password must contain uppercase, lowercase, number
- Password cannot be common (password123, qwerty, etc.)
- Password cannot match username

title: Test Spec: Core Auth Flow
