title: e2e suite defaults to the PO's live instance, so any state-changing spec would mutate real channel data
description:
Found during bead i85dg implementation, when writing an end-to-end push-down test turned out to be unsafe rather than merely hard.

playwright.config.ts defaults E2E_BASE_URL to http://localhost:6100, which is the PO's LIVE ECM instance holding real channel data.

CONSEQUENCE: any spec that stages and applies a channel-number push-down, a cross-group move, a merge, a delete, or any other write would renumber or mutate the PO's real lineup for anyone who runs the suite locally without overriding the variable. The default is the dangerous value, and nothing in the config or the specs warns about it.

This is why i85dg shipped its blast-radius coverage as a rendered component test rather than an E2E. That was the right call for that bead, but it means the one place a full push-down would be exercised end to end does not exist, and cannot safely exist until this is fixed.

COMPOUNDING: e2e/*.spec.ts is not run in CI at all (deferred to bead 2lw25), so the suite's only execution path today is a developer running it locally against that default.

FIX DIRECTION: make the default a disposable instance, or remove the default entirely and fail loudly when E2E_BASE_URL is unset, rather than shipping a default that silently targets production. If a default must exist it should point at the port the disposable-stack tooling brings up. Pairs naturally with 2lw25, which needs a disposable instance for CI anyway.

Related: 2lw25 (e2e not in CI), 63aqu (e2e neither typechecked nor linted), lpvh0 and uhi27 (e2e login rate-limit exhaustion), 67onh (shared storage state).
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #868 (build 0.18.1-0109). PO decision 2026-08-15: remove the dangerous default, fail loudly, do not build disposable-stack tooling (that overlaps bead 2lw25).

playwright.config.ts defaulted E2E_BASE_URL to http://localhost:6100, the PO's live ECM instance. Any spec performing a write would have mutated real channel data for anyone running the suite locally. The dangerous value was the DEFAULT and nothing warned about it.

Real cost already incurred: bead i85dg could not write an end-to-end push-down test because doing so would have been unsafe, so that coverage shipped as a rendered component test instead.

FIX: playwright-base-url.mjs resolveE2EBaseURL now throws when E2E_BASE_URL is unset or empty and exactBuild is false. It throws at module load, ahead of defineConfig, so it fires before any browser launches. The message names the removed default, states plainly that it was the PO's live instance holding real channel data, describes the write hazard, and gives three copy-pasteable commands.

CI PATHS VERIFIED UNAFFECTED by running the two jobs' exact invocations rather than reading the config: Screen-Reader-Only Rendering Guard and Operator Workspace Release Matrix both run E2E_START_SERVER=true E2E_EXACT_BUILD=true, which short-circuits to its own preview URL at 127.0.0.1:4173 before the throw path. Both listed their tests successfully with E2E_BASE_URL unset. Codex independently confirmed both resolve.

SMOKE-TESTED BOTH DIRECTIONS with the real playwright CLI: unset -> threw, exit 1; set -> 13 tests listed, exit 0.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE worth knowing: the local npm run test:css-guard:* scripts relied on the removed default and now require an explicit E2E_BASE_URL. That is the intended effect; docs/testing.md documents it.

NOT DONE, deliberately and per the PO: no disposable-stack tooling, no e2e in CI. The suite still has nowhere to run, which is bead 2lw25's job.

title: Password-reset link host is caller-controlled: X-Forwarded-Host poisoning delivers the live token to an attacker
description:
Found during the cb1e1 rebase (PR for bead cb1e1). PRE-EXISTING, unrelated to that fix, and reaches further than the bug that surfaced it. This is classic password-reset poisoning.

backend/auth/routes.py:1443-1447:
  forwarded_proto = request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-Proto', request.url.scheme)
  forwarded_host  = request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-Host', request.url.netloc)
  base_url = f'{forwarded_proto}://{forwarded_host}'

base_url becomes reset_url = f'{base_url}/reset-password?token={reset_token}' (routes.py:138), which is the link the account actually receives by email.

BOTH headers are caller-supplied and unvalidated. Grepped backend/main.py and backend/config.py for TrustedHost, allowed_hosts and ALLOWED_HOSTS: none exist, so nothing constrains the value. The request.url.netloc fallback is itself Host-derived, so the default is not safe either.

ATTACK, unauthenticated, no prerequisites beyond knowing a victim's email address:
  POST /api/auth/forgot-password  with the victim's email and header X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.example
The victim receives a GENUINE ECM reset email, sent from ECM's own SMTP, carrying a LIVE reset token in a link pointing at the attacker's host. If the victim clicks, the token is delivered to the attacker, who resets the account.

WHY THIS IS RATED P1 RATHER THAN THE P2 THE FINDING ENGINEER SUGGESTED: the outcome is account takeover; it needs no log access, no prior compromise and no privileged position; and it arrives through a channel the victim has every reason to trust, unlike cb1e1 which requires an attacker to already be able to read application logs. The PO should override this rating if their deployment always sits behind a proxy that overwrites the header, but that is a deployment assumption ECM does not currently enforce or document.

NOT COVERED by the _client_address work in PR #865. That validates X-Forwarded-For for a LOG LINE. This is a different header used for a different purpose, and #865 does not touch it.

FIX DIRECTION: derive the host from configured settings (ECM already has a settings surface), or allowlist the forwarded host. Do not simply fall back to request.url.netloc, which is Host-header-derived and equally attacker-controlled. Consider whether any other outbound link construction in the codebase shares the idiom.

RELATED: cb1e1 (the same credential leaking via the log, fixed), nymj6 (unbounded caller-supplied username in login logs).
acceptance_criteria: Reset links use a configured canonical public origin or forwarded headers accepted only from explicitly trusted proxies with host allowlisting; spoofed Host and X-Forwarded-* cannot alter the emailed origin; tests cover direct and supported proxy deployments; the reset token never reaches an attacker-controlled origin.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #868 (build 0.18.1-0109). PO decision 2026-08-15: configurable public base URL, used verbatim when set, current behaviour preserved when unset.

THE VECTOR: backend/auth/routes.py built the reset-email link from caller-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host, falling back to request.url.netloc which is also Host-derived. Verified nothing constrained it: no TrustedHost middleware, no allowed_hosts, no ALLOWED_HOSTS anywhere. An unauthenticated caller who knew a victim's email could POST /api/auth/forgot-password with X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.example and the victim received a GENUINE ECM email from ECM's own SMTP carrying a live reset token in a link pointing at the attacker's host. No log access needed, and it arrives through a channel the victim trusts.

FIX: config.DispatcharrSettings.public_base_url, exposed on GET/POST /api/settings and a Settings section, admin-gated because whoever controls it controls where a reset link points. When set, the request is not consulted at all. normalize_public_base_url validates a bare origin and rejects path, query, fragment, userinfo, whitespace and bad ports. The READ path re-validates rather than trusting the stored value, because settings.json is hand-edited and restored from backups. The request field is Optional[str] = None so a stale frontend bundle cannot silently clear a security setting on an unrelated save. One-shot-per-process warning at startup when unset, re-armed by clear_settings_cache.

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL, PO's explicit choice: an operator who never sets it stays exposed. The trade was taken so no existing install's password-reset email breaks.

SWEEP for other outbound link construction: 15 documented searches over headers, request.url, url_for/.netloc, email senders, notification payloads, templates, MCP, and origin-construction patterns. Only one other site shares the idiom, routers/channels.py _ecm_origin for logo cache URLs, and it was deliberately left: every call site mutates a dict it is about to return, nothing persists the rewritten URL, so poisoning it poisons only the caller's own response. Codex independently confirmed that reasoning.

CODEX: no findings on this bead across two review rounds. Configured links do not consult request headers; normalization, preserve-on-omit, admin gating and both warning paths verified correct.

VERIFIED: backend 10073 passed 9 skipped; frontend 217 files / 2966 tests; six ratchets by exit code. Red-without-fix proven by four separate source mutations. Emitted-link tests assert on the bytes handed to smtplib.sendmail, not on helper arguments.

title: Password-reset email failure logs the live reset token in plaintext
description:
Found during the Codex-review fix pass on bead upkp1 (PR #865). PRE-EXISTING, unrelated to that branch, and worse than the finding that surfaced it.

backend/auth/routes.py:1455:
  logger.warning('[AUTH] Password reset email failed for %s, token: %s', user.email, raw_token)

On the email-failure branch this writes a LIVE, WORKING password-reset credential into the application log, alongside the user's email address.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE UPKP1 FINDING IT WAS FOUND BESIDE: that one could leak a token HASH via a caller-supplied header, and required the attacker to supply the value. This one writes a working credential the SERVER minted, unprompted, on an ordinary failure path (SMTP down, bad credentials, network blip). Anyone who can read the log can reset that user's password. ECM logs get pasted into GitHub issues; the project has already imported two such issues containing log excerpts.

Same class as the L-4 rule the upkp1 security spec states for the refresh path ('NEVER log the token or the full sha256 hash'), which this predates and violates.

FIX: log that the send failed and for which user id, never the token. If an operator needs a recovery path when email is down, that is a deliberate feature (an admin-triggered reset link surfaced in the UI to an authenticated admin), not a log line.

Check while there: whether any other branch of the reset flow, or the reset-token creation path at routes.py:1307-1312, logs the raw token.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #866 (merge 4b5c9031, build 0.18.1-0107).

The email-failure branch of forgot_password logged a live, working password-reset token in plaintext alongside the account email. Now logs only 'user_id=%s', which also brings the line onto the user_id= convention every other [AUTH] line in the file uses.

SWEEP, not just the reported line. Nine searches over the reset flow, its email helper and the frontend, with commands recorded rather than a bare 'verified': raw_token (12 hits, only this one logged), reset_token (no log call), reset_url (email-body interpolation only), token_urlsafe (single mint site), the request objects (field access only, never passed to a logger), whole-object formatting into loggers via .dict()/model_dump()/.json()/repr()/vars()/__dict__ (ZERO matches repo-wide), request URL and body logging (main.py logs request.url.path, which excludes the query string), journal/audit writes from the reset flow (none), and frontend console.* near token/reset/forgot (none). send_password_reset_email's four log calls are constant strings or %s on a caught SMTP exception.

NO CAPABILITY LOST, checked before removing rather than after. Two recovery paths already exist for broken email: PATCH /api/admin/users/{user_id} (auth/admin_routes.py, gated on get_current_active_admin) accepts a password field and is exactly the admin-triggered reset this would otherwise need, and backend/reset_password.py is a CLI using getpass that never prints. Worth knowing if anyone documents that path: the OTHER admin update_user in auth/routes.py does not accept a password.

VERIFIED: backend 9883 passed 9 skipped (dev 9882/9, exactly +1). Six ratchets by exit code. Red-without-fix re-proven AFTER a rebase onto the post-#865 dev, failing on the right assertion with the 43-character token visible in the captured log.

REBASE NOTE: branched at 449c5bd5, rebased onto 1faf0cc0 after PR #865. auth/routes.py did not actually conflict; #865 left the vulnerable line byte-identical and merely moved it. #865's new logging helpers were checked for redundancy against this fix and are complementary, not overlapping: those constrain CALLER-SUPPLIED input reaching a log, while this is a SERVER-MINTED credential passed as an explicit argument, which no input sanitizer can see.

FOUND DURING THIS WORK AND FILED, both worse or broader than the bead itself:
- qsqfv (P1): the reset LINK host is caller-controlled via X-Forwarded-Host, so an unauthenticated attacker can make ECM email a victim a genuine reset link pointing at the attacker's host. Same credential, different channel, and it needs no log access.
- 5u5h9 (P3): the success path still logs the full account email, twice per event.

title: Auto-renumber on channel insert overflows into subsequent groups instead of stopping at the gap
description:
PO REPORT 2026-08-14, observed on the live instance. Reported as happening 'again', so check whether this regressed rather than assuming it is new.

SYMPTOM: inserting a channel triggers an auto-renumber that does not stop at the end of the target group. Channels in later, unrelated groups are renumbered too.

EXPECTED, in the PO's words: renumber should +1 each channel in the SAME group only, unless there is no gap between groups. Worked example the PO gave:
  group A occupies 201-500
  group B occupies 600-699
  insert at 300
  -> ONLY group A renumbers. Group B must not move, because the gap between 500 and 600 absorbs the shift.

ACTUAL: group B and subsequent further groups renumber as well.

So the defect is that the cascade has no stop condition at the first sufficient gap. The correct rule is that the +1 shift propagates only as far as it must to keep numbers unique, and terminates at the first free number, which in the example is 501.

Related open work, check for overlap before designing a fix: epic enhancedchannelmanager-ic884 'Make channel numbering safe and predictable across edit workflows' and its children, particularly ic884.2 'Preflight the final channel-number state across all staged operations' and ic884.3 'Apply channel-number swaps and renumbers without partial state', plus vdxbx 'Warn before staging duplicate channel numbers in normal edits'. This bead may be a concrete instance of ic884.2's class, or may be independent.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #867 (merge 2e98cb90, build 0.18.1-0108). PO-reported from the live instance.

ROOT CAUSE was frontend planning logic in App.tsx, not a backend cascade. Two defects: the shift moved every channel in the target group at or after the insertion point rather than stopping at the first free number; and the cross-group stop condition was whole-group interval arithmetic (targetGroup.maxNum + shiftAmount < nextGroup.minNum), so because the first defect guaranteed maxNum always moves, a SINGLE outlier high-numbered channel inflated the running max past every downstream group's minimum and swept them all. A third defect, opposite symptom: the same interval model CREATED duplicates when a group whose minimum sorted earlier overlapped the shifted range.

NOT A REGRESSION, and the PO's 'again' was accurate. git log -S currentMaxAfterShift returns exactly one commit, a2913d22 (2026-03-14), byte-identical since. What it replaced shifted every channel in the lineup, the identical complaint. Prior closed beads e81, 1x68, 100 are the same lineage. This was the FOURTH pass at this code, and three prior single-site fixes are why it kept returning.

FIX: one pure planner, frontend/src/utils/channelNumberShift.ts, implementing a global occupancy walk where group membership is an input to intent and never to the arithmetic. Both defective call sites migrated and the interval machinery deleted; a tripwire test asserts both files reference the planner and neither contains currentMaxAfterShift. An independent Codex second opinion confirmed the interval approach has no sound formulation under the real data model, since it would require groups to be contiguous, disjoint and range-ordered and none of the three holds.

CODEX REVIEW found three defects in the first cut, all fixed. The important one: the walk treated the number line as continuous rather than as an insertion lattice, so 300.5 forced a shift when slot 300 was free, AND THE PROPERTY ORACLE ENCODED THE SAME ASSUMPTION while the generator emitted integers only. The suite was green and wrong. The oracle is now derived from the rule and deliberately finer-grained than the planner, so it is a genuine independent check. Second: source-group gap-closing ran outside the plan, so a mover and a remaining channel could both land on the same number; fixed by shared occupancy rather than folding compaction into the planner. Third: rounding could merge two inputs onto one output.

PO CONSTRAINT mid-review (one significant decimal digit in Dispatcharr) retired a whole class of complexity. The grid moved from 1/1000 to tenths, matching the real resolution and the 0.1 insertion step exactly, and the sub-tick machinery was DELETED rather than documented because it covered inputs the system cannot produce. A Codex residual finding about sub-tick minimality is moot on those grounds, not accepted-with-justification. Under tenths the comparison is exact, not conservative: Math.round(x*10) is injective on one-decimal numbers.

VERIFIED: coverage of this behaviour was ZERO before this PR. Red-without-fix proven by porting the OLD algorithm behind the new signature and running the same tests against it: 11 failed, 5 passed. The PO's live bug moved 402 channels under the old algorithm and 201 under the new. Duplicate-freedom failed across 250 randomized sets. Frontend 211 files / 2850 tests; backend diff is two version literals; six ratchets by exit code after committing.

NO E2E, and the reason is a hazard rather than effort: playwright.config.ts defaults E2E_BASE_URL to the PO's live instance, so a spec staging a push-down would renumber real data. Filed as 536bl (P1). Blast-radius coverage shipped as a rendered component test.

Filed from this work: 536bl (P1), z0u1m (P2, the em-dash gate scans only docs/**/*.md so the prose rule is unenforced in code comments), and the PO's precision constraint recorded on ic884.1 which owns enforcement.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE 2026-08-14 (read-only pass, no edits, live instance not modified).

ROOT CAUSE: frontend/src/App.tsx:2072-2141, the push-down cascade in handleBulkCreateFromGroup. This is a FRONTEND, EDIT-MODE-STAGED operation. There is no backend cascade; _run_bulk_commit only replays what the frontend staged. Fix belongs in the frontend planning layer.

TWO defects, and the second is what the PO is seeing:

DEFECT A, App.tsx:2115-2117. The shift never stops at the first free number. It shifts EVERY channel in the target group at or after startingNumber. A hole at 350 in a 201-500 group does not stop it.

DEFECT B, App.tsx:2122-2131. The cross-group stop condition is whole-group interval arithmetic: targetGroup.maxNum + shiftAmount < nextGroup.minNum. maxNum is the max over the ENTIRE group including any outlier, and defect A guarantees maxNum always moves. So a SINGLE stray high-numbered channel anywhere in the target group inflates currentMaxAfterShift past every downstream group's minNum and the loop sweeps them all.

THIRD defect, same root cause, opposite symptom: the interval model also CREATES duplicates. A group whose minNum sorts before the target but whose maxNum overlaps the target's tail is never examined. A=201-500, X={100,505}, insert 5 at 300 -> only A shifts, A's 500 lands on 505, duplicate.

REPRODUCED by porting App.tsx:2073-2141 verbatim into a Node harness:
  A=201-500, B=600-699, C=700-799, D=900-999, insert 1 at 300 -> A only. CORRECT (the PO's idealized example passes).
  Same + one stray channel in A numbered 8000 -> A(202), B(100), C(100). OVERFLOW.
  Same + 3 placeholders at 9900-9902 -> A(204), B(100), C(100). OVERFLOW.
  Same + ungrouped bucket spanning 350-9999 -> A(201), ungrouped(2), B(100), C(100).
  A=201-500, B=503-599, insert 5 at 300 (gap 2 < shift 5) -> B shifted by the full 5, not the 3 it needed.
Deployed-artifact check: the minified bundle on the live instance carries the same algorithm token for token, so no stale-bundle confound.

LONGSTANDING, NOT A REGRESSION, and the PO's 'again' is accurate. git log -S currentMaxAfterShift returns exactly ONE commit ever, a2913d22 (2026-03-14), and the block is byte-identical to HEAD. What a2913d22 REPLACED was a version that shifted every channel in the lineup: the identical complaint. It introduced group-awareness and fixed the clean case, but chose a model (groups as sorted disjoint [min,max] intervals) that is only correct when the lineup is disjoint and outlier-free. Nothing enforces that. Prior closed beads in the same lineage: e81, 1x68, 100. This is the FOURTH pass at this code, and it will keep returning until the rule stops depending on group range geometry.

BLAST RADIUS, two call sites in two files with two independently-written implementations:
  App.tsx:2072-2141 (the cascade) - defects A + B + duplicate-creation
  ChannelsPane.tsx:4434-4483 (cross-group move) - shares defect A; cannot overflow, but silently pushes the target group's tail into the next group's numbers
Verified OK: ChannelsPane gap-closing renumber, drag-reorder, Sort & Renumber, backend channel_pipeline_executor (_get_next_channel_number already implements the correct first-free-number primitive), csv_handler, merge.

TEST COVERAGE: ZERO. No unit test touches the shift behavior; grep over e2e/ for pushDown / 'Channel Number Conflict' returns nothing. That is how three prior fixes each shipped an incomplete rule.

NOT COVERED BY ic884. Opened ic884, ic884.2, ic884.3 and vdxbx and read their acceptance criteria. ic884.2 is validation: it would BLOCK a bad plan, not produce a good one. ic884.3 is application ordering in _run_bulk_commit Phase 2. vdxbx explicitly scopes out cross-group move/renumber workflows. i85dg is shift PLANNING and sits upstream of all three. Recommendation: make i85dg a child of ic884, do NOT fold into ic884.2, keep P1 and ship ahead of the epic.

CORRECT RULE (group membership is an input to intent, never to arithmetic):
Given the set U of all occupied channel numbers in the working copy, an insertion point s, and a count n, find the smallest k >= 0 such that the n+k consecutive slots starting at s can be freed by moving each occupied number in [s, s+n+k-1] up by exactly n. Equivalently: walk upward from s and stop at the first run of n consecutive free numbers. Shift exactly the channels between s and that stop point.

Groups are NOT guaranteed disjoint, verified not assumed: nothing in routers/channels.py, the Channel type or the Dispatcharr contract constrains channel_number by channel_group_id, and the UI even offers 'Create anyway - create with duplicate channel numbers'. Under the occupancy rule that is a non-issue, because the rule never asks where the gap between groups is, only which numbers are free.

Open question for the implementer: whether Dispatcharr enforces channel_number uniqueness server-side could not be settled from this repo. It decides whether 'occupied' is global or per-group. The rule holds either way but the implementation must pick.

ALSO: decimal inserts already drift. shiftAmount = channelCount * 0.1 at App.tsx:2075-2078 gives 3 * 0.1 = 0.30000000000000004, reproduced. Work in integer tenths, divide at the end.

OPERATOR-FACING: the conflict dialog says 'N existing channels would conflict', counting only [s, s+n-1]. It does not say 'and 400 further channels will be renumbered'. Adding the shifted count is part of this fix, not a follow-up.

SIZE: Medium. Algorithm is small; the Medium is two call sites in two files, the test matrix and one E2E. Deliberately not Small: three prior single-site fixes are why we are here a fourth time.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SECOND OPINION (Codex, PO-requested, 2026-08-14). Run independently: Codex was given the PO's bug report and the repository ONLY, and told to reach its own conclusion BEFORE seeing our diagnosis, then to adjudicate ten specific falsifiable claims and explicitly not to defer to us.

INDEPENDENT CONCLUSION: matches ours. Frontend planning logic, not a backend cascade. The March 14 'group-aware' fix models each group as one continuous [min,max] interval, which is false because groups can contain gaps, outliers, overlap or interleave; it also shifts every target-group channel at or above the insertion point, so an outlier expands the calculated maximum and pulls downstream groups into the cascade. Same correct rule: a global occupancy walk.

ADJUDICATION of our ten claims: 8 CONFIRMED outright (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8), 2 CONFIRMED with refinements (9,10). Zero refuted.

REFINEMENT 1, claim 9. Occupancy must be GLOBAL, and the reason is the product rule, not server enforcement. Three implementation qualifications we had not stated: the planner must retain ALL channels per occupied slot (duplicates already exist in the wild), must REMOVE channels being moved from source occupancy where applicable, and must operate on STAGED working state rather than the persisted set. Also: shift all occupants when duplicate numbers already exist at a slot.

REFINEMENT 2, claim 10, and this CORRECTS us. We said decimal inserts drift. Narrower than that: final shifted and newly created decimal numbers ARE rounded to one decimal place, so the OUTPUT does not carry ordinary drift. The defect is in the COMPARISON: currentMaxAfterShift is not rounded before it is compared, so 0.7 + 0.1 evaluates below 0.8 and falsely detects a gap, while other combinations evaluate above the exact boundary and falsely cascade. So float drift is a cause of BOTH wrong-stop and wrong-cascade, not a cosmetic output problem. Our framing would have sent an implementer to the wrong line.

PART 3, the two questions our diagnosis could not settle:

1. DOES DISPATCHARR ENFORCE channel_number UNIQUENESS? NO. Not as a server or database invariant in the recorded 0.28.2 contract. channel_number is indexed but NOT unique; Dispatcharr's release notes state duplicate channel numbers are permitted; the current model declares channel_number as a non-unique float field. There is a same-group clean() check on the model, but Django REST serializers do not automatically call full_clean() and no database constraint backs it, so it is not reliable enforcement.
   CONSEQUENCE: 'occupied' must be GLOBAL, but the deciding factor is the PO's own requested behaviour (propagation across an abutting group boundary), NOT server uniqueness. Codex called this the most important point our diagnosis left unsettled.

2. CAN THE GROUP-INTERVAL APPROACH BE CORRECTED? No, not soundly under the actual data model. It could only work if every group were guaranteed contiguous, mutually disjoint and ordered by range, and none of the three is true. Adding enough exceptions for gaps, outliers, overlaps, interleaving, duplicates and staged changes just becomes an occupancy planner under another name. Extracting one shared occupancy planner for both call sites is the sound formulation.

NET: the diagnosis stands, the recommended fix stands, and the implementation brief must carry refinement 2 (round before comparing, work in integer ticks) and the three staged-state qualifications from refinement 1.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO CONSTRAINT 2026-08-15, authoritative: decimal precision in Dispatcharr is ONE significant digit. Only the tenths place matters.

This retires an entire class of complexity the planner had grown, and moots a Codex finding rather than merely explaining it.

WHAT IT CHANGES:
- The planner used a 1/1000 tick grid, so 1.0001 and 1.0004 were distinct inputs that collapsed to one comparison slot. Under the real contract neither value can exist.
- Codex's residual MEDIUM ('minimality still fails for valid sub-tick channel numbers') was predicated on those values being VALID. They are not. The finding is moot, not accepted-with-justification.
- The machinery added to preserve sub-tick precision on output, and the three tests pinning conservative sub-tick behaviour, cover a case the system cannot produce.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this planner has now been rewritten four times, and the previous rewrite (a2913d22, 2026-03-14) failed because it carried a model of the data that was not true. Carrying machinery for impossible inputs is the same shape of mistake in the opposite direction: it makes the module harder to reason about and gives the next engineer a false picture of what the data can be.

ACTION: align the tick grid to tenths so the planner's notion of a slot matches Dispatcharr's actual resolution and the 0.1 insertion step exactly, and delete the sub-tick handling rather than documenting it.

OUT-OF-CONTRACT INPUT is the one thing to keep deliberate. backend/csv_handler.py:126 accepts any positive float with no precision check and there is no ECM column for channel_number at all, so a 1.05 could still be imported. Under a tenths grid such a value collapses to the nearest tenth for COMPARISON, which is conservative (it can only over-move, never merge two channels onto one number). That behaviour should be stated and tested, not left implicit. Enforcing the contract on input belongs to bead ic884.1, not here.

title: Refresh-token rotation strands a client that never receives the rotated token
description:
THE ACTUAL MECHANISM behind bead suuoh, whose own headline was wrong. Nothing revokes anything at 30 minutes; 30 minutes is access_token_expire_minutes, the first moment a refresh is exercised at all.

ECM rotates the refresh token on EVERY refresh, with a 10 second wall-clock grace (REFRESH_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS, bd-x67qe). The server rotates unconditionally. If the client never receives the response (navigation or abort mid-flight, which browser automation does constantly), its token is permanently dead past 10 seconds and there is no non-interactive way back.

REPRODUCED by QA 2026-08-14 in ~15 seconds at the token-rotation API layer:
  login -> capture refresh cookie R1
  POST /api/auth/refresh with R1, response DISCARDED (simulates the aborted navigation)
  retry with R1 at t+1s  -> 200  (inside the grace window)
  retry with R1 at t+13s -> 401  {"detail":"Session not found or revoked"}
The only variable between 200 and 401 is the delay, isolating the grace window as the cause.

Ruled out, with the checks that ruled them out: no scheduled task touches UserSession (grep over task_registry and tasks/ returns zero); no sibling-session revocation on login (routes.py:688-707 only inserts); container restart purges expired sessions only (RestartCount=0, one startup purge line); 0 rows on the live instance where expires_at != created_at + 7 days.

OPTIONS, and this is a PO security-posture decision, deliberately not made unattended:
(a) leave as-is. Strongest replay-detection posture, keeps stranding long-running clients.
(b) widen the grace window (e.g. 60s). Proportionally widens the window in which a stolen predecessor token is usable.
(c) switch from wall-clock grace to ROTATION CONFIRMATION: keep the predecessor valid until the successor is first used. Removes the stranding class entirely without a fixed exposure window, but is a real change to the rotation contract and needs its own security review.

Engineer recommendation was (c). Not implemented.

Also unlogged: /api/auth/refresh 401s produce no log line at all (38 hours of container logs contain zero refresh-related lines, success or failure), which is why this had to be diagnosed from a browser error body. AuthenticationError raises silently at routes.py:842. Filed separately.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #865 (merge 1faf0cc0, build 0.18.1-0106). PO chose option (c), rotation confirmation, on 2026-08-14.

The predecessor refresh token now stays valid until its successor is ACTUALLY USED, replacing the 10-second wall-clock window that stranded any client whose rotated response never arrived.

NO MIGRATION AND NO NEW STATE. The rotation UPDATE already wrote prior_refresh_token_hash = the token just presented, so the moment a successor is accepted the predecessor's hash is overwritten out of the row and stops matching. 'Valid until the successor is used' IS 'valid until it is overwritten'. Confirmation fell out of the existing single-generation storage, so models.py changed by comment only and the substance of the change was DELETING the wall-clock condition. REFRESH_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS is gone from the repository, not widened and not renamed: a constant set to 3600 and relabelled would have been option (b) wearing option (c)'s name, and the acceptance test sleeps a real 13 seconds specifically so it cannot pass that way.

DESIGN FIRST. A security specification was written by the security-engineer persona before any code, covering the normative acceptance rule, reuse detection, why no new outer bound is needed, StaticPool concurrency constraints, chain depth, and three reject-on-sight review gates. The implementing engineer contradicted the spec in three places and was right each time, including that a required test property would have passed for the wrong reason as written.

DELIBERATE DECISIONS, recorded rather than discovered later: no revocation on a superseded token (with one generation retained, a superseded hash exists in no row, so the server cannot tell a replay from a deleted session or a stale cookie, and in ECM one session row IS the chain, so revoking would log the operator out of everything on five classes of legitimate client); and no new outer bound (the predecessor is already bounded by its own JWT exp and by expires_at, which the predecessor path deliberately does not extend).

CODEX REVIEW found four issues, all fixed in 4bb0b2c8. The High is the one to remember: _client_address() logged X-Forwarded-For VERBATIM AND UNBOUNDED, and User-Agent was truncated at 80 characters, which a 64-character sha256 digest fits inside intact. An unauthenticated caller could write a refresh token or its full hash into the auth log through the logging this very change added, and our own negative test missed it because it only checked cookie-derived tokens. Fixed by validation rather than truncation: an address is rendered from ipaddress and never echoed, free-form fields have secret-shaped runs redacted BEFORE truncation so a secret cannot straddle the cut. Four pre-existing login-path call sites carried the same idiom and were fixed rather than filed. Also fixed: an expiry boundary accepting exact equality, a spec that contradicted itself on whether the account check was a fifth acceptance condition (the code was right), and a residual-risk claim that overstated acquisition equivalence.

VERIFIED: backend 9882 passed 9 skipped, frontend clean, all six ratchets by exit code after catching that tail was masking a real check_secrets failure. Every new regression test proven red without the fix by source mutation.

KNOWN AND NOT FIXED: this does NOT fix bead 67onh. With N contexts sharing one captured token, stranding now begins at the second rotation (about one access-token lifetime) instead of t0+10s. A large practical improvement, not a fix.

Filed from this work: cb1e1 (P1, password-reset token logged in plaintext), nymj6 (P3, unbounded username in login-failure logs).

title: Alert-method reads return Discord webhooks, Telegram tokens and SMTP passwords in plaintext, bypassing the masking that already exists on the model
description:
Found by an independent adversarial review (OpenAI Codex) of the 9kwzp.10 reconnaissance, then verified against origin/dev at 9884d14c.

THE DEFECT. GET /api/alert-methods (backend/routers/alert_methods.py:150) and GET /api/alert-methods/{method_id} (:266) hand-roll their response dict and put the credential blob in it RAW:

    "config": json.loads(m.config) if m.config else {},

The router contains ZERO masking (grep for mask/***/redact returns 0). Per the test-route documentation in the same file, that config can hold Discord webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and SMTP passwords. Neither read route carries a route-level auth dependency, so any authenticated caller AND the MCP service principal can read them in plaintext.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN A MISSING FEATURE. The masking already exists and the router bypasses it. backend/models.py AlertMethod.to_dict(include_sensitive=False) builds masked_config and substitutes '********' for sensitive keys; its docstring says 'By default, sensitive config values are masked.' The two read routes do not call to_dict at all.

AND THE CODEBASE BELIEVES THE MASKING IS LIVE. backend/routers/backup.py:131-133 says the backup redaction set 'Matches the masking set in AlertMethod.to_dict (models.py) so backup redaction stays in lock-step with the API-response masking already shipped to clients.' That written assumption is false for these two routes, which means a future reader reasoning about where alert credentials can leak will reach the wrong answer from the comments.

RELATION TO 9ej7f. This is the same class that bead fixed on GET /api/settings, which withheld discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id from exactly this principal. Note the irony worth recording: 9ej7f redacted the SHARED Telegram token from the settings surface while the per-alert-method surface continued to hand out the same category of secret unmasked, in plaintext rather than as a masked tail.

SCOPE, TWO PARTS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE.
1. AUTHORIZATION, being handled under bead 9kwzp.10 item 4, which is already gating these routers. Not this bead.
2. REDACTION, this bead. Route the reads through AlertMethod.to_dict(include_sensitive=False), or apply the same masking inline, so a permitted reader still does not receive plaintext credentials. Decide deliberately whether any caller should ever get include_sensitive=True over HTTP, and if so which. Then correct or delete the now-false lock-step comment at backup.py:131-133, and add a test pinning that the read routes never emit a raw credential value, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart again.

Also check GET /api/alert-methods/types and the PATCH/POST response bodies for the same raw-config shape; only the two GETs were inspected here.

METHOD NOTE. This was surfaced by adversarial review rather than by the audit that produced 9kwzp.10, and it outranks every item in that bead. The reviewer had no shell access and worked from a code dump, which suggests the finding was reachable from reading alone and the earlier sweep simply did not look at read-path redaction while it was busy with authorization.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #857, merged to dev as b0e0a5ad, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms the registry carries 0.18.1-0096 built from a successful run of that commit.

GET /api/alert-methods and GET /api/alert-methods/{id} hand-rolled their response dict around json.loads(m.config), emitting Discord webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and SMTP passwords in clear. Both now serialize through AlertMethod.to_dict(include_sensitive=False), which already existed and already substituted '********' for password, bot_token, webhook_url and api_key. The masking was not missing; the routes bypassed it.

WHY MASKING RATHER THAN 9ej7f's EMPTY REDACTION. The round-trip hazard that forced empty redaction on the settings surface was checked specifically and does not apply here: AlertMethodsSection reads only id/name/method_type/enabled and never touches config; the SMTP-recipient save in SettingsTab builds a FRESH {to_emails: ...} object rather than spreading the loaded config back; and to_emails, the only key read out of a loaded config, is not in the masking set. Those are the only non-test callers, and the MCP tool never echoes config. No caller returns a masked value to the server.

EVERY ROUTE IN THE ROUTER WAS CHECKED, not just the two the bead named. POST, PATCH, DELETE, POST /{id}/test and GET /types do not emit config. The two GETs were the only leaks. include_sensitive=True has no caller and was given none: the legitimate need to prove a credential works is already served by POST /{id}/test, which sends with the stored value without disclosing it. Pinned by an AST-based test, because a substring grep matches the docstrings that explain the rule.

THE FALSE COMMENT IS NOW TRUE. backup.py asserted that backup redaction stayed 'in lock-step with the API-response masking already shipped to clients'. That claim was false and is why the hole stayed invisible: a reader reasoning about where alert credentials could leak got the wrong answer from a comment. Corrected rather than deleted, and it now records which clause used to be false.

THE DURABLE PART is the anti-drift guard, parametrized over routers.backup._ALERT_METHOD_CREDENTIAL_KEYS, so adding a key to the backup denylist without adding it to the model's masking set fails a test. That drift is what let the two surfaces disagree in the first place. Nine tests; red-before-green proven by restoring the pre-fix handler, which reds the 5 masking tests while the 4 contract tests still pass.

RESPONSE SHAPE: to_dict returns one additional field, updated_at. Nothing is dropped. Allowed through as a compatible addition consistent with the two timestamps already returned; popping it would have been a second divergence to maintain. Pinned by test_list_still_carries_every_previously_returned_field.

RESIDUALS RECORDED, NOT FIXED. First, the MCP principal can still read a Telegram method's chat_id, while bead 9ej7f withholds telegram_chat_id from that same principal on GET /api/settings. It is a destination identifier rather than a credential (posting still needs the masked bot_token), and widening the mask would also change _ALERT_METHOD_CREDENTIAL_KEYS and therefore DBAS backup redaction, so it is recorded in four places rather than decided unilaterally. Needs a PO call. Second, update_alert_method REPLACES the config blob rather than merging; not a live bug today because validate_config() rejects a config missing required fields and to_emails is an SMTP method's entire config, but it is a whole-object write and is now documented as one.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING. This bead exists because an independent adversarial review asked what the routes RETURN while the audit that produced 9kwzp.10 was asking who may CALL them. Gating a route and redacting its response are different questions, and only one of them was asked. Verification of the fix then found a stale marker the author's own sweep missed, and pushing back on that single instance surfaced two more plus an unrelated overstatement about what _mask_credentials discloses for credentials of eight characters or fewer. Backend 9639 passed / 9 skipped.

title: The entire /api/tls/* router carries zero route-level auth: cert upload, cert deletion, DNS credentials and HTTPS lifecycle are reachable by any authenticated user and by the MCP key
description:
Found by the sibling-endpoint audit while fixing bead enhancedchannelmanager-9kwzp.8, and independently verified. This is the closest structural sibling to 9kwzp.8 and is arguably larger.

THE DEFECT. backend/tls/routes.py contains ZERO route-level auth dependencies. Verified: grep -cE 'Require|Depends\(get_current' backend/tls/routes.py returns 0, across a router with ten-plus mutating endpoints:

  POST   /api/tls/configure            (:189)
  POST   /api/tls/request-cert         (:251)
  POST   /api/tls/complete-challenge   (:437)
  POST   /api/tls/upload-cert          (:522)
  POST   /api/tls/renew                (:595)
  POST   /api/tls/https/start          (:644)
  POST   /api/tls/https/stop           (:671)
  POST   /api/tls/https/restart        (:685)
  DELETE /api/tls/certificate          (:724)
  POST   /api/tls/test-dns-provider    (:762)

Everything rests on the global middleware in main.py, which only establishes that the caller is authenticated. So any authenticated non-admin, AND the MCP service principal (which _build_mcp_service_principal stamps is_admin=True and main.py:565-571 accepts across the whole /api/ surface), can upload or delete TLS certificate material, rewrite TLS configuration, exercise DNS-provider credentials against a caller-influenced target, and stop or restart the HTTPS server.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS SEVERAL ALREADY-FIXED SIBLINGS. Beads i4qrp, 9kwzp.6 and 9kwzp.7 closed eleven outbound-test sinks whose worst case is a status-code oracle plus a send of stored credentials. Bead 9kwzp.8 closed an escalation path. This router combines both shapes and adds a third: DELETE /api/tls/certificate and POST /api/tls/https/stop are availability impact on the operator's own TLS termination, and POST /api/tls/upload-cert accepts attacker-supplied cert material. Bead 2owpi separately records that DNS-provider credentials are stored in plaintext in /config/tls_settings.json, so test-dns-provider exercises secrets that are already weakly protected.

SCOPE.
1. Decide the tier per endpoint rather than blanket-applying one. Most are admin-only configuration and fit the ordinary admin tier; the credential-touching and destructive ones (upload-cert, certificate DELETE, test-dns-provider, the https lifecycle trio) are the human-admin shape that RequireHumanAdminForServiceCredential and RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest already implement. Do NOT reach for RequireAdminIfEnabled without checking: it admits the MCP principal, which is the half that matters here.
2. Check for a first-run path before gating. TLS configuration may legitimately be reachable during initial setup; if so, the require_auth/setup_complete no-op behaviour of the existing dependencies already covers it, but verify rather than assume, exactly as beads i4qrp and 9kwzp.8 did.
3. Pin every verdict in backend/tests/test_admin_gate_inventory.py, which asserts both the MCP-denied and MCP-admitted sets exactly, and follow the four-case test shape those beads established: non-admin refused, MCP principal refused, admin reaches handler, first-run still reaches handler.

CONTEXT WORTH RECORDING. The same audit noted roughly 140 mutating /api/* routes rely solely on the global middleware. That is the epic's standing posture question and is deliberately NOT this bead; this bead is the one router where the material at risk is TLS private-key and certificate lifecycle. Two smaller items were also listed and not actioned: POST /api/settings/reset-stats (no dependency, wipes seven stats tables, destructive-data class rather than identity) and GET /api/settings/mcp-status (read-only probe of an env-configured host, informational).

Shipped in PR #854, merged to dev as 9884d14c, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0094 built from a successful run of that commit.

backend/tls/routes.py had ZERO route-level auth dependencies across 13 routes; everything rested on the global middleware, which establishes only that the caller is authenticated. All 13 are now gated (verified on merged dev: 13 route handlers, 13 _admin bindings).

TIERS, decided per endpoint rather than blanket-applied, because the routes span four risk classes:
- RequireHumanAdminForTLSMaterial (new 4th constant over the existing factory, MCP refused) on 10: upload-cert (accepts caller-supplied cert AND private key, makes it the instance's transport identity), DELETE /certificate (destroys operator material, no undo), configure (writes the DNS credentials bead 2owpi records as plaintext on disk), request-cert / complete-challenge / renew (drive stored credentials, mint private keys), the https start/stop/restart trio (availability of the operator's own TLS termination, gated as a unit since restart-without-stop is an arbitrary split), and GET /settings.
- RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest (reused, not re-worded) on test-dns-provider: the i4qrp shape verbatim, and its existing 403 body already names that shape, so TLS wording would misdirect triage.
- RequireAdminIfEnabled on GET /status and GET /https/status: neither returns credential material, and subject/issuer/validity are served to every TLS client anyway.

GET /settings is denied to the MCP principal deliberately, on the reasoning that MASKED IS NOT ABSENT: it emits the last four characters of dns_api_token, aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key plus dns_zone_id and acme_email in clear, which is the class bead 9ej7f withheld from this same principal.

NO LOCKOUT, verified not assumed: SetupPage.tsx has zero TLS references and imports one API function; the only consumer is TLSSettingsSection under a settings id already carrying adminOnly: true; the https lifecycle routes have zero frontend consumers; no /api/tls path is in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS (now pinned by a test); mcp-server exposes no TLS tool; the renewal scheduler calls in-process rather than over HTTP.

TESTS, 91 new. Two design choices worth carrying forward: test_every_tls_route_has_a_recorded_verdict walks the live app, because the inventory can only see GATED routes and a future 14th ungated route would otherwise be invisible to it; and every case asserts a per-route witness mock so a refusal is proved to be the gate answering rather than the handler erroring for an unrelated reason. Backend 9517 passed / 9 skipped.

UNTOUCHED DELIBERATELY: the GET /settings masking and POST /configure's startswith('***') round-trip guard. That pairing is already correct and is the guard backend/routers/settings.py lacked, which is why 9ej7f had to use empty redaction there instead. Scope here was authorization, not redaction.

CAVEAT ON ALL OF THE ABOVE, from a later adversarial review: every Require*IfEnabled gate no-ops when require_auth is false or setup is incomplete. These routes are admin-gated in the normal authenticated posture, not categorically.

title: POST and DELETE /api/settings/mcp-api-key carry no auth dependency: any authenticated non-admin can mint an admin-equivalent credential
description:
Found during the RequireAdminIfEnabled per-site audit for bead enhancedchannelmanager-9kwzp.7, and independently verified.

THE DEFECT. Both handlers take no parameters and carry no Depends of any kind:

  backend/routers/settings.py:2326  @router.post("/mcp-api-key")
  backend/routers/settings.py:2327  async def generate_mcp_api_key():
  backend/routers/settings.py:2337  @router.delete("/mcp-api-key")
  backend/routers/settings.py:2338  async def revoke_mcp_api_key():

WHY THIS IS PRIVILEGE ESCALATION, not just a missing admin gate. The MCP API key is not an ordinary setting. backend/auth/dependencies.py:66 builds the MCP service principal with is_admin=True, and backend/main.py:565-571 accepts the static key as an alternative to a JWT for the whole /api/ surface. So any authenticated non-admin can mint themselves a credential that the middleware treats as admin, then use it for everything the admin tier allows. The revoke half is a denial-of-service on every legitimate sidecar integration.

This is arguably more severe than the four sinks bead i4qrp closed and the seven bead 9kwzp.6 and 9kwzp.7 closed, all of which required an already-privileged caller to be useful.

SCOPE. Gate both handlers. Choose the tier deliberately rather than copying the outbound-test dependency: minting the MCP credential is an identity operation, not an outbound probe, so the human-admin family (reject_mcp_service_principal=True) is very likely correct here for a different reason than it was there. The MCP principal should almost certainly not be able to rotate or revoke its own key. Confirm no first-run or setup path calls either endpoint before gating, the same check bead i4qrp made, and pin the verdict in backend/tests/test_admin_gate_inventory.py so the classification is asserted rather than assumed.

Also audit sibling identity operations in the same router for the same omission.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #851, merged to dev as faba3218, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0091 built from a successful run of that commit.

POST /api/settings/mcp-api-key and DELETE /api/settings/mcp-api-key took no parameters and declared no dependency, so any authenticated caller could mint a credential the middleware treats as admin (_build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True and main.py accepts the static key as a JWT alternative across all of /api/). Both now carry RequireHumanAdminForServiceCredential, a sibling of the RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest gate from build 0089 rather than a reuse of it: the behaviour matches but the 403 body does not, and nothing on this route reaches the network, so an outbound-test denial message would misdirect triage. The MCP principal is refused for a reason distinct from the outbound sinks, namely that it would be the bearer of a credential rotating and revoking that same credential; a minted key is disclosed only in the response body, so a holder of a leaked key could mint a successor surviving the operator's own rotation. Setup mode verified rather than assumed, no first-run caller. test_admin_gate_inventory.py records the verdict under _SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_LIFECYCLE; the MCP-denied set is now 16 routes asserted exactly. Backend 9381 passed / 9 skipped.

PUBLISH INCIDENT DURING THIS SHIP, recorded because the bead's own verification hit it. The first post-merge publish run for faba3218 FAILED: a single frontend flake (StickySectionNav re-arm, now tracked as bead vmk2m.1) failed 'Wait for Test Suite', which gated every image-build job, so all five skipped and nothing published. dev sat at 0091 while the registry carried 0090. Recovered by re-running the failed test job, then re-running the publish workflow, then confirming the marker moved. Worth knowing that a flake anywhere in the frontend suite can diverge dev from the registry; that is a different door into the staleness class beads i24jr and t8fqg addressed by detection.

Sibling findings from this bead's audit, filed and NOT fixed: 9kwzp.11 (P1, the entire /api/tls/* router carries zero route-level auth) and 9kwzp.12 (POST /api/settings/reset-stats ungated, wipes seven stats tables).

title: Worktree agents are branched from origin/main, not dev, so work silently lands on a stale base
description:
THIRD harness-level worktree bug in this environment, alongside the cwd-trap and lock-accumulation pair already documented in CLAUDE.md under 'Worktree & Agent Isolation'. This one is more dangerous than either, because nothing looks wrong: the agent works, its gates pass, and its branch is simply built on code from weeks ago.

EVIDENCE. A worktree agent spawned 2026-08-12 for the GH #801 cluster produced this reflog on its own branch:

  ae25ad70 worktree-agent-aa96dfb009a431e01@{4}: branch: Created from origin/main

ae25ad70 is 'Merge pull request #748 from MotWakorb/release/v0.18.0', dated 2026-07-26. The project works on dev, which was at eecd257a. The worktree was therefore 858 files and roughly 141k lines behind before the agent typed anything.

CONCRETE HARM MEASURED IN THAT RUN. The brief named _find_unique_channel_by_exact_identity, added by PR #848 (bead ukgj9) on dev, as a second call site the fix had to cover. That symbol DID NOT EXIST on the worktree's base, so the requirement was unsatisfiable until the agent noticed and rebased onto origin/dev mid-task. The rebase hit a conflict in docs/user_guide/channel-pipeline/debugging-rules.md from an upstream em-dash scrub. An agent that did not notice would have produced a branch that passes its own gates, silently omits half the fix, and reverts 141k lines of unrelated work on merge.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS. origin/main is the repository's default branch, so a worktree created without an explicit start point takes it. Everything downstream looks healthy: git status is clean, the tests pass, the diff against the worktree's own base is small and correct.

SCOPE.
1. Find where the worktree start point is chosen. If it is settable on our side, pin it to the branch the session is actually on (dev), not the default branch.
2. If it is not settable, make detection cheap and mandatory: a first-action check in every worktree brief comparing the worktree's merge-base against origin/dev, plus a documented rebase step.
3. Document it in CLAUDE.md's 'Worktree & Agent Isolation' section as a third standing caveat, and add the merge-base check to the standing worktree brief.
4. Audit any other worktree branch still on disk for the same stale base before trusting or merging it.

RELATED: bead enhancedchannelmanager-fekkc (worktrees have no .venv, so backend pytest silently uses the wrong interpreter) is the same family of problem, a worktree that looks usable but is quietly not equivalent to the main checkout.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-13, from an audit of my own bead-writing. One claim in this bead's description is WRONG and must not be relied on when the work is picked up.

The description says a stale-base branch 'silently omits part of its fix and reverts everything dev gained since the stale base, on merge'. The second half is not how a three-way merge behaves. Changes made only on dev since the merge base are PRESERVED when the stale branch did not touch those paths. Git does not revert unrelated upstream work just because a branch is old.

The real hazards, which are still serious and still justify the priority:
- Work built against code that no longer exists, so the fix is incomplete or targets the wrong shape. That is what actually happened: the brief named _find_unique_channel_by_exact_identity, added on dev by PR #848, and it did not exist on the worktree's base at all.
- Local verification that means nothing, because gates pass against a tree that is not what will merge.
- Conflicts in any file both sides touched, which on that run was CHANGELOG.md.
- A PR diff large enough that review is useless.

Keep the P1. The harness-integrity problem is real and the measured evidence (branch created from origin/main at ae25ad70, 858 files behind dev at eecd257a) is unchanged. Only the merge-damage claim was overstated.

ALSO UNVERIFIED, recorded so nobody assumes otherwise: the component that chose origin/main is not in this repository, so scope item 1, pinning the start point, may not be actionable in-repo at all. Item 2, the mandatory merge-base check in every worktree brief, is the part that is certainly actionable here.

title: A rename into a .md path hides the source file, so a code-deleting PR classifies docs-only and all seven required checks go green having run nothing
description:
Found by a security review of PR #815 on 2026-08-10, verified end to end, and independently re-verified by the orchestrator against a real commit in this repository. PRE-EXISTING in CI. Not introduced by that PR, which is why it did not block it.

THE MECHANISM. 'git diff --name-only A...B' with default rename detection prints ONLY THE DESTINATION for a renamed file. GitHub's compare API has the same shape: the detect job's jq is '.[].filename', and 'previous_filename' is discarded.

VERIFIED ON THIS REPO, commit b47ced96:
  git diff --name-only b47ced96^...b47ced96              -> 18 files
  git diff --name-only --no-renames b47ced96^...b47ced96 -> 19 files
The path present only in the second is frontend/src/components/settings/SecuritySettingsSection.css, the rename source. The API confirms it: status 'renamed', previous_filename set, and the detect job throws that field away.

WHY IT MATTERS. The classifier verdict decides whether six of the seven required status checks execute ANYTHING. On docs_only=true, Backend Tests, Frontend Tests, MCP Server Tests, Semgrep Lint and both CodeQL Analysis contexts gate every step on docs_only != 'true'. Only Version Consistency does real work, and only its consistency half.

AND dev REQUIRES NO REVIEWS. Verified: 'gh api .../branches/dev/protection --jq .required_pull_request_reviews' returns null. Green checks are the entire gate. The merging actor is frequently an agent whose standing instruction is to drive the merge once the required checks are green, so the likelihood factor is not a careless human, it is an automated merge on a green rollup.

ATTACK SCENARIO, reproduced end to end by the reviewer against the real hook:
  git mv backend/tests/unit/test_auth_middleware.py docs/legacy_auth_test_notes.md
  title it 'docs: archive superseded test notes'
Verdict is documentation-only. All seven required contexts report success having executed nothing. No review required. A follow-up PR then changes auth with that test gone.

THIS IS NOT BEAD gnz19. gnz19 says the docs-only DEFINITION is too broad. This is the INPUT SET omitting a path that genuinely changed. Broadening or narrowing the glob list does not fix it, and fixing this does not fix gnz19.

REMEDIATION, both verified working by the reviewer, neither applied:
  CI half, P1: .github/workflows/test.yml detect job, change the jq to '.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)'. Verified to emit both sides on b47ced96.
  Hook half, P2: .claude/hooks/version-advance-guard.sh:228-229, add --no-renames to the git diff.
Fix CI first. The hook is advisory and local; CI is the actual gate.

VERIFICATION TO ADD: a fixture case in backend/tests/unit/test_classify_changed_paths.py asserting a rename-to-.md classifies as CODE, plus a hook case mirroring the reproduction above. Without those this silently regresses.

CONTEXT: bead t4d5w (PR #814) made documentation-only PRs a real path for the first time by giving them their own gate, and bead uf2gh (PR #815) makes that path reachable agent-side. Neither created this defect, but together they make it materially easier to hit.
close_reason: CI and hook halves merged via PRs #816 and #815; rename-source blind spot closed with --no-renames.
