title: Secrets audit: add a secrets arm to the PII guard, and sweep git history for already-committed credentials
description:
PO-directed 2026-08-10. Two halves that answer different questions: prevention stops new secrets landing, detection tells us whether we are already leaking. Neither substitutes for the other.

CURRENT POSTURE, measured:
  secret_scanning                        ENABLED
  secret_scanning_push_protection        ENABLED
  secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns  DISABLED
  secret_scanning_validity_checks        DISABLED
  dependabot_security_updates            DISABLED
  repo-side tooling (gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets)  NONE

GitHub's scanning covers PROVIDER patterns: AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Stripe keys and similar. It does NOT cover ECM's own credential shapes, which is precisely where this application's risk lives: mcp_api_key, Dispatcharr username and password, Discord webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens, SMTP passwords, TLS private keys, Emby/Plex/Jellyfin tokens.

That gap is not hypothetical. Today's work found three separate mishandlings of exactly those values: gi4zn (P1, standard redacted DBAS backup leaves the XC/M3U username in cleartext while redacting the password), 9ej7f (GET /api/settings returns discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id raw while correctly redacting seven sibling secrets), and 9kwzp.2 (an attacker-supplied backup can plant a persistent mcp_api_key that survives the operator later re-enabling require_auth).

ATTEMPTED AND FAILED: enabling the two disabled toggles via 'gh api -X PATCH repos/.../security_and_analysis'. Returns HTTP 200 with the state unchanged, with no warning header, on a token carrying the accepted 'repo' scope. Characteristic of an Advanced Security feature unavailable on a free personal public repo rather than a permissions problem. Needs the PO in Settings > Code security > Secret scanning, or is simply unavailable.

HALF ONE, PREVENTION. Add a secrets arm to scripts/check_pii.py. That script already has the right architecture and a documented seam for a second arm (left for fu6yd's image arm; this fits the same slot): added-lines-only ratchet computed at runtime via git show of the merge base, masked output because CI logs are public, identifiers stored as SHA-256 rather than plaintext, fail-closed on unparseable input, and a fixture self-test. Reuse it; do not build a parallel tool.

HALF TWO, DETECTION. Sweep git history for already-committed credentials. Findings drive ROTATION, which is a real-world action with side effects, not a code change. The PII sweep already found a private mockup URL, absolute local filesystem paths and real EPG/Dispatcharr account names in committed docs, so the prior is not zero.

HANDLING CONSTRAINT ON HALF TWO, NON-NEGOTIABLE: a report that quotes a found secret re-leaks it into transcripts, bead descriptions and PR bodies. Findings must be recorded as location plus type plus liveness only, never the value. Same discipline check_pii.py already applies by masking its own output.

RELATED: dependabot_security_updates is disabled. Adjacent but a separate decision; not in scope here.
close_reason: Merged in PR #818; ECM-specific and generic secret ratchets shipped with base-derived immutable authority and value-free reporting.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
TOGGLE QUESTION RESOLVED (2026-08-10): the two disabled settings CANNOT be enabled on this repo, and no PO action remains.

The PO checked Settings > Security and Quality > Advanced Security. The only options offered are:
  - Secret Protection / partner patterns: always on for public repositories, not configurable
  - Push protection: available, and already ENABLED

secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns and secret_scanning_validity_checks are GitHub ADVANCED SECURITY features. They are paid and are not offered on a free personal public repository. That explains the earlier API behaviour precisely: 'gh api -X PATCH' returned HTTP 200 with state unchanged and no warning header, on a token carrying the accepted 'repo' scope. The endpoint accepts and silently ignores a request for a feature the plan does not include.

THE IMPLICATION, which changes this bead's priority rather than reducing it:

There is now NO GitHub-side path to covering ECM's own credential shapes. Partner patterns cover third-party provider formats such as AWS, Stripe and GitHub tokens. They will never cover mcp_api_key, Dispatcharr username/password/API key, Discord webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens, SMTP passwords, Emby/Plex/Jellyfin tokens, TLS private keys, or session and JWT signing secrets. Non-provider scanning is exactly the feature that would have, and it is behind the paywall.

So half one of this bead, the secrets arm on scripts/check_pii.py, is not defence in depth. It is the ONLY control that will ever catch this class in this repository.

Two consequences for whoever builds and reviews it:

1. PRECISION IS NOW LOAD-BEARING. If the arm is noisy and somebody disables it, nothing replaces it. There is no second layer. Prefer five precise rules over fifteen approximate ones, and treat a rule class that cannot be made precise as a finding to report rather than a threshold to tune.

2. PUSH PROTECTION IS STILL A REAL BACKSTOP, but only for partner patterns. Do not let its presence be read as broader coverage than it has. It will block an AWS key at push time; it will not notice an mcp_api_key.

Also confirmed unchanged and out of scope: dependabot_security_updates remains disabled. Separate decision.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
HISTORY SWEEP COMPLETE (2026-08-10), half two. NO VALUES RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS COMMENT.

TWO REAL mcp_api_key VALUES FOUND. BOTH CONFIRMED DEAD. NO ROTATION NEEDED.

Finding 1, PUBLICLY EXPOSED. A live ECM mcp_api_key was committed in .mcp.json (mcpServers.ecm.url, api_key= query param), reachable from BOTH origin/main and origin/dev. Present in the tip from 2026-03-31 (4aa050f8 / fd44e61c) to 2026-05-22, removed by 861e72a9 ('security(mcp): remove hardcoded api_key from committed .mcp.json'). Roughly 52 days in the tip, permanently in public history. The URL also disclosed the internal MCP hostname and port 6101 over plain http.

Finding 2, LOCAL ONLY, NEVER PUSHED. A different mcp_api_key value in an unreachable stash commit (caca1bdf, 2026-05-16), inside a Playwright a11y snapshot that had captured the Settings > MCP Integration card with the key rendered in a code element. The agent built the full object graph (19,260 trees, 7,226 commits) and confirmed the blob sits in 0 refs and 0 reachable commits, so git never pushed it. Exposure is local disk plus anything that copied .git wholesale.

LIVENESS RESOLVED WITHOUT USING EITHER CREDENTIAL. The agent supplied an offline hash comparison; the orchestrator ran it against the live container. Current key SHA-256 prefix c64cc042bb41ab03. Finding 1 is 020dd76a1db9a801, Finding 2 is 966a609b4cb5497d. Neither matches, so both leaked keys were already rotated out. No third party was contacted and no credential was authenticated with, per the PO's explicit no-verification ruling.

PO DECISION: NO HISTORY REWRITE. Rotation neutralises a leaked key, and rewriting is only worth it when a secret cannot be rotated. This one has a Regenerate button and is already dead. Rewriting main and dev would invalidate in-flight PRs, every fork and clone, all 5,210 commit SHAs and the commit hashes this repo cites in its own docs and beads, and GitHub keeps the old objects reachable by SHA regardless. Consistent with the precedent set on il1xz: accept the historical exposure, ratchet against new ones.

CLEAN RESULTS, WITH COVERAGE. All 16,372 blobs scanned, not sampled: 16,052 text across three passes and 320 binary. Covers all 5,210 reachable commits across 90-plus local refs AND unreachable objects, which is how Finding 2 surfaced. Nothing size-skipped. 20 pattern classes, 11 ECM-specific and 9 provider. Zero real Discord webhooks (4 placeholders), zero Telegram bot tokens (not one match for the real digits-colon-35-char shape), zero real SMTP passwords (13 placeholders), zero real Dispatcharr credentials (21 fixtures), zero real Emby/Plex/Jellyfin tokens, zero real TLS private keys, two synthetic and expired JWTs, .beads/ clean across 620 blobs, backend/ecm.db committed once as a ZERO-BYTE file, and auth_settings.json NEVER existed in history.

PRECISION DATA, and the empirical case for the guard arm's rule design. Pass 1 with generic keyword-anchored rules: 274 hits, 1 true positive, a roughly 99.6 percent false-positive rate. Pass 2 with shape-anchored rules: of 51 distinct high-entropy 43-character values, 50 were npm lockfile integrity hashes and 1 was the real key. The fix is to anchor mcp_api_key to 'api_key=' in a URL or an mcp_api_key assignment rather than to the bare token_urlsafe(32) shape.

THE BOUNDARY THAT MUST BE DOCUMENTED. Both findings are invisible to a working-tree scanner. Finding 1's tip was cleaned in 2026-05; Finding 2 never had a tip. detect-secrets with a baseline, and the check_pii ratchet, both scan CURRENT files. The guard arm prevents the next leak; it does not detect existing ones. 'The arm is green' must never be read as 'history is clean'.

TOOLING. gitleaks, trufflehog, detect-secrets and ggshield were all absent from the environment, so the agent wrote purpose-built stdlib Python with no network access rather than fetching a scanner at run time, explicitly declining the supply-chain exposure. It authenticated to nothing, and verified its own findings JSON programmatically for raw-value leakage.

REMAINING GAPS, priority order: 144 of 152 images received byte-pattern and metadata checks only, never OCR (filed separately); objects that exist only on GitHub, since this scan covered the local object DB; and partial path attribution (1,525 blobs unattributed because git log --raw skips merges, which degrades labelling only, not coverage).

title: Phase 1: give documentation-only PRs a real gate before the version hook stops forcing bumps
description:
From an architecture spike on 2026-08-10. PO approved Phase 1; Phase 2 (aggregator job plus branch-protection migration) is deferred to a separate decision.

THE PROBLEM. On a documentation-only PR, six of the seven required status checks on dev run a single echo and report SUCCESS having executed nothing: Backend Tests (test.yml:163), Frontend Tests (:378), MCP Server Tests (:293), Semgrep Lint (:795), and both CodeQL Analysis contexts (build.yml:156). Only Version Consistency does real work, and only its consistency half. Meanwhile Operator Docs (test.yml:118), the one job that actually examines documentation, is NOT required.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BITTEN. The repo-tracked hook .claude/hooks/version-advance-guard.sh blocks gh pr create unconditionally, so every PR carries a version bump and therefore never classifies as docs-only. 15 of the last 40 merged PRs (37%) are 'documentation plus a version bump and nothing else' and would classify docs-only without it. The unconditional hook is currently the only thing keeping the hollow-pass path from executing.

SEQUENCING, AND THE REASON THIS IS P1. A parallel branch teaches that hook to consult classify_changed_paths.py and skip on docs-only. That change ACTIVATES this defect on roughly 37% of PR traffic. It is written and deliberately held. This bead must land first.

THE HOLE IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT THEORETICAL. backend/tests/unit/test_check_em_dashes.py:42 reads docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md as a live test fixture. Commit 185a4009 exists because deleting a different .md file broke Backend Tests, and it was caught only because that PR also touched code. Today a .md-only PR would hollow-pass and land the breakage on dev, where it surfaces as a red gate on somebody else's unrelated work.

SCOPE (all of it is no-protection-change, so wedge risk is zero):

1. Run 'mkdocs build --strict' on pull_request. Simplest placement is a step in the existing Operator Docs job, which already runs on every event and is ungated. This absorbs bead pb2s4 (the docs site build never runs on a PR, so a broken link merges green). Note npm run docs:check and mkdocs build --strict check DISJOINT things; pb2s4 documents a broken link that passed the first and failed the second.

2. Extend scripts/classify_changed_paths.py with a second output, docs_site_affected, using the path list docs-pages.yml already carries (docs/user_guide/**, docs/images/user_guide/**, docs/index.md, mkdocs.yml, docs/requirements-docs.txt). Have docs-pages.yml consume it, collapsing a sixth copy of a path list into the one classifier.

3. Add a GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY line to every required job stating what it actually did ('documentation-only: no backend source changed, suite not run' versus 'ran N tests'). Does not change conclusions; makes the rollup readable.

4. Fix the ship consumer. docs/shipping.md step 6 says 'gh pr checks <#> --watch'. That reports check conclusions ONLY and cannot report merge conflicts. Replace with a read of statusCheckRollup per-context conclusion PLUS mergeable and mergeStateStatus. This is worth doing on its own merits regardless of the rest.

DOCS-ONLY DEFINITION REWORK, from the same spike (may be split out if it makes the PR too large):
  - '**.md' is too broad because .md files are live test fixtures. Either carve the fixture paths out, or better, assert in the backend suite that no test reads a repo .md outside a declared allowlist so this cannot silently reappear.
  - '.beads/**' is the wrong granularity. issues.jsonl, issues.jsonl.bak and metadata.json are machine-generated and reasonably inert. config.yaml GOVERNS how bd behaves inside release-cut-gate.yml:257 and is code.
  - Consider renaming the output to code_paths_changed: positive rather than defined-by-opposition, and the fail-open default becomes the natural true.

NOT IN SCOPE: any branch-protection change, any required-context rename, the aggregator job. All of that is Phase 2, deferred. Do not touch .github/workflows in a way that alters which contexts are emitted.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: bead 6u2pa's duplicate-emitter half is ALREADY FIXED (docs-only-pass.yml deleted in abd325bb under bead 5rwzy, with an invariant test at backend/tests/unit/test_classify_changed_paths.py preventing recurrence). What remains of 6u2pa is the different defect described here: the check name lies about what ran. Phase 2 would close that half; Phase 1 does not.

ALSO FOUND, not in scope: docs/shipping.md describes Release Cut Gate as enforcing the release-cut gates, but it is not in main's required contexts. Semgrep Lint, Version Consistency and MCP Server Tests are required on dev but not on main. Doc and reality have drifted.

title: Unbounded decompression and unbounded RAM read on the anonymous restore surface
description:
Found during the security review of branch fix/lf29s-restore-initial-auth-gate. CWE-409, OWASP A05.

Two sites:
  backend/routers/backup.py:1924 — db_header = zf.read('journal.db')[:16] materialises the ENTIRE decompressed member into memory in order to slice 16 bytes off the front.
  backend/routers/backup.py:2331 — content = await file.read() with no cap.

MEASURED by the reviewer: a 261,180-byte ZIP expands to a 268,435,456-byte journal.db member, a ratio of 1028 to 1, and peak RSS grew from 525 MiB to 613 MiB inside _validate_backup_zip alone. A roughly 2 MB upload therefore yields roughly 2 GB of resident memory.

The correct pattern already exists in the same file and is used by the DBAS path: _stream_upload_to_temp (:449, :2427) with _RESTORE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 2 GiB. These two sites simply do not use it.

Mitigating: both sites sit AFTER _guard_initial_restore, so post-lf29s they are reachable only in the states the endpoint is designed to serve open — a genuine first run, a DR rebuild waiting for its restore, or an instance deliberately running require_auth off. The disk-spool half is reachable pre-guard in the qg14z window but is bounded by request lifetime.

Related accuracy note for whoever picks this up: the lf29s commit message claims removing the path from AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS turns anonymous uploads away 'before FastAPI spools an attacker-controlled ZIP to disk'. That is overstated. Starlette 0.50.0 applies max_part_size (1 MB) only to non-file parts; file parts go to a SpooledTemporaryFile and then to disk unbounded, and the multipart body is consumed during dependency resolution, i.e. before the handler. The benefit is real on healed instances and absent in the qg14z window. Soften the comment at backend/main.py:511-533 and the matching CHANGELOG sentence while fixing this.

FIX: reuse _stream_upload_to_temp and _RESTORE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES; check ZipInfo.file_size before calling zf.read. Effort: Low.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy initial/authenticated restore streams uploads through a hard cap; ZIP entry count, declared total expansion, compression ratio, and per-member size are rejected before decompression/read; large and high-ratio adversarial archives keep memory bounded and return a clear 4xx; valid first-run and DR restores still pass end-to-end.
notes: Implementation pushed in PR #880 at commit 0b5cdfdb, build 0.18.1-0117. Both legacy restore endpoints now use bounded streaming temp-file ingestion; legacy ZIP validation applies the shared entry/expansion/ratio guard before reads and reads only 16 bytes from journal.db. Red-first regression evidence: 4 new tests failed on the unfixed tree and pass after the fix. Verification: 110 focused restore/auth/ZIP-bomb tests passed; full backend suite completed at 79.00% coverage with no failures recorded; frontend production build, version consistency, docs checks, mkdocs strict, em-dash ratchet, py_compile, and diff check passed. PR remains open pending CI and independent review; do not close until merged.
close_reason: Merged in PR #880 (merge commit 4c5eb53c). Team review approved after cancellation cleanup and legacy-backup compatibility fixes; all GitHub checks passed on head cd61d899.

title: [epic] Authentication posture rests on one boolean pair, one code path fails to set it, and the exempt surface is unpinned
description:
Unifying statement for the auth findings surfaced 2026-08-10 by a security trace that started from a frontend fail-open report and found worse things underneath it.

The backend's 'auth disabled means fully permissive' short-circuit is a DELIBERATE and CONSISTENTLY applied design, not sloppiness. The identical guard appears at backend/auth/dependencies.py:281, :320, :391, backend/routers/settings.py:160, backend/routers/stats.py:57 and backend/main.py:540. The problem is not that it is scattered; it is that it makes one boolean pair (require_auth AND setup_complete) the ENTIRE security posture, with a single point of failure and no test pinning the surface around it.

Verified good and NOT in scope, credit where due: the global middleware added 2026-03-17 in commit 1f7f8618 is a sound secure-by-default design that closed jy006's reported class of bug four months before jy006 was filed. No path-normalization bypass exists. Zip-slip is properly defended. Constant-time comparison is used on the static MCP key at both middleware and dependency layers. uvloop is pinned away from with the response-cross-contamination CVE cited inline.

Live instance ecm-ecm-1 verified ENFORCING: unauthenticated GET returns 401 on /api/settings, /api/channels, /api/streams and /api/journal. Nothing here is exploitable on the running instance as configured. The exposure is fresh and rebuilt instances, which is a state this project enters deliberately during backup and restore drills.

Standup signal: YELLOW, not RED.

Children: the setup_complete defect (root cause), restore-initial (unauthenticated DB replacement), cleartext Discord and Telegram secrets on read, and pinning AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS.

i4qrp stays OUTSIDE this epic: verified still accurate, but POST /api/settings/test IS covered by the global middleware, so it needs a token. It is a different problem with a different fix and is correctly scoped already.

The frontend tri-state bead also sits outside this epic: it is a UX and recoverability defect, not a security finding, once backend enforcement is confirmed holding.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Drop the setup_complete clause from the title and body, that half is dead (bead qg14z persists the gate at auth/routes.py:551-570, and bead lf29s removed the restore-initial exemption). Surviving scope: the auth posture is still one boolean pair, repeated at auth/dependencies.py:281, :320, :391, routers/settings.py:160, routers/stats.py:57 and main.py:555; the exempt surface is still unpinned (bead ne2yy); and the require_auth:false blast radius is undecided (bead jy006).
close_reason:
19/19 children complete. The final eight shipped together in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5, build 0.18.1-0104): jy006, ne2yy, 9kwzp.9, 9kwzp.5, p388h, mkocf, suuoh, 2owpi.

The epic's unifying claim was that ECM's authentication posture rested on one boolean pair (require_auth AND setup_complete) with a single point of failure and no test pinning the surface around it. Both halves are now addressed. The exempt surface is pinned by a snapshot test whose failure message is the reviewer's checklist. The boolean pair no longer decides everything: three identity primitives (restore-initial, the mcp_api_key lifecycle, and the ten TLS certificate/key-material and HTTPS-lifecycle routes) enforce an authenticated human admin even when require_auth is false, on any instance that already holds an operator identity, with a documented no-identity carve-out so a fresh or headless install is never bricked.

Verified three independent ways rather than one: full backend and frontend suites (9843 backend, 2825 frontend, all green), two Codex review rounds (three findings in round one, all fixed; no findings in round two), and a live eight-state by thirteen-operation matrix on a disposable container that was torn down, with the PO's live instance never modified.

Two credential-disclosure paths were found by auditing rather than hypothesised, and both are closed: a Cloudflare exception whose str() carried the whole bearer token into logs and into a persisted, API-served last_renewal_error; and the 422 validation-error handler, which logged raw request bodies and echoed them to callers. The second escalated during review: what the first fix covered for two path prefixes turned out to affect sixteen credential-bearing write routes, so the prefix allowlist was deleted and every request body on every path is now redacted, which makes the failure mode for a route added tomorrow 'redacted' rather than 'leaked'.

One finding is deliberately NOT resolved here and needs the PO: enhancedchannelmanager-upkp1 (P1), refresh-token rotation strands a client that never receives the rotated token. That is the real mechanism behind suuoh, whose own headline was disproven. It is a security-posture choice between widening the grace window and switching to rotation confirmation, and the PO asked explicitly not to have that decided unattended. QA reproduced it in about 15 seconds and the options are written up in the bead.

Thirteen follow-on beads filed from this work: upkp1, 2u4e0, xztoc, 8bqv3, 67onh, sa99p, w9vv0, boltm, xzqvb, d85p2, 9hdfr, yhk3r, 1x3yu, c7wv8. Corroborating evidence added to nkwh0.1.

title: POST /api/auth/setup never persists setup_complete, leaving a fresh install anonymous-open
description:
Verified at source. This is the real root cause behind pzref and jy006.

initial_setup() (backend/auth/routes.py:458-515) creates the admin user and UserIdentity, commits, and returns. It never sets setup_complete and never issues tokens. 'grep -n setup_complete backend/auth/routes.py' shows the flag only in the response model (line 259) and in an accidental repair inside the status endpoint (lines 419-429), never in the setup handler.

Archaeology: mark_setup_complete() shipped 2026-02-03 in commit 2b9e6750 and was never called by the setup route. It was deleted as dead code on 2026-03-29 in commit a9385dd8 ('Tech debt cleanup'). The cleanup removed the helper instead of wiring it up.

Client half: SetupPage.tsx:63-64 calls completeSetup() then onSetupComplete(), and ProtectedRoute.tsx:66-71 does setSetupRequired(false) and refreshUser() without re-fetching auth status. authStatus keeps its pre-setup value, so useAuthRequired() stays false and the shell renders with no login prompt.

Server side agrees: setup_complete is still false on disk, so the gate at backend/main.py:540 ('if auth_settings.require_auth and auth_settings.setup_complete') is skipped, and every require_admin_if_enabled returns None. Fully anonymous read AND write until the next full page load triggers the status-endpoint auto-repair. For an API-driven or headless install that page load may never happen.

This reproduces pzref's measured POST /api/channels 200, DELETE /api/channels/1 200, POST /api/settings 200, and jy006's four 200s.

CORRECTION TO pzref: its premise that auth is off by default is WRONG. require_auth has defaulted to True since the auth module was created (git show 2b9e6750:backend/auth/settings.py:141), and load_auth_settings() writes require_auth true on a fresh install. The proposed 'flip the default plus migration' plan is unnecessary work carrying real lockout risk and should be dropped.

FIX: call save_auth_settings with setup_complete=True inside initial_setup() before returning, and have the frontend re-fetch auth status on setup completion. No migration, no default flip, no lockout: every install that has served one page load already has setup_complete true, and installs deliberately running require_auth false are untouched.

ACCEPTANCE: fresh disposable stack, complete the wizard via POST /api/auth/setup only with no page reload, then an unauthenticated GET /api/settings must return 401.

NOT YET REPRODUCED on a live disposable stack. Code, git archaeology and live config inspection only.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SECURITY REVIEW ADDENDUM (2026-08-10) — the blast radius is wider than this bead's description states, and one route was named by nobody.

The description frames the exposure via write routes. The reviewer enumerated the full router and found that EVERY admin-gated route in the application is anonymous in this window, because require_admin_if_enabled and require_auth_if_enabled both short-circuit on 'not setup_complete' and auth_middleware skips entirely when either flag is false.

That includes POST /api/backup/restore-saved, POST /api/backup/restore-dbas, POST /api/backup/restore-yaml and POST /api/settings — and critically:

  GET /api/backup/create

which hands an ANONYMOUS caller a full journal.db containing every admin password hash. That is an exfiltration route, not merely a write route, and it appears in no bead. An attacker does not need to alter anything; they can simply download the credential store.

SCOPE CORRECTION on the window's duration: GET /api/auth/status (backend/auth/routes.py:419-429) self-heals AND PERSISTS setup_complete=True whenever user rows exist, and the SPA calls it on every mount (frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.tsx:86). So for any instance whose UI has loaded after setup, the window is seconds, not indefinite. It remains indefinite only for an API-driven or headless install that never receives a page load — which is exactly the disaster-recovery rebuild path.

RELATED CORRECTION, recorded so this bead is not over-credited: the unauthenticated takeover demonstrated on 2026-08-10 did NOT depend on this window. Anonymous GET /api/settings was answering 401 during that exploit, which means setup_complete was already true. That takeover worked purely because /api/backup/restore-initial sat in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS, and it is fixed by bead lf29s. Do not close lf29s, jy006 or 9ej7f as 'handled by' this bead, and do not close this bead as 'handled by lf29s' — lf29s hardens one of three _restore_from_zip entry points against a weakness the other two still carry.

The security reviewer rates this the highest-priority remaining item in the epic.

title: POST /api/backup/restore-initial is unauthenticated and gated on Dispatcharr config, not auth state
description:
Verified at source. backend/main.py:514 lists /api/backup/restore-initial in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS, so the global auth middleware never gates it. backend/routers/backup.py:2197 declares 'async def restore_backup_initial(file: UploadFile = File(...))' with no auth dependency of any kind. Its only guard is backend/routers/backup.py:2203 'if settings.is_configured(): raise 403', and is_configured() (backend/config.py:533-548) means a Dispatcharr URL and credentials are present. That is a Dispatcharr configuration check standing in for an authentication check.

_restore_from_zip (backend/routers/backup.py:2073-2133) overwrites /config/settings.json and /config/journal.db and clears and rewrites uploads/logos, tls and m3u_uploads. journal.db is the application database (backend/database.py:24) and the users table lives in it (backend/models.py:1751-1756). An unauthenticated caller who can reach the port on an instance where Dispatcharr is not configured can therefore replace the user table including admin password hashes, plus the TLS directory, then log in with credentials of their own choosing.

Exposed state is a fresh container or a disaster-recovery rebuild sitting empty waiting for its restore, which is a state this project enters deliberately during backup and restore drills. Zip-slip is already properly defended (_validate_backup_zip, backup.py:1919-1928) and is not the issue.

COUPLING: do not gate on setup_complete alone. POST /api/auth/setup never persists setup_complete (separate defect), so on the affected instances setup_complete is still false after an admin exists. Gate on whether any user row exists, optionally OR setup_complete, keeping is_configured() as an independent third refusal condition.

Verified live on ecm-ecm-1 that healthy configured instances return 403 from this endpoint, so production as configured is not exposed.

title: MCP contract sets omit allow_manual_channel_merge, so the documented workaround is unreachable via the sidecar
description:
Reported as a secondary finding in GitHub issue #801 by @ruckusvol.

The documented workaround for the auto_created churn bug -- setting
`allow_manual_channel_merge: true` on the rule -- cannot be applied through the
MCP sidecar at all.

- `mcp-server/tools/channel_pipeline.py` accepts the parameter and forwards it
  into the payload (lines ~744, ~940-941, ~1088, ~1128).
- `mcp-server/_endpoint_contracts.py` omits `allow_manual_channel_merge` from
  `_AC_RULE_CREATE_FIELDS` / `_AC_RULE_UPDATE_FIELDS` -- verified: the file has
  zero occurrences of the field name.
- So `call_endpoint('ac_update_rule')` rejects it client-side, before the
  request ever leaves:

  ```
  body key(s) ['allow_manual_channel_merge'] not in this endpoint's request_fields [...]
  ```

The backend PUT accepts the field fine
(backend/routers/channel_pipeline.py:152, 327-328).

Adding the field to both contract sets unblocks the workaround while the root
cause is open. While in there, audit the two field sets against the backend
`RuleCreate` / `RuleUpdate` models for any other silently-unreachable fields --
this is a whole class of bug, not a single missing entry. Related:
enhancedchannelmanager-nv9mw (DBAS backup fixture also omits
`allow_manual_channel_merge`).

title: create_channel if_exists=merge/skip never matches the rule's own channels across runs: full delete/recreate churn every run
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #801 by @ruckusvol against ECM v0.18.0 / Dispatcharr 0.28.2.

## Symptom

`create_channel` with `if_exists: merge` (or `skip`) never matches channels the
same rule created on a PREVIOUS run. Every pipeline run creates a full new set
of channels and the orphan pass deletes the prior run's set. Result: permanent
delete/recreate churn -- every channel ID is replaced on every run, and on
every M3U refresh when `run_on_refresh` is set. Cross-provider stream merging
via `if_exists: merge` is impossible across runs.

## Root cause (reporter-traced, spot-verified in source)

1. `_execute_create_channel` stamps the marker only on the in-memory dict:
   `new_channel["auto_created"] = True`
   (backend/channel_pipeline_executor.py:1396). The create payload sent to
   Dispatcharr (~1361-1366: name, channel_number, channel_group_id, streams)
   has no such key, and Dispatcharr neither persists nor echoes it.
2. The next run rebuilds the channel index fresh from Dispatcharr
   (channel_pipeline_engine.py::_load_existing_data, ~1154-1178), so every
   ECM-created channel comes back with no `auto_created`.
3. `_is_manual_channel` (channel_pipeline_executor.py:5123) is
   `not channel.get("auto_created", False)` -- a missing key reads as MANUAL.
   The `block_manual` gate in `_find_channel_by_name`'s `_in_scope`
   (~5172, ~5201-5215) then rejects the exact-name candidate, since the rule
   default is `allow_manual_channel_merge=False`.
4. `_execute_create_channel` falls through to "not found" and creates a
   duplicate; the orphan pass (keyed by `managed_channel_ids`,
   channel_pipeline_engine.py ~5185-5201) deletes the previous run's channels.

The manual-channel protection therefore cannot distinguish a genuinely
hand-built channel from one this same rule created earlier, because the marker
it depends on is never persisted anywhere.

The codebase already concedes this for one internal path: the event_sync
promotion flow sets `allow_manual_channel_merge=True` precisely because "a
previously-promoted channel reads as 'manual' on later runs (Dispatcharr does
not persist ECM's in-run auto_created marker)"
(channel_pipeline_executor.py ~4720-4727). Ordinary pipeline rules get no
equivalent treatment.

## Reproduction

1. Any rule with `create_channel` (`if_exists: merge` or `skip`),
   `orphan_action: delete`, a `target_group_id`, matching N streams.
2. Run the pipeline twice with unchanged streams.
3. Observed: both runs report "Channels created: N, Stream merges: 0"; all
   channel IDs replaced. Expected: run 2 merges/skips against run 1's
   channels, IDs stable.

## Suggested fix (from reporter)

At lookup time / in `_is_manual_channel`, treat a candidate whose ID is in the
firing rule's persisted `managed_channel_ids` ledger as auto-created,
regardless of the never-persisted `auto_created` key. The ledger already
exists and survives across runs, so no schema change is needed.

Needs a design decision on whether the ledger is authoritative enough to
override the manual-channel guard, or whether the marker should instead be
persisted ECM-side (e.g. a local channel-provenance table). Confirm the
interaction with the event_sync promotion path so its `allow_manual_channel_merge=True`
workaround can be reassessed.
acceptance_criteria: Running a create_channel rule (if_exists: merge or skip, orphan_action: delete) twice against unchanged streams reports 0 channels created and N merges/skips on run 2, with all channel IDs unchanged from run 1. A genuinely hand-built channel with a colliding name is still protected (not merged into) when allow_manual_channel_merge is false. Regression test covers both cases across a simulated two-run boundary where the in-memory auto_created marker is dropped. The event_sync promotion path's allow_manual_channel_merge=True workaround is re-evaluated and either kept with a justifying comment or removed.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
BACKLOG VALIDITY AUDIT (bead enhancedchannelmanager-bewu9), 2026-08-12. Verdict: VALID, still P1. Every link in the original chain reproduces at HEAD eecd257a.

IMPORTANT, THE SCOPE HAS GROWN. Commit fc8ef767 ('fix(pipeline): carry normalized merge identity', bead ukgj9, PR #848) does NOT fix this bead, and it INHERITS the same defect rather than avoiding it.

That commit's behavioural diff is confined to ActionExecutor.execute's merge_streams branch (channel_pipeline_executor.py:1893-1950). It does not touch _execute_create_channel, _is_manual_channel, _load_existing_data, the create payload, or managed_channel_ids.

The new helper it introduces, _find_unique_channel_by_exact_identity, filters candidates with 'if block_manual and self._is_manual_channel(candidate): continue' (channel_pipeline_executor.py:5166-5169), called with block_manual=not allow_manual_channel_merge (:1948). That is the same never-persisted auto_created marker, read the same way. On run 2 of a normalize-then-merge pipeline, every channel run 1 created returns from Dispatcharr without the marker, _is_manual_channel returns True, all candidates filter out, and the stream skips.

The GH #845 tests do not catch this because they hardcode auto_created: True into their fixtures (test_channel_pipeline_executor.py, TestNormalizeThenMergeIdentity), simulating a within-run world that never crosses the run boundary where the marker is dropped. That is exactly the two-run boundary this bead's acceptance criteria require and that no test in the repo currently exercises.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: there are now TWO call sites to satisfy, not one, _find_unique_channel_by_exact_identity alongside _execute_create_channel's _find_channel_by_name. This strengthens this bead's own alternative framing: make provenance authoritative at the _is_manual_channel boundary (ledger-backed or an ECM-side provenance table) rather than patching each lookup. It also argues for re-examining the allow_manual_channel_merge=True workaround at :4827, which a correct provenance source would make unnecessary.

Supporting evidence that the root cause is conceded in-tree: channel_pipeline_executor.py:4722-4726 states 'a previously-promoted channel reads as manual on later runs (Dispatcharr does not persist ECM's in-run auto_created marker)'.

PO has asked for this to be re-examined before anyone picks it up.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
GH #801 EVIDENCE (added 2026-08-12). Read the upstream thread carefully before starting: the reporter filed this diagnosis, WITHDREW it an hour later after further testing, then RE-CONFIRMED it 40 minutes after that with a clean repro. Reading only the middle comment would wrongly suggest this bead is invalid. The settled position is that GH #801 contains TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, both real, and fixing either does not fix the other:

(a) Merge-lookup scope pinned to a group the rule never creates channels in. Now tracked separately as bead enhancedchannelmanager-rtst2.1.

(b) THIS BEAD, the never-persisted auto_created marker. Re-proved on a fresh rule with scope pinned CORRECTLY, create_channel if_exists=merge, orphan_action=delete, allow_manual_channel_merge at default False.

DIRECT API-LEVEL EVIDENCE for (b), stronger than the static trace this bead was filed on:
- Within a single run, merging works perfectly: 47 matched streams produced 27 channels created plus 20 merges, because the in-memory auto_created=True annotation is visible to the same run's lookups.
- An immediate second run again reported 27 created / 20 merges, with every channel ID replaced and the old set orphan-deleted.
- Fetching one of the just-created channels through the Dispatcharr API returns auto_created: False. The marker is provably never stored.

That within-run versus across-run split independently corroborates the audit finding that the GH #845 tests cannot catch this: they hardcode auto_created: True into their fixtures (TestNormalizeThenMergeIdentity), so they simulate a within-run world and never cross the boundary where the marker is dropped.

CONVERGENT FIX. The reporter's suggested fix and this audit's independent conclusion agree: treat a lookup candidate whose ID is in the firing rule's persisted managed_channel_ids ledger as auto-created regardless of the marker. The ledger already exists and survives runs. Note it is currently read ONLY by the orphan pass (channel_pipeline_engine.py:2546, :5186) and never consulted for provenance.

Environment: ECM v0.18.0, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, Docker on Debian 13. Reporter has offered to test a fix.

comments.text:
PO DECISION 2026-08-12: the allow_manual_channel_merge=True workaround at backend/channel_pipeline_executor.py:4827 (event_sync promotion path) is to be REMOVED as part of this fix, not retired separately.

Rationale: the workaround exists only because the auto_created marker was never persisted, as the comment at :4722-4726 states directly. Once the managed_channel_ids ledger makes provenance authoritative at the _is_manual_channel boundary, the special case treats a symptom that no longer exists, and leaving it would keep a second, weaker provenance path alive alongside the real one.

Conditions on the removal: (1) the event_sync promotion path must be covered by a test proving it still merges into a previously-promoted channel across a run boundary with the workaround gone, using the same drop-the-marker-on-reload shape as the main two-run test; (2) if removal provably breaks event_sync promotion, leave the workaround in place and report exactly what the ledger does not cover, rather than forcing the removal or widening the ledger untestably.

title: A channel left bound to a placeholder stream reports success on every LATER restore/sync cycle, because the rebind pass only ever inspects placeholders it created this run
description:
Found during backup/restore drill run 3 follow-up. Raised by the project-engineer during daziw analysis; the code chain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED by the orchestrator.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM daziw
enhancedchannelmanager-daziw makes a restore report completed_with_failures when it leaves a channel with no playable stream. That fix computes its signal INSIDE rebind_placeholder_streams -- which early-returns before computing anything when this run synthesized no placeholders. So daziw closes the first-cycle hole and NOT this one. A channel already stuck on a placeholder from an earlier cycle still reports success forever.

THE CHAIN (each link verified in source on dev @ v0.18.1-0026)

1. backend/dbas/placeholder_rebind.py:
       placeholder_ids = _ledgered_ids(ledger, EntityType.STREAM)
       if not placeholder_ids:
           return result
   The pass only ever considers placeholders THIS run ledgered. A placeholder created by a previous run is invisible to it.

2. backend/dbas/importers/channels.py:_fetch_candidate_streams -- paginates get_streams and returns 'the full candidate universe'. It applies NO url filter. Contrast backend/dbas/placeholder_rebind.py:271, where the rebind DOES filter: '... not in placeholder_ids and s.get("url")'. So the importer will happily match a URL-less placeholder; the rebind never would.

3. backend/dbas/importers/channels.py:651 -- match_stream(archived_stream, candidates, ...) is called with that unfiltered list. A hit is recorded as 'Matched an EXISTING destination stream: attached, not created -- so it is an updated STREAM, never ledgered (nothing to roll back).'

CONSEQUENCE
Cycle 1 (fresh target, or a sync where ADR-013 S9 suppresses the deferred auto-sync so B has no provider streams yet): archived streams MISS, placeholders are synthesized and ledgered, channel binds to a placeholder.
Cycle 2+: the archived stream Tier-3 matches (EXACT_NORMALIZED_NAME, any provider) the placeholder left behind by cycle 1 -- same name, and nothing filters it out. tier != MISS, so it is 'updated', NOT ledgered. EntityType.STREAM ledger is therefore empty, rebind_placeholder_streams early-returns, channels_needing_stream_reattach stays 0, and the run reports SUCCESS.

The channel still cannot play. This is the exact 'success while unplayable' failure daziw exists to kill, one cycle later and permanently.

Cross-instance sync is the worst exposure because it runs on a schedule: the first apply against a fresh B strands every channel on a placeholder, and every subsequent cycle then reports clean success forever.

POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS (not prescribing)
- Have the rebind pass consider ALL URL-less streams bound to restored channels, not only the ones this run ledgered. Needs care: it must still never touch a stream the operator created deliberately, which is exactly why the ledger restriction exists. The synthetic 'ECM Custom Streams (DBAS restore)' account may be the safe discriminator -- membership of that account, rather than the ledger, identifies 'a placeholder ECM made'.
- Or exclude URL-less streams from the importer's candidate list so a placeholder can never be re-matched, forcing a fresh synthesize + ledger each cycle. Cheaper, but churns stream rows every cycle and may have knock-on effects on the STREAM category counts.
- Or compute the unplayability signal outside the rebind pass entirely (e.g. a final post-apply sweep over restored channels), which would make daziw's aggregate correct in both cycles.

VERIFICATION
Live: restore onto a fresh target so a channel strands on a placeholder, then run the SAME restore again without fixing anything, and assert the second run does NOT report success. Currently it does.
close_reason:
FIXED and PROVEN END-TO-END. Shipped in PR #781, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0029.

CAUSE: the playability verdict in placeholder_rebind.py was nested inside 'did THIS run's placeholder survive?' — the per-channel loop skipped any slot whose id was not in placeholder_ids (this run's RollbackLedger), so a channel stranded by an EARLIER restore had every slot skipped, held_placeholders stayed empty, and the verdict never ran for it. There was also an early 'if not placeholder_ids: return result' that abandoned the pass entirely on a restore that synthesized nothing — precisely the repeat-restore case.

FIX: the verdict is now taken for EVERY restored channel, from what it is actually left holding (final_ids) against candidate_ids (the real URL-bearing destination streams). Who created a bad slot is irrelevant to whether the channel plays. Bad slots are named from the destination's own stream list so a prior run's placeholder is reported by its real name rather than '<unknown>'. The early return is gone. Rebinding and DELETION remain strictly ledger-scoped — nothing this run did not create is ever rebound or deleted; only the AUDIT widened.

PROVEN END-TO-END (run 6, 2026-08-06-run6-oebpv, disposable drill stack) — full detail in the bead comment above. Summary:

A channel was bound to a custom stream that exists ONLY on the source, so the destination can never recreate it and the channel stays stranded across restores. Then an A/B with ONLY placeholder_rebind.py swapped (ixdaw fix present in BOTH arms, marker-verified at each swap):

                                    ARM A (unfixed)   ARM B (fixed)
  outcome                           success           completed_with_failures
  channels_needing_stream_reattach  0                 1
  channels_with_no_playable_stream  0                 1
  stream_reattach_details           []                names the channel, has_playable_stream: false
  notes[]                           []                names it
  notification                      success           warning — 'Task Completed with Warnings'
  ACTUAL CHANNEL                    HTTP 500          HTTP 500

The instance was byte-for-byte identical in both arms and the channel was dead in both. ONLY THE REPORTING DIFFERED. That is the defect and its fix, demonstrated rather than inferred.

NO OVER-TRIGGER: the control channel plays, appears in neither arm's stream_reattach_details, and is not counted — bead daziw's requirement that a still-playing channel must not trigger is intact. Verified again in run 5: a healthy instance reports 0/0 with no detail rows and no notes.

GATES (re-run independently by the orchestrator): 8472 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failures. The 3 new rebind tests were independently red-proofed — reverting the fix in isolation turns them red, and the restored file was verified byte-identical to the fixed version.

CAVEAT: runs 5 and 6 patched the fixed modules into the drill container, so the live evidence describes code that was not yet published as :dev at measurement time. It is now merged to dev.

RELATED: the root cause that MADE channels strand in the first place was bead ixdaw (case-differing stream names colliding onto one destination id, then failing Dispatcharr's unique_channel_stream constraint). That is fixed in the same PR, so the stranding this bead reports on is now much harder to reach in practice — but the reporting blindness was a real, separate defect and is fixed on its own merits.

survives in the instance, unbound. The archived uppercase stream id 102 exists WITH A URL and is

     channels_needing_stream_reattach = 0
     channels_with_no_playable_stream = 0

The instance is byte-for-byte the same in both arms and the channel is dead in both. ONLY THE REPORTING DIFFERS. Arm A tells the operator everything is fine while a channel cannot play; Arm B names it, counts it in both counters, downgrades outcome, and alerts as a warning.

NO OVER-TRIGGER: 'Control Channel' plays and appears in NEITHER arm's stream_reattach_details and is not counted, so bead daziw's requirement (a channel that still plays must not trigger) is intact.

Fix shipped in PR #781 (merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0029).

title: DBAS restore reports outcome=success while leaving channels unplayable; an unplayable channel must downgrade to completed_with_failures
description:
PO decision, 2026-08-05: 'Completed with failures. It is a failure if it isn't playable post-restore.'

This is the headline/severity half that bead enhancedchannelmanager-ixdaw deliberately left out of scope. ixdaw fixed one CAUSE of an unplayable channel (v0.18.1-0026); this bead is about what the restore CALLS the result.

OBSERVED (drill run 2026-08-05-run3, ECM 0.18.1-0024 / Dispatcharr 0.28.2)
A restore finished with:
    outcome: success
    failed: 0
    channels_needing_stream_reattach: 1
    stream_reattach_details: [{channel_id: 12, name: 'Drill KERA Dallas', placeholder_streams: [...]}]
    notes: ['1 channel(s) are still bound to a placeholder stream and will not play; ... Attach a real stream to each named channel.']
That channel returned HTTP 500 with 0 bytes on /proxy/ts/stream/<uuid>, verified by fetching, not inferred. The restore reported success for an instance that could not play a channel it had just restored.

Same shape on the redacted path at step 1: outcome=success with channels_needing_stream_reattach = 12 -- every channel unplayable, reported as success.

WHY THIS IS ALREADY A CONTRACT VIOLATION
dbas/restore_contracts.py::RestoreOutcome documents, verbatim:
    'The contract is: NEVER report SUCCESS on mixed state. If any entity failed,
     the outcome is one of the non-success states -- the UX never labels those success.'
A restored channel that cannot play is mixed state by any reasonable reading. The code does not currently honour its own stated contract for this case, because the placeholder-rebind pass is a post-create best-effort step whose shortfall is recorded in report fields rather than as a category failure.

WANTED
In dbas/restore_orchestrator.py (the outcome decision around the RestoreOutcome.SUCCESS return, ~line 535), a non-dry-run apply that finishes with report.channels_needing_stream_reattach > 0 must return COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES, not SUCCESS. The applied state is real and kept -- COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES already means exactly that ('ran to completion and NOTHING was rolled back') -- so no rollback behaviour changes. Only the label and what follows from it.

Dry runs must be unaffected: a preview predicting a reattach shortfall is a prediction, not a failure.

BLAST RADIUS -- must be assessed before implementing, this is not a one-line change
Callers treat SUCCESS as 'it worked':
  - tasks/dbas_restore.py:470       return report.outcome == RestoreOutcome.SUCCESS
  - tasks/dbas_sync.py:542          succeeded = is_dry_run or report.outcome == RestoreOutcome.SUCCESS
  - tasks/dbas_sync_engine.py:985   and result.outcome == RestoreOutcome.SUCCESS
  - tasks/dbas_sync_engine.py:1005  if result.outcome == RestoreOutcome.SUCCESS
CROSS-INSTANCE SYNC RUNS ON THE SAME ENGINE. A sync that leaves a channel needing reattach would start reporting failure where it previously reported success, and the task-alert layer fires type=error rather than type=success -- so operators with alerts configured will get new emails/Discord/Telegram on runs that previously looked clean. That may be correct and desirable, but it is a behaviour change operators will notice and it needs a CHANGELOG call-out. Decide deliberately whether the sync path should share the downgrade or keep its own definition.

VERIFICATION
Unit: a report with channels_needing_stream_reattach > 0 and zero category failures resolves to COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES on apply, and to the unchanged outcome on dry run.
Live: next drill run -- seed the ixdaw trigger, restore, and assert the reported outcome is completed_with_failures rather than success.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run3/REPORT.md, notes/apply-round1-encrypted.json, notes/apply-round2-standard-step1.json
notes:
MERGED to dev in PR #779 (merge bf18e04d, commit cd50527b), v0.18.1-0027. Option B as chosen by the PO, plus PO decision 2 (warning, not 'Task Failed').

WHAT SHIPPED
- placeholder_rebind.py measures genuine unplayability per channel (does it retain ANY URL-bearing stream), from the list the channel is ACTUALLY left holding, so a failed PATCH counts as unplayable. Uses the candidate set the pass already holds; no re-fetch.
- restore_contracts.py: additive optional RestoreReport.channels_with_no_playable_stream and StreamReattachDetail.has_playable_stream (default True), written only via record_stream_reattach_needed. NO CONTRACT_VERSION bump -- verified against the module's own rule at line 54: 'Bump when a field's MEANING changes (not for additive optional fields).' channels_needing_stream_reattach is unchanged in VALUE; only its docstring now describes what it actually counts.
- restore_orchestrator.compute_outcome: non-dry-run apply with channels_with_no_playable_stream > 0 -> COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES. Dry runs unaffected. No rollback behaviour changed.
- tasks/dbas_restore.py: the operator summary's '%d channel(s) have NO playable stream' now renders the NEW aggregate; the placeholder counter gets wording true of it; combined clause when both are non-zero.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED (not taken on the agent's report)
- Red before green: with ALL production files reverted to pre-fix and the new tests kept, the new tests fail. With the fix, 69 passed across the two new files plus the 51 existing ixdaw tests.

NOT CLOSED. Verified at unit level only. Close after a live drill run confirms: seed a channel with no matchable stream, restore, and assert the reported outcome is completed_with_failures with a warning alert -- and that a leftover-placeholder channel still reports success.

STILL OPEN AND DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE

title: Setup wizard never persists setup_complete, so the auth gate is skipped on a fresh install (require_auth already defaults ON)
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-10 (Project Engineer, re-verified at source). The original
diagnosis in this bead was wrong. The proposed fix is dropped. The
measurements below are real and are preserved unchanged.

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION

require_auth has defaulted to True since the auth module's creation, not
False. Verified: `git show 2b9e6750:backend/auth/settings.py:141` shows
`require_auth: bool = True` on the AuthSettings model, and the same field and
default are unchanged in the current backend/auth/settings.py:79.
load_auth_settings() (backend/auth/settings.py:140-188) constructs a fresh
AuthSettings() -- i.e. require_auth: true -- and persists it via
save_auth_settings() on first run when no config file exists yet, then reads
back whatever is on disk on every subsequent load. Live confirmation: the
running instance's /config/auth_settings.json reads "require_auth": true,
with nobody having set it.

So the wizard does not leave authentication off. The proposed fix -- flip
the default to ON and write a migration for existing installs -- targets a
default that is already ON. It would be unnecessary work, and the migration
half of it (silently changing behavior for installs deliberately running
with require_auth: false) carries the exact lockout risk this bead itself
warned about: automation with no credentials would be locked out with no
warning. That plan is retracted. Do not implement it.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

The real defect is that POST /api/auth/setup (initial_setup() in
backend/auth/routes.py) creates the admin user but never sets
setup_complete=True and never persists it. The global auth middleware
(backend/main.py, auth_middleware(), decorated at line 540, gate condition
at line 555: `if auth_settings.require_auth and auth_settings.setup_complete:`)
only enforces auth when BOTH flags are true. With require_auth true but
setup_complete still false on disk, the middleware skips enforcement
entirely for every /api/* path, and every admin-gated dependency
(auth/dependencies.py::require_admin_if_enabled and friends) short-circuits
to anonymous. That -- not an off-by-default require_auth -- is why the
drill's unauthenticated writes below succeeded.

Root cause, full reproduction, and the fix live in
enhancedchannelmanager-qg14z ("POST /api/auth/setup never persists
setup_complete, leaving a fresh install anonymous-open"). That bead traces
the missing setup_complete persistence, the frontend's stale-auth-status
re-fetch gap, and the git archaeology of a helper (mark_setup_complete())
that shipped 2026-02-03 in commit 2b9e6750 and was deleted as unused dead
code on 2026-03-29 (commit a9385dd8) without ever having been wired into the
setup route. Treat qg14z as the actionable fix for this whole symptom; this
bead's WANTED section below is superseded by it.

ORIGINAL MEASUREMENTS (preserved, still accurate)

PO decision, 2026-08-05, made under the incorrect premise above and now
moot: 'That should be the default and users should have to choose to turn it
off.' Observed during backup/restore drill run 3 on a disposable stack.

BUILD: published ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev 0.18.1-0024.

Completing ECM's first-run wizard -- the screen headed 'Welcome to Enhanced
Channel Manager / Create your administrator account to get started', which
ends with a button labelled 'Create Admin Account' -- creates the admin user
but the instance was left answering as anonymous. Measured consequence on a
freshly-set-up instance with an admin account created: unauthenticated write
endpoints succeeded from anywhere that could reach the port. e.g.

  POST /api/channels {"name":"__auth_probe__"}   -> HTTP 200, channel created
  DELETE /api/channels/1                          -> HTTP 200
  POST /api/settings <full blob>                  -> HTTP 200

The entire drill was in fact driven over the unauthenticated API after the
wizard had completed.

WHY IT MATTERED (still true, just re-attributed)

The wizard's own words ('Create your administrator account', 'This account
will have full administrator privileges') read as 'this instance is now
protected'. An operator who completes it has no signal that the API is still
open in this window. ECM holds provider credentials and drives Dispatcharr,
and this is the state a headless or API-driven install lands in -- including
disaster-recovery rebuilds, which is exactly when nobody is inspecting
settings. The actionable version of this concern is now tracked by qg14z's
acceptance criteria (unauthenticated GET /api/settings must return 401
immediately after POST /api/auth/setup with no page reload).

WANTED -- RETRACTED

The require_auth-default-flip-plus-migration plan described above is
dropped in full: unnecessary (default is already ON) and risky (lockout).
Do not resurrect it without new evidence that require_auth's default has
changed.

NOT YET INVESTIGATED (secondary, carried over unchanged)

Whether require_auth is exposed anywhere in the current Settings UI at all --
it was not found under Settings -> General/Integrations/etc during the
original drill. If it is only settable via API or config file, that's a
separate, smaller UX gap from the one this bead originally described, and is
not blocking on qg14z.

title: Standard (redacted) DBAS backup leaves the XC/M3U username in cleartext while redacting the password
description:
PO decision, 2026-08-05: the standard backup should be FULLY redacted. Found in backup/restore round-trip drill run 3 on a disposable stack, not production.

BUILD: published ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev 0.18.1-0024 (sha256:8a7d301d21829010fb32d8b3a424b1fc1dd7ef980db19ddc14087f7e0f2728f2), Dispatcharr 0.28.2.

OBSERVED
Unzipping a STANDARD (non-encrypted, default) artifact and reading categories/m3u_accounts.yaml:

    name: Infinity
    server_url: https://infinity.gives
    account_type: XC
    username: mot2                      <-- CLEARTEXT
    password: '***REDACTED***'
      profiles[0].custom_properties.user_info:
        username: mot2                  <-- CLEARTEXT (second copy)
        password: '***REDACTED***'

The password is correctly replaced with the sentinel in both places. The username is not touched in either.

WHY IT MATTERS
For an Xtream Codes provider the username is half of the credential pair, and it is the half that identifies the subscription. ECM renders XC stream URLs as https://host/live/<username>/<password>/<id>.ts, so the username is a real subscription identifier, not an incidental label. A standard backup is the DEFAULT artifact, is the one most operators will hold, and is described in the user guide simply as 'redacted' / 'Sensitive data (passwords, API keys) are redacted' -- which an operator will reasonably read as covering the provider credential as a whole. These artifacts get copied to NAS shares, cloud buckets and support tickets.

Note the upstream contributing factor already recorded in the drill notes: Dispatcharr's apps/m3u/serializers.py declares password write_only and then re-adds it in cleartext in to_representation for user_level >= 10, which ECM always is. ECM's redactor is therefore the ONLY thing keeping provider credentials out of a standard artifact -- so its coverage needs to be complete.

EXPECTED
A standard artifact carries no part of the provider credential. Username should be redacted to the same sentinel (or omitted), in BOTH the account row and profiles[].custom_properties.user_info. Apply to EPG source usernames too, for the same reason the password rule already does.

BEWARE ON THE RESTORE SIDE
The restore currently reports credentials needing re-entry per field. Once the username is redacted, credential_reentry_details for an m3u_account must name the username field as well, and the restore must NOT write the sentinel into the destination username (the password path already correctly writes 'absent' rather than the sentinel -- bead 6pilh). The drill's inventory classifies a credential three ways (absent / sentinel / present+fingerprint) and will catch a sentinel leaking into the destination.

VERIFICATION FOR THE NEXT DRILL RUN
Unzip a standard artifact, grep categories/m3u_accounts.yaml and categories/epg_sources.yaml for the real username; expect no hits. Then restore onto a fresh target and confirm the inventory reports username_state.state == 'absent', not 'sentinel'.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run3/REPORT.md (finding F4), artifact/ecm-backup-2026-08-05_174319.zip
notes:
PO DECISION 2026-08-17: this bead now GATES enhancedchannelmanager-pui76 (the one-click backup control). It must ship first.

The reasoning, which is new since this bead was written: today the ONLY UI path that produces a DBAS artifact is the Encrypted Backup card, which encrypts the whole artifact - so the cleartext XC/M3U username this bead reports is currently sitting inside an encrypted envelope. The scheduled task produces the unencrypted standard artifact, but it ships disabled and this instance has never run it, so no plain artifact exists to leak.

Adding a one-click button would create the first easily-obtainable unencrypted artifact carrying that username. Those are exactly the files operators attach to support tickets, post on forums, and copy between machines. So the passphrase ceremony is currently acting as an accidental brake on this defect, and pui76 would remove it.

Your 2026-08-05 decision that the standard backup should be FULLY redacted is unchanged and unimplemented. This is now on the critical path rather than parallel to it.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #875 (merge f538340b, build 0.18.1-0113). Commits fd3c6606, ff7c05fa, 2299dc1b, d9d81ef7, 9287753e, 685c3ecb, 0b3aeafb, 45eb2bd5.

YOUR 2026-08-05 DECISION IMPLEMENTED: the standard artifact is fully redacted. The bead reported one cleartext username. That was the smallest thing wrong with it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY LEAKING, in the order it was found:
- Three WHOLE bearer credentials - emby_api_key, jellyfin_api_key, plex_token - never redacted at all, because the denylist matched key names EXACTLY and <vendor>_api_key never matched api_key.
- The operator's own ECM admin bcrypt hash, session refresh-token hashes, IP addresses and user agents, because the journal.db scrub only ever visited alert_methods.
- The operator's OIDC/SAML/LDAP identity: user_identities carries provider, external subject and login email.
- EIGHT TABLES NO MODEL DECLARES - remnants of a removed health-monitor subsystem and a deleted rules engine - carrying services.health_endpoint, incidents.created_by and service_alert_history.acknowledged_by. They exist in every live database and shipped in every artifact ever produced.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX, and the reason it matters: the journal.db scrub is now an ALLOWLIST. Fourteen named configuration tables may ship; everything else is dropped, then VACUUMed with secure_delete (byte-scanned to prove DELETE alone leaves values in the page file). A table added to the schema later ships nothing until someone classifies it, and a ratchet fails the build until they do.

The eight orphan tables are the whole argument for inverting. They are not in models.py, and every denylist in this codebase is maintained by reading models.py - so no amount of careful list maintenance could ever have reached them. Three rounds of adding tables to a purge list did not find them; the allowlist found them on its first pass, by construction.

ALSO CLOSED: redaction now fails CLOSED. An unparseable alert_methods.config loses its whole value to the sentinel, and an unreadable database fails the entire backup instead of shipping unscrubbed. Both paths previously shipped the data they could not inspect.

CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: dropping the users table rather than emptying it silently disabled _reassert_auth_rows_after_restore, which would have logged an admin out of their own instance behind a 200. And CodeQL found py/polynomial-redos in the new URL scan - measured at 24.7 seconds on 200k of scheme-legal characters, reachable through ffmpeg_profiles.config and dummy_epg_profiles templates, both unbounded Text columns. Replaced with a linear scan, proven equivalent by a differential fuzz over 1,030,000 random strings after the first attempt at it silently stopped scrubbing a real URL.

VERIFIED BY BUILDING ARTIFACTS, not by reading code: three of the defects were found by producing a ZIP, unzipping it and querying the database. That is how the bead itself was found, and reading the code repeatedly said it was fine.

HONEST LIMITS, documented rather than smoothed: a standard artifact from this code should only be restored by this code or newer - four gaps exist in the other direction, the worst of which can log the restoring admin out. The legacy full .zip is NOT a redacted artifact and never was: it ships tls/ private keys and raw m3u_uploads/ verbatim, and its settings.json still carries settings.username in clear. That path is out of this bead's scope and its UI card already warns operators.

TWO ADVERSARIAL REVIEW ROUNDS, deliberately split by question after a combined review proved too large to complete twice.

title: DBAS restore: a channel whose streams normalize to the same name is left unplayable — the rebind PATCHes a duplicate stream id, Dispatcharr 500s on unique_channel_stream, and the whole channel reverts to placeholders
description:
Found unprimed in backup/restore round-trip drill run 3 (2026-08-05), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack, NOT production.

BUILD: published ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev build 0.18.1-0024, digest sha256:8a7d301d21829010fb32d8b3a424b1fc1dd7ef980db19ddc14087f7e0f2728f2. Dispatcharr pinned ghcr.io/dispatcharr/dispatcharr:0.28.2. No image patching, no workarounds.

REPRODUCED ON BOTH ARTIFACT VARIANTS (encrypted+credentials, and standard redacted). Deterministic.

SYMPTOM
A restore reports outcome=success, failed=0, and 11 of 12 channels play. One channel -- the only one with more than one stream -- is left bound to three URL-less placeholder streams under the synthetic 'ECM Custom Streams (DBAS restore)' account and returns HTTP 500 with 0 bytes on /proxy/ts/stream/<uuid>. Playback verified by fetching real media bytes, not inferred: the other channels return HTTP 200, video/mp2t, 262144 bytes.

The restore DOES name it (channels_needing_stream_reattach=1, stream_reattach_details names the channel and its held placeholders, plus a report note). So it is not silent -- but outcome=success with an unplayable channel is the wrong headline, and the cause is a fixable de-duplication gap.

SEED THAT TRIGGERS IT
One channel with three streams in a deliberate order:
  'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA', 'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA', 'TX | Austin | PBS KLRU'
The first two differ ONLY in the case of Dallas/DALLAS.

ROOT CAUSE -- established from source and logs, not inferred
1. Re-running ECM's own matcher against the live destination returns:
     'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA' -> tier=2 match_id=101
     'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA' -> tier=2 match_id=101   <-- SAME id
     'TX | Austin | PBS KLRU' -> tier=2 match_id=98
   Tier 2 is EXACT NORMALIZED NAME + SAME PROVIDER; the normalizer folds case, so both archived slots claim the same destination stream.
2. dbas/placeholder_rebind.py rewrites each slot in place and PATCHes the whole ordered list, i.e. streams=[101, 101, 98]. There is no guard against two slots resolving to the same destination id.
3. ECM log:
   [DBAS-REBIND] Could not rebind channel 'Drill KERA Dallas' (id=12): Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url http://<dispatcharr>/api/channels/channels/12/
4. Dispatcharr log gives the real reason:
   psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "unique_channel_stream"
   DETAIL: Key (channel_id, stream_id)=(12, 101) already exists.
5. placeholder_rebind's exception handler then reverts the ENTIRE channel to placeholders -- by its own design, since the PATCH is all-or-nothing -- including the KLRU slot that had a perfectly good unique match. Net: 3 placeholders held, channel unplayable.

So the run-1 rebind pass (2o0cz) works; what is missing is a de-dup guard between the matcher and the PATCH.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION
On the redacted path, the step-3 recovery re-run surfaced the same failure as a first-class failed row rather than a best-effort note:
  outcome: completed_with_failures
  stream: created 0, updated 14, failed 1
  failure_details: [{reason: upstream_api_error, label: 'Drill KERA Dallas', message: "Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url .../api/channels/channels/12/"}]

IMPACT
Any channel carrying two streams whose names differ only by case/spacing/punctuation comes back unplayable, and re-running the restore does not clear it (same collision). Multi-stream channels are the normal shape for failover lineups, and providers commonly ship near-duplicate names.

SUGGESTED FIX
In dbas/placeholder_rebind.py, when rewriting the ordered slot list, skip a match whose destination id is already present in the list being built (keep that slot on its placeholder and count it in channels_needing_stream_reattach) so the PATCH can never contain a duplicate. Optionally have match_stream exclude already-claimed candidate ids for the same channel.

EVIDENCE
~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run3/
  inventory/DIFF-encrypted.md, inventory/DIFF-standard.md
  notes/dispatcharr-500-unique-channel-stream.txt (the verbatim traceback)
  notes/apply-round1-encrypted.json, notes/apply-round2-standard-step3.json
  inventory/playback-after-*.json (the fetched playback results)

Operator-facing workaround is now documented in docs/user_guide/backup-restore/troubleshoot-restore.md: reattach that channel's streams by hand.
notes:
FIX MERGED to dev in PR #778 (merge f8298bde, commit fefaafbb), v0.18.1-0026.

Fix is in dbas/placeholder_rebind.py, in the caller that assembles the ordered id list -- NOT in the matcher. rebind_placeholder_streams now tracks claimed_ids for the channel and demotes a colliding match to MatchTier.MISS, so the slot keeps its placeholder and is counted/named through the existing record_stream_reattach_needed path. One ambiguous slot now costs one slot instead of the whole channel. Archived order preserved; best-effort posture preserved; stream_matcher.py unmodified.

REFINEMENT over the fix suggested in this bead's description: claimed_ids is seeded with the REAL streams the importer had already bound, not only ids written during this pass. Those are equally unique-constrained, so a placeholder slot could otherwise still claim an id a non-placeholder slot already held and reproduce the identical 500. Pinned by test 4.

The bead's optional second suggestion -- have match_stream exclude already-claimed candidates -- was deliberately REJECTED: it would make a documented pure function stateful across calls and break its determinism contract.

Tests: 4 new regressions in backend/tests/dbas/test_restore_state_loss.py on the drill's exact seed. Verified RED before the fix by the orchestrator independently, in a throwaway worktree with the pre-fix module restored -- all four failed, the first with the measured production symptom verbatim: 'duplicate stream id in PATCH: [101, 101, 98]'. Green after: 51/51 in that file, full tests/dbas/ suite green, full backend suite 8451 passed / 9 skipped under the project venv.

NOT closing yet. This is verified at unit level only. The confirming evidence is a live re-drill: seed a channel with two case-differing stream names, restore onto a fresh target, and assert the channel binds to real streams and PLAYS (2xx + real media bytes). Close after the next drill run confirms it end-to-end.

STILL OPEN, deliberately out of scope for this fix: the restore reports outcome=success when a channel is left unplayable for other reasons. That headline/severity question needs its own decision.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live. Shipped in PR #781, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0029.

ROOT CAUSE (not the symptom): stream_matcher's exact-name tiers (2 and 3) compared only the CASE-FOLDED name with a lowest-id tie-break, so a destination pair differing only in capitalisation was a single match to them. A channel archived with 'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA' (id 102) and 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA' (id 101) had BOTH slots handed 101, while 102 — a byte-identical name match — sat unused with a working URL. The 0026 claimed_ids guard correctly stopped the duplicate reaching the PATCH, but it was treating the symptom: the matcher was picking the wrong stream in the first place.

FIX: within each exact-name tier, among the candidates that tier's predicate already admits, a candidate whose RAW name is byte-identical to the archived name is preferred; the lowest-id tie-break then runs inside whichever set was selected. When no candidate is a raw-name match the selected set is unchanged, so a run without such a pair is bit-identical to the previous behaviour. Tier integers unchanged. Still pure, no I/O, order-independent. claimed_ids is retained byte-identical as the backstop for a GENUINE identical-name collision, which no pure per-stream matcher can resolve.

VERIFIED LIVE (run 5, 2026-08-05-run5-fixverify, disposable drill stack):
- The channel now restores to [102, 98, 101] — all three real, url=SET, in EXACT archived order. Zero placeholders anywhere in the instance.
- Rebind log: "Channel 'KERA Dallas PBS' (id=12): 3 placeholder(s) rebound" and "14 slot(s) rebound across 12 channel(s); 14 placeholder(s) deleted; 0 channel(s) still hold a slot that cannot play". Run 4 rebound 13 of 14 and left one dead slot.
- PLAYBACK FETCHED: 200, video/mp2t, 262144 bytes — on BOTH artifact variants. On the standard redacted path in run 4 this same channel returned HTTP 500.
- Encrypted round trip produced a ZERO-FINDING inventory diff ('Did the restore reproduce the instance? YES') — the first in this drill's history.
- Standard redacted round trip: zero CHANNEL findings, all 12 channels on real streams, all playing.
- A second restore of the same artifact is now a genuine no-op; run 4's silently dropped a slot and reordered the channel.

REGRESSIONS CHECKED, none: uploaded-logo sha256 identical, 12/12 EPG links, credential fingerprint 0ea118b1 unchanged, enabled groups 1/375, custom stream profile still resolves to DrillAgent4 BY NAME on a target where id 4 is a decoy, profile membership exact, all 4 non-default ECM settings preserved. daziw's warning behaviour unregressed.

GATES (re-run independently by the orchestrator, not taken from the authoring agent): 8472 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failures. The 4 new matcher tests were independently red-proofed — reverting the fix in isolation turns them red, and the restored file was verified byte-identical to the fixed version.

CAVEAT ON THE LIVE EVIDENCE: run 5 patched the fixed modules into the drill container; the result describes code that was not yet published as :dev at measurement time. It is now merged to dev.

      WORKING URL (m3u_account=2) and is simply never bound to the channel.

  returned HTTP 500 on playback with ALL THREE slots still placeholders. It lost EVERY slot,
  not at most the contested one.

  psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation: duplicate key value violates unique constraint
  "unique_channel_stream"
