title: DBAS restore preview mis-predicts the logo category: dry run reports every URL-restorable logo as a failure
description:
Found on the backup/restore round-trip drill (run 2026-08-04-run2), disposable stack, NOT production. ECM 0.18.1-0023, Dispatcharr 0.28.2.

SYMPTOM
The dry-run preview reports ALL 11 archived logos as failures:

  logo  would_create=0 would_update=0 would_skip=0 FAILED=11
  every row: reason=validation_error, message='unsafe or empty logo filename'

The subsequent APPLY of the very same artifact then reports:

  logo  created=10 updated=0 skipped=0 failed=1

So 10 of the 11 predicted failures did not happen. The preview is wrong about the whole category, in the pessimistic direction.

ROOT CAUSE (read from the shipped image's source)
dbas/importers/logos.py, the URL re-create path is gated on NOT being a dry run:

    if not is_dry_run and not hydratable_bytes(archive_logo, content_provider):
        remote_url = _remote_logo_url(archive_logo)
        if remote_url is not None:
            await _create_logo_from_url(...)
            continue

In a dry run that branch is skipped entirely, so every byte-less logo record falls through to _validate_logo(), which requires archive_logo['filename']. The archived logo records are {id, name, url} - there is no 'filename' key at all - so _safe_basename(None) returns None and every record is rejected with 'unsafe or empty logo filename'.

WHY IT MATTERS
The product's own guidance, the runbook, and the restore UI all say 'preview first, always'. An operator who follows that sees 11 of 11 logos failing and would reasonably conclude the artifact is corrupt and abort a restore that would in fact have restored 10 of them correctly.

It also HIDES the one real problem. The single genuinely unrestorable logo (a Dispatcharr-volume-local one) is indistinguishable in the preview from the 10 that are fine - identical reason, identical message. The signal an operator actually needs is buried in noise the preview invented.

SUGGESTED FIX
Let the dry run simulate the URL path: evaluate _remote_logo_url() and count a would_create for records that have a usable absolute http(s) URL, regardless of is_dry_run, and only fall through to the byte-validation path for the rest. The preview would then report 10 would_create + 1 failure, matching the apply.

REPRODUCTION
Seed logos with remote CDN URLs, back up, wipe, roll out fresh, run the restore in Preview mode. Reproduced 1/1. Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-04-run2/notes/preview-postwipe-encrypted-raw.json vs notes/restore-encrypted-raw.json.

RELATED
Sibling of enhancedchannelmanager-d0agi (the apply-side fatal classification). Both stem from the logos category added by the dfkbn fix.
notes:
RUN-3 LIVE EVIDENCE (drill 2026-08-05-run3, published :dev 0.18.1-0024 sha256:8a7d301d..., Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable stack).

The logo CATEGORY counts now match: preview 'logo would_create 12' vs apply 'logo created 12'. Run 2's 'every URL-restorable logo reported as a failure' did NOT reproduce. logo_misses: 0 on every restore this run.

BUT a preview/apply mismatch remains in the same family, on the reattach split counts:

  Round 1 (encrypted artifact onto a GENUINELY FRESH target)
    PREVIEW logo_reattach: {mode: preserve, created_channels: 0,  existing_channels: 0, preserved_channels: 0}
    APPLY   logo_reattach: {mode: preserve, created_channels: 11, existing_channels: 0, preserved_channels: 0}

  epg_link_reattach on the SAME run predicted correctly (preview created_channels: 11, apply 11), so this is specific to the LOGO reattach pass on the created-channels path.

On a POPULATED target (Phase 6b) both passes matched the apply exactly in both modes:
    preserve : preview {created 0, existing 0, preserved 11} == apply
    overwrite: preview {created 0, existing 11, preserved 0} == apply

So the under-prediction appears only when the restore is CREATING the channels. Not re-filed as new; recorded here per the drill's do-not-duplicate rule.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run3/notes/preview-round1-encrypted.json vs notes/apply-round1-encrypted.json
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live. Shipped in PR #784, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0032.

Run 4 measured, fresh target, same artifact, preview then apply back to back:
  logo_reattach.created_channels     preview 0  -> apply 11
  channels_needing_stream_reattach   preview 0  -> apply 12
  channels_with_no_playable_stream   preview 0  -> apply 12
  profile_membership_drift           preview 0  -> apply 6
Per-category would_create matched the apply's created EXACTLY for every category, so the CATEGORY counts were always sound; the HEALTH counters were confident zeroes derived from having looked at nothing.

FIX — three counters, three different honest answers:
 * logo_reattach.created_channels: REAL PREDICTION. A fresh target matches no logo, so every logo is a would-create with no destination id and the importer registers no dry-run remap entry. Added LogoImportResult.would_create_source_ids (SOURCE ids, both create branches, never a fabricated destination id) plus a dry-run-only widening gated on 'is_dry_run and dest_logo_id is None', so a matched logo never reaches it and a preserved channel is decided before any logo resolution.
 * profile_membership_drift: REAL PREDICTION. The flip set is computable from the archive alone and the apply's own count never reads current membership either, so preview and apply run identical arithmetic; only the PATCH is skipped. Exact, not a bound.
 * channels_needing_stream_reattach / channels_with_no_playable_stream: EXPLICITLY NOT PREDICTED. Genuinely unknowable — the pass matches against streams the DEFERRED M3U refresh materializes and a preview refreshes nothing. Both are now int | None, and run_restore calls mark_stream_health_unpredicted() on the dry-run branch. Rather than fake a number, the report says what is true.
 * streams_rebound deliberately left at 0 — literally true on a preview, and a work-done counter rather than an alarm.

BACKWARD COMPATIBLE, verified: every consumer already coerces with 'or 0', including the daziw degraded key (restore_orchestrator.py:517) and tasks/dbas_restore.py (3 sites). NO frontend component renders either counter — only the api.ts type, widened to number | null. mark_stream_health_unpredicted() is a no-op once a detail row exists so it can never erase a real count, and is only reachable from the dry-run branch.

POPULATED-TARGET SPLITS UNCHANGED (the regression that would have hurt most). Three distinct correct shapes remain correct: fresh -> created 12/11; populated+overwrite -> existing 12/11; populated+preserve -> preserved 12/11. Both populated shapes are parametrized over None / set() / {55,56} and pinned exact.

VERIFIED LIVE (run 7, 2026-08-06-run7-verify, disposable drill stack, build 0032 patched in). Fresh target, same artifact, preview then apply:
  logo_reattach.created_channels      11 -> 11   MATCH
  profile_membership_drift             6 ->  6   MATCH
  epg_link_reattach.created_channels   0 ->  0   MATCH
  channels_needing_stream_reattach  null -> 12   not-predicted (honest)
  channels_with_no_playable_stream  null -> 12   not-predicted (honest)

epg_link_reattach reads 0/0 only because run 7's seed carried no EPG source; it is consistent between preview and apply, NOT a regression — checked explicitly rather than assumed.

GATES (re-run independently by the orchestrator): 8504 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failures; frontend 183 files / 2546 tests passed; tsc --noEmit clean. Red-without-fix confirmed per sub-fix.

ALSO SHIPPED IN THE SAME PR (they share the same pass): the orphaned-placeholder sweep and the empty-synthetic-account drop. Runs 4 AND 5 both finished the redacted round trip holding 14 URL-less placeholder streams bound to no channel, and run 5 left the synthetic account behind even when empty. Run 7, same redacted recovery cycle:
  streams_summary  110 (with_url=96, without_url=14)  ->  96 (with_url=96, without_url=0)
  accounts  ['custom','ECM Custom Streams (DBAS restore)','Infinity']  ->  ['custom','Infinity']
Zero residue, no leftover account, m3u_accounts back to 2 — matching the source exactly. Playback 4/4, 200, 262144 bytes each.

Sweep predicate (narrowest that catches the measured residue): on the synthetic account AND no URL AND referenced by no channel (reference set built from ALL destination channels, not just restored ones, so a placeholder held by an untouched channel is protected) AND not already deleted by the ledger pass. The account is identified by the union of a live name match and the ledger; unidentifiable means no-op, never a guess. The empty-account drop relaxes ONLY the 'who created it' condition — emptiness is still verified against the destination's own stream list.

KNOWN, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: the preview summary now reads 'N profile membership(s) corrected' — right number, wrong tense for a dry run. Filed as enhancedchannelmanager-juu3c.

CAVEAT: live evidence from a drill container patched with the merged modules.

title: DBAS restore silently drops all logos, all EPG links, channel-profile membership and non-default ECM settings while reporting success with 0 failures
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK, NOT production. ECM v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Affects BOTH artifact variants identically. Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n. Measured by natural-key inventory diff (before.json vs after-encrypted.json / after-standard.json).

The restore reported 'Restore success: created 32, failed 0 across 12 categories'. Four categories of state were lost anyway, none of them counted as a failure or a skip.

1. LOGOS -- 13 -> 0, total loss, misreported as clean
   Every channel came back with logo_id=None. The report says 'logo created=0 ... logo_misses=0'.
   logo_misses=0 is not merely unhelpful, it is wrong: 12 channels lost a logo they had.
   Root cause: routers/backup.py line 70, BACKUP_DIRS = ['uploads/logos','tls','m3u_uploads'] -- the artifact's binary subtree only carries logos from ECM's OWN /config/uploads/logos/. Verified on both filesystems: ECM /config/uploads/logos/ is EMPTY, while the logo uploaded through ECM's own Logo Manager lives at Dispatcharr /data/logos/drill-logo.png (9373 bytes). So binary/metadata.json is {'logo_count': 0, 'logos': []} even for a logo the operator uploaded via ECM, and after a wipe those bytes are unrecoverable from the ECM backup.
   The 12 CDN-URL logos are a separate case: their URLs are archived, but nothing re-resolves them on restore either.
   Proof the upload path itself is sound: the uploaded PNG's sha256 through ECM matched the source file byte for byte (09b1732a1defcde737b981fd53f1167696183da6ef43ee08d5c265695db32b01) BEFORE the wipe.

2. EPG LINKS -- 10 of 12 channels linked -> 0
   Every restored channel has epg_data_id=None. The EPG SOURCE restores fine ('EPG Guru US', 14668 entries) but no channel is reconnected to it. Re-linking all 10 by hand is the only path back.

3. CHANNEL PROFILE MEMBERSHIP -- 9 of 12 -> 12 of 12
   Profile 'Drill Subset' was seeded with deliberately NON-DEFAULT membership (channels 101, 102, 103 excluded). It restored containing ALL 12 channels. The profile's name and existence survive; the thing that made it a profile does not. Silently reverting to 'everything' is the worst possible default -- a profile used to scope a lineup now exposes channels it was built to exclude.

4. NON-DEFAULT ECM SETTINGS reverted to defaults
   user_timezone:        'America/Chicago' -> ''   (default)
   stats_poll_interval:  37 -> 10                  (default)
   Both were set through the ECM Settings UI before the backup and both are in the compared inventory. The restore's settings category reported 'updated=7' -- so it DID write settings, just not these.

WHY IT MATTERS
Each of these individually is recoverable by hand. Together they mean 'the restore succeeded' is not a statement an operator can act on: counts reconcile perfectly (channels 12->12, groups 377->377, profiles 1->1) while logos, guide data, profile scoping and settings are gone. Nothing in the restore report, the preview, or the UI says so.

REPRODUCED: yes, identically on both variants, each on its own clean rollout.

SUGGESTED FIX
Report honestly first, then fix coverage. logo_misses must count channels whose archived logo could not be reinstated, and the report needs equivalent counters for unrestored EPG links and for profile membership. Then: carry Dispatcharr-side logo binaries in the artifact (or re-resolve archived logo URLs on restore), reattach epg_data_id via the archived tvg_id, and restore profile membership rather than defaulting to all-channels.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9): fixed in commit 2c99a44c (v0.18.1-0024), never closed. dfkbn: EPG-link half shipped via _resolve_epg_link_natural_keys (backup.py:2749) stamping ARCHIVE_EPG_TVG_ID_KEY, consumed at channel_reattach.py:497; drill run 9 measured 9/9 seeded EPG links surviving on both artifact variants, and CHANGELOG.md:80 already stated the bead was closed. x548h: the match-sense logo_misses producer was removed (logos.py:956) and the counter now has one loss-only definition in restore_contracts.py. nlg9i: self.passphrase = None added to _reset_run_transients (dbas_restore.py:233), called from execute()'s finally, with a paired test at test_dbas_restore_task.py:596.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
RUN 2 VERDICT: MOSTLY FIXED, one half still failing. Drill run 2026-08-04-run2, ECM 0.18.1-0023, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable stack, not production. Both artifact variants, each on its own clean rollout, with the d0agi workaround applied.

NOW PASSING

* Non-default CHANNEL-PROFILE MEMBERSHIP survives. Source 'Drill Profile Scope'
  had a deliberately non-default 9 of 12 members; restored membership is 9 of
  12, the same 9 by name. Run 1 measured 9 -> 12 (silently widened to 'all').
  The report also names the drift it applied (profile_membership_drift=3 with
  channels_disabled listed).
* Non-default ECM SETTINGS survive. stats_poll_interval 37 (default 10) and
  user_timezone America/Chicago (default UTC) both restored exactly. Run 1
  measured both reverting to defaults.
* LOGOS: 10 of 11 restored with sha256-IDENTICAL bytes (compared on the image
  bytes, not on 'a logo appears').
* logo_misses is now CORRECT and non-zero: logo_misses=1, with
  logo_miss_details naming the lost logo and the channel it belonged to
  (FOX News). Run 1's logo_misses=0 while 12 channels lost a logo is fixed.
  The one loss is legitimate: 'Drill Uploaded Logo' lived at
  /data/logos/drill-logo.png inside DISPATCHARR's volume, which the drill
  destroys, so its bytes cannot round-trip. Reported honestly rather than lost
  silently - exactly what this bead asked for.

STILL FAILING: EPG LINKS

All 7 linked channels lost their guide link. epg_data_id -> None on every one,
on BOTH variants. This is not a timing artifact: the EPG SOURCE restored fine
and had already re-fetched all 14,668 epgdata rows (same count as source) at the
time of measurement. The guide data is present; only the link is gone.

The product reports it: epg_links_unrestored=7, and epg_link_miss_details lists
each channel with tvg_id: '' - which is the cause.

Cause, from the shipped source: dbas/channel_reattach.py deliberately (and
correctly) relinks by the channel's archived tvg_id rather than by epg_data_id,
because epg_data_id cannot round-trip. But the artifact's channel rows carry
epg_data_id=<source id> with tvg_id=None, so the index lookup has nothing to
match on and every link is dropped.

This is NOT a drill seeding artifact. Verified empirically on the restored
instance: PATCHing a channel's epg_data_id through ECM's OWN API leaves tvg_id
null:

  channel before: epg_data_id=None tvg_id=None
  PATCH {epg_data_id: 1}
  channel after : epg_data_id=1    tvg_id=None

So ECM itself produces EPG-linked channels that carry no tvg_id, and for those
the reattach cannot help.

Suggested fix: resolve the link's natural key at BACKUP time - when gathering
channels, look up the referenced epgdata row and record ITS tvg_id alongside
epg_data_id. The reattach then works regardless of whether the channel row
happens to carry a redundant tvg_id. (The drill's own inventory script does
exactly this resolution, which is how the before/after comparison could name the
specific tvg_id each channel lost.)

Keeping this bead open for the EPG-link half only.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTION (PO review, run 2026-08-04-run2). Not reopening this bead; recording that one factual assumption its fix enshrined is wrong.

The fix's own comment in routers/backup.py states that for logos 'their URLs are
the only thing that CAN round-trip', and dbas/importers/logos.py builds on the
same premise - that a Dispatcharr-volume-local logo names bytes 'that do not
survive the source instance'.

That is false at BACKUP time. The drill fetched the uploaded logo's bytes over
HTTP from Dispatcharr's own logo cache endpoint with just the API key ECM already
holds, byte-identical to the original file
(sha256 09b1732a1defcde737b981fd53f1167696183da6ef43ee08d5c265695db32b01). The
bytes only stop existing once the source volume is destroyed, which is the event
the backup is supposed to survive.

The consequence - logo_count: 0 in every artifact and an unrestorable uploaded
logo - is filed as enhancedchannelmanager-xb58a (P0).

Everything else recorded in this bead's previous run-2 comment stands unchanged:
profile membership, non-default settings, logo BYTES for remote-CDN logos, and
correct non-zero logo_misses are all verified fixed; the EPG-link half is still
failing and is the reason this bead stays open.

title: DBAS Backup task keeps encryption+credentials from a manual encrypted backup for the rest of the process lifetime
description:
FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK (bkr-ecm / bkr-dispatcharr, project ecmbkr), NOT production. ECM build v0.18.1-0022, Dispatcharr 0.28.2 (ghcr.io/dispatcharr/dispatcharr@sha256:3eb0ec77...). Artifact variant in play: both. Drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n.

SYMPTOM
After an operator uses Settings -> Backup & Restore -> 'Encrypted Backup (Migration)' -> Create Encrypted Backup, EVERY subsequent run of the 'DBAS Backup' scheduled task in the same container process produces an ENCRYPTED artifact that also CARRIES CREDENTIALS, using the passphrase entered for that one manual export. The operator is never told.

STEPS
1. Settings -> Scheduled Tasks -> DBAS Backup -> Run Now.
   Log: [BACKUP] Built artifact ecm-backup-2026-08-04_145924.zip (schema_version=1, 22 members, encrypted=False, include_credentials=False)  <- correct default
2. Settings -> Backup & Restore -> Encrypted Backup (Migration): enter a passphrase, tick 'Include credentials for migration', tick the acknowledgement, Create Encrypted Backup.
   Log: ... encrypted=True, include_credentials=True   <- as requested
3. Settings -> Scheduled Tasks -> DBAS Backup -> Run Now AGAIN. Change nothing.
   Log: POST /api/tasks/dbas_backup/run -> [BACKUP] Built artifact ecm-backup-2026-08-04_150434.zip (schema_version=1, 22 members, encrypted=True, include_credentials=True)   <- WRONG

EXPECTED (quoted from the code's own stated invariant, /app/tasks/dbas_backup.py:182-188)
'Whole-artifact passphrase encryption (ADR-012 D12 / u81kh) -- MANUAL-RUN ONLY transients, passed as ad-hoc run parameters and DELIBERATELY excluded from get_config so a passphrase is never persisted to the schedule store (journal.db). A SCHEDULED run therefore always produces the default redact-by-default backup: there is nowhere safe to keep a passphrase at rest for an unattended run, so encrypted backups are opt-in + interactive only.'

ROOT CAUSE
get_config() correctly omits passphrase/include_credentials/acknowledge_unrecoverable, so nothing is written to journal.db. But set_config() assigns them to the LIVE TASK SINGLETON (self.passphrase, self.include_credentials, self.acknowledge_unrecoverable) and nothing ever resets them after a run. The task object outlives the manual run, so the transients contaminate every later execution -- including an unattended scheduled one -- until the process restarts. The invariant holds for persistence but NOT for the in-process object.

REPRODUCED: yes, deterministically. Proof that it is in-memory residue rather than persisted config: 'docker restart bkr-ecm', then POST /api/tasks/dbas_backup/run with no other action -> encrypted=False, include_credentials=False again. GET /api/tasks confirms the dbas_backup config block contains no encryption fields at any point.

WHY IT MATTERS
1. Scheduled backups an operator believes are redacted silently begin carrying credentials.
2. Those artifacts are encrypted under a passphrase entered once for an unrelated one-off migration export. If it was not recorded, every scheduled backup produced afterwards is permanently unrecoverable -- and the operator has no signal that anything changed.
3. It is timing-dependent and invisible: it disappears on container restart, so it will not reproduce for anyone who restarts before testing.

SUGGESTED FIX
Reset the three encryption transients to their defaults in a finally: block at the end of execute(), so they genuinely apply to a single run. A regression test should assert that two consecutive task runs, with an encrypted manual run in between, produce encrypted=False on the second.
close_reason:
VERIFIED FIXED on drill run 2026-08-04-run2 (ECM 0.18.1-0023, digest sha256:787bf82f..., disposable stack, not production).

Three backups taken with NO ECM restart between them (container RestartCount=0, StartedAt 2026-08-04T23:28:00Z; all three built after that instant). Container log '[BACKUP] Built artifact ...' lines verbatim:

  1. ecm-backup-2026-08-04_232832.zip  encrypted=False, include_credentials=False   (Scheduled Tasks -> DBAS Backup -> Run Now)
  2. ecm-backup-2026-08-04_232925.zip  encrypted=True,  include_credentials=True    (Encrypted Backup card, passphrase + Include credentials)
  3. ecm-backup-2026-08-04_233003.zip  encrypted=False, include_credentials=False   (Run Now again)

Backup 3 is the test: under the run-1 defect it would have inherited encrypted=True/include_credentials=True from the in-memory task singleton until a container restart. It is a clean redact-by-default artifact. The encryption settings no longer leak across runs.

title: User guide ships 25 screenshots from the pre-rework UI, including the whole Getting Started walkthrough
description:
The operator workspace rework changed the app shell from a horizontal tab bar to a left sidebar with grouped nav. 25 committed screenshots still show the old shell, so a new operator following Getting Started sees an app that does not match their screen.

Split, verified by inspection:
- docs/images/user_guide/getting-started/ (12): old UI, footer v0.17.6. This is the worst case, it is the first thing a new operator reads.
- docs/images/event_sync/ (7): old UI. Already tracked separately as enhancedchannelmanager-qguc7, which notes four UI elements were removed outright, so prose needs correcting too, not just recapture.

title: The docs site build never runs on a PR, so a broken link merges green and silently stops the site updating
description:
Found while shipping the tutorial epic (bead gsnw0), and confirmed by reading the workflows.

.github/workflows/docs-pages.yml runs `mkdocs build --strict` and deploys to GitHub Pages. Its triggers are PUSH TO DEV and workflow_dispatch. It is the ONLY workflow that references mkdocs.

So no pull request ever builds the documentation site. The sequence is:
  docs PR opens -> seven required checks run, none of which touch mkdocs
  PR merges green
  push to dev fires docs-pages
  mkdocs build --strict fails
  the public site silently stops updating, and the only signal is a failed workflow after the merge

CONFIRMED CONCRETE INSTANCE: docs/user_guide/getting-started/installation.md links to ../../../README.md, which resolves outside the docs tree. `mkdocs build --strict` aborts on it — exactly one warning, and strict treats it as fatal. Caught only because the site was built manually before pushing.

THE TWO GATES CHECK DIFFERENT THINGS, and that is the trap:
  npm run docs:check  = scripts/check-operator-docs.mjs — internal links and heading anchors WITHIN the docs tree. Knows nothing about mkdocs nav membership, files excluded from the built site, or links that escape the tree. It PASSED on the broken link.
  mkdocs build --strict = the published-site build. Fails on links to files not in the site, and on nav problems.

Nine writers were told docs:check was the gate. All nine ran it, all nine passed, and the site build was broken the whole time. That is not the writers failing a check; it is a check that could not see the failure, paired with one that could and never ran.

SCOPE: add a docs-site build to PR CI. `mkdocs build --strict` against docs/requirements-docs.txt, on pull_request, path-filtered the same way docs-pages already is. It does not need to deploy — building is the gate.

DECIDE DELIBERATELY whether it becomes a REQUIRED check. Making it required blocks merges on documentation problems, which is right for a project that publishes a public site; not making it required reproduces the current situation with extra steps.

While in there: docs-pages is path-filtered to docs/user_guide/**, docs/images/user_guide/**, docs/index.md, mkdocs.yml and requirements-docs.txt. A link INTO docs/ from outside those paths could still break the build without triggering it. Worth checking whether the filter and the build are consistent.

title: Edit Mode stages some destructive actions and silently commits others, including Merge and CSV Import
description:
Found while writing the Channel Manager tutorials (bead gsnw0.2/.3), verified EMPIRICALLY against the running instance rather than inferred from source. This is a data-safety finding, not a documentation one.

Edit Mode presents itself as a staging area: make changes, then Apply All or Discard. Operators reasonably read that as "nothing is real until I apply". THAT IS TRUE OF SOME ACTIONS AND FALSE OF OTHERS, with nothing on screen distinguishing them.

STAGED, discardable — verified by assigning and then discarding, and reading the stored value back via get_channel between the two:
  Create Channel
  Bulk Delete  (its own confirm dialog even says "Changes can be undone while in edit mode")
  Bulk Assign EPG

IMMEDIATE, despite requiring Edit Mode to be ON — each created or mutated real records that Discard did not touch, and had to be cleaned up afterwards through the API:
  Create new channel group
  Import CSV
  Merge  (BOTH the toolbar Merge button and the merge inside Find Duplicates)

MERGE IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. It is destructive, it is not trivially reversible, and it sits behind a mode whose entire promise is that you can back out. An operator who merges twenty channels, decides against it, and hits Discard has lost the originals — while the dialog vocabulary and the surrounding mode have told them the opposite.

CSV IMPORT is the same shape at scale: an operator testing an import inside Edit Mode expecting to review before committing has already committed.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ASKING FOR: a decision that everything must be staged. Some of these may be genuinely impractical to stage — a merge reconciles records across providers, an import may be streamed. The defect is that the interface does not distinguish them. Either stage them, or say plainly at the point of action that this one applies immediately and cannot be discarded.

The tutorials written under gsnw0.2/.3 now open with a table classifying every action as staged or immediate, because it could not be explained any other way. THAT TABLE IS A WORKAROUND FOR A UI PROBLEM. Documentation telling operators which half of a mode means what it says is not a fix.

Verify the list is complete before acting: only the actions the writer exercised are classified above. Every other action reachable in Edit Mode needs the same treatment, and the ones not yet checked are the risk.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Inventory corrected: 11 actions stage, 10 write immediately. STRIKE 'Create new channel group' from the bead body, it now stages (ChannelsPane.tsx:2889-2925, bead vtapf, build 0052). ADD these immediate writers the bead missed: Profile visibility (ChannelsPane.tsx:2122 api.updateProfileChannel), Set Logo from M3U (:1811), Set Logo from EPG (:1863), Restore hidden group (:3001), Clear stream stats (:2197), logo upload (:6216, :6228). Merge stays immediate: MergeChannelsModal.tsx:134 calls api.mergeChannels and the component contains ZERO occurrences of isEditMode, so there is no staging branch. Find Duplicates merge at FindDuplicatesModal.tsx:137, CSV Import at CSVImportModal.tsx:94. The sharp edge is the contradiction: the three delete dialogs still render 'Changes can be undone while in edit mode' at ChannelsPane.tsx:5828, :5937, :6039. Fold bead i4yk1 in here, same defect class, same toolbar, one fix shape.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). PO chose the HYBRID. Commits f37c794b, 9823968c, b7dbb1ff, 165d00b3, 98ed692e, 6461f531, 0cc5efdf, 5f442e9f, 046ebb61, 410fd0f3.

THE BEAD SAID THE INVENTORY WAS THE RISK AND IT WAS RIGHT. It had already been rescoped once. Three further independent enumerations each found actions the previous one missed: two dedup Merge affordances calling api.addStreamToChannel on click, and a THIRD probe entry point (handleProbeGroup) reached from a group menu that exists solely in Edit Mode. The bead's instruction not to close on the named list was the single most valuable line in it.

FINAL DISPOSITION: 7 actions converted to staged (profile visibility, Set Logo from M3U/EPG, restore hidden group, clear stream stats, both dedup merges). 3 that genuinely cannot stage carry an explicit checkbox-gated acknowledgement (toolbar Merge, Find Duplicates merge, CSV Import). Probe and profile create/rename/delete stay immediate with a non-blocking note - PO decisions, both. The three delete dialogs no longer promise an undo they could not deliver.

DEVIATION FROM THE PO'S LIST, accepted: logo add/upload was NOT staged. The channel-facing effect (logo_id) already stages; what is immediate is a catalog row, which is additive and non-destructive, so discarding leaves litter not lost data.

A LATENT DEFECT FOUND IN PASSING THAT WOULD HAVE EATEN THIS WORK: _consolidate_operations silently DROPPED any operation type it did not enumerate, and the frontend always sends consolidate:true. Every new staged op type would have been staged, counted, reported committed, and never sent. It later lost a known field the same way, then inverted submitted order - three defects, one function - and was finally reshaped to copy a template rather than rebuild from parts.

FOUR reviewer rounds, mostly on journal correctness: journal.log_entries reports failure by RETURNING FALSE and its return was discarded; finish() guarded the flush but not row construction; the nothing_to_journal sentinel could legitimise a landed mutation via the free-form data bag; and CancelledError bypassed the flush entirely. Fixed structurally - recording a landed write now REQUIRES its journal row as a defaultless keyword argument.

FULFILS enhancedchannelmanager-i4yk1, closed separately, per that bead's own NOTES.

Left open: enhancedchannelmanager-62ja6 (checkpoint-revert writes immediately from this same toolbar; needs a semantics decision), ftidn, 1e4at, t683u.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECISION 2026-07-31: option (b) — stage the immediate actions properly, rather than merely labelling them. NOT YET; deferred, not declined.

Rejected: (a) labelling at point of action, and (c) blocking those actions while in Edit Mode.

So the mode is to keep its promise rather than qualify it. Two things follow for whoever picks this up:

1. THE FEASIBILITY QUESTION IS NOW THE FIRST TASK, not a side note. It is established that Merge and Import CSV bypass staging; it is NOT established WHY. Determine whether each can be staged before estimating. Merge reconciles records across providers and may need server-side support to represent as a reversible diff — if so, that is the real work and it should be sized before anything is promised. Create-channel-group is the likely genuine exception: a staged channel needs a real group id to reference, so the group may have to exist first. If that holds, say so explicitly rather than forcing it.

2. THE UNCHECKED ACTIONS ARE THE RISK. Only six actions were classified, by exercising them. Every other action reachable in Edit Mode is unclassified, and this bead should not be closed on the six.

INTERIM STATE, and it is not nothing: until this lands, the ONLY warning an operator gets is a table in the Channel Manager tutorials classifying each action as staged or immediate. That table exists because the UI does not distinguish them. It is documentation compensating for a UI defect, and it should shrink to a pointer once this ships — but while the work is deferred it is load-bearing, so do not remove it early.

Merge remains the sharp edge: destructive, not trivially reversible, behind a mode that promises reversibility, and next to a Bulk Delete dialog that explicitly says changes can be undone in edit mode.

title: GitHub #755: copying or reordering pipeline rules floods the server past its concurrency limit
description:
USER-REPORTED, GitHub issue 755, v0.18.0, reporter FractalBoy, Priority 2 "ECM is severely degraded".

SYMPTOM, from the reporter steps:
  1. Channel Pipeline, copy a rule -> it appears at the BOTTOM, and an error toast fires
  2. refresh -> the rule is now in the RIGHT place
  3. reorder a rule -> another error toast, the reorder appears to fail
  4. refresh -> the rule IS in the place it was moved to
So the writes land; the UI reports failure and does not reflect them until reload. A user cannot tell a successful operation from a failed one.

THE LOG IS THE DIAGNOSIS. After a successful POST /api/channel-pipeline/rules -> 200 and an "Updated rule id=139" line, the server emits a long unbroken run of:

  WARNING:  Exceeded concurrency limit.

That is uvicorn refusing requests past --limit-concurrency. backend/entrypoint.sh:409 sets it, defaulting to 100 (ECM_LIMIT_CONCURRENCY, entrypoint.sh:425).

So a copy or reorder is issuing a BURST of individual requests -- plausibly one write per rule to renumber execution order -- and on an instance with enough rules the burst exceeds 100 in flight. The refused ones surface as the error toast; the accepted ones explain why a refresh shows the correct state.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING, because the obvious fix may be the wrong one:
  - How many requests does one reorder actually issue, and are they parallel or sequential? Measure it in the browser; do not infer it from the code.
  - Is there already a bulk endpoint? The MCP surface exposes bulk_toggle_channel_pipeline_rules, so a bulk pattern exists in this area. If a bulk reorder endpoint exists and the UI is not using it, that is the fix.
  - Raising ECM_LIMIT_CONCURRENCY IS NOT THE FIX. It moves the threshold and leaves an N-request write amplification that scales with rule count. A user with more rules hits it again.

THE SECOND DEFECT IS SEPARATE AND ALSO REAL: the copy lands at the bottom and only sorts correctly after a refresh. That is a client-side cache or ordering bug independent of the concurrency flood -- the server clearly knows the right order. Do not let fixing the request burst hide it; verify the list reorders in place without a reload.

Guard both: one write path per reorder rather than N, and the list reflecting server state without a refresh. Reproduce with enough rules to exceed the limit -- a two-rule instance will not show it, which is likely why this was never caught.

title: GitHub #754: hardcoded loopback blocklist overrides the mode-aware SSRF policy on settings save
description:
USER-REPORTED, GitHub issue 754, v0.18.0 docker compose, reporter kmac, Priority 2 "ECM is severely degraded".

SYMPTOM: a new user running Dispatcharr behind a shared gluetun network must address it as http://localhost:9191. The TEST CONNECTION SUCCEEDS. Saving the same URL is rejected:

  [SETTINGS] Rejected Dispatcharr URL on save (scheme/host): Invalid host -- loopback
  and link-local addresses are not allowed (e.g. localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, 169.254.169.254)

Their workaround was to configure outside gluetun, stop the stack, hand-edit settings.json, then re-add gluetun. THE APPLICATION THEN RUNS FINE ON THAT URL -- so the validator blocks a configuration the runtime happily accepts.

DIAGNOSIS, read from source rather than inferred:

backend/routers/settings.py _validate_outbound_base_url_on_save runs TWO stages, and its own docstring calls them "no new policy":
  stage 1  _sanitize_base_url  -- scheme allowlist + netloc reconstruction
  stage 2  security.ssrf.validate_outbound_url under the persisted ssrf_outbound_mode, described in that docstring as "the CANONICAL, mode-aware host validator"

Stage 1 contains a HARDCODED, NON-MODE-AWARE check -- _host_is_blocked(parsed.hostname) at roughly settings.py:1739 -- which emits exactly the message above and rejects loopback unconditionally.

Stage 2 would have ALLOWED it. backend/security/ssrf.py:97 SSRFMode has two values, and the DEFAULT is LAN_FRIENDLY, whose own comment reads "RFC1918 private + 127/8 loopback ALLOWED (default -- ADR-012 D4)". PUBLIC_ONLY is the opt-in that blocks them.

So the non-mode-aware pre-check fires before the mode-aware policy is ever consulted, and lan_friendly -- the shipped default, and a documented ADR decision -- CANNOT BE HONOURED for loopback on the save path. The knob exists, is documented, defaults to permissive, and does nothing here.

ALSO EXPLAINS THE INCONSISTENCY THE USER HIT: the docstring says _sanitize_base_url previously ran ONLY in the test-connection endpoints. The user reports test-connection PASSING while save fails, which suggests the Dispatcharr test path does not call it while the save path does. Establish which endpoints call which validator before changing anything -- a user being able to prove a connection works and then being refused permission to save it is its own defect, independent of the policy question.

DO NOT simply delete the blocklist. It was added by bead kgz3k SEC-1/2 to close a real SSRF plus key-exfiltration hole -- a stored 169.254.169.254 base URL that the runtime pollers would GET with the stored credential every few seconds. The fix is to make stage 1 defer to the mode rather than pre-empt it, so PUBLIC_ONLY still blocks loopback and link-local while LAN_FRIENDLY permits loopback and RFC1918 as documented. Note link-local 169.254.169.254 is the cloud-metadata case and may warrant blocking in BOTH modes; decide that deliberately and write down why.

Reproduce first: set the mode to its default, save http://localhost:9191, observe the rejection. Then verify PUBLIC_ONLY still rejects it after the fix. Regression test both modes.

title: test_epg.py:434 is an exact structural twin of the event-loop budget that failed CI
description:
tests/routers/test_epg.py:434, test_large_xml_index_parse_does_not_block_event_loop, is structurally identical to the test that blocked PR 756 twice and was rewritten in commit bb4dc67c: time.sleep(0.1) inside the patched parser, await asyncio.sleep(0.01) on the loop, assert elapsed < 0.05.

Same property, same measurement, same inverted discrimination. IT IS A LATENT COPY OF A FAILURE ALREADY OBSERVED IN CI TWICE, and it will fail the same way when a runner is loaded enough. It has not fired yet only because that job has not been unlucky yet.

THE ARGUMENT, measured during bb4dc67c rather than assumed:
  healthy, work off-loop      0.0109 s
  genuinely broken, inline    0.1005 s
  loaded CI runner, healthy   0.7936 s and 0.9696 s
The noise band is entirely ABOVE the signal band, so no threshold both catches the regression and survives the load. A larger budget does not fix it; it only makes the test stop proving anything.

FIX IS A MECHANICAL PORT of bb4dc67c. Replace the budget with two event-driven assertions and no clock:
  1. the patched parser records threading.get_ident(); assert it differs from the loop thread ident
  2. a handshake instead of a sleep -- the worker signals it has entered and blocks, the loop observes and releases, so the work is GUARANTEED in flight when liveness is observed rather than racing a timer
Keep only a generous deadlock guard, which is not a threshold.

PRECEDENT IN-REPO: tests/integration/test_event_loop_responsiveness.py already made this move for the same property and documents why. bb4dc67c is the second instance; this would be the third.

PROVE IT RED BOTH WAYS, as bb4dc67c did: inject the violation two independent ways with production source untouched, and verify each assertion is falsifiable on its own -- the mechanism assertion fires first and will mask the liveness one, so test the liveness assertion with the mechanism one removed. A guard that cannot be made to fail is decoration.

ALSO NOTED, lower risk, not this bead: tests/services/test_shared_match_core.py:247,256 and tests/services/test_dedup_matcher.py:387 carry absolute wall-clock budgets, but they measure pure CPU rather than event-loop scheduling, so contention degrades them proportionally rather than catastrophically. The 5.0s budgets elsewhere have roughly 100x headroom and are fine.

title: 121 of 167 labelled control targets fail WCAG 2.5.8 on height
description:
Split out of bead m26f8 (commit 24049628), which fixed the 44 controls that had no label at all. This is the other half of the same census and it is larger.

RE-MEASURED on the current tree, both viewports: of the 167 checkbox/radio controls that DO have a working label, 46 clear the WCAG 2.5.8 24x24 minimum and 121 do not. EVERY failure is height -- ZERO fail on width. The failing heights are 18, 19, 20 and 21px.

(An earlier figure of 66/167 came from a dialog run at 1440x900. Direction and cause agree; the number here is from the current tree at the supported viewports.)

WHY IT WAS NOT FOLDED INTO m26f8: it is a different fix in different files. Lifting an 18-21px row to 24px means row height and padding on .checkbox-label in shared/common.css and its per-component cousins, which reach nearly every settings row and most dialog forms. That is a large visual change and wants its own before/after -- the same territory as the PO report behind bead 7lwe0, where checkboxes reading oversized against 13px text was the complaint. Folding it into m26f8 would have made that change before/after uninterpretable.

DO NOT SOLVE IT BY GROWING --control-box-size. The box is 16px deliberately: it is 1.23em of the 13px body role, above the em box so it reads as a control and below the row line box so it does not drive row height. Growing it restores exactly the defect 7lwe0 fixed. The height has to come from the row.

WATCH FOR: a row that grows to 24px changes the vertical rhythm of every settings form and dialog it appears in. Measure the resulting form heights, not just the targets -- a dialog that newly scrolls is a regression even if every target passes.

GUARD: this is the natural FOURTH arm of e2e/control-box-size.spec.ts, which already has arm 1 (box size), arm 2 (label census, allowlist now empty) and arm 3 (accessible name). It was deliberately NOT added during m26f8 because it would fail on 121 sites today. Add it with the fix, ratcheted like the others.

Note the spec walks routes and opens no dialogs, so a dialog-side fix will be unguarded until bead enhancedchannelmanager-48jr2 lands.

title: 44 checkboxes and radios have no label, so the box itself is the WCAG 2.5.8 target
description:
CENSUSED, not estimated, during bead 7lwe0 (commit 4429a46f). Every visible checkbox and radio in the app: 211 controls across the ten primary routes, the seventeen settings sub-routes and 81 of the 82 catalogued dialogs. Identical in all six viewport x theme cells.

  167 (79%)  have a working label -- clicking the text toggles, so the target is the row
   44 (21%)  have NO label at all -- the 16px box is the entire target
    0 of 211 reach 24x24 on their own

WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) sets a 24x24 CSS px minimum. For the 44 there is no row to fall back on, so they fail it outright. The 7lwe0 sizing pass made 29 of them BIGGER (13px UA default -> 16px) and shrank exactly one, so it improved the situation without resolving it. The remedy is markup, not CSS -- a size token cannot create a hit area that the DOM does not offer.

THE 44, enumerated:
  29  th/td.col-select in the channel-pipeline table and nine cp-* dialogs
   8  div.sort-priority-list on settings/channel-defaults
   3  print-guide .group-checkbox-area
   3  div.schedule-item in the three task dialogs
   1  .pending-merges-select

SEPARATE AND ALSO REAL: of the 167 that DO have a label, only 66 clear 24x24. The rest are wide but only ~18-21px tall, so they pass on width and fail on height. Decide whether that is in scope here or its own piece of work -- it is a different fix (row height / padding) from giving an unlabelled control a label.

FIX SHAPE: wrap the control in a <label>, or associate one with htmlFor/id, so the clickable region becomes the row. Where a table cell holds a bare selector, the cell itself may be the right target. Do not solve it by growing the box to 24px -- that would undo 7lwe0 and make every checkbox in the app oversized against 13px text again, which is the defect the PO reported in the first place.

GUARD EXISTS ALREADY: e2e/control-box-size.spec.ts arm 2 pins the census with an ALLOWED_UNLABELLED list seeded from the ten route sites. It is ratcheted, so fixing a site and not removing its entry fails the build. ALLOWED_UNLABELLED currently cites no bead id -- put this one in when the work starts.

Note the spec opens no dialogs, so 34 of the 44 are outside its reach; bead enhancedchannelmanager-48jr2 covers extending guard coverage into the harness.

title: Reset Stuck Probe is hidden by the exact condition it exists to recover from
description:
CONFIRMED IN SOURCE by me, not only reported. The control documented as the recovery path for a stuck probe is unreachable in the failure mode it documents.

THE LOOP:
- SettingsTab.tsx:5087 gates the whole section on {!probingAll && (
- probingAll is driven by the probe-progress poll, which reports in_progress from StreamProber._probing_in_progress
- force_reset_probe_state() (backend/stream_prober.py:977) is what SETS _probing_in_progress = False
- The sections own copy reads "If a probe appears stuck or was interrupted, use this button to clear the probe state."

So a wedged probe reports in_progress: true indefinitely, probingAll stays true, and the section that clears the flag is never rendered.

THE BANNERS CANCEL IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH. cancel_probe() (stream_prober.py:931) returns "cancelling" and only sets _probe_cancelled = True for the probe loop to observe. A wedged loop never observes it and never clears _probing_in_progress. Verified by reading both functions.

ONLY REMAINING RECOVERY: the backend self-heal at routers/stream_stats.py:603 ("Probe state shows in_progress - resetting before starting new probe"), reachable only by starting a DIFFERENT probe from ChannelsPane on another tab. An operator following the on-screen instructions cannot get there.

RECOMMENDED FIX: render the section unconditionally. Disable the two ordinary buttons while probingAll with a visible reason, and leave "Reset Stuck Probe" ENABLED -- gating a recovery control on the thing it recovers from is circular. This also removes the rail churn described below at no extra cost.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and why it loses: an always-visible reset during a HEALTHY probe is a foot-gun that force-cancels a legitimate run. Real, and answered by disabled-with-reason rather than by hiding. Hiding makes the healthy case marginally safer and the broken case unrecoverable.

RAIL SYMPTOMS OBSERVED LIVE (probe-progress fulfilled client-side; no probe was started and nothing was written to the instance):
- idle rail 9 entries, probe starts -> 8, every entry below moves UP 38px. The reader caused none of it: a backend-SCHEDULED probe flips probingAll via a 5s poll, and Stream Probe has an active schedule on this instance.
- deep link to ?section=settings-maintenance-section-reset-probe-state during a probe: anchor absent from t=0.40s, reader parked at scrollTop 0, aria-current silently falls back to another section. No error, no notice.
- when the probe ends the section returns, items changes, and the deep-link effect re-fires: scrollTop 82 -> 1586 over t=6.41-7.01s. Same yank bead mch8j fixed for Stats, except the trigger is a background event of UNBOUNDED duration -- a probe over a large library runs for many minutes, so the reader is thrown 1586px down minutes after opening the link.

Guard it the way Stats and Settings were guarded (commits 22fef24d, 4af8f487): fetches left pending, proven red first.

title: init_db stamps past drop-only migrations, so destructive migrations silently never run
description:
OBSERVED IN PRODUCTION on this instance, 2026-07-30, deploying migration 0041 (drop lookup_tables). The log line was:

  alembic.runtime.migration: Running stamp_revision 0040 -> 0041

alembic_version now reads 0041 and lookup_tables is STILL PRESENT. The drop never executed, and neither did the row-dump safety net 0041 carries for populated instances.

CAUSE — database.py:584, the bd-5w6jz fast path. It stamps forward instead of upgrading when current_rev != head AND _schema_matches_head(engine). The predicate's own docstring names the hole: it verifies that every Base.metadata table and column EXISTS in the live DB, and explicitly ignores 'extra columns or tables in the DB that aren't on the model'. A drop-only migration is therefore structurally invisible to it -- every model artifact is present precisely BECAUSE the migration's whole job is to remove something the model no longer declares.

The comment at database.py:574-583 reasons the symmetric guard is benign. That reasoning holds for the rolled-back-container-code case it was written for. It does NOT hold for a destructive migration:

1. The row dump is bypassed on exactly the instances that have rows to lose. 0041 writes every row to <db_dir>/lookup_tables_dropped_0041.json before dropping; on a stamped instance that never runs, so the safety net is absent on the only instances that need it.
2. alembic downgrade 0040 on a stamped instance tries to CREATE a table that already exists and fails, so the documented rollback path is broken.
3. alembic_version asserts a schema state that is not true, which every future autogenerate and drift check now inherits.

SCOPE. Make the fast path refuse to stamp across any pending migration that drops something -- i.e. before stamping, walk the revisions between current_rev and head and fall through to a real upgrade if any of them is destructive. Detecting 'destructive' by AST-inspecting the revision modules for op.drop_table / op.drop_column / op.drop_index / batch_op equivalents is the cheap honest version; a declarative marker on the revision (e.g. a module-level ) is the version that cannot silently miss a case, at the cost of every future author remembering it -- which is the exact failure mode this fast path was introduced to end (see the bd-ax3uj / bd-5w6jz history in the comment above the branch). Pick deliberately and write down why.

Do NOT simply delete the fast path: it exists because create_all() got ahead of alembic and per-migration idempotency was whack-a-mole. Removing it reopens that.

STATE OF THIS INSTANCE. lookup_tables was deliberately left in place rather than dropped by hand, so the symptom stays observable for whoever verifies the fix. It has 0 rows and no code references, so it is inert. The real DB is /config/journal.db; /config/ecm.db exists with zero tables.

Also worth deciding: whether a stamped-but-not-run instance needs a self-heal on the next boot, since there is now a population of instances whose alembic_version is ahead of their physical schema.
close_reason: Already implemented and merged to dev in commit 40b70ef7. Current-dev revalidation on 2026-08-17: backend tests/integration/test_alembic_smoke.py passed 80/80. The shipped code detects pending destructive migrations, selectively replays them instead of stamping past them, and self-heals known previously stamped-past table drops; the original live instance was healed during the 40b70ef7 deployment per recorded evidence.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Correction to the description: one phrase was eaten by shell substitution when the bead was filed. The sentence should read "a declarative marker on the revision (e.g. a module-level destructive = True flag) is the version that cannot silently miss a case".

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION (implementation in progress, gate pending).

Detection: AST inspection is the mechanism; the declarative marker survives
only as an override. Rejected the marker-as-mechanism because its failure mode
is "the author forgot", which is exactly the per-migration discipline the
bd-5w6jz fast path was built to end -- and it fails silently: no test goes
red, no log fires, the migration is stamped over and the data is gone.
AST inspection protects an author who never heard of this machinery. Its hole
(a removal expressed in a form the scanner cannot see) is narrower and
closable. Overrides: `destructive = True` opts IN for what the scanner cannot
see (applied to 0011, whose FK drop is a batch copy_from rebuild with no
drop_* call); `destructive = False` opts OUT of a false positive and must be
justified in the revision docstring.

Remediation: NOT a plain fall-through to `upgrade head`. With a destructive
revision at head, every lagging instance has one pending, so the fast path
would never fire for anyone again -- that REMOVES the fast path rather than
narrowing it. Instead: replay each destructive pending revision individually
(stamp to its predecessor, upgrade to it by id) and stamp over everything
else. From 0005 that runs 5 revisions for real and stamps over 31.

Detected destructive set across the current history: 0010 (drops+recreates a
view), 0011 (FK), 0012 (DELETE FROM), 0029 (drop_table), 0041 (drop_table).
All five are already idempotent, so over-detection is cheap -- which is the
right bias when the alternative is silent data loss.

Self-heal: YES, implemented. Not the _BOOTSTRAP_CANARIES shape (re-stamp at
baseline + replay everything) -- this state has exactly one revision's worth
of work missing and replaying 40 revisions to recover it multiplies blast
radius for no gain. Instead a closed registry of revision -> tables it drops;
if alembic_version claims the revision is applied but the tables are still
there, stamp to the predecessor, run that one revision, restore the version
row. Hand-curation is acceptable here precisely because the list is CLOSED BY
CONSTRUCTION: no future migration can be stamped past, so none can need an
entry. Covers table drops only (a table's absence is cheap unambiguous
evidence); dropped columns/constraints/indexes and DELETEd rows have no
equally cheap generic probe and are not healed.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD, from reading the live DB: this instance was stamped
past TWICE, not once. /config/journal.db still holds ffmpeg_saved_configs,
playlist_profiles, publish_configurations and publish_history from revision
0029, alongside lookup_tables. All five have 0 rows.

ALSO INACCURATE: consequence 2 ("alembic downgrade 0040 ... tries to CREATE a
table that already exists and fails"). 0041's downgrade() is inspect-guarded
and returns early, so a stamped instance silently no-ops instead of failing.
The consequence holds for an unguarded drop revision, not for this one.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: GATE (worktree wt-newui, branch newui, final code): backend/ python -m pytest tests/ -q -> exit 0, 0 failures, 8059 collected (baseline ~8035 + 11 new), coverage 76.21% vs 56% floor (baseline 76.2%). Red-first proven: the two headline tests fail on unfixed code with 'lookup_tables is still present'; the self-heal test proven red by neutralising _STAMPED_PAST_DROP_HEAL. Scratch-DB proof against a read-only snapshot of the live /config/journal.db: 0040 -> 0041 logged 'Running upgrade 0040 -> 0041' (not stamp_revision) and '[0041] Dropping lookup_tables (4 row(s))' with the JSON dump written. Live container NOT touched: alembic_version still 0041, lookup_tables still present. Not committed or deployed - PO verifies.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECISION 2026-07-30, on the open question in the 40b70ef7 commit: the boot-time heal ALWAYS drops revision 0029 tables, logging row counts at ERROR first. Ratifies the behaviour already implemented and shipped in 40b70ef7 -- no code change required.

The tradeoff was put to the PO explicitly and taken knowingly: revision 0029 writes no row dump (its author chose not to), so on any instance that holds rows in ffmpeg_saved_configs / playlist_profiles / publish_configurations / publish_history, those rows are destroyed with no dump and no recovery path. The ERROR log line naming the row counts is the only record. Rejected alternatives were drop-only-when-empty (preserves data, leaves affected instances permanently inconsistent) and report-only (never drops at all).

Rationale for the choice: every instance ends physically consistent with its own alembic_version, and the discrepancy does not accumulate across future migrations.

All four tables were empty on this instance and were dropped during the 40b70ef7 deploy, so this decision changes nothing here -- it governs other operators upgrading.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING, not actioned: the 0041 removal already ships a blocking upgrade note at docs/user_guide/epg/lookup-tables-retired.md. A short paragraph there about the 0029 tables would give operators the same export-before-upgrade warning for the case that has no dump behind it, which is the weaker of the two. Cheap, and the only mitigation available under this decision.

title: Login page inputs render in Arial - the font reset does not reach them
description:
REAL DEFECT ON THE FIRST SCREEN EVERY OPERATOR SEES, and the typeface guard structurally cannot see it.

Found while root-causing why e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts fails against a backend-less preview build. Without a backend every route renders the LOGIN PAGE, and .login-field input computes to Arial while its ancestors carry the Inter stack. The guard passes against the live container because it authenticates first — so it only ever measures post-login surfaces.

frontend/src/components/LoginPage.css declares NO font-family, so the reset added in index.css (button, input, select, textarea { font-family: inherit }) should reach those inputs. It does not, and the investigating agent could not fully root-cause why. Candidates worth checking: cascade order against a later bare rule, a shadow boundary, or the login page rendering before the stylesheet the reset lives in is applied.

Four independent proofs this is not caused by the modal type-scale pass: that diff contains zero font-family changes; the guard's probe is fixed at 16px/400 so size changes cannot move it; the reset IS present in that build's output; and the guard passes against the live container.

TWO PIECES OF WORK:
1. Fix the reset so it reaches the login inputs.
2. Extend e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts to cover the UNAUTHENTICATED login page. A guard that only runs authenticated cannot see defects on the screen every operator meets first — and this is the proof of that gap, not a hypothetical.

Sizing: Small for the fix, Small for the guard extension.

title: Rendered-CSS regression guards: sr-only, frozen-chrome, route-typography-scale
description:
COMPLETE, uncommitted. Converts ephemeral verification into checked-in Playwright specs so no claim about rendered CSS rests on a report again.

WHY: an adversarial audit proved the entire .sr-only accessibility fix (commit d4641593) could be reverted with all 16 CSS guard tiers staying green. A user-facing a11y bug — aria-live regions rendering as visible text, 1308x24px on the Dashboard — had NO regression guard of any kind. Separately, every 'frozen chrome unmoved' and row-height measurement in this work lived in scratchpad scripts that no longer exist; the claims were true (the auditor reproduced them exactly) but nobody could re-check them.

SHIPPED: e2e/sr-only-hidden.spec.ts (2 tests), e2e/frozen-chrome.spec.ts (6 tests, 3 themes x 2 viewports x 10 routes), e2e/route-typography-scale.spec.ts (10-route walk with a ratcheted allowlist), e2e/fixtures/css-guard.ts, 4 package.json scripts, a CI job, and docs/testing.md section 'Rendered-CSS regression guards'.

EACH PROVEN RED AGAINST ITS DEFECT, not written and assumed to work:
- sr-only: reverted d4641593 in a scratch build; both tests red where all 16 tiers stay green — dashboard reporting position:static, clip:auto, 1004px wide, occupiesSpace:true. Also proven red under the exact CI serving mode.
- frozen-chrome: appended a bare equal-specificity .primary-sidebar{width:248px} to LogoManagerTab.css — the historical leak shape — and got 15 drift entries. The output demonstrates the visit-order dependency: routes visited BEFORE Logo Manager are clean, every route after reports 248px.
- route-typography-scale: both arms in one run. NEW caught an injected 22px .account-name; STALE caught an allowlist entry whose site had been fixed.

THE GUARD CORRECTED ITS OWN AUTHOR, which is the best evidence it is not decoration: the concurrent completion pass (bead 6z299.8) landed mid-session and the STALE arm flagged all nine now-fixed entries for deletion. It also caught a site the agent had forgotten to allowlist, on its first run. Final allowlist is 10 entries across 6 routes — 4 permanent frozen-band, 3 pending em/rem-relative, 3 pending 24px Material Icons defaults.

CI: only sr-only-hidden is wired, and that is a measured limit not an omission — on a backend-less preview build Channel Manager's .channels-pane never mounts (waitForSelector times out at 60s), so any ten-route walk needs a live container. The other three are manual, stated in docs/testing.md with that measurement as evidence. The new job is NOT in the required-check set; making it required also needs a matching sentinel in docs-only-pass.yml or docs-only PRs hang.

FOUND IN PASSING: login is rate-limited at 5/minute (backend/auth/routes.py) and surfaces as 'Too Many Requests', which reads like a broken assertion rather than a flake — the fixture now logs in once per file and backs off. And e2e/*.ts is neither typechecked nor linted by any gate: no root tsconfig, frontend tooling covers only frontend/src, and Playwright's esbuild strips types without checking them. Pre-existing standing gap; tsc --strict run manually against all four new files is clean.

ALLOWLIST ATTRIBUTION: entries currently cite f4yc7, a CLOSED bead, because no open bead existed to own the exceptions. To be re-pointed at 6z299.8 and this bead.

title: 48 CSS custom properties are referenced but never defined; 63 references have no fallback
description:
Found by the contrast pass, then independently re-counted: 48 distinct custom properties are used via var() and defined nowhere in the tree. 223 references. 63 of those have NO fallback, so they resolve to nothing and the declaration is silently dropped.

Worst: --border-color 75 refs (25 no-fallback), --error-color 29, --card-bg 16 (ALL no-fallback), --error-text 9, --status-error 8, --status-warning 7, --accent-primary-rgb 5, --accent 5.

THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. It has already produced a literally invisible UI element and three separate wrong-value bugs, each found by a different agent on a different bead:
- --text-on-accent (defined nowhere): .event-sync-exclusions-count and .event-sync-review-count rendered white-on-white at 1.00:1 in dark and 1.07:1 in high contrast. Not low contrast — ABSENT. Fixed under dlavh.
- --border-color (defined nowhere): ModalBase's chassis would have painted a fixed #3a3a5a hex in every theme where the live rule was theme-aware var(--border-primary). Caught under 87o0c.
- --error-color (defined nowhere): PrintGuideModal's field-error always resolved to a hardcoded hex instead of the theme's --error. Caught under 6z299.3.
- --accent-warning (defined nowhere): StatsTab's unknown-bucket row never received the high-contrast theme's --warning. Caught under wjbwr.
- --drag-handle-color: undefined in the LIGHT theme only, so drag handles inherited #fff at 1.09:1 — invisible. Fixed under dlavh.

The pattern: a fallback makes the bug silent and plausible, and no fallback makes the declaration vanish. Neither fails loudly, and CSS has no mechanism that would.

Two pieces of work:
1. Triage the 48. Each is either (a) a typo for a real token, (b) a token that should exist, or (c) dead. The no-fallback 63 are the priority since those declarations currently do nothing.
2. A lint rule so this cannot recur. The CSS guard already parses every stylesheet and derives chunks; asserting 'every var() reference resolves to a definition' is a natural fifth tier and cheap next to what is already there. Note theme-scoped definitions ([data-theme=light] etc.) mean the check must be per-theme, which is exactly how --drag-handle-color slipped through.

Sizing: Medium for the triage, Small for the lint rule.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Counts corrected by independent re-parse (comments stripped, var() occurrences counted): 45 distinct undefined properties, 210 references, 59 with no fallback. Not 48/223/63. The bead's own 2026-07-29 comment had already corrected toward this. Worst offenders: --border-color 72 refs / 25 no-fallback, --card-bg 16/16 all no-fallback, --error-text 9, --status-error 8, --status-warning 7. Defect class fully intact; neither the triage nor the lint rule has been done.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION — all three headline numbers are wrong, and the cause is systematic and worth knowing.

WRONG: 48 distinct / 223 references / 63 no-fallback. Actual, on the current worktree with var() occurrences inside /* */ EXCLUDED: 46 / 215 / 59. At HEAD: 49 / 225 / 59. Per-token: --border-color is 73 refs (I said 75), --error-color 27 (I said 29). The other six worst-offenders are confirmed exactly: --card-bg 16 refs / 16 no-fallback, --error-text 9, --status-error 8, --status-warning 7, --accent-primary-rgb 5, --accent 5.

THE CAUSE, and it explains more than this bead. Re-running the same parse WITH comment text counted as code reproduces my numbers exactly — --border-color 75, --error-color 29. I did not strip comments. This codebase's CSS is unusually comment-dense and the wave comments deliberately QUOTE the selectors and tokens they document (ModalBase.css:59 and :73 both mention var(--border-color, #3a3a5a) inside a comment explaining that very token). So a comment-inclusive count is biased upward, systematically, in one direction, for every token. Separately, grep | wc -l counts LINES not OCCURRENCES, which biases the other way on one-liner rules.

That is very likely the source of the '97 sites' in bead 4l51b too (actual 92), and possibly other counts I have published this session.

METHOD RULE going forward: any number that appears in a bead title or drives a decision needs a comment-stripping parse behind it, and the bead should state which method produced it. Otherwise the next person recounts, gets a different answer, and cannot tell which of us is wrong.

STATUS CHANGES since filing: --drag-handle-color is RESOLVED (defined in both themes, index.css:111 and :285). --text-on-accent is resolved ONLY IN THE UNCOMMITTED WORKING TREE — at HEAD it is still undefined, so the bead's 'Fixed under dlavh' is true of the tree and not of any commit. --accent-warning is still undefined but its surviving reference has moved to ProviderStreamUsagePanel.css:113; wjbwr fixed StatsTab's.

CONFIRMED: the guard already parses every stylesheet and derives chunks, so a fifth tier is cheap. And the per-theme requirement is real — index.css has three theme blocks and tokens genuinely differ between them, which is exactly how --drag-handle-color hid (defined in dark, undefined in light).

title: Modal harness: force-render every dialog with stub props for before/after verification
description:
BLOCKS the remap. PO decision 4.

62 TSX files render a modal or dialog, and most cannot be reached against this instance's data — no pending merges, empty review queues, conditions not met, probe results absent. Every prior round of this work ended with an honest 'measured what I could reach, reasoned about the rest', which concentrates the residual risk in rarely-opened dialogs. That is precisely where a regression survives longest.

Build a dev-only route that force-renders every dialog with stub props, so all 62 can be measured before and after. It stays in the repo as a test artefact and will be needed again by the look refactor, which touches the same dialogs.

Requirements:
- Enumerate dialogs from the source rather than a hand-maintained list, so a dialog added later is covered automatically. 62 TSX currently match modal-container / ModalOverlay / role=dialog / role=alertdialog.
- Dev-only: must not ship in a production build, and must not appear in the router for a normal operator.
- Stub props must render each dialog's REAL markup — the point is to measure the component, not a hand-built approximation. Where a dialog needs data to render at all, stub the data, not the DOM.
- Report which dialogs cannot be force-rendered and why. Honest gaps are fine; silent ones are not.

Sizing: Medium.

comments.text:
