title: .sr-only aria-live regions render as visible text on Dashboard and Settings
description:
PRE-EXISTING accessibility/UI defect, surfaced by the 87o0c same-chunk reconciliation. Not introduced by it.

.sr-only is declared in exactly ONE place: frontend/src/components/channelPipeline/ConditionEditor.css:269, which ships in the ChannelPipelineTab lazy chunk. (ActionEditor.css carried a byte-identical second copy in the same chunk; 87o0c deleted it, which changes nothing about this defect.)

But the class is rendered outside that chunk by two live regions:
  frontend/src/components/tabs/OperatorDashboard.tsx:179  <div className='sr-only' role='status' aria-live='polite'>  (EAGER chunk)
  frontend/src/components/tabs/SettingsTab.tsx:5876        <div className='sr-only' role='status' aria-live='polite'>  (Settings chunk)

Neither chunk contains the rule. So until the operator visits Channel Pipeline, both regions have NO visually-hidden styling and their announcement text renders as ordinary visible text on the Dashboard and in Settings. After a Channel Pipeline visit the lazy stylesheet is appended and never removed, so the same regions silently become correct for the rest of the session.

This is the same load-order mechanism the P1 sweep was about (docs/css_guidelines.md section Load order), in its least visible and most embarrassing form: an accessibility affordance that works only if you happen to have opened an unrelated page first.

Fix: promote .sr-only to shared/common.css section 2 UTILITIES, beside .visually-hidden which was consolidated there by bead 6z299.1 for exactly this reason, and delete the ConditionEditor copy. Note the two utilities are near-duplicates and should probably become one — .visually-hidden uses the clip-rect recipe with !important throughout; .sr-only should be compared against it rather than blindly copied.

Not done inline because it changes what renders on two surfaces: text currently visible would disappear. That is the correct behaviour, but it is a visible change and belongs to a decision rather than to a reconciliation pass whose acceptance bar was render-neutrality.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Fixed and committed as d4641593.

Merged with .visually-hidden rather than added beside it: the two blocks were property-for-property identical — same nine declarations, same values, same order — differing only in !important. They are one utility under two names, so they are now one rule with two selectors. Kept as an alias rather than renamed, because the five .sr-only call sites live in files carrying the PO's uncommitted work; zero TSX touched.

MEASURED on a fresh context with Channel Pipeline never visited:
  Dashboard region  position:static, clip:auto, 1148px wide, box 1148x24, returned by elementFromPoint — genuinely visible
              after  position:absolute, clip rect(0,0,0,0), 1x1, overflow hidden, no longer the hit
  Settings region   800px wide, box 800x24 -> 1x1
  .sr-only rules in loaded sheets: 0 -> 1
  All three Channel Pipeline labels byte-identical including rects, reached through the real UI (Create Rule -> Standard -> Add Condition/Action -> Create Channel)
  Full-page pixel diff of the Dashboard black apart from an animated pill's antialias edge and a clock three minutes apart

!important verified rather than assumed: all nine properties are hiding properties, so promoting them can only make an element more hidden. Exactly one call site sits under a higher-specificity rule (.action-field label) which declares only font-size/weight/colour, disjoint from the nine — that label measures 13px on a 1x1 clipped box before and after.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF, one of them mine to own:
1. I gave the agent a FABRICATED bead ID (d3ubm). bd create's output was truncated to Priority/Status without the ID line and I invented one rather than looking it up, then cited it in a comment on 87o0c. That comment is now corrected. The agent found the real bead and proceeded correctly.
2. I asked it to 'verify the tiers reflect the removal of a cross-chunk exposure'. That rests on a wrong model — no tier could have changed. All three model DUPLICATE DECLARATIONS, and .sr-only had exactly one declaration in the whole tree, so nothing ever collided and every tier was green for the entire life of the bug. Spun out as bead nraba: the guard has no tier for declaration-site / render-site chunk mismatch, which is the more dangerous half of the family — a collision renders something either way, whereas this rendered nothing until an unrelated navigation, and hid an accessibility affordance.
3. Minor: ActionEditor.css:485 carried a pointer comment naming ConditionEditor.css as the owner, which the move made stale. Updated, along with the shared-utility entry in docs/css_guidelines.md. Four files, not two.

title: Cleanup pass: modal/pane bidirectional collision, inline-empty unification, guidelines
description:
Final shared-layer pass of the P1 sweep.

HEADLINE — a live, user-visible P1 that predates the sweep and nobody had recorded. ChannelProfilesListModal.css and ChannelsPane.css both declare .channel-item, and both are EAGER. ChannelsPane is emitted later, so its .channel-item{display:grid; grid-template-columns:...} overrode the modal's flex row: the Manage Channels list rendered channel names inside a 32px grid track as 'Fl...1', 'Fl...2'. Unusable. Simultaneously the modal's .channel-item .channel-number/.channel-name (0,2,0) were setting the type on every Channel Manager row and donating min-width:50px and text-align:right, contradicting that column's own 'digits are centered' comment.

Scoping the modal's whole .channel-item family to its real root (.channel-profiles-modal) fixes BOTH directions at once, because 0,2,0 also outranks ChannelsPane's bare 0,1,0 inside the modal.

Measured: modal .channel-name width 32px -> 515px; modal .channel-item display grid -> flex. CM .channel-number text-align right -> start, min-width 50px -> auto, box w50 @x397 -> w7.83 @x418.08 (finally centred in its 52px column). CM row heights unchanged at 48/52px. The Channel Manager wave's defensive .channel-wrapper .channel-item{gap} workaround was pure leak-compensation and is deleted.

Also: common.css section 28's comment corrected to say .header-stat is FROZEN chrome and must not be remapped (it previously claimed the page waves owned it, contradicting the spec). Inline-empty treatment unified — .alert-methods-empty and .team-aliases-empty moved onto .empty-inline, plus two more found in passing (.saved-backups-empty, .lookup-tables-empty), with the enumeration comment rewritten and now accurate. Orphaned guard-baseline comment deleted.

docs/css_guidelines.md gains two sections: 'Partial redeclaration' (four confirmed instances from this sweep, plus the icon single-class-ties-with-base trap) and 'Adopting a role' (plain text takes the full triplet; interactive controls take the size token only and keep authored weight; icons chosen by role not nearest pixel). Rollout status now reads all ten route pages remapped, and the closing guidance is upgraded to 'Never write a bare font-size in a content-pane rule.'

.email-recipient-tag kept at badge 10px after live A/B screenshots at 10/11/13px. Legible, no truncation, and the value is re-checkable in the input beneath. My stated reason for not exempting it was WRONG and the agent corrected it: .tag-chip and .alert-method-type-badge never co-render with it. The real reason is that one class serves three call sites, two of which are short tokens that belong at badge size. If it should be bigger, the least-inconsistent fix is a new class for the identifier-carrying chip only.

Note: in-code comments cite 'the enhancedchannelmanager-6z299 cleanup pass' across 8 files and should be re-pointed at this bead ID.

title: Wave 3: regression guard for cross-chunk shared-class leaks
description:
DONE, in the tree, landing red as intended (9 violations, all Wave 1 targets).

Two deliverables:
1. frontend/src/cssAudits/sharedClassChunkLeak.audit.test.ts — parses every CSS file, derives chunk membership from the import graph via the TypeScript compiler API (no hardcoded file list, so a page added next year is covered automatically), and fails when one selector carrying typography properties is declared bare in two different chunks. Validated against a real build: reproduces every chunk in dist/assets/*.css including the four shared-across-lazy-roots chunks.
2. e2e/cross-route-css-leak.spec.ts — walks all ten routes in a SINGLE context in two different orders plus a revisit pass, asserting computed typography agrees. Two contexts are mandatory: running order B inside order A's context would measure a fully-loaded head and could never disagree. Navigates by location.hash because navigateToTab()'s recovery path calls page.reload(), which would discard every lazily-appended stylesheet and turn a real failure into a pass.

Why this was needed: e2e/css-smoke.spec.ts is structurally incapable of catching this defect class — each test takes a fresh appPage fixture and visits exactly ONE route, while the leak only manifests after visiting route A then route B. It stayed green through all four historical instances.

Historical replay: caught 3 of 4 (list-header/qlc4h, group-count/sccol, action-btn). status-label/f4yc7 correctly NOT caught — at that revision there was only one bare declaration with EPG and M3U already scoped, so no equal-specificity collision existed; that bead was preventive scoping.

WIRING STILL NEEDED (deliberately not done by the agent to avoid a package.json collision): add postcss as an explicit devDependency of frontend/package.json (it currently resolves only as a transitive dep of vite), and optionally a test:css-leak script entry.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Tier-2 (layout/paint) extension complete. Guard is now three assertions in one file, 200 -> 530 lines, runtime unchanged (~630ms, CSS index built once and shared).

Tier 1 (typography) is semantically untouched and still reports exactly 9 — it stays unbaselined and red because it is the metric the sweep is tracked against.

Tier 2 covers width/height/min-*/max-*, padding, margin, display, position, flex/grid/gap/align/justify, colour, background, border, box-shadow/opacity/overflow, cursor. Excluded transition/animation/transform as the highest-churn declarations in the tree — costs zero coverage today, since all 3 such findings sit on selectors tier 2 already catches by other properties.

The noise fear did not survive measurement. display was the predicted problem (21 findings) and every one is genuine: the guard keys on identical selector TEXT, and scoping IS the fix, so a scoped rule is invisible by construction and the properties it sets are irrelevant. Only bare duplicates ever reach the comparison. Tier 2 also uses strict same-property matching (a display collision in one chunk and a padding collision in the other do not contend in the cascade), which cut 56 -> 49 and removed the only real false-positive class.

Of the 49, SEVENTEEN have divergent values across chunks — they render differently today depending on visit order. The other 32 are latent.

ORCHESTRATOR DECISIONS (PO asleep, within the authority granted):
1. The 15 collisions belonging to no wave are filed as their own bead (enhancedchannelmanager-mktnb) rather than bolted onto Wave 1, which is already dispatched and scoped. Nine of the fifteen are live-divergent.
2. Tier 2 ships GREEN with an explicit 49-entry baseline rather than standing red. Accepted the agent's reasoning: a permanently-red assertion gives no regression signal during the sweep and historically never gets converted afterwards. The baseline cannot rot — it fails on a new collision (NEW LEAK), on a baseline entry whose collision is gone (STALE ENTRY), on an entry whose chunk set moved (CHUNKS MOVED), on any entry with a blank bead, on duplicate entries, and on an untriaged count above a budget that may only be lowered.

Confirmed against the real pre-fix tree (git archive of 42cf25f9^, running the actual test file): tier 2 catches the .action-btn box collision with DIVERGENT VALUES on padding, and tier 1 at that same commit did NOT — it flagged only .action-btn .material-icons. The box collision was genuinely invisible to the old guard.

Seven failure drills run and reverted, including appending a real new collision to App.css and confirming it was reported with the right file:line pair and the right property.

Largest honest gap: shorthand/longhand is not reconciled (padding vs padding-left, border vs border-color, flex vs flex-basis), and @media overlap is not modelled.

title: Wave 1: scope-only pass — give 18 bare cross-chunk declarations a page-root ancestor
description:
SERIAL, specificity-only, zero intended render change. Keeping it separate from Wave 2 means any pixel movement in Wave 2 is attributable.

Spec: scratchpad/p1-consolidation-spec.md section 5.

Targets include .section-title (StatsTab), .detail-label/.detail-row/.detail-item (three pages inventing 'detail'), .refresh-btn and .channel-count (GuideTab, consumed unscoped by two Stats panels and a modal), .expand-icon (TagEngineSection 1.5rem leaking onto three eager modals), .btn (RuleBuilder — a class named .btn declared bare in a leaf editor), .btn-icon (LookupTableSection AND TagEngineSection, same Settings bundle, later import silently wins today), .pane-header (ChannelsPane + StreamsPane), TagEngineSection's whole modal chassis (prefer delete + reuse ModalBase).

Also: rename .action-badge in M3UFiltersModal to .filter-mode-badge — a filter-mode chip and a journal event-type chip are unrelated concepts colliding on one name.

Note: ChannelDetail.css .close-btn is listed in the spec as a target but ChannelDetail is dead code (imported by nothing) — that line item is a no-op, see the dead-code bead.

The Wave 3 guard currently reports 9 violations; all but .modal-header h3 are resolved by this wave, and .modal-header h3 resolves via the TagEngineSection chassis deletion rather than by hoisting (PO decision 5 says do not hoist it).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Wave 1 complete. Guard TIER 1: 9 -> 0.

THE AGENT CORRECTED MY BRIEF, AND WAS RIGHT. I told it to scope .header-stat and .filter-select to their page roots. RouteHeaderSlot is a real createPortal (RouteHeaderSlots.tsx:36), so those elements render inside App's .route-page-status-outlet / .route-page-controls-outlet and .journal-tab / .m3u-changes-tab are NOT ancestors — a page-root scope would have stopped matching and silently deleted the styling. It hoisted .header-stat to common.css instead and scoped .filter-select via a new per-page class. Second time the spec has been wrong about portaled elements.

THE :where() IDIOM. Every added ancestor is wrapped in :where(), which contributes zero specificity, so every rule keeps exactly the specificity it had and only its match set narrows. That makes render-neutrality provable rather than argued. It is load-bearing: a plain .stats-tab .stat-label would be (0,2,0), tying with .enhanced-stats-panel .stat-label, and StatsTab.css is emitted AFTER the panels in the chunk — so a plain scope would have started winning and resized every Stats panel.

LIVE BUG FOUND AND FIXED: StreamsPane.tsx:1830/1945 passes filter-select to CustomSelect, so Channel Manager's stream filters were taking Journal's / M3U Changes' 14px and 18px !important arrow after a single visit to either page.

.toggle REGRESSION FIXED — the whole switch family in M3UGroupsModal.css scoped to :where(.m3u-groups-modal), specificity preserved at (0,1,0), so the modal's own switches are unchanged and the five 'action-btn toggle active' buttons revert to 32x32.

HOIST-EXPOSURE AUDIT (the corollary I asked it to sweep for): after the .toggle fix, .action-btn has no remaining exposed sibling. One live finding — Guide's .time-slot-header renders a HYBRID today: GuideTab.css redeclares font-size/font-weight bare in the lazy chunk, beating eager common.css, but does NOT redeclare letter-spacing/text-transform, so those DO come from .micro-label. Result is 12.8px/600 uppercase with 0.08em tracking, which is neither the old look nor the micro role. Matches my live measurement exactly. Assigned to Wave 2.

.modal-header h3 / TagEngine chassis: spec section 5 said 'delete and reuse ModalBase'. Not safe — geometry genuinely differs (max-width 400px vs ModalBase size classes, border-radius 12px, no backdrop blur, .modal-close not .modal-close-btn, h3 not h2). Scoped the whole private chassis to :where(.tag-engine-group-modal) instead; conversion left for a page wave. Scoping only the h3 while its parent still leaked would have looked done and not been.

Two same-chunk duplicates deleted after proving them dead: .enter-edit-mode-btn (ChannelsPane's copy — lightningcss already drops it from the built bundle as unreachable) and .group-toggle-btn (byte-identical in both panes, given one owner in common.css).

NOT RESOLVED, deliberately: .settings-btn — App.css's copy is dead except that its :hover is the only hover rule reaching the button when DISABLED (the modal's own is :hover:not(:disabled)), so deleting it removes a real hover state. Left, per the render-neutrality constraint. Also .logo-option-none, .modal-btn, .preview-more, .setup-hint, .pane-header, .search-input, .edit-mode-* — in each, neither copy fully shadows the other, so reconciling means choosing a look. All same-chunk and deterministic; none is order-dependent.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 177 files / 2468 tests, 2467 passing. The one failure is guard TIER 2, red with 19 STALE ENTRY and ZERO new leaks — i.e. 'you fixed these, delete the lines'. Baseline prune dispatched separately.

NOT VERIFIED: no browser render. Render-neutrality rests on specificity preservation, per-case TSX ancestor checks, and one built-chunk ordering check.

title: Wave 0: consolidate the shared CSS layer (index.css + common.css) and delete rogue page duplicates
description:
SERIAL, one commit, blocks every other wave.

Why serial: shared/common.css is emitted at byte 263,255 of the 263,419-byte eager bundle (verified against the built asset) — LAST. It beats eager stylesheets but loses permanently to any lazy tab chunk, which is appended on first visit and never removed. So a hoist only takes effect when EVERY page copy is deleted. A partial hoist looks green in the diff and still renders wrong. The deletions span files owned by five different page agents, so no partition makes them disjoint.

Spec: scratchpad/p1-consolidation-spec.md section 4.

Scope: new --type-label-* / --icon-badge / --icon-empty tokens; off-scale shared value fixes; icon tokenization (16 raw material-icons sizes in common.css, only one tokenized before this); new sections 25-28 (pagination strip, field messages, filter bar, metric tile) plus .empty-inline, .visually-hidden, .file-*, .group-*, .error-message, button variants; all 65 card/panel titles onto the 15px section role; .action-btn whole rule family hoisted with the 32x32 box as canonical; docs/css_guidelines.md gains a Load order section.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Wave 0 implemented, uncommitted, gates verified independently by the orchestrator (not taken from the agent's report): tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 176 files / 2466 tests passing, 1 failure = the Wave 3 guard which is supposed to be red. Main checkout confirmed clean — no worktree pollution.

Guard went 40 -> 9 cross-chunk typography leaks. The 31 resolved include .btn-primary/.btn-secondary families, .search-box, .form-group label, .test-result, .warning-message, .group-name/.group-count, .file-name/.file-size, the whole pagination strip, .visually-hidden, .header-left h2, .error-message, .separator-btn, .btn-small/.btn-icon and .action-btn.

THE AGENT CORRECTLY REFUSED TWO SPEC ITEMS, and it was right. Spec sections 4.3/4.4 called for a section 27 FILTER BAR and a section 28 METRIC TILE. Every class they name renders inside RouteHeaderSlot — the frozen route-header band. Verified independently: JournalTab.tsx:246 (.header-stats in name=status), :289-383 (three .filter-select in name=controls), ChannelPipelineTab.tsx:1011 (.channel-pipeline-stats in name=status). Building those sections would have moved frozen chrome. Root cause of the bad spec: section 4.3's line list came from the duplication audit while section 7's exclusions came from the TSX-verified inventories, and the merge did not reconcile them. New sections are therefore numbered 25 Pagination Strip, 26 Field Messages, 27 Group Rows.

.stat-value/.stat-label deferred to Wave 1 scoping rather than hoisted: the two donors are different components, and hoisting would shrink the frozen band 24->20px while growing Stats' card values 14->20px inside a minmax(140px,1fr) grid.

Deliberate render changes to check visually: .badge 12->10px and .type-badge 11->10px app-wide; .btn-icon glyph 18->16px; Stats' 18px panel titles and Pipeline's 16px section header -> 15px; .loading-state icon 48->64px; RuleBuilder's footer secondary button becomes the shared filled .btn-secondary; StreamsPane .separator-btn.active gains a background it never had (its old value was the invalid 'var(--accent-primary)22', silently dropped by the parser).

One TSX change: M3UGroupsModal.tsx:390-391 btn-small -> 'btn-secondary btn-small'. .btn-small is a size modifier at 6 of 8 call sites and a standalone button at 2; the canonical rule is the modifier.

NOT YET DONE: nobody has opened the running app. No visual claim is made for Wave 0.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
VISUAL VERIFICATION of Wave 0 against the deployed build (localhost:6100, 1600x1000, authenticated, all ten routes measured by computed style — not screenshots).

CONFIRMED CORRECT: .badge 10px/500, .type-badge 10px/500 uppercase ls0.8px, Pipeline .section-header h3 15px/600, .empty-state p 13px (was UA 16px), .empty-state icon 64px, .action-btn glyph 16px, .page-info 13px, .micro-label and .list-header 10px/700 ls0.8px uppercase.

FROZEN CHROME INTACT on all ten routes: rail label 14px/400 lh21px, route title 20px/700 lh26px.

GUIDE GEOMETRY RISK DID NOT MATERIALISE: all 22 .guide-row exactly 60px, 44 .program-block, ZERO overflowing. The ROW_HEIGHT=60 virtualisation desync the inventory flagged as the sweep's highest severity did not occur.

REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED (handed to Wave 1): M3UGroupsModal.css:245 declares a bare .toggle switch widget (width:40px; height:22px). Five components render a row action button classed 'action-btn toggle active' — an unrelated use of the word. Both selectors are (0,1,0). Before Wave 0, .action-btn's 32x32 lived in M3UManagerTab.css, emitted AFTER M3UGroupsModal.css in the M3U chunk (M3UManagerTab.tsx imports the modal at line 7, so the child's CSS lands first), so .action-btn won. Wave 0 hoisted .action-btn into common.css — eager, therefore EARLIER than the lazy M3U chunk — so the bare .toggle now wins. Measured: M3U Manager toggle buttons compute to 22px tall against 32px for their plain siblings in the same row. EPG Manager shows it too, but only after the M3U chunk has loaded.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which the spec did not state: a hoist moves a rule EARLIER in the cascade, so it can expose unrelated bare rules in lazy chunks that were previously losing to the page copy. Wave 0 hoisted many classes; Wave 1 has been asked to sweep for the same shape.

NOT A REGRESSION (pre-existing, confirmed): .action-btn width shrinks below 32px on M3U/EPG because .account-actions is a 180px flex row holding 7 buttons (7x32 + 6x4 gap = 248px) and .action-btn has never carried flex-shrink:0. Identical before Wave 0. Backlog candidate.

STILL PENDING for Wave 2, both predicted by the inventories and now confirmed live: Guide's .micro-label measures 12.8px/600 because .time-slot-header still declares font-size/font-weight at equal specificity, so the class is inert; .m3u-changes-tab .list-header measures 11.2px/600 because its scoped override still repeats list-header typography; Stats' bare .section-title measures 14px/600 uppercase, left by Wave 0 as a micro-label idiom rather than a card title.

title: Stats section nav scrolls the document and exposes empty space below the shell
description:
PO report: navigating to #stats?section=stats-section-popularity via the Stats quick section nav scrolls the entire screen rather than the content pane, leaving black space below the app shell.

The app shell is height:100% with overflow:hidden, so a scroll of the document or body should not be possible; something in the section-nav scroll path is scrolling an ancestor that is not the intended scroll container.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9); all verified in code, not just in CHANGELOG. 2896r.16: TabNavigation.tsx:125-130 renders the Settings drill-in nav with a 'Back to main navigation' control, regression-tested in TabNavigation.test.tsx (commit 73a02a22). 2896r.17: App.tsx:2601-2617 builds routeHeading from settingsSectionHeading() into PageHeader; in-pane headings removed. 2896r.21: StatsTab.tsx:875 wraps the summary counts in RouteHeaderSlot name='status', portalled into the shared route header (commit 661031f6). cujyo: StickySectionNav.tsx:38 scrollWithinContainer() replaces scrollIntoView so the shell no longer scrolls, with a regression test asserting scrollIntoView is never called. vh6hh: ChannelManagerTab.tsx:552 passes defaultLeftWidth={50} explicitly at the call site. 1bpl8: root-caused — detect-secrets drops VERIFIED_FALSE results via is_ignored_due_to_verification_policies, and the Telegram plugin's verify() is a live network call; 9 of 27 plugins behave this way. ECM's own gate is immune because check_secrets.py:149 and :332 both pass --no-verify. Residual: comment that --no-verify is load-bearing for confidentiality.

title: Order-dependent flake recurs: Channel Manager permission-state test fails only in full-suite order
description:
During PO-review verification the operator-shell suite failed one test, 'Channel Manager permission state exposes no protected panes or actions' (e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts around line 2837), with 64 passed.

Evidence that it is order-dependent rather than a regression:
- Isolated run of the same test on the same build: passed in 284ms.
- Immediate full-suite re-run with byte-identical code: 65/65 passed.
- The change under test at the time was the sidebar brand mark (inline SVG logo + ECM wordmark), which does not touch Channel Manager permission handling.

This is the same class as enhancedchannelmanager-a0ekz - passes in isolation, fails only in full-suite order - but a different test. a0ekz was closed on the basis that deterministic layout settling had resolved the class, so either that fix does not generalise or this test has its own leakage.

Worth an ordered-prefix reproduction audit before the epic ships, since a suite that fails roughly one run in two on a rotating test will not give a trustworthy CI signal.

title: newui: smoke.spec.ts and example.spec.ts fail against the epic's own shell restructure
description:
npm run test:e2e uses testMatch '**/*.spec.ts' and therefore runs every spec, but the operator-workspace validation only ever ran e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts. Running the rest surfaces 7 pre-existing failures.

Reproduced identically at newui HEAD 18961c1d (7 failed / 8 passed) and with the PO-review work applied (7 failed / 8 passed), using a detached baseline worktree, so these are caused by the epic's own restructuring and not by the review changes.

Cause: the specs encode the pre-epic shell.
- e2e/fixtures/test-data.ts selectors.headerTitle is 'header h1', but 2896r.4 moved the route h1 into <main> via PageHeader; <header> now contains no h1 at all. assertAppLoaded therefore fails for every consumer.
- example.spec.ts asserts the page h1 contains 'Enhanced Channel Manager'; the h1 is now the route breadcrumb.
- smoke.spec.ts navigation tests drive .tab-button style tab controls; primary navigation is now grouped sidebar links.

Impact: a PR from newui into dev will fail CI if the pipeline runs the full Playwright project rather than just the operator-shell spec. Needs either updating these specs to the current shell or an explicit decision to retire them.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Half the diagnosis does not reproduce. STILL TRUE: selectors.headerTitle is 'header h1' (e2e/fixtures/test-data.ts:81) and App.tsx:2626 renders a header with no h1 inside it, so smoke.spec.ts:11, :18-19 and assertAppLoaded (e2e/fixtures/base.ts:333-334) are structurally broken. NOT TRUE: the .tab-button half. TabNavigation.tsx:185, :199 still render 'primary-navigation tab-navigation' and 'navigation-destination tab-button' with data-tab, and git log -S shows that compat class was present from the original restructure commit 3346fc54, so it never broke. example.spec.ts uses the unauthenticated page fixture and lands on LoginPage's h1, so its two tests likely pass. Rescope to fixing headerTitle/assertAppLoaded only, roughly 2 of the ~15 tests in scope.

title: Dashboard card freshness text fails WCAG AA contrast in the light theme
description:
OperatorDashboard.css sets .dashboard-card-freshness to var(--text-muted). Under [data-theme=light] that renders #999 on --bg-secondary #f5f5f5, measured 2.61:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement for normal text. Dark measures 4.82:1 and high-contrast 8.52:1, so only the light theme fails.

Introduced with the dashboard in enhancedchannelmanager-2896r.3, not by the PO-review changes in 2896r.15. The epic's axe matrix ran the dashboard in the default dark theme only; the multi-theme contrast matrix from rv84z covered Channel Manager selectors, so this fell between the two.

The same token is used for the tone-neutral status icon, which is a non-text component at 2.61:1 against a 3:1 requirement, though the adjacent text carries the meaning.

Fixed under 2896r.15 by moving both to var(--text-secondary): light 5.26:1, dark and high-contrast higher. Filed separately so the root-cause gap - dashboard axe coverage never running the light or high-contrast themes - stays visible.
notes:
Fixed under 2896r.15 (var(--text-muted) -> var(--text-secondary); light 2.61:1 -> 5.26:1).

Root cause addressed: the epic's all-routes axe sweep runs in the default dark theme only, so no dashboard selector was ever measured in light or high-contrast. Added e2e test 'Dashboard and header status meet AA contrast with no serious violations across every theme' covering 2 viewports x 3 themes x 2 states (populated and one failed card) over 11 selectors, with a scoped axe run and a JSON evidence artifact per combination.

title: entrypoint.sh depends on PATH for interpreter resolution — pin to /opt/venv explicitly + self-diagnosing preflight
description: Field-reported 2026-07-27: an operator on 0.18.0 hit '✗ Required Python packages missing' + ModuleNotFoundError: fastapi, reproduced byte-for-byte with 'docker run -e PATH=/usr/local/bin:...' (PATH override strips /opt/venv/bin). The published image is sound (both arches verified); the defect is that backend/entrypoint.sh calls bare python3 at 7 sites (lines 82,83,91,175,181,196,197) and 'exec gosu appuser uvicorn' at line 317, all resolved via PATH, so any operator-side PATH override or mount over /opt/venv silently falls back to system python3 (which reports a reassuring 'Python 3.12.13' with zero ECM packages). NOTE: uvicorn exists ONLY in /opt/venv/bin — fixing preflight alone just moves the failure one line down. Work: (1) resolve ECM_PYTHON=${ECM_PYTHON:-/opt/venv/bin/python} once with a command -v python3 fallback, use it at all 7 sites; (2) exec /opt/venv/bin/uvicorn with fallback; (3) Dockerfile:92 HEALTHCHECK has the same bare-interpreter exposure — pin it; (4) make check_python self-diagnosing: print the RESOLVED interpreter path next to the version, and on failure emit interpreter path + sys.prefix + $PATH + whether /opt/venv/bin/python exists (this alone would have resolved the field case from the first log paste); (5) per engineering-discipline 'enforcement code tests itself', add a fixture test running preflight under a stripped PATH — red-without-fix is provable with the repro command above.
notes: Field outcome 2026-07-27: root cause confirmed and operator restored to service via container delete+recreate with a proper /config volume. This validates the diagnosis (stale pre-0.16 container env inherited across an in-place Container Station update, so bare python3 resolved to the system interpreter). The fix in this bead prevents the failure class entirely — a PATH-independent interpreter means an inherited stale PATH is harmless.

title: Stop M3U Digest API failure retry/toast storm and provide recoverable error state
description:
## Problem
When Settings > M3U Digest cannot load its digest/provider dependencies, the current UI repeatedly issues request batches, accumulates duplicate error toasts, leaves the page stuck at “Loading digest settings…”, and can move focused toast-dismiss controls offscreen at both 1920x1080 and 1280x720. Confirmed in a current-HEAD Playwright audit on 2026-07-26.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run ECM where the digest/provider dependency returns an error.
2. Sign in and navigate to Settings > M3U Digest.
3. Observe the loading state, repeated network requests, and accumulating duplicate error notifications.
4. Continue keyboard traversal until focus reaches displaced toast-dismiss controls.

## UX impact
The operator cannot diagnose or recover from the failure, notification noise obscures the page, and keyboard focus can land on inaccessible offscreen controls. Violates Nielsen 1, 5, and 9 and affects WCAG focus order/visibility.

## Likely surface
UI lifecycle around GET /api/settings/m3u-digest and GET /api/providers; explicit idle/loading/success/error state and notification deduplication are needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- One failed page activation produces no more than one request batch.
- Loading terminates in a stable inline error state with actionable guidance.
- Retry issues exactly one new request batch.
- Equivalent notifications are deduplicated and visible toast count is capped.
- Toasts and dismiss controls remain inside 1920x1080 and 1280x720 viewports.
- Keyboard focus never moves to an offscreen toast action.
- Rendered-browser regression coverage proves the failure and recovery path.
close_reason: Shipped PR #746 (merge 160277bb, v0.17.6-0173), team review PASS no changes: digest load-failure latch (one request batch per activation), inline role=alert recoverable error panel with Retry, zero toasts on load failure, app-wide toast dedup + pinned visible cap. Red-first tests + live-container Playwright verification at 1920/1280. Final container bundle deploys with PR #747.

title: PR 721 follow-up: surface incomplete exclusive profile reconciliation
description:
Team review of merged PR #721 found that per-profile PATCH failures are caught and counted, but _execute_assign_channel_profile still returns success/modified. A failed profile-universe fetch is also collapsed to an empty universe, degrading to enable-selected-only while reporting success. This can reproduce GH #720 silently.

IMPLEMENTED + REVIEWED, shipped in build 0.17.6-0151 (PR #722, merged).
Fix: _apply_exclusive_profile_membership returns a ProfileMembershipResult carrying failed_profile_ids; _execute_assign_channel_profile returns a non-success ActionResult on partial write failure and FAILS when the profile universe is unavailable (explicit None sentinel vs [] empty). _assign_default_profiles stays a benign no-op on empty/unavailable universe.

--- 0152 completion (build 0.17.6-0152) — IMPLEMENTED + REVIEW-APPROVED + IN PR ---
Fix-forward on 0151: the ACTION was truthful but the RUN still finalized green. 0152 closes five gaps:
(1) Run status — engine aggregates failed actions at finalization -> new terminal status 'completed_with_errors' (distinct from green completed; not a blanket failed), persists error count + summary, top-level API result success=false. Executions UI: amber badge + 'Completed with Errors' label/toast, rollback affordances kept. UNATTENDED auto-fire path (post-M3U-refresh scheduled run) no longer notifies green on a failed-action run: TaskResult(success=True, failed_count=N) -> ONE 'Task Completed with Warnings' warning WITH external alerts (established stream_probe partial-failure path), not a green success and not a hard 'Task Failed'; the task's own completion toast is suppressed on failed runs (deferred to the task engine) to keep it to one coherent warning. Defensive guard: a completed_with_errors run always reports failed_count>=1 so the engine never takes the green branch even if the count were ever 0 (decoupled from the engine invariant).
(2) Dry-run universe validation — a dry run with an unavailable profile universe returns an explicit blocking outcome, no rosy 'Would assign N'.
(3) No-op write — total profile-write failure counts modified=False (no phantom update/rollback entity); partial still counts.
(4) Event Sync — assign_channel_profile now actually executes on the real execute_event_sync_rule attach path (new + promoted channels), the GH #720 case; 0151 exercised only a synthetic no-streams path.
(5) Rollback honesty — assign_channel_profile is non-rollbackable (no reversible previous-state); no longer recorded as a rollback entity.

Frontend: canRollback + rollback/revert buttons + status badge/toast + poll TERMINAL set all handle completed_with_errors.
The ENGINE pipeline-result contract (success=not failed_actions) and persisted execution.status='completed_with_errors' remain the honest record; only the task-execution envelope reports completed-with-warnings (PO decision).

Gates green: full backend suite 7671 passed / 13 skipped; frontend 2146 passed, tsc clean, build clean; version consistency 3/3 at 0.17.6-0152. Code review: APPROVED (+ optional defensive-hardening nit closed). Deployed + container-smoked on ecm-ecm-1.

STATUS: implemented, reviewed (approved), version-bumped, in PR against dev for the agent team to test. Do NOT close — PO closes after merge.

NOTE (intentional, not a regression): _assign_default_profiles (channel_pipeline_executor.py:3646) is BEST-EFFORT — on partial/total profile-PATCH failure it only LOGS failed profile ids and does NOT escalate to completed_with_errors, and treats a falsy universe (None or []) as a benign no-op.
