title: Concurrent requests on the JWT-cookie auth path may crash the backend process (no traceback, ExitCode 0)
description:
Imported from GitHub issue #546: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/546

### Summary
Opening the Auto-Creation tab in the web UI frequently (but not always) crashes the backend container. Root cause isolated to: **multiple concurrent requests authenticated via the `access_token` cookie can crash the process; a single request never does, regardless of endpoint.** This reads as a race condition — likelihood, not certainty, on each concurrent burst.

### Environment
- Image: `ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:latest`
- Revision: `ab76a4f8248303f608a12cd2849af608d33ddbd2`
- Deployed via Docker Compose behind nginx-proxy-manager (openresty), HTTPS terminated at the proxy
- ~189 auto-creation rules, ~31k streams across 8 M3U providers

### Notable timing detail
The instance ran for roughly a week with no crashes before a bulk rule-creation session brought the rule count up to 189. Crashes on opening the tab became frequent only after that. This is consistent with a race condition whose probability scales with request/response size (more rules → larger payload → longer request duration → wider window for two concurrent requests to collide) rather than a deterministic bug tied to any specific rule content — we separately verified the rules themselves are well-formed (`/rules/analyze` reports no findings).

### Reproduction
The Auto-Creation tab fires three requests in parallel on mount:
- `GET /api/auto-creation/rules`
- `GET /api/auto-creation/executions`
- `GET /api/normalization/rules`

Replaying these exact requests confirms the trigger is concurrency + cookie auth, not the tab or its data:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Single request, `access_token` cookie, via nginx | `200 OK` |
| 3 of the above requests fired in parallel, via nginx | All `502`, container restarted (reproduced on 2 of 2 attempts at this rule count) |
| Same 3 requests in parallel via the project's MCP server (uses a static API key, bypasses the JWT-decode path in `auth_middleware`) | Succeeded every time, no crash |

`docker inspect` after a crash shows `ExitCode=0`, `OOMKilled=false`. Cgroup `memory.events` shows `oom_kill 0` (checked across two separate container instances). Host `dmesg` is clean. Setting `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` produces **no output** at the crash — ruling out SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGFPE/SIGILL. The process simply disappears mid-log with no shutdown sequence, then the entrypoint's "Startup Preflight Checks" banner reappears. Nothing useful is ever logged, even watching `docker logs -f` live through a crash.

Given `ExitCode=0` and no signal-based death captured by Docker, this looks like a clean voluntary exit somewhere in-process, not an OS-level kill — and the inconsistent reproduction (loads fine most of the time at lower rule counts, fails more often at higher ones) is consistent with a race rather than a deterministic fault.

### Suspected area
In `backend/main.py`, the global `auth_middleware` branches on credential type:
```python
if (
    settings.mcp_api_key
    and token
    and hmac.compare_digest(token, settings.mcp_api_key)
):
    return await call_next(request)
if not token or not decode_token_safe(token):
    ...
```
The MCP static-key path returns early; the JWT-cookie path falls through to `decode_token_safe()` (`backend/auth/dependencies.py` → `backend/auth/tokens.py`). `decode_token` itself looks safe on read (in-memory revocation set, well-scoped exception handling around `python-jose`), so the bug is more likely in something shared across concurrent requests on that path — e.g. JWT secret retrieval (`_get_secret_key()` → `get_jwt_secret_key()`) or a settings/session lookup that isn't safe under concurrent access (possibly SQLite connection/session contention). Haven't instrumented far enough to pin the exact line.

### Impact
Any UI view that fires more than one request at once while cookie-authenticated has some chance of crashing the backend; the odds appear to rise with response size/request duration. The Auto-Creation tab is just the first place we noticed it, since it always fires 3 requests together on mount and our rule count made the window wide enough to hit reliably.

### Suggested next steps
- Reproduce with `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` plus heavier logging around `auth_middleware` / `decode_token_safe` to catch the actual exit path.
- Audit whatever `get_jwt_secret_key()` / settings lookup does on the hot path for thread/coroutine-safety under concurrent requests.
- Consider whether something in that path calls `sys.exit()`/`os._exit()` directly instead of raising an `HTTPException`.
- Test reproduction at varying rule counts to confirm/refute the size-correlates-with-failure-rate theory.
notes:
INVESTIGATION + FIX (container-first, not committed):

REPRODUCTION ATTEMPTS: Could NOT reproduce the crash locally despite extensive effort: exact 3-request cookie-auth bursts (100+), 60-90-way concurrent bursts (6000+ total requests), seeded 190 auto-creation rules to match reporter payload (~900KB), client aborts/cancels mid-response, AND deploying the reporter's exact v0.17.5 (ab76a4f8) backend code into ecm-ecm-1 (dependency pins identical). Zero crashes.

MECHANISM PINNED EMPIRICALLY (end path, not raiser): On this exact stack (uvicorn 0.46.0 + uvloop 0.22.1 + Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware chain), a SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt raised during request handling propagates out of asyncio.Task.__step INTO the event loop itself (cannot be caught at any await), aborts uvicorn's serve() with NO shutdown sequence, and a bare SystemExit exits the interpreter with status 0 and no traceback. Verified live with a probe app in the container: /boom route raising SystemExit -> process gone, connection refused. This matches every element of the reported signature (ExitCode 0, no faulthandler output, no shutdown logs, mid-log disappearance). Also verified the CONVERSE: external SIGTERM produces a fully visible shutdown sequence -> reporter's crash is NOT an external signal.

FIX: exit_diagnostics.BaseExceptionContainmentMiddleware — pure-ASGI guard registered as the INNERMOST user middleware (first add_middleware in main.py), running in the same task as route handlers. Catches SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt (NOT Exception, NOT CancelledError, NOT GeneratorExit), logs CRITICAL [EXIT-DIAG] with full traceback naming the culprit, converts to RuntimeError -> ordinary logged 500. Auth semantics untouched (guard sits INSIDE auth_middleware).

VERIFIED LIVE in ecm-ecm-1: guarded probe survives 3x SystemExit (500 each, [EXIT-DIAG] logged); ECM burst verification 60x3 + 50x60 concurrent cookie-auth requests all 200, container healthy; auth: valid cookie 200, invalid 401, missing 401, MCP key 200, exempt health 200.

GATES: backend pytest full suite 6982 passed, 4 skipped (pre-existing documented skips), incl. 15 new regression tests in tests/integration/test_base_exception_containment.py. py_compile clean; no regex changes (semgrep rule N/A).

FILES: backend/exit_diagnostics.py (+70), backend/main.py (+12), backend/tests/integration/test_base_exception_containment.py (new).

RESIDUAL: The RAISER of the SystemExit in the reporter's env is still unpinned (cannot reproduce locally; no sys.exit/os._exit callers on any ECM request path; grepped venv for interrupt_main/raise_signal — only uvicorn's own). With this guard + exit_diagnostics (0.17.6-0052), the next field occurrence becomes a logged 500 with full traceback instead of a silent death. Reporter is on v0.17.5 which predates BOTH; upgrading gets the auth RLock fix, exit diagnostics, and this containment. FOLLOW-UP recommendation: uvloop 0.22.1 has open upstream issues (segfault #706 in FastAPI-in-container, response-leak #645 under load) — consider a bead to evaluate pinning --loop asyncio.
Shipped in PR #663, merged to dev at 3b5456ad3047faa358296be56986d784488d4e39 (v0.17.6-0097). Awaiting reporter confirmation on GH #546.

title: Test coverage: CertificateStorage (tls/storage.py) — private-key handling almost entirely untested
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091) — HIGHEST-severity finding. CertificateStorage (backend/tls/storage.py, 347 lines) is almost entirely untested: only ensure_directory() and has_certificate() are covered.

Add unit tests for save_certificate/load_certificate (round-trip of cert+key bytes), parse_certificate (valid + malformed PEM), validate_pair (matching vs mismatched cert/key), get_certificate_info/is_expiring_soon, delete_certificate, and save_acme_account/load_acme_account. This is security-sensitive code (handles TLS private key material and certificate validation) with zero regression protection today. Confirmed via repo-wide grep — no other test file in backend/tests references CertificateStorage, tls.acme_client, or tls.renewal beyond a bare import-smoke-test.

SITE: backend/tests/unit/test_tls.py:161. backend/tls/storage.py handles private key material directly; 14 of 16 public methods (save/load/parse/validate_pair/delete/ACME-account persistence) have NO coverage anywhere in the suite. Add a focused CertificateStorage test suite.

title: Task-scheduler observability: log silent parent-disabled/not-registered skips + suppression reasons
description:
Task-scheduler observability: make silent skips + suppression reasons visible (parent vkktd). This is the highest-value fix — it turns a multi-hour diagnosis into a 10-second log read.

ADD LOGGING at the silent decision points:
1. task_engine.py:638 — parent-disabled skip is a silent `continue`. Add a THROTTLED DEBUG (once per task per N min to avoid per-tick spam): "child schedule for %s is due but parent task is disabled — not firing (enable the task to run)".
2. task_engine.py:631 — `if not instance: continue` (schedule in DB but task not registered — the export_publish/"in DB but not registered" case). Add a WARNING: a due schedule with no registered instance can NEVER run and is a real misconfiguration.
3. ChannelPipelineTask.should_run() suppressions (breaker / no enabled run_on_refresh rule / watermark not newer than consumed) are DEBUG-only. When a refresh watermark IS pending but the run is suppressed, surface the reason at INFO (throttled) so "why didn't matching run after refresh?" is answerable from logs.
4. routers/m3u.py:176 + tasks/m3u_refresh.py:262 — the "auto-creation picks it up on its next tick" line prints on EVERY refresh even when auto_creation is disabled. Make it conditional (or append "(auto_creation task is currently disabled — will NOT run)").

ACCEPTANCE:
- Reproduce the parent-off state; logs now contain a clear line explaining auto_creation isn't firing and why.
- No per-tick log spam (throttle verified).
- Existing task tests still pass.

title: Auto-creation matching silently never fires when parent task gate is off — invisible in logs + debug bundle
description:
Field report (2 users, 2026-07-14): "matching isn't working/executing on M3U refresh." Investigated via user debug bundle (ecm-debug-bundle-20260714-024333, ECM 0.17.6-0087, 6091 channels, 78 rules) + reproduction on dev container ecm-ecm-1.

ROOT-CAUSE MECHANISM (confirmed in code): auto-creation runs on M3U refresh via the interval-scheduled ChannelPipelineTask (task_id=auto_creation), which consumes a refresh watermark. FIRING REQUIRES BOTH: child task_schedules.enabled AND parent scheduled_tasks.enabled (task_engine.py:634-638). auto_creation is OPT-IN (default_enabled=False, channel_pipeline.py:84) so the PARENT row is seeded DISABLED; the CHILD is always seeded enabled=True (task_registry.py:373-388).

THE TRAP: when the parent is disabled, task_engine.py:638 silently `continue`s every tick — NO log at any level. The task never fires; child next_run_at stays frozen at the seed date; last_run_at stays None. Meanwhile the debug bundle exports ONLY the child table (task_schedules.json → enabled=True), so the bundle makes a gated-OFF task look ENABLED. This class of issue is INVISIBLE in both logs and the bundle — it cost a multi-hour investigation.

USER STATE (from bundle): auto_creation child enabled=True, next_run_at=2026-07-04 (frozen), last_run_at=None → parent almost certainly OFF; task has never fired. Breaker clear (auto_creation_run_on_refresh_disabled=false). User HAS 6 enabled run_on_refresh rules, so their config intent is real — they believe it's enabled (UI/bundle reads Enabled) but it never runs.

REPRODUCED on ecm-ecm-1: child-on/parent-off → 0 scheduling events, 0 logs (Step A). Enabling the parent → task fires (confirmed via live last_run + HTTP toggle test).

Children: A (scheduler observability), B (debug-bundle effective-enabled), C (UX enabled-vs-effective). See each.
close_reason: COMPLETE — all 5 children shipped and verified in dev. The class of bug (auto_creation is opt-in so the PARENT scheduled_tasks gate is seeded disabled; when off, task_engine silently skips every tick with no log, and the debug bundle exported only the child table so a gated-off task looked enabled) cannot be 'fixed' (parent-off is by design) — the goal was to make the silent failure VISIBLE, achieved: vkktd.1 scheduler observability log (task_engine.py:656-665 'parent task is disabled — not firing', throttled); vkktd.2 debug bundle exports effective (parent AND child) enabled; vkktd.3 UX no longer reads 'Enabled' when it won't run; vkktd.4 frontend effective_enabled 'enabled but won't run' warning (AutoCreationGateBanner) + reconcile; vkktd.5 MCP list_tasks shows effective_enabled. Verified in code: effective_enabled across backend routers (channel_pipeline.py, tasks.py) + frontend (api.ts, taskPillState.ts, ScheduledTasksSection, TaskStatusPill, AutoCreationGateBanner) + mcp-server/tools/tasks.py, with test_vkktd_effective_enabled.py. No residual epic-level work.

title: Event Sync never matches like events (racing streams exist in Dispatcharr but never attach)
description: User report via PO: Event Sync lets you pick master + secondary provider/groups, but it never parses/matches — streams that clearly exist (shown via a Dispatcharr search) never get matched/attached. User notes events are named similarly but have different dates/times (different racing events). Suspect: parse failure OR title-similarity scoring below threshold OR date/time handling excluding them. Separate from the m1s38 UX redesign (presentation-only). Investigate matching pipeline: parse patterns -> title score -> time/date handling -> attach threshold.
notes:
LIVE DIAGNOSIS via preview_event_sync on rule 1 (Test Sync, USA|Flo Racing master — same scenario as the user report). Result: 41 secondary streams -> 8 ATTACH (score=1.0), 0 ambiguous, 33 PARSE FAILED (reason=no_parsed_time) | 50 master channels, 45 unparsable. The matcher WORKS: every stream that carries a real event title + date/time attaches at score 1.0 (e.g. 'AMSOIL Championship Off Road @ Jul 12 9:00 AM', 'RoC Modifieds at Shangri La II @ Jul 12 3:00 PM'). The 33 failures are streams with NO date/time in the name — generic provider slots: ':Flo Racing 07', 'Flo Racing 12 :', '##### FLO RACING PPV #####', 'PBR RidePass :Flo Racing 01', 'FloRacing 24/7'. These are event-less placeholder slots; there is no event identity or time to match on -> no_parsed_time by design (documented: event_sync.md 'Nothing matches' + 'no_parsed_time' + master-as-ceiling). 45 master channels are unparsable for the same reason (Flo Racing 07-20 with no assigned event). This is NOT a matching-logic bug — it is provider data (unassigned slots) + expectation. The time-window-ignored matches that DO span different times (e.g. dt=360m on Zenith Racing @9:15AM -> master @3:15PM, score 1.0) are the intended 'same fixture, different published start time' case. LIKELY user issues: (a) expected the generic Flo Racing NN slots to match (can't — no event/time), (b) didn't see/understand the parse-failure panel. Actionable ECM options are UX-clarity or a new slot-number matching feature (risky, ti939.4 territory), NOT a matcher fix. Awaiting PO direction before any code change.
OBSERVABILITY AUDIT (PO asked what logging can prove out matching). Core matcher services/event_sync_resolver.py (635 lines) has ZERO logging — no import logging, no logger calls. It is a PURE function returning a structured EventSyncResolution: tuple[ResolvedStream] each carrying full per-candidate result — parsed title, parsed start, score, band, disposition, best master, teams verdict, time delta (dt), reject/parse-fail reason, ambiguous_reason, matched_via provenance (which relaxations admitted it) — plus unparsed_master_names. models.py matcher region: also no per-candidate logging. Executor channel_pipeline_executor.py: only COARSE logging (info/warning at run boundaries, attach caps, errors; one debug line) — NOT per-candidate. CONCLUSION: no tail-able backend DEBUG logging of matching decisions exists today. The proof lives as DATA on three surfaces: (1) preview_event_sync / POST event-sync-preview — richest, zero-write, per-candidate parse/score/dt/band/reason incl in-window rejected pairs w/ machine reason (the authoritative prove-it-out surface); (2) journal (get_journal) — live-run ATTACHES ONLY, one entry each w/ score/band/dt/team verdict/provenance (does NOT record rejects/parse-fails); (3) resolution unparsed_master_names + parse-failure reasons. Debug bundle = general pipeline data (channels/streams/stats), NOT matching detail. Log level is env-configurable (get_log_level_from_env) + runtime-settable (set_log_level). GAP/OPTION: to get tail-able per-candidate logs during real runs (incl rejects the journal omits), add logger.debug lines in event_sync_resolver.py (one structured line per candidate), gated behind LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG — small, safe, no behavior change.
DISPOSITION (PO decision 2026-07-17): working as designed — matcher attaches every stream carrying real event identity + date/time at score 1.0; the 33 non-matches are event-less provider placeholder slots (no_parsed_time by design). No code change. Reporter reply drafted and handed to PO for relay (report arrived via PO channel; no GH issue exists). Residual option if matching questions recur: per-candidate DEBUG logging in event_sync_resolver.py (see observability audit above) — not authorized, noted only.

title: Rollback/snapshot end-to-end verification + circuit-breaker coverage + manual-run gating verification (SRE ship-blocker)
description:
Verify recovery mechanisms end-to-end for event_sync runs. SRE ship-blocker: do not assume snapshots cover the new path — prove it.

**Verifications**:
1. **Snapshot/rollback round trip**: run attach -> ChannelPipelineSnapshot captured pre-mutation -> rollback_execution -> all attachments from that run removed, master channels themselves untouched (ECM never created them, rollback must not delete them). Automated test preferred; a scripted, recorded verification acceptable if the harness can't express it.
2. **Auto-sync flags**: confirm snapshot restore does NOT need to touch Dispatcharr auto_channel_sync flags in this model — Phase 1 never toggles them (guidance-only UI). Assert no code path writes group settings.
3. **Circuit breaker**: confirm the existing channel-pipeline circuit breaker covers event_sync runs (trips on repeated failures, reset works).
4. **Runbook**: add a short "Undo a bad event_sync run" section to docs/event_sync.md troubleshooting: rollback via execution id, what the journal shows, and the reminder that a deterministic matcher will repeat the bad match on the next manual run until the rule is adjusted.

**Acceptance criteria**: rollback test/verification recorded in the PR; docs updated; any gap found (e.g. snapshot missing stream-membership coverage) becomes its own bead before 1B ships.

Size: Small. Depends on: 1B resolver bead.

title: Lifecycle + idempotency + dry-run parity integration tests (refresh survival, event-end detach, ordering race, slot rename)
description:
Integration tests for the full event_sync lifecycle against a mocked Dispatcharr client. These encode the verified Dispatcharr behaviors (UUID preservation, in-place updates, master-scoped deletion) as fixtures, so a future Dispatcharr behavior change surfaces as a test-fixture conversation rather than silent production breakage.

**Required scenarios**:
1. **Idempotency**: run attach twice on unchanged data -> second run performs ZERO mutations (no duplicate attaches, no removals).
2. **Refresh survival**: simulate a master auto-sync refresh (channels updated in place, same UUIDs, names possibly tweaked) -> previously attached secondary streams remain attached; re-run performs no duplicate work.
3. **Event ends**: master channel deleted by Dispatcharr (master stream gone) -> attachments disappear with the channel; next ECM run completes with no errors and does NOT re-attach the orphaned secondary stream anywhere.
4. **Refresh-ordering race** (accepted at home-lab): new event appears in a secondary group before Dispatcharr has materialized the master channel -> stream lands in unmatched this run, attaches on the next run once the master channel exists. Assert convergence, not immediacy.
5. **Slot rename**: master channel renamed in place ("TBD vs TBD" -> real matchup, same UUID) -> re-match works against the new name; document (assert current behavior) what happens to a stream attached under the stale name.
6. **Dry-run parity**: the preview endpoint's decisions == the actual run's decisions on identical fixtures (freeze time; shared fixtures with the preview tests — parity is structural, but this test catches accidental divergence).
7. **Manual-run-only**: the unattended watermark task never executes event_sync rules.

**Acceptance criteria**: all scenarios green in pytest following docs/pytest_conventions.md; fixtures shared with preview endpoint tests where applicable; scenarios named so failures read as behavior statements.

Size: Medium. Depends on: 1B resolver bead.

title: Event-mode resolver + merge_streams attach execution + per-run attach cap + journal provenance + run summary line
description:
Implement the attach execution path.

**Executor changes** (channel_pipeline_executor.py):
- Event-mode candidate resolution as a SIBLING of _resolve_scored_fuzzy (~L3214): fetch + parse the master group's channels ONCE per run (reuse the existing _channel_by_id caching pattern), then resolve each secondary stream through services/event_sync_matcher.py. Candidates are exclusively the master group's channels (tighter scoping than the existing scored-fuzzy path, preserving the mandatory-scoping rail).
- Attach via the existing add-stream-to-channel merge internals. Idempotent by construction: stream already attached -> no-op (this is what makes stateless re-runs after every refresh safe).
- Respect band semantics from the matcher: attach band -> attach; ambiguous -> skip + count; reject/hard-reject -> skip with reason.

**Blast-radius controls** (all Phase 1 ship-blockers from SRE/security review):
- Per-run attach cap, default ~100, configurable: on overage stop attaching, WARN in the execution log, record the overage count. Rationale: the existing created-channel cap does not cover merge/attach operations.
- Journal entry per attach: category "event_sync", batch_id = execution id, secondary stream name + id, provider, master channel name + id, score, band, time delta, team-token verdict. Record NAMES alongside IDs — channel IDs go stale when events end; journal is historical audit with lazy resolution (ADR-008 §D4 precedent).
- Run summary line in the execution log: "event_sync: X attached, Y ambiguous skipped, Z unmatched, W parse failures" — this is the operator's drift detector (a silently broken parse pattern must be visible in one line within a day).
- Manual-run-only enforcement: the unattended watermark task path must exclude event_sync rules (explicit check + test).

**Acceptance criteria**: attach honors threshold + hard-reject; cap enforced with warning; journal rows complete and name-carrying; summary line present in execution log and execution record; no managed_channel_ids ever populated; unit tests for band handling, cap overage, and manual-only gating.

Size: Medium. Depends on: 1A matcher + 1A schema beads. Model note: security-sensitive merge path — Opus-class engineer agent.

title: Preview endpoint: dry-run event matching against live master channels (zero writes) + MCP wrapper
description:
Preview endpoint: run the event matcher against live data with ZERO writes. `POST /api/channel-pipeline/event-sync-preview` accepting either a saved rule id or an inline event_sync_config (so the rule editor can preview before saving).

**Behavior**:
1. Run the pre-flight check (from the schema bead): master auto-sync ON, secondaries OFF; include results in the response (do not hard-fail preview — the operator needs to see the misconfiguration).
2. Fetch the master group's channels and the secondary groups' streams from Dispatcharr.
3. Run services/event_sync_matcher.py — the EXACT resolver code path Phase 1B will use for attachment (dry-run parity by construction). No divergence permitted between preview scoring and future attach scoring.
4. Return:
   - Per-candidate rows: secondary stream raw name, provider, parsed title + parsed start time, matched master channel (name + current id), score, band (attach/ambiguous/reject), team-token verdict, time delta, reject reason where applicable.
   - Unmatched secondary streams (the master-as-ceiling visibility hedge — PO-accepted tradeoff; this list is the evidence base for any future Phase 3 promotion feature).
   - Parse failures grouped by pattern/group (a silently broken pattern must be loud here).
   - Summary counts: would-attach / ambiguous-skipped / unmatched / parse-failed. Counts must reconcile with detail rows.

**Also in scope**: an MCP tool wrapper (mcp-server/tools/, e.g. preview_event_sync) mirroring the endpoint — cheap, and lets agents/the PO exercise the matcher headlessly.

**Acceptance criteria**: deterministic output for fixed inputs; integration tests with mocked Dispatcharr client covering happy path, pre-flight failure surfacing, parse-failure surfacing, and count/detail reconciliation; endpoint documented in docs/api.md table.

Size: Small-Medium. Depends on: matcher service bead + schema bead.

title: event_sync rule kind: schema, validation, Alembic migration, engine wiring + orphan-pass bypass (no execution)
description:
Add the event_sync rule kind at the schema/persistence/engine-wiring level. NO execution path in this bead — preview-only phase.

**Migration**: one nullable Text column `event_sync_config` on `auto_creation_rules`, guarded Alembic add_column following the 0027 idempotency pattern (column-existence check before add; SQLite; no batch mode needed; clean downgrade). No new tables (PO decision: stateless recompute).

**Config shape (JSON)**: master_group_id, secondary_group_ids[], parse patterns (per-group or shared: title/time/date regexes), time_window_minutes (default 30), attach_threshold (default 0.80), enabled.

**Write-time validation** (channel_pipeline_schema.py, alongside the existing scored-fuzzy Q1/Q2 validators):
- master_group_id present; secondary_group_ids non-empty; master not in secondaries. Mandatory scoping is the rail that prevented recurrence of the 1,341-incident — schema-enforced, not convention.
- Parse regexes compile via safe_regex at save time (operator regex is the ReDoS surface; bd-ltjyx precedent).
- attach_threshold hard-clamped >= 0.80.
- Validation errors must teach (field, got, expected, doc link) — match existing validator style.

**Engine wiring (no execution)**:
- event_sync rules are excluded from per-stream Pass 1/Pass 2 rule evaluation in this phase.
- Hard-bypass Pass 4 orphan reconciliation for this rule kind: never populate managed_channel_ids, orphan_action semantics forced to none. Rationale (verified): Dispatcharr owns the master channels' lifecycle and preserves UUIDs; half-populated managed_channel_ids against Dispatcharr-owned channels would make Pass 4 reconcile channels ECM doesn't own.
- Pre-flight check helper (shared by preview now, runs later): master group has auto_channel_sync ON in Dispatcharr; secondaries have it OFF. Failures surface in results — a disabled master auto-sync is otherwise a silent whole-feature failure.

**Verified non-work, document in code comment**: NO bypass of auto_creation_exclude_auto_sync_groups is needed — secondary groups (auto-sync OFF) already pass the filter (channel_pipeline_engine.py ~L1017-1063), and the master group's streams never need to enter the pipeline (Dispatcharr already attached them). Edge to note: Dispatcharr groups are global by name (bd-dgs64, config.py ~L104-117); a secondary provider publishing the SAME group name as the master would share the group ID and be excluded — real event groups are provider-distinct-named; documented, not coded around.

**Acceptance criteria**: migration up/down clean; invalid configs rejected with teaching errors; backward-compat test loads existing pre-feature rules unchanged; unit tests for every validation branch; pre-flight helper unit-tested against mocked group settings.

Size: Medium.

title: Frozen event-name regression corpus + precision/recall CI gate (tests/fixtures/event_sync/matcher_corpus.jsonl)
description:
Build the frozen, git-tracked regression corpus that gates the matcher in CI: `tests/fixtures/event_sync/matcher_corpus.jsonl` + `tests/test_event_sync_matcher_corpus.py`.

**Corpus format**: one JSON object per line: {name_a, name_b, label, reason} where label is one of same_event / not_same / ambiguous. Names are FULL raw provider strings (with slot prefixes and time suffixes), so the corpus exercises parse + block + score end to end.

**Required trap coverage** (the cases that caused or resemble the 1,341-false-positive incident):
- Same teams, different date/time (must NOT match — time-blocking proof).
- Women's vs men's same fixture; U21/reserves variants (must NOT match).
- Replay vs live of the same fixture at different times (must NOT match).
- Abbreviation variants: Man United / MUFC / Man Utd / Manchester United (must match when same fixture+time).
- Home/away order swaps and separator variants (vs, v., @).
- Multi-sport same city + same kickoff time (must NOT match — e.g. two teams sharing a city name).
- Both observed date formats: "Mercury vs. Aces @ 11 Jul 06:00 PM ET" and "Cagliari vs. Juventus @ Jan 17 02:45 PM ET".
- Slot prefixes: "Fubo Sports Network 07 :", "Peacock 14:".
Seed real pairs from the live instance (search_streams / the group's stream listings) plus engineered traps. Start with 30-50 labeled pairs; policy: add one pair for every matcher bug ever found, never delete.

**Gate assertions**:
- Per-label band correctness (same_event -> attach band; not_same -> reject; ambiguous -> ambiguous band).
- Aggregate floors on the attach band: precision >= 97%, recall >= 85%. Gate fails the pytest run (and therefore CI / merge to dev) if floors are violated.
- Runs offline, < 5s, no network, no Dispatcharr.

**Acceptance criteria**: corpus file + gate merged; documented header comment explaining the add-only policy and label semantics; gate red/green verified by intentionally flipping one label locally (not committed).

Size: Small-Medium. Can proceed in parallel with the matcher module; the two land together.

title: Matcher service: parse → time-block → parsed-title scoring with event admission policy (services/event_sync_matcher.py)
description:
Create the isolated event-matching service: `backend/services/event_sync_matcher.py`. This is the hard part of the feature and the top product risk; it must be a pure, engine-independent module (same pattern as services/dedup_matcher.py).

**Layered matching (in order)**:
1. **Parse**: stream/channel name -> (event_title, start_datetime). Reuse dummy_epg_engine machinery (`extract_groups`, `compute_event_times`) — operator-authored regex patterns run through safe_regex against untrusted provider strings. Handle both observed date shapes: "11 Jul 06:00 PM ET" and "Jan 17 02:45 PM ET". Length-cap derived titles before they leave the module.
2. **Time-window blocking**: candidate pairs only when parsed start times are within +/- window_minutes (default 30, configurable per rule). This is candidate generation, not a safety rail.
3. **Fuzzy score of PARSED TITLES** (never raw names) via services/dedup_matcher.py RapidFuzz token_set_ratio with LOCALS cleaning.
4. **Team-token check**: split title on vs / v. / @, compare the two sides order-insensitively. Token CONFLICT (both titles parse to team pairs and the pairs clearly differ) -> HARD REJECT, score 0.0 — mirrors the M1 callsign hard-reject rail. Security holds this as non-negotiable. Token agreement raises confidence.
5. **Event admission policy**: a NEW, structurally separate branch — its own named function and its own floor constant (e.g. EVENT_ATTACH_FLOOR), NOT a reuse of allow_no_callsign / NO_CALLSIGN_FLOOR. Two different risk profiles must never share one knob (drift protection). Default auto-attach floor 0.80 (PO decision: "calibrated"), per-rule adjustable, clamped >= 0.80.

**Output**: per secondary stream, an ordered candidate result with matched master channel identity (by name/parsed identity — NEVER cache channel IDs across runs), score, band (attach / ambiguous / reject), parsed fields, team-token verdict, time delta, and machine-readable reject reasons (for the preview UI and journal).

**Acceptance criteria**:
- Pure module: no imports from channel_pipeline_engine/executor.
- Table-driven unit tests covering: DST transition edges, year inference around Dec 31/Jan 1, 12h/24h and both date formats, order-swapped teams, separator variants, hard-reject conflict cases, parse-failure fallback (no time captured -> stream is unmatchable, never guessed).
- The frozen corpus gate (sibling bead, tests/fixtures/event_sync/matcher_corpus.jsonl) passes its precision/recall floors against this module.

Size: Medium. Model note: security-sensitive matching logic — implement with Opus-class engineer agent.

title: Event Sync Phase 1B: attach path — event-mode merge execution, manual-run-only, gated on PO preview validation
description:
Turns the validated preview into actual stream attachment. An event-mode candidate resolver in the executor (sibling of _resolve_scored_fuzzy, channel_pipeline_executor.py ~L3214) consumes services/event_sync_matcher.py; attachment rides the EXISTING Pass 2 merge execution — no new engine pass (the cluster-first pre-pass design was withdrawn after the master-group reframe; each secondary stream independently resolves to at most one master channel, which is per-stream semantics Pass 2 already has).

**Gate**: this epic does not merge until the PO has reviewed Phase 1A preview quality on their real providers (that review is the whole point of preview-first phasing). Implementation work may proceed on a branch, but the merge waits for the PO's explicit go on matcher quality.

**Hard constraints**:
- Manual-run-only: event_sync rules must never fire from the unattended watermark task in this phase (auto-run is a Phase 2 explicit opt-in flag).
- Per-run attach cap (the existing created-channel cap does not cover merges).
- Journal provenance on every attach decision; run summary line in the execution log.
- ECM still never creates or deletes channels. Ambiguous band = skip + count (no review queue until Phase 2).
- Snapshot/rollback verified end-to-end before ship (SRE ship-blocker).

Size: Medium.

title: Event Sync Phase 1A: preview-only matcher — validate matching on real provider data before any write path exists
description:
Ships a complete, usable preview experience with ZERO writes to Dispatcharr. The operator can: configure an event_sync rule (master group, secondary groups, parse patterns, time window, threshold), test parse patterns against live stream names, and preview exactly which secondary streams would attach to which master channels — with scores, confidence bands, team-token verdicts, parse failures, and an unmatched-secondary-streams list.

**Why this phase exists**: it inverts the failure mode of the prior 1,341-false-positive-merge incident. The matcher is validated on the operator's real provider data BEFORE any write path exists. Phase 1B (attach) is gated on the PO reviewing preview quality.

**Hard constraints**:
- No merge_streams execution, no channel mutations, no auto-run, no apply button anywhere in the UI.
- The preview endpoint must call the SAME resolver code path 1B will use for attachment (dry-run parity by construction, not by test alone).
- Matcher lives in services/event_sync_matcher.py (isolated service module), never inline in channel_pipeline_engine.py.

**Definition of done for the epic**: operator can go from zero to a previewed rule using shipped default parse patterns without writing a regex; the frozen corpus CI gate is green; docs/event_sync.md operator walkthrough ships in the same window.

Size: Medium.

title: Event Sync: one channel per live event across providers (master auto-sync group + secondary stream attachment)
description:
## User problem
Operators with multiple IPTV providers get N duplicate channels per sports/PPV event (one per provider auto-sync group), or hand-build channels. They want ONE channel per real-world event with every provider's stream attached (failover + quality choice). Same event is named differently per provider (slot prefixes, team abbreviations, date formats), so exact matching fails.

## Decided model (team-plan 2026-07-11; supersedes the cluster-first design explored in bead enhancedchannelmanager-fcri5)
One provider's event group is designated the MASTER (reference) group: Dispatcharr `auto_channel_sync` stays ON for it, and Dispatcharr owns the FULL channel lifecycle (create/update/delete) from that group. Other providers' event groups are SECONDARY: auto-sync OFF, pure stream sources. ECM's new `event_sync` capability matches each secondary stream to a master channel — parse stream name to (event title, start time) reusing dummy-EPG machinery, then time-window blocking, then fuzzy scoring of PARSED TITLES via the unified scoring core (services/dedup_matcher.py) with a new event admission policy, then attaches the stream to the matched channel via existing merge machinery. **ECM never creates or deletes channels in this feature.**

## Verified feasibility (read from Dispatcharr source, apps/m3u/tasks.py `sync_auto_channels`)
- Channel UUIDs are preserved across refreshes (in-place updates, not recreation).
- The sync task builds its channel map from the master account's streams only and has NO code path that resets a channel's stream list — foreign (ECM-attached) streams survive refreshes.
- Channels are deleted only when the master provider drops the stream (event over); the cascade detaches secondary streams cleanly.
So the attach model works WITH Dispatcharr. Attachments persist across refreshes; the pipeline re-runs after refresh to attach streams for newly appeared events.

## PO decisions (2026-07-11)
1. **Preview-first phasing**: Phase 1A ships preview-only (zero writes); the attach path (1B) ships only after the PO validates match quality on real providers.
2. **Calibrated threshold**: default auto-attach floor 0.80 on parsed-title score, per-rule adjustable, hard-clamped >= 0.80 in schema validation.
3. **Team-token conflict = hard reject** (score 0.0, mirrors the M1 callsign rail). Non-negotiable (security).
4. **Master-as-ceiling accepted**: events carried only by secondary providers get no channel. Hedge: every preview/run reports unmatched secondary streams so real data can justify (or kill) a Phase 3 promotion feature.
5. **Stateless recompute**: NO new tables. Durable state = one nullable JSON config column on auto_creation_rules + journal provenance rows. Never persist or cache channel IDs across runs — master channels are the identity anchor.
6. **Orphan bypass**: event_sync rules never populate managed_channel_ids and hard-bypass Pass 4 orphan reconciliation (Dispatcharr owns lifecycle).
7. **Manual-run-only** until Phase 2's explicit opt-in auto-run flag.

## Key constraints for all child work
- Matcher logic lives in an isolated service module, NOT inline in the 4,100-line engine.
- Wrong attachments are reversible and non-compounding but NOT self-healing — deterministic matcher repeats a bad match until the operator adjusts a pattern/threshold or the provider renames. Docs must say this verbatim.
- The prior fuzzy-matching incident (1,341 false-POSITIVE merges) is the trust benchmark: precision over recall everywhere; frozen regression corpus gates CI.
- Any state that must survive refreshes (Phase 2 review decisions, exclusions) keys on content fingerprints / event identity, never channel/stream IDs.
- Effective tier: home-lab. No SLOs, no ADR file for this feature (rationale lives in docs/event_sync.md + code comments).

Overall size: Medium (reduced from Large by the master-group reframe).

title: Find Duplicates: scope to selected channels + merge-blind safety net + list virtualization
description: From triage q4yr3, PO decisions 2026-07-10: scope = checkbox-selected channels; fix now. (1) Backend: optional channel_ids (list) param on POST /api/channels/find-duplicates (channels.py:2697, filter the scan loop :2711-2726); absent = global (backward compatible). (2) Frontend: ChannelsPane onFindDuplicates passes the selected channel ids; api.findDuplicateChannels(channelIds?) sends them; FindDuplicatesModal displays the scope ('Scanned N selected channels' vs global). (3) Safety net regardless of scope: disable Merge button when groups.length>0 but zero rows have rendered (defensive check), and add content-visibility:auto virtualization to .dup-group-list matching ChannelsPane.css:1585 pattern so 985-group results paint. (4) MCP parity: find_duplicate_channels tool gets the channel_ids param. (5) Tests: FindDuplicatesModal render-assertion tests at nontrivial scale (50-100 synthetic groups) + backend scope-filter tests + MCP pass-through. Size: Small-Medium. Merge-blind risk documented in q4yr3 — user could merge 985 groups sight-unseen.

title: UX C2: Channel/stream group rows not keyboard-focusable — expand/collapse is mouse-only
description: From UX assessment (vr0y7). Channel Manager group-row headers are generic [cursor=pointer] divs, not buttons; Tab order skips them (verified: focus jumps from 'tune' filter button straight to 'speed' probe button inside a row). title: Bug [CRITICAL]: stop_processing action breaks the whole Pass 2 loop — only 1 stream processed (gh #225)
description: GH #225 (reporter Koalamanx). auto_creation_engine.py Pass 2 (the 'for stream, winning_rule, losing_rules, stream_rules_log in sorted_entries' loop, ~line 1225): each iteration executes the winning rule's actions on one stream; if any action is STOP_PROCESSING, stop_processing=True; at end of the per-stream block (~line 1364-1365) 'if stop_processing: break' — this break exits the ENTIRE sorted_entries loop, so the first stream whose winning rule has a stop_processing action ends Pass 2 for all remaining streams → streams_matched=1 every run. CONFIRMED in code; reporter's diagnosis exact. Note: Pass 1 already resolves one winning rule per stream and has its own per-stream short-circuit (rule.stop_on_first_match → break the per-stream rule loop, ~line 1111). The STOP_PROCESSING *action* in Pass 2 has no remaining rules to stop (one winning rule per stream) — so its only legit meaning is 'don't keep processing THIS stream' i.e. continue to next stream, OR it's a Pass-1 concept mis-applied. Fix candidates: (a) break → continue; (b) drop the Pass-2 stop_processing handling entirely (treat STOP_PROCESSING as a Pass-1-only thing); needs a small design call on intended semantics, then a tiny code change + a regression test (rule with stop_processing action + 50 matching streams → all processed). Severity: P1 — niche feature (stop_processing action) silently broken when used; workaround: use rule.stop_on_first_match=True instead. Same reporter as #221-224, #226.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.16.0-0079 (PR #233) — Pass 2 stop_processing break→continue + regression test (12 streams). GH #225 commented & closed below.

title: Stats tab broken with React error 185 (infinite re-render) after heatmap work
description:
ROOT CAUSE: recharts 3.x is incompatible with React 19. Recharts 3.x uses react-redux + @reduxjs/toolkit internally. Under React 19's stricter concurrent rendering, recharts' YAxis -> RenderedTicksReporter useEffect dispatches setRenderedTicks with a fresh ticks array reference every render, causing an infinite re-render loop.

TIMELINE:
- 2026-04-16 (62ea5c5f): recharts 3.7.0 -> 3.8.1 (introduced RenderedTicksReporter)
- 2026-04-24 (ca6e5019): React 18.3.1 -> 19.2.5 <- actual trigger; broke Stats tab
- 2026-04-25 (571b2e85): heatmap commit (purely additive, NOT the cause)

FIX: pin recharts to 2.15.4 (latest 2.x; supports React 19 in peerDeps; pre-dates the redux refactor).

VERIFICATION: 110 stats panel tests pass; tsc clean; container browser test confirms 0 console errors and both charts render.

title: ADR-005 Phase 4: Canary observation window for CodeQL delta-zero enforcement (first 10 PRs)
description:
Per ADR-005 (docs/adr/ADR-005-code-security-gating-strategy.md) Section 'Sequencing & Rollout' Step 4 (Week 3 — canary observation window).

Phase 3b enforcement shipped via PR #108 (merge commit e20d5f6, 2026-04-22). The first 10 PRs to land under enforcement are the canary. Observe for the following NUMERIC ROLLBACK TRIGGERS — fall back via Soft Exit if ANY fire:

1. **>=3 false-positive dismissals across distinct PRs** — indicates either a noisy rule or a systemic sanitizer pattern CodeQL doesn't understand. Investigate before continuing enforcement.
2. **Any single PR blocked >24 hours** on a CodeQL finding subsequently classified as false-positive or a correctly dismissed test-only sink.
3. **CodeQL runner time exceeds 8 minutes** (matrix-wide wall clock) on any single run — indicates quota or scan-size pathology outside ADR-005's tunable parameters.

Exceeding any threshold REVOKES Phase 3b enforcement (revert to Phase 1 advisory — drop the workflow polling step) pending root-cause investigation. Phase 1 (signal-on) remains in place; the signal is still cheap value. Explicit PO re-approval required to re-enable enforcement after rollback.

## Tracking method

Maintain an observation log in this bead's notes:
- PR # | merge date | CodeQL outcome | dismissals (rule, justification, dismisser) | wall-clock time
- Updated as each canary PR merges.

Track via: gh api repos/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/code-scanning/alerts (dismissal log) + GitHub Actions run history for codeql-analysis job timings.

## Acceptance

- 10 PRs observed under Phase 3b enforcement after PR #108 merge (2026-04-22).
- Observation log filled per PR.
- One of:
  (a) All thresholds clear -> close bead, ADR-005 moves Proposed -> Accepted, file first monthly dismissal-log audit bead (Phase 5).
  (b) Threshold exceeded -> file rollback bead, escalate to PO with the trigger evidence.

## Counter starts: PR #108 merge (2026-04-22).

Related:
- enhancedchannelmanager-kgjci (parent — ADR-005 implementation tracker)
- enhancedchannelmanager-sm3n3 (ADR-005 itself)
- ADR-005 'Sequencing & Rollout' (docs/adr/ADR-005-code-security-gating-strategy.md)
close_reason: Outcome A: canary complete + clear. 10 of 10 canary PRs observed (#107, #109, #110, #111, #112, #114, #115, #116, #117, #118). All three numeric rollback triggers PASS: 0 distinct-PR FP dismissals on enforcement-relevant (HIGH/CRITICAL) alerts (4 in-window dismissals were note-severity on alembic file from a single PR, later resolved by config exclusion in PR #137); 0 PRs blocked >24h (longest creation-to-merge ~45 min); max matrix wall-clock 2m24s vs 8m threshold (70% headroom). Phase 3b enforcement remains active. ADR-005 status already reads Accepted. Phase 5 first-monthly dismissal-log audit tracked under bead o8t26. Full observation log in comment.

title: Journal table retention + missing batch_id/entity indexes (post bd-91mcq)
description:
Per DBA standup finding 2026-04-23: bd-91mcq added per-entity journal rows with shared batch_id, but journal_entries has zero index on batch_id and no composite (entity_type, entity_id, timestamp DESC). Also no retention policy in backend/tasks/cleanup.py for this table; bulk operations now amplify row growth N-fold with no upper bound.

Confirmed gaps:
- backend/models.py:35-37 — JournalEntry has indexes only on timestamp DESC, category, action_type
- backend/alembic/versions/20260420_2034_0001_baseline_initial_schema.py:248,252-254 — baseline DDL confirms missing indexes
- backend/tasks/cleanup.py — no journal retention defined

Scope:
1. Alembic migration adding idx_journal_batch_id and idx_journal_entity (entity_type, entity_id, timestamp DESC)
2. Define retention policy (proposal: 90d hot retention, then archive-or-drop) wired into backend/tasks/cleanup.py
3. Backfill plan if production journal_entries is already large (concurrent CREATE INDEX, batched DELETE)

User value: forensic audit queries ("show me batch X" / "history for rule N") stay sub-second as journal volume grows; bulk operations don't silently bloat the table without bound.

Success signal: explain analyze on representative batch-id and entity-history queries shows index usage; cleanup.py retention test proves rows older than threshold are pruned; migration runs cleanly on 5M-row test fixture.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: PR #99 introduced POST /api/auto-creation/rules/bulk-update. The single-rule PUT path calls _lint_auto_creation_rule_request(...) to reject catastrophic-backtracking patterns in sort_regex (and conditions/actions) — this is the gate added by bd-eio04.7 safe_regex work. The bulk endpoint does NOT call the linter, even though BulkUpdateAutoCreationRulesRequest inherits sort_regex and _apply_rule_scalar_updates applies it. A caller can plant a ReDoS pattern on up to 500 rules per request that the PUT would reject. Fix: call _lint_auto_creation_rule_request(scalar_update.conditions, scalar_update.actions, scalar_update.sort_regex) once before the rule loop in bulk_update_auto_creation_rules (backend/routers/auto_creation.py ~L420). Add a regression test that mirrors the single-rule lint-bypass test: POST with a known-bad pattern -> assert 422. Fix-forward PR tracked separately; not a block on #99.

title: v0.16.0-0051: auto-creation Bad Gateway + execution history refresh
description:
Root cause: bd-w3z4h introduced a 30s request-timeout middleware in backend/main.py with _TIMEOUT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES = (stream-preview, ffmpeg, tasks, backup). /api/auto-creation/ was not exempt, so pipeline runs exceeding 30s returned 504 Gateway Timeout client-side. Work continued server-side (engine commits as it progresses via run_cpu_bound thread pool), which is why execution history showed up after browser refresh but not in-session (frontend runPipeline only calls fetchExecutions inside the try block — 504 falls into catch).

Fix (this bead): add '/api/auto-creation/' to _TIMEOUT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES in backend/main.py. One-line change, matches the pattern of /api/tasks/ and /api/backup/ which also cover both CRUD and long-running operations under one prefix.

Follow-up (separate bead bd-enfsy, P2): convert /run endpoints to 202 + poll background-task pattern, then remove the exempt prefix to restore defense-in-depth on auto-creation CRUD. Also fix useAutoCreationExecution.runPipeline to call fetchExecutions() in a finally block.

Verified in container: docker cp + docker restart ecm-ecm-1 succeeded, /api/health returns 200, grep on deployed /app/main.py confirms new prefix present. Middleware integration tests (test_event_loop_responsiveness.py) still pass. Full backend suite: 2937 passed, 8 pre-existing alembic env failures unrelated.

title: Audit sync CPU work in async handlers; thread-pool wrapper + uvicorn concurrency limits
description:
Backlog — discovered during ReDoS spike on GH #104. Not part of normalization-parity epic; general operational weakness.

SRE finding: ECM deploys uvicorn with 1 worker, no --limit-concurrency, no request-timeout middleware, no reverse proxy, and NormalizationEngine.normalize() is a plain sync method called directly inside async FastAPI handlers. Any CPU-heavy sync work blocks the single-worker event loop for every concurrent request.

Scope:
- Audit all async handlers for sync CPU work (regex-heavy, tight loops, large JSON parsing).
- Wrap identified callsites with asyncio.to_thread or run_in_executor so offending requests only block a thread, not the event loop.
- Add uvicorn --limit-concurrency bound in backend/entrypoint.sh:244.
- Consider slowapi rate limits on /api/normalization/* and /api/auto-creation/*.
- Add [SLOW-REQUEST] counter metric; SLO review.

Reference files:
- backend/entrypoint.sh:244 (uvicorn invocation)
- backend/main.py:179-472 (middleware stack — no request-timeout)
- backend/auth/routes.py:46 (slowapi wired but only on two login endpoints)
- backend/normalization_engine.py:865 (sync normalize in async context)

- `backend/routers/normalization.py` (+44/-28): `run_cpu_bound` on `/test`, `/test-batch`, `/normalize`, `/rule-stats` rule×stream loop; `@limiter.limit("30/minute")` on `/test-batch`
- `backend/routers/channels.py` (+7/-4): `run_cpu_bound` on both `engine.normalize()` sites (POST /channels, POST /channels/bulk createChannel)
- `backend/routers/dummy_epg.py` (+22/-13): `run_cpu_bound` on /preview, /preview/batch, /xmltv (×3 generate_xmltv sites), /generate (×2 sites)
- `backend/routers/auto_creation.py` (+4/-2): `run_cpu_bound` on /validate

Net: 10 source files, +128/-25 diff to existing files, +579 new lines.

### Test output
Full suite (`cd backend && python -m pytest tests/ --tb=short --no-header -p no:warnings`): **2278 passed in 46.35s**. No regressions.

Targeted bd-w3z4h tests:
- `tests/unit/test_concurrency.py` — 11 passed (includes `test_does_not_block_event_loop`)
- `tests/integration/test_event_loop_responsiveness.py` — 4 passed

TDD verification: stubbed `run_cpu_bound` to run inline → `test_health_under_500ms_while_normalize_batch_runs` correctly fails with `/api/health took 0.803s` (matches the 800ms blocker). Confirms the test actually exercises event-loop responsiveness and isn't a pass-by-coincidence.

### Container healthcheck verification
Deployed to ecm-ecm-1, restarted. After ~36s the healthcheck reports `(healthy)`. `/proc/1/cmdline` inspection confirms:
```
/usr/local/bin/python /usr/local/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6100 --limit-concurrency 100 --timeout-keep-alive 30
```
`curl http://localhost:6100/api/health` returns in ~18ms, well under the 10s HEALTHCHECK timeout.

### Scope changes / deferred
- No scope split needed — 13 offending call sites, under the 20-site cutoff.
- slowapi rate limit: only applied `@limiter.limit("30/minute")` to `/test-batch`. Bead mentioned also applying to `apply-to-channels`, which doesn't exist as an endpoint in current code (bd-eio04.2 frontend reuses bulk/createChannel). Flagging for bd-eio04.12 scope.
- XMLTV endpoints (`/api/dummy-epg/xmltv*`) offloaded but NOT exempted from the 30s timeout. Large catalogs may still see 504. Follow-up recommendation (not blocking this bead): move XMLTV generation to a background task that writes to the cache; endpoint reads cached blob only. Documented in runbook.
- The two channels.py `engine.normalize()` sites referenced in the spec at L287/L1363 are at current L278/L1350 (file now 1972 lines, not 2034 — recent churn). The third site at L2034 doesn't exist — appears to have been removed by earlier work. Verified via grep: only 2 `engine.normalize(` occurrences in routers/channels.py, both offloaded.

### Ready to ship?
Awaiting user signal. All quality gates green: compile, unit, integration, full suite, container healthy, runbook written.

title: NFC Unicode normalization in _match_single_condition and convert_superscripts
description:

title: GH-104: apply normalization rules to existing channels on refresh/rebuild (P1 bug)
description:
# GH-104: Normalization rules don't apply to existing channels

**Source**: GitHub issue #104 filed by @MotWakorb 2026-04-22 00:08 UTC on ECM v0.16.0-0040
**Debug bundle**: https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26950164/ecm-debug-bundle-20260421-234006.tar.gz

## Symptom
Channel Normalisation rules (regex replace) work at channel-creation time but do NOT apply retroactively to existing channels or during refresh/reconciliation. Reporter added rule `(ᴿᴬᵂ|RAW|UHD|FHD|HD|4K|1080P|720P) → ""` and validated via "Test Rules" that "PROSIEBEN ᴿᴬᵂ" normalizes to "PROSIEBEN". But existing channel "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" remains untouched, creating duplicate channels "RTL" + "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ".

## Verdict
**Bug / feature gap, not expected-by-design.** The rename-existing code path exists in the auto-creation executor but only fires under very narrow conditions that don't cover the reporter's scenario.

## Root cause

1. **Normalization is invoked ONLY from the auto-creation `create_channel` action**
   - `backend/auto_creation_executor.py:482-493` — normalization applied to the new channel name during rule execution
   - `backend/auto_creation_executor.py:532-555` — existing-channel rename happens ONLY when `_find_channel_by_name(normalized_name)` returns an existing channel AND its stored `existing_core` differs from `channel_name` (specifically handles the number-prefix case like "107 | RTL ᴿᴬᵂ")
   - When the stored name is "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" and no "RTL" channel exists yet, the lookup at line 514 misses and we fall through to create a brand-new "RTL" channel. The original "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" is never touched.

2. **Refresh path only runs rules with `run_on_refresh=True`**
   - `backend/tasks/auto_creation.py:205-244` — `run_auto_creation_after_refresh()` filters to `AutoCreationRule.run_on_refresh == True` only
   - `backend/models.py:1424` — `run_on_refresh` defaults to `False`, so most users' rules are never re-run on refresh
   - Even for rules with `run_on_refresh=True`, the pipeline re-evaluates all streams (not existing channels), so it still hits the same gap above

3. **No other entry point re-applies normalization**
   - `backend/routers/normalization.py` exposes only test/migrate/import/export endpoints — no "apply to existing channels" action
   - `backend/routers/channels.py` merge endpoints (`POST /channels/merge`, `POST /channels/bulk-merge` at lines 1745, 2083) are fully manual — user picks channels and target name, no normalization involvement
   - No task in `backend/tasks/` iterates existing channels against normalization rules
   - `run_on_refresh` only runs the auto-creation pipeline — that pipeline is stream-driven, not channel-driven

## Normalization engine architecture (brief)
- `backend/normalization_engine.py` — `NormalizationEngine` class, loads `NormalizationRuleGroup`+`NormalizationRule` from DB, applies rules multi-pass with superscript conversion. Pure text-in/text-out; no channel awareness.
- `NormalizationEngine.normalize(name, group_ids, preserve_superscripts)` — entry point
- `NormalizationEngine.test_rule(...)` at line 1143 — the "Test Rules" UI endpoint. Works correctly because it applies rules to arbitrary text — exactly what reporter confirmed.
- `NormalizationEngine.extract_core_name(name)` at line 1014 — used by `merge_streams` action for reconciliation lookups; already iterates existing channels at executor init (`auto_creation_executor.py:190-225`) to build a `_normalized_name_to_channel` and `_core_name_to_channel` map. **Proof the engine CAN be applied to existing channel names — it's just not used to rename them.**

## Why refresh/reconciliation doesn't apply normalization today
The engine was designed as a stream-name → channel-name transform on creation, not as a channel-maintenance pass. The reporter's hypothesis is correct:
> "normalisation is only applied at channel creation time, not during reconciliation or refresh."

Refresh fetches new streams from the M3U provider and runs auto-creation rules, but auto-creation iterates **streams**, not **channels**. An existing "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" channel is invisible to the rule engine — only "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" streams are evaluated, and they match against the existing channel by exact name (`_find_channel_by_name`), so they get re-attached and nothing gets renamed.

## Fix direction comparison

**Option A — Re-normalize existing channels on refresh** (automatic, opt-in)
- New channel-iteration pass after M3U refresh (or after rule save): for each existing channel, apply enabled normalization groups, rename if result differs and no collision
- Effort: **M** (1-2 days) — new pass in `auto_creation_engine.py` or a standalone task; needs collision handling (see below)
- Pro: invisible to user, "just works"
- Con: silently renames channels, hard to undo; needs dry-run preview

**Option B — Auto-merge channels with matching normalized names** (automatic or dedup-driven)
- On refresh or via new action: find all pairs of channels where `normalize(A.name) == normalize(B.name)`, offer merge
- Effort: **L** (3-5 days) — this is a dedup feature, not a rename feature; needs UI for conflict resolution (which streams go where, which metadata wins)
- Pro: solves duplicate problem at the symptom level
- Con: bigger scope, touches merge engine; still leaves renamed-but-collision-free cases unaddressed

**Option C — "Force re-normalize existing channels" action/button** (manual, safe)
- New `POST /api/normalization/apply-to-channels` endpoint that walks all channels, applies rules, returns a preview diff; user confirms, endpoint executes renames + optional merges
- Effort: **S-M** (1-2 days for the preview+execute backend; +1 day for the settings-page UI button/modal)
- Pro: user-initiated, explicit, includes dry-run preview, easy to undo (journal already logs renames)
- Con: manual step — if user forgets, they keep accumulating duplicates

## Data-integrity considerations

When retroactively renaming "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" → "RTL":
1. **No existing "RTL"** → safe rename (single `update_channel`). Journal entry via existing `channel:rename` pattern.
2. **"RTL" already exists** → collision. Three policies possible:
   - **Skip** (don't rename, flag in preview) — safest default
   - **Merge** — move all streams from "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" into "RTL", delete the ᴿᴬᵂ channel. Reuses existing `merge_channels` logic. Needs decision on metadata precedence (channel_number, logo_id, epg_data_id, stream_profile_id).
   - **Append suffix** — rename to "RTL (2)" (bad UX, just defers the problem)
3. **Group mismatch** — "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" and "RTL" may be in different groups. Merge should respect/prompt on target group.
4. **Channel number prefix handling** — existing rename code at `auto_creation_executor.py:535-547` already preserves the "107 | " prefix; a channel-sweep should reuse this pattern.
5. **Streams already assigned** — collision merge must dedupe streams by ID (existing `merge_channels` already does this via `seen_streams`).
6. **Active viewers / sessions** — renaming a live channel may disrupt playback; recommend warning or schedule-during-off-hours (probably out of scope for v1).

## Related UX surfaces

If Option C ships, UI surface is likely **Settings → Normalization Rules → new button**: "Apply to existing channels". Modal shows:
- Current name → normalized name (diff list, only non-empty diffs)
- Collision flag per row (icon + "matches existing channel 'X'")
- Per-row action: Rename / Merge into existing / Skip
- Bulk "accept all non-colliding" button
- Execute button → journal entries + toast

If Option A ships, UI surface is a settings toggle ("Auto-normalize channels on refresh") and a post-refresh notification showing N channels renamed.

## Reporter's 3 asks — mapping to options
1. "Existing channels re-normalized on refresh/rebuild" → Option A
2. "Auto-merge of channels with matching normalized names" → Option B
3. "A 'force re-normalize existing channels' action/button" → Option C

## Recommended direction
**Option C first**, with Option A as a follow-up toggle.

Rationale:
- Option C is the smallest safe change, exposes the diff to the user before mutating anything (matches project conventions — see merge_streams prune `dry_run` pattern)
- Reuses existing `NormalizationEngine.normalize()`, `extract_core_name()`, and the rename/merge code paths in `auto_creation_executor.py:532-555` and `routers/channels.py:merge_channels`
- Lets us discover edge cases (collisions, group mismatches, unicode oddities) on user-initiated runs before making it automatic
- Once stable, Option A becomes "run Option C's execute path on M3U refresh" with a settings toggle

Option B (auto-merge) is not recommended as the first delivery — merging semantics vary (which logo/EPG wins?) and conflating normalization with dedup will confuse users. Leave the existing manual merge UI alone for now.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed — PO to refine)
- [ ] New endpoint `POST /api/normalization/apply-to-channels` with `dry_run: bool` returning per-channel diff + collision flags
- [ ] Execute path renames non-colliding, optionally merges colliding (per-row `action` param), writes journal entries
- [ ] Settings page button + modal showing diff, enables user to accept/reject per row or in bulk
- [ ] Unit tests: normalization application, collision detection, merge-on-collision
- [ ] Integration test: seed DB with "RTL ᴿᴬᵂ" + apply rules + assert renamed to "RTL"
- [ ] No regression: existing `_execute_create_channel` rename path (line 532-555) still works on new-channel creation

## Unexpected findings
- The executor already builds `_normalized_name_to_channel` and `_core_name_to_channel` maps for every run (`auto_creation_executor.py:190-225`), so the cost of iterating channels through normalization is already paid on every auto-creation pipeline run — we just never **write back** the normalized names. Reusing this index for Option C is almost free.
- `run_on_refresh` defaults to `False` (`models.py:1424`). Even users who **have** enabled normalization don't get the existing-channel rename path (line 532-555) triggered on refresh unless they also flip this flag per rule. This is a UX trap — consider surfacing it in the normalization settings (out of scope here, but worth noting).
- GH-92 (`enhancedchannelmanager-r9mtd`) — "separate-not-merge option" — is related conceptually (both touch auto-creation name handling) but solves the inverse problem (user wants explicit separation, not auto-merge). No shared code-change surface expected.

**Do NOT close this bead.** Investigation only — PO reviews findings, picks a direction, then spawn fix bead(s).
notes: 2026-04-22: PO picked combined scope (Option A from revised recommendation) = Option C (force-re-normalize button + dry-run preview + backend endpoint) PLUS the lookup fix at backend/auto_creation_executor.py:514 to consult the already-built _normalized_name_to_channel map. Rationale: Option C alone cleans existing duplicates but doesn't prevent future ones; the lookup fix is 'almost free' (map already built) and prevents new duplicates at creation time. Together = 'just works' without needing Option A's (auto-on-refresh) automation. Delegated to project-engineer subagent 2026-04-22. PO directive: 'do it right away.'

title: security: add XSS regression test for print-guide title (CodeQL 1360)
description:
CodeQL alert 1360 flags py/reflected-xss in the /api/export/print-guide endpoint for the channel/guide title field.

Technical status: FALSE POSITIVE — _escape_html is in fact applied at backend/routers/export.py:1235 before the title renders into the HTML response. CodeQL's dataflow does not appear to trace the escape call.

Why a bead exists instead of a direct dismissal:
ADR-005 Phase 1 policy requires a regression test that PROVES the sanitizer fires before dismissing any reflected-XSS alert. We cannot dismiss 1360 without landing the test first.

Task scope:
1. Add regression test to backend/tests/routers/test_export.py:
   - Payload: title containing <script>alert(1)</script> plus quote/angle-bracket variants
   - Assertion: response body contains <script> (or equivalent entity-encoded form) and does NOT contain raw <script>
   - Assertion: _escape_html is called on the title field (can mock/spy or just assert on rendered HTML)
2. After test lands and passes in CI, dismiss alert 1360 as 'false positive' with dismissal comment citing the test file path + line number.

Secondary concern (PO DECISION REQUIRED, NOT IN SCOPE OF THIS BEAD):
/api/export/print-guide endpoint has NO auth dependency — no RequireAdminIfEnabled. Combined with reflected output of user-supplied fields, this creates a CSRF/XSS angle should the sanitizer ever regress (attacker could craft a link that an authenticated admin clicks and exfiltrates session). Recommendation: add RequireAdminIfEnabled to this endpoint. Flagging explicitly; will NOT do this in this bead unless PO approves.

Acceptance criteria:
- New test lands in backend/tests/routers/test_export.py, named e.g. test_print_guide_escapes_title_xss
- Test passes in CI
- CodeQL alert 1360 dismissed with reason=false positive and dismissal comment referencing test path:line
- PO decision on the auth side-item recorded (separate follow-up if approved)

References:
- CodeQL alert 1360 (py/reflected-xss)
- backend/routers/export.py:1235 (sanitizer location)
- ADR-005 Phase 1 policy (test-before-dismiss for XSS)

File a separate bead for mechanical automation of G1a + G1b + G5 + G6 + G7 via a GitHub Action on release-cut PRs. Requires bd available in CI for G1a. Deferred — Phase 1 manual verification is acceptance-sufficient.

title: Implement ADR-005: CodeQL gating on PR-to-dev + merge protection rules
description:
Implementation of ADR-005 (docs/adr/ADR-005-code-security-gating-strategy.md).

Three changes, all small, but must land in the sequence the ADR specifies (W1 → W2 mid → W2 end → W3 canary). DO NOT collapse into a single PR — the sequencing is load-bearing.

## Phase 1 (W1) — unblocked now
