title: FLAKE: TestTraceIdMiddleware fails under certain test ordering (tp681 baseline)
description:
Surfaced by tp681 flake audit 2026-04-20. 2 tests fail non-deterministically depending on test ordering:

- tests/routers/test_observability_middleware.py::TestTraceIdMiddleware::test_trace_id_appears_in_log_line
- tests/routers/test_observability_middleware.py::TestTraceIdMiddleware::test_generated_trace_id_matches_uuidv4_format_in_logs

Reproduction: 
- PASS in isolation: pytest tests/routers/test_observability_middleware.py
- PASS with adjacent file: pytest tests/unit/test_observability.py tests/routers/test_observability_middleware.py (either order)
- FAIL when preceded by the second half of tests/integration/ (test_api_tags through test_router_registration): pytest tests/integration/test_api_tags.py ... tests/routers/test_observability_middleware.py

Likely root cause: contextvar/logging-handler state from an integration test leaks. The capture_json_logs fixture in test_observability_middleware.py builds a StringIO handler; the middleware emits via _access_log.info (the 'ecm.access' named logger). One of the integration tests likely:
- Removes handlers from the root logger
- Calls install_json_logging with side effects that stack filters
- Leaks a trace_id contextvar token that makes the request-scoped set_trace_id return the wrong value

Symptom: 'no log record carried trace_id=trace-log-check-42' OR 'no log records carried a non-sentinel trace id'. The middleware's _access_log.info call is not producing a record that makes it into the capture buffer.

Mitigation (temporary): pass --deselect for these two tests when running full BE suite in the container. Documented in docs/testing.md flake-policy section.

Fix approach (ordered cheapest first):
1. Make the capture_json_logs fixture attach the handler to 'ecm.access' directly (not root) — eliminate the propagation dependency.
2. Add an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py that re-runs observability.install_observability() after each test, so state is always fresh.
3. Audit integration tests that touch logging and scope their changes.

Acceptance:
- Full BE suite (pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e) passes 3 consecutive times in ecm-ecm-1 WITHOUT --deselect for these 2 tests.
- Root cause identified and documented in the test module's docstring.
acceptance_criteria: 3 consecutive BE full-suite greens in ecm-ecm-1 without deselections; root cause documented
close_reason: Resolved by PR #87 (mcnj0). Same root cause as the order-dependent trace_id flake QA identified in tp681 audit: backend/alembic/env.py fileConfig() without disable_existing_loggers=False was disabling ecm.access logger and pinning root level to WARNING. DBA fix scopes fileConfig to standalone alembic CLI case only; embedded invocation from main.py retains JSON handler + trace-id filter + root level. No separate PR needed.

title: Remediate py/path-injection in backend/routers/backup.py (CodeQL alerts 1416-1419)
description:
## Context
GitHub CodeQL Default Setup (enabled via PR #82's workflow additions) flagged 4 HIGH-severity py/path-injection errors in backend/routers/backup.py:
- Alert 1416 — line 1165 (Path.exists() in download_saved_backup)
- Alert 1417 — line 1167 (Path.read_text() in download_saved_backup)
- Alert 1418 — line 1181 (Path.exists() in delete_saved_backup)
- Alert 1419 — line 1183 (Path.unlink() in delete_saved_backup)

CWE-22/23/36/73/99. Source: 'filename' URL path parameter. Sink: Path operations under BACKUPS_DIR (= CONFIG_DIR/'backups').

## Exploitability Assessment — effective risk LOW
1. Both endpoints gated by RequireAdminIfEnabled (admin-only when auth is enabled)
2. Existing sanitization: strict regex allowlist at lines 1162/1178:
     _BACKUP_FILENAME_RE = re.compile(r'^ecm-backup-\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{6}\.yaml$')
   This anchored regex permits only: literal 'ecm-backup-' prefix, digits/hyphens/underscore in a fixed YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS shape, literal '.yaml' suffix. No '/', no '..', no backslash, no null bytes, no absolute paths.
3. CodeQL flags this because its dataflow tracker cannot symbolically prove the regex constrains the value; this is a known SAST limitation with anchored-regex validators.
4. No concrete exploit path exists with current code. Confirmed false-positive modulo regex bypass (none identified).

Rating: CVSS-adapted Low (1.8) — auth-gated + hardened allowlist, no path traversal possible, theoretical-only risk.

## Remediation (fix shape — do NOT rush; get it right)
Belt-and-suspenders canonicalization + containment. Match the pattern already established in commit a591105c ('Harden zip backup path validation with canonicalization (OWASP A03)'):

  import os
  safe_root = BACKUPS_DIR.resolve()
  candidate = (BACKUPS_DIR / filename).resolve()
  try:
      candidate.relative_to(safe_root)
  except ValueError:
      raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='Invalid filename')

This closes the CodeQL finding by making containment explicit and defense-in-depth against future regex regressions. Apply to BOTH download_saved_backup (lines 1159-1172) AND delete_saved_backup (lines 1175-1185).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Canonicalization + containment check added to download_saved_backup and delete_saved_backup
- [ ] CodeQL alerts 1416, 1417, 1418, 1419 closed on next scan (or dismissed-with-justification and 'won't fix' dismissal comment citing regex + auth if team prefers; preferred path is FIX not DISMISS)
- [ ] Unit tests in backend/tests/routers/test_backup.py cover:
      * '../' traversal attempt returns 400
      * Absolute path attempt ('/etc/passwd') returns 400
      * Symlink-escape attempt (if feasible in test fixture) returns 400
      * Valid filename still works end-to-end
- [ ] docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md updated with a note on backup.py path-handling controls (short addendum)
- [ ] No regression in existing backup tests (2447+ BE tests stay green)

## Related
- Existing hardening precedent: commit a591105c ('Harden zip backup path validation with canonicalization')
- Threat model: docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md (backup.py is DBAS-adjacent)
- Triage bead: enhancedchannelmanager-rbmkt
- PR #82 surfaced these findings (CodeQL Default Setup enablement)
- Similar patterns exist in backend/routers/export.py (lines 397/408/433/444) and backend/export_manager.py (lines 87/89) — filed separately if prioritized.

Labels: security, codeql, path-traversal

title: ADR-005: Code security gating strategy (CodeQL delta-zero on PR-to-dev + PR-to-main)
description:
Architectural follow-on to ADR-001 and PR #82. ADR-001 scoped its PR-to-dev validation gate to DEPENDENCY UPGRADES only (paths-filter on manifest files). It does NOT gate general code-security findings at PR time. PR #82 exposed this gap: 4 HIGH-severity py/path-injection alerts landed on dev (and were only surfaced when the PR-to-main aggregation check ran).

Architectural question: should the CodeQL-delta gate be extended beyond dep-bump PRs to cover ALL PRs that touch Python/JS source?

ADR must cover:
- Problem: current custom CodeQL (.github/workflows/build.yml) only runs on push to main/dev and PR-to-main. PR-to-dev has no CodeQL signal. New HIGH-severity findings can land on dev and only surface on the next dev->main promotion attempt (as they did for PR #82).
- Options:
  (1) Extend custom CodeQL to run on ALL PR-to-dev (not just dep-bump paths-filter scope from ADR-001) — ~2 min CI cost per PR, full coverage.
  (2) Run CodeQL on PR-to-dev but advisory only (don't block merge); block only on PR-to-main. Keeps dev velocity, surfaces findings earlier.
  (3) Keep status quo (CodeQL only on PR-to-main + push) and rely on ADR-002's release-cut gate to catch new findings before they promote.
  (4) Add 'no new HIGH/CRITICAL CodeQL alerts vs. base' as required status check on main branch protection (currently only 'Backend Tests' + 'Frontend Tests' are required — CodeQL failure is visible but non-blocking).
- Decision: TBD — architect leans toward (1)+(4) combination if CI cost is acceptable.
- Consequences: PR latency, dev velocity, how we triage pre-existing vs. new findings, dismiss-with-comment process
- Relationship to ADR-001 (dep-bump-only paths-filter gate) and ADR-002 (dev->main release-cut gate)

Also in scope: decide whether to promote CodeQL failure to a REQUIRED status check on main branch protection. Currently 'CodeQL' check is visible but main protection only requires 'Backend Tests' + 'Frontend Tests' — meaning a PR to main can theoretically merge even with HIGH CodeQL findings as long as the team has admin merge.

Priority P1 because gap is actively biting (PR #82) and low-effort remediation options exist.
notes: Renumbered from ADR-003 → ADR-005 on 2026-04-20 per PO/PM decision. Prior ADR-003 slot is held by enhancedchannelmanager-d42ko (WebSocket introduction & long-running job pattern, parked). Architect filed this bead 2026-04-20 without visibility into the existing parked ADR-002/003.

title: ADR-004: Release-cut promotion discipline (dev→main merge strategy)
description:
Architectural follow-on to ADR-001 and PR #82. PR #82 shipped an ADR doc but swept in 90 unrelated commits from dev (38+ feature merges since v0.15.2), exposing the lack of an explicit release-cut discipline. Architecturally, dev->main merges currently happen as side-effects of whatever doc/fix PR next targets main — there is no explicit "release-cut" flow, no version bump convention, no pre-promotion gate, no way to scope what gets promoted.

ADR must cover:
- Problem: ad-hoc dev->main side-effect promotions vs. intentional release cuts
- Options: (1) formal release-branch flow (git-flow lite), (2) squash-merge release-cut PR with CHANGELOG+version bump required, (3) trunk-based with tagged releases off main and stricter dev->main gate, (4) status quo + documented conventions
- Decision: TBD — likely (2) given current team size + release cadence
- Consequences: PR latency, reviewability of large integration PRs, ability to hold security fixes out of an unrelated release cut
- Required pre-promotion gate (beyond current 'Backend Tests' + 'Frontend Tests'): should include CodeQL delta-zero (no new HIGH findings) and a CHANGELOG entry
- Relationship to ADR-001 (ADR-001 gates PR-to-dev; this ADR gates dev-to-main)

Priority P1 because the gap was surfaced by an active blocked PR (#82) and affects how ALL future dev->main promotions are executed. Not sprint-critical (PR #82 itself can be unblocked by the security remediation in parallel), but should be drafted before the next release cut.
notes: Renumbered from ADR-002 → ADR-004 on 2026-04-20 per PO/PM decision. Prior ADR-002 slot is held by enhancedchannelmanager-t71c5 (DBAS restore engine transaction model, parked behind v0.17.0 hold). Architect filed this bead 2026-04-20 without visibility into the existing parked ADR-002/003.

title: Alembic baseline up/down smoke test against realistic data
description:
## Why
PR #81 (bd-c5wf5, commit f996ec9b) landed the Alembic baseline revision 0001 on 2026-04-20 with 36 tables and a hand-written downgrade that drops every table + index. We have tests for up-only paths (test_upgrade_head_on_fresh_db_creates_schema, test_baseline_matches_metadata_no_drift) and FK enforcement, but we have NOT exercised a real round-trip (upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade) against a seeded database. A silently-broken downgrade in the baseline would not surface until the first real rollback, which is the worst possible time to discover it.

DBE flagged this YELLOW in today's standup; PO uplifted into sprint scope. Scope is DBE framing: exercise the baseline, don't rewrite it.

## Scope
- Author a pytest integration test (first-usable-version, not a framework) that:
  1. Runs `alembic upgrade head` on a fresh SQLite DB.
  2. Seeds realistic-shape data: >=100 rows across tables with FK relationships (JournalEntry, TagGroup/Tag, AlertMethod, ScheduledTask/TaskExecution). Use existing backend/tests/fixtures/factories.py.
  3. Snapshots the schema (SQL DDL from sqlite_master + alembic_version).
  4. Runs `alembic downgrade base`.
  5. Asserts the DB has no app tables (only alembic_version OR empty).
  6. Runs `alembic upgrade head` again.
  7. Re-snapshots schema and asserts identity with the pre-downgrade snapshot.
  8. Reseeds a subset and confirms inserts succeed on the regenerated schema.
- If downgrade fails, STOP and file a separate P1 bug bead with repro details; do NOT fix baseline bugs in this scope.

## Out of scope
- Writing new migrations (baseline is the only revision).
- Production-data volume testing (realistic shape >=100 rows is the bar).
- Full CI pipeline integration if the smoke test lands cleanly — the pytest integration test runs in the existing suite and that's enough for v1.
- Docs reconciliation — that's bd-b20u4, owned by a parallel DBE agent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integration test `backend/tests/integration/test_alembic_smoke.py` runs up/down/up cycle successfully.
- [ ] Schema diff before-downgrade vs after-reupgrade is empty (byte-for-byte DDL match for tables, indexes, and FKs).
- [ ] Seed data includes FK-bearing rows (>=100 across parent/child tables) to exercise ON DELETE CASCADE paths during downgrade.
- [ ] Test runs green in the existing backend pytest suite (docker exec ecm-ecm-1 pytest backend/tests/integration/test_alembic_smoke.py).
- [ ] PR opened against dev with green test run.

## Related
- Parent work: bd-c5wf5 (Alembic baseline, PR #81, landed 2026-04-20)
- Sibling: bd-b20u4 (Docs reconcile — different agent, different worktree, merge conflicts at PR time expected and resolvable)
notes: CI green on PR #87 after bundled fix. Root cause: alembic/env.py defaulted fileConfig() to disable_existing_loggers=True, which silently disabled ecm.access logger and pinned root to WARNING. Smoke test's alembic invocations (at collection position 2) triggered the pollution before observability tests ran, surfacing the latent bug. Fix: only load alembic.ini logging when root has no handlers (embedded vs CLI heuristic). 2430/2430 tests pass. Awaiting PM merge.
close_reason: PR #87 merged to dev. Alembic baseline up/down smoke test landed (up→down→up round-trip + cascade delete regression). Bundled with fix for backend/alembic/env.py fileConfig() production observability regression (would otherwise have silenced all INFO logs in prod since PR #81).

title: Define SLOs + alert rules on /metrics baseline
description:
## Why

PR #80 (bd-ak1db, merged 2026-04-20) shipped the observability baseline — structured JSON logging + Prometheus `/metrics` exposition with four series:

- `ecm_http_requests_total{method,path,status}` (Counter)
- `ecm_http_request_duration_seconds{method,path}` (Histogram)
- `ecm_health_ready_ok` (Gauge, 0/1)
- `ecm_health_ready_check_duration_seconds{check}` (Histogram)

ak1db explicitly deferred SLOs ("needs baseline data first") and Alertmanager/alert rules ("separate bead"). PO uplifted SRE YELLOW into sprint scope today: **signal without thresholds** — on-call has metrics but no way to alert, no commitment on what "good" looks like, and no runbook path from alert to mitigation. This bead resolves that YELLOW by turning signal into actionable policy.

## Scope

Define initial SLOs for the 4 baseline metrics and ship Prometheus alert rules that match:

1. **Availability SLO** — derived from `ecm_health_ready_ok`. Target conservative (99% 30-day to start; calibrate once we have real traffic data).
2. **Latency SLO** — derived from `ecm_http_request_duration_seconds` p95. Target p95 < 500ms against the histogram buckets ak1db shipped (5ms–10s, tuned for local/LAN).
3. **Error-rate SLO** — derived from `ecm_http_requests_total` grouped by status. Target < 1% 5xx rate over rolling 30d (excluding `/metrics` which is self-skipped by middleware).
4. **Readiness sub-check latency** (stretch) — `ecm_health_ready_check_duration_seconds` per `check` label; informational dashboard signal, alert threshold optional for v1.

Corresponding Prometheus alert rules written as `rules-as-code` YAML. Burn-rate alerts (multi-window fast+slow) where feasible; single-window acceptable for scaffold.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SLO document exists (`docs/sre/slos.md`) covering: SLI definition, SLO target, error budget, error-budget policy (what triggers when budget burns).
- [ ] Prometheus alert rules committed as YAML (`docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml` or equivalent) with severity labels and runbook annotation links.
- [ ] Runbook stubs linked from alert rules — expected path `docs/runbooks/<alert-name>.md` (coordinate with sibling bead bwly4 which scaffolds `docs/runbooks/`; reference the path even if the directory lands later).
- [ ] `docs/backend_architecture.md` §Observability → Out of scope updated to cross-link the new SLO doc (no longer out of scope).
- [ ] Commit on dev, PR opened, CI green.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Deploying Prometheus/Alertmanager (rules-as-code only; deployment is a future bead).
- Grafana dashboards (future bead).
- Distributed tracing (ak1db deferred; separate bead).
- SLO calibration against real traffic (targets are initial — must be re-tuned once 30 days of metrics exist).

## Labels

sre, observability, slo

## Cross-references

- Parent baseline: bd-ak1db (closed, PR #80) — https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/pull/80
- Sibling: bd-bwly4 (in-flight) — scaffolds `docs/runbooks/` directory + template

title: Reconcile docs/database_migrations.md with Alembic baseline (PR #81)
description:
Why:
Tech Writer flagged docs/database_migrations.md RED in 2026-04-20 standup: risk that the next migration runs from stale instructions. PR #81 (commit f996ec9b) landed Alembic on 2026-04-20 and the accompanying doc was authored as part of that same commit, so while there is no 'predecessor' to delete, the doc has specific inaccuracies that will mislead the next engineer running a migration.

What is stale/wrong (as of doc introduced in f996ec9b):
- Section '4. Test locally' step uses 'rm -f /tmp/mig_test.db && CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/mig_test alembic upgrade head'. env.py + database.get_database_url() resolve the DB URL from CONFIG_DIR as '$CONFIG_DIR/journal.db', so the actual DB lands at /tmp/mig_test/journal.db — the preceding 'rm' targets the wrong path and CONFIG_DIR is a directory, not a file. Command will silently produce stale state on re-run.
- 'Authoring a migration' does not call out that the container-side Alembic tree is /app/alembic/ (not /app/backend/alembic/); the backend deploys flat to /app per backend/CLAUDE.md. New engineers copying from backend/CLAUDE.md will otherwise cp to the wrong path.
- The doc does not explicitly note that the baseline has not been exercised with a real up/down cycle (DBE YELLOW in 2026-04-20 standup) — silent acceptance that revision 0001 is 'proven' is a trap.
- Minor: 'stamp head' path is described in runtime behaviour but not explicitly as a knob for manual recovery (operators coming in cold need to know the recovery story).

What the current Alembic-based flow actually is:
- Config: backend/alembic.ini (script_location = %(here)s/alembic, filename template YYYYMMDD_HHMM_<rev>_<slug>, DB URL falls through env.py to ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL or database.get_database_url()).
- env.py: imports database + models + export_models + ffmpeg_builder.persistence so Base.metadata is fully populated; runs online by default, offline supported; compare_type + compare_server_default both True.
- Runtime bootstrap (database._bootstrap_alembic): fresh install → upgrade head; pre-Alembic install (tables exist, no alembic_version) → stamp head; at head → no-op; behind head → upgrade.
- Baseline revision: backend/alembic/versions/20260420_2034_0001_baseline_initial_schema.py (944 lines, 36 tables).
- Drift guard: backend/tests/unit/test_alembic_baseline.py (test_baseline_matches_metadata_no_drift).
- Operator visibility: GET /api/health/schema returns current_revision, head_revision, up_to_date, foreign_keys_enabled, journal_mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- docs/database_migrations.md reflects the actual Alembic flow with no command that silently fails or targets the wrong path.
- No contradictory instructions remain between docs/database_migrations.md, backend/alembic/env.py docstring, and backend/CLAUDE.md deploy rules.
- A DBE joining the project can onboard from this doc alone to: (a) create a new migration, (b) run up/down, (c) understand baseline semantics, (d) know the SQLite batch-mode rule, (e) know where to look when an upgrade fails at boot.
- Doc calls out that baseline (0001) has not yet been exercised with a real up/down cycle so engineers do not mistake 'passes drift test' for 'proven reversible'.

Out of scope:
- Actually running a baseline up/down smoke test. That is a separate follow-up bead.
- Retroactive migrations for historical ad-hoc _add_* helpers in database.py.

Labels: database, documentation, migrations

title: Flake audit & baseline: 3-run cadence to de-flake 2445 BE + 1118 FE suite
description:
**Why:** QA flagged during grooming 2026-04-20: no flake audit cadence exists. 2445 backend + 1118 frontend tests accumulate without pruning. bd-6rrl5 dep bumps need a flake baseline BEFORE upgrades so we can distinguish upgrade-induced flake from pre-existing.

title: Structured logging + /metrics endpoint (observability baseline)
description:
## Why

No observability platform today. Deep health (`/api/health/ready`, bd-w0iyw) just landed — a signal nobody listens to. DBAS import (bd-gb5r5.3) is a long-running destructive operation whose 14-category partial-failure states are undebuggable without correlation IDs and structured logs. DBAS sync (bd-gb5r5.4) compounds this with two-instance failure modes. Rollback today (v0.16.0 / bd-vgm4l) left no metric trace. Flagged during grooming 2026-04-20 as blocker for v0.17.0 DBAS epics.

## Scope

**Structured logging:**
- JSON formatter on the root logger
- Per-request correlation ID via middleware (trace-id from header if present, else generated)
- Log fields: `ts`, `level`, `logger`, `msg`, `trace_id`, plus structured context (`restore_id`, `sync_id`, `phase`, etc.)
- Python `structlog` or stdlib `logging.Formatter` subclass — PE picks

**/metrics endpoint:**
- Prometheus-compatible text exposition via `prometheus_client`
- Minimum metric set:
  - `ecm_http_requests_total{method,path,status}`
  - `ecm_http_request_duration_seconds{method,path}`
  - `ecm_health_ready_ok`
  - `ecm_health_ready_check_duration_seconds{check}`
- Cardinality rules enforced: bounded labels only (no user_id, no trace_id, no unbounded paths)

**No platform required:** expose the endpoint only. Prometheus/Grafana wiring is a separate future bead. Curl-scrape-able is enough for v0.17.0 blocker-clear.

**Instrumentation standards:**
- Update `docs/backend_architecture.md` with logging + metrics patterns (metric naming: `<namespace>_<subsystem>_<name>_<unit>`, structured log schema, cardinality rules)
- Update the SRE persona SKILL.md reference if needed so new code adds metrics as a matter of course

## Acceptance

- `/metrics` returns Prometheus text for the minimum metric set
- Every request produces one JSON log line with a `trace_id`
- `docs/backend_architecture.md` updated with logging + metrics patterns
- Instrumentation standards documented (metric naming, cardinality rules, required log fields)
- Correlation ID propagates from HTTP header → log context → response header

## Out of Scope

- SLOs (separate bead — needs baseline data first)
- Alertmanager / alert rules (separate bead)
- Distributed tracing (Jaeger / Tempo / OTel exporters) — separate bead
- Prometheus / Grafana / Loki deployment — separate bead

This is the substrate those beads will stand on.

title: STRIDE threat model: DBAS import/restore endpoint (gb5r5.3)
description:
**Why:** bd-gb5r5.3 restores ZIPs containing credentials (M3U auth, user agents), users table, plugins, settings — each a distinct attack surface. Current bead lacks any security analysis. Security flagged this as privilege-escalation + RCE surface during grooming 2026-04-20.

**Scope — STRIDE analysis of:**
- ZIP upload path (Spoofing archive origin, Tampering with entries, Info disclosure via extracted secrets)
- ZIP extraction (Zip Slip path traversal, symlink escape, zip bombs, entry-count DoS)
- User-table restore (privilege escalation — attacker-supplied archive grants admin)
- Plugin restore (RCE if plugins are executable code; PO clarification needed — are plugins code or config?)
- M3U/API-token restore (credential exfiltration; secrets-in-logs during dry-run)
- Endpoint authz (admin-only? separate 'restore' permission?)
- Audit logging (who restored what, when, per-category counts)

**Deliverables:**
- docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md — STRIDE table, hardening decisions, test cases
- Security acceptance criteria added to bd-gb5r5.3 description:
  - Zip Slip hardening (path normalization, symlink rejection, size+ratio+entry-count caps)
  - Admin-only endpoint + opt-in flag for users/plugins categories
  - Current authenticated admin account NEVER overwritten by restore
  - Secrets redacted in all logs including dry-run
  - Full audit log entry per category with request ID
  - Archive integrity check (SHA-256 manifest)
  - Dry-run guaranteed side-effect free (tempdir cleanup verified)

**Out of scope:** implementation (engineer's work); DBAS sync (gb5r5.4) has its own threat model once instance trust questions resolved via ADR-004.
notes: Threat model authored: docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md (50 STRIDE rows, 17-item hardening checklist, 6 PO assumptions flagged). Hardening checklist cross-filed on bd-gb5r5.3 notes. CLAUDE.md Reference Guides table updated. PR: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/pull/79 (doc-only, no CI checks run). Bead stays open — PO closes after PR merges.

title: Introduce Alembic + schema baseline (blocks DBAS restore/sync)
description:
Why:
DBAS import/restore (bd-gb5r5.3) needs schema versioning. Without Alembic, a DBAS ZIP backup taken on schema v1 restored against schema v2 silently corrupts. DBA flagged as hard blocker during grooming 2026-04-20. Also precondition for bd-gb5r5.4 (sync reuses import path).

Scope:
- Add alembic to backend deps; initial 'alembic init'
- Baseline the current SQLite schema as revision 0001 (autogenerate + hand-review)
- Wire 'alembic upgrade head' into container startup per docs/backend_architecture.md
- Document per-connection PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON enforcement (SQLite default is OFF; quiet FK violations possible today)
- Document PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL verification
- Add schema-version field that restore engine can gate on
- Document migration authoring conventions in docs/backend_architecture.md or a new docs/database_migrations.md

TDD:
- A test that asserts the baseline revision matches the live schema (guard against drift)

Out of scope:
- Retroactive migrations for legacy schema changes; just baseline current state.
acceptance_criteria:
- 'alembic upgrade head' runs cleanly on a fresh container
- Schema version is readable via API or known-path query
- FK enforcement verified via test that attempts an invalid FK insert and sees rejection
- No existing test regressions

title: Smart sort: primary criteria not applied within failed-rank buckets (#73)
description:
## Summary
GitHub issue #73 (filed by ferteque, labeled P3 by reporter). PO has elevated to P1 — sprint-blocker for the v0.16.0 re-release. Reporter notes this is a follow-on from issue #58 (the persistence bug, fixed in v0.16.0-0027); #58 was closed today when ferteque agreed this is a distinct defect.

## Observed behavior
With smart sort configured as priority=['resolution','framerate','m3u_priority','bitrate','audio_channels','video_codec'] (all enabled) and deprioritize-failed enabled with failed_stream_sort_order=['black_screen','low_fps','failed'], streams do land in the correct failed-rank buckets — but ordering INSIDE each bucket does not follow the configured primary criteria.

## Hypothesis (for engineer to confirm/refute)
Primary criteria are not being applied within failed-rank buckets. Evidence from the reporter's log (channel-591424, 13 streams):

- Rank 0 (black_screen) bucket: resolutions 1024x576, 1920x1080, 1024x576 and all @ 25fps. If primary criteria were applying, the 1920x1080 stream should sort first inside the bucket. It lands at #2 behind a 1024x576 stream.
- Rank 2 (failed) bucket: 1920x1080 @ 50fps streams land at #8, #9, #11, #12 — behind a 1280x720 @ 25fps stream at #7. Higher resolution + higher framerate should sort ahead.

This points at the bucket secondary-sort not receiving (or not honoring) the active criteria comparator.

## Repro (from reporter)
1. Go to Channel Manager
2. Manually start a stream probe for a channel with known black-screen streams
3. After probe completes, trigger Smart Sort on that channel
4. Expected: streams within each failed-rank bucket sorted by configured primary criteria. Actual: within-bucket order appears random relative to configured criteria.

## Log excerpt (from issue #73)
```
[STREAM-PROBE-SORT] Channel 'channel-591424': Sorting 13 streams
[STREAM-PROBE-SORT] Sort config: priority=['resolution','framerate','m3u_priority','bitrate','audio_channels','video_codec'], enabled={all True}
[STREAM-PROBE-SORT] Active criteria (in order): ['resolution','framerate','m3u_priority','bitrate','audio_channels','video_codec']
[STREAM-PROBE-SORT] Deprioritize failed streams: True
[STREAM-PROBE-SORT] Failed stream sort order: ['black_screen','low_fps','failed']
  Stream 962110 (D.LaLiga2): status=success, res=1024x576, fps=25.0
  Stream 959174 (MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 UHD): status=success, res=1920x1080, fps=25.0
  Stream 959167 (MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 SD): status=success, res=1024x576, fps=25.0
  Stream 962109 (K.LaLiga2): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=25.0
  Stream 958629 (M.LALIGA 2 RAW): status=success, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 958471 (VO MOVISTAR LALIGA 2 RAW): status=success, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 1465610 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD): status=failed, res=1280x720, fps=25.0
  Stream 1465608 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 1465609 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 B): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 1151442 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD): status=failed, res=1280x720, fps=25.0
  Stream 1151440 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 1151441 (M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 B): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=50.0
  Stream 962111 (S.LaLiga2 HD): status=failed, res=1920x1080, fps=25.0
  D.LaLiga2: DEPRIORITIZED (black screen, rank=0)
  MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 UHD: DEPRIORITIZED (black screen, rank=0)
  MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 SD: DEPRIORITIZED (black screen, rank=0)
  K.LaLiga2: DEPRIORITIZED (status=failed, rank=2)
  M.LALIGA 2 RAW: DEPRIORITIZED (black screen, rank=0)
  VO MOVISTAR LALIGA 2 RAW: DEPRIORITIZED (black screen, rank=0)
  ... (remaining status=failed deprioritized at rank=2)
Sorted order:
  #1: D.LaLiga2 (success, 1024x576)          <-- rank 0
  #2: MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 UHD (success, 1920x1080)  <-- rank 0, should be #1 within bucket
  #3: MOVISTAR LA LIGA 2 SD (success, 1024x576)    <-- rank 0
  #4: M.LALIGA 2 RAW (success, 1920x1080)    <-- rank 0
  #5: VO MOVISTAR LALIGA 2 RAW (success, 1920x1080) <-- rank 0
  #6: K.LaLiga2 (failed, 1920x1080)          <-- rank 2
  #7: M. La Liga TV 2 HD (failed, 1280x720)  <-- rank 2, should land BELOW 1920x1080 @50fps
  #8: M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 (failed, 1920x1080)  <-- 50fps, should lead bucket
  #9: M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 B (failed, 1920x1080)
  #10: M. La Liga TV 2 HD (failed, 1280x720)
  #11: M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 (failed, 1920x1080)
  #12: M. La Liga TV 2 HD 1080 B (failed, 1920x1080)
  #13: S.LaLiga2 HD (failed, 1920x1080)
```

## Code location
- Backend Python: `backend/stream_prober.py` (search for `[STREAM-PROBE-SORT]` log tag)
- Likely area: `_smart_sort_streams` / `smart_sort_streams` — specifically the composite key that combines bucket rank with the primary-criteria comparator. The rank prefix is working (buckets are correct); the tiebreaker within the rank is what's misfiring.

## Related history
- Issue #58 (closed): original persistence bug for `failed_stream_sort_order`. Fixed in v0.16.0-0027 (commit 7a5a6203). Ferteque agreed in #58 comment (2026-04-20) that this is a distinct symptom and opened #73.
- Prior PR #72 merged into dev (tip a145250e).
- v0.16.0 was rolled back today (bd-vgm4l) specifically to clear PO-flagged bugs before re-cutting the tag. This bead is one of those bugs.

## Links
- GitHub: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/73
- Prior: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/58

## Sprint context
- Sprint goal: clear PO-flagged bugs, then re-cut v0.16.0.
- main is at v0.15.2 (post-rollback). dev is at a145250e. package.json: 0.16.0-0040.
- Independent of bd-zjge5 (ESLint baseline, in_progress) — no dependency either direction.

## Owner & methodology
- Owner hint: Project Engineer (backend Python).
- TDD required: failing pytest that demonstrates the within-bucket ordering is wrong on current dev, THEN the fix. Do not land a fix without a test that was RED first.
- Deploy-to-container iteration per CLAUDE.md before shipping.

## Out of scope
- Do not touch bucket-assignment logic (ranks are already correct per the log).
- Do not refactor the sort API surface unless the minimal fix requires it — this is a bugfix sprint, not a cleanup sprint.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pytest case reproduces the bug: within a single failed-rank bucket (e.g. rank=0 black_screen, rank=2 failed), streams with higher priority in the configured criteria order (resolution, framerate, m3u_priority, bitrate, audio_channels, video_codec) sort first. Test is RED against current code on dev @ a145250e.
- Test passes GREEN after fix.
- No regression in existing [STREAM-PROBE-SORT] pytest coverage (full suite green).
- Fix is visible in [STREAM-PROBE-SORT] debug log output so reporter (ferteque) can verify visually on re-report — per-bucket ordering should be legible in the log.
- Manual repro from issue #73 (channel-591424 13-stream probe) now orders 1920x1080 streams above 1024x576 inside the black_screen (rank=0) bucket, and orders 1920x1080 @ 50fps streams above 1280x720 @ 25fps inside the failed (rank=2) bucket.
notes: Correction 2026-04-21: my reopen NOTES were based on a misread of the timeline. The fix was NOT rolled back. Fix commits 23a755b6 (sw883, stream probe) and 13dbe496 (bqpq0, auto-create) were authored 2026-04-20 at 17:07 UTC — 29 minutes AFTER reporter filed GH-73 at 16:38 UTC. Reporter's v0.17.0-0000 build was a pre-fix dev tip. Both fix commits are on current dev and present in every :dev GHCR image since ~17:30 UTC 2026-04-20. Project Engineer (subagent ac4d6376) verified: (a) current in-container code returns correct sort order for reporter's exact 13-stream scenario, (b) pre-fix simulation via monkey-patching reproduces the bug, (c) 2487 backend tests pass. Two regression tests added to nail down coverage — landing via PR from worktree-agent-ac4d6376 to dev. Bead closes on regression-test PR merge.

title: Execute v0.16.0 release: version bump, merge to main, tag, GH release, verify GHCR
description:
# Execute v0.16.0 Release

Owner: Project Engineer (same persona who drove bd-t8xw3 and bd-v3xfl; fluent with scratch-branch/worktree workflows).
Coordinator: Project Manager (tracks; does not execute).
Authoritative workflow: docs/shipping.md (sections: "Release Workflow (Merging to Main)" + the shipping checklist).

## Trigger Condition — DO NOT START until ALL of these are true
- [ ] PR #66 (bd-v3xfl) merged to dev
- [ ] PR #65 (docs: CHANGELOG/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTING) merged to dev
- [ ] Branch protection on `main` is configured (bd-8w33i complete)
- Optional / nice-to-have if they've landed: bd-844yr, bd-trfd0 (not required to ship v0.16.0)

Companion beads referenced: bd-v3xfl (v3xfl PR), bd-nv36s (release notes drafted in notes field), bd-vighz, bd-ehf2q, bd-8w33i (branch protection).

## Execution Steps (per docs/shipping.md)

1. Verify dev is at expected tip and recent PRs are merged:
   - git fetch --all
   - git log --oneline origin/dev -n 10
   - confirm PR #66 and #65 merge commits are present
   - confirm CI on dev is green

2. Version bump: edit `frontend/package.json`
   - from current `0.16.0-NNNN` (build-counter suffix)
   - to `0.16.0` (drop suffix)

3. Rebuild frontend to confirm build still passes:
   - cd frontend && npm run build

4. Commit the version bump on dev:
   - commit message: `Bump frontend version to 0.16.0 for release`
   - git push origin dev
   - confirm `git status` shows "up to date with origin"

5. Worktree-merge dev -> main (per docs/shipping.md — do NOT check out main in the main working tree):
   ```
   git worktree add /tmp/ecm-main main
   cd /tmp/ecm-main && git merge dev --no-edit && git push origin main
   git worktree remove /tmp/ecm-main
   ```
   - Root checkout MUST stay on dev at all times.

6. Push main (covered by step 5 `git push origin main`). Verify remote main now points at the merge commit.

7. Create GitHub Release using release notes from bd-nv36s's notes field:
   - Extract notes from bd-nv36s: `bd show enhancedchannelmanager-nv36s` (notes field)
   - Write to /tmp/v0.16.0-release-notes.md
   - `gh release create v0.16.0 --target main --title "v0.16.0" --notes-file /tmp/v0.16.0-release-notes.md`

8. Verify GHCR auto-publishes the image:
   - Watch the GitHub Actions release workflow complete
   - Confirm tags exist on `ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager`:
     - `v0.16.0`
     - `0.16`
     - `latest`
   - Confirm multi-arch (AMD64 + ARM64) via `docker manifest inspect`

9. Open the next minor's build counter on dev:
   - edit `frontend/package.json` version -> `0.17.0-0000`
   - cd frontend && npm run build (sanity)
   - commit: `Open v0.17.0 build counter`
   - git push origin dev

10. Announce on Discord per docs/discord_release_notes.md
    - Use the drafted v0.16.0 release notes
    - Post in the release channel per the documented format

## Success Criteria
- `v0.16.0` tag exists on main (annotated by the GH release)
- GitHub Release `v0.16.0` published with the drafted notes attached
- GHCR has `ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:v0.16.0`, `:0.16`, and `:latest` (all multi-arch AMD64 + ARM64)
- `main` branch protection holds (required checks pass; no force-push allowed)
- `dev` branch is at `0.17.0-0000` ready for v0.17.0 work
- Discord announcement posted

## Out of Scope
- v0.17.0 feature work (tracked under bd-gb5r5)
- Backporting fixes (not needed; release is cut from current dev)
- Changelog backfill for v0.4-v0.15 (PO explicitly chose to kill the file, not backfill)

## Hard Constraints
- Follow docs/shipping.md exactly — do not invent steps
- Root checkout MUST stay on dev throughout; use worktree for main merge
- Work is NOT complete until `git push origin dev` (version bump), `git push origin main` (merge), `gh release create` all succeed AND GHCR publish is verified
- Do NOT skip the 0.17.0-0000 counter-open step — that's what unblocks the next sprint's "ship the fix" flow

## Priority Rationale
P1 — release is the sprint goal. This is the last step to get v0.16.0 out the door.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Release-scoped. ECM is a public OSS project on GHCR; it has no SECURITY.md and no documented channel for reporting security vulnerabilities. Shipping a release (especially one that contains a security fix, v3xfl) without a vuln-reporting policy is a gap.

Scope:
- Create SECURITY.md at repo root following the GitHub standard template (supported versions, reporting a vulnerability, disclosure policy).
- Explicit vulnerability reporting channel: prefer GitHub Security Advisories (private disclosure via the Security tab) over email. If the maintainer wants an email fallback, use a dedicated alias, not a personal one.
- Brief disclosure timeline expectations (e.g., triage within 7 days, patch within 30 days for critical). Realistic for a solo-maintainer OSS project; don't overpromise.
- List which versions are supported for security fixes (likely just 'latest' since this is a single-maintainer project on a rolling release cadence).

Reference: current practice evidence — the closed OWASP epic (ppe28) and ongoing work on v3xfl suggest the maintainer already acts on security issues, so this is about making the process legible, not creating new process.

Out of scope:
- GitHub Security Advisory workflow setup beyond the doc itself (the maintainer enables it in repo settings).
- Bounty program (N/A for this project).

Flagged by Technical Writer during /onboard 2026-04-19. Promoted to P1 because the project is about to ship a release containing a security fix.
notes: SECURITY.md drafted on docs/release-foundation branch. PO question: do you want an email fallback alongside the GitHub Security Advisories flow? If yes, provide a dedicated alias (NOT a personal email) — e.g., security@<domain>. Current draft uses GHSA as sole reporting channel. If you want email added, tell me the alias and I'll amend the doc.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Release-scoped (sprint goal: get 0.16.0 fully released). CHANGELOG.md is 12 minors stale (last entry v0.3.1 from 2026-01-02; current dev is v0.16.0-0040).

Decision point:
- Option A: Kill CHANGELOG.md, replace with a one-line pointer to GitHub Releases. Use GitHub Releases as the canonical release notes source. Future releases = tag v0.16.0, write release notes in the GitHub UI.
- Option B: Backfill CHANGELOG.md with entries for every vX.Y.Z release between 0.3.1 and 0.16.0. Significant grind (37+ build commits in v0.16.0 alone).
- Option C: Hybrid — kill the historical content in CHANGELOG.md but keep the file as a redirect header: 'For release notes, see GitHub Releases.' Lowest maintenance, preserves file for anyone who looks for it.

Recommendation (Technical Writer discretion): Option C. It's modern OSS practice, costs nothing to maintain, and doesn't lose time on grunt backfill.

Also in scope:
- Write v0.16.0 release notes (markdown) suitable for GitHub Releases. Source the content from commit messages on dev ahead of main (40 commits). Group by category: features, fixes, security, infrastructure. Highlight user-visible changes.
- Link the release notes in the PR description or attach them to the bead for the PO to paste into the GitHub Releases UI when tagging v0.16.0.

Out of scope:

Flagged by Technical Writer during /onboard 2026-04-19.
notes:
# v0.16.0 — MCP Server & Claude Integration

Enhanced Channel Manager gets a full Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, letting Claude drive ECM through natural language. This release also ships a security fix, a fleet of smart-sort and auto-creation improvements, and a hardened dependency/build pipeline.

## Highlights

- **New MCP server (124 tools across 14 domains)** — a separate optional container (`ecm-mcp`) that exposes channels, streams, EPG, auto-creation, stats, FFmpeg, and more via SSE with API-key auth. Wire it into Claude Desktop or Claude Code and manage ECM by talking to it.
- **Find & Merge Duplicate Channels** — scan for channels with matching normalized names and merge groups of duplicates in one pass.
- **YAML backup task and restore modal** — full configuration backup/restore with scheduled task support.
- **Enhanced Dummy EPG template engine** — lookup tables for richer generated guide data.
- **Dispatcharr 0.23.0 compatibility** — auth flow updates plus API-key service auth.

## Features

- Per-rule normalization group selection in Auto-Creation rules (#54)
- Video codec as a Smart Sort criterion (#50)
- Configurable ordering for deprioritized stream categories (black screen, low FPS)
- Per-category Smart Sort toggles for black screen / low FPS (#56)
- Set Logo from EPG bulk action (UI + MCP)
- Bulk Channel Profile assignment in Channel Manager
- User column in Watch History; watching user shown in Stats tab active-stream list
- Channel-groups diagnostic endpoint + `channel_groups_diagnostic.json` in debug bundle
- "Generate Debug Bundle" button in Settings > Logging; settings and task schedules now included in the bundle
- Error/success notifications for Auto-Sync group creation
- Reflect probe `stream_stats` back to Dispatcharr (#57)

## Fixes

- Black screen scan no longer erases manual-probe findings on timeout
- Preserve staged streams across search changes in channel edit mode
- Preserve superscript characters in auto-creation output names (#61)
- Correct stream stats (width/height, source_fps) pushed to Dispatcharr (#60, thanks @krog)
- Persist Failed Stream Ordering setting (#58)
- Fix Channel Manager static groups disappearing after server move
- Fix Guide tab not populating channels on direct load
- Fix missing task failure logs; suppress SQLAlchemy log noise
- Fix auto-create rule creation failing with NOT NULL constraint
- Fix black screen streams not deprioritized in sort order
- Fix bulk delete for missing channels
- Invalidate stream-groups cache on M3U refresh
- Fix bulk probe not triggering Smart Sort when `auto_reorder_after_probe` is enabled
- Fix ExportPublishTask init crash
- Disable Export Publish task by default; preserve user's enabled setting across restart

## Security

- Apply Debian security updates in final image, including openssl CVE-2026-28390
- Bump vite to patch three high-severity advisories
- Scrub home-directory paths from tracked agent docs

## Infrastructure

- Pin all dependency versions for reproducible builds; apply safe minor/patch updates
- Separate MCP server as an optional component with its own CI pipeline
- Fix Docker build OOM via multi-stage Python builder

## Upgrade Notes

- The MCP server is optional. If you do not use Claude/MCP, no action needed — ECM itself upgrades in place.
- To enable MCP, add the `ecm-mcp` service to your compose file (see README) and generate an API key in Settings > MCP Integration.
- First-run of v0.16.0 on existing installs will migrate the watch-history schema to include the user column; no manual steps required.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Companion bead to enhancedchannelmanager-t8xw3. Becomes actionable after t8xw3 lands (which fixes the ajv override so lint is runnable).

Background:
- Lint has been broken on dev for ~2 months due to a stale ajv override in frontend/package.json. t8xw3 removes that override.
- Once runnable, 'npm run lint' reports 71 errors and 98 warnings across the codebase. t8xw3 grandfathers these via changed-files-only enforcement; this bead zeroes them.
- Majority of errors are @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any in logger.ts, api.ts, and a handful of other files. Remainder: unused eslint-disable directives, one empty-interface.

Scope:
- Drive the baseline to zero: 0 errors, 0 warnings with --max-warnings 0.
- Once at zero, flip t8xw3's lint strategy from 'changed-files-only block + full-lint informational' to 'full-lint blocking on every run.' Update .github/workflows/test.yml accordingly.
- Document in docs/frontend/ or CLAUDE.md why --max-warnings 0 is enforced.

Approach:
- Fix batches by rule (all no-explicit-any first, then unused directives, etc.) for reviewability.
- Some 'any' usages might be justified — replace with 'unknown' and narrow, or add a targeted eslint-disable-next-line with a comment explaining why.
- Do NOT bulk-disable rules to hit zero; that defeats the purpose.

Expected effort: 1-3 sessions depending on how many 'any' need genuine type-narrowing work vs. rote replacement.

Flagged by Project Engineer during t8xw3 preflight 2026-04-19. Split out so t8xw3 could ship without scope bloat.
notes: Session 3 PR #76 opened 2026-04-20. Lint: 17 errors -> 0 errors, 89 warnings -> 0 warnings. Zero baseline achieved. CI flipped to full-lint blocking (t8xw3 workflow update included). Fixes: setState-in-effect cluster (13) via Outer/Inner modal split pattern + useState initializers + handler-owned transitions; react-compiler memoization (3) via whole-object deps; rules-of-hooks (1) via hook-before-early-return; notifications dep cluster (~48) via memoized context value + dep additions; react-refresh/only-export-components disables for co-location patterns; SORT_MODE_LABELS moved to module scope; autoSyncRelatedGroups/annotations useMemo wrapping. New docs/frontend_lint.md explains the zero-warnings policy and canonical fix patterns. All 1118 unit tests pass, typecheck + build clean. UI smoke test against ecm-ecm-1 confirms React tree mounts cleanly. Ready for close after merge.

title: Ratchet vitest/pytest coverage thresholds from measured baseline (t8xw3 companion)
description:
Companion bead to enhancedchannelmanager-t8xw3. Must wait until t8xw3 has been running for at least 1 week so we can observe real coverage numbers across typical PRs.

Current state (verified during /onboard):
- frontend/vitest.config.ts: thresholds set to 20% (lines/branches/functions/statements) — a floor, not a measurement
- backend/pytest.ini: no coverage configuration
- Neither enforced in CI today (because t8xw3 hasn't landed)

Scope:
- After t8xw3 has been running for ~1 week, analyze actual coverage numbers from CI runs
- Set vitest threshold at (measured - small buffer) to prevent regression without breaking day one
- Add pytest --cov-fail-under=N based on measured backend coverage
- Evaluate using diff-coverage (coverage of CHANGED lines only) as the gate instead of whole-codebase coverage — likely better for a codebase this size
- Document the ratcheting cadence in docs/testing.md (e.g., quarterly review, raise by 5 points if current is holding)
- Do NOT pick arbitrary numbers; base all thresholds on observed data

Explicitly NOT in scope:
- Retroactively forcing coverage on low-coverage modules (that's a backlog grooming task, not a gate)
- Mandating 80%+ coverage on legacy modules — unrealistic for a 61K-line codebase

QA Engineer pushed for 60% vitest + 50% pytest during /onboard 2026-04-19, but measurement-first approach was agreed as better than guessing. Defer decision until data exists.
close_reason: PR #91 merged to dev. Coverage ratchet landed: backend threshold 56% (measured 58%), frontend 13/12/13/13 (measured 15.46/14.13/15.28/15.17). pytest-cov wired via backend/pytest.ini + .coveragerc; vitest thresholds in frontend/vitest.config.ts; CI enforces via .github/workflows/test.yml (frontend switched to npm run test:coverage blocking). Ratchet cadence documented in docs/testing.md — re-ratchet after 2-4 weeks of real PR data. Single-snapshot baseline per PO 2026-04-20 (pragmatic override of the bead's original 1-week-wait methodology).

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: Onboarding finding (YELLOW, UX resilience). No React ErrorBoundary anywhere in frontend. A single uncaught render error white-screens the SPA mid-edit-session, losing unsaved edit-mode state (which useChangeHistory/useEditMode carefully preserve). Fix: add top-level boundary in App.tsx and per-tab boundaries so a broken Stats tab doesn't kill Channel Manager. Flagged by UX Designer during /onboard 2026-04-19.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: Onboarding finding (YELLOW, operability). backend/routers/health.py returns hardcoded 'status: healthy' + version env vars only. Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK will report healthy even if SQLite is locked, Dispatcharr is unreachable, or ffmpeg/ffprobe is missing. Fix: add /api/health/ready that performs DB SELECT 1, cached (30s) Dispatcharr ping, shutil.which('ffprobe') check. Keep /api/health as cheap liveness. Highest-ROI operability improvement per the SRE assessment. Flagged by SRE during /onboard 2026-04-19.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: Onboarding finding (YELLOW, data integrity). Live DB verified as journal_mode=delete (rollback journal, not WAL) and foreign_keys=0. Two consequences: (1) rollback journal serializes readers against writer — probe/bandwidth/task writes will block HTTP request loop under load, producing 'database is locked' errors; (2) 9 ForeignKey declarations + ON DELETE clauses in models.py are declared but not enforced, allowing orphan rows. Also: routers/backup.py:86 calls PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) which is a no-op in rollback-journal mode. Fix (~15 lines): add SQLAlchemy event.listens_for(Engine, 'connect') listener in database.py that issues PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection. Flagged by Database Engineer during /onboard 2026-04-19.

title: MCP: Improve fuzzy stream matching quality
description:
The fuzzy_match_stream and match_streams_to_channels tools have two categories of problems discovered during DirecTV lineup build:

FALSE POSITIVES - matcher picks wrong stream:
- MTV matched WMTV (substring false match)
- Pop TV matched Vevo Pop (substring false match)
- Family Movie Channel matched Starz Kids & Family
- Bloomberg TV matched Bloomberg Originals
- EWTN matched EWTN Radio (TV vs Radio confusion)
- STARZ matched Starz in Black (should be main channel)
- HBO matched HBO Hits (should be main channel)
- Fox News matched Live Now from FOX
- MAVTV matched NBA Dallas Mavericks
- Lifetime matched Lifetime Movie

MISSED MATCHES - name structure too different:
- Locals: channel 'WISC (CBS Madison)' vs stream 'WI | Madison | CBS WISC' - need to extract call signs
- ESPN variants: 'ESPNews' vs 'ESPN News', 'ESPN2' vs 'ESPN 2', 'ESPNU' vs 'ESPN U' - need abbreviation expansion
- FS1/FS2: 'FS1' vs 'FOX Sports 1' - need common abbreviation map
- SundanceTV vs 'Sundance TV', 'RFD-TV' vs 'RFD TV' - need hyphen/space normalization
- MTV/MTV2 search picking up WMTV - need exact word boundary matching

FIXES NEEDED:
1. Score exact-word matches higher than substring matches (MTV should not match WMTV)
2. Add abbreviation expansion map: FS1->FOX Sports 1, ESPN2->ESPN 2, ESPNU->ESPN U, ESPNews->ESPN News
3. Strip hyphens and normalize spaces in comparisons
4. Penalize Radio streams when matching TV channels
5. When channel has a parenthetical like '(CBS Madison)', extract call sign for local matching
6. For premium multiplex, prefer the base channel name exact match over sub-channels
7. Add word-boundary awareness to prevent substring false positives

title: MCP: Add fuzzy_match_stream tool
description: Add MCP tool that searches for a stream by name with automatic variant expansion. Given a channel name and optional market/timezone, tries: exact name, with/without 'TV' suffix, with/without 'Channel'/'Network' suffix, East/West variants based on market. Discovered during DirecTV build where 'GRIT' missed 'GRIT TV', 'Cozi' missed 'Cozi TV', 'REELZ' was skipped entirely. Supersedes enhancedchannelmanager-z94iw (close that bead when this is implemented).

title: MCP: Add bulk_search_streams tool
description: Add MCP tool wrapping multiple search queries in one call. Takes a list of search terms and returns results for all of them. title: MCP: Add match_streams_to_channels tool
description: Add MCP tool that auto-matches all unassigned channels in a group to provider streams. Given a group_id and provider_id, iterates channels with 0 streams, searches for matching streams using channel name variants, and assigns best matches. Should handle East/West preference, HD/FHD/SD preference, and common suffix variations (TV, Channel, Network). Eliminates the biggest pain point from the DirecTV lineup build where 90% of tool calls were stream searches.

description:
Add rate limiting to /api/auth/login and /api/auth/dispatcharr/login using slowapi library. In-memory backend (no Redis needed — single-process Docker app). Apply to login endpoints only, not globally. Suggested limit: 5 attempts/minute per IP.

Steps:
1. Add slowapi to requirements.txt
2. Initialize Limiter in auth/routes.py with default key_func (client IP from X-Forwarded-For)
3. Add @limiter.limit() decorator to login() and dispatcharr_login()
4. Register SlowAPIMiddleware and 429 exception handler in main.py
5. Tests for rate limit behavior

title: Add safe security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy)
description:
Add middleware to main.py setting three risk-free security headers on all responses:

- X-Frame-Options: DENY (prevents clickjacking)
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (prevents MIME sniffing)
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (prevents URL leakage)

These are unconditionally safe — no risk of breaking the SPA or LAN access.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:

Leave 400/404/409 responses alone — those contain user-meaningful feedback (validation errors, not-found IDs, duplicate names, YAML parse errors) that the UI needs.

Pattern: replace detail=str(e) with a generic message (e.g., 'Operation failed') and ensure the exception is already logged via logger.error/warning/exception above the raise.

title: Register WebSocket Status as monitored service
description:
Add WebSocket Status service to service registry.

Health Check Implementation:
- Verify WebSocket endpoint is accessible
- Check active connection count
- Monitor heartbeat health (30s interval)
- Track message queue status

Status Indicators:
- healthy: WebSocket accepting connections, heartbeat working
- degraded: High connection count or message backlog
- unhealthy: WebSocket endpoint not responding

Impact: Status page won't receive real-time updates when unhealthy.

title: Register Health Scheduler as monitored service
description:
Add Health Scheduler to service registry (meta-monitoring).

Health Check Implementation:
- Verify health check loop is running
- Check last check timestamp per service
- Monitor check success rates
- Track incident detection working

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Check loop running, checks executing on schedule
- degraded: Checks delayed or partial failures
- unhealthy: Check loop stopped

Note: This is the service that performs health checks on other services. Self-monitoring.

title: Register Stream Prober as monitored service
description:
Add Stream Prober to service registry with health checks.

Health Check Implementation:
- Verify ffprobe binary exists and is executable
- Check recent probe success/failure rates
- Monitor active probe tasks
- Track last probe run timestamp

Status Indicators:
- healthy: ffprobe available, recent probes successful
- degraded: High failure rate or stale probe data
- unhealthy: ffprobe not found or all probes failing

Dependencies: Requires ffprobe binary in PATH.

title: Register Bandwidth Tracker as monitored service
description:
Add Bandwidth Tracker to service registry with health checks.

Health Check Implementation:
- Verify tracker is polling Dispatcharr
- Check last poll timestamp (stale if > 2 minutes)
- Monitor poll success rate
- Track connected client count

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Polling successfully, fresh data
- degraded: Stale data or intermittent poll failures
- unhealthy: Not polling or Dispatcharr unreachable

Impact: Statistics tab shows stale/missing data when unhealthy.

title: Important Internal Services
description:
Register and monitor important internal ECM services. These provide key functionality but system can operate in degraded mode without them.

Services:
- Bandwidth Tracker: Polls Dispatcharr stats, powers Statistics tab
- Stream Prober: ffprobe-based stream health monitoring
- Health Scheduler: The service that runs health checks
- WebSocket Status: Real-time UI updates

title: Register Database as monitored service
description:
Add Database (journal.db) as a separate monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Test database connectivity with simple query
- Check database file exists and is accessible
- Monitor query response times
- Track database file size

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Queries execute successfully, response time < 100ms
- degraded: Slow queries (> 500ms) or large file size
- unhealthy: Cannot connect or file inaccessible

Note: Currently checked as ECM Backend component. This promotes it to standalone service for granular monitoring.

title: Register Task Engine as monitored service
description:
Add Task Engine to service registry with health checks.

Health Check Implementation:
- Verify engine is running (is_running property)
- Check active task count vs max concurrent
- Detect stuck/long-running tasks
- Report registered task count
- Track last successful task execution

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Engine running, no stuck tasks
- degraded: High task load (>50 active) or stale executions
- unhealthy: Engine not running or not initialized

Alert Integration:
- Create incidents when engine stops
- Alert on stuck tasks (running > 1 hour)

title: Critical Internal Services

Register and monitor critical internal ECM services that the system depends on. These services should trigger alerts when unhealthy.

Services:
- Task Engine: Background scheduler running M3U refresh, EPG sync, stream probes
- Database Service: SQLite journal.db for all persistent data

Note: ECM Backend and Dispatcharr are already implemented.

title: LDAP Authentication

title: SAML Authentication

title: OIDC Authentication

title: Local Authentication

title: Dispatcharr Authentication

title: Auth Foundation - Core Infrastructure

title: Authentication System
description: Roadmap 0.11.5: Add authentication methods to ECM supporting OIDC, SAML, LDAP, Local, and Dispatcharr SSO. This enables secure multi-user access with flexible identity provider integration.

description:
HIGH IMPACT: Consolidate duplicate EPG search logic into single utility function.

FILE: frontend/src/components/BulkEPGAssignModal.tsx

DUPLICATE FUNCTIONS:
1. ConflictCard component has matchesSearch() (lines 900-916)
2. EPGSearchCard component has matchesSearch() (lines 1089-1104)

Both functions are nearly identical:
- Normalize EPG name and tvg_id to lowercase
- Strip non-alphanumeric characters for fuzzy matching
- Check if all search words match any of the fields

MINOR DIFFERENCE:
- ConflictCard version includes EPG source name matching
- EPGSearchCard version omits source matching

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Create utility function in frontend/src/utils/epgMatching.ts:
   matchesEPGSearch(epg: EPGData, searchWords: string[], options?: { includeSource?: boolean, epgSources?: EPGSource[] }): boolean
2. Export from epgMatching.ts (file already exists with other EPG utilities)
3. Update ConflictCard to use utility with includeSource: true
4. Update EPGSearchCard to use utility with includeSource: false
5. Remove duplicate implementations

ESTIMATED SAVINGS: 30-40 lines

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:

- Example: getNotifications() (lines 1840-1847) builds URLSearchParams inline
- Example: createNotification() (lines 1851-1860) also uses inline construction

- fetchJson() wrapper has proper error handling (lines 94-129)
- But some endpoints call raw fetch() directly:
  - deleteChannelGroup (line 294): await fetch(..., { method: 'DELETE' })
  - deleteEPGSource (line 861): await fetch(..., { method: 'DELETE' })

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Find all inline URLSearchParams construction, replace with buildQuery()
2. Find all raw fetch() calls, replace with fetchJson()
3. Ensure consistent error handling across all API functions
4. Add tests to verify error handling works correctly

ESTIMATED SAVINGS: 30-50 lines + improved error handling consistency

title: Ops: enable a dbas_backup schedule on the production instance, which currently holds zero backups
description:
Filed 2026-08-17 alongside the closure of bead xdjbs, at PO instruction. This is an OPERATIONAL action on the running instance, not a code change. No PR, no branch, no gates.

THE STATE, established by read-only investigation and recorded in full on xdjbs: /config/backups/ on the live ECM is empty. dbas_backup is registered but disabled (live row: enabled=0, schedule_type='manual', last_run_at NULL), task_schedules holds 7 rows and none is dbas_backup, and the backups directory mtime has not moved since 2026-04-21 - four months, predating the task's ship date. The task has never run on this instance. Retention is ruled out twice independently; this is never-ran, not ran-and-pruned.

Everything about that is the product working as designed. dbas_backup ships disabled by an explicit PO decision, reaffirmed 2026-08-17, so that ECM does not write to an operator's disk on a schedule nobody chose. The consequence is that somebody has to choose, and on this instance nobody has.

WHY IT IS TRACKED RATHER THAN JUST DONE. The PO was offered the option of simply enabling it without a bead and declined, on the grounds that four months of an empty directory is itself the evidence that an untracked backup intention does not happen on its own.

THE ACTION: enable dbas_backup on a schedule. docs/user_guide/backup-restore/backup-overview.md:115 already recommends daily as sufficient for most operators, so daily unless the PO wants otherwise. Reachable through Settings, Scheduled Tasks, DBAS Backup - or through the BackupScheduleBanner's 'Set one up' CTA, which dispatches OPEN_TASK_EDITOR_EVENT with taskId dbas_backup and is not a dead end.

ONE THING WORTH DECIDING FIRST: bead gi4zn (P1, open) means the standard redacted artifact still carries the XC/M3U username in cleartext. Scheduled backups produce exactly that artifact. Enabling a schedule before gi4zn ships means the instance starts accumulating artifacts with a known credential leak in them, on the same volume as journal.db. Either enable after gi4zn lands, or enable now and accept that the artifacts produced in the interim carry it. The PO has already decided gi4zn gates the one-click button for this same reason.

RELATED: xdjbs (closed, carries the full evidence), iij6s (the dismissible banner that let this state persist unnoticed), pui76 (the one-click control), 1vm5r (retention UI, stays P3 since nothing writes unattended until this bead is actioned).

title: One click permanently silences the only signal that an install has zero backups
description:
Found 2026-08-16 during the read-only investigation of beads pui76 and xdjbs. This is the finding that investigation considers the ACTUAL recoverability risk, ahead of the missing button both of those beads are about. Line references are the investigating engineer's; not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. BackupScheduleBanner is the only in-product signal that an ECM install has no enabled backup schedule and therefore no backups. It is a ONE-TIME banner, dismissible, and the dismissal is stored in localStorage - so it is per browser, per profile, and permanent. One click by one operator in one browser silences it forever, on an install that has never taken a backup and never will until somebody notices.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE MISSING BUTTON. dbas_backup ships disabled by an explicit PO decision, with the stated reason that a less-engaged operator must not silently end up with zero backups. The banner is the entire mechanism enforcing that intent. If the banner can be permanently dismissed without acting, the decision's safeguard is one click deep and the operator ends up in exactly the state the decision was written to prevent.

THE LIVED PROOF IS THIS INSTANCE. /config/backups/ is empty and the directory mtime has not moved since 2026-04-21, four months and predating dbas_backup's ship date - so the task has never run here, on a production instance, while the banner presumably fired at some point and was dismissed. Bead xdjbs records the full evidence.

WHAT TO DECIDE, because this is a product question and not only a bug: should the banner be non-dismissible until acted on; should it be dismissible but recurring on a cadence; should dismissal be per-install rather than per-browser-localStorage; or should the underlying decision change so dbas_backup ships enabled with a default schedule, at which point the banner's job changes entirely. Note the last option makes bead 1vm5r (retention_enabled / last_n / max_age in the Settings UI) a prerequisite rather than a P3, because unattended daily backups write unbounded full-instance ZIPs into the same volume as journal.db and retention_enabled currently defaults to False.

RELATED: pui76 (the one-click control, Small, mostly wiring), xdjbs (established as not-a-defect, the four questions answered), 1vm5r (retention UI), gi4zn (P1 - the redacted backup still leaks the XC/M3U username in cleartext, which a one-click button would make trivially easy to produce and share).
notes:
PO DECISIONS 2026-08-17 raise this bead's weight, twice over.

FIRST: dbas_backup stays DISABLED by default (D2). The PO kept the prior decision and explicitly identified this banner as the thing that failed rather than the decision. So this bead is no longer a side-observation about a dismissible banner - it is the ENTIRE enforcement mechanism for a standing product decision. If the banner can be permanently silenced by one click in one browser, the decision's safeguard is one click deep.

SECOND: the operator guide will now LEAD with taking a manual backup, then setting up a schedule (D4). The orchestrator flagged, and the PO accepted, that this means more operators will end up holding exactly one stale backup and no schedule - believing they are covered. That is precisely the state this banner exists to catch. Leading with the manual path makes the banner MORE load-bearing, not less.

So the sequencing question this bead should be read with: it wants to ship alongside or before the guide rewrite in pui76, not after it.
MERGED to dev in PR #878 at merge commit 552191b3 after required checks passed, including rendered QA and final CI.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in PR #878: zero-schedule warning now snoozes for at most 30 days, reappears after expiry, rejects forged longer snoozes, and clears when a schedule is enabled. Rendered Chromium QA and adversarial mutation checks passed; final review approved.

title: A debounced second channel load blanks the list 500ms after mount and closes any menu the operator has open
description:
Found by the project-engineer while diagnosing a CI-only guard failure during the Edit Mode epic's merge-blocking round (2026-08-16). Pre-existing, not introduced by that epic. Deliberately not fixed: touching load orchestration on a merge-blocking round is the wrong trade. Line references are the engineer's; not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. App.tsx:1749-1759, the 'Reload channels when search changes' effect, fires a SECOND full loadChannels() roughly 500ms after mount, in addition to the initial load. loadChannels() flips loadingStates.channels before it awaits, so ChannelsPane.tsx:7966 swaps the entire .pane-content group tree for a loading placeholder and back. Every ChannelListItem and GroupHeader unmounts and remounts.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE. Any menu open during that window is destroyed, because menuOpen is component-local state and the row that owns it unmounts. A real operator who lands on Channel Manager and immediately opens a channel row or group three-dot menu can have it vanish under them with no explanation. The list also visibly blanks.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and why it is worth trusting. An e2e guard passed locally and failed only in CI. The engineer instrumented the preview build with a MutationObserver and captured the ordering: /api/channels?page=1&page_size=500 at 617ms, ADD DIV.loading at 619ms with the dropdown node removed in the same batch, list rebuilt at 623ms, against a measurement landing at about 618ms. Fast hardware wins that race and slow CI hardware loses it.

The orchestrator had hypothesised a CSS change was responsible. That was disproven empirically: with the suspected max-width declarations removed, the same reproduction still failed. The cause is the unmount, not styling.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD. The guard spec now waits for no loading placeholder AND no channel-list request for a full second before measuring, stated as an invariant rather than a sleep. That makes the test honest about the race; it does not remove the race.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Establish why the search-reload effect fires on mount at all when the search term has not changed. A mount-time guard, or reusing the initial load, is likely enough. Verify against the case the effect exists for, an actual search change, and note that loadingStates.channels driving a full-tree swap is arguably the deeper issue: a background refresh should not blank a list the operator is interacting with.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-08-16 by PO triage, not forgotten. This bead was filed during the Edit Mode / channel numbering epic (PR #870) or its follow-up (PR #871), reviewed for operator impact, and consciously ranked below backup availability (beads pui76 and xdjbs - there is no way to take or schedule a DBAS backup from the UI, and the live instance holds zero backup artifacts).

title: Range renumber journals a starting number it did not send when consolidation is off
description:
Found by the technical-writer while documenting the bulk-commit contract for the Edit Mode epic (2026-08-16). Out of that pass's scope, not acted on. Line references are the writer's report and were not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. On the consolidate: false path, the executor sends startingNumber=None upstream while journaling the operation as having started at 1. Dispatcharr, receiving no starting number, picks its own. So the journal records a number ECM never sent and Dispatcharr may not have used, on the one surface the operator guide tells operators to trust for tracing what happened.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH THE EPIC THAT JUST SHIPPED. Bead ic884.2's fix round settled the omitted-startingNumber default as 1 across four layers: the frontend materialiser, the backend plan materialiser, the executor, and consolidation. Before that round, consolidation turned an omission into an explicit 0 while everything else defaulted to 1. The fix made all four agree on 1 as the PLAN value. What it did not reconcile is what actually goes on the wire when consolidation is off: the plan says 1, the journal says 1, and the request says None.

Under consolidate: true, which is what the ECM frontend always sends, consolidation materialises the start and the discrepancy does not arise. This is therefore a non-UI-caller defect: MCP tools, scripts and any direct API client that omits both startingNumber and consolidate.

USER VALUE. Same class as several defects this epic closed, and the reason it is worth filing rather than shrugging at: the journal is the operator-facing record of what the system did, and here it records an intent rather than an action. An operator reconciling ECM against Dispatcharr finds numbers that do not match what the journal claims, with no indication which is right.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Decide whether the executor should materialise the default before sending (so the wire matches the plan and the journal), or whether the journal should record the absence honestly. Materialising is probably right, since three of the four layers already treat 1 as the value rather than as a fallback, but confirm that sending an explicit start where none was sent before does not change Dispatcharr's behaviour for existing callers.

RELATED, from the same review pass, cheaper and unrelated: BulkCommitResponse declares 9 of 12 live fields and is not used as a response_model, and the frontend types name 3 of 6 validation issue types. Worth folding in if this bead is picked up, since both are the same documentation-drift-from-code shape.

title: Consolidation inverts submitted order for stream operations the way it did for channel numbers
description:
Found by the project-engineer while fixing the numbering half of exactly this defect (bead ic884.2 fix round 3, 2026-08-16). Deliberately left unfixed and flagged, with reasoning. Not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. backend/routers/channels.py _consolidate_operations emits reorderChannelStreams BEFORE addStreamToChannel and removeStreamFromChannel, regardless of the order the caller submitted them. A submitted addStream then reorder pair is therefore inverted: the reorder is applied against a stream list that does not yet contain the added stream, and the add lands afterwards, appending to whatever order the reorder produced. The operator asked for one final stream order and gets another.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. It is the same class as the numbering defect just closed, where consolidation destroyed last-write-wins across operation kinds and made the browser preview disagree with what Apply applied. That one was fixed as a property: a channel_number_owner map records which kind of operation last set each channel's number, so exactly one emitted operation writes it and emission order cannot change the answer.

The stream case needs the same treatment but a different mechanism, and it is genuinely broader: fixing it means changing GLOBAL emission ordering in that function rather than adding a per-channel ownership map. The engineer judged that too large to fold into a fix round unbriefed, which is the right call. It is also outside numbering entirely, so it was not covered by that round's invariant, and no external reviewer reported it.

WHAT MAKES IT LOWER SEVERITY THAN ITS NUMBERING SIBLING. Nothing in the frontend previews the resulting stream order, so there is no preview-versus-Apply divergence for an operator to be misled by; they simply get an order they did not ask for and can see it afterwards and fix it. The numbering version was worse precisely because the dialog actively promised the wrong outcome.

DO NOT scope a fix to the addStream-then-reorder pair. CLAUDE.md's rule about stating acceptance criteria as invariants was learned on this epic and this function has now produced three defects of the same shape: it silently dropped unrecognised operation types, it dropped a known field while rebuilding an operation from parts, and it inverted submitted order across kinds. The invariant is that consolidation never changes the outcome of any submitted operation sequence, for any operation kind. Reuse the ownership approach already proven for channel_number if it fits, and note _NUMBER_SCOPED_UPDATE_FIELDS is pinned against BulkUpdateChannelOp.model_fields so a new field forces a classification rather than being silently mishandled.
