title: bulkAssignChannelNumbers has no server-side staleness check, so a non-UI caller can silently clobber another operator's renumber
description:
Found by the project-engineer while implementing concurrent-change detection (bead ic884.4) on 2026-08-16. Deliberately scoped out and proposed as a follow-up. Not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. ic884.4 added a pre-Apply staleness check: the browser reads the server before Apply writes, compares against the session baseline, and offers a per-channel keep-mine / take-theirs reconcile. On the server side, an updateChannel operation carries expectedNumber and the executor refuses a write whose expectation has gone stale.

bulkAssignChannelNumbers cannot carry that guard. One upstream call places many channels, so there is no per-channel write for an expectedNumber to attach to. The browser's half of the protection still covers the Edit Mode UI, because the reconcile runs before the request is built. But a non-UI caller — an MCP agent, a script, any direct API client — issuing a range renumber has no check anywhere in the stack, and will silently overwrite whatever another operator did after it last read the lineup.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The MCP surface is a first-class caller in this product, not a corner. Bead ic884.4's whole premise is that a stale session must not silently overwrite newer work; that premise holds for the UI and does not hold for the API. A range renumber is also the highest-blast-radius numbering operation there is, since one call can move an entire group.

CONSTRAINED BY A MEASURED FACT. Dispatcharr 0.28.x offers no conditional update: a fetch of GET /api/schema/?format=json (HTTP 200, ~717KB) found zero occurrences of If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, ETag or 412, and no version or modified-at field on Channel or PatchedChannel. So this cannot be solved with upstream optimistic concurrency. It needs an ECM-side expectation, most plausibly a per-channel expected-number map on the operation itself rather than a single expectedNumber field, validated in the same place the executor already validates the single-write case.

DO NOT let the fix close only the demonstrated path. CLAUDE.md's rule about stating acceptance criteria as invariants was learned on this exact epic: the invariant is that no staged numbering write overwrites a server-side change made after its baseline was captured, from ANY caller, on any branch. A fix scoped to the range case that leaves another multi-write operation unguarded is the same defect again.

RELATED: backend/channel_number_apply.py, frontend/src/utils/channelNumberConcurrency.ts, and the ConcurrentNumberAcknowledgement shape {channelId, baselineNumber, serverNumber} which already binds a reconcile decision to the specific change it resolved.

title: 75 of 80 journal write call sites discard the return value, so a failed journal write is invisible to the caller
description:
Found by AST sweep of backend/ during bead kz089 round 5 (2026-08-16), after an external reviewer confirmed the defect on one endpoint. Deliberately scoped out of that round and filed here. Counts and line numbers are the engineer's report, pre-commit, and were not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE MECHANISM. journal.log_entry() converts write failures into a None return (backend/journal.py:258-266); journal.log_entries() returns False. Neither raises. A caller that ignores the return value therefore cannot distinguish a journalled mutation from an unjournalled one, and reports success either way. When the local journal database is read-only, unavailable, or out of disk, the upstream mutation has landed and nothing anywhere says the audit trail is missing.

THE SCOPE. An AST sweep found 75 of 80 call sites discard the return value. Ten are in routers/channels.py alone, all the same shape as the one already fixed: create_channel (:772), assign_channel_numbers (:1571), clear_auto_created_flag (:3584), merge_channels (:3889), delete_channel (:3941), add_stream_to_channel (:3986), add_streams_to_channel (:4054), remove_stream_from_channel (:4100), reorder_channel_streams (:4189), bulk_merge_channels (:4452). The remainder spread across routers/m3u.py (13), routers/channel_pipeline.py (9), routers/epg.py (8), task_engine.py (5) and 18 other modules.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED, so this bead does not redo it: the bulk-commit path and PATCH /api/channels/{id} both now route through the module-scope write_journal_rows helper, which retries row by row and reports the residue as journalRowsUnwritten on the response envelope. That helper is the mechanism to reuse; the pattern is established and tested.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN ONE SWEEP. Each remaining endpoint needs its own decision about WHERE the advisory hangs. Some return a bare upstream object with no envelope to extend, some return lists, some are fire-and-forget task-engine paths with no caller to tell at all. A mechanical sweep that bolts a field onto 75 responses would change 22 modules' response shapes without anyone having reasoned about the consumers, which is the failure mode this epic has hit repeatedly. Task-engine and scheduled-task paths in particular may want a log-and-alert route rather than a response field, since there is no synchronous caller.

USER VALUE. The operator guide tells operators the journal is how they trace a channel's history. Any of these 75 paths can produce a mutation with no trace and no warning. This is the same class as the two journal defects already closed in this epic, at 75x the surface.

SUGGESTED SEQUENCE. routers/channels.py's ten first, since the helper already lives in that module and they are the highest-traffic operator actions. Then decide the fire-and-forget policy for task_engine.py before touching the remaining routers, because that decision sets the shape for most of what is left.
notes:
PO DECISION 2026-08-16 on the fire-and-forget policy, which was the blocker on the remaining 65 call sites. The engineer's proposed SPLIT is accepted rather than one uniform rule.

RULE 1, where the row records ECM'S OWN EXECUTION and there is no synchronous caller: record the residue on the artifact that already exists for that run - the TaskExecution row - as a journal_rows_unwritten count, and log at ERROR. Do NOT fail the task. This covers the five task_engine.py lifecycle sites (start, cancel, fail, complete, error), which lose information that the TaskExecution row and the completion notification already carry, so alerting on them would be noise.

RULE 2, where a fire-and-forget path records an UPSTREAM MUTATION: raise the residue through the existing alert path. This covers scheduled paths that call Dispatcharr - tasks/dbas_sync.py and tasks/channel_pipeline.py are the named examples. A scheduled run that mutates channels and loses its journal rows is this bead's defect at its worst: nobody is watching, there is no response envelope, and the audit trail for a real change is simply gone.

Rejected: alert on everything (the lifecycle sites would generate alerts operators learn to ignore, and an ignored alert channel is worse than none), and log-only everywhere (closes the discarded-return-value defect while leaving the nobody-finds-out defect, which is how several defects in this codebase stayed invisible).

STATUS OF THIS BEAD. The ten routers/channels.py sites are fixed on branch fix/journal-truthfulness via a shared journal_rows_for() tail, with update_channel folded onto the same mechanism. This bead therefore stays OPEN after that branch merges: 65 sites across 21 modules remain - routers/m3u.py (13), channel_pipeline.py (9), epg.py (8), task_engine.py (5), cloud_targets.py (4), tasks/dbas_backup.py (4), and 15 modules with 1 to 3 each.

SUGGESTED SEQUENCE now that the policy is settled: apply rule 1 to task_engine.py first, since it is the smallest coherent set and proves the TaskExecution carrier works. Then rule 2 to the scheduled mutation paths, which is where the user value is. Then the remaining routers, which mostly have an envelope to hang the advisory on and can reuse the channels.py shape.
PARTIALLY FULFILLED by PR #871 (merge 8f7107eb, build 0.18.1-0112). NOT closed, and deliberately moved back to open rather than left in_progress, because nobody is working it.

WHAT LANDED: the ten routers/channels.py sites the bead named, via a shared journal_rows_for() tail with update_channel folded onto the same mechanism - one mechanism rather than eleven. assign-numbers and bulk-merge now write one batch under one id rather than N transactions, and bulk-merge flushes on its 422 exit so an earlier item's row does not leave with the exception. PATCH /api/channels/{id} and the bulk-commit path were already done by the preceding epic.

The 75-of-80 figure was CONFIRMED independently twice during this work - once by the implementing engineer with a smoke-tested scanner, once by a technical-writer running its own AST sweep - so the count in this bead is measured, not inherited.

WHAT REMAINS: 65 sites across 21 modules. routers/m3u.py (13), routers/channel_pipeline.py (9), routers/epg.py (8), task_engine.py (5), cloud_targets.py (4), tasks/dbas_backup.py (4), and 15 modules with 1 to 3 each. One of the 21 is routers/channel_groups.py itself: DELETE /api/channel-groups/orphaned still discards, in the same router whose sibling delete path this PR fixed. That is named in docs/api.md so the new section is not read as covering the whole router.

THE POLICY IS NOW SETTLED - see the earlier note on this bead for the PO's ratified split, and follow the sequence it gives: task_engine.py first to prove the TaskExecution carrier works, then the scheduled mutation paths where the user value is, then the remaining routers which mostly have an envelope to hang the advisory on and can reuse the channels.py shape.

DEFERRED 2026-08-16 by PO triage: the remaining 65 are lower operator value than backup availability (beads pui76 and xdjbs), which is where the next effort goes.

title: Two channel-number staging paths still create conflicts the operator only discovers at Apply
description:
Found by the project-engineer while implementing the duplicate warning and final-state preflight (beads vdxbx, ic884.2, ic884.5) on 2026-08-16. Both were out of that brief's scope and deliberately not fixed. Line references are the engineer's report and were not independently re-verified by the orchestrator. Two distinct defects, filed together because they are the same family: channel-number staging paths that skip a guard their siblings apply.

DEFECT 1 — Group Reorder never applies the automatic rename. handleGroupReorderConfirm (frontend/src/components/ChannelsPane.tsx:4767) is the ONLY channel-number staging path that does not apply the automatic channel rename, even when the auto_rename_channel_number setting is on. Every other renumber path does. An operator who reorders a group therefore ends up with channel numbers and channel names out of step, silently, and only on this one route.

Note this interacts with work that just shipped: bead ic884.5 added a rename preview to the Apply dialog which reproduces computeAutoRename against each staged operation's before-snapshot. Because this path stages no rename, the preview correctly shows none — the preview is honest, the producer is the gap. Fixing the producer should make the preview light up for this path with no preview change needed, and that is worth verifying rather than assuming.

DEFECT 2 — Shift and Renumber can manufacture a collision. Mass renumber's 'Shift & Renumber' option moves conflicting channels to endNum+1 and upward WITHOUT checking what already occupies those numbers. It can therefore create a duplicate that did not exist before the operation. Since bead ic884.2 shipped, the operator now discovers this at Apply, where the final-state preflight refuses the whole commit — which is a strictly better outcome than the silent duplicate it used to produce, but it means a routine bulk operation can now be refused for a conflict the operator did not knowingly create and was given no warning about while staging.

This is the shape CLAUDE.md's 'state acceptance criteria as invariants, not reproductions' rule warns about, and it is worth reading before fixing: an external reviewer blocked ic884.1 twice for exactly this, a fix that closed the demonstrated path while an adjacent branch still returned an occupied number. The invariant here is that no staging path may place a channel on a number it has not established is free, on any branch, at any magnitude.

SUGGESTED SEQUENCE. Defect 2 first, because it produces a refused Apply today and is therefore operator-visible. Defect 1 is a silent inconsistency and cheaper to fix once the shared occupancy check from defect 2 exists. frontend/src/utils/channelNumberPlan.ts (added by ic884.5) already holds canonical tenths-grid comparison and channelsHoldingNumber, so both fixes should reuse it rather than adding a third comparison site.

This bead was filed during the Edit Mode / channel numbering epic (PR #870) or its follow-up (PR #871), reviewed for operator impact, and consciously ranked below backup availability (beads pui76 and xdjbs - there is no way to take or schedule a DBAS backup from the UI, and the live instance holds zero backup artifacts).

The ranking that produced this: v3wr1, bv8n7 and 62ja6 were judged to have real operator impact and are the first candidates if this theme is resumed. jjjnh, 0by9g, oypsc and t683u are real confirmed defects with low operator impact - t683u is already fully auditable even though unconstrained, oypsc has nothing previewing the affected order, 0by9g is a wrong number in a journal line, and jjjnh affects non-UI callers only.

title: The updateChannel data bag and PATCH /api/channels/{id} body are unvalidated dicts forwarded to Dispatcharr wholesale
description:
Surfaced 2026-08-16 while closing a journal defect on the same code (bead kz089 round 4). Named as a deliberate residual rather than fixed, with reasoning. Line references are the engineer's; not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. BulkUpdateChannelOp.data and the body of PATCH /api/channels/{id} are unvalidated dicts forwarded to Dispatcharr wholesale. Any key any caller invents reaches upstream. The channel-number contract from bead ic884.1 is the only key-level check either path applies. This is reachable by any authenticated bulk-commit or PATCH caller, including through MCP, whose own six-field guard (mcp-server/_endpoint_contracts.py:101, _CHANNEL_PATCH_FIELDS) is CLIENT-SIDE and not enforced by the backend.

This is the same family as the validation gap closed on setProfileMembership, restoreChannelGroup and clearStreamStats in an earlier round of this epic. Those three got constrained models and Phase 0 resolution; this one did not.

WHY IT WAS LEFT OPEN. The engineer declined to constrain it in that round and the reasoning is worth preserving, because it is the reverse of the usual over-fitting trap. An allowlist would be a guess about callers that cannot be read: the two that can be read (the frontend's stageUpdateChannel, typed Partial<Channel>, and MCP's six-field guard) do not bound the third. The failure mode of guessing the allowlist too narrow is a silently refused Apply All on a field that was previously legal, which is worse than the gap it closes. Doing it properly needs a survey of the field values callers actually send, which could not be run without touching the operator's live instance.

The journal defect that surfaced it WAS fully closed by a different mechanism: describe_channel_update is now total over the payload, so an unrecognised field still produces a journal row rather than being silently absorbed. So the write surface is now fully AUDITABLE even though it is not constrained. That materially lowers the urgency but does not close it.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP. Survey what callers actually send before writing any filter. The engineer specifically flagged that writing the allowlist first is the way this goes wrong.

SURFACED IN THE SAME ROUND, UNRELATED, recorded so it is not lost: main.py:1526 shutdown_event() does not drain _BULK_COMMIT_BACKGROUND_TASKS. Delivery of cancellation to an in-flight bulk commit depends on the event loop's own task cancellation at close. Round 4 made the journal flush survive that cancellation, so rows are no longer lost, but an explicit lifespan drain (cancel, then await) would let the flush run while the app is fully alive and let the job status record what happened. Medium; narrower than it was before the flush fix.

title: Edit Mode staged work dies when the session expires; persist and restore it bound to the operator identity
description:
PO-authorised feature, built 2026-08-16 under epic r93hq. Filed as the tracking record for work that shipped in commit d0730bc7 — the agent that built it is hook-blocked from creating beads. To be closed with the epic.

WHY IT EXISTED. Earlier epic work put in-app navigation, browser Back/Forward and Sign Out through the Edit Mode exit guard so staged channel work could not be silently discarded. One path could not be guarded: session expiry, a failed token refresh, or a 401/403 from /me clears the user in useAuth, ProtectedRoute swaps the app for LoginPage, and the in-memory staged ledger dies. Apply is impossible at that moment because the session is already dead and every commit call would 401. The PO chose persistence over the cheaper 'tell them what was lost' option.

WHAT SHIPPED. stagedOperations plus the undo grouping are serialised to sessionStorage under a fixed key, stamped with operatorKey = auth_provider#user.id. The key is fixed rather than per-operator deliberately: a foreign ledger has to be findable in order to be destroyed. On mismatch the ledger is cleared, not withheld, in useEditMode's first-render lazy initializer before the persistence effect can run. Restore is OFFERED rather than automatic, because part of a ledger may not survive staleness checks and a silent restore drops the operator into Edit Mode holding a quietly smaller ledger with Apply as the next action. Twelve-hour age bound. A standing badge marks a restored session, because the change count reads identically for restored and fresh work and that difference decides whether Apply is trustworthy.

THE ONE THING NOT DERIVABLE, and it is not a derivation defect: the undo GROUPING. stagedOperations records what will be applied; the undo stack records how the operator grouped it. A profile-membership change over 20 channels is 20 operations and 1 undo entry, stagedOperationCount is localUndoStack.length, and handleExitEditMode tests it before it will open the Apply dialog at all. One entry per operation would report 20 changes for one action; none would make Apply unreachable.

BACKLOG CANDIDATE FOUND HERE, worth acting on if anyone re-wires it: ChannelsPane.tsx:1392 is 'void onCreateChannel;' while the prop is still threaded from App.tsx:3132 through ChannelManagerTab.tsx:618. It is dead code, but it is currently the ONLY thing preventing a data:image/ or blob: logo URI from reaching a persisted staged operation — LogoModal accepts both. If that prop is ever re-wired, logoUrl must be re-audited against what may enter sessionStorage. The audit at build time found the ledger carries names, numbers, ids, tvg_id, tvc_guide_stationid and logoUrl, and no credentials, tokens or file bytes.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits d0730bc7, 0599b372.

Serialises stagedOperations plus the undo grouping to sessionStorage, stamped with operatorKey = auth_provider#user.id. Provider-qualified because User.id is a row id and nothing forbids a local id colliding with a Dispatcharr one.

THE KEY IS FIXED RATHER THAN PER-OPERATOR, deliberately: a foreign ledger has to be findable in order to be DESTROYED. On mismatch it is cleared, not withheld, in useEditMode's first-render lazy initializer before the persistence effect can run - so another operator's staged work is gone from the tab before the app paints. Proven at three layers including a browser test asserting sessionStorage is null after paint.

Restore is OFFERED, not automatic, because part of a ledger may not survive staleness checks and a silent restore drops the operator into Edit Mode holding a quietly smaller ledger with Apply as the next action. The dialog has no Escape and no click-away - both would destroy staged work by accident, the exact failure the epic's exit guard exists to stop.

STALENESS IS TRANSITIVE: a dropped createChannel takes everything referencing its temp id, or a negative primary key goes back on the wire. bulkAssignChannelNumbers drops WHOLE, because its numbers are positional. Stream membership is projected through the ledger rather than read off the server, since staging add-then-remove in one session is legal. Three id classes are deliberately unchecked, each named in the module header with its reason.

ONE THING WAS NOT DERIVABLE and the analysis is worth keeping: the undo GROUPING. stagedOperations says what will be applied; the undo stack says how the operator grouped it. A profile change over 20 channels is 20 operations and 1 undo entry, and stagedOperationCount IS localUndoStack.length, which handleExitEditMode tests before it will open the Apply dialog at all.

A final cross-component review found the ledger surviving a Discard when sign-out unmounted the tree before the clearing effect ran - so a decision the operator made was reversible on next sign-in, and after Apply could repeat non-idempotent creates. Now cleared SYNCHRONOUSLY on an operator decision only; an unmount clears nothing, so session expiry and a forced 401 still preserve it.

Audited what the ledger carries: names, numbers, ids, tvg_id, tvc_guide_stationid, logoUrl. No credentials, tokens or file bytes. The secrets ratchet was smoke-tested with a planted key before its clean result was trusted.

title: The immediate delete-group path writes no journal row, so half the delete trail exists only for bulk commits
description:
Found by the project-engineer while making the journal row a required part of recording an upstream write, for bead kz089 (2026-08-16). Out of that round's brief. Line references are the engineer's report, not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. backend/routers/channel_groups.delete_channel_group — the immediate, non-Edit-Mode delete path fixed under bead auocn — writes NO journal row at all. Not for the channels it reparents, not for the group deletion itself. The bulk-commit path now writes both: one update row per reparented channel plus the group_delete row, all under the run's batch_id, because kz089 round 3 made the journal row a required argument of recording a landed write.

So the same operator-visible action produces a full journal trail through one route and silence through the other. The immediate route is the one reachable from the MCP delete_channel_group tool and from any direct API client, which is precisely where auocn established the fix pays, since the Edit-Mode UI menu for it is currently gated off.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN PASSING. The hook now exists: reparent_group_channels gained an on_channel_moved callback for exactly this shape. Wiring only that callback would produce HALF a trail, rows for the moved channels and nothing for the delete, which is arguably worse than silence because it reads as a completed move with no explanation. Doing it properly means giving the immediate path the same row-with-write discipline the bulk path now has, which is a small refactor rather than a callback hookup.

SECOND, SMALLER HOLE, same invariant, recorded so it is not lost: OperationLedger.record_applied() does not require record_persisted(), so a branch that writes upstream and tells the ledger nothing at all is still expressible. Three branches legitimately apply WITHOUT writing (createGroup on an existing name, add-stream and remove-stream when the stream is already in the desired state), so closing it needs a second sentinel distinguishing applied-without-writing from applied-and-forgot-to-say. The engineer named this rather than claiming invariant 1 was fully closed.

USER VALUE. An operator tracing what happened to a channel finds the group deletion that moved it only if it went through Edit Mode. docs/user_guide/channels-streams/the-journal.md tells operators the journal is how they trace a channel's history by name; for this action through this route, it is not.

RELATED: backend/bulk_commit_accounting.py (record_write, record_persisted, nothing_to_journal), backend/channel_group_reparent.py (on_channel_moved).
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #871 (merge 8f7107eb, build 0.18.1-0112). Commits af044792, 80637152.

The immediate, non-Edit-Mode delete path now writes the trail the bulk path already left: a per-move row queued the instant each reparent PATCH returns, a group_delete row only when the delete actually landed, one shared batch_id, flushed in a finally on every exit, with journalRowsUnwritten on the 200.

THE BEAD'S WARNING WAS HEEDED. It said wiring the on_channel_moved hook alone would produce HALF a trail - rows for moved channels and nothing for the delete - which reads as a completed move with no explanation. That is exactly what was avoided.

BEYOND THE BEAD, and this is the part worth carrying forward: OperationLedger.record_applied() now RAISES unless the operation recorded a write or called applied_without_writing(reason). That closes a hole the preceding epic disclosed honestly and left open - a branch that wrote upstream and told the ledger nothing was still expressible. An external reviewer confirmed all three uses of the new escape hatch are genuine no-write branches (add-stream already present, remove-stream already absent, group already mapped) and that it is not becoming a lazy default.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS WORK, in the same router: DELETE /api/channel-groups/orphaned still discards its journal result. Named explicitly in docs/api.md so the new section cannot be read as covering the whole router. It is one of the 65 sites remaining under bead ftidn.

title: Bulk-commit envelope cannot report a multi-side-effect operation that landed partially
description:
Found by the project-engineer while implementing the bulk-commit accounting invariant for bead e9e5o (2026-08-15), and recorded in the module docstring of backend/bulk_commit_accounting.py rather than papered over. Not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. The bulk-commit envelope carries exactly one outcome per operation: applied or failed. deleteChannelGroup has two side effects in sequence — it reparents the group's member channels to a fallback group, then deletes the now-empty group. If the reparent lands and the delete fails, there is no way to say so. The operation is reported as FAILED, which is the safer of the two available lies but is still not what happened: the channels really did move, and they stay moved.

WHY IT WAS LEFT. The engineer chose 'failed' deliberately. Marking it applied would tell an operator the group is gone when it is not, which is the worse error. Reporting it accurately needs a third outcome shape in the envelope, which is a contract change rather than a bug fix, and the accounting invariant landed in the same commit was already enforcing applied + failed == len(operations). Adding a partial-outcome category touches that invariant, the audit in finalize_bulk_commit_result, the MCP presentation layer and docs/api.md together.

USER VALUE. Same family as the rest of this epic: the system reports something that is not what occurred. An operator who retries the 'failed' delete finds the channels already moved and may not understand why, and an MCP agent acting on the envelope has no way to learn that a reparent landed. Narrower than its siblings because it errs toward under-claiming rather than over-claiming, which is why it was filed instead of fixed.

RELATED CONTEXT WORTH READING FIRST: backend/bulk_commit_accounting.py (OperationLedger, record_setup_failure, finalize_bulk_commit_result) and the auocn work on backend/channel_group_reparent.py, which established the reparent-then-delete sequence and its own separate limitation that Dispatcharr 0.28.x offers no conditional update.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Decide whether the envelope gains a partial-outcome category or whether multi-side-effect operations are decomposed into separately-reported operations. The second may be cleaner and would also serve any future operation with more than one upstream write.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #871 (merge 8f7107eb, build 0.18.1-0112). Commit 80637152.

The bulk-commit envelope can now report an operation that landed writes of its own and then failed. deleteChannelGroup reparents channels then deletes the group; if the reparent lands and the delete fails, the operation is no longer reported as a flat failure while the channels stay moved.

THE SHAPE CHOSEN, and why: a partial-outcome CATEGORY (operationsPartiallyApplied plus errors[].sideEffectsLanded), not decomposition into separately-reported operations. Decomposition would break the identity between operations SUBMITTED and operations REPORTED - which the accounting rule is written on and which errors[].operationId correlates against. Five staged things would read as six outcomes, and every consumer comparing counts to len(operations) would need rework.

IT IS DERIVED, NOT DECLARED. A record_write inside an open operation is BY DEFINITION a landed write that is not that operation's outcome, so the ledger already sees it and no branch has to remember to say so. That is the same make-it-impossible shape the preceding epic used for the accounting counters and the journal row.

The audit still raises: operationsPartiallyApplied must match the ledger, can never exceed operationsFailed, and each one must name itself via sideEffectsLanded. An external reviewer verified the derivation cannot double-count and that the audit stays satisfiable.

Also changed, and documented: partial is now (applied > 0 or partiallyApplied > 0) and (failed > 0 or incomplete > 0), so a run whose only operation failed after landing a write returns operationsApplied: 0 with partial: true.

title: Revert to this checkpoint writes to the server immediately from an Edit Mode only toolbar
description:
Found by the project-engineer while enumerating every Edit Mode action for bead kz089 (2026-08-15). Out of that bead's brief, deliberately not fixed, filed here. Line references are the engineer's report and were not independently re-verified by the orchestrator.

THE FINDING. The HistoryToolbar's 'Revert to this checkpoint' is rendered ONLY in Edit Mode (App.tsx:3083), and it calls api.updateChannel, api.addStreamToChannel, api.removeStreamFromChannel and api.reorderChannelStreams IMMEDIATELY (useChangeHistory.ts:414). Undo and Redo, sitting beside it in the same toolbar, ARE correctly swapped for local staged variants when Edit Mode is active. This one is not.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST ANOTHER kz089 ITEM. kz089 closed the mechanical cases: six affordances were converted to staged operations and three that genuinely cannot stage now carry an explicit irreversible-action acknowledgement. This one resisted that treatment because the question it raises is a design decision, not a mechanism: what SHOULD reverting to a checkpoint mean inside a staging session? Plausible answers include reverting the staged working copy to the checkpoint rather than the server, refusing the action while changes are staged, or treating it as another irreversible action with an acknowledgement. Each implies a different mental model of what a checkpoint is, and picking one is the PO's call.

USER VALUE. Same class as the epic that produced it. An operator inside a mode whose whole promise is 'nothing is real until Apply' clicks a control in that mode's own toolbar and writes to Dispatcharr. Discard does not undo it. The two controls immediately next to it behave the opposite way, which is the strongest possible signal that this one is an oversight rather than a deliberate exception.

ALSO OBSERVED, lower severity, recorded so it is not lost: Pending Merges accept/dismiss (ChannelManagerTab.tsx:539 subnav, ungated; PendingMergesPage.tsx:229/234) is reachable while Edit Mode changes are staged. It is a separate view with its own confirmations, so the engineer judged it reporting-only rather than a defect. Worth a glance if this bead is picked up, since the two share a mental model.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP. Decide the semantics before writing code. The mechanical work is small once the answer is chosen; choosing wrong is what costs.
notes:
PO DECISION 2026-08-16: SPLIT THEM. Undo/Redo stay in Edit Mode operating on staged changes; the checkpoint list moves OUT of Edit Mode, where its own premise is true. Options rejected: refuse-while-staged (closes the hole, leaves the incoherence), revert-the-staged-copy (creates two kinds of checkpoint that look identical in one list), and an irreversible-action acknowledgement (acknowledging the write does not make overwriting the working copy coherent).

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, from reading the code on 2026-08-16.

LINE REFERENCES ARE STALE. The toolbar renders at ChannelsPane.tsx:6174, gated on 'isEditMode && onUndo && onRedo && onCreateSavePoint && onRevertToSavePoint && onDeleteSavePoint' at :6173. revertToSavePoint is wired at App.tsx:3296 (App.tsx:638 is only the destructure) and reaches the toolbar via ChannelManagerTab.tsx:660. The bead's App.tsx:3083 no longer resolves.

WHAT REVERT ACTUALLY DOES. A checkpoint is {name, historyIndex, channelSnapshot[]}, the snapshot holding channel_number, name, channel_group_id and streams per channel. Reverting takes history.past.slice(savePoint.historyIndex).reverse(), awaits executeReverseOperation on each - immediate API calls - then overwrites the local channel list from the snapshot, clears the redo stack and sets hasUnsavedChanges false.

A HYPOTHESIS THAT LOOKED RIGHT AND IS WRONG, recorded so nobody re-derives it: reverting does NOT issue reverse API calls against un-applied staged changes. recordChange is called only on the non-Edit-Mode branch - verified at App.tsx:2863-2881, where the isEditMode arm calls stageBulkAssignNumbers and only the else arm records. So history.past contains exclusively changes that really were applied upstream.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, which is why splitting is the fix. The toolbar is visible ONLY inside Edit Mode, while the checkpoint list it carries can only have been built OUTSIDE Edit Mode - and clearHistory() runs on every Edit Mode exit path (App.tsx:737, 789, 798). So one toolbar serves two data sources with inverted visibility: Undo/Redo read the staged ledger, the checkpoint list reads applied server history. Reverting mid-session therefore writes to Dispatcharr underneath staged work AND overwrites the channel list that Edit Mode's working copy derives from. The bead frames this as 'writes immediately while Undo/Redo beside it are staged', which is true but is the symptom.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE. The gating expression treats the toolbar as one unit, so splitting means the checkpoint list needs a home outside Edit Mode that it does not currently have. That is the bulk of the work; the Edit Mode side is a subtraction. Check whether checkpoints can be CREATED in Edit Mode today (onCreateSavePoint is passed through the same gate) and decide what that should mean once the list lives elsewhere.

This bead was filed during the Edit Mode / channel numbering epic (PR #870) or its follow-up (PR #871), reviewed for operator impact, and consciously ranked below backup availability (beads pui76 and xdjbs - there is no way to take or schedule a DBAS backup from the UI, and the live instance holds zero backup artifacts).

title: Accepting a pending merge reports success even when no stream matched, so Dispatcharr may never be updated
description:
Found by the project-engineer while enumerating dedup trigger paths for bead ok8tj (2026-08-15). Out of that bead's scope, not acted on, filed here. NOT independently re-verified by the orchestrator — treat the line references as the engineer's report and confirm before fixing.

THE FINDING. backend/routers/channel_merges.py:1101-1114 — accepting a pending merge whose stream-name match is ZERO or AMBIGUOUS still flips the row to 'merged', writes a journal entry, and returns HTTP 200. frontend/src/components/PendingMergesPage.tsx:198 treats any non-throwing response as success, so the operator sees the merge confirmed and the row leave the queue.

WHY IT MATTERS. The upstream Dispatcharr instance may never have been updated. The operator is told a destructive-adjacent reconciliation happened, the queue row is gone, and the journal agrees with the false version. There is no in-product signal that anything was skipped, and no way to find the affected merges afterwards except by comparing ECM against Dispatcharr by hand.

This is the same defect CLASS as ok8tj (an outcome the operator cannot distinguish from success) but a different SHAPE: ok8tj was silence where a modal was expected, this is a positive success claim that may be untrue. ok8tj's fix does not touch it.

RELATED, same enumeration pass, lower severity — decide whether to fold in or drop:
- backend/routers/channel_merges.py:1339 — stream search silently truncates at the 500-row page ceiling, logger.warning only, so a candidate past row 500 is invisible.
- backend/channel_pipeline_executor.py:1426 — if the dedup hook raises unexpectedly the channel is created as though no candidate existed, producing a duplicate with no operator-visible trace.
- backend/tasks/channel_pipeline.py:482 — the pending-merges toast is suppressed entirely when a run had failed actions, so the pending count is announced nowhere proactively on exactly the runs most likely to need attention.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Accepting a merge that could not be applied upstream should not report success: either refuse with an actionable reason, or apply and report partial completion naming what was skipped. Whichever is chosen, the journal must record what actually happened rather than the intent.
notes:
PO DECISION 2026-08-16: an unapplicable merge KEEPS ITS QUEUE ROW, marked unapplied, so it stays in front of the operator and can be retried once the cause clears.

This CHANGES what was built. The implementation on branch fix/journal-truthfulness currently transitions the row to 'merged' and removes it from the queue, carrying dispatcharr_updated:false, an unapplied_reason, a merge_unapplied journal row and a UI notice. That shape was chosen because refusing outright would reverse ADR-008 section D6's audit-first contract, and an external reviewer confirmed it is internally consistent. The PO's objection is not correctness but placement: the reason outlives the row, but only an operator who goes looking in the journal will ever find it.

WHAT THE DECISION REQUIRES. The row stays in Pending Merges, visibly flagged as not applied, carrying its reason, and remains retryable. A retry that succeeds should behave like an ordinary accept. Rejected: leaving it as built (findable but out of sight), and refusing the accept outright (reverses the ADR and discards the case where the operator wants the decision recorded even though ECM could not apply it).

CONSEQUENCES TO WORK THROUGH RATHER THAN ASSUME. This needs an ADR-008 amendment, since D6's audit-first contract and D1's accept envelope both describe the current shape. It needs a queue state that is neither 'pending' nor 'merged' - or a flag on 'pending' - and every consumer of that state audited, including the count badge, the bulk accept path and the MCP dedup tools. The three-valued dispatcharr_updated (true / false / null-for-replay) already exists and should map onto it rather than being duplicated. And the idempotent-replay path needs re-thinking: today a replay returns null because that request obtained no upstream evidence, which is a different thing from a row that is deliberately still queued.

DO NOT scope this to the no-match case. The unapplied reasons are: no match, lookup failed, page truncated so uniqueness is unknown, and a single match with no usable id. All four leave the merge unapplied and all four must behave the same way.
PO RATIFICATION 2026-08-16 of the metric contract change, recorded here because docs/sre/slos.md now asserts it and the evidence needs to be findable outside a chat transcript.

THE CHANGE. ecm_dedup_merge_requests_total gained the label value status="unapplied", in commit 379b0a6b. The metric is under the standing BD-M locked contract, so this is a contract change and not an implementation detail.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED. The same day's PO decision keeps an unapplicable merge in the queue, flagged, rather than transitioning it. SLI-10b's numerator counts terminal-state transitions OUT of the pending queue. A flagged row makes no such transition, so continuing to bump status="success" would have reported the queue as clearing while flagged rows accumulated in it, and would have suppressed ECMDedupPendingMergeResolutionStale on exactly the installs that most need it. Dropping the emit entirely was considered and is worse: the request did happen, and omitting it shrinks SLI-10c's error-rate denominator instead.

WHAT THE PO WAS SHOWN AND CHOSE. Three options were put: ratify the new label; ratify but hold the merge for an SRE review of the SLI maths first; or revert it and file separately, shipping in the knowledge that the success counter is wrong and the stale-resolution alert suppressed. The PO chose to RATIFY. The change is additive - {status=~"success|dismissed"} and {status="error"} are unaffected, no alert rule or recording rule changed, and SLO-10's cardinality bound moves from about 4 to about 5.

WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS. The engineer who introduced the label flagged, correctly, that it needed ratification and that it had not been given at the time of its report. A later documentation pass then wrote 'PO-ratified' into docs/sre/slos.md:459 and :646. Both statements were true at their respective moments, but the engineer had no visibility into the PO exchange and was right to refuse to let an unevidenced sign-off stand in an SLO document, where a false provenance claim is durable and gets trusted later. The claim is correct; this note is the durable record behind it.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #871 (merge 8f7107eb, build 0.18.1-0112). Commits a57b318e, cac0112a, 301350b4, 3e04ed88, 379b0a6b.

THE BEAD'S SYMPTOM: accepting a pending merge with a zero or ambiguous stream match flipped the row to 'merged', journalled it, returned 200, and the frontend treated any non-throwing response as success - while Dispatcharr may never have been updated.

THE DEFECT WAS ONE LAYER DEEPER THAN THE BEAD SAID. The resolver collapsed THREE distinct facts into an empty list: the lookup FAILED, the search hit its 500-row page ceiling, and there genuinely was no match. A fourth was found in passing: a single match carrying no usable id. Reporting a lookup outage as 'no streams matched' turns an infrastructure failure into an accusation against the operator's catalogue.

PO DECISION 2026-08-16, which changed what had already been built: an unapplicable merge KEEPS its queue row, flagged and retryable, rather than transitioning and leaving. The first implementation removed the row and was internally consistent - an external reviewer confirmed that - but the reason survived only in the journal, where an operator had to go looking. Implemented as a flag on 'pending' (migration 0043, pending_merges.unapplied_reason), not a fourth status; accept transitions only when it applied and CLEARS the flag on a retry that lands.

THE FIX THAT MATTERED MOST was a type change, not a check: StreamLookup.conclusive_match() is now the only way to get a stream id out, and it is shut whenever completeness is unknown in either direction. The accept path no longer indexes matches at all. Verified as a property over all 24 cells of (failed x truncated x 0|1|2 matches x usable id); the reviewer's reproduction was one cell.

THREE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW ROUNDS, and two of them found regressions the previous round's fix had introduced - moving journal-row construction earlier to survive cancellation put it in front of a null check, and produced a row asserting a merge that had not happened.

A LOCKED METRIC CHANGED, PO-ratified, recorded in this bead's notes with its reasoning: ecm_dedup_merge_requests_total gained status='unapplied', because SLI-10b counts terminal transitions out of the queue and a flagged row makes none. Counting it as success would have reported the queue clearing while flagged rows accumulated, suppressing ECMDedupPendingMergeResolutionStale.

ADR-008 amended at D1, D3, D5, D6, D7 and D8.

title: Operator-facing follow-ups from the auth and channel-numbering batch
description:
PO-approved 2026-08-15. Six beads survived a value review of the twenty filed during the 9kwzp auth epic, the upkp1 rotation work, and the i85dg / ic884.1 channel-numbering work. The other fourteen were DELETED as having no operator-facing value: refactors, preventive classes, developer tooling, documentation accuracy, and one hypothetical guarded by data that does not exist.

NOT STARTED. The PO approved these as worth keeping, not as work to begin.

TWO THEMES, and the first is the one worth pulling on.

THEME 1, SILENT WRONG VALUE: ECM accepts a number or an action and quietly does something else. Four of the six are this shape, and so was the bug the PO reported that started this work (auto-renumber overflowing into other groups, bead i85dg). That is five instances of one defect class in one area, which suggests the CLASS is the finding rather than any individual bug.
  - fprsq (P2): 'Push channels down' is a silent no-op on manual-entry insert. The handler never reads the argument, so the operator clicks a button that does nothing and gets a duplicate channel number instead.
  - ay3iq (P2): the Channel Pipeline accepts a fractional channel_number spec, then silently assigns an unrelated integer. Partly created by ic884.1 making 1.1 valid without making it work.
  - j3pyx (P3): renumber inputs parse with parseInt, so a typed 1.5 silently becomes 1. Same shape, and it contradicts the reject-not-normalize policy the PO chose for ic884.1.
  - xztoc (P2): backend/reset_password.py enforces uppercase/lowercase/number rules that auth/password.py deliberately dropped, so an operator recovering by CLI hits rules the UI and API do not have.

THEME 2, two standalone hygiene items the PO judged worth keeping:
  - 2u4e0 (P2): eleven outbound-test sinks stay open under require_auth:false, the named residual of the jy006 decision. An anonymous caller on an auth-disabled instance can exercise stored DNS-provider credentials, while the masked settings read is refused.
  - 5u5h9 (P3): the password-reset success path logs the full account email twice per event.

SEQUENCING NOTE for whoever grooms this: fprsq and j3pyx both touch the channel-number entry points ic884.1 just enforced, so they are cheaper together than apart. ay3iq needs a product decision first (honour tenths in the pipeline, or reject a fractional spec at validation) and should not be started until that is made.
close_reason: All six children shipped in a single PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110): fprsq, ay3iq, xztoc, 2u4e0, j3pyx, 5u5h9. Two PO decisions taken 2026-08-15: ay3iq honours tenths in the executor (option a); 2u4e0 closes all twelve outbound-test sinks with the operator cost accepted. THEME 1 held up: treating the silent-wrong-value CLASS as the finding surfaced four more instances the individual beads never named, all fixed in the same PR: an occupied channel 0 read as free by the pipeline, an exhausted min-max range spilling onto an occupied number, two truncation sites in the pipeline ActionEditor, and a rule remaining saveable while a start field displayed a rejection. The first two shipped long before this batch (channel 0 back to v0.13.0-0010) and carry their own CHANGELOG entries. Three rounds of Codex review: round 1 found three defects, round 2 blocked on two of the three not being fixed at the invariant level, round 3 approved. No follow-up beads filed, per PO instruction.

title: Channel Pipeline silently ignores a fractional channel_number spec
description:
Found during bead ic884.1 (PR pending, build 0109), and partly CREATED by it: making one-decimal values canonical means a pipeline rule can now be set to 1.1, pass validation, and then be silently discarded at execution.

backend/channel_pipeline_executor._get_next_channel_number is typed -> int and understands only an integer literal, the string 'auto', and an integer 'min-max' range. A rule whose set_channel_number or create_channel.channel_number is 1.1 is IN CONTRACT after ic884.1, passes the schema validation ic884.1 added, and is then dropped at execution: the channel gets the next free INTEGER with no error and no log line.

So the operator sets a fractional number, ECM accepts it, and the channel comes out with a different number. Silent wrong-result, which is the worst of the three possible outcomes (correct, error, silently wrong).

Note this was NOT reachable before ic884.1, because nothing validated the field at all and the executor's integer-only behaviour was the de facto contract. ic884.1 deliberately did not change executor numbering semantics, which was the right call for that bead's scope, but it leaves this gap open.

DECISION NEEDED, two coherent options:
(a) Honour a one-decimal spec: walk the tenths grid, matching the 0.1 insertion step the frontend already uses and the tenths grid frontend/src/utils/channelNumberShift.ts plans on. Consistent with the rest of the app.
(b) Reject a fractional spec at validation time with a 'whole number' message, making the executor's integer-only contract explicit rather than implicit.

Do NOT leave it silently dropping. Whichever is chosen, add a test that a fractional spec produces either the fractional result or a clear error, never an integer substitution.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). PO decision 2026-08-15: option (a), honour tenths. ActionExecutor._get_next_channel_number now walks a tenths grid in integer ticks; occupancy moved to a tick set; return type widened to int|float with whole numbers still rendering as 800 not 800.0. validate_channel_number_spec relaxed to the canonical contract and the PROVISIONAL docstring removed; PIPELINE_CHANNEL_NUMBER_RULE_MESSAGE shrank to the two shapes the executor genuinely cannot honour (a fractional range, and a literal not written as plain digits). Three Codex rounds also closed: an occupied channel 0 read as free (shipped bug, own CHANGELOG entry), a float-bound duplicate above 2**49, an exhausted min-max range spilling onto an occupied number (shipped bug, own entry), and a rule remaining saveable while its start field showed a rejection.

title: Protect backup confidentiality and bound encrypted-artifact KDF work
description: User value: theft or upload of a backup does not disclose ECM identities, password hashes, TLS private keys, or credentials, and a malicious encrypted artifact cannot exhaust ECM resources. Legacy saved ZIPs are plaintext, may contain journal.db and tls/, lack explicit 0600 mode, and DBAS scheduled encryption is not the default. Encrypted artifact headers can supply unbounded scrypt parameters before authentication. Evidence: backend/routers/backup.py:93-94,205-224,423-433,4350-4379; backend/tasks/dbas_backup.py:180-274; backend/dbas/artifact_crypto.py:198-236,291-321.
acceptance_criteria: Every persisted/off-host backup class has an explicit confidentiality policy; plaintext artifacts omit authentication hashes, TLS private keys, and live credentials or are replaced by authenticated encryption; local artifacts are 0600; scheduled recovery has a practical key strategy and verified restore; encrypted headers require exact supported version/KDF/AEAD and tightly bounded n/r/p, salt, nonce, and chunk parameters before KDF invocation; malformed/extreme fixtures prove KDF is never called; docs and redaction tests match actual artifact contents.

title: Correct security-critical operator guidance and high-risk UI confirmations
description: User value: home-lab operators understand which surfaces are protected and do not lose access/data by following stale instructions or one-click destructive controls. Current docs normalize plaintext MCP URLs, describe retired OAuth, use wrong DR ports/actions, misstate password and TLS restore behavior, and imply ECM TLS protects MCP. High-risk UI actions have inconsistent warnings/confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Current static-key MCP threat/rotation guidance is authoritative; DR commands are exercised against the disposable environment and use current ports/tasks; restore docs match password/privilege collision behavior; DBAS TLS coverage is stated accurately; TLS-vs-MCP transport is explicit; disabling auth, key rotation, destructive restore/delete, and equivalent high-impact actions use accessible scoped confirmations; security-critical doc claims have executable regression checks where practical.

title: Make settings secret persistence atomic and owner-only
description: User value: ECM credentials are not exposed through permissive local modes and key rotation cannot corrupt settings or unexpectedly disable MCP. settings.json contains multiple plaintext secrets and is written directly without locking, fsync, atomic replacement, or explicit 0600 mode. Evidence: backend/config.py:738-809; mcp-server/config.py:63-90; compare backend/auth/settings.py:290-320.
acceptance_criteria: settings.json uses the proven locked temporary-file, fsync, atomic-replace, directory-fsync, mode-0600 pattern; last-known-good state survives failed/interrupted writes; concurrent writers yield a complete valid document; behavior is independent of umask; MCP key rotation remains immediately and reliably observable.

title: Protect browser sessions when ECM TLS is enabled
description: User value: operators who enable HTTPS do not unknowingly transmit login and refresh cookies over the still-available HTTP listener. Cookie helpers always emit secure=False, HTTP remains exposed, and UI/docs call it a normal fallback. Evidence: backend/auth/routes.py:389-441 and call sites 712,1148,1310,1762; docker-compose.yml:6-8; frontend/src/components/settings/TLSSettingsSection.tsx:345-351.
acceptance_criteria: HTTPS login/refresh cookies include Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax based on trusted external-scheme/TLS configuration; HTTP cannot receive authenticated cookies after TLS activation except through an explicit documented break-glass mode; trusted proxy behavior is tested; HSTS/redirect behavior is applied only where safe; UI/docs accurately communicate fallback risk.

title: Isolate and harden the ECM MCP sidecar
description: User value: compromise of the AI-facing MCP process does not expose all ECM credentials, data, TLS keys, backups, and encryption material. MCP runs as root and mounts the entire /config volume read-only although it needs one service key. Evidence: mcp-server/Dockerfile:1-22; docker-compose.mcp.yml:10-15; mcp-server/config.py:13-90.
acceptance_criteria: MCP runs as a fixed non-root UID; it receives only narrowly scoped key material and cannot open settings.json, auth_settings.json, journal.db, tls, or backups; root filesystem is read-only with dropped capabilities and no-new-privileges plus only required tmpfs/resources; key rotation and authenticated MCP health/tool integration still work; runtime-hardening assertions run in CI.

title: Enforce uniform safety policy for destructive MCP tools
description: User value: ambiguous instructions or prompt injection cannot delete backups, channels, groups, EPG sources, schedules, tags, notifications, or other state in one tool call. Existing content-bound confirmation guardrails cover only selected tools. Evidence: mcp-server/tools/_guardrails.py; unguarded examples in tools/system.py:184-207, epg.py:542-555, tasks.py:237-264, tags.py:204-222, streams.py:491-539.
acceptance_criteria: Every MCP tool is inventoried and classified read-only/mutating/destructive; all destructive or bulk operations require a mutation-free preview and expiring content-bound confirmation tied to the resolved target set; drift invalidates confirmation; batch caps remain enforced; appropriate MCP annotations are present; a registry test fails for an unclassified or one-call destructive tool.
close_reason: Completed in PR #886, exact reviewed head b374acc2 merged as 74b4a775. Preserved all MCP tools while adding uniform destructive previews, exact bounded single-use prepare/commit plans, staged refresh flows, public/private sidecar credential separation with request-bound backend claims, non-root shared-identity projection, recovery/audit parity, and deterministic CI test isolation. Terminal code/security/QA/SRE approved. Hosted Backend Tests passed in 12m15s; all four ECM/MCP AMD64/ARM64 image builds passed. Final exact CI-equivalent backend: 10,900 passed, 3 skipped, 2 deselected, 78.78%. All required checks green; no branch-protection bypass used.

title: Apply SSRF controls to stream preview and probing
description: User value: a compromised Dispatcharr, playlist, or stream record cannot use ECM to reach loopback, link-local, metadata, or other forbidden network services. Stream preview, redirects, probing, and bitrate measurement bypass the strong shared SSRF validator. Evidence: backend/routers/stream_preview.py:63-130; backend/stream_prober.py:1013-1173; backend/security/ssrf.py:340-445.
acceptance_criteria: HTTP preview/probe paths use resolve-once validation and revalidate every redirect; metadata/link-local/multicast destinations are always denied; LAN targets follow the configured policy/allowlist; FFmpeg destinations receive equivalent prevalidation or a documented bounded design; tests cover literal, DNS, mixed-answer, redirect, and DNS-rebinding cases while preserving legitimate configured IPTV access.
close_reason: Merged PR #883 exact head 64ffd47b / merge 72bdff74. Code, security, QA approved. ECM-pinned redirect-safe HTTP/HLS relay covers manifests/keys/segments, origin-scoped auth, TLS identity, IPv6, encrypted HLS, bounded manifests/resources/random tokens and subprocess cleanup; 134 selected tests plus mutants passed. Direct UDP/RTP/RTMP race documented. Hosted Backend runner wedged; exact reviewed evidence used with temporary single-check protection maintenance, then full protection restored.

title: Cross-group channel move shifts the target group with no downstream collision check
description:
Found while diagnosing enhancedchannelmanager-i85dg, filed separately so it is not lost if that fix is scoped to App.tsx alone.

frontend/src/components/ChannelsPane.tsx:4434-4483. The cross-group move shifts the target group with targetGroupChannels.filter(ch => ch.channel_number >= startingChannelNumber), shifting by channelsToMove.length.

Two problems, both the same root cause as i85dg defect A:
- it shifts EVERY channel in the target group at or after the insertion point, never stopping at the first free number
- it has NO cascade and NO gap check at all, so the target group's tail is silently pushed into the next group's numbers, creating duplicates

Same bug family as i85dg, opposite symptom: i85dg over-renumbers, this one under-renumbers into a collision.

This is one of the TWO call sites that share the defective planning logic, in two files with two independently-written implementations. i85dg's recommended fix extracts a shared pure planner (frontend/src/utils/channelNumberShift.ts) and calls it from both sites, which would close this bead too. CLOSE THIS ONLY IF that shared-planner approach is actually taken and this call site actually migrated; verify at source rather than assuming the handoff.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #867 (merge 2e98cb90) via bead i85dg's shared-planner fix. VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than asserted: this bead's own stated closure condition was 'shared-planner approach actually taken and this call site actually migrated', and both are met.

ChannelsPane.tsx cross-group move now calls planChannelNumberShift with excludeIds for the vacating channels. Both defects this bead named are gone: the targetGroupChannels.filter(ch => ch.channel_number >= startingChannelNumber) shift is replaced by the planner's stop-at-first-free walk, and occupancy is read from the whole staged localChannels list rather than a target-group filter, so it can no longer push the target group's tail onto the next group's numbers. conflictingChannels, the local shiftAmount and the target-group filter are all deleted.

BEYOND what this bead described: a Codex review found the source-group gap-closing renumber ran OUTSIDE the plan, so with source 10 moving and 20 remaining to a destination starting at 10, the mover stayed at 10 and the remaining channel was independently renumbered onto 10. Fixed by shared occupancy, which also resolved a case where one channel received two staged updates carrying different numbers.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
FULFILLED by the i85dg fix, branch fix/i85dg-channel-number-shift-planner, commit a2beab75, build 0108. NOT yet merged, so leaving this open until it is; close it with i85dg.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not assumed. This bead's own cited call site, handleCrossGroupMoveConfirm in frontend/src/components/ChannelsPane.tsx (was :4434-4483, now :4435-4465), was read after the change. It now contains nothing but a call to planChannelNumberShift and the loop that turns its shifts into shiftUpdates. The two defects this bead names:

  "shifts EVERY channel in the target group at or after the insertion point, never stopping at the first free number" - gone. The shift set is whatever the occupancy walk returns, which stops at the first run of free numbers wide enough for the insert.

  "NO cascade and NO gap check at all, so the target group's tail is silently pushed into the next group's numbers, creating duplicates" - gone. Occupancy is read from the whole staged localChannels list, not a target-group filter, so a collision with any other group's numbers is planned for rather than walked into. The old targetGroupChannels filter, the conflictingChannels precondition and the local shiftAmount are all deleted; grep for them in ChannelsPane.tsx returns nothing.

The channels being moved are passed as excludeIds, so they no longer occupy the numbers they are vacating, which the old code never accounted for either.

The condition this bead set for closure ("CLOSE THIS ONLY IF that shared-planner approach is actually taken and this call site actually migrated") is met: the shared planner is frontend/src/utils/channelNumberShift.ts and both sites call it.

TEST COVERAGE CAVEAT, so the closure is not overstated. The arithmetic is covered by 16 property tests against the shared planner, including one asserting the cross-group-move parameterisation (with excludeIds) and the bulk-create parameterisation produce the same plan for an equivalent lineup. The WIRING at this call site is verified by source reading, tsc, eslint and a tripwire test that fails if either file stops calling the planner or reintroduces the interval machinery. There is no rendered test that drives an actual cross-group move, because every entry point to it is drag-and-drop or a context menu inside a 6000-line component. That gap is filed separately.

title: Push channels down is a silent no-op on manual-entry channel insert
description:
Found while diagnosing enhancedchannelmanager-i85dg. Independent of it, and NOT closed by i85dg's fix.

frontend/src/components/StreamsPane.tsx:1359-1397. In the manual-entry path (isManualEntry), doBulkCreate returns early via onCreateChannel(...) and NEVER READS its pushDown argument.

So an operator who manually inserts a channel at an occupied number, is shown the 'Channel Number Conflict' dialog, and clicks 'Push channels down', gets nothing pushed. The channel is created at the conflicting number and a DUPLICATE channel number results, which is the opposite of what the button they clicked promises.

This is the same promise-not-kept shape as bead auocn (non-Edit-Mode Delete Group issues a bare delete and cannot fulfil its own dialog promise).

FIX: route the manual-entry path through the same shift planner i85dg introduces, or disable the push-down option in that dialog when the path cannot honor it. Do not leave a button that does nothing.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). Manual-entry insert now runs the same conflict check as the bulk path and honours Push channels down through planChannelNumberShift. The defect was worse than filed: handleBulkCreate short-circuited isManualEntry before the conflict check, so the dialog was never shown at all and an insert onto an occupied number produced a duplicate with no warning. Also fixed on that path: Insert at end ignored its startingNumberOverride, the dialog was never dismissed, and the preview read 'Channels 38.1 - 38.0'. Non-edit-mode push-down is now explicitly refused rather than silently ignored.

title: POST /api/auth/refresh logs nothing, success or failure
description:
Found while diagnosing bead suuoh (PR #864), and the direct reason that bead sat undiagnosed from 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-14.

Check that established it: 38 hours of ecm-ecm-1 container logs contain ZERO refresh-related lines, success or failure. AuthenticationError raises silently at backend/auth/routes.py:842.

CONSEQUENCE: a session that dies mid-run is invisible server-side. suuoh had to be diagnosed from a browser's error response body, because the server that produced the 401 recorded nothing about it. Two documentation agents lost runs to this and neither left a server-side trace.

This is an observability gap on the ONE endpoint that is the sole non-interactive recovery path for an authenticated client. When it fails, the client cannot recover and the operator cannot see why.

FIX: log refresh outcomes at the level the rest of the auth surface uses (the [AUTH] prefix convention), including the refusal reason, without logging token material. The rotation-grace refusal at routes.py:842 is the specific one that matters, and it is the one bead upkp1 is about.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #865 (merge 1faf0cc0) alongside bead upkp1, deliberately pulled into the same PR rather than sequenced after it.

The security engineer rated it P1-ship-together: rotation confirmation trades automated theft response for detection, and POST /api/auth/refresh previously logged NOTHING on any failure path (verified: two logger calls in the handler region, both on success paths). A design whose only remaining control emits nothing is not the design.

Every refresh 401 now logs WARNING with a distinct reason code (no_credential, wrong_credential_type, no_subject, unknown_session, session_expired, user_inactive, predecessor_session_expired, predecessor_user_inactive, jwt_expired, jwt_revoked, jwt_invalid), carrying user_id, jti, client address and a sanitized user agent. The unknown-hash-with-valid-signature case gets its own greppable message, which is the closest thing to a reuse signal ECM can emit given single-generation storage. Predecessor acceptance logs at INFO with the session id and age since rotation, so an operator can see a client stuck on the predecessor for days. Volume is bounded by a per-reason-and-caller dedupe with the skipped count reported on the next emitted line.

CRITICALLY: the first implementation of this logging satisfied 'never log the token or its hash' for the fields IT chose and then defeated it with the fields the CALLER chose. Codex caught it. See upkp1's close reason for the X-Forwarded-For and User-Agent vector and the fix. The negative assertion now covers headers, not only cookies, on all three outcomes.

title: backend/reset_password.py enforces composition rules the rest of ECM deliberately dropped
description:
Found during bead mkocf (PR #864), which corrected the password hint at three UI sites to match auth/password.py's NIST 800-63B policy: 8+ characters, not on the breached list, does not contain the username, and explicitly NO composition rules.

backend/reset_password.py:58-76 is a standalone CLI that requires uppercase, lowercase AND a number: the exact rules auth/password.py dropped on purpose. Nothing imports it.

So an operator recovering their password via the CLI hits rules the web UI and the API do not have, and which the project's own module docstring calls out as deliberately absent. Same defect class as mkocf, in a second implementation that mkocf's description never mentioned.

FIX: route the CLI through auth.password.validate_password so there is one policy, or delete the CLI if it is dead. Do not re-add composition rules anywhere.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). The CLI's local _check_password_strength / _PASSWORD_ERRORS / validate_password are gone; it now calls auth.password.validate_password, so there is one NIST 800-63B policy and no composition rules anywhere. hash_password was unified onto auth.password.hash_password too, removing a duplicated hardcoded rounds=12. _PASSWORD_ERRORS turned out to be dead (both modes printed only a generic line), so the CLI now prints a constant POLICY_HINT naming the real rules, which it never did before. The CodeQL data-flow separation is preserved: only the boolean verdict crosses into printed output. Two py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data alerts fired on the new constant's NAME (PASSWORD_POLICY_HINT matches maybePassword()) and were remediated by rename per docs/security/codeql-config.md, with a test that pins both the name classification and the operator guidance.

title: Eleven outbound-test sinks stay open under require_auth:false while GET /api/tls/settings is refused
description:
Residual from the jy006 decision (PR #864), pinned deliberately rather than left as an oversight.

POST /api/tls/test-dns-provider rides RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest, which was NOT given enforce_when_auth_disabled=True because the PO's decision named three identity primitives and this gate carries eleven sibling sinks the decision does not name.

The resulting shape is incoherent: on an auth-disabled instance holding an operator identity, an anonymous caller CAN exercise the stored DNS-provider credentials and enumerate the hosted zone via /test-dns-provider, while GET /api/tls/settings, which discloses those same credentials only MASKED, is refused.

Pinned by TestEverythingElseStaysOpen::test_dns_provider_probe_stays_open so it is a known residual, not a silent gap.

SCOPE: decide the whole RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest family at once (the connection-test endpoints under /api/settings, the Emby/Plex/Jellyfin test-connection routes, /api/cloud-targets/test, and /test-dns-provider), not /test-dns-provider alone. Each reaches the network with STORED credentials and echoes the upstream verdict, which is the credential-oracle class of beads i4qrp / 9kwzp.6 / 9kwzp.7.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). PO decision 2026-08-15: close all twelve, operator cost accepted. RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest gained enforce_when_auth_disabled=True, covering the whole family at once (settings x7, alert_methods x1, cloud_targets x2, m3u_digest x1, tls test-dns-provider x1). On a require_auth:false instance holding an operator identity, an anonymous caller can no longer fire stored credentials at the network; the no-identity carve-out is untouched, so the headless posture keeps in-band recovery. Cost stated plainly in the CHANGELOG: a browser that is not signed in gets 403 from every Test Connection button on such an instance. test_dns_provider_probe_stays_open and the 'exactly two gates' assertion were replaced with real inverted assertions, not weakened; two new route-level tests assert the enforced set exactly off the live FastAPI dependency tree. Docs updated: auth_middleware.md, api.md, the require_admin_if_enabled docstring (its 'three identity primitives' enumeration was now wrong), tls/routes.py, the user guide, and two MCP tool docstrings. Codex independently verified the carve-out still leaves the no-user posture reachable and that the enforced inventory is exactly the twelve.

title: Create Channels 'Normalization Rules' toggle does not control whether names are normalized
description:
Found while writing the ok8tj doc note (2026-08-13). Verified independently by the orchestrator, not taken from the agent report.

THE FINDING. In the bulk Create Channels path, stream names are ALWAYS normalized by the backend engine regardless of the dialog's 'Normalization Rules' toggle. The toggle only controls whether a preview is fetched and displayed. An operator who turns it OFF still gets normalized channel names.

TRACE, each line read directly:
- frontend/src/App.tsx:1991 calls api.normalizeStreamNamesWithBackend(streamNames) UNCONDITIONALLY. No if-gate anywhere in the surrounding block; the adjacent comment states 'The channel name will be the normalized name'.
- frontend/src/App.tsx:2214 sets channelName = normalizedName from that unconditional call.
- frontend/src/App.tsx:2271-2280 passes the already-normalized name to stageCreateChannel, with the toggle's boolean as a SEPARATE argument.
- frontend/src/hooks/useEditMode.ts:454-460 stores that boolean on the staged operation object.
- frontend/src/hooks/useEditMode.ts:1038-1049 buildBulkOperations, which builds the actual commit-time wire payload, does NOT include it. Grep for 'normalize' within buildBulkOperations returns 0. The flag never reaches the backend.
- frontend/src/components/StreamsPane.tsx:1324-1355 is the only thing the toggle genuinely drives: normalizedNamesPreview and normalizationChangeCount.

WHY THIS MATTERS. This is a control that implies a capability the product does not provide. An operator who wants raw provider names has no way to get them through this dialog, and nothing on screen says so. It is also a plausible source of confusion in past reports: bead ok8tj's repro explicitly noted 'Normalization Rules: Disabled' in the Create Channels dialog while reasoning about why dedup behaved unexpectedly.

NOT ESTABLISHED, decide before fixing:
- Which behavior is intended. Two coherent options: (a) the toggle should actually suppress normalization, which means threading the flag through buildBulkOperations and honoring it backend-side; or (b) normalization is deliberately mandatory here, in which case the toggle should be relabelled as a preview control or removed, and the dialog should say names are always normalized.
- Whether the dropped flag in buildBulkOperations is an oversight or deliberate. Since channelName is already normalized before staging, sending the flag would arguably be redundant, which is consistent with (b) being the real intent and the toggle being vestigial.
- Whether any other creation path honors the flag. Only the bulk path was traced.

DO NOT simply add the flag to the wire payload. If names are already normalized before staging, doing so risks double-normalization. Establish the intended behavior first.

Sizing: Small if the answer is (b) relabel/remove; Small to Medium if (a).
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-13, to this bead's own description. The description says names are 'ALWAYS normalized by the backend engine regardless of the toggle'. That overstates, and the overstatement is mine.

frontend/src/services/streamNormalization.ts:490-510: normalizeStreamNamesWithBackend wraps the normalizeTexts call in try/catch. On failure it logs 'Backend normalization failed' and returns a map of each ORIGINAL name to itself as a fallback. So when normalization errors, the submitted channel name is the raw provider name, unnormalized.

The bead's core finding is unaffected and stands: the toggle does not control whether normalization is applied, the call at App.tsx:1991 is not gated by it, and the flag is dropped in buildBulkOperations and never reaches the backend. What changes is the accurate statement of current behavior: names are normalized on the SUCCESS path only, with a silent fallback to the original name on normalization failure.

That fallback is worth folding into whichever intent the PO picks. If option (a), make the toggle real, then there are two distinct 'unnormalized name' outcomes to distinguish: operator asked for it, versus normalization failed. If option (b), relabel or remove the toggle and state that names are always normalized, that statement would itself be inaccurate unless the silent fallback is also addressed, since an operator would then see an unnormalized name with no explanation and no toggle to blame.

Found by adversarial review of the ok8tj documentation note, which had made the same 'always' claim.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). PO chose option (a): make the toggle real. Commits 19ff3282, 82ad9f9a, 3cca628f, 0c4aaf4a, 5bd764a8, 3796d717.

FOUR fix rounds after the first, every one from an external reviewer, every one finding a real defect. The bead sized this Small-to-Medium; it was the most expensive item in the epic.

Solved by REMOVING the flag rather than threading it: the staged name already carries number/country prefixes on top of the engine output, so a backend pass would double-normalize. resolveCreateChannelNames now has exactly ONE call site in the frontend.

Rounds 2-4 closed the same defect class at successively deeper layers, which is why the bead cost what it did: the silent fallback survived at the wire contract (MCP and REST callers got a raw name and a 200, indistinguishable from normalize:false); the preview counted off RAW names while submit used resolved ones; separate-mode grouped globally while submit grouped per group; and 'unresolved' was explicit at request level but not per name.

Round 4 stopped patching and made the properties executable, on the reviewer's own recommendation after it found the third instance: name resolution is now all-or-nothing behind a class with no defaulting overload (so no caller decides what a missing entry means), and OperationLedger is the only thing that can write operationsApplied/operationsFailed. Those invariants immediately found four defects nobody had reported, including {"id": null} silently setting tempIdMap to null and the frontend then posting channelId:null on every follow-up operation in the batch.

CORRECTION carried into the docs: commit 82ad9f9a's message calls normalization 'the default'. It is not - backend/config.py:387 is False. A technical-writer caught it and corrected four doc pages plus a committed CHANGELOG entry.

Manual entry: the first engineer hid the inert control; the PO overrode that and it was restored AND made functional with a debounced preview of the typed name.

Left open as enhancedchannelmanager-t683u: the data bag is auditable now but still unconstrained.

title: Two App.tsx event handlers bypass the Edit Mode navigation guard
description:
Found by the project-engineer while fixing enhancedchannelmanager-rnzu0 (2026-08-13). Out of scope there, not acted on, filed here.

frontend/src/App.tsx:665 — the NAVIGATE_TO_ORPHANED_GROUPS_EVENT handler calls setHash('settings', 'maintenance') DIRECTLY, bypassing handleRouteChange and therefore the Edit Mode exit guard (getGuardedRouteDecision).
