That event is dispatched by the 'Clean up empty groups' action in the ChannelsPane filter panel, which lives on Channel Manager, the one page that HAS Edit Mode.

frontend/src/App.tsx:652 — the 'ecm:open-task-editor' handler has the same shape.

CONSEQUENCE: an operator with staged, unsaved channel edits who triggers either action navigates away with no confirmation dialog, and the staged changes are silently abandoned. The guard exists precisely to prevent that, and these two paths route around it.

NOT ESTABLISHED, verify before fixing:
- Whether either path is reachable while Edit Mode is actually active with staged changes. The Clean up empty groups action lives on Channel Manager so it looks reachable, but confirm rather than assume.
- Whether routing these through handleRouteChange introduces a regression: the guard can return 'confirm', which defers navigation, and these handlers may assume navigation is synchronous.

The e2e specs repointed under rnzu0 now cover the rail entry point into the guard, so there is a working harness to extend to these two paths.

Sizing: Small, pending the reachability check.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits 89964d26, cfefeaed, dd0ce107, d77cb341.

The bead named two App.tsx handlers. The fix covers those AND browser Back/Forward, because the invariant is that no navigation with staged changes escapes the guard, not that two specific handlers were patched. An external reviewer found Back/Forward bypassing it entirely: ecm:before-route-change had exactly ONE production listener in the whole frontend (SettingsTab's unsaved-form guard) and App.tsx never registered one.

The bead's own 'NOT ESTABLISHED, verify before fixing' items were both established. Reachability: confirmed for both paths. The regression risk was real and worse than the bead guessed - NotificationCenter writes sessionStorage BEFORE dispatching and SettingsTab has a mount-only effect that reads it, so a deferred-then-cancelled navigation hijacked the operator's NEXT visit to any Settings page. Closed by an onCancel hook on the deferred-navigation state, proven by a three-stage red/green where the middle stage isolates exactly that.

Also fixed: StickySectionNav passed null as replaceState state, un-numbering the entry the operator was sitting on - the in-product producer of the unindexed entries that corrupted history bookkeeping. And the traversal protocol was rebuilt around destination tokens with an epoch, because the original bare booleans claimed whatever popstate arrived next.

Five inline copies of the sessionStorage key were consolidated into frontend/src/utils/openTaskEditor.ts; the bead's premise found three.

title: Five M3U account list/select surfaces do not apply the 'custom' filter
description:
Split out of enhancedchannelmanager-l5plc (PO decision 2026-08-13).

Seven sites filter the internal 'custom' M3U account out of lists. Five list or select surfaces do NOT, and will offer it to the operator:

- frontend/src/components/channelPipeline/ConditionEditor.tsx:484 — the Channel Pipeline provider-condition dropdown. FLAG THIS HARDEST: a pipeline rule can target 'custom' as a provider, which is a functional decision rather than a cosmetic one. Establish what such a rule actually does before deciding.
- frontend/src/components/tabs/M3UChangesTab.tsx:316 — 'Filter by Account' dropdown.
- frontend/src/components/tabs/SettingsTab.tsx:1729 — digest account multiselect, rendered at :4537.
- frontend/src/components/StreamsPane.tsx:1806 (checkbox list), :1835 (single-select), :1794 ('Select All' maps every provider id).
- frontend/src/components/tabs/SettingsTab.tsx:918-919 — excluded only INCIDENTALLY, by 'is_active && max_streams > 0'. The custom account has max_streams 0 today, so this exclusion is accidental and leaks the moment that value changes. It should not be relied on.

Correctly unfiltered and NOT in scope (id-to-name lookups rather than lists): ProvidersPanel.tsx:390, ChannelsPane.tsx:5423/5446/7483, StreamsPane.tsx:2204.

DECIDE PER SURFACE rather than blanket-filtering. Hiding the account from a picker is not automatically right: if an operator has manually-added streams in the custom bucket, a digest filter or stream picker that cannot reach them may be the actual defect. Establish intent per surface.

Depends on the shared-predicate helper from the sibling bead; drive whatever is decided from that single definition so it cannot drift again.

Sizing: Small to Medium depending on how many surfaces the PO aligns.

title: M3U Manager renders 'No M3U Accounts' when accounts exist but are all filtered
description:
Split out of enhancedchannelmanager-l5plc (PO decision 2026-08-13: split the correctness bug from the UX question).

THE BUG. frontend/src/components/tabs/M3UManagerTab.tsx:804-806 computes visibleAccountCount by applying the SAME name-keyed predicate as filteredAccounts (:793). Both therefore derive from the filtered set, and the empty-state ternary at :969-971 uses visibleAccountCount to choose its copy. That means the component cannot distinguish 'no accounts exist' from 'every account was hidden'.

CONFIRMED LIVE, not theoretical. The instance returns exactly one M3U account (id=1, name 'custom', status error), which is the one the filter hides. filteredAccounts.length === 0 AND visibleAccountCount === 0, so the UI renders the heading 'No M3U Accounts' with body 'Add an M3U account to start importing streams.' The API says one account exists; the UI asserts none do.

This is a correctness defect rather than a UX preference, which is why it is split from the indicator question. The copy must not claim zero accounts when accounts.length > 0 and the emptiness is an artifact of filtering. The existing 'No matching M3U accounts' branch is the right shape; the input to the ternary is what is wrong.

SCOPE: fix the empty-state determination, and extract the duplicated 'is this account displayable' predicate to ONE shared helper. Seven duplicated copies (M3UManagerTab.tsx:583, :608, :793, :805; TaskEditorModal.tsx:142; M3ULinkedAccountsModal.tsx:57; StatsTab.tsx:752) with four historical repair commits (a87aa478, fc0e1c60, 0f0a0584, e58f1bc6) is the mechanism that produced the drift. StatsTab.tsx:748-752 already extracted it locally for that exact reason.

ADD TEST COVERAGE. Grep for 'custom' across M3UManagerTab.test.tsx, M3ULinkedAccountsModal.test.tsx and StatsTab.test.tsx currently yields one unrelated fixture hit. A seven-site load-bearing predicate is pinned by nothing. At minimum pin: all-accounts-filtered does not render the absolute empty state, and the shared helper is the only definition.

Sizing: Small.

title: Live instance /config/backups/ is empty: no backup artifacts exist on the running ECM
description:
Surfaced 2026-08-13 while deciding whether to keep the 2026-08-05 restore-drill artifacts (since deleted at PO instruction, they were drill output rather than production backups).

OBSERVATION, not a diagnosis: /config/backups/ on the live instance is empty. ECM has backup functionality (backend/routers/backup.py, APP_VERSION touchpoint, encrypted ECMBKENC envelope format) and a documented restore drill, but the running instance currently holds no backup artifact.

WHY IT MATTERS: the restore drill exercises the mechanism, not the habit. A drill that passes on artifacts generated during the drill proves the code path works; it proves nothing about whether an operator would actually have something to restore FROM after a real loss. If journal.db is lost today, the observed state suggests there is nothing to recover.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST (do not assume a defect):
- Is a scheduled/automatic backup task supposed to be writing there? Check task_registry / tasks/ for a backup task and whether it is registered, enabled, and running on this instance.
- If backups are manual-only by design, that is a documentation and operator-guidance question rather than a bug, and the fix is to say so plainly plus recommend a cadence.
- Is /config/backups/ even the path the running configuration writes to on this instance, or is it configured elsewhere? Confirm against the live container rather than against defaults.
- Distinguish 'never ran' from 'ran and pruned'. A retention policy that pruned to zero is a different defect from a task that never fired.

Filed at PO request. Priority reflects that this is a recoverability gap rather than a live outage.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-16, read-only, against the live instance. This bead's own four questions are answered. VERDICT: established, NOT a defect.

1. IS A BACKUP TASK REGISTERED? Yes. dbas_backup is registered at tasks/__init__.py:21 and the live DB row reads ('dbas_backup', 0, 'manual', None, None, None, None) - present, DISABLED, schedule_type manual, last_run_at NULL. task_schedules holds 7 rows and none of them is dbas_backup, so nothing schedules it. The disabled state is not drift: backend/tasks/dbas_backup.py sets default_enabled = False with the reason in its docstring, an explicit prior PO decision - 'Ships OFF by default per the PO decision: a less-engaged operator can not silently end up with zero backups.' (The 26sfc-style stale row does exist and was found independently: export_publish, enabled=0, no task class. Different thing.)

2. MANUAL-ONLY BY DESIGN? Manual by DEFAULT, schedulable on request. In-product guidance already exists: BackupScheduleBanner fires when no enabled schedule exists and its CTA dispatches OPEN_TASK_EDITOR_EVENT with taskId dbas_backup, handled at App.tsx:946. Not a dead end.

3. RIGHT PATH? Yes, confirmed live: CONFIG_DIR=/config, BACKUPS_DIR = CONFIG_DIR / 'backups', and ls /config/backups/ is empty.

4. NEVER RAN, OR RAN AND PRUNED? NEVER RAN. stat /config/backups shows Modify 2026-04-21 15:43:58, Birth 2026-04-21 15:43:37. A directory mtime moves on every create and unlink; it has not moved in about four months, and dbas_backup shipped after that date. Retention is independently ruled out twice: retention_enabled defaults False, and dbas/retention.py's NEVER-ZERO invariant prunes only after a verified-successful NEW backup with last_n clamped to at least 1. CAVEAT STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: task_executions holds zero dbas_backup rows, but CleanupTask.task_history_days = 30 prunes that table, so that evidence corroborates only 30 days. The directory mtime is what carries the claim. The query instrument was smoke-tested - the same query returned 20 dbas_sync rows, so the silence is real.

SO THE EMPTY DIRECTORY IS THE INTENDED OUT-OF-BOX STATE. It is not a consequence of pui76 either: the UI CAN already take a backup today, through Scheduled Tasks then Run Now, and EncryptedBackupCard.tsx:43 already calls api.runTask('dbas_backup') from the Backup and Restore page itself. Adding a 'Back Up Now' button would not by itself put an artifact here. Closing this as fulfilled by pui76 would be exactly the rule-3 handoff error CLAUDE.md warns about, so it was not done.

WHAT REMAINS A REAL QUESTION, and it is a PO decision rather than a defect: should dbas_backup ship enabled with a default schedule (reversing the recorded decision), stay disabled, or stay disabled with a harder-to-ignore signal. See the sibling bead filed from this investigation about the dismissible banner - that, not the missing button, is the actual recoverability risk this instance demonstrates.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-08-17 by PO decision as ESTABLISHED, NOT A DEFECT. This bead asked the right questions and instructed 'do not assume a defect'; a read-only investigation answered all four and the instruction was correct.

THE FINDINGS, in full on this bead's notes: dbas_backup IS registered (live row present, disabled, schedule_type manual, last_run_at NULL) and is disabled by an explicit prior PO decision recorded in its own docstring, not by drift. /config/backups/ IS the path the running configuration writes to, confirmed live. The task NEVER RAN rather than ran-and-pruned - the directory mtime has not moved since 2026-04-21, four months and predating dbas_backup's ship date, and retention is independently ruled out twice. The UI can already take a backup today via Scheduled Tasks then Run Now, so the empty directory is not a consequence of the missing button either.

So the empty directory is the intended out-of-box state of a product that deliberately does not schedule backups for you.

WHAT THIS BEAD CORRECTLY REFUSED TO BE. The orchestrator's working hypothesis was that this was simply a consequence of pui76 and should close as fulfilled by it. That was wrong on both clauses, and closing it that way would have been the rule-3 handoff error CLAUDE.md warns about - asserting a handoff without opening the target.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS. The production instance still holds zero backup artifacts. That is an operational step, not a code defect, and it is tracked separately - see the ops bead filed alongside this closure. The underlying product question of whether an operator can silently reach this state is bead iij6s, which the PO's decisions of 2026-08-17 made the enforcement mechanism for keeping dbas_backup disabled by default.

title: check_publish status line transiently reports 'queued' for a run that is in_progress
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-13/14, on two different publish runs (0.18.1-0098 from 0f09e1f1, and 0.18.1-0099 from e7315f5d).

WHAT WAS OBSERVED (not a diagnosis):
scripts/check_publish.py prints a 'status :' line for the build run. On both runs that line went in_progress -> queued -> in_progress while the run was healthy and progressing. At one such moment 'gh run list' reported the same run as in_progress, and 'gh run view <id> --json jobs' showed the run genuinely mid-flight with the four image-build matrix jobs running and Wait for Test Suite already successful. So the two views disagreed at that poll.

WHY IT MATTERS:
check_publish is the post-merge gate operators are told to trust (docs/shipping.md section 6). A status field that appears to move backwards invites the reader to conclude the run restarted or regressed, and the documented remediation for a stuck publish is to re-run the workflow. Acting on a spurious 'queued' could mean re-running a build that was fine, or worse, concluding a healthy publish had failed.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is check_publish reading a field that legitimately reports queued at the run level while matrix jobs re-queue, or the GitHub API transiently returning a stale/aggregate status, or a bug in how the script selects the run/attempt. Do not assume the script is at fault without checking the API response first.

SUGGESTED SCOPE: reproduce by polling both the run-level status and the job-level statuses during a multi-arch publish; if the run-level field is genuinely unstable, have check_publish derive its displayed status from job states (or label it explicitly as run-level and therefore approximate) rather than printing a field that can appear to regress.

Low priority: it is cosmetic today because the PASS/FAIL verdict itself was correct both times. It is filed because a verification tool that misreports state is the exact failure class the CLAUDE.md verification-discipline section was just written about.

title: Record verification-discipline rules in CLAUDE.md; correct overstated stale-base consequence
description:
From the 2026-08-13 error retro (~/retros/2026-08-13-19_(project-d-proxy-not-referent).md). Two parts:

1. Add a 'Verification Discipline — Check the Thing, Not a Proxy' section to CLAUDE.md with four rules: smoke-test instruments before arming them; report the check run rather than the conclusion drawn; never assert a bead handoff without opening the target bead; treat your own verification as needing verification (prefer external adversarial review on judgment, uncurated inputs). Drafted content saved at scratchpad CLAUDE.md.verification-discipline.

2. Correct CLAUDE.md:64 (committed in ad3df496). The stale-base bullet says a stale-base branch 'reverts everything dev gained since the stale base, on merge.' That is wrong: a three-way merge uses the stale commit as the merge base and preserves dev-only work on dev's side. Codex flagged this during the self-audit and is right. The hazard is real (branch may omit symbols added on dev; gates passing on a stale base prove nothing about the merge; conflicts can be resolved badly) but the stated consequence overstates it and would drive the wrong remediation. Rewrite the consequence, keep standing rule 4 (verify merge-base) unchanged.

Blocked until the docs/fix-stale-required-check-count PR merges — that engineer is working in the main checkout and CLAUDE.md must not ride along in its diff.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #861, merged to dev as e7315f5d, published and verified at the registry marker: ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0099 built from e7315f5d8e02.

Both parts of the bead landed.

1. CLAUDE.md gained the 'Verification Discipline: Check the Thing, Not a Proxy' section (now at line 42) with four rules: smoke-test an instrument on a known-good AND known-bad input before arming it; report the check that ran rather than the conclusion drawn; never close a bead on an unread handoff; treat your own verification as needing verification, with uncurated external adversarial review. Verified present on dev after merge.

2. The stale-base bullet's claim that such a merge 'reverts everything dev gained since the stale base' is corrected. Verified empirically first rather than argued: in a throwaway repo, branching from an old commit, advancing the target four commits and merging preserved all target-side work and files, with the merge base confirmed as the stale commit. Grep on dev shows 0 remaining occurrences of the old wording. Standing rule 4 (verify merge-base) left unchanged, since it was always the right control and only its justification was wrong.

Three defects in my own work were caught by the repo's gates during this change and fixed before commit: the em-dash ratchet rejected six added lines (rewritten, not en-dash substituted); a naive bump regex clobbered the documentation example 'APP_VERSION = "..."' in backend/routers/backup.py while leaving the real assignment at 0098, caught by check_version_consistency.py and restored; and the version-advance requirement was read from classify_changed_paths.py is_inert_path rather than guessed (only .beads/*.jsonl and .beads/metadata.json are inert, so a .md-only change is still a code path).

Follow-up filed, not fixed here: enhancedchannelmanager-37okg, check_publish's status line transiently reporting 'queued' for a run that is in_progress, observed on both this publish and the preceding one.

title: Load-dependent async-settling flakes: fix the class, not the instances
description:
PO decision 2026-08-13: treat beads 5dckk and vmk2m.1 as ONE piece of work rather than two instances.

THE PATTERN, with two independent confirmations on a single day.

Both are load-dependent tests that assert on a TOLERANCE rather than on an observable the component actually settles. Both were previously 'fixed' by relaxing that tolerance rather than removing the race, and both recurred straight through the fix:

  5dckk    frontend/src/components/tabs/PendingMergesPage.test.tsx
           'restores the original paginated view when a 51-row all action is cancelled'
           Prior fix 6wkgm raised the waitFor timeout to 5000ms. Recurred at the raised timeout.

  vmk2m.1  frontend/src/components/StickySectionNav.test.tsx
           're-arms when the URL names a different section'
           Prior fix 7zp6g added a waitFor on aria-current before asserting scrollTo call count.
           Recurred with both awaits present.

BLAST RADIUS, why this is not cosmetic. Frontend Tests is a REQUIRED status check, and 'Wait for Test Suite' in the publish workflow gates every image-build job on the Tests run. So one flaky frontend test can:
- block a merge outright (observed on PR #859, a change touching two docs files and one Python test, no frontend code at all); and
- on a post-merge run, skip all five build jobs so NOTHING publishes, leaving dev and the registry diverged (observed after PR #851 merged: dev at 0.18.1-0091 while ghcr carried 0090 until the run was manually re-run).

Two flakes, two blast radii, one day. That is a publish-availability problem reached through a test, which is a different door into the staleness class beads i24jr and t8fqg addressed by detection.

SCOPE.
1. Fix both named tests structurally. The shape to aim for: assert on something the component genuinely settles (a rendered state, an aria attribute reaching its final value, a resolved promise the code under test actually awaits) rather than on a duration. Where two conditions are awaited together, split them so a failure names WHICH one lost the race; both current tests fail without saying that.
2. Then sweep the suite for the same anti-pattern rather than waiting for the third instance to find itself. Candidate signals: a waitFor carrying an explicit timeout, an assertion on call COUNT immediately after an await, a test whose only defence against a race is a raised tolerance. Report what the sweep finds even if you fix nothing else; the inventory is worth having.
3. Record the anti-pattern where a test author will meet it. docs/style_guide.md 'Test Conventions' or docs/testing.md, whichever is the better home. The rule to write down: raising a timeout is not a fix, it is a longer wait for the same race, and a green run on an idle machine is not evidence either way.

DO NOT close this by raising a tolerance. That is what both prior fixes did.

RELATED, deliberately not folded in: bead k4bwl records that docs/testing.md's flake baseline is stale by roughly 1400 tests, so the record that would tell anyone how often this happens is itself wrong. Worth doing near this work, but it is documentation of a different fact.

VERIFICATION NOTE. Both tests pass on an idle machine and both passed on the PR runs that preceded their failures. A green local run proves nothing here. Prove a structural fix by reasoning about the race that was removed, not by re-running until green.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #877 (merge 8d7c4ce9, build 0.18.1-0114), together with both children vmk2m.1 and 5dckk. The PO's 2026-08-13 decision to treat these as ONE piece of work was confirmed by CI mid-branch: the re-run at f538340b failed on 5dckk, the run before it on vmk2m.1, same commit. Fixing either alone would have shipped and then blocked the next publish on the other. The class diagnosis in this bead was correct: both asserted on a tolerance rather than an observable the component settles, and both recurred through a tolerance-widening fix. Both races are now removed rather than outrun. A further mechanism found this round: the 6wkgm fix raised a waitFor budget to 5000ms, which EQUALS vitest's testTimeout, so the test timeout always preempted the wait and the run died with a bare 'Test timed out in 5000ms' naming only the it() line. Three CI re-runs produced no diagnosis for that reason alone. Class-level output beyond the two instances: docs/style_guide.md gains a 'Waits are not fixes' subsection under test validity, banning a waitFor budget at or above testTimeout, requiring an uncontrolled timer to be owned rather than waited on, and requiring a clock stub to assert it was installed (measured: 10 of 11 tests stayed green with the stub misnamed). A banned-patterns table row was added for waitFor-on-uncontrolled-timer. Sweep reported: the 5000/5000 pairing was unique to the test fixed here; ScheduledTasksSection.sectionRail.test.tsx:294 is the same false-green shape and is the next item worth fixing, but fails open rather than red so it cannot block a publish. Deliberately NOT done: suite testTimeout not raised, 51-row fixture not shrunk; both are the tolerance move that already failed twice here.

title: Make Operator Docs a required status check on dev, pinned by a workflow contract test
description:
PO decision 2026-08-13. Adds the Operator Docs job to branch protection on dev.

WHY. That job hosts SIX gates and none of them could block a merge: npm run docs:check, the em-dash ratchet, the PII/ECM-credential ratchet, the detect-secrets ratchet, the binary-artifact guard (bead 6mqn5), and mkdocs build --strict. Three of those are credential-exposure controls. It caught real defects on two consecutive PRs the same day, #849 (synthetic credentials tripping the secrets ratchet) and #850 (a dead cross-file docs anchor orphaned when an analyzer finding code was added), and BOTH were mergeable at the time. The only enforcement was the shipper reading the status rollup, which worked twice because it was being done deliberately. Same shape as the hollow-pass problem bead t4d5w fixed.

ORDERING, AND WHY IT MATTERS. A required status check that never reports deadlocks every PR on the branch permanently. Operator Docs is safe to require because it has no job-level if:, needs:, strategy:, uses: or paths: filter; its only conditions are step-level (github.event_name == 'pull_request'), so the job always runs and always reports a conclusion. On a push the four ratchets skip because they have no base ref to diff against, but the job still reports. That was verified before the flip, not assumed. Nothing however stops a future edit from adding job-level gating, renaming the job, or moving a gate out of it, so the contract test landed FIRST and protection was flipped onto an already-pinned state.

WHAT THE TEST PINS (backend/tests/unit/test_classify_changed_paths.py, TestOperatorDocsRequiredContext): a job-key allowlist that refuses if/needs/paths/paths-ignore/strategy/uses/continue-on-error and any unregistered key; both the YAML job key AND the displayed name:, because branch protection matches on the DISPLAYED name and a rename is the quiet way to orphan a context; per-gate assertions that each of the six is a step of THIS job, actually invokes its command, is not continue-on-error, and carries either no condition or exactly the pull_request one; and a derivation check that the pinned gate set equals the set of steps.<id>.outcome references the job's own run summary emits, so the workflow's self-declared inventory and the contract cannot drift.

Proven by nine injections, each restored: job-level if, job-level paths, a strategy matrix, a display-name rename, a job-key rename, job deletion, a deleted gate, a gate deleted and unwired from the summary, a gate MOVED into Backend Tests, continue-on-error on the secrets ratchet, a narrowed step condition, and an unregistered seventh gate.

ACCEPTED COST, recorded so nobody rediscovers it at 2am: Operator Docs installs detect-secrets and the mkdocs dependencies from the network. As an advisory job a PyPI or npm outage was survivable; as a required check it blocks merges to dev rather than parking PRs at UNSTABLE.

DOCS THAT HAD TO MOVE WITH IT: docs/shipping.md's 'When UNSTABLE is the terminal state' section listed Operator Docs among jobs deliberately NOT required and used a broken user-guide link as its example, which is now a blocking failure; UNSTABLE remains reachable from the genuinely advisory jobs, so the section was rewritten rather than deleted. docs/testing.md asserted the job was deliberately not required and that making it so was out of scope. The required-context list is now EIGHT, not seven.

FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE, not actioned: a repo-wide rule that any required-context job declaring needs: must carry !cancelled(). It holds for every required context today and operator-docs is covered twice over by the allowlist, so the shared helper was left alone rather than widening scope.

title: StickySectionNav re-arm flake recurs on dev after the 7zp6g fix; it also blocked the dev image publish
description:
RECURRENCE. Observed on dev at faba3218 (post-merge run for PR #851), 2026-08-13.

  FAIL frontend/src/components/StickySectionNav.test.tsx
    > StickySectionNav - the deep link fires once per navigation (bead ue130)
    > re-arms when the URL names a different section
  Test Files  1 failed | 206 passed (207)
  Tests       1 failed | 2790 passed (2791)

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKY TEST. It is not just noise; it broke the release path. 'Wait for Test Suite' in the Build and Push Docker Image workflow gates on the Tests run, so a single frontend flake made every image-build job skip and NOTHING published. dev and ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev were left diverged, dev at 0.18.1-0091 while the registry still carried 0090. That is exactly the silent-staleness class beads i24jr and t8fqg exist for, reached this time through a flake rather than a build error. A flake in this suite is therefore a publish-availability problem, not only a CI annoyance.

THE FIX IT RECURRED THROUGH. Commit 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g, 'test(frontend): await settled async state') modified this exact test, adding a waitFor on the button's aria-current before asserting scrollTo call count. That is the fix this failure went straight through. The current test body at StickySectionNav.test.tsx:~214-216 has both awaits and still flaked.

CLOSURE CORRECTION. Bead ur9we was closed earlier the same day on the finding that both of its identified manifestations were fixed, Observation 1 by 05bccf77 and Observation 3 by 494c8c6a. This failure is Observation 3's test. That closure was premature for that half. Do not reopen ur9we; its other observation is genuinely fixed and its description is now misleading. Track the recurrence here instead.

SAME SHAPE AS 5dckk. Bead 6wkgm raised a timeout on the PendingMerges cancel-restore test, the flake recurred at the raised timeout, and 5dckk records that the remaining fix is structural rather than another tolerance bump. This is the second test in the suite with that history. Prefer a structural fix over a longer wait: make the assertion depend on an observable the component actually settles, or split the two awaited conditions so the failure names which one lost the race.

REPRODUCTION NOTE. It passes locally and on PR runs; it failed only on the post-merge dev run, consistent with load dependence. A green local run is not evidence the fix worked, which is precisely the trap 7zp6g's fix fell into.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #877 (merge 8d7c4ce9, build 0.18.1-0114). The StickySectionNav deep-link scroll runs inside requestAnimationFrame, and jsdom implements rAF as a lazily-started 60Hz setInterval; the test was waiting on that timer with a wall-clock budget. The test now owns the frame clock: rAF queues, flushFrames() runs the queue inside act, counts asserted synchronously. The prior fix 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g) added a waitFor on aria-current, which proves the component decided but does not make the frame arrive; that wait is kept but split out so a failure names which half lost. Mutation-proven: per-mount latch goes red at the aria-current wait, latch removal goes red in 3 tests including both does-not-re-fire negatives. Instrument audit found the rAF stub could silently no-op (10 of 11 tests stayed green when misnamed); it now asserts installation.

title: POST /api/settings/reset-stats has no auth dependency and wipes seven stats tables
description:
Listed but deliberately not fixed during the sibling audit for bead enhancedchannelmanager-9kwzp.8, because it is a different defect class and the brief's bar was 'unambiguously the same defect'.

POST /api/settings/reset-stats carries no route-level auth dependency, so any authenticated non-admin can wipe seven statistics tables. It is the same OMISSION SHAPE as POST /api/settings/restart-services (closed by bead 9kwzp.6) but a different class: destructive data operation rather than identity or privilege escalation, and nothing about it reaches the network or mints a credential.

Choose the tier on its own merits. restart-services took the ordinary admin tier and deliberately kept admitting the MCP principal, because rebuilding background services from already-saved settings is work a settings write schedules anyway. Reset-stats is destructive and irreversible, so the reasoning does not transfer automatically; decide whether the MCP automation surface should be able to wipe operator statistics, and record the verdict in backend/tests/test_admin_gate_inventory.py either way.

Also recorded from the same sweep, no action needed: GET /api/settings/mcp-status carries no dependency but is a read-only reachability probe of an env-configured host (MCP_HOST, never caller-named) returning reachability and a tool count. Informational; listed here so a future audit does not re-derive it.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #855, merged to dev as 0044d1ad, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms the registry carries 0.18.1-0095 built from a successful run of that commit.

9kwzp.12: POST /api/settings/reset-stats carried no dependency at all and deletes every row of seven statistics tables. Now RequireHumanAdminForStatisticsReset. The MCP half was decided on its own merits rather than copied from restart-services (9kwzp.6), which kept admitting the principal because it rebuilds services from already-saved settings, work a settings write schedules anyway. Nothing re-derives those tables: no compensating write, no rollback ledger, which is also what distinguishes it from the Channel Pipeline rollback routes that stay admitted because they ARE the pipeline's reversal mechanism. GET /api/settings/mcp-status confirmed a read-only probe of an env-configured host; no action.

9kwzp.10 item 1: PATCH /api/settings/security now RequireHumanAdminForOutboundPolicy. It is the only FIELD-SPECIFIC writer of ssrf_outbound_mode (the strong 'only writer' claim was refuted: wholesale restore paths persist it data-driven with no source-level assignment a grep can find). Gating eleven outbound sinks while their policy stayed writable by the same principal was a partial control.

9kwzp.10 item 2, the durable finding: THE GATE WENT STALE WHEN THE CAPABILITY GREW. Not the inconsistency the bead assumed. Three commits prove it: 21f93e683 (2026-06-19) shipped /restore-dbas on the ordinary admin tier when a DBAS restore applied denylist-filtered settings to the Dispatcharr upstream and never touched ECM's settings.json; e83d31b1 (2026-07-08, bead 6n76m) human-gated the legacy /restore, /restore-saved and /restore-yaml because those already wrote ECM's blob, and DELIBERATELY left DBAS alone for exactly that distinction; fd63235d (2026-08-04, bead dfkbn item 4) added dbas/importers/ecm_settings.py with a generic attribute-assignment loop plus save, which made the distinction stale. Nothing about the route or its dependency ever changed, so the route inventory structurally cannot catch this class.

The two DBAS routes then diverged on purpose, because that reasoning covers APPLY and not a preview that writes nothing. /restore-dbas takes a caller-supplied upload streamed to the config partition and decoded before confirm_apply is read, and has no MCP tool (no file upload over MCP), so it is refused outright including dry run. /restore-dbas-saved names an artifact only an admin could have saved, keeps the ordinary admin tier, and refuses only the apply in the handler. The zero-mutation property is structural: restore_orchestrator.py forces the dry-run marker whenever confirm_apply is false and documents it as the single choke point a caller cannot opt out of.

9kwzp.10 items 3 and 4, and the PO amendment: sync-target, cloud-target and alert-method writes were gated. Non-admin humans are refused everywhere. Per PO decision the MCP principal was then RE-ADMITTED on the seven routes its shipped tools need (list_alert_methods, cloud-target create/update/delete, sync-target create/update/delete) by moving them to RequireAdminIfEnabled, which keeps the non-admin fix while restoring tooling. RequireHumanAdminForOutboundDestination was built for those writes and then REMOVED rather than left unused, because a shipped gate constant whose prose says a route is refused is worse than no constant when the route is admitted.

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL, tracked as bead 9kwzp.13 (P1, open): GET /api/alert-methods returns AlertMethod.config unredacted, so the re-admitted MCP principal can read Discord webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and SMTP passwords in clear. Recorded under a STOP banner in test_admin_gate_inventory.py plus alert_methods.py, auth/dependencies.py, mcp-server/tools/notifications.py, CHANGELOG.md and docs/api.md so no reader mistakes the plain gate for an uninteresting one.

TWO REGRESSIONS CAUGHT BEFORE MERGE, both by adversarial review rather than by CI, which was green throughout. First, SettingsTab.tsx called listAlertMethods() with no admin guard and left the recipient control editable, so every non-admin opening Settings would have hit a guaranteed 403 and lost their SMTP-recipient state. Second, found while fixing the first: useAuth returns early WITHOUT fetching the user when auth is disabled or setup is incomplete, so a 'user?.is_admin ?? false' predicate reads null as not-admin and would have locked the operator out of their own UI on an auth-disabled install, where every gate here no-ops server-side anyway. Now one derived isAdminUser = !user || user.is_admin, matching the predicate BackupRestoreSection already used.

Backend 9630 passed / 9 skipped; frontend 208 files / 2798 tests. Every gate no-ops when require_auth is false or setup is incomplete; these routes are admin-gated in the normal authenticated posture, not categorically.

title: Secrets ratchet advertises an inline pragma it has deliberately disabled, and under-reports duplicate findings
description:
Hit for real on PR #849 (beads 9ej7f, i4qrp, 9kwzp.6, 9kwzp.7). Cost roughly an hour of diagnosis on a branch whose code was already correct. Nobody did anything wrong; the guard is well designed and its operator experience is the problem.

THREE COMPOUNDING PROBLEMS.

1. The advertised remedy is inert. scripts/check_secrets.py runs detect-secrets-hook with --disable-filter detect_secrets.filters.allowlist.is_line_allowlisted, so an inline '# pragma: allowlist secret' does nothing. That pragma is EXACTLY what detect-secrets' own failure output instructs the author to use. The gate therefore tells you to do something it has deliberately prevented from working.

2. The failure output names no finding. _report_changed_path_failure prints 'FAIL: possible secret finding or ambiguous baseline mutation.' followed by the full changed-path list, which on a normal PR is every file you touched. That withholding is correct, since findings must not be echoed into public CI logs, but there is no documented local path to see them either. Reproducing required copying the script and instrumenting the subprocess result by hand.

3. The scanner silently under-reports duplicates. detect_secrets.PotentialSecret.__eq__ ignores line number, so two identical values in one file collapse to a single reported finding. On PR #849 a third occurrence of the same literal at test_i4qrp_connection_test_admin_gate.py:197 was never listed. An author who fixes exactly what the report names pushes again and fails again. Relatedly, the KeywordDetector denylist regex has no word boundary, so 'smtp_password' matches the 'password' rule; a reader scanning for the literal key will not find it.

THE CONVENTION ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNDISCOVERABLE. backend/tests/unit/test_check_pii.py solves this and says so in its module docstring: fixtures are assembled from repeated or obviously patterned characters so they carry the right SHAPE without resembling a real secret to a human or a scanner. That file appears ZERO times in .secrets.baseline despite being full of credential shapes, so the convention is proven rather than assumed. Nothing points anyone at it.

SCOPE, all cheap.
1. Document the convention in docs/pytest_conventions.md or docs/testing.md, citing test_check_pii.py as canonical, with both techniques: split literals when the value's shape is load-bearing, and angle-bracket placeholders when it is not (is_templated_secret's lookahead means a value starting with '<' never becomes a candidate).
2. Make the local failure path discoverable. Either a documented flag on check_secrets.py that prints findings when run locally but never in CI, or a line in the failure text pointing at the doc from item 1.
3. Note the duplicate-collapse behaviour and the unanchored keyword regex wherever item 1 lands, so an author knows the report may be incomplete and that fixing only the named lines can fail again.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: loosening the guard. Disabling the inline allowlist is a sound decision, since a pragma is exactly what an attacker would add. The fix is discoverability, not permissiveness.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION FOR THE PO, do not action here. The secrets ratchet runs inside the Operator Docs job, which is NOT a required status check. A red secrets scanner therefore parks a PR at UNSTABLE rather than blocking it, and merging past it depends on the shipper reading the rollup. That is the same shape as the hollow-pass problem bead t4d5w fixed. Whether a secret-scanning failure belongs in a non-required job is a branch-protection question and needs its own bead and PO decision.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORROBORATED from the outside during PR #864 (bead 9kwzp epic), with a concrete instance for each claim plus a third finding.

1. DUPLICATE UNDER-REPORTING, with an instance. AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE appeared at BOTH line 56 and line 73 of a new test file. detect-secrets-hook reported ONLY line 56. An engineer who fixed the reported line and re-pushed would have failed again with an identical message. docs/pytest_conventions.md already warns about this ('A clean-looking failure report can still be incomplete'), which means the doc is doing work the tool should do.

2. THE DISABLED PRAGMA IS STILL ADVERTISED. The hook's own failure text says 'Mark false positives with an inline pragma: allowlist secret comment' while check_secrets.py:334 passes --disable-filter ...is_line_allowlisted. Confirmed verbatim in captured stdout.

3. NEW, and the expensive one: THE FAILURE REPORT NAMES NO FILE. The gate printed 44 'Location:' lines, every changed path on the branch, for 3 findings in 3 files. Suppressing the findings themselves from CI logs is sound, but the result is a signal-to-noise ratio of 3/44, and learning anything requires locally re-deriving the hook call. A cheap fix that leaks nothing: print the COUNT of findings and the SET of files they occurred in, without line, type, or value. That alone would have collapsed a multi-step investigation to minutes.

Also worth capturing here: there is no .pre-commit-config.yaml and no local git hook running check_secrets.py, so this whole class is discoverable only in CI or by a manual local run. Given the repo already documents the fixture convention, a pre-push hook is a natural pairing.

description:

title: Backup read path leaks discord_webhook_url and telegram_chat_id to the MCP principal, bypassing the 9ej7f redaction
description:
Found during the RequireAdminIfEnabled per-site audit for bead enhancedchannelmanager-9kwzp.7, and independently verified.

THE DEFECT. Bead enhancedchannelmanager-9ej7f made GET /api/settings withhold discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id from any caller that _resolve_settings_admin classifies as non-admin, which includes the MCP service principal. The backup read path defeats two thirds of that.

backend/routers/backup.py:122-129 defines _SETTINGS_CREDENTIAL_FIELDS as password, dispatcharr_api_key, api_key, smtp_password, telegram_bot_token, mcp_api_key. Verified: telegram_bot_token IS redacted, so that one field is safe. discord_webhook_url and telegram_chat_id are NOT in the set and are not covered by _ALERT_METHOD_CREDENTIAL_KEYS either, which matches keys inside alert_methods.config JSON rather than the top-level settings fields.

GET /api/backup/create, GET /api/backup/export and GET /api/backup/saved/{filename} all carry RequireAdminIfEnabled, which admits the MCP principal because _build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True. So the exact principal just blocked from reading those values on the settings endpoint can still read two of the three out of a standard backup artifact.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO FIELDS. This is a read-path parity defect, not just two missing strings. Any future field added to the settings redaction set will leak the same way unless someone remembers to add it in a second place. Bead enhancedchannelmanager-gi4zn is the same shape on the same file: the standard redacted artifact leaves the XC/M3U username in clear while redacting the password.

SCOPE. Add the two fields. Then close the class: derive the backup redaction set from the settings read-redaction partition (the _ADMIN_ONLY_READ_REDACTED_FIELDS frozenset added on the 9ej7f branch) rather than maintaining a parallel literal tuple, or add a test asserting the settings partition is a subset of the backup denylist so the two cannot drift again. Consider doing this together with gi4zn, which touches the same denylist for the same reason.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5). Closed the CLASS, not just the two fields, as the bead required.

ADMIN_ONLY_READ_REDACTED_FIELDS moved to backend/config.py, the leaf both routers already import and where DispatcharrSettings is defined. routers/settings.py re-exports it under the historical private name so the existing 9ej7f test still passes untouched. routers/backup.py _SETTINGS_CREDENTIAL_FIELDS now DERIVES the partition, which propagates automatically to _REDACT_KEYS (DBAS deep redactor), the ZIP export, the YAML export and the debug bundle. Deleted the local _DEBUG_BUNDLE_EXTRA in routers/channel_pipeline.py, whose comment ('these two aren't credential-class in the backup contract') was the defect rather than a distinction.

Derivation chosen over a subset test deliberately: importing settings->backup works today but is a router-to-router import on a cycle-fragile path, and the fix for a future cycle would be re-duplicating the tuple, which is exactly this bead.

Codex confirmed the canonical set reaches ZIP, YAML, DBAS deep redaction and debug bundles.

gi4zn is NOT closed by this and does not share a mechanism, only a file: username, user, xc_username and m3u_username remain absent from both denylists, verified concretely. What the derivation gives gi4zn is one denylist to edit instead of two.

Operator note recorded in CHANGELOG: a plain (non-passphrase) backup now restores without discord_webhook_url and telegram_chat_id, matching how telegram_bot_token already behaved. Restore preserves the destination's existing values rather than blanking them.

title: Emby, Plex and Jellyfin test-connection endpoints use RequireAdminIfEnabled, which admits the MCP service key
description:
Found while fixing bead enhancedchannelmanager-i4qrp. These three carry RequireAdminIfEnabled and were cited in i4qrp's own description as the CORRECT pattern that /api/settings/test was missing:

  POST /api/settings/emby/test-connection       backend/routers/settings.py:1919
  POST /api/settings/plex/test-connection       backend/routers/settings.py:1977
  POST /api/settings/jellyfin/test-connection   backend/routers/settings.py:2022

That premise turned out to be only half right. RequireAdminIfEnabled closes the non-admin half but NOT the MCP half, because _build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True (backend/auth/dependencies.py:66). So the MCP service key still reaches all three, each of which POSTs operator-supplied or stored credentials to a caller-named host and echoes the upstream result back.

This is the same defect class i4qrp fixed for /test, /test-smtp, /test-discord and /test-telegram, and the fix is a one-line dependency swap per endpoint to RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest (backend/auth/dependencies.py:389) plus the four-case test shape i4qrp established (non-admin refused, MCP refused, admin reaches handler, first-run still reaches handler).

WORTH DOING AS PART OF THIS: audit every remaining RequireAdminIfEnabled call site in the codebase and decide, per site, whether admitting the MCP service principal is intended. Several are certainly fine, since the MCP sidecar is a legitimate admin automation surface for ordinary configuration. The ones that are not fine are exactly the sinks that reach the network with credentials or perform destructive operations. Record the verdict per site so the next reader does not have to re-derive it, and consider a test that pins the intended set.

title: Five more outbound-test sinks carry no admin gate and are reachable by the MCP service key
description:
Found while fixing bead enhancedchannelmanager-i4qrp, which asked directly whether other MCP-reachable routes perform outbound requests with stored credentials. They do. i4qrp closed four sinks in backend/routers/settings.py (/test, /test-smtp, /test-discord, /test-telegram) using the new RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest dependency. These were deliberately left out of scope and need the same treatment:

  POST /api/alert-methods/{id}/test   backend/routers/alert_methods.py:380
  POST /api/m3u/digest/test           backend/routers/m3u_digest.py:366
  POST /api/cloud-targets/{id}/test   backend/routers/cloud_targets.py:376
  POST /api/cloud-targets/test        backend/routers/cloud_targets.py:434

All four are reachable by any authenticated caller and by the MCP service key. The alert-method and digest ones send using STORED credentials, which is the same class as test-smtp, not merely caller-supplied ones.

A fifth item of a DIFFERENT class rides along here for convenience, and should be judged separately rather than assumed to want the same dependency: POST /api/settings/restart-services (backend/routers/settings.py:2231) carries no auth dependency at all. It is not an outbound credential sink; it is an unguarded operational action. Decide its correct gate on its own merits.

USE THE RIGHT DEPENDENCY. Do NOT use RequireAdminIfEnabled here. _build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True (backend/auth/dependencies.py:66), so RequireAdminIfEnabled admits the MCP principal and would close the non-admin half while leaving the MCP half, which is the half these beads are about, wide open. Use RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest (backend/auth/dependencies.py:389), which is built on the reject_mcp_service_principal=True path and takes a per-call-site mcp_denial_detail so the 403 body names the right surface.

Mirror i4qrp's test shape: per endpoint, assert a non-admin is refused, assert the MCP principal is refused, assert an admin reaches the handler, and assert first-run/auth-disabled still reaches the handler so no lockout is introduced.

title: Rule analyzer is blind to a merge-lookup scope pinned to a group the rule never creates channels in
description:
From GH #801 (reporter ruckusvol, 2026-08-08), surfaced by the backlog validity audit bead enhancedchannelmanager-bewu9.

THE DEFECT. A Channel Pipeline rule can have its merge-lookup scope pinned to a channel group it never creates channels in. Lookups then faithfully search a group the channels were never in, every same-name lookup misses, and with orphan_action=delete the rule silently full delete/recreates its whole channel set on every run. The reporter measured create-49 / delete-49 churn run after run until an operator repinned the scope, after which the very next run was 23 merges / 1 create and the one after that a clean no-op with stable IDs.

WHY NOTHING WARNS. match_scope_group_id is a real column (backend/models.py:2031) that pins the scope. The analyzer never reads it: grep for match_scope_group_id in backend/channel_pipeline_rule_analyzer.py returns ZERO hits. The only merge-scope finding, MERGE_SCOPE_NOT_TARGET_GROUP (:310), early-returns at :280-281 when match_scope_target_group is true, which is exactly the state in which a pin is active. So the analyzer is structurally blind to this direction.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF p6ko9. Closed bead p6ko9 (GH #226) covered the INVERSE footgun: match_scope_target_group=false searching all groups and merging into the wrong one. It shipped the default flip plus the MERGE_SCOPE_NOT_TARGET_GROUP advisory for that direction only. This bead is the opposite case and is uncovered.

SCOPE. Emit an analyzer finding when a rule's match_scope_group_id differs from the group its create_channel action actually lands in (resolve through the same chain the create path uses: action.group_id, then create_group context, then rule.target_group_id). Severity should reflect that orphan_action=delete turns it into silent data churn rather than a cosmetic mismatch. The reporter has offered to test a warning.

RELATED. GH #801 carries a second, independent mechanism tracked as bead enhancedchannelmanager-0ippw (the never-persisted auto_created marker). Both are real; the reporter proved each separately. Fixing one does not fix the other.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #850, merged to dev as 2f664d86, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0090 built from a successful run of that commit. Upstream GitHub #801.

0ippw (P1): provenance now comes from the rule's persisted managed_channel_ids ledger rather than the in-memory auto_created marker Dispatcharr never stored. Fixed at the _is_manual_channel boundary, which covers BOTH lookup call sites including _find_unique_channel_by_exact_identity, the helper PR #848 added that had inherited the same defect. Provenance uses the union of every rule's ledger, not the firing rule's alone, because 'was this hand-built?' is a property of the channel rather than of the asker; per-rule scoping would have reproduced the same divergence in a new form. Hand-built channels stay protected because ledger entry is gated on created_channel_ids or pre_run_managed_ids, so a channel a rule merely merged into never enters it. Every test fixture drops the auto_created key on reload and the client stub asserts the create payload never carries it, which is what the GH #845 tests could not do since they hardcode it.

The event_sync allow_manual_channel_merge=True override at :4827 was REMOVED per PO decision, and it was harmful rather than merely redundant: the promotion path registers adopted channels into the managed set, so a hand-built channel in the promotion target group could be adopted and then registered, placing it in scope for orphan deletion. Removal was proven by neutering the ledger with the override gone, which turned exactly the two promotion idempotence tests red and nothing else.

rtst2.1: new MERGE_SCOPE_PINNED_TO_OTHER_GROUP analyzer finding. match_scope_group_id previously appeared zero times in the analyzer and the one merge-scope check early-returned exactly when a pin was active. Resolves the landing group through the same chain the executor uses and stays silent when a create_group action makes the destination a runtime decision.

0fn69: allow_manual_channel_merge added to the MCP rule contract, plus a reverse-direction test (backend subset of contract union exclusions). The pre-existing test only checked contract subset of backend, which is the direction this shipped through.

Gates: 9369 passed / 9 skipped backend (dev baseline 9333), 207 files / 2791 tests frontend, 630 MCP sidecar, secrets ratchet, version consistency and em-dash guards all green.

Related bead filed, not fixed: rtst2.2 (the analyzer emits a ninth code, RULE_REFERENCES_DISABLED_NORMALIZATION_GROUP, that no operator doc describes; pre-existing on dev, confirmed by git show).

title: Guard channel-number ranges, clearing, and automatic rename effects
description:
## Problem
Range operations, clearing a number, and automatic channel-name updates can have consequences beyond the edited field. Operators may create unsupported or overlapping ranges, clear required numbers accidentally, or apply unexpected name changes.

## Scope
Add workflow-specific safeguards for range boundaries and overlap, intentional unassignment, and previews of automatic rename effects. Preserve approved move and auto-shift behavior.

## User Value
Operators understand the full impact of numbering actions before Apply and avoid accidental unnumbering, range collisions, or surprising channel-name changes.

## Success Signal
Range and clearing actions are validated before staging, and every automatic rename caused by numbering is visible in the change preview.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Bulk ranges validate start, end, count, supported bounds, canonical precision, and final-state overlap before staging or applying.
2. Overflow and unsupported ranges are blocked with actionable guidance.
3. Clearing a channel number is distinguished from incomplete or malformed input and requires deliberate confirmation when downstream behavior may be affected.
4. Numbering-driven automatic name changes are shown in single and bulk previews before Apply.
5. Preview counts and examples match the actual final channel numbers and names persisted.
6. Existing move, insertion, renumber, and auto-shift behavior remains intact unless it violates the shared numbering contract.
7. Component and rendered E2E tests cover boundary ranges, overlap, clearing or canceling, auto-rename enabled and disabled, and preview-to-persist consistency.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits d2260c6e, cfd26589.

channelNumberRangeError checks the RUN, not the individual value, wired into all four renumber paths. Renumber All Groups validates every group before staging the first; Group Reorder validates before it reorders. Clearing a number is confirmed, driven by a matcher shared with the rename so the two cannot disagree. Automatic renames caused by numbering are listed with before/after in the Apply dialog (EditModeExitDialog).

HOW auto_rename_channel_number INTERACTS, which the brief asked to establish rather than assume: it is NOT an input to the preview and does not need to be. It gates the PRODUCERS, so when it is off nothing stages a name. deriveAutomaticRenames reproduces computeAutoRename against each operation's before-snapshot. Reading staged consequences rather than the setting keeps the preview honest across a setting changed mid-session and a ledger restored into a session whose setting differs - both real cases now that staged work survives a dead session.

A reviewer found the preview listing renames that never happen: it reported every matching historical operation while execution merges later data over earlier, so the dialog promised '5 | ESPN -> 6 | ESPN' when the name that lands is 'ESPN HD'. Fixed by having deriveAutomaticRenames take the FinalNumberingPlan - the same materialisation the validator validates and consolidation will send. One producer feeding both, the same resolution this epic applied to the Create Channels dialog.

Left open as enhancedchannelmanager-v3wr1: Group Reorder is still the only numbering path that never applies the automatic rename, and Shift and Renumber can manufacture a collision it does not check for.

title: Detect concurrent channel-number changes before Apply
description:
## Problem
An edit session can be based on stale channel numbers if another operator or Dispatcharr changes them after Edit Mode begins. Applying staged updates can then overwrite newer work or invalidate an otherwise clean numbering plan.

## Scope
Compare the numbering state used to stage changes with the latest server state at commit time and surface material conflicts before mutation. Preserve safe changes that do not overlap where possible without silently choosing conflict policy.

## User Value
Operators are warned before overwriting somebody else's numbering changes and can refresh or intentionally reconcile them.

## Success Signal
A stale edit session cannot silently overwrite a channel number changed after its baseline was captured.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Edit Mode retains the baseline information required to identify server-side channel-number changes relevant to staged operations.
2. Apply fetches or otherwise verifies current server state before numbering mutations begin.
3. A changed number on a channel touched by the staged plan produces an actionable conflict showing baseline, current, and proposed values.
4. The conflict blocks silent overwrite and offers a safe refresh, cancel, or explicit reconciliation path approved by UX.
5. Unrelated server-side changes do not unnecessarily block a valid staged plan.
6. Tests cover overlapping changes, unrelated changes, channel deletion, newly created server channels occupying a proposed number, and a successful retry after refresh.
7. A rendered E2E test uses changed server state to verify the warning before mutation.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. This is cheaper than filed. A candidate implementation ALREADY EXISTS as dead code: checkForConflicts at frontend/src/hooks/useEditMode.ts:874-919 fetches fresh channels and diffs channel_number/name/streams against baselineSnapshot. It has ZERO call sites; the only three references repo-wide are its definition, its type at types/editMode.ts:278, and its own export at useEditMode.ts:1657. Unwired since Edit Mode's original commit 07153abe. Scope is therefore: (a) wire it into the pre-Apply path, (b) surface an actionable UI conflict, (c) extend it to cover new server-side channels claiming a proposed number, which the current stub does not do (it only compares channels already in baselineSnapshot).
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). PO decision: per-conflict reconcile, not a blanket block. Commits 45b55070, b256eb16, 410fd0f3.

New frontend/src/utils/channelNumberConcurrency.ts. Apply now does a fresh server read, compares against the session baseline, and offers a per-channel keep-mine / take-theirs choice in NumberingConflictDialog. A read that FAILS refuses and says so - it is never a clean bill of health. The final-state preflight then runs against that fresh list, so it also catches a channel another operator created on a proposed number.

THE COMPARISON IS OVER CHANNELS THE PLAN WILL WRITE, not channels it moves. plannedNumberWrites deliberately does not read FinalNumberingPlan.placements, because a channel moved and moved BACK is still PATCHed and still overwrites. The engineer's first implementation had that hole and its own boundary test caught it.

THE BASELINE IS NOT PERSISTED. restoreStagedLedger re-captures it from today's lineup, because a stored baseline would be exactly the stale value this check exists to catch. Two tests pin that a restored session expects today's number, never the dead session's.

A reconcile decision is bound to the change it resolved - {channelId, baselineNumber, serverNumber} - and stops matching if the server value moves again, the same shape as vdxbx's duplicate acknowledgement.

TWO DESIGN TRADES, both deliberate and both stated in the product: take-theirs on a bulkAssignChannelNumbers drops the WHOLE range and says why, because its numbers are positional and removing one channel would move everyone after it to a number nobody was shown. And take-theirs withdraws the AUTOMATIC rename staged in the same operation - without it the channel would be named '150 | ESPN' while sitting on 199. An operator-typed name is untouched, decided by reproducing computeAutoRename rather than asking producers to flag themselves.

The dialog gained a real accessible identity in the final round: it had no role='dialog', no aria-modal and no accessible name, which is why the modal inventory could not see it at all.

Left open as enhancedchannelmanager-jjjnh: bulkAssignChannelNumbers has no per-channel write to hang an expectedNumber on, so non-UI callers still have no staleness check.

title: Apply channel-number swaps and renumbers without partial state
description:
## Problem
Sequential updates can make a valid final numbering plan fail midway, such as swapping two occupied numbers, and a later failure can leave only part of a renumber operation applied.

## Scope
Plan numbering mutations so valid swaps, cycles, and range shifts can execute safely, and ensure failure semantics do not leave an unexplained partially applied numbering state. Work within Dispatcharr API capabilities and make any unavoidable compensation behavior explicit and observable.

## User Value
Operators can perform common reorganizations confidently without repairing half-completed numbering changes manually.

## Success Signal
Valid swaps and multi-channel renumbers reach the previewed final state; injected failures either preserve or restore the prior numbering state, or clearly report deterministic recovery instructions where atomicity is impossible.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two-channel swaps, multi-channel cycles, vacated-number reuse, and ordered range shifts execute without transient uniqueness collisions.
2. The implementation selects a safe mutation order or temporary-number strategy compatible with the defined channel-number domain.
3. Numbering preflight completes before execution.
4. A failure at each mutation position is tested; the operation does not silently report success or leave state without explicit recovery handling.
5. Retry behavior is idempotent and converges on the intended final state without creating new conflicts.
6. The UI reports the actual persisted outcome after failure and retains enough context to retry or recover.
7. Backend integration and rendered E2E tests cover successful swaps and an injected mid-operation failure.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Narrow the acceptance criteria to the swap-ordering / temp-number mechanism. AC item 'UI reports the actual persisted outcome after failure' is now satisfied generically by build 0052 (beads udq1j + vtapf + 75k49), which made partial bulk-commit failure visible. The core defect is untouched: _run_bulk_commit Phase 2 (backend/routers/channels.py:1996-2010) processes ops in client-sent order with no temp-number strategy, so an A-to-B swap collides on uniqueness.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). PO decision: best-effort compensating rollback, then report. Commits 45b55070, 594ba35d, a9d619cb.

New backend/channel_number_apply.py. order_numbering_writes does a Kahn ordering over 'W wants the slot V is vacating', so no channel moves onto a number another write in the same plan has not left. Cycles - a two-channel swap being the smallest - are NAMED and broken explicitly, sharing a number for exactly one write. NumberingCompensator records landed and failed writes and produces one inverse write per channel, newest first, restoring the value held BEFORE the run rather than an intermediate this run created. Where compensation itself fails, numberingRecovery names the channel, where it is, where it should be, and the one action that closes the gap - surfaced to the operator through the existing failure dialog, not just logged.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE, and it changes what the work is for: the note says an A-to-B swap 'collides on uniqueness'. Measured against ic884.1's findings, that is wrong - channel_number is a non-unique float and DRF never calls full_clean(), so swaps already worked. Ordering does NOT make swaps possible; it makes every intermediate state one the operator would recognise, which is what makes a failure report readable. Written into the module docstring rather than left implied.

WHAT IS GUARANTEED VERSUS REPORTED, stated in the code as well as here: every landed numbering write is recorded and a compensating write is attempted for each. Whether it succeeds is only reported. A change another client makes between the failure and the repair is neither detected nor preserved - there is no conditional update to detect it with (measured: Dispatcharr 0.28.x has no If-Match/ETag/412 and no version field). Every compensating write goes through the ledger and journals like any other landed write.

A reviewer found the cycle broken at the WRONG NODE when a chain feeds into a cycle - release(start) released a non-member, so a write entered an occupied slot and the cycle survived to need a second forced release (and was reported twice). Now release(min(cycle)). Verified exhaustively: every mapping of n channels onto n numbers for n<=4, 288 plans, plus 81 with duplicate starts, all against one invariant helper.

title: Preflight the final channel-number state across all staged operations
description:
## Problem
Validating staged numbering operations independently misses collisions created by their combined result, especially across edits, new channels, moves, shifts, and bulk renumbers.

## Scope
Materialize and validate the proposed final numbering state before Apply mutates Dispatcharr. Validation must account for all staged operations and use canonical channel-number semantics.

## User Value
Operators learn about conflicts before any changes are applied and can resolve the exact staged operations responsible.

## Success Signal
Apply is blocked with actionable validation details whenever the complete proposed final state violates numbering invariants, while valid combined plans pass.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Preflight constructs the effective final state from the latest server state plus all staged channel creates, updates, moves, shifts, deletes, and bulk-number assignments.
2. Duplicate and invalid final numbers are detected using the shared canonical-number contract.
3. Channels being deleted or moved away do not cause false conflicts; newly created and previously staged channels are included.
4. Validation runs before the first numbering mutation and blocks execution on error.
5. Errors identify each conflicting number and affected channel or staged operation sufficiently for correction.
6. Backend integration tests cover cross-operation conflicts that per-operation validation would miss, plus valid swaps and vacated-number reuse.
7. A rendered E2E path demonstrates that Apply stops before mutation and displays actionable feedback.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits d2260c6e, e69430a3, cfd26589, 6e3e10f4.

A final-state preflight materialises the combined result of every staged operation and refuses Apply if it collides, in both the browser and the backend, running above the first request rather than inside the per-batch loop - creates go up in their own call, and a batch that fails halfway has already written.

The bead's interaction with vdxbx was handled explicitly, as briefed: a duplicate the operator deliberately confirmed is not re-raised as a preflight failure. The rule is that a duplicate is deliberate iff every channel THIS SESSION placed on that number carries consent for it; pre-existing occupants are not contributors, and one unacknowledged newcomer re-raises the whole pile-up naming only that newcomer.

A creates-only batch previously fetched no lineup at all, so the check had nothing to detect a collision against; a create carrying an explicit number now asks for one.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY REVIEW, both fixed as properties rather than at the reproduction:
- Consolidation destroyed submitted last-write-wins ACROSS operation kinds, so the browser previewed one number and the backend applied another. Fixed with a channel_number_owner map: exactly ONE emitted operation writes any given channel's number, for any submitted order across all three number-setting kinds.
- The backend preflight FAILED OPEN - a failed lineup fetch left existing_channels empty and the check reported no conflict. Now numbering_preflight_unavailable, severity error, joining the existing continueOnError contract: a non-UI caller (default false) is refused, Edit Mode proceeds because the browser validated against the lineup it loaded.

An omitted startingNumber is now 1 on all four layers (it became an explicit 0 in consolidation), an explicit 0 is honoured, and an empty channelIds no longer refuses a no-op.

title: Define and enforce valid canonical channel-number values
description:
## Problem
Channel-number inputs are parsed in multiple workflows without one enforced definition of valid values or canonical equivalence. Malformed, non-finite, non-positive, or textually different but numerically equal values can bypass consistent feedback or conflict checks.

## Scope
Define the supported channel-number domain, including whether fractional values are supported, and apply one canonical parsing and comparison contract at UI and API boundaries. Do not silently broaden or narrow Dispatcharr compatibility.

## User Value
Operators receive immediate, consistent feedback and cannot stage values that will fail later or compare incorrectly.

## Success Signal
Every channel-number entry surface applies the same validity and equivalence rules, and equivalent values cannot evade duplicate detection.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The supported channel-number domain is explicitly defined, including null or unassigned, minimum, maximum if applicable, precision, and fractional-number behavior.
2. Empty input, malformed text, NaN, infinity, zero, negative values, overflow, and unsupported precision are rejected or handled according to that contract.
3. Canonically equivalent inputs such as 7, 7.0, and 07 compare as the same number.
4. Shared parsing and comparison logic is reused by ordinary edits, staged-state checks, and commit preflight.
5. Invalid input cannot create a staged operation or API mutation.
6. Unit and rendered component tests cover valid boundaries, invalid classes, canonical equivalents, and null or clearing behavior.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #868 (merge 7426791e, build 0.18.1-0109). PO answered this bead's acceptance criterion 1 directly on 2026-08-15: decimal precision in Dispatcharr is one significant digit, only the tenths place matters.

CANONICAL VALUE: a non-negative number with at most one decimal place. null means unassigned and stays valid. No maximum (the PO's rule named none). No uniqueness (Dispatcharr permits duplicates; different question).

PO ALSO DECIDED the enforcement policy: REJECT out-of-contract values at the boundary with a clear operator-facing message, not silent normalization, accepting that a CSV import which previously succeeded may now fail, on the grounds that surfacing bad data beats altering it.

ONE DEFINITION, MANY CALLERS: backend/channel_number.py and frontend/src/utils/channelNumber.ts, with one sentence byte-identical on both sides. Enforced at channel create/patch/merge/assign-numbers/bulk-commit, CSV import and preview, the Channel Pipeline rule spec, and four frontend inputs.

THE SWEEP FOUND MORE THAN THE HANDED-DOWN LIST, including the highest-traffic entry point of all: the channel list's inline number editor. Also PATCH /api/channels/{id}, all three bulk-commit ops, and a SECOND bare float() in the CSV import route separate from the one in csv_handler.

DELIBERATELY NOT ENFORCED, each with a reason: uniqueness; pipeline range specs like '10000-99999' and '800-99999', because the PO's own live rules use them and narrowing the vocabulary would invalidate them; DBAS restore, because enforcing there would make a restore of a pre-enforcement archive fail and restore fidelity beats contract purity; integer-only parseInt renumber inputs, which produce a strict subset of the contract.

BLAST RADIUS CHECKED BEFORE SHIPPING, not after. The connected Dispatcharr reports zero channels; a scan of 1585 historical channel_number values in the April journal backup plus 11 live found ZERO out-of-contract values (1585 integers, 0 one-decimal, 0 sub-tenth, 0 negative). The instrument was smoke-tested first: profiles and M3U accounts returned real data and a bad key returned 401, so the zero is real rather than an auth failure.

CODEX FOUND FOUR ISSUES ACROSS THREE ROUNDS, all on this bead, all fixed:
- a validator that CRASHED instead of rejecting (1e308 raised OverflowError, a 500 where a 422 belonged)
- an entry point the enforcement missed, the separate-group bulk-create path, worse than reported: the guard checked only the FIRST group so later groups reached parseInt entirely unvalidated, and the preview reproduced the truncation
- a BLESSED SILENT-WRONG-RESULT: the schema accepted 1.1 while the executor auto-numbered. Wider than reported: 1.0, '1.0' and '1.1' were all silently auto-numbered. Rejected at the schema provisionally, pending bead ay3iq
- A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THE FIRST FIX: dodging the overflow by scaling only the fractional part rejected 10000000.1, an ordinary in-contract value, at roughly 61% of one-decimal values at magnitude 1e6 and about 80% across 1e7 to 1e14. Worse than the crash it replaced. Corrected with a 2**53 magnitude guard.

The final pass ENUMERATED THE SIX PROPERTIES the predicate must satisfy SIMULTANEOUSLY and demonstrated each, rather than fixing the named findings and hoping nothing else moved. Verified over 3.4M sampled values and a 46-value cross-half agreement vector. Codex confirmed all six hold with no discontinuity at the 2**53 boundary.

VERIFIED: backend 10073 passed 9 skipped; frontend 217 files / 2966 tests; six ratchets by exit code. Red-without-fix proven per fix.

FILED FROM THIS WORK: ay3iq (P2, pipeline silently ignores a fractional spec), j3pyx (P3, renumber inputs truncate silently), kg6wy (P3, derived numbers can inherit an out-of-contract value from another Dispatcharr client), 4azcp (P3, whitespace range spec validates then auto-numbers), 52e8a (P3, e2e trigger effect asymmetry).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO CONSTRAINT 2026-08-15, authoritative, recorded here because this bead owns the canonical-value definition: decimal precision in Dispatcharr is ONE significant digit. Only the tenths place matters.

So the canonical channel-number value this bead must define and enforce is a non-negative number with AT MOST ONE DECIMAL PLACE.

Evidence gathered on the way to this, worth keeping: there is no ECM database column for channel_number at all (channels live in Dispatcharr; grep over backend/ finds no such Column). Dispatcharr declares it as a NON-UNIQUE float field and its release notes state duplicate channel numbers are permitted; a same-group clean() check exists on the model but DRF serializers do not call full_clean(), so nothing enforces it server-side either. backend/csv_handler.py:126 accepts any positive float with no precision check, and the frontend parses with a bare parseFloat.

So today NOTHING in the stack enforces either uniqueness or precision, and the one-decimal rule lives only in the PO's head and in Dispatcharr's practice. That is precisely the gap this bead exists to close.

Bead i85dg (channel-number shift planner) consumes this: it aligns its slot resolution to tenths and treats an out-of-contract value as its nearest tenth for comparison, which is conservative. It deliberately does NOT enforce the invariant, because that is this bead's job.

title: Make channel numbering safe and predictable across edit workflows
description:
## Outcome
Channel operators can edit, swap, bulk-renumber, and apply channel numbers without creating invalid values, hidden collisions, partial numbering state, or overwriting concurrent changes unknowingly.

## Scope
Deliver a coherent set of safeguards for ordinary duplicate edits, valid and canonical number handling, final-state preflight across staged operations, swap-safe and failure-safe application, and commit-time concurrency detection.
