The safeguards must work together across inline edits, Edit Channel, staged creates, moves, shifts, and bulk renumbering without changing approved numbering behavior unnecessarily.

## User Value
Operators can trust that Apply will either produce the previewed final numbering or stop with actionable feedback before changing channel state.

## Success Signal
Supported numbering workflows reject invalid or conflicting final states before mutation, valid swaps and renumbers complete reliably, concurrent edits are surfaced, and automated rendered tests cover the critical user paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All child beads are completed and their acceptance criteria pass.
2. Channel numbering has one documented definition of valid and canonically equivalent values shared by UI validation and commit preflight.
3. The proposed final channel-number state is validated before mutations begin.
4. Valid multi-channel swaps and renumbers do not fail because of operation ordering.
5. Numbering failures do not leave an unexplained partially applied final state.
6. Concurrent server-side numbering changes are surfaced before overwrite.
7. Unit, component, backend integration, and rendered E2E coverage collectively exercise the protected workflows.
close_reason:
EPIC COMPLETE. All 7 children closed. Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111); ic884.1 and i85dg had shipped earlier.

The epic's outcome statement was that operators can edit, swap, bulk-renumber and apply channel numbers without creating invalid values, hidden collisions, partial numbering state, or overwriting concurrent changes unknowingly. All four now have a mechanism: the canonical value contract from ic884.1; a duplicate warning bound to the specific collision consented to; a final-state preflight over the combined result of every staged operation; a write ordering that never enters a slot its occupant has not left, with compensation and per-channel recovery steps; and a pre-Apply server read with per-channel reconcile.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED EVERYTHING, measured not assumed: Dispatcharr 0.28.x offers no conditional update. GET /api/schema/?format=json (HTTP 200, ~717KB) contains zero occurrences of If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, ETag or 412, and no version or modified-at field on Channel or PatchedChannel. So this epic detects and reports; it never prevents atomically, and no code, test, log line or operator-facing string claims otherwise. Compensation guarantees an inverse write is ATTEMPTED, not that it succeeds.

THE EPIC'S OWN LESSON HELD AGAIN. CLAUDE.md's rule about stating acceptance criteria as invariants rather than reproductions was learned on ic884.1, where two competent, tested, red-proven fixes were each scoped to the demonstrated case. It recurred here: a fix that closed the reported ordering bug left an adjacent kind unfixed; a cycle break released the wrong node when a chain fed the cycle; consent accumulated across a channel's history. Each was closed as a property, and each property found further defects nobody had reported.

Left open, filed from this work: jjjnh, v3wr1, 0by9g, 1e4at.

title: Warn before staging duplicate channel numbers in normal edits
description:
## Problem
Users editing a channel number can currently assign a number already used by another channel. Both inline channel-number editing and the Edit Channel modal stage the conflicting value without warning; the conflict may surface only when the edit session is applied, potentially causing a failed or partially applied commit.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Channel Manager with two channels using different channel numbers.
2. Enter Edit Mode.
3. Change one channel number through inline editing, or through Edit Channel, to the other channel's number.
4. Save the field or modal.
5. Observe that the conflicting number is staged without a warning; any rejection occurs only when changes are applied.

## Scope
Add a duplicate-number guard to ordinary single-channel edits. The check must use the effective edit-mode state, including previously staged channel-number changes, and must exclude the channel being edited. Preserve the existing cross-group move/renumber workflows and their conflict handling. Backend/API rejection remains a final safety net rather than the primary user feedback.

## User Value
Operators receive immediate, actionable feedback before staging an invalid or conflicting number, avoiding late apply failures and uncertainty about which changes were saved.

## Success Signal
Duplicate numbers are detected consistently from both normal edit surfaces before staging, while retaining the current number and choosing an unused number remain warning-free.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Inline channel-number editing in Edit Mode detects when the proposed non-null number is effectively assigned to another channel and presents a clear warning before staging the change.
2. The Edit Channel modal performs the same duplicate check before staging or saving a changed channel number.
3. The channel being edited is excluded, so retaining its current number does not warn.
4. Detection accounts for effective local state, including channel-number changes and newly created channels already staged in the current edit session, rather than only the last server-loaded channel list.
5. Invalid numeric input is handled explicitly and cannot stage NaN or another malformed value. Clearing a number remains supported if currently allowed.
6. The warning identifies the conflicting channel sufficiently for the operator to resolve it and prevents accidental staging until the conflict is changed or explicitly handled according to the approved UX.
7. Existing move, insertion, bulk renumber, and auto-shift conflict behavior is unchanged.
8. Component tests cover inline editing and the Edit Channel modal for duplicate, unchanged/self, unused, malformed, and staged-state conflict cases; a rendered integration/E2E test verifies the user-visible warning and blocked staging path.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). PO decision: WARN with explicit confirmation, do NOT hard-block. Commits d2260c6e, 9c34954a, cfd26589, 6e3e10f4, 6d0319b1.

The blocking option was rejected because ic884.1 deliberately declined to enforce uniqueness - Dispatcharr permits duplicate channel numbers - so refusing would contradict a shipped decision. AC 6's 'prevents accidental staging until explicitly handled' is satisfied by an explicit confirm.

THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS BOUND TO THE COLLISION, NOT THE NUMBER: {number, occupantChannelIds}, recording the occupants the DIALOG RENDERED, on the operation's apiCall. Deliberately not a separate registry - that is the exact shape whose failure blocked ic884.1 round 2, where deleting an unrelated action silently emptied a validity registry.

THREE REVIEWER ROUNDS, and the first found the feature broken on its own happy path: _consolidate_operations rebuilt the merged op via a constructor and dropped acknowledgedDuplicate entirely, before preflight ran, with the frontend always sending consolidate:true. Reproduced directly. So a confirmed duplicate had its legitimate commit refused. Fixed by copying a template rather than rebuilding, plus a preservation guard that fails if any future field is dropped.

Round 2 also found acknowledgements ACCUMULATING forever (move to 5 with consent, move to 6, move back to 5 without consent - still authorised) and a restored acknowledgement surviving the occupant set changing while the session was dead. Both closed, the latter by two independent routes because the same defect is reachable inside one live session.

THE CONSENT RULE, adjudicated deliberately and worth preserving: it is a SUBSET test, not equality. Consent to a worse collision covers a lesser one; a stranger arriving makes standing NOT a subset and is still refused. Requiring equality would re-interrogate an operator whose situation strictly improved. Pinned with mutation-proven tests on both sides so it is not re-litigated. A final review found restore was stricter than Apply and disagreed with the documented contract; restore now matches.

Adjudicating that rule also exposed a live dead end: the walk demanded consent from the FIRST arrival on a FREE number, where no dialog can ever fire. Two ordinary edits reached it. Fixed.

AC 8's rendered integration test is e2e/edit-mode-numbering-guards.spec.ts, passing in CI.

title: The compare API truncates at 300 files, so a large push can classify docs-only over thousands of unexamined code files
description:
From the code review of PR #816, 2026-08-10. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by that PR, and in the same quiet direction as the bypass it fixed. Filed rather than raised as a blocker so it does not get normalised away.

THE DEFECT. The push branch of the classify step in .github/workflows/{test,build,docs-pages}.yml uses:

  gh api --paginate repos/.../compare/A...B

GitHub's compare endpoint returns AT MOST 300 file entries regardless of pagination. The reviewer measured it: a range where 'git diff --name-only' lists 1818 paths returns exactly 300 through the API.

THE CONSEQUENCE. If a push of more than 300 files happened to have its first 300 entries all under '.beads/**' or '**.md', the classifier would report docs_only=true over thousands of unexamined code files, and every gated step would skip. The API returns entries roughly path-sorted with dot-directories first, so '.beads/**' leads, which makes the unlucky ordering more plausible than random chance would suggest. Beads exports are also exactly the kind of change that produces very large file counts.

EXPOSURE IS LIMITED, which is why this is P2 and not P1. This is the PUSH path, which runs post-merge, so it degrades the signal on dev rather than gating a PR. The PR path uses 'pulls/N/files', which paginates properly to 3000.

MITIGATION, cheap and fails open in both polarities: have the step treat 'length == 300' as UNDETERMINED and empty changed_files.txt. An empty file yields no docs_only verdict, every '!= true' gate runs, and docs_site_affected's opposite polarity also errs toward rebuilding. Do not try to reconstruct the full list from a different endpoint; treating truncation as 'I do not know' is both correct and simpler.

VERIFY WHEN FIXING: the reviewer did not establish whether 'pulls/N/files' truncates above 3000, only that it paginates further than compare does. If a PR can exceed 3000 changed files in this repo, the same treatment is needed there.

RELATED: bead ifx16 covers the guard's own completeness gaps from the same review. Bead gnz19 covers the classifier's docs-only definition. This bead is about the INPUT SET being incomplete, which is the same class of defect as 9ogyd, just triggered by volume rather than by renames.

title: The rename-source guard enumerates three workflows by name, so a fourth detect workflow silently reintroduces the hole
description:
From the code review of PR #816 (bead 9ogyd), 2026-08-10. Non-blocking, so #816 merged; this is the completeness gap the guard itself has.

THE DEFECT. backend/tests/unit/test_classify_changed_paths.py:470 hardcodes the allowlist:

  DETECT_WORKFLOWS = ('test.yml', 'build.yml', 'docs-pages.yml')

The reviewer added a FOURTH workflow calling scripts/classify_changed_paths.py with the defective '.files[]?.filename' expression. ALL 81 TESTS PASSED. So a future detect workflow silently reintroduces the exact bypass 9ogyd closed, and nothing goes red.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. The counter-argument is already in the same file, twenty lines above, in TestWorkflowContract._workflow_files's own docstring: globbing only '*.yml' 'would make a .yaml workflow invisible to every assertion in this class ... so the guard would pass while the defect it exists to catch was present.' That reasoning applies verbatim to enumeration. The file contradicts itself.

THE SHAPE TO REACH FOR is discovery, not enumeration: iterate _workflow_files(), keep every workflow whose detect job steps mention classify_changed_paths.py, assert the discovered set is NON-EMPTY so the discovery cannot silently find nothing, then assert on each. That also makes the finding below disappear for free and makes the guard survive a .yaml rename by design rather than by accident.

ALSO FIX WHILE THERE, from the same review:

  _array_shaped / _compare_shaped at :546 and :553 over-constrain to exactly one match. Adding a legitimate second 'gh api --jq' call inside the classify step, a diagnostic say, turns three or more tests red with 'expected one array-shaped expression'. The direction is noisy and self-announcing so it is acceptable today, but selecting expressions by the endpoint the surrounding gh api call queries, rather than by count, removes the trap. Subsumed by the discovery rewrite.

  jq is an unguarded binary dependency of six of the nine new tests. ubuntu-latest ships it and the engineer deliberately built a non-skippable textual assertion alongside, which was the right instinct. But this repo already owns the mechanism: backend/scripts/verify_test_deps.py (bead s8kq3), whose docstring names 'silent skips that CI treats as success' as its reason to exist, runs as a fast-fail step before pytest, and checks Python imports only. Adding a binary check for jq closes the loop with the pattern the repo already chose.

  scripts/classify_changed_paths.py:78's docstring documents the local command as 'git diff --name-only origin/dev...HEAD | python scripts/classify_changed_paths.py'. That command is rename-blind, which is the very defect 9ogyd fixed. A developer following it gets docs_only=true on exactly the rename CI now catches, so the local answer disagrees with CI in the permissive direction. One word: --no-renames. Note bead gnz19 also touches this file and PR #815 touches the hook's own copy of that command, so coordinate.

title: OCR the 144 unreviewed committed images: a credential rendered as pixels is invisible to every scanner in use
description:
Split out of the h9av3 history sweep, 2026-08-10, by PO decision. This is the largest remaining gap in that audit.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not hypothetical. The sweep's Finding 2 was a live mcp_api_key captured in a Playwright accessibility snapshot of the Settings > MCP Integration card, with the key rendered inside a code element. It was found ONLY because an a11y snapshot is text. A PNG screenshot of that same screen would have been invisible to every scanner used in the audit, and to gitleaks, detect-secrets and GitHub secret scanning alike. Byte-pattern scanning cannot see pixels.

CURRENT COVERAGE. Of 152 committed images, 8 were reviewed visually by eye, chosen as the highest-risk credential-entry screens (Dispatcharr connection, MCP integration, and similar). All 8 were sanitized: dispatcharr.example.local, empty password fields, 'Unconfigured' states, localhost:8199/demo.m3u. The other 144 received byte-pattern scanning and PNG metadata checks (tEXt, iTXt, zTXt, eXIf chunks, all clean) but NO visual inspection.

SCOPE: OCR all 152 committed images and review the extracted text for credential shapes. Include images that exist only in history, not just those present at the tip, since Finding 2 demonstrates the tip is not where the risk lives.

WORTH BUILDING RATHER THAN DOING ONCE. The docs/images/ tree grows with every user-guide refresh, and today's work already queued a screenshot re-shoot (bead gk4d0, 25 pre-rework screenshots, P1). A one-off OCR pass goes stale the moment the next screenshot lands. Consider whether this belongs as the image arm of scripts/check_pii.py, which already has two documented seams for exactly that (_kind_for and _SEGMENTERS) left by bead fu6yd.

That would make three arms sharing one ratchet: text PII (il1xz), ECM-specific secrets (h9av3), and images (fu6yd plus this). fu6yd covers the PII bar on images; this covers credentials on images. Same mechanism, and they should almost certainly be one implementation rather than two.

HANDLING CONSTRAINT, same as the parent sweep: if OCR surfaces a real credential, record location, type and liveness only. Never the value, and never validate liveness by using the credential. Reports flow into transcripts and PR bodies on a public repository.

CONTEXT: bead h9av3 carries the full sweep findings. Two real mcp_api_key values were found in history, both confirmed dead by offline hash comparison, and the PO has ruled against history rewriting.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Split the pool by risk class before sizing. Counts confirmed exactly (152 ever-added image blobs, 151 at tip, 144 unreviewed, unchanged since the bead was filed). But only ~114 are live-instance screenshots and therefore a credential surface: docs/images/user_guide 105, docs/images/event_sync 7, docs/images/normalization 2. The other 37 are deterministic test oracles and static assets (e2e/snapshots 33, e2e/visual/__screenshots__ 1, frontend/public 3, frontend/src/assets 1), fixture-rendered and not a credential surface. Confirmed absent: any OCR tooling anywhere in the repo, any image arm in scripts/check_pii.py (the fu6yd seams at :339 and :1005-1016 are still literally unimplemented comments), and any png entry in .secrets.baseline.

title: Nothing enforces the classifier/hook output contract; a third key could break the ship guard silently
description:
Found by the engineer implementing uf2gh, 2026-08-10, after the same class of break was caught by hand hours earlier.

THE COUPLING. .claude/hooks/version-advance-guard.sh consumes scripts/classify_changed_paths.py's stdout to decide whether to skip the build-advance check. The hook extracts docs_only BY KEY from key=value lines. The classifier is obliged to keep emitting that key. Nothing enforces the obligation in either direction.

HOW CLOSE THIS ALREADY CAME. Commit 76e19f88 of the hook compared the classifier's ENTIRE stdout against the literals 'docs_only=true' and 'docs_only=false'. Bead t4d5w then added a second output line, docs_site_affected. Two lines match neither literal, so every invocation would have taken the fail-open path: a permanently degraded guard that warns on each run while enforcing nothing. Demonstrated live at the time, including a non-advancing CODE change passing with a warning phrased as though the guard were working.

That was caught by hand, by cross-reading two branches that happened to be in flight together. No test, no gate, and no type would have caught it. If t4d5w had merged a week later, or if the two had been worked by people who never spoke, it ships.

WHAT IS PINNED TODAY, and what is not. The hook's five TestVerdictIsReadByKey cases pin the HOOK's side: extra key before, extra key after, docs_only buried among four keys, docs_only=false alongside another key, and CRLF. Nothing pins the CLASSIFIER's obligation to keep emitting docs_only at all. A future change that renames or drops that key passes every existing test and silently disables the agent-side guard.

Bead gnz19 makes this concrete and near-term: it proposes renaming the output to code_paths_changed. That rename is exactly the change this gap fails to catch, which is why gnz19 is already sequenced to land only after uf2gh merges. That sequencing is a human promise, not a mechanism.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, for whoever picks it up: a test asserting the classifier emits docs_only on every stdout path, including its error paths, and ideally a contract test exercised from the hook's side against the real script rather than a fixture. The engineer verified by hand that every path in the real main() emits both keys today, including the unreadable-input path at line 214, so the property holds now and just needs pinning.

RELATED: check_pii.py is about to gain a second arm under bead h9av3, and the fu6yd image arm after that. Same shape of contract, same absence of enforcement, so a general answer is likely worth more than a one-off test.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9). 6u2pa: the docs-only sentinel workflow was deleted in commit abd325bb ('One source of truth per required status check', bead 5rwzy); every required-check name now has exactly one emitting job, pinned by TestWorkflowContract in test_classify_changed_paths.py. m1ug0: test_output_is_exactly_the_two_github_output_keys now pins the classifier's exact two-key contract across normal, empty and malformed inputs, and the hook extracts by key rather than whole-output comparison. i24jr: superseded by bead t8fqg (closed, PR #797), which shipped scripts/check_publish.py as a mandatory docs/shipping.md step verifying both the build run's conclusion and the published tag's ECM_VERSION marker. ykev5: premise was already false at filing — 38 semver tags run unbroken from 0.7 through 0.18.0 (verified against the live GHCR registry), well past the claimed 0.8.3 ceiling.

title: Rework what 'documentation-only' means: .md test fixtures, .beads granularity, and the output name
description:
Split out of bead t4d5w during Phase 1 implementation. t4d5w cannot be fully closed until this lands.

Three separate problems with scripts/classify_changed_paths.py's current rule ('**.md' OR '.beads/**'), from the architecture spike on 2026-08-10.

1. '**.md' IS TOO BROAD BECAUSE .md FILES ARE LIVE TEST FIXTURES. backend/tests/unit/test_check_em_dashes.py:42 reads docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md as REAL_FILE_FIXTURE. Commit 185a4009 exists precisely because deleting a different .md file broke Backend Tests with a FileNotFoundError, and it was caught only because that PR also touched code. Today a .md-only PR touching a fixture path classifies docs-only, Backend Tests hollow-passes, and the breakage lands on dev where it surfaces as a red gate on somebody else's unrelated work.

   Two ways to fix, and the second is better: carve the known fixture paths out of the docs classification, OR invert it and assert in the backend suite that no test reads a repo .md outside a declared allowlist. The second prevents recurrence rather than patching the instance.

2. '.beads/**' IS THE WRONG GRANULARITY. Tracked contents are issues.jsonl, issues.jsonl.bak, metadata.json, config.yaml, README.md and .gitignore. The first three are machine-generated state and are reasonably inert. config.yaml GOVERNS how bd behaves inside .github/workflows/release-cut-gate.yml:257 - the --no-db --no-daemon flags there exist because of what it says - so it is code. Classify .beads/*.jsonl, .beads/*.jsonl.bak and .beads/metadata.json as inert; classify .beads/config.yaml and .beads/.gitignore as code.

3. THE OUTPUT IS NAMED BY OPPOSITION. 'docs_only' says what a change is NOT. What the classifier actually computes is 'no changed path is an input to any code gate'. Renaming to code_paths_changed makes it positive and makes the fail-open default the natural 'true'.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT ON ITEM 3, and the reason it was deferred rather than done. The held branch fix/version-guard-docs-only (bead uf2gh) consumes docs_only BY NAME. Renaming the output under an unmerged consumer breaks that branch. Item 3 must land AFTER uf2gh merges, or the two must be coordinated in one change. Items 1 and 2 have no such constraint.

WHY THIS WAS SPLIT OFF t4d5w. Items 1 and 2 change what six required CI checks actually EXECUTE ON. That deserves its own reviewable diff rather than riding inside a 1,098-line CI change where it would be rubber-stamped. Structurally, consider replacing the two-constant heuristic with an explicit commented allowlist, one entry per line with a rationale, so every future addition is a deliberate act reviewed against 'can this path change the outcome of any gate?'. The current form invites someone to add '**.txt' without noticing docs/requirements-docs.txt.

RELATED: mkdocs.yml is 'code' under the current rule, so editing it runs the full backend suite, which is wasteful. Phase 1 added a docs_site_affected output that covers the site-input half; this bead should make sure the two outputs do not disagree about it.

title: version-advance-guard.sh blocks docs-only PRs that CI exempts; w9irb's scoping half was never implemented
description:
The repo-tracked hook .claude/hooks/version-advance-guard.sh performs no path classification, so it blocks gh pr create on documentation-only changes that CI deliberately exempts.

NOT AN OVERSIGHT, A HALF-FINISHED BEAD. Bead w9irb, which created this hook, already specified 'SCOPE using the EXISTING docs-only classification.' Only the CI half was implemented. test.yml gates its advance step on needs.detect.outputs.docs_only != 'true' with the comment 'Documentation-only PRs are exempt: they carry no build to advance.' The hook never got that half.

The hook's own header calls it 'the agent-side half of the build-advance gate' (line 6) and states 'a false block here is a friction bug, not a safety gap' (line 39), so exceeding CI was never the intent.

MEASURED COST, 2026-08-10. A two-line .beads/issues.jsonl PII redaction was forced to bump three version touchpoints across frontend/package.json, backend/main.py and backend/routers/backup.py, files it had no business touching, and consumed a build number another in-flight branch already held. More broadly: 15 of the last 40 merged PRs (37%) are 'documentation plus a version bump and nothing else' and would classify docs-only if the bump were not forced.

FIX, implemented on branch fix/version-guard-docs-only, commit 328e07b1, HELD pending bead t4d5w:
  - hook shells out to scripts/classify_changed_paths.py in its already-resolved PROJECT_DIR, so there is ONE definition of docs-only rather than a bash reimplementation
  - classification uses git diff --name-only origin/<base>...HEAD, three-dot, matching the file set the PR will actually contain rather than the working tree
  - fails OPEN on classifier failure, matching the hook's existing missing-checker behaviour at line 125 and check_version_advances.py's own soft-pass on an unavailable baseline
  - only 'true' and 'false' are recognised verdicts; anything else is 'could not classify' and fails open, so a garbled classifier can neither skip the gate nor manufacture a block
  - every fail-open path warns loudly naming the reason, so a degraded guard is visible rather than silent
  - 421-line fixture self-test, closing the gap yxtuz recorded as a backlog candidate. 23 tests. Reverting the hook to origin/dev fails exactly 12 of 23, so the 11 deny-side and injection cases are not vacuous.

SEQUENCING, NON-NEGOTIABLE. This change ACTIVATES a latent defect: on a docs-only PR, six of seven required checks on dev report success having executed nothing. The unconditional hook is currently the only thing preventing that path from running. Bead t4d5w must land first. Do not merge this before it.

FAIL-OPEN RESIDUAL, for the security reviewer: while the classifier is broken, a non-advancing build on a CODE change is caught only by CI. Given the hollow-check finding above, that residual deserves an explicit look rather than being discovered at review.

RELATED GAP FOUND AND NOT FIXED HERE: the docs-only exemption is documented NOWHERE for operators. The only prose is the test.yml:517 comment. docs/shipping.md section 3 'Increment the Version' reads unconditionally with no carve-out, so the hook will behave differently from the only written instruction. That docs edit belongs with t4d5w rather than here, because editing docs/ would change this branch's own classification mid-exercise.
close_reason: Merged in PR #815; parser-free docs-only version guard shipped with reviewed conservative candidate detection.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
LANDING CONSTRAINT, checked rather than assumed (2026-08-10).

The engineer flagged a concern worth recording precisely, because the version of it that is true is narrower than the version that is scary.

THE CONCERN AS RAISED: if t4d5w's second classifier output line (docs_site_affected) lands while this branch does not, the shipped hook goes dead silently.

WHY THAT SPECIFIC SCENARIO IS NOT REACHABLE: dev's currently-shipped .claude/hooks/version-advance-guard.sh does not reference classify_changed_paths.py at all - verified, 0 occurrences. It is still the unconditional version this bead exists to fix. So t4d5w merging on its own cannot break the shipped guard; there is nothing in it that reads the classifier. The dead-guard scenario required the old whole-output parser to already be on dev, and it never was.

WHAT WAS GENUINELY DANGEROUS, and was caught before shipping: commit 76e19f88 on this branch compared the classifier's ENTIRE stdout against the literals 'docs_only=true' and 'docs_only=false'. Against t4d5w's two-line output that matches neither, so every invocation would take the fail-open path. Demonstrated live by the engineer with both hook versions against the same branch and the same resolved root:

  docs+beads only, no bump   OLD: WARNING, unrecognised verdict -> exit 0   NEW: SKIPPED, docs_only=true -> exit 0
  CODE change, no bump       OLD: WARNING, unrecognised verdict -> exit 0   NEW: FAIL, build 59 equals baseline 59 -> exit 2

The second row is the one that mattered. Under the old parsing a genuine non-advancing CODE change passed, with a warning phrased as though the guard were working. A permanently degraded guard that looks alive is worse than an absent one.

FIXED in dbcc8527: docs_only is extracted BY KEY via sed rather than by whole-output equality. A missing or unrecognised VALUE for that key still fails open and is never read as false; only the presence of other keys stopped being fatal. Duplicate docs_only lines fail open rather than letting the first win, and CRLF is stripped so a checkout with Windows line endings cannot degrade the guard the same way.

Five new tests in TestVerdictIsReadByKey, all confirmed red against 76e19f88: extra key after, extra key before (so nothing depends on line order), docs_only buried among four keys, docs_only=false alongside another key still blocking, and the CRLF case. 29 cases total on the hook, 95 across the related suites.

REMAINING ORDER REQUIREMENT, unchanged and for a different reason: t4d5w still lands FIRST, because THIS branch activates the hollow-required-check path on documentation-only PRs and t4d5w is what gives those PRs a real gate. That is the constraint, not the parsing one.

title: Refreshing .beads/issues.jsonl during concurrent agent work snapshots other agents' in-flight state
description:
A standing process hazard, found on 2026-08-10 while closing bead il1xz. Not a one-off.

WHAT HAPPENED. The task was to propagate a two-record PII redaction into the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl. The obvious route is a full regeneration: 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl'. The engineer measured that route before taking it and found it produces 142 ADDED records and 23 CHANGED ones against the tracked file, as a roughly 3.8 MB diff.

The changes were legitimate, and the timestamps identified them:

  enhancedchannelmanager-iotbh  status open -> in_progress   updated_at -> 2026-08-10T15:08:17Z
  enhancedchannelmanager-meh0a  status in_progress -> closed updated_at -> 2026-08-10T15:33:05Z
  enhancedchannelmanager-w8u1e  status open -> closed        updated_at -> 2026-08-10T16:26:57Z

Those were two other agents' bead state, being written at that moment from their own worktrees. A full refresh would have snapshotted their in-flight work into an unrelated PII fix, in a diff no reviewer could meaningfully read, with a large conflict surface against any other branch that also regenerated.

The engineer instead replaced only the two affected records with their authoritative 'bd export' output and copied every other line byte for byte: 2 lines changed, order preserved, all 2984 records parsing, verified with a measured delta rather than asserted.

WHY THIS RECURS. Commit 845ead93 (2026-08-02, 'chore(beads): refresh JSONL export') shows the full refresh IS the established precedent, and it is the natural thing to reach for. The hazard only becomes visible if someone measures the diff first, which is not the habit.

WHAT TO DECIDE AND RECORD:
  1. A full 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' refresh should happen only when no agents are mid-flight, and the person doing it should confirm that rather than assume it.
  2. For a targeted change to N records, the surgical route (replace those records from 'bd export' output, copy the rest byte for byte) is correct and should be the documented default.
  3. Decide where this lives so it is actually read: CLAUDE.md's beads section, or docs/shipping.md. The Beads Quick Reference in CLAUDE.md currently documents 'bd sync', which does not exist in the installed build. That is worth fixing in the same pass.

RELATED: the beads worktree at .git/beads-worktrees/beads is a red herring for propagation. It sits on branch 'beads' at e985de9a (v0.16.0-0033, April) and is NOT an ancestor of dev, so committing there goes nowhere. Worth stating explicitly wherever this is documented, because CLAUDE.md's phrasing invites the assumption that it is the sync mechanism.

title: contrast-aa fails with 14 empty-state violations on a container with no M3U or EPG sources
description:
Found during the fix/ux-batch-0057 work and proven PRE-EXISTING: the engineer ran contrast-aa against the UNMODIFIED baseline build on the same data and got the byte-identical 14 violations, so this is not caused by that branch.

All 14 are empty-state artifacts of an instance with zero M3U accounts and zero EPG sources:
  - the 64px 'add' glyph on '.empty-state > .btn-primary' in both M3U Manager and EPG Manager, across all three themes and both viewports
  - a 'warning' glyph on the dashboard in light theme

The interesting question is not the glyphs, it is what this says about the guard. contrast-aa logs into a LIVE container and measures whatever that container happens to contain, so its pass/fail depends on instance data rather than on the code under test. An instance with sources configured would not surface these at all. That makes the guard's result non-reproducible between environments and is arguably a design gap in the guard as much as a styling defect.

DECIDE, then fix accordingly:
  (a) the empty-state glyphs are genuinely under the AA floor and should be re-toned, or
  (b) they are decorative and belong in the allowlist with a rationale, the way the dashboard card glyphs were deliberately ratified in commit e510c95a, or
  (c) the guard should seed a known data state rather than measuring whatever is present.

Note (c) interacts with bead 2lw25, which records that contrast-aa structurally cannot run backend-less.

Related: bead rnzu0 tracks three separate operator-shell contextual-settings specs that are also failing on dev today. Between the two, more of the rendered-CSS guard estate is red than the docs imply.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECISION 2026-08-12 (backlog validity audit bd bewu9): RE-TONE. Fix the glyph colours so they meet AA contrast. Do NOT allowlist the violations, and do not treat this as a seed-data/empty-state guard problem.

This bead is now engineering work, not a decision. The 14 violations were live-reproduced during the audit by running 'npx playwright test e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts' against the running ecm-ecm-1 container, and the failing set matches the bead's enumeration exactly:

- m3u-manager and epg-manager, '.empty-state > button.btn-primary > span.material-icons' with the 'add' glyph, failing in all three themes at both viewports (12 rows):
    dark 2.78 vs 3.0
    light 1.13 vs 3.0
    high-contrast 2.16 vs 3.0
- dashboard, light theme, 1920x1080, tone-warn 'warning' glyph: 1.97 vs 3.0 (1 row)
  (the twelfth/thirteenth rows are the same two empty-state cases at the second viewport; 14 bracketed violation blocks total)

Scope: re-tone the empty-state primary-button glyph and the tone-warn glyph so all three themes clear 3.0, then confirm contrast-aa runs green with no allowlist entries added. Note the light-theme empty-state case at 1.13 is the worst offender by a wide margin and will need the largest shift.

title: Guard against PII in committed text: personal email is in two bead descriptions and re-committed on every sync
description:
PO instruction 2026-08-10: the existing exposure in public git history is accepted and will not be rewritten, but no NEW instances should be added.

CURRENT STATE, measured today on dev:

  docs/runbooks/stats-v2-deployment-safety.md   1 occurrence
  docs/runbooks/stats-v2-write-failures.md      1 occurrence
  .beads/issues.jsonl                           2 occurrences

The two runbook instances are already redacted on branch docs/salvage-orphaned-worktree-edits, which is queued to merge. That work was originally written on 2026-08-01 as part of a wider PII sweep (private mockup URL, a local filesystem path, real EPG source names, Dispatcharr usernames) which was orphaned uncommitted in a stale worktree and never landed. That sweep is the reason this bead exists at all.

The .beads instances are NOT covered and are the ongoing vector. The email sits in the description field of two closed beads:
  enhancedchannelmanager-6l7s7      SMTP test email fails with generic error
  enhancedchannelmanager-skqln.11   Stats v2: SLOs, storage-growth alerts, deployment-safety

.beads/issues.jsonl is TRACKED, not gitignored, so every bead operation re-commits both records. Redacting the two descriptions stops that.

SCOPE:
1. Redact the personal email from those two bead descriptions, replacing it with a role placeholder rather than deleting the escalation context.
2. Add a CI guard that fails when a personal-identifier pattern is ADDED to tracked text. Follow the shape of scripts/check_em_dashes.py, which already does added-lines-only checking against a base ref, so pre-existing occurrences do not block every PR. Cover at minimum docs/ and .beads/.
3. Decide the pattern set deliberately. A bare email regex over .beads/ will be noisy, since bead records legitimately carry a committer identity. Target the specific personal address and the classes the 08-01 sweep found (private URLs, absolute local filesystem paths, real provider account names) rather than everything shaped like an email.

RELATED: bead fu6yd covers the same gap for IMAGES (no CI enforcement of the PII bar on screenshots under docs/images/). That bead and this one should probably share one guard script with two arms. Do not close fu6yd as part of this; coordinate with it.

NOT IN SCOPE: rewriting git history. The PO has explicitly accepted the existing exposure.
close_reason: Merged in PR #817; added-lines PII ratchet shipped with zero-value reporting and fail-closed unscannable handling.

title: Three operator-shell contextual-settings specs are failing on dev right now
description:
A live red gate on dev that is in no bead. Found independently by two agents during the wave-1 CSS work and confirmed pre-existing by both.

Failing specs in e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:
  - contextual settings links use stable current hashes
  - staged contextual navigation (partial title, exact wording in the spec)
  - contextual settings navigation cleanly exits

VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the in-flight guard branch. The guard-repair engineer confirmed by stashing its own changes and re-running against unmodified origin/dev, both backend-less and against a live container on port 6100. The code reviewer independently corroborated structurally: every hunk in that branch is confined to lines 445-643 (the contrast machinery) plus two addStyleTag insertions at 1261 and 1437 inside the two contrast tests, none of which these three specs touch. The engineer's own run logs show the same story from the other side: operator-full.log has 4 failures including the contrast test, operator-full2.log has 3 with the contrast test passing.

Nobody has diagnosed WHY they fail. That is this bead's work: determine whether the specs are wrong, the app regressed, or the fixtures drifted, then fix whichever it is.

Context that may matter: operator-shell.spec.ts is one of the seven rendered-CSS guards, it needs a live backend, and it is manual-only rather than CI-gated (docs/testing.md:166-224 documents that split deliberately). So these have been red without anything shouting about it. Related: bead 63aqu records that e2e/ is covered by neither typecheck nor lint, and two genuine type errors already slipped through as a result.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-08-13 after an independent audit of my own closure work (OpenAI Codex) found the closure unsupported. It was wrong and the reasoning was mine.

I closed this saying the diagnosis was complete and that updating the stale assertions would 'ride with hmr0e'. Verified: hmr0e is 'Remove the Linked account settings link from M3U Manager', is still in_progress, and contains ZERO mentions of operator-shell.spec.ts, these specs, or the 'Channel default settings' link. Nothing was going to pick this up.

The stale assertions are still present on dev, and there are FOUR, not the three the bead names:

  e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:3249
  e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:3256
  e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:3301
  e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:3314

All still do getByRole('link', { name: 'Channel default settings' }), while frontend/src/components/routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks so that link no longer renders. The label in the Settings sidebar is now 'Channel Defaults' (settingsSections.ts:97), and it is a sidebar destination rather than a contextual route-header link.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RIGHT: the diagnosis. The specs are stale, the app is correct, and this is not a product defect. That half stands and was live-reproduced against the running container (3 failed / 3 run on the named -g filter).

WHAT REMAINS, which is this bead's actual deliverable: update or delete the four assertions so they match the shipped navigation. Decide per assertion whether the test still has a reason to exist once the contextual link is gone, rather than mechanically repointing all four at the sidebar; two of them are exercising Edit Mode exit behaviour that may want a different entry point entirely.

PROCESS NOTE FOR ME: a closure that defers its remaining work to another bead must verify that bead actually covers it. I asserted a handoff without reading the target. That is the same failure mode as trusting a comment instead of the code, which I spent the day catching in other people's work.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #862, merged to dev as 3786ce63, published and verified at the registry marker: ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0100 built from 3786ce6359a7.

ROOT CAUSE: the specs were stale, the product was correct. routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 stopped passing settingsLinks for Channel Manager (bead mer2o: Channel Defaults has its own Settings nav entry, so the header link was a redundant second path), and routeHierarchy.test.ts:154 pins that. Four statements in e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts still targeted the removed 'Channel default settings' link. Established against the route hierarchy and a live-built UI snapshot, NOT against another bead's description.

NOTE ON THE EARLIER CLOSURE. This bead was previously closed on the claim its fix 'rides with' hmr0e. That was wrong: hmr0e covers removing an M3U Manager link and none of this work. The bead was reopened during a Codex audit of the orchestrator's own judgment. This is the incident behind CLAUDE.md's 'never assert a handoff without opening the target' rule.

WHAT SHIPPED. Three specs repointed from the removed contextual link to the primary navigation rail, which still routes through handleRouteChange -> getGuardedRouteDecision. Two specs ADDED, each recovering a guard path nothing covered:
- 'a deep settings destination exits an emptied edit session without prompting': handleRouteChange('settings','channel-defaults') with edit mode active and staged count zero, the deep-route exit-and-navigate shape.
- 'Keep Editing cancels a deep settings request and leaves the rail drilled in': Keep Editing cancelling a pending route carrying a settingsPage, plus the post-cancellation rail state.

Both shapes are reachable: TabNavigation.tsx:216 calls openSettingsSections() BEFORE onTabChange, so with staged changes the guard defers navigation while the rail has already drilled in; Keep Editing leaves it drilled in; and edit mode's local undo (App.tsx:1569) empties the staged count without leaving edit mode.

VERIFICATION. Five mutation proofs, each showing the specs fail against a broken product rather than passing vacuously: guard forced to 'navigate' (3 failed); Channel Pipeline settingsLinks removed (exact-one-link assertion failed); exit-and-navigate branch dropping the settings page (1 failed, the new deep spec only); confirm branch skipped for deep requests (2 failed, exactly the two deep-pending specs); openSettingsSections() removed (3 failed, the rail-dependent specs). Nothing skipped, deleted, loosened, or given a wider timeout. Full 'operator shell navigation behavior' block: 25 passed, run independently by the orchestrator on the merged SHA.

REVIEW. Four adversarial review rounds. Two found real coverage gaps hiding behind overstated summaries; the code was correct from the first submission. Reviewed finally against a fixed rubric with no blocking findings.

FILED, NOT FIXED HERE: enhancedchannelmanager-6fi7p, App.tsx:665 and :652 call setHash(...) directly and bypass the Edit Mode guard entirely, so an operator with staged edits who triggers 'Clean up empty groups' loses them with no dialog.

title: journal.db is validated by magic bytes only, so a schema-mismatched backup bricks the instance
description:
Found during the security review of branch fix/lf29s-restore-initial-auth-gate. Pre-existing; also reachable by an admin via POST /api/backup/restore.

backend/routers/backup.py:1922-1925 validates journal.db by reading its first 16 bytes and checking the SQLite magic header. Nothing checks that the database actually carries the application schema.

OBSERVED, not theorised. The reviewer's first synthetic payload was a valid SQLite file containing only a users table. _validate_backup_zip accepted it, _restore_from_zip installed it, and init_db() in the finally block raised sqlalchemy.exc.NoSuchTableError: auto_creation_rules. The instance is left running against a wrong-schema database.

Impact: an anonymous single-request persistent denial of service on precisely the state restore-initial exists to serve — a fresh install or a DR rebuild. Recovery requires manually replacing /config/journal.db, which an operator part-way through a disaster recovery is least equipped to do.

FIX: after the magic-byte check, open the candidate database read-only and assert a few required tables exist before installing it. Natural companion to the unbounded-decompression bead, since both live in _validate_backup_zip. Effort: Low.

title: Backup artifact is unsigned and settings.json is unvalidated, so a restore can plant a persistent mcp_api_key
description:
Found during the security review of branch fix/lf29s-restore-initial-auth-gate. OWASP A08:2021, Software and Data Integrity Failures.

_validate_backup_zip (backend/routers/backup.py:1900) checks zip-slip and the SQLite magic bytes. It does NOT check any signature or integrity of the artifact, and _merge_settings_preserving_redacted (:1939) applies JSON-parse validation ONLY to settings.json, with no schema check, before merging it into the live settings blob.

DEMONSTRATED by the reviewer on the by-design-open branches: an anonymous upload installed itself as the only admin AND set mcp_api_key='ATTACKER-PLANTED-KEY' AND wrote attacker-controlled tls/key.pem and tls/cert.pem. Harness output: users=['attacker'] mcp_api_key='ATTACKER-PLANTED-KEY'.

Why this matters beyond the obvious takeover: the planted mcp_api_key is a PERSISTENT ADMIN-EQUIVALENT BEARER CREDENTIAL THAT SURVIVES THE OPERATOR LATER RE-ENABLING require_auth. Both auth_middleware and get_current_user honour it. So an operator who notices the compromise and turns auth back on does not evict the attacker. The attacker-supplied tls/ likewise becomes the server's TLS identity material.

Existing mitigations: zip-slip is properly defended; is_configured() blocks the common case; after the lf29s fix this requires admin or one of the two deliberately-open states (genuine first run, or require_auth off). DispatcharrSettings is a Pydantic v2 model defaulting to extra='ignore', so unknown keys are dropped, but every KNOWN key including mcp_api_key is settable.

FIX: validate settings.json against the settings model before writing, and treat mcp_api_key the way redacted credentials are already treated (preserve the existing value, never take it from the artifact). Effort: Medium.

title: Every restore path downgrades the TLS private key from 0600 to world-readable
description:
Found during the security review of branch fix/lf29s-restore-initial-auth-gate. Pre-existing, NOT introduced by that commit. Shared by POST /api/backup/restore, POST /api/backup/restore-saved and POST /api/backup/restore-initial.

backend/routers/backup.py:2111-2127 does shutil.rmtree(dir_path), then dir_path.mkdir(...), then target.write_bytes(...), which recreates the directory and files at the default umask. The application deliberately enforces os.chmod(self.tls_dir, 0o700) and os.chmod(self.key_path, 0o600) at backend/tls/storage.py:82 and :127, and the Dockerfile does chmod 700 /config/tls at line 69. Every restore silently undoes all of that.

MEASURED, not inferred. Post-restore in the reviewer's harness: tls_dir_mode=0o775, key.pem_mode=0o664 under umask 002. Under a container umask of 022 it is 0755/0644, still a downgrade from 0700/0600.

Impact: the HTTPS private key becomes group and world readable. With /config bind-mounted, it is readable by any host user, not only in-container.

Interacts with the unsigned-artifact finding: an attacker-supplied backup can write its own tls/key.pem and tls/cert.pem, so a later HTTPS enablement would serve a key the attacker knows, at permissions that let any local user read it.

FIX: re-apply 0700 and 0600 after the directory loop, or route the tls/ members through CertificateStorage so the existing enforcement runs. Effort: Low.

title: Modal/contrast guard hygiene: no geometry diff arm, duplicated canvas model, silent ratio rounding
description:
Three non-blocking findings from the code review of branch guards/wave1-measurement-layer (beads pbkwo, iotbh, j5m9v). N1 from that review was fixed on the branch itself; these three were deferred here by PO decision.

N2 — --diff never compares geometry. scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs:466-473 builds its comparison tuple from font-size, font-weight, line-height, letter-spacing and text-transform only. The iotbh fix made the geometry arm trustworthy for the first time (two consecutive frozen runs move 0 of 411 rows), and docs/testing.md now advertises that, but nothing reads it. The geometry rows are captured and then never diffed, so '--diff reports 0' does NOT mean the boxes did not move. At minimum state this explicitly in docs/testing.md so a downstream engineer does not misread it; adding an actual geometry arm is now worthwhile and was not before. Relevant to the roughly 18 CSS beads that will lean on this instrument.

N3 — the canvas measurement model lives in two files with only prose holding them together. e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts and e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:514-628 both carry the accepts()/group-opacity/paint core and cross-cite each other with 'a change to the model belongs in both'. The justification is technically correct, because a page.evaluate body is serialised and cannot close over a module import, but nothing enforces parity and e2e/ has no lint or typecheck gate to notice drift (see bead 63aqu). Options: extract the shared core to a module that exports it as a string and inject it into both evaluate bodies, or add a cheap test asserting the two extracted source regions are textually identical.

N4 — the ratio is rounded before assertion, slightly loosening the guard. e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:617 applies Math.round(ratio * 100) / 100 where the previous implementation returned the raw value, so a true ratio of 4.4951 now rounds to 4.50 and passes. That is an implicit epsilon of about 0.005 that did not exist before. Immaterial today because every measured selector clears 4.5 with room, and it is consistent with contrast-aa's own rounding, but it is a silent contract change rather than a deliberate one. contrast-aa at least makes its tolerance explicit via RATIO_EPSILON; do the same here or drop the rounding.

Two further nits recorded but not worth their own beads: getAnimations() is sampled once in freezeAndSettle(), so a script-driven animation starting in the one-evaluate-round-trip window would be missed (CSS animations are still covered by the override, and measured drift is zero); and diff() at scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs:453 iterates after.dialogs only, so it reports NEW DIALOG but never REMOVED DIALOG.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
TWO ADDITIONAL FINDINGS from the N1 review round (2026-08-10). Both are MODEL-LEVEL and both must land in BOTH copies of the canvas measurement core, which is why they belong here alongside N3 rather than in their own bead.

1. PSEUDO-ELEMENT GRADIENTS ARE NOT COVERED. The N1 fix makes the measurement refuse to proceed when a background-image is found in the chain, and the reviewer worked six escape routes and confirmed five are covered: the 'background' shorthand (getComputedStyle returns the resolved longhand), a gradient on the measured element itself (the chain loop starts at element, not element.parentElement), url() and raster images (the test is !== 'none'), layered 'none, linear-gradient(...)' lists, and the top of the chain.

The one real residual is ::before / ::after. getComputedStyle(node) with a single argument does not see pseudo-elements, so an overlay like '.operator-dashboard-card::before { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(...) }' would paint over the surface and the guard would not fire. That is a very common overlay idiom.

Latent today: the only pseudo-element gradient in the tree is .drop-indicator-line::after, on a leaf that is never an ancestor of measured text. contrast-aa shares the limitation exactly, so this is a boundary of the shared model rather than something the N1 fix introduced.

2. THE FAILURE MESSAGE IS UNDER-SPECIFIED. e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts:565 builds its locator from node.tagName.toLowerCase() only. The N1 proof output reads 'Found on article: linear-gradient(...)' and is legible purely because 'article' happens to be unique in that chain. A gradient on one of the several divs in 'span.dashboard-card-value < div < article < section < div#root < body' would print 'div: linear-gradient(...)' and leave the engineer bisecting by hand.

contrast-aa already carries a signature(el) helper emitting 'tag.class > tag.class' for exactly this. Appending className closes it in a few characters.

Two smaller wording points while in there: the message says 'in the ancestor chain' though the check also covers the measured element itself, and .slice(0, 48) truncates the gradient value mid-string (the closing paren is cut in the proof output).

Neither blocked the N1 merge. Both want fixing in both copies, which is the same constraint N3 describes.

title: useAuth resolves unknown auth state to permissive and unknown admin state to hidden; make it tri-state
description:
Supersedes and absorbs ee5f1. One component, one shape of defect (two states used for three situations), two opposite polarities. Cheaper to fix together than either alone. Not a security finding on its own: backend enforcement was verified holding live (401 on /api/settings, /api/channels, /api/streams, /api/journal on ecm-ecm-1).

FAIL-OPEN HALF (this finding). frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.tsx:250-258: useAuthRequired() does 'if (isLoading || !authStatus) return false'. When the auth-status fetch fails, authStatus stays null and the hook reports auth not required. frontend/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:50-64 has the same shape: 'catch { setSetupRequired(false) }' with the comment 'If we can't check, assume setup is not required'. Both feed ProtectedRoute.tsx:97, 'if (!authRequired) return <>{children}</>', so the full app shell renders.

Two concrete costs:
- httpClient.ts has no global '401 means redirect to login', so the operator gets an app full of errors with no login prompt.
- ProtectedRoute.tsx:97-102 rewrites /login to / via history.replaceState in that branch, so the operator cannot reach the login page even by typing the URL. That is a recoverability defect.

The requireAdmin prop skip in the same early return is NOT exploitable: the prop is declared and never passed by any caller.

FAIL-CLOSED HALF (ee5f1). App.tsx:2679 passes isAdmin={Boolean(user?.is_admin)} into TabNavigation, which defaults isAdmin=false and calls settingsSectionGroups(isAdmin) (TabNavigation.tsx:37,80). Unknown resolves to hidden, so an admin briefly sees nothing. Purely usability: backend admin enforcement is independent and broad (94 RequireAdminIfEnabled, 10 RequireHumanAdminIfEnabled, 15 get_current_active_admin/require_admin sites).

FIX: make the hook tri-state ('resolving' | 'required' | 'not-required') and render a retryable 'Cannot reach ECM' screen with an explicit Log in link for the unresolved state instead of children. Same for ProtectedRoute's catch: an unreachable setup check is unknown, not no. Lockout risk is nil, because in the trigger state the app cannot function anyway.

TEST GAP, and the reason this survived: there is no ProtectedRoute test file at all, and frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.test.tsx:21 sets getAuthStatus as a default mockRejectedValue, so the whole suite runs permanently in the fail-open state and never asserts on it.

Trigger is a degraded backend, not an attacker primitive: no global rate limit exists, /api/auth/status carries no per-route limit, uvicorn's --limit-concurrency 100 503s everything including index.html, and there is no service worker. The one selective path is request_timeout_middleware (backend/main.py:445-472) 504ing /api/* while static files bypass it.

ProtectedRoute renders a retryable 'Cannot reach ECM' screen with a working Log in link instead of children. The setup probe's catch yields 'unknown', not false.

title: AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS contents are not pinned by a test
description:
The global auth middleware (backend/main.py:531-559) is the entire authentication gate for /api/*, and its exempt set is unpinned.

The gate is proven by exactly one test: backend/tests/routers/test_client_errors.py:344-352, test_missing_jwt_returns_401_when_auth_enabled. Nothing asserts the CONTENTS of AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS. Adding a data route to that set is a one-line, silent, total-exposure change that ships with green CI.

backend/tests/integration/test_api_auth.py:568-581 even documents deliberately not asserting 401 on /api/settings because the fixture runs in setup mode, which is the same blind spot from the other direction.

The live consequence of an unpinned exempt set is not hypothetical: /api/backup/restore-initial sits in that set today and is a full database replacement endpoint (see the restore-initial bead).

Related hardening already verified good and not in scope: no path-normalization bypass exists (//api/settings, /./api/settings, /API/settings, /api/./settings, /api//settings, /api/settings%2f, and a traversal attempt were all checked and none reach data).

title: GET /api/settings returns discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id in cleartext
description:
Verified at source. An incomplete application of a correct pattern, not an absent one.

_ADMIN_ONLY_PROTECTED_FIELDS (backend/routers/settings.py:126-134) covers password, dispatcharr_api_key, emby_api_key, plex_token, jellyfin_api_key and smtp_password, all correctly surfaced on read as *_configured booleans only. But discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id sit in _ADMIN_ONLY_SETTINGS_FIELDS (settings.py:92-94), which is admin-gated on WRITE only, and are returned raw on read:

  backend/routers/settings.py:744  discord_webhook_url=settings.discord_webhook_url
  backend/routers/settings.py:747  telegram_bot_token=settings.telegram_bot_token
  backend/routers/settings.py:748  telegram_chat_id=settings.telegram_chat_id

The handler at settings.py:654-660 carries no dependency of any kind, and SettingsResponse (settings.py:506-510) types these as plain str with no field_serializer or model_serializer.

Two consequences:

1. Answers jy006's stated 'single most important thing to determine': yes, a populated Discord webhook URL and Telegram bot token ARE returned in cleartext to an unauthenticated caller whenever the endpoint is anonymous, i.e. during the setup_complete window. jy006 can move from 'not proven' to 'proven by code inspection'; the disposable-stack experiment it proposes is no longer needed for this question.

2. Independent of that window: any authenticated non-admin, and the static MCP service key, can read these. That contradicts the kgz3k/6n76m threat model, which goes to real lengths (_resolve_settings_admin, settings.py:137-167) to deny the MCP principal WRITE access to exactly these fields.

FIX: mirror the existing *_configured pattern, returning discord_configured / telegram_configured only, or redact to a sentinel for non-admin callers.

Code-verified, not verified live (would require credentials or the MCP key).
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #849, merged to dev as 97d59a3f, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0089 built from a successful run of that commit.

9ej7f: GET /api/settings now depends on _resolve_settings_admin, the same predicate that already gated WRITE on these fields, and returns an empty value for discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id to a non-admin or the MCP service principal. Empty redaction was chosen over a masked tail because SettingsTab round-trips these values and update_settings writes the webhook literally with no preserve-on-omit, so a placeholder would have overwritten a live webhook on a non-admin's next save.

i4qrp: the four settings test endpoints (/test, /test-smtp, /test-discord, /test-telegram) now carry RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest.

9kwzp.6: four more sinks gated (alert-methods/{id}/test, m3u/digest/test, cloud-targets/{id}/test, cloud-targets/test). POST /api/settings/restart-services gained the ordinary admin tier and deliberately still admits the MCP key, pinned by a test.

9kwzp.7: emby, plex and jellyfin test-connection moved off RequireAdminIfEnabled, which does NOT refuse the MCP key because _build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True. Full per-site audit recorded in backend/tests/test_admin_gate_inventory.py, which walks the live FastAPI dependency tree and asserts both the 14-route MCP-denied set and the 79-route admitted set exactly.

title: Edit Mode never stands down after a batch containing only staged group creations
description:
Found by the project-engineer during review of the enhancedchannelmanager-vtapf fix, not by the drill. Filed retroactively so the fix on branch fix/drill-run18-defects-r18fx has a bead behind it.

Staged groups travel to the backend in 'groupsToCreate', which is a PHASE of the bulk commit rather than an entry in the 'operations' array. A batch consisting only of staged group creations therefore comes back with operationsApplied: 0 even though the groups were created successfully. Edit Mode reads that zero as 'nothing was applied' and never stands down, so the operator is left in Edit Mode with a commit that actually succeeded.

Only reachable once 'Create new channel group' stages instead of committing immediately (vtapf), which is why the drill never saw it: on 0.18.1-0051 that control wrote straight through to Dispatcharr.

Fixed in commit de84272f on fix/drill-run18-defects-r18fx.

Found on a disposable drill stack context, not production. Dispatcharr pin 0.28.2, ECM 0.18.1-0051. Related: enhancedchannelmanager-vtapf.

description:

title: Restored multi-stream channel carrying the case-differing stream pair returns 188 bytes; a freshly-built multi-stream channel on the same instance plays - possible ixdaw regression
description:
Found unprimed in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-09-run18, ECM 0.18.1-0051 / Dispatcharr 0.28.2, DISPOSABLE drill stack (project ecmbkr), not production. Artifact variant: standard (redacted), after the documented Step 6a two-step recovery.

SYMPTOM: channel #30 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA' - the seeded multi-stream channel whose slots are
  1 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA'
  2 'TX | Austin | PBS KLRU'
  3 'TX | DALLAS | PBS KERA'   <- differs from slot 1 only in case, deliberately NON-adjacent
returns HTTP 200, Content-Type video/mp2t, TS sync byte valid, but only 188 BYTES, then the stream ends. Reproduced on 3 consecutive fetches with a 60s deadline each.

The DATA restored perfectly: archived slot order preserved exactly, all three slots carry a URL.

WHAT RULES OUT THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATIONS:
1. Not the provider. Fetching each of the three upstream provider URLs directly returns HTTP 200 and 131,072 bytes each.
2. Not the instance. Fetched in the same session: #1, #20, #21, #22 all return 262,144 bytes.
3. Not 'multi-stream channels in general'. A CONTROL channel #90 was built fresh on the same instance through the same UI (create from one stream, then drag a second onto it) with 2 slots - it returns 262,144 bytes, PASS.
4. Not a cold-fetch artifact. Three attempts, 60s deadlines, identical 188-byte result.

DISPATCHARR LOG at the moment of the fetch:
  live_proxy.manager Failed to find alternative streams after 2 attempts for channel: 3e7d1263-8278-4327-9092-39384a0841d8
  live_proxy.manager Updated channel ... state to ERROR in Redis after stream failure (owner=self)
Note '2 attempts' for a channel holding 3 slots.

HONEST LIMIT ON THE DIAGNOSIS: this run never fetched channel #30 on the SOURCE instance before the backup (the source playback check covered #1/#2/#3 only), so it is not proven that the restore caused this rather than the channel never having played. That is a gap in this run's method, not evidence either way.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the appendix's per-bead checklist requires, for the closed bead enhancedchannelmanager-ixdaw, that 'a channel carrying two streams whose names differ only in case comes back bound to real streams, in archived order, and PLAYS (2xx + real media bytes) - on both artifact variants'. Order and binding pass; playback does not. A regression of a closed bead is worse than a new defect, so this is filed rather than shrugged off.

NEXT RUN MUST DO: fetch the multi-stream channel on the SOURCE before taking the backup, so cause is attributable. Add it to the source playback set explicitly rather than relying on 'first N channels'.
close_reason:
RETRACTED — my own error, not an ECM defect. Closing per the drill's findings policy, which requires a bead that turns out to be the run's mistake to be closed by the run that filed it and marked retracted in place.

Channel #30 'TX | Dallas | PBS KERA' returned 188 bytes because it was the ONLY channel in the run-18 seed carrying a non-default stream profile — 'Run18 Custom Profile' — and that profile has command: '' and parameters: '' with locked: false. An unlocked Dispatcharr stream profile with an empty command is not runnable, so live_proxy fails every slot ('Failed to find alternative streams after 2 attempts'). The stock Proxy/Redirect profiles also have empty commands but are locked: true and special-cased.

Verified independently from run 18's own artifacts, not taken on trust:
- inventory/before.json (the SOURCE, captured BEFORE the backup) shows #30 on 'Run18 Custom Profile' while all 11 other channels are stream_profile: None.
- The archived categories/stream_profiles.yaml inside ecm-backup-2026-08-09_133553.zip records id: 6, name: Run18 Custom Profile, command: '', parameters: '', locked: false, user_agent: 4.

So the channel was unplayable ON THE SOURCE, before any backup was taken. The restore reproduced it faithfully; both post-restore inventories match the source exactly. The case-differing stream pair is exonerated and closed bead ixdaw is NOT regressed.

Why the run got it wrong: the control experiment (#90, freshly built, 2 slots, played fine) varied slot count but not stream profile, so the profile remained an uncontrolled confound. The run correctly reported at the time that cause was unattributable because it never fetched #30 on the source — that missing baseline is exactly what would have caught this.

ROOT CAUSE IS A DOCUMENTATION DEFECT, now fixed on branch fix/drill-run18-defects-r18fx: the drill article's own seed recipe curl for the custom stream profile omits command and parameters, so following the article manufactures an unplayable channel and then makes it the ixdaw playback subject. Without that fix every future run re-files this same false P1.

title: Edit Mode drops a channel created into a still-pending group: staging group id -1000 sent unremapped, 400, and the UI reports nothing
description:
Found unprimed in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-09-run18 on ECM 0.18.1-0051 / Dispatcharr 0.28.2, on a DISPOSABLE drill stack (project ecmbkr), not production.

STEPS (all in ECM's UI, Channel Manager > Edit Mode):
1. Select streams, Create in... > 'Create in new group...', name it 'Drill Locals'. Stage 8 channels.
2. Same session: stage 3 more into another NEW group 'Drill Movies'.
3. Same session: select one more stream, Create in... > pick 'Drill Locals' from the menu (it is still PENDING, not yet created in Dispatcharr).
4. Done > Exit Edit Mode > Apply All.

EXPECTED (docs/user_guide/.../run-a-restore-drill.md Step 2): everything staged reaches Dispatcharr on Apply All.

ACTUAL: the native alert says 'Staged 1 channels for creation!', the Channels pane shows 'Drill Locals 9 #1-30', and Apply All creates only 11 channels. The 12th is silently dropped. Edit Mode exits normally. Nothing is surfaced to the operator - no toast, no banner, no notification (Notifications panel held only two unrelated 'Task Completed: M3U Change Monitor' entries).

SERVER LOG (evidence file evidence-bulk-commit-silent-failure.log in the run dir):
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Job cdaf9cc7... enqueued (12 operations)
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Operation op-11-createChannel failed: Channel creation failed: 400 - {"channel_group_id":["Invalid pk \"-1000\" - object does not exist."]}
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Completed (batch=ff2e5f2a): success=False, applied=11, failed=1
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Operation op-11-addStreamToChannel failed (channel: Channel -12) (stream: TX | Dallas | PBS KERA): 404 .../api/channels/channels/-12/

ROOT CAUSE (from the log): the group's negative staging id (-1000) is passed to Dispatcharr unremapped, even though the same batch created that group and remapped it correctly for the other 11 channels.

TRIGGER ISOLATED: repeating the identical action against a group that ALREADY exists in Dispatcharr gives success=True, applied=1, failed=0. So the trigger is precisely 'the target group is itself still pending in the same batch', reached via Create in... > <pending group>. The 'Create in new group...' path is unaffected.

SECOND HALF: the backend's success flag is correct (success=False) - ayfn9(b) works - but the failure never reaches the operator. The Exit Edit Mode dialog also mis-summarised the batch: 'You have 24 pending changes: 12 streams added, 12 new channels created, 2 new groups created' (26 line items against a total of 24), while the expanded detail list correctly held 2 group ops + 11x2 channel ops = 24.

Self-inflicted-failure checks all cleared: every control read back from the DOM; waited through the full commit and re-read Dispatcharr; the container log states the backend refused and why.

title: Non-Edit-Mode Delete Group path still issues a bare delete and cannot fulfil its own dialog promise
description:
Split out of enhancedchannelmanager-ayfn9, which fixed the Edit-Mode path only. Found during backup/restore drill run 2026-08-08-run17 follow-up; flagged by the implementing engineer as out of that bead's brief.

CONTEXT
ayfn9 fixed the Edit Mode bulk-commit path (backend/routers/channels.py _run_bulk_commit): it now reparents a group's member channels to 'Default Group' before deleting, because Dispatcharr rejects both a delete of a non-empty group and a null channel_group_id:
    DELETE /api/channels/groups/<id>/                          -> 400 {'error':'Cannot delete group with associated channels'}
    PATCH  /api/channels/channels/<id>/ {'channel_group_id':null} -> 400 {'channel_group_id':['This field may not be null.']}

THE REMAINING PATH
The non-Edit-Mode delete (frontend App.tsx -> DELETE /api/channel-groups/{id} -> backend/routers/channel_groups.py delete_channel_group) still issues a bare delete with no reparent. It reaches the same user-facing dialog copy, which promises the channels will be moved.

DIFFERENCE FROM ayfn9
This path is NOT silent: upstream_http_exception surfaces Dispatcharr's 400 to the operator, so the failure is visible. But it still cannot do what the dialog says it will, so deleting a non-empty group from this path always fails for the operator with no in-product way to succeed except emptying the group by hand first.

SUGGESTED FIX
Reuse the helpers ayfn9 added rather than duplicating them: _resolve_ungrouped_target_group() and _reparent_group_channels() in backend/routers/channels.py, plus the shared frontend copy resolver in frontend/src/utils/ungroupedTargetGroup.ts. Apply the same guards (no destination group present; the group being deleted IS the destination; an empty group needs no destination).

PRIORITY
Lower than ayfn9 was, because the failure is visible rather than silent. Worth closing so the two delete paths cannot drift.

Found on a disposable drill stack, not production.

Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits 478260c4, 47dafeb1.

Deliberately called a CHECK, not a fix, in its docstring, log line and test names - Dispatcharr 0.28.x offers no conditional update, MEASURED from GET /api/schema/?format=json (HTTP 200, ~717KB): zero occurrences of If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, ETag or 412, and no version field on Channel/PatchedChannel. title: Delete Group silently fails for a group that has channels; UI promises to move them to Ungrouped and never does
description:
FIXED and VERIFIED LIVE (build 0.18.1-0051, branch fix/drill-run17-defects-qka89, NOT yet merged).

TWO defects in one repro, both fixed.

(a) CORRECTNESS. ECM never reparented the group's channels before deleting, so Dispatcharr rejected the delete with 400 {'error':'Cannot delete group with associated channels'}.
IMPORTANT: the FIRST fix attempt reparented to channel_group_id: null and STILL failed live. Dispatcharr rejects that too:
    PATCH /api/channels/channels/1/ {'channel_group_id': null} -> 400 {'channel_group_id':['This field may not be null.']}
    PATCH /api/channels/channels/1/ {'channel_group_id': 378}  -> 200
A Dispatcharr channel cannot be group-less. 'Ungrouped' (ChannelsPane.tsx models it as channel_group_id === null) is a state ECM can READ but never WRITE.
Final fix in backend/routers/channels.py: resolve the destination BY NAME (UNGROUPED_TARGET_GROUP_NAME = 'Default Group'), never by assuming id 1; reparent members to it; then delete. Refuses with an actionable message when no such group exists, and when the group being deleted IS the destination. An empty group still deletes with no destination needed.

(b) VISIBILITY. The Edit-Mode bulk commit reported overall success while an individual operation had raised. success is now operationsFailed == 0 unconditionally, so one successful op can no longer launder a failure beside it.

LIVE VERIFICATION (patched container bkr-ecm, real UI, 6-channel group, 'Also delete' UNCHECKED):
  dialog now reads: 'This group contains 6 channels. The channels will be moved to "Default Group".'
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Moving 6 channel(s) from group 377 to 'Default Group' (id=1) before deleting it
  DELETE .../api/channels/groups/377/ -> 204 No Content
  [CHANNELS-BULK] Completed: success=True, applied=1, failed=0
  after: Default Group members=[201,202,203,204,205,206]; group 377 gone; 11 channels total, nothing lost
(b) was independently proven on the FAILING attempt, which correctly reported success=False, applied=0, failed=1 instead of laundering it.

Tests: 8 in backend/tests/routers/test_channels.py (5 red before the fix). The test double now raises on a null channel_group_id carrying the verbatim live 400 body, and fixtures place the baseline group at id 42/907 so a test cannot pass by accident on id 1. That double is exactly why the first cut shipped green and 400'd on the first real click.

NOT FIXED, candidate follow-up: the non-Edit-Mode path (App.tsx -> DELETE /api/channel-groups/{id}, routers/channel_groups.py) still issues a bare delete. It is not silent there (upstream_http_exception surfaces the 400), but it still cannot fulfil the same dialog's promise.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.18.1-0051, merged as 903ad1d3 (PR #805), published image verified. Both halves closed. (a) Delete Group now resolves 'Default Group' BY NAME, reparents members, then deletes: verified live with 6 channels reparented, DELETE -> 204, success=True applied=1 failed=0, nothing lost, and the dialog now names the real destination. (b) the Edit-Mode bulk commit no longer launders a failed operation into overall success, proven on the failing first attempt which correctly reported success=False applied=0 failed=1. NOTE: the first fix attempt reparented to a null group and still failed live because Dispatcharr rejects that; the test double has been tightened to raise on a null channel_group_id with the verbatim live 400 body. The non-Edit-Mode delete path remains open as enhancedchannelmanager-auocn.

title: EPG picker shows 'No EPG data found' until full app reload after adding an EPG source
description:
FIXED and VERIFIED LIVE (build 0.18.1-0051, branch fix/drill-run17-defects-qka89, NOT yet merged).

Fix uses the existing useServerDataInvalidation bus (no polling, no refetch-on-focus, so bead 5z7c9's closing condition still holds). Two new keys, 'epg-data' and 'channel-groups', subscribed in App.tsx to loadEpgData / loadChannelGroups.
- EPGManagerTab detects guide-download completion on the ROWS (noteGuideDownloadProgress), fed from all three fetch paths (loadSources, the per-source poller, the Refresh-All poller), so no poller can win the race and skip it.
- Anchored on updated_at, not status alone, so a STALE 'success' reading cannot satisfy the watch. An error result ends the watch without publishing.
- A source already downloading when the tab mounts is adopted rather than missed.
- DbasRestoreModal and DbasRestoreSavedModal publish 'channel-groups' on a terminal report when is_dry_run === false.
- EditChannelModal gains a distinct 'Guide data has not loaded yet' empty state on both pickers, so an unloaded cache no longer renders as 'No EPG data found'.
