1. ADD an EPG source (the filed repro): GET /api/epg/data fired 2x, while the source was still status='parsing'. PASS
2. channel-group list after an APPLIED restore: each mode=apply immediately followed by 2x GET /api/channel-groups, none before; dry runs correctly publish nothing. PASS
3. per-source refresh of an already-'success' source: FAILED on the first cut (0 refetches over 6.5 min while the refresh completed in 65s). Root causes were (i) detection lived in loadSources, which the per-source refresh never calls, and (ii) the poller stopped on the pre-click stale 'success'. After rework: 2 refetches, no reload. PASS

Implemented on the existing useServerDataInvalidation bus with no polling and no refetch-on-focus, so bead 5z7c9's closing condition still holds.

title: Restore task progress.status reports 'failed' and the scheduler logs 'Task failed' for a completed_with_failures restore that rolled nothing back
description:
Found unprimed in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-08-run16 on published :dev 0.18.1-0047.
Reproduced twice: the redacted-artifact round and the deliberate logo-failure round.

SYMPTOM
A restore that ends outcome=completed_with_failures, with failed:0 in every category and nothing
rolled back, is described five different ways:

GET /api/tasks/dbas_restore -> progress.status   = 'failed'
task-history status / success                    = 'completed_with_warnings' / True
details.outcome                                  = 'completed_with_failures'
notification type                                = 'warning'
restore dialog                                   = 'nothing was rolled back'

Container log shows two components disagreeing about the same event:
WARNING task_scheduler  [dbas_restore] Task failed: Restore completed_with_failures: created 32,
failed 1 across 13 categories; 1 logo(s) could not be reinstated; ...
WARNING task_engine     [dbas_restore] Task completed in a degraded state: ...

Contrast: a clean restore (outcome=success) correctly reports progress.status='completed'.
So the mapping is completed_with_failures -> progress.status='failed'.

WHY IT MATTERS
progress.status is the field carrying the stage/percentage the UI renders, and is the natural
thing to poll when waiting for a restore to finish. A script or operator polling it sees a
terminal 'failed' for a restore that succeeded with recoverable warnings. Separately, anyone
grepping the log for 'Task failed' - which docs/user_guide/troubleshooting/read-the-logs.md
encourages - gets a false positive on every degraded restore.

RELATIONSHIP TO enhancedchannelmanager-fexq1
fexq1's own criterion PASSES and must stay passing: the task-history row correctly stores
completed_with_warnings / success:true, and a clean run stores completed. This is a DIFFERENT
pair of surfaces (the live progress object, and the task_scheduler log line) that fexq1 did not
cover. Do not reopen fexq1; fix these two surfaces to agree with it.

EXPECTED
completed_with_failures should map to a non-failed terminal progress status that agrees with the
history row and the warning-level alert. 'failed' should be reserved for outcomes that actually
failed or rolled back (partial_failed_rolled_back, failed_rollback_incomplete) and for
orchestration errors - the same rule the alert severity already follows per cwmid.

SCOPE
backend/task_scheduler.py (task_outcome / execution_status), and the task_scheduler log line.

Found on a disposable drill stack (project ecmbkr), NOT on production.
Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-08-run16/REPORT.md finding F1.

---
IMPLEMENTATION (PR #802, build 0.18.1-0048)
Root cause: the live TaskProgress terminal status ("completed" if result.success else "failed")
and the finalized progress notification status were each written by hand from result.success
alone, which means "cleanly, with nothing to report" - not "did this run produce what it was
asked for". Both now call execution_status(), the same single projection of task_outcome() the
persisted history row uses, so the three surfaces cannot disagree. TaskScheduler.run() logs
"Task completed with warnings" for a TaskOutcome.WARNING run instead of "Task failed".
'failed' stays reserved for TaskOutcome.ERROR (rolled back / orchestration error / exception);
a cancelled run now reports 'cancelled' rather than 'failed'. on_complete() stays gated on
result.success. Frontend useRestoreProgress + notificationGrouping learn the terminal status,
so a degraded restore finalizes its dialog instead of polling to the 30-minute cap.
Tests: backend/tests/integration/test_degraded_run_progress_agrees_with_history.py pins both
directions. fexq1 / cwmid / daziw tests untouched and passing.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged in PR #802 (v0.18.1-0048, merge 2598a3ab). Root cause: TaskScheduler.run() and _finalize_progress_notification wrote the terminal progress status by hand as 'completed' if result.success else 'failed'; TaskResult.success means 'cleanly, nothing to report', so a degraded-but-successful run (completed_degraded=True / TaskOutcome.WARNING) and a cancelled run were both spelled 'failed'. The persisted history row already used the single task_outcome -> execution_status derivation from fexq1; these two surfaces had never been moved onto it.

Fix: progress.status and the finalized notification status both now call execution_status(result), so the three surfaces cannot disagree by construction. WARNING runs get their own branch: TaskStatus.COMPLETED plus 'Task completed with warnings'. 'failed' is reserved for TaskOutcome.ERROR (rolled back / orchestration error / exception); cancelled now reports 'cancelled'.

Also required (would otherwise have regressed the UI): frontend useRestoreProgress TERMINAL_STATUSES and notificationGrouping FINAL_PROGRESS_STATUSES were closed sets missing completed_with_warnings, so a finished degraded restore would have polled to the 30-minute cap and its notification never collapsed.

Independently verified by the orchestrator, not taken from the agent report: merge present on origin/dev; targeted backend suite (new integration file + task_scheduler/execution_status/task_outcome/degraded selectors) all passing; frontend typecheck clean; useRestoreProgress + notificationGrouping tests 34/34; code read to confirm BOTH directions hold - TaskStatus.FAILED and 'Task failed' are still emitted for genuine failures and exceptions.

Invariants preserved: fexq1 (history row), cwmid (alert severity), daziw (no-playable-stream).

title: Empty channel group has no Group actions menu, so it cannot be renamed or deleted from ECM
description:
Found unprimed in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-08-run16 on published :dev 0.18.1-0047.

SYMPTOM
In Channel Manager > Edit Mode, a channel group with zero members renders its header row WITHOUT the more_vert 'Group actions' control. That menu is the only place ECM offers 'Rename Group' and 'Delete Group'. A populated group has it; the same group loses it the moment its last channel leaves.

Measured by reading control state out of the DOM (not appearance), three groups in one list:
  Drill Locals RENAMED  hasGroupActionsMenu=true   (7 channels)
  Drill Empty           hasGroupActionsMenu=false  (0 channels)
  Drill Specials        hasGroupActionsMenu=false  (0 channels)

WHY IT MATTERS
1. ECM's own 'Create new channel group' button creates empty groups. An empty group created by
   mistake, or left behind after moving its channels out, cannot be removed from the screen that
   created it - the operator must leave for Dispatcharr's UI.
2. It breaks a documented procedure. docs/user_guide/backup-restore/run-a-restore-drill.md Step 8
   > Construction instructs: 'Delete a different archived channel group outright. Move its
   channels out of the group first. Dispatcharr refuses to delete a group that still has
   channels.' Following that instruction in ECM produces exactly the state in which ECM's delete
   control disappears. Hit live during the drill; the documented step could not be completed in
   ECM's UI and required falling back to Dispatcharr.

EXPECTED
An empty channel group should still expose Group actions (at minimum Rename Group and Delete
Group). Deleting an empty group is the safest possible case - there are no members to strand.

SCOPE
Frontend (Channel Manager group header row rendering). Also update the restore-drill article's
Step 8 once the UI supports it, or note the Dispatcharr fallback if it does not.

Found on a disposable drill stack (project ecmbkr, containers bkr-ecm/bkr-dispatcharr), NOT on
production. Dispatcharr pin 0.28.2. Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-08-run16/REPORT.md finding F2.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged in PR #803 (v0.18.1-0049, merge 1d9a6c9e). Root cause traced with git log -L: the guard was inherited, not deliberate. 38dc4ca7 (v0.7.20028) put 'isEditMode && !isEmpty' on a standalone sort-streams-by-quality button, where needing members was correct. e5743ea2 (v0.14.0-0021) replaced that button with the more_vert menu and carried !isEmpty onto the WHOLE menu. Rename Group and Delete Group were added inside it later and silently inherited a condition that was never about them.

Fix: split the guard per item rather than removing it. Probe Group / Sort Streams / Sort & Renumber keep !isEmpty (meaningless with no channels). Rename Group has no member gate. Delete Group stays gated on isManualGroup (= !isProviderGroup && !isAutoSyncRelated), which it always was - never on member count. The menu button renders when at least one item would render, so empty Uncategorized still shows nothing. Dividers render only between items.

Provider safety unchanged and verified by orchestrator code read: an M3U-backed group is not deletable from ECM empty or not, because the next refresh recreates it. At the drill's 378 groups / 375 provider-backed, the only change for those 375 is that an empty one now offers Rename.

Independently verified by the orchestrator, not taken from the agent report: merge present on origin/dev; npm run lint clean at --max-warnings 0; npm run typecheck clean; new ChannelsPane.groupActions.test.tsx 7/7 passing; canDelete/canRename/canProbe gating read directly out of the merged source.

Residual gap, stated honestly: verification is rendered-DOM via Testing Library (the same layer the drill measured hasGroupActionsMenu at), not a live browser against a running instance. The drill stack was torn down. Worth confirming in the next restore drill, where seeding an empty channel group is already a construction requirement.

title: Credential-bearing DBAS artifacts get staged into the repo working tree, and .playwright-mcp/ is not gitignored
description:
Found on the disposable drill stack (project ecmbkr, bkr-ecm/bkr-dispatcharr) during backup/restore round-trip drill run 2026-08-08-run14 on ECM 0.18.1-0047 / Dispatcharr 0.28.2. NOT production.

SYMPTOM
.playwright-mcp/enc-artifact.zip (dated 2026-08-05, left by an earlier drill run) is an ENCRYPTED DBAS artifact; its sibling std-artifact.zip is a readable standard artifact. The directory .playwright-mcp/ is NOT gitignored: 'git check-ignore -v .playwright-mcp/enc-artifact.zip' returns nothing and 'git status --porcelain' shows '?? .playwright-mcp/'. A 'git add -A' in this PUBLIC repository would stage a credential-bearing backup artifact.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING (structural, not carelessness)
Playwright's file-upload sandbox only permits paths under the repo root ('File access denied: ... is outside allowed roots'). Any drill round that uploads a backup artifact through ECM's Restore-from-artifact UI is FORCED to copy that artifact into the repo directory first. Run 14 hit the identical constraint and had to stage both artifacts there.

An encrypted artifact created with 'Include credentials' carries the live XC provider credential.

EXISTING GUARD DOES NOT COVER THIS
_tooling/obfuscate.js guards SCREENSHOTS against PII. It does not guard artifacts staged for upload. There is no CI check either.

REPRODUCED: yes - run 14 was forced into the same staging step.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add '.playwright-mcp/' to .gitignore.
2. Add an explicit teardown step to docs/user_guide/backup-restore/run-a-restore-drill.md: delete any artifact staged inside the repo for browser upload.
3. Consider a CI check for *.zip under .playwright-mcp/ or anywhere outside the artifact allowlist.

NOTE: run 14 deleted only its OWN staged files. The 2026-08-05 files were left in place - they are a previous run's evidence and removing them is the PO's call.

Second, std-artifact.zip is NOT credential-bearing: it was inspected read-only and is genuinely redacted:true, with all six secret keys holding an identical sentinel. The credential risk is confined to enc-artifact.zip, a passphrase-encrypted ECMBKENC envelope. Remaining scope: the CI zip/binary guard (proposed fix 3), and a PO decision on deleting the 3.1 GB still on disk.

All three items complete. Shipped across PR #852 and PR #853; final piece merged as 5bc4470a and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0093 built from a successful run of that commit.

ITEM 1, containment (PR #852, build 0092). .gitignore covers .playwright-mcp/ plus root-anchored scratch globs with negations for every tracked root file; .beads/.gitignore covers five beads-local runtime artifacts; root .coverage ignored. Verified 'git ls-files -z | git check-ignore -z --stdin' returns empty, so nothing tracked became ignored. Deliberately NOT a widened h9av3 glob: 'snapshot' is a live word in this repo and *snap*.yml would eventually swallow a real config.

ITEM 2, deletion. The 3.1 GB is gone. Inventory before removal was 1,912 .yml a11y snapshots, 372 .log, 35 .png and 2 .zip spanning 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-10, no unexpected file types, nothing tracked by git. The two drill artifacts were preserved at ~/ecm-drill-artifacts-2026-08-05/ (verified byte-identical with cmp before the delete) rather than destroyed, because /config/backups/ on the live instance is EMPTY and they were the only backup artifacts on the box. They sit outside the repo so they cannot be committed; PO may delete at will.

ITEM 3, the CI guard (PR #853, build 0093). scripts/check_binary_artifacts.py blocks credential-bearing and bulk binary artifacts on a PR. Scope is files the change ADDS, from the merge-base diff UNION git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; that second source is the point, since the incident was untracked and a diff-only guard would have seen nothing until the artifact was already staged. Three rules: leading-byte signature over ten formats (size- and extension-independent, so a ZIP renamed .png is still blocked, with ECMBKENC and the DBAS manifest.json shape named specifically), unrecognized-binary by NUL in the first 8 KiB, and size ceilings of 2 MiB per file / 25 MiB aggregate. Escape hatch is .binary-artifacts.allowlist, exact paths only, mandatory reason, globs rejected, shipped empty.

The allowlist is a list of TYPES, not PATHS, and that was the load-bearing decision: a census of all 1,861 tracked files found 151 PNGs and nothing else binary, and new screenshots land in new docs/images/user_guide/<section>/ directories constantly, so a path allowlist would red-line the next user-guide PR. A guard that costs people PRs gets disabled. TestTrackedTreeIsClean pins the whole tree against live git ls-files instead. There are now FOUR security ratchets that cannot block a merge: em-dash, PII, detect-secrets, and binary artifacts. This is not hypothetical: Operator Docs caught real defects on both PR #849 (synthetic credentials tripping the scanner) and PR #850 (a cross-file dead anchor), and both could have been merged past. title: Docs-only stub jobs emit permanent-green duplicates of required contexts on mixed PRs
description:
Concrete mechanism behind the long-known enhancedchannelmanager-6u2pa ('CI emits same-named status checks from more than one workflow; gh pr checks --required can report green over a real failure').

.github/workflows/test.yml triggers on paths-ignore: ['**.md', '.beads/**'] — i.e. it runs when a PR touches anything else.
.github/workflows/docs-only-pass.yml triggers on paths: ['**.md', '.beads/**'] — i.e. it runs when a PR touches any of those.

These are NOT mutually exclusive. A MIXED PR (code AND markdown, which is most PRs in this repo, since the shipping flow requires a CHANGELOG.md entry on every change) matches BOTH workflows.

docs-only-pass.yml emits jobs named exactly 'Backend Tests', 'Frontend Tests', 'Semgrep Lint', 'Version Consistency', 'MCP Server Tests' — the required contexts — whose only step is an echo. They always pass. So on a mixed PR each required context exists twice: once real, once permanently green.

OBSERVED LIVE on PR #797 (2026-08-08): 'Backend Tests' reported BOTH failure (the real job in test.yml, 2 failed / 8604 passed) and success (the stub in docs-only-pass.yml) on the same commit. The failure was a genuine test defect, not a flake. It was caught only because the orchestrator reads every instance of every required context individually rather than trusting the summary; the aggregate view showed a green 'Backend Tests'.

The stub exists for a legitimate reason: a genuinely docs-only PR skips test.yml via paths-ignore, so branch protection would otherwise block forever. The defect is that the exclusion is one-directional.

WANTED: make the two mutually exclusive. paths filters cannot express 'ONLY these paths changed', so options include a single workflow with a change-detection job gating the real vs stub jobs, or having the stub jobs inspect the changed file set and refuse to report green when non-doc files are present. Either way, a required context must never be satisfiable by a job that did not run the thing it is named for.
notes:
Implemented on branch fix/single-source-required-checks-5rwzy, PR #800 (v0.18.1-0047). NOT merged; PO drives the merge.

DESIGN: one emitter per required context, always present. test.yml and build.yml lose their path filters and run on every PR. A detect job in each classifies the changed file set via the new scripts/classify_changed_paths.py (single definition of the docs-only rule). Every job carrying a required name always runs and gates its expensive STEPS on that classification. docs-only-pass.yml deleted. build.yml: codeql-analysis step-gated (its matrix carries 2 required contexts); wait-for-tests skips on docs-only, and every image-build job already requires its success, so they skip and nothing publishes.

PROOF on head f7551b01: each of the 7 required contexts appears exactly ONCE on the commit, all success. Backend Tests job 93059617069 step 8 'Run pytest' ran 9m08s, 8653 passed / 3 skipped, coverage 77.02%; the docs-only no-op step reported 'skipped'.

NOT PROVEN LIVE: the genuinely-docs-only case. It cannot be exercised pre-merge, because a pull_request run takes its workflow files from the merge commit, so a docs-only PR against dev would still run the OLD workflows until this lands. Covered by unit tests (classifier verdict) and by the static invariant test that no required-context job can be skipped.

Fixed and merged via PR #800 (119f8f0e), build 0.18.1-0047.

ROOT CAUSE: test.yml used paths-ignore ['**.md','.beads/**'] and docs-only-pass.yml used paths ['**.md','.beads/**']. Not mutually exclusive, so any MIXED PR matched both. docs-only-pass.yml emitted echo-only jobs named exactly the 7 required contexts, so on most PRs in this repo (nearly all are mixed, since the shipping flow requires a CHANGELOG.md entry) every required context existed twice: once real, once permanently green. Observed live on PR #797: Backend Tests reported failure AND success on the same commit, and the failure was a genuine test defect.

FIX: one source of truth per context. Path filters removed from test.yml and build.yml so both run on every PR. A detect job classifies the changed file set. Every job carrying a required name ALWAYS runs, so the context exists exactly once, and gates its expensive STEPS rather than the job. docs-only-pass.yml deleted.

Note a trap that shaped the design: GitHub treats a SKIPPED job as satisfying a required check, so gating at job level would have reproduced the same hole. The distinction is demonstrated in the PR's own run: Backend Security Scan is a job-level skip and reports conclusion=skipped, while Backend Tests had a skipped STEP and reported conclusion=success.

Engineer decisions beyond the brief, all kept: the classifier is a tested script (scripts/classify_changed_paths.py, 36 unit tests) rather than inline bash duplicated across three paths blocks; the changed-file set comes from the GitHub API rather than git diff, sidestepping the depth-1 checkout trap from t8fqg; and the gate is written != 'true' so it FAILS OPEN, meaning a broken detector runs the real work rather than skipping it.

Also removed, unspotted by me: docs-only-pass.yml carried a REAL duplicated Operator Docs job under a 'keep byte-identical' comment. That job now exists once.

VERIFIED on the fix PR itself, which is a mixed PR and therefore exercises the exact bug: each of the 7 required contexts appears exactly ONCE, all success, nothing non-success anywhere, and the job emitting Backend Tests demonstrably ran pytest (8653 passed).

NOT PROVEN, stated honestly rather than asserted: the genuinely-docs-only case. A pull_request run takes its workflows from the merge commit, so no pre-merge construction can exercise the new config on a docs-only diff. Covered instead by unit tests on the classifier and a static test asserting no required-context job carries a job-level if that can evaluate false, proven red without the fix.

Also corrected: docs/shipping.md said 5 required checks and listed 5; dev actually requires 7.

title: Add an em-dash lint ratchet over docs and code comments
description:
docs/style_guide.md is canonical per CLAUDE.md and bans em-dashes in prose, explicitly covering documentation prose AND code comments. There is no automated enforcement.

Evidence it is needed: two separate agent documentation passes introduced 144 violations across two merged PRs (47 docs, 97 code comments/docstrings), and three reviewers (two technical-writer agents and the orchestrator) shipped them without noticing. Measured density in the affected article went from 0.2 per 1,000 words to 12.9, roughly 60x. It surfaced only because the PO asked directly, and cost a third PR to fix the docs half.

This is not project-specific drift that better briefing fixes. The same tic appears at the same density in the agent's session retros, in a different repo with no such rule. It is a default property of the model's prose in every register. Only mechanical enforcement holds the line.

MUST BE A RATCHET, NOT A CLIFF. The PO chose 'add the guard, defer the remaining cleanup', so the check has to tolerate the ~97 known code-comment violations and 3 known instances in neighbouring backup-restore docs while failing on anything NEW. Standard options: check only changed lines against the merge base, or carry a baseline/allowlist that is only ever allowed to shrink. Do not red-line CI on existing debt.

Honour the rule's own exemptions: code blocks, quoted log lines, quoted UI strings, filenames, URLs, commands. En-dashes and arrows are not em-dashes.
close_reason:
Merged via PR #797 (edf9c794), build 0.18.1-0044, confirmed published.

scripts/check_em_dashes.py enforces docs/style_guide.md's no-em-dashes-in-prose rule. SCOPED TO DOCUMENTATION per PO direction ('I'm only worried about em-dashes for documentation'): Markdown under docs/ plus top-level README.md, CHANGELOG.md and CLAUDE.md. Python and TypeScript scanning was built and then removed; the scanners are deleted, not disabled. That cut the scan surface from 915 files and 12034 violations to 188 Markdown files and 1271 violations, and the script from 629 to 478 lines. It also removed the riskiest machinery, a tokenize/ast pass for Python and a hand-rolled TS string/template-literal scanner, both of which existed only to avoid false positives on log lines and UI copy.

A RATCHET, NOT A CLIFF. Fails only on lines a PR adds, so the 1271 pre-existing violations do not red-line CI. Untracked files count as fully added. Only U+2014 is flagged; en-dashes and arrows never are. Markdown exemptions: fenced blocks, inline code spans, link destinations, URLs. em-dash-ok: <reason> suppresses a genuine false positive.

CI home: the Operator Docs job in BOTH .github/workflows/test.yml and .github/workflows/docs-only-pass.yml. The second is load-bearing, because a Markdown-only PR skips test.yml via paths-ignore and a Markdown-only PR is exactly how the original 144 violations arrived. No new required-check context.

docs/style_guide.md states plainly that enforcement covers documentation only and that the code-comment clause remains a review-enforced convention. The underlying prose rule is unchanged.

PROVEN IN PRODUCTION: PR #798, the very next PR, was documentation prose written by an agent and passed the ratchet cleanly (46 added lines across 2 files, zero new em-dashes).

Deferred, recorded rather than lost: ~9200 Python and ~1550 TS/TSX violations are now out of enforcement scope entirely by PO decision.

title: Add a post-merge publish check to the shipping flow
description:
Fourth recurrence of the published :dev tag silently lagging dev. On 2026-08-07, PR #793 (the three restore fixes, 0.18.1-0041) merged and its dev 'Build and Push Docker Image' run FAILED. Root cause read from the log, not inferred: the dev Tests workflow failed on a single order-dependent frontend flake (StickySectionNav.test.tsx 're-arms when the URL names a different section', bead ue130; 1 failed / 189 passed), and the publish gate CORRECTLY refused to publish from a failed suite.

The gate behaved right. The defect is that nothing surfaced it. dev carried the fixes and the published image did not, for about five hours, until PR #794's merge republished and self-healed it. Nobody noticed until it was looked for directly.

Prior recurrences (per the drill's own history): a Buildx flake that skipped the multi-arch manifest, a GitHub Actions outage that orphaned queued runs, and a frontend test flake that correctly gated the publish. Every time the repo looked healthy and nothing surfaced the drift.

WANTED: make 'confirm the image actually published' an explicit, documented step after every merge in docs/shipping.md, ideally backed by a small script that (a) confirms the Build and Push Docker Image workflow succeeded for the merge commit, and (b) reads the published tag's build marker and compares it to the expected version. The drill already mandates an image gate BEFORE every run for exactly this reason; the same check belongs AFTER every merge.

IMPLEMENTED (build 0044, branch chore/ship-time-guardrails-t8fqg-3tflw): scripts/check_publish.py + backend/tests/unit/test_check_publish.py; docs/shipping.md section 6 now ends at a verified image; docs/user_guide/backup-restore/run-a-restore-drill.md gains Step 0 (the image gate the bead assumed already existed but did not). Deliberately NOT a CI gate. Verified against the real incident: --commit 5e75476a reports run #2928 conclusion=failure and marker 0.18.1-0041 expected vs published.
close_reason:
Merged via PR #797 (edf9c794), build 0.18.1-0044, and CONFIRMED PUBLISHED by the check itself: 'PASS: ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0044, built from a successful run of edf9c7945da3.'

scripts/check_publish.py verifies two things for a commit: the 'Build and Push Docker Image' push run concluded success (PR runs sharing a head SHA are filtered out), and the published tag's build marker equals frontend/package.json AT THAT COMMIT (git show <sha>:..., never the working tree). Marker read from the registry config blob via imagetools inspect, so no layer download; --pull gives the heavier rmi/pull/inspect form. Documented as a post-merge step in docs/shipping.md. Deliberately NOT wired into CI: a post-merge check cannot gate its own merge.

Retro-detects the original incident correctly: against 5e75476a (PR #793's merge) it reports both the failed build run and the marker mismatch.

ALSO SHIPPED, unplanned but load-bearing: the drill article had no image gate at all. That sequence existed only in the operator's private drill prompt, so anyone following the published docs never checked which build they were measuring. Added 'Step 0: Confirm the image you are about to measure', cross-referenced from docs/shipping.md. It reads ECM_VERSION and GIT_COMMIT from the image env rather than grepping source files.

One defect found and fixed pre-merge: two of the new tests reached for the origin/dev remote-tracking ref, which exists in a developer clone but not in a depth-1 single-branch CI checkout. They were replaced with a synthetic git repo built in a tmp_path fixture, and hermeticity was proven by reproducing the CI shape (git clone --depth 1 --single-branch) and showing the old tests failing there and the new ones passing. Coverage went from 2 git-backed tests to 14.

title: Remove em-dashes from the backup/restore operator docs (style guide violation)
description:

title: Add a populated-target round (Step 8) to the restore-drill procedure
description:
The restore-drill article's executable procedure is Steps 1-7, all against a freshly-wiped target. The 'Restoring onto a populated target' section is reference material describing behaviour — it never tells a drill-runner to construct a populated target and test it. So a drill following the article does not exercise that path at all.

That gap matters now: enhancedchannelmanager-r1ei7, -3t74w and -tddmw were fixed in 0.18.1-0041, and the article itself records that the r1ei7 fix is 'not yet proven by a live drill run against a populated target' (run 12 measured the PRE-fix state).

Adds Step 8: construct the divergence (rename an archived group; delete another, moving its channels out first since Dispatcharr refuses to delete a non-empty group; create a name collision with different id and members; diverge one channel's logo and clear one channel's EPG link so the relink modes are distinguishable; record the exact before-state), restore twice from an identical baseline (preserve, then overwrite), and assert by measurement: drift reported non-zero and nothing moved under preserve; reported AND moved under overwrite; drift count visible on the dry-run preview; already_exists_name_match rather than already_exists_identical for channel groups while profiles keep already_exists_identical; the channel_groups preview caveat and the 'not predicted' Streams row; playback fetched; and the 'grouping not checked' note when channel_groups is deselected.

Also updates 'What a passing drill looks like' and 'What this drill does not cover'. Deliberately leaves the 'not yet proven by a live drill' claims in place — they stay true until Step 8 actually runs.

Docs-only. Found while closing out backup/restore drill run 12.

title: Dry-run preview diverges from apply on channel_groups counts and omits the Streams category entirely
description:

Pins: ECM 0.18.1-0040 (sha256:3833904000860622a989975850e563c7f862fc38d77939847609f8eaaf8b0b21), Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Both artifact variants.

DOC CLAIM UNDER TEST — docs/user_guide/backup-restore/run-a-restore-drill, Step 6, warning 'What a preview does and does not predict': 'As of 0.18.1-0032, the per-category counts, the logo and EPG-link reattach splits, and profile_membership_drift all match what the apply then does.'

(a) channel_groups counts do NOT match
    preview: Channel groups  378 WILL CREATE / 0 WILL SKIP
    apply  : Channel groups    3 CREATED     / 375 SKIPPED
    Every other category matched exactly. End state is correct (378 groups), so this is a
    reporting divergence, not data loss. Mechanism is visible in the ordering: the restore
    creates the M3U account first, whose ingest materialises the 375 provider groups, so by
    the time the channel_groups category runs they already exist. A preview refreshes
    nothing, so it predicts 378 creates against the state it can see.

(b) the Streams category is ABSENT from the preview
    apply reports 'Streams 9 CREATED'. The preview has no Streams row at all — not shown
    as 0, simply missing. This is the category that synthesizes placeholder streams when
    the matcher misses, i.e. exactly what an operator would want forewarning of. The docs
    say only that the two stream-health COUNTERS read null on a dry run; they do not say
    the whole category disappears.

REPRODUCED: yes, identically on the encrypted and the redacted artifact.

Severity: MINOR each. An operator sanity-checking preview counts against apply counts sees a 375-row discrepancy and would reasonably think something went wrong. Adjacent to enhancedchannelmanager-dgnms (closed) but not a regression of it — dgnms's specific claims (logo split, profile_membership_drift, stream-health counters null not 0) all held.

Separately the Streams category, previously absent from the preview entirely (not 0 — missing), now renders flagged 'not predicted', reusing the dgnms null-counter precedent. title: Channel-to-group membership is never restored on a populated target, in either relink mode, and is not reported
description:
Found UNPRIMED in backup/restore drill run 12 (2026-08-07), DOC-FOLLOWING mode, on a disposable drill stack (project ecmbkr) — NOT production.

Pins: ECM 0.18.1-0040 (sha256:3833904000860622a989975850e563c7f862fc38d77939847609f8eaaf8b0b21), Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Artifact: encrypted + include_credentials.

STEPS
1. Restore an archive onto a fresh target (fully populated afterwards).
2. Diverge the target: rename archived group 'Drill Sports' (id 376) to 'Drill Sports RENAMED'; move channels between groups so memberships no longer match the archive.
3. Restore the SAME artifact again — once with relink 'preserve' (default), once with 'replace', from an identical baseline each time. Radio state read back off the input, not the label.

EXPECTED: a restore reproduces the archived lineup, or reports where it could not.

ACTUAL: not one channel's group assignment was corrected to the archive's value, in EITHER mode:
  ch101   archive: Drill Sports  -> after: Drill Movies
  ch102-104 archive: Drill Sports -> after: Drill Sports RENAMED
  ch201-203 archive: Drill Movies -> after: Drill Sports RENAMED
Both runs reported outcome=success, failed 0, notification type=success.

Groups themselves ARE restored (archived names recreated as new empty groups). It is the channel->group EDGES that are not reconciled. No counter, panel or note covers them: profile_membership_drift is channel-PROFILE membership, and there is no equivalent for channel-GROUP membership.

REPRODUCED: yes, in both relink modes.

NOTE ON SCOPE: it is arguable that leaving existing channels alone is intended for relink=preserve. It is NOT explained by preserve, because (a) 'replace' behaved identically, and (b) the documented meaning of the relink modes covers only 'an existing channel's own EPG link and logo'. Even if the behaviour is deliberate, it is unreported, which is the part being filed.

WHY IT MATTERS: restoring onto a populated instance (the migration and DR case) silently keeps the target's grouping. Counts reconcile perfectly, so a diff reads clean.

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-07-run12/inventory/DIFF-populated-target.md (Q5).

New post-channels pass reconcile_channel_groups(): preserve reports channel-group drift naming each channel + its current group + the archived group and PATCHes nothing (never-overwrite contract and xp6mp ruling hold); overwrite reports AND moves. Drift predicted on the dry-run preview. Channels this restore created are excluded. Comparison is by group NAME, not remapped id — the id version mis-reported 3 of run 12's 7 drifted channels and was caught by a preview/apply-parity test. Relink now covers grouping; UI copy and docs updated. Gates re-run independently of the implementing agent: backend suite exit 0 (77.05% coverage), frontend 190 files/2602 tests, lint/typecheck clean, mkdocs --strict clean. RESIDUAL: not yet proven by a live drill against a populated target — carried by enhancedchannelmanager-rjroq.

title: DBAS restore adopts a same-named but different channel group on a populated target, silently
description:
Found UNPRIMED in backup/restore drill run 12 (2026-08-07), DOC-FOLLOWING mode, on a disposable drill stack (project ecmbkr, containers bkr-ecm/bkr-dispatcharr) — NOT production.

Pins: ECM 0.18.1-0040 (ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager@sha256:3833904000860622a989975850e563c7f862fc38d77939847609f8eaaf8b0b21), Dispatcharr 0.28.2. Artifact variant: encrypted + include_credentials.

PHASE: populated-target restore (the round enhancedchannelmanager-oebpv-era runs never reached, because every prior restore landed on a freshly-wiped target).

STEPS
1. Restore an archive onto a fresh target so it is fully populated. Archive contains channel group 'Drill Movies' (id 377) holding channels 201,202,203.
2. On the target, move those channels out, DELETE group 'Drill Movies' (id 377), then CREATE a NEW group also named 'Drill Movies' (id 379) holding a DIFFERENT channel (101).
   Result: same NAME, different id, different members.
3. Restore the SAME artifact again (relink mode preserve, and separately replace).

EXPECTED (per docs/user_guide/backup-restore/restore-a-backup and run-a-restore-drill): either the archived group is recognised as a different object, or the difference is reported.

ACTUAL: the restore matched on NAME and reused the target's id 379. It did not create a separate group for the archived one and did not flag the collision. Afterwards a group named 'Drill Movies' exists holding channel 101 — a channel the archive says belongs to 'Drill Sports'. The archive's actual members (201,202,203) were never placed in it.

title: CI: dev image publish silently leaves :dev stale when any upstream step fails
description:
Observed three times in two days (2026-08-06/07) during the backup/restore drill fix cycle. Three DIFFERENT root causes, one identical and silent symptom: the ghcr :dev tag keeps pointing at an older build while dev has moved on, with nothing surfacing that fact.

OCCURRENCES
1. #789 merge (dev -> 0.18.1-0037). 'Build Docker Image (AMD64)' failed at 'Set up Docker Buildx - retry' (infrastructure flake; the workflow's own retry also failed). ARM64 pushed, AMD64 did not, so 'Create Multi-Arch Manifest' was SKIPPED. Published :dev stayed at 0036 while dev said 0037.
2. GitHub Actions major_outage. Runs enqueued during the incident were orphaned, sat queued 4h39m with zero jobs, and 'gh run rerun' on a run cancelled while queued produced a zombie with no jobs at all. Closing and reopening the PR re-fired the workflows on the same SHA and unstuck it.
3. #791 merge (dev -> 0.18.1-0039). Frontend Tests flaked on dev (StickySectionNav.test.tsx 're-arms when the URL names a different section', a waitFor timeout; the known order/load-dependent flake family - passes 3/3 in isolation and 190 files/2588 tests green locally on the same commit). 'Wait for Test Suite' CORRECTLY refused to publish on a failed suite and every build job skipped. Published :dev stayed at 0038 while dev said 0039.

NOT A REQUEST TO WEAKEN THE GATE. Occurrence 3 is the system working as designed - do not publish an image from a commit whose tests failed. The gate is right.

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM IS SILENCE. In all three cases the repo looked healthy: PR merged, dev green, no alert. The staleness was only found because a drill happened to pull :dev and check the build marker. Anyone pulling :dev in that window gets an older build with no indication, and any validation run against it silently measures the wrong artifact - which is precisely the trap docs/user_guide/backup-restore/run-a-restore-drill.md warns about ('start before the merge and CI publish have landed and docker pull hands you the previous build, every target fails, and the run looks legitimate while proving nothing').

SUGGESTED (design is the engineer's call, not prescribed here):
- Alert when a push to dev does not end with a successful 'Create Multi-Arch Manifest'. A merged-but-unpublished dev is the condition worth paging on.
- Consider a cheap drift check: compare the version in dev's frontend/package.json against the build marker in the published :dev image, and fail/notify on mismatch.
- Consider auto-retrying the publish once Tests goes green on a re-run, so a flake does not require a human to notice and re-trigger.

Severity is about trust in the published tag, not about any single failure. Each individual cause is legitimate or transient; the compounding silence is the defect.

Found by the orchestrator while driving PRs #788-#792, not by an automated check.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9). 6u2pa: the docs-only sentinel workflow was deleted in commit abd325bb ('One source of truth per required status check', bead 5rwzy); every required-check name now has exactly one emitting job, pinned by TestWorkflowContract in test_classify_changed_paths.py. m1ug0: test_output_is_exactly_the_two_github_output_keys now pins the classifier's exact two-key contract across normal, empty and malformed inputs, and the hook extracts by key rather than whole-output comparison. i24jr: superseded by bead t8fqg (closed, PR #797), which shipped scripts/check_publish.py as a mandatory docs/shipping.md step verifying both the build run's conclusion and the published tag's ECM_VERSION marker. ykev5: premise was already false at filing — 38 semver tags run unbroken from 0.7 through 0.18.0 (verified against the live GHCR registry), well past the claimed 0.8.3 ceiling.

description:

STEPS
1. Restore a standard (redacted) DBAS artifact. The restore report correctly names the account and
   field needing re-entry:
     credentials_needing_reentry = 2
     'Infinity' -> profiles[0].custom_properties.user_info.password, password
2. Follow the published article's Step 6a: 'Re-enter the provider credential on every M3U account
   the restore report or the post-restore UI names as needing it.'
3. M3U Manager -> the named account -> Edit.

ACTUAL: the password field is correctly EMPTY (verified: input.value === '', length 0; and the
Dispatcharr API reports password state 'absent', NOT a ***REDACTED*** sentinel — the sentinel bug
stays fixed). But its placeholder reads:

    'Leave blank to keep current'

There IS no current value to keep — the redacted artifact never carried one, which is the entire
reason Step 6a exists. The hint is wrong in exactly the situation the recovery flow puts the
operator in, and it advises the one action that guarantees the account keeps failing to
authenticate.

SUGGESTED: when the stored credential is absent, the hint should say the credential is missing and
must be entered (the restore report already knows this and names the field). The generic
'leave blank to keep current' is only correct when a value actually exists.

(Infinity: username state 'present', password state 'absent') and REPORT.md finding P-7.

Both now carry checklist rows in the sealed drill appendix, so drill run 2026-08-07-run12 will re-measure them on the published image as regression checks. If run 12 contradicts this closure, reopen.

title: DBAS restore: a logo-miss degradation raises error/'Task Failed' while a no-playable-stream degradation correctly raises warning
description:
Found UNPRIMED in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-06-run9 (DOC-FOLLOWING), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack (project ecmbkr) — NOT production.

Pin: ECM :dev build 0.18.1-0035, digest sha256:4e66fdb851d876fa10d7b04e8c97a9a8449b43754316b349a0de3697c656df77. Dispatcharr 0.28.2.

Two restores in the same run produced the SAME outcome value (completed_with_failures) but DIFFERENT alert severities, and the severity ordering is backwards.

CASE A — redacted artifact, nothing playable (this is the daziw trigger). CORRECT.
  outcome                          = completed_with_failures
  channels_with_no_playable_stream = 12
  logo_misses                      = 0
  log:
    [dbas_restore] Alert settings: type=warning ...
    [NOTIFY-SVC] Dispatching alerts: type=warning
                 title=Task Completed with Warnings: DBAS Restore

CASE B — encrypted artifact, one logo genuinely unwritable (destination path occupied by a
directory: docker exec bkr-dispatcharr mkdir -p /data/logos/run9-uploaded-logo.png). WRONG.
  outcome                          = completed_with_failures
  channels_with_no_playable_stream = 0
  logo_misses                      = 2 (see enhancedchannelmanager-k2r7m; one logo actually failed)

Exactly ONE alert was dispatched in each case, so the 'one severity per degraded run' property is intact. The defect is the MAPPING.

  '1 logo row(s) could not be restored; this category is non-fatal, so the rest of the restore was
   applied and nothing was rolled back.'
- The published article warns that after a failed attempt 'the instance is not necessarily back to
  its exact pre-restore state ... treat the next attempt as starting from an unknown state.'
  An operator who trusts the alert will re-run a restore that did not need re-running.
- The ordering is inverted for triage: the restore where NOT ONE CHANNEL CAN PLAY is a warning,
  and the one where a single cosmetic logo is missing is an error titled 'Failed'. Logos were
  deliberately made a non-fatal category; the alerting did not follow.

degraded-but-successful tasks): the task-history API returns status: 'failed', success: false for

disagree about the same run.

title: DBAS restore: logo_misses double-counts a single failed logo (reports 2 for 1)
description:
Found UNPRIMED in backup/restore drill run 2026-08-06-run9 (DOC-FOLLOWING), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack (project ecmbkr, containers bkr-ecm/bkr-dispatcharr) — NOT production.

Pin: ECM :dev build 0.18.1-0035, digest sha256:4e66fdb851d876fa10d7b04e8c97a9a8449b43754316b349a0de3697c656df77. Dispatcharr 0.28.2 (sha256:3eb0ec779f3437ec64c08a9b3f545a355a8f512f3740cdeaac42b80f1021637d). Artifact variant: encrypted + include_credentials.

This is the first time the genuine-logo-failure path (d0agi) has been exercised live in nine runs.

STEPS
1. Seed a source instance with one logo uploaded through ECM's Logo Manager (ECM writes it to Dispatcharr /data/logos/<file>).
2. Take an encrypted + credentials DBAS backup; evacuate and sha256-verify.
3. down -v the stack, roll out clean, rebuild identities.
4. BEFORE applying the restore, make the archived logo's destination path unwritable by occupying it with a directory:
     docker exec bkr-dispatcharr mkdir -p /data/logos/run9-uploaded-logo.png
5. Apply the restore.

EXPECTED (per the published article, 'a logo that cannot be restored is counted and named'): the count of logo misses equals the number of logos that actually failed.

ACTUAL: exactly ONE logo failed, and the report says so three times and contradicts itself once.

  logo category:  created 12, updated 0, skipped 0, FAILED 1
  failure_details: [{"reason": "upstream_api_error", "label": "Run9 Uploaded Logo",
                     "message": "Upstream rejected the logo upload request.",
                     "source_export_id": 13}]
  note:  "1 logo row(s) could not be restored; this category is non-fatal, so the rest of the
          restore was applied and nothing was rolled back."

  logo_misses = 2                                    <-- WRONG
  logo_miss_details = [
    {"source_export_id": 13, "label": "Run9 Uploaded Logo",
     "channels": [{"channel_id": 12, "name": "AL | Birmingham | PBS WBIQ"}]},
    {"source_export_id": 13, "label": "logo #13 (archived)",
     "channels": [{"channel_id": 12, "name": "AL | Birmingham | PBS WBIQ"}]}
  ]

Both logo_miss_details entries carry the SAME source_export_id (13) and the SAME single affected channel. One failed row is emitted twice under two different labels ('Run9 Uploaded Logo' and 'logo #13 (archived)').

On-screen/operator-facing consequence: the restore-complete message reads
  'Restore completed_with_failures: created 47, failed 1 across 13 categories;
   2 logo(s) could not be reinstated; 3 profile membership(s) corrected'
i.e. it says 'failed 1' and '2 logo(s) could not be reinstated' in the same sentence. logo_misses is the number an operator reconciles against; an inflated one sends them looking for a second broken logo that does not exist.

REPRODUCED: once (the only execution of this path). Not retried, because the surrounding restore behaviour it depends on was verified correct in the same run.

NOT A REGRESSION OF THE FIX: the rest of d0agi holds — the restore COMPLETED (outcome completed_with_failures, never rolled back), nothing before the logo step was lost (channels 12/12, streams 96/96 with_url, groups 377/377, profile 9 members, settings preserved — all counted against before-counts.txt), the failure was NAMED with a reason, and the instance still played (2/2 channels, HTTP 200, video/mp2t, 262144 bytes, including the very channel whose logo failed).

Evidence: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-06-run9/inventory/round3-logo-failure-apply-report.json and inventory/DIFF-logo-failure.md.

A miss with no archive id still gets its own row. Regression coverage: backend/tests/dbas/test_logo_miss_dedup.py (8 tests, 5 red before the fix), incl. the drill scenario end-to-end through both producers asserting logo_misses == 1.

title: Restore preview says 'corrected' for changes it would only make on apply
description:
Found by the project-engineer while fixing bead enhancedchannelmanager-dgnms; flagged rather than fixed because the file was outside that change comma brief.

LOCATION: backend/tasks/dbas_restore.py, the _credential_reentry_suffix helper.

It is appended to the DRY-RUN summary message as well as the apply comma so a preview now reads:

    N profile membership(s) corrected

Right number, wrong tense. A dry run makes no changes at all -- it would be "would be corrected". The number itself is correct and newly trustworthy: dgnms made the preview predict profile_membership_drift exactly rather than reporting 0.

WHY THIS MATTERS SLIGHTLY MORE THAN A TYPO: the whole point of the dgnms work is that an operator can trust what a preview tells them BEFORE they commit. A preview that says something was "corrected" in the past tense actively undercuts that -- it reads as though the restore already happened.

Also worth checking the sibling phrases in the same summary builder for the same tense problem on a dry run. For example "account(s) need credentials re-entered" reads fine, but anything past-tense would not.

SCOPE: wording only. Do not change the counters or the summary structure.

Context: drill runs 4-6, ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/. Related: enhancedchannelmanager-dgnms (shipped the accurate preview counters).
close_reason:
FIXED. Shipped in PR #785, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0033.

_credential_reentry_suffix in backend/tasks/dbas_restore.py now takes an is_preview flag and selects a future-tense variant: '%d profile membership(s) corrected' becomes '%d profile membership(s) would be corrected' on a dry run. Sibling phrases were checked — 'account(s) need credentials re-entered' reads correctly either way and is unchanged. Wording only; no counter or structure changed.

VERIFIED LIVE (run 8): the dry-run summary now reads future tense throughout —
  'Dry-run complete: would create 401, update 8, skip 119, 0 conflict(s) across 12 categories; 2 account(s) need credentials re-entered'
and the apply summary is unchanged —
  'Restore completed_with_failures: created 415, failed 0 across 13 categories; 2 account(s) need credentials re-entered; 12 channel(s) have NO playable stream'

The exact 'would be corrected' phrase could not be exercised on the live stack because run 8's seed carried no channel profile, so profile_membership_drift was 0 in every live preview. Verified by RED-PROOF instead: reverting tasks/dbas_restore.py to origin/dev turns 7 of 10 tense tests red; restoring it byte-identically returns 10/10.

PROCESS NOTE, recorded because it nearly produced a false conclusion: the orchestrator's first red-proof attempt used 'git stash push' on a change that was already COMMITTED to the branch. That is a no-op, the working tree was unchanged, and the tests passed — which momentarily looked like the tests were not load-bearing. title: dbas_backup parameter-schema reports 'No configurable parameters' but the endpoint accepts passphrase/include_credentials
description:
Found on the run-4 backup/restore drill (2026-08-05-run4), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack, NOT production.

ECM 0.18.1-0027 (published :dev, digest sha256:3b8c40e7b88327f8244d1a8ea1386daa9116c72b101b5e1b8cfde5b9113c2001).

PHASE: 4, while looking for the documented way to drive an encrypted backup over the API.

STEPS:
1. GET /api/tasks/dbas_backup/parameter-schema

   -> {"task_id":"dbas_backup","description":"No configurable parameters","parameters":[]}

2. POST /api/tasks/dbas_backup/run with
   {"parameters":{"passphrase":"...","include_credentials":true,"acknowledge_unrecoverable":true}}

EXPECTED: the parameter-schema endpoint describes the parameters the run endpoint accepts, so a client can discover them.

WHAT HAPPENED: the schema endpoint reports there are none, yet the nested parameters ARE honoured and are the only way to produce an encrypted artifact over the API. Confirmed from the container log:

  [BACKUP] Built artifact ecm-backup-2026-08-05_224633.zip (schema_version=1, 24 members,
           encrypted=True, include_credentials=True, sha256=08be9bd3...)

versus a plain run:

  [BACKUP] Built artifact ecm-backup-2026-08-05_224606.zip (schema_version=1, 24 members,
           encrypted=False, include_credentials=False, sha256=ed15672c...)

IMPACT: a caller trusting parameter-schema cannot discover the encrypted-backup path at all, and -- worse -- sending the same fields at the TOP level rather than nested under 'parameters' is silently ignored and yields a PLAIN artifact while the caller believes they have an encrypted one. The schema endpoint is the natural place that trap would be avoided.

SEVERITY: minor / discoverability, but it sits directly in front of the credential-carrying backup path.

REPRODUCED: yes.

EVIDENCE: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run4/ -- REPORT.md finding P8, RUNLOG.md 'Phase 4'.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live. Shipped in PR #783, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0031.

FIX: TaskScheduler.run_parameter_schema (class-level declaration, default None), declared by DbasBackupTask for passphrase / include_credentials / acknowledge_unrecoverable with type, label, one-line description, required and default. GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/parameter-schema reads it off the registered task CLASS (never instantiated) and surfaces it. The run endpoint's request shape is untouched and top-level parameters are still ignored — this was a discoverability fix only.

DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISION, and it is the important part: the run parameters are surfaced under a SEPARATE 'run_parameters' key and are NOT merged into 'parameters'. That list is the SCHEDULE form — ScheduleEditor renders each entry as a field and persists the values into task_schedules.parameters in journal.db. Putting passphrase there would create a UI path that writes an operator passphrase to disk and makes every unattended scheduled run emit an encrypted CREDENTIAL-BEARING artifact, which tasks/dbas_backup.py already documents as forbidden (it deliberately excludes the passphrase from get_config for exactly this reason). A frontend-side filter would not be enough: a stale bundle mid-deploy would still render the field. The engineer raised this unprompted; it is a better answer than the brief asked for.

An anti-drift test pushes each declared name through update_config and asserts the task state actually changed, and a second asserts none of them appear in get_config() — the dict that reaches journal.db.

VERIFIED LIVE (run 7, disposable drill stack, build 0032 patched in):

  GET /api/tasks/dbas_backup/parameter-schema
  -> parameters: []
     run_parameters: [passphrase, include_credentials, acknowledge_unrecoverable]
        each with type, label, description, required, default

  parameters is [] so the schedule editor renders nothing and no passphrase can be persisted.
  A task with genuine schedule parameters (m3u_refresh) still returns them normally.

docs/api.md documents both keys.

GATES (re-run independently by the orchestrator): 8484 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failures. Red-without-fix: reverting the router half fails 3 schema tests; reverting the task declaration fails those 3 plus 2 in test_dbas_backup_task.py.

CAVEAT: live evidence from a drill container patched with the merged modules.

title: Saved-backup restore modal claims an unencrypted artifact is encrypted
description:
Found on the run-4 backup/restore drill (2026-08-05-run4), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack, NOT production.

ECM 0.18.1-0027 (published :dev, digest sha256:3b8c40e7b88327f8244d1a8ea1386daa9116c72b101b5e1b8cfde5b9113c2001). Dispatcharr pinned 0.28.2.

PHASE: 6b, while running the modal-remount stale-preview check.

STEPS:
1. On a fresh install, trigger a plain DBAS backup with NO passphrase:
   POST /api/tasks/dbas_backup/run  -d '{}'
2. Settings -> Backup & Restore -> Saved Backups -> the artifact's 'Restore as DBAS backup' button (aria-label 'Restore as DBAS backup').
3. Read the modal.

EXPECTED: the modal should not claim the artifact is encrypted, because it is not. A plain backup needs no passphrase.

WHAT HAPPENED: the 'Restore Saved DBAS Backup' modal renders the line

    This backup is encrypted

verbatim, for an artifact that is demonstrably not encrypted:

    docker exec bkr-ecm python3 -c "
    from pathlib import Path
    from dbas.artifact_crypto import is_encrypted_artifact, read_header
    p=Path('/config/backups/ecm-backup-2026-08-05_231528.zip')
    print(is_encrypted_artifact(p))"
    -> False
    read_header(p) -> 'Not an ECM encrypted artifact'
    zipfile.ZipFile(p) -> opens as a plain zip, 25 members

ROOT CAUSE (likely): the saved-backup listing endpoint carries no encryption flag at all. GET /api/backup/saved returns only:

    [{"filename":"ecm-backup-2026-08-05_231528.zip","size_bytes":124850,
      "created_at":"2026-08-05T23:15:28.210645+00:00","type":"zip"}]

so the modal has nothing to base the claim on and appears to default to 'encrypted'.

IMPACT: an operator restoring their own scheduled backup is told they need a passphrase they never set. It is not blocking -- the preview and apply both proceed normally -- but it is exactly the kind of message that makes someone abandon a restore during an incident.

REPRODUCED: yes.

NOTE: the equivalent UPLOAD modal ('Restore from artifact...') did NOT show this -- it correctly showed no encryption notice for the same plain artifact.

EVIDENCE: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run4/ -- REPORT.md finding P6, RUNLOG.md '23:15 Incidental UI/behaviour observations'.
close_reason:
RETRACTED — my own error, not a product defect.

I filed this from drill run 4 after reading the saved-backup restore modal's innerText and seeing the line 'This backup is encrypted' on a backup that was demonstrably NOT encrypted.

That line is a CHECKBOX LABEL, not an assertion the UI makes. In
frontend/src/components/DbasRestoreSavedModal.tsx:41 it is:

    const [isEncrypted, setIsEncrypted] = useState(false);

so it renders UNCHECKED by default, offering the operator a way to say 'mine is encrypted' and reveal the passphrase field. The modal never claims anything about the artifact.

My own capture proves it was unchecked: the passphrase field is gated behind {isEncrypted && (...)} (line 212) and did NOT appear anywhere in the innerText I recorded — the text ran straight from 'This backup is encrypted' to 'Channels that already exist here'. Had the checkbox been checked, a Passphrase field would have been between them.

Root cause of my mistake: I read control labels out of document.innerText and treated them as UI assertions without reading the control STATE back out of the DOM. The drill prompt explicitly warns about this exact failure ('Did the input actually take? Read every control you set back out of the DOM... A predecessor filed and had to retract a bead over exactly this') and I did not apply it to a control I was merely observing rather than setting.

Consequences being cleaned up:
- The documentation paragraph added on the back of this in docs/user_guide/backup-restore/restore-a-backup.md (merged in PR #780) is being reverted, since it documents a defect that does not exist.
- The finding is marked RETRACTED in place in the run-4 and run-5 reports rather than deleted, so the false start stays visible.

No product change is needed. There is a separate, real question of whether the saved-backup listing API SHOULD carry an encryption flag so the modal could pre-tick the box for the operator — but that is an enhancement, not the defect I described, and I am not filing it as one off the back of a retraction.

title: Degraded DBAS restore emits two notifications with contradictory severity (warning + error)
description:
Found on the run-4 backup/restore drill (2026-08-05-run4), on a DISPOSABLE drill stack (bkr-ecm / bkr-dispatcharr), NOT production.

ECM 0.18.1-0027 (published :dev, digest sha256:3b8c40e7b88327f8244d1a8ea1386daa9116c72b101b5e1b8cfde5b9113c2001). Dispatcharr pinned 0.28.2. Artifact variant: STANDARD (redacted), ecm-backup-2026-08-05_224606.zip.

2. Wipe both ECM and Dispatcharr with their volumes; roll out clean.
3. POST /api/backup/restore-dbas?confirm_apply=true with the redacted artifact.
