  type='warning'  title='Task Completed with Warnings: DBAS Restore'
  type='error'    title='DBAS Restore'

both carrying the identical message:
  'Restore completed_with_failures: created 420, failed 0 across 13 categories; 2 account(s) need credentials re-entered; 12 channel(s) have NO playable stream; 6 profile membership(s) corrected'

The warning is correct and satisfies daziw. The second, error-severity notification is not, and an operator sees both in the notification list.

This is not specific to the degraded case: a SUCCESSFUL restore likewise emits two notifications ('Task Completed: DBAS Restore' and 'DBAS Restore'), both type='success'. There appear to be two emitters -- one from the task scheduler and one from the restore itself -- and only the scheduler's honours the degraded->warning mapping.

REPRODUCED: yes, on every degraded restore in the run (states 1 and 3 of the redacted path).

RELATED: bd daziw (the warning mapping this defect sits beside); bd fexq1 (the same run's task history records status='failed', success=False while failed_count=0 and outcome='completed_with_failures').

EVIDENCE: ~/ecm/backup-restore-runs/2026-08-05-run4/ -- REPORT.md finding P3, notes/apply-STANDARD.json, RUNLOG.md 'Cycle B'.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live. Shipped in PR #783, merged to dev, build 0.18.1-0031.

ROOT CAUSE was not a duplicate alert. The second record is the PROGRESS notification: TaskScheduler._create_progress_notification creates it at run start with title=self.task_name (the bare 'DBAS Restore'), and _finalize_progress_notification re-types it at the end. That finalize had its own severity ladder ending 'else: notification_type = error' and never learned completed_degraded (the rule bead daziw shipped) — only the task engine knew about it.

FIX: extracted task_scheduler.completion_notification_type(result) as the single severity map (cancelled -> warning, success with failures -> warning, clean success -> success, degraded -> warning, otherwise error — byte-identical to what the engine already did). Both emitters now call it. Re-mapped rather than suppressed: the progress notification is the live per-run entry the NotificationCenter and the restore progress UI key on, so deleting it would remove a surface operators depend on.

The progress payload's status field is deliberately NOT re-mapped — the frontend treats it as a closed set (notificationGrouping.FINAL_PROGRESS_STATUSES, useRestoreProgress) and a new value would hang the restore spinner.

VERIFIED LIVE (run 7, 2026-08-06-run7-verify, disposable drill stack, build 0032 patched in). A standard redacted restore onto a fresh target — which legitimately degrades because no credentials means no streams materialize — produced:

  DBAS Restore notification severities: ['warning', 'warning', 'success', 'success']
  contains 'error'? -> False

Before (runs 4, 5 and 6, all three reproduced it): warning + error for the same event, identical message, nothing to say which was authoritative.

NO REGRESSION TO daziw: titles and messages untouched — the engine's branch structure still selects the wording, only the severity literal moved into the shared function, and for the degraded branch it returns 'warning', the same literal it replaced. All five engine call sites were verified provably equivalent, including the cancel branch whose guard is literally 'if result.error == CANCELLED' — the same condition the function checks first. The run-7 restore still reported outcome=completed_with_failures with the 'Task Completed with Warnings: DBAS Restore' title.

GATES (re-run independently by the orchestrator, not taken from the authoring agent): 8484 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failures. Red-without-fix confirmed: reverting only the finalize hunk fails test_a_degraded_run_never_reports_an_error with assert ['warning','error'] == ['warning','warning'] — the measured defect exactly; the other four tests stay green as controls.

CAVEAT: the live evidence came from a drill container patched with the merged modules; the base image was still published :dev 0027.

title: A Docs-Only Sentinel workflow emits same-named passing status checks, so 'gh pr checks --required' can read green while the real job failed
description:
PO decision, 2026-08-05: file it. Found while shipping PR #778.

WHAT HAPPENED
On PR #778 (a backend change, NOT docs-only), I ran:
    gh pr checks 778 --watch --required
It printed every required context as 'pass' and exited 0. Frontend Tests had in fact FAILED.

The rollup contained TWO checks named 'Frontend Tests' from two different workflow runs:
    Frontend Tests   pass   4s        run 31043407561   <- 'Docs-Only Sentinel CI'
    Frontend Tests   fail   4m50s     run 31043410020   <- the real 'Tests' workflow
Same for Backend Tests, MCP Server Tests, CodeQL, Semgrep and Version Consistency: the sentinel workflow emits a fast no-op check under each required context name.

Because the names collide, a consumer filtering by required-context NAME can match the sentinel's pass and never see the real job's failure. 'gh pr checks --required' did exactly that and exited 0.

WHAT DID NOT GO WRONG
Branch protection held correctly -- 'gh pr merge' refused with 'the base branch policy prohibits the merge' and the PR sat at mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Nothing merged that should not have. The actual gate is sound.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS
The failure mode is a FALSE GREEN in the tool humans and agents use to decide 'is this ready'. The documented shipping flow in docs/shipping.md step 6 literally instructs 'gh pr checks <#> --watch' and then merge. Following the documented procedure gives a green reading on a PR whose tests failed. The only thing that caught it here was that the subsequent merge was refused -- i.e. the safety net, not the signal.

It also costs real time: the reflex on a green-then-refused merge is to hunt for a branch-protection or review problem, not to re-read the checks.

POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS (not prescribing)
- Give the sentinel workflow's checks distinct names (e.g. 'Frontend Tests (docs-only sentinel)') so no required context name is ever emitted by two workflows.
- Or scope the sentinel so it does not run at all on PRs that touch non-docs paths -- it should not have run on #778, which changed backend/ and frontend/package.json.
- Or update docs/shipping.md step 6 to verify via the statusCheckRollup conclusion per context rather than 'gh pr checks', if the duplicate names are deliberate and must stay.

REPRO
    gh pr view <non-docs PR#> --json statusCheckRollup \
      -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.name=="Frontend Tests") | "\(.name) \(.conclusion) \(.detailsUrl)"'
Expect two rows with different conclusions.

Note: the JournalTab failure that exposed this was itself an unrelated vitest flake (passed on re-run with no code change) -- see beads yo74u / 7iid7. The flake is not this bead; the false-green reporting is.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9). 6u2pa: the docs-only sentinel workflow was deleted in commit abd325bb ('One source of truth per required status check', bead 5rwzy); every required-check name now has exactly one emitting job, pinned by TestWorkflowContract in test_classify_changed_paths.py. m1ug0: test_output_is_exactly_the_two_github_output_keys now pins the classifier's exact two-key contract across normal, empty and malformed inputs, and the hook extracts by key rather than whole-output comparison. i24jr: superseded by bead t8fqg (closed, PR #797), which shipped scripts/check_publish.py as a mandatory docs/shipping.md step verifying both the build run's conclusion and the published tag's ECM_VERSION marker. ykev5: premise was already false at filing — 38 semver tags run unbroken from 0.7 through 0.18.0 (verified against the live GHCR registry), well past the claimed 0.8.3 ceiling.

title: Restore modal: give-up signature is a convention, and the finalize effect is duplicated across both modals
description:
P3 maintainability. Found by the round-6 ship review of the channel-reattach MODE changeset. Not a defect today; both items are ways the current correctness could be lost silently.

1. THE GIVE-UP SIGNATURE IS A CONVENTION, NOT A TYPE

useRestoreProgress.ts:81-106, DbasRestoreModal.tsx:91, DbasRestoreSavedModal.tsx:70.

RestoreProgressView permits isError: true with progress: null for ANY producer. That this combination means 'the hook gave up waiting for the run to start' is enforced only by three prose comments and one characterization test. The reviewer verified exhaustively that it holds today: viewFromProgress always assigns the payload, the transient-catch branch spreads the previous view and never sets isError, and the give-up branch returns immediately.

The hazard is the obvious next change. MAX_POLL_DURATION_MS (line 253) currently returns silently; publishing a synthesized timeout view there is the natural improvement, and it would land on the SAME signature - so a 30-minute stuck apply would be reported to the operator as 'the restore did not start, it may already be running', which is wrong copy for that state.

Fix: make the invariant load-bearing rather than documented - an explicit runStartTimedOut: boolean on the view, or a discriminated union.

Related in the same cluster: the give-up message string exists in three places (hook line 224 plus a fallback in each modal), and the two modal fallbacks are dead code - the hook always sets error on that path.

2. ~55 LINES OF THE FINALIZE EFFECT ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS BOTH MODALS

DbasRestoreModal.tsx:169-226 vs DbasRestoreSavedModal.tsx:111-168 differ only in comment wording (verified by diff). The runDidNotStart derivation and the 'Back to options' footer branch are duplicated too.

This is the THIRD consecutive review round editing the same block in two files in lockstep: round 3 added the footer, round 4 the runKey, round 6 the give-up bail. Each time it landed correctly in both. That is three coin flips won, not a process.

Fix: extract a useDbasRestoreFinalize(...) hook.

RELATED
enhancedchannelmanager-zt801 (the remaining half of the stale-report class).

title: Restore progress hook can publish a previous session's terminal payload on first poll after remount
description:
P3. Found by round-5 code review of the channel-reattach MODE changeset. Pre-existing shape; the round-5 runKey/started_at work narrows it within a modal session but does not close it across sessions.

SYMPTOM

frontend/src/hooks/useRestoreProgress.ts:201

    let confirmedNewRun = previousRunStartedAt === null;

A freshly mounted hook has no baseline, so the FIRST poll after a remount is published unconditionally - including a previous session's terminal payload, if TaskScheduler.run() has not yet restamped started_at for the new run.

Reachable by: reopening the restore modal, opening a second browser tab, or a page reload, then starting a restore.

Same user-visible family as the round-4 block (a stale report rendered as if it described the run the operator just started), reached ACROSS sessions rather than within one. The realistic outcome is a false 'Restore failed' rather than a stale success report, because the new run's 'running' history row usually beats the finalize effect's read - but the race is the same one.

WHY NOT SHIPPED-BLOCKING

The within-session case (which is the one the operator hits by using the modal's own Back to options control, immediately before an irreversible apply) is closed by the runKey + started_at work. This residual needs a remount to reach, and its likely outcome is a spurious failure banner rather than a misleading success.

SUGGESTED FIX

Persist or derive a baseline across mounts - e.g. treat a payload as stale unless its started_at is at or after the moment this hook instance requested the run, rather than treating 'no previous timestamp' as 'this must be new'.

RELATED
enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn (the changeset this was found in).
notes:
RUN-3: DID NOT REPRODUCE on published :dev 0.18.1-0024 (Dispatcharr 0.28.2, disposable drill stack, populated target holding 12 restored channels).

Ran the exact remount scenario this bead describes, twice:

1) UPLOAD modal ('Restore from artifact...'): preview in preserve -> click Done (modal closes) -> reopen -> re-upload -> select 'Replace their guide data and logos with the backup's' (verified radio checked in the DOM) -> Run preview. The SECOND preview showed the CORRECT report for Replace:
   'Channels you already have would be affected / Guide data - Would replace on 11 channels you already had: ... / Logos - Would replace on 11 channels you already had: ...'
   No stale 'would be left alone' copy, destructive count non-zero as it should be.

2) SAVED-BACKUP modal ('Restore as DBAS backup'), which remounts per file: reopening reset cleanly to the configure step with NO stale report carried over, and the second preview in Replace again showed the correct destructive warning.

So the reassuring-copy-with-a-destructive-mode-armed failure this bead is about did not occur by either route in this build. Recording as live negative evidence; not closing, since the underlying remount/task-singleton structure may still be reachable another way.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
STRONGER EVIDENCE from the round-6 ship review - same defect, probed against the real hook and with broader reachability than I originally wrote.

useRestoreProgress.ts:200-201

    const previousRunStartedAt = publishedStartedAtRef.current;
    let confirmedNewRun = previousRunStartedAt === null;

publishedStartedAtRef is per-hook-instance and is only written at line 232. On a fresh mount restoreTaskId is null, so the poll effect early-returns and NEVER SEEDS IT. The first run of every mount therefore starts with confirmedNewRun = true and publishes whatever the task reports on poll 1 - including the PREVIOUS run's terminal payload, during exactly the fire-and-forget window MAX_RUN_START_POLLS exists to cover.

Chain: isComplete -> finalize effect -> GET /task-history?limit=1 -> the previous run's report rendered as this run's, above an enabled 'Apply these changes'.

Probed against the real hook: started_at 'RUN-1', fresh instance, runKey 1 -> isComplete true, progress.started_at === 'RUN-1'.

Reachability is wider than the 'second tab / reload' I first described:
  * preview -> Done -> reopen the modal -> run again
  * DbasRestoreSavedModal is per-file and REMOUNTS EVERY TIME it is opened
  * page reload
  * simply being the first operator to open the modal in a process where
    dbas_restore has run at any point since startup, because TaskProgress is a
    live singleton on the registered task instance

WHY IT WAS NOT A SHIP BLOCKER
On dev this case is broken identically (no guard at all), so the reattach-mode changeset does not regress it - it closes the in-session half and leaves this one. Blocking a strict improvement over a defect it does not introduce was judged the wrong trade.

But the changeset must NOT be described as having closed the stale-report class. It closed one half, and the shipped copy/CHANGELOG should not overclaim.

FIX OPTIONS
  * cheapest, frontend-only: seed the baseline - issue a getTask before the
    trigger and pass it as baselineStartedAt
  * durable: have the trigger endpoint stamp started_at synchronously before it
    returns, removing the fire-and-forget window entirely

VALIDATION
This is the class a live drill surfaces and unit tests structurally cannot. Per the reviewer: a drill that runs a preview, closes the modal, reopens it, and previews again with the other mode would either exonerate the race or reproduce the original P0 in about a minute. Added to the run-3 drill document.

title: Logo reattach pass runs when LOGO is selected but CHANNEL is not
description:
P3. Found by round-4 code review of the channel-reattach MODE changeset. Currently UNREACHABLE from any shipping surface; filed so it cannot become reachable silently.

SYMPTOM

backend/dbas/restore_orchestrator.py:1370 guards the logo reattach pass on _selected(ctx, EntityType.LOGO), while the EPG pass guards on _selected(ctx, EntityType.CHANNEL). _entities() (line 1110) returns entities regardless of selection.

So with CHANNEL deselected and LOGO selected, the logo pass sees every archived channel against an EMPTY remap and an empty created-set. Under the default PRESERVE that means it names up to REATTACH_NAMED_CHANNEL_CAP (50) of them to the operator as 'existing channels left untouched' on a destination that has none of them.

WHY IT IS NOT REACHABLE TODAY

  * backend/dbas/restore_artifact.py:451 defaults every plan category to selected=True
  * neither restore endpoint exposes per-category selection
  * the sync path (tasks/dbas_sync_engine.py) builds its own steps and never calls
    either reattach pass

So no shipping caller can produce the state. The risk is that per-category selection is a plausible future feature, and whoever adds it will not know this guard is mismatched.

SUGGESTED FIX

Guard the logo reattach pass on CHANNEL selection as well as LOGO - the pass operates on channels, so it needs the channel population to be meaningful. Same shape as the fix in the sibling bead about the preserve/overwrite split asymmetry; worth doing together.

RELATED
enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn.

title: Reattach split: preserve counts an unresolvable channel that overwrite correctly excludes, and now renders its name
description:
P2. Found by round-4 code review of the channel-reattach MODE changeset (bead dfkbn family). Not a shipping blocker; filed so the asymmetry does not sit undocumented.

SYMPTOM

A channel the restore's channel importer refuses (the ambiguous null-channel_number CONFLICT path, or DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED) has no CHANNEL remap entry and is not in created_source_ids.

After the round-4 fix, the two reattach modes disagree about whether that channel exists:

  * OVERWRITE  - correctly excluded from the split (dry run resolves the CHANNEL
                 remap and continues on None)
  * PRESERVE   - still counted as preserved_channels += 1

and the round-4 truncation-marker work now RENDERS preserved_channels_named, so an archived row the restore explicitly declined to identify with any destination channel is displayed to the operator by name as one of their own channels that was 'left alone'.

WHY IT IS NOT A BLOCKER

Traced by the reviewer through backend/dbas/importers/channels.py: ALREADY_EXISTS_IDENTICAL adds the remap, and both create paths add the remap plus the created-id. The ONLY channels reaching the reattach passes without a remap entry are CONFLICT and DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED - and both increment cat.failed. CHANNEL is not in NON_FATAL_FAILURE_CATEGORIES, so on an apply the run aborts and compensating-rolls-back.

So there is no scenario where the wrong 'left alone' line appears without a loud, counted, named channel-category failure beside it. Blast radius is a cosmetic off-by-one in a report the operator is already reading as broken.

SUGGESTED FIX

Symmetric and cheap: resolve the CHANNEL remap before _is_preserved in BOTH passes and drop unresolvable channels from the split entirely, matching what the dry-run branch now does for the actionable set. Costs no I/O - the remap is in-memory and the guide fetch stays behind the same early return.

It changes assertions in two existing tests, which is why it was deferred out of round 5 rather than folded in.

RELATED
enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn (the EPG-link half this changeset serves).

title: Cross-instance sync still drops every ECM-uploaded logo
description:
P2. Found by code review of the xb58a logo-bytes change (drill run 2026-08-04-run2).

backend/tasks/dbas_sync_engine.py:283 - _gather_live_logos reads only ECM's own /config/uploads/logos/, and its docstring claims it 'reads the EXACT set of files a backup artifact would archive.'

After xb58a that parity claim is FALSE: the backup artifact also carries logo bytes fetched from Dispatcharr, and the sync gather does not.

Consequence: cross-instance sync (A -> B) still drops every logo uploaded through ECM's Logo Manager, for the same root reason the BACKUP used to - it looks in ECM's own upload directory, which is empty because Dispatcharr is the source of truth for logos (PO decision, recorded on xb58a).

Two separable pieces:
1. The false docstring - being corrected as part of the xb58a changeset, since leaving an untrue parity claim standing is worse than the gap itself.
2. THIS BEAD: the actual functional gap. Cross-instance sync should reuse the same fetch-from-Dispatcharr path xb58a introduces, so a replica gets the same logos the primary has.

Note cross-instance sync was explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the backup/restore drill (stated in the run-2 report's 'what this drill does not cover'), so this gap is unverified against a live pair - it is inferred from the code path, and should be confirmed on a disposable stack before closing.

Related: enhancedchannelmanager-xb58a (the backup-side fix whose approach this should reuse).

title: DBAS backup logo fetch has no wall-clock bound and can stall a scheduled backup
description:
P2. Found by code review of the xb58a logo-bytes change (drill run 2026-08-04-run2).

backend/routers/backup.py - the new logo fetch loop is strictly sequential over up to _MAX_FETCHED_LOGO_COUNT (5000) logos, and DispatcharrClient's timeout is 30s per request (dispatcharr_client.py:257).

A slow or half-hung Dispatcharr therefore turns a SCHEDULED, unattended backup into an arbitrarily long run: worst case 5000 x 30s. Nothing caps the aggregate.

Individual fetch failures already degrade to a counted miss and never fail the backup, so the failure mode is duration, not correctness.

Fix direction: an overall deadline for the fetch phase, or a consecutive-failure circuit-break, that degrades the remainder to counted misses once tripped - reusing whatever reporting surface the degraded-gather work lands on (see the zt3kf pattern).

Found by code review, not by a live failure.

title: DBAS restore decodes every archived logo's bytes into memory at once
description:
P2. Found by code review of the xb58a logo-bytes change (drill run 2026-08-04-run2). Pre-existing, but that change makes it materially worse.

backend/dbas/restore_artifact.py:376 - _decode_logo_records base64-encodes EVERY binary/logos/* member into one list before the importer sees any of them.

The 'one payload live at a time' discipline (D8) is real INSIDE import_logos, but not in the decode that feeds it. This was latent only because the binary logo subtree was always empty in practice. xb58a makes a populated subtree the NORM, and permits up to 512 MiB of members, which becomes roughly 683 MiB of base64 strings held simultaneously in a single-process container.

At realistic hosted-logo counts (tens) this is fine. The exposure is the budget ceiling, not the median case - the classic 'bulk operations multiply latent severity' shape.

Fix direction: stream/iterate logo members rather than materialising the full list, or bound the decode by the same headroom-derived budget the producer uses.

Pairs with the artifact-budget work in xb58a: if the producer's budget is derived from remaining headroom against _ARTIFACT_MAX_TOTAL_UNCOMPRESSED, the consumer should not then need to hold all of it at once anyway.

Found by code review, not by a live failure. No operator has reported it.

title: ECM serves /api/settings, /api/channels, /api/streams and /api/journal without authentication
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-10 (Project Engineer, re-verified at source and against the
live instance). The observation and its measurements below are right and
preserved. The diagnosis was stale -- it blamed a missing auth dependency
that has since been superseded by a global middleware. Three follow-on
questions the original bead raised are now answered elsewhere; pointers
below.

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION

This bead was filed 2026-08-04 believing the exposed routers had no auth
dependency wired up. That was true once, but a global auth middleware has
existed since 2026-03-17: `git log -S 'AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS' --oneline --
backend/main.py` surfaces exactly one commit, 1f7f8618 ("v0.15.0-0026: Add
/swagger redirect, JWT auth in Swagger UI, update API docs"), roughly four
and a half months before this bead was filed. The middleware
(auth_middleware() in backend/main.py, decorated at line 540, function body
starting line 546) gates every /api/* path by default and only exempts paths
explicitly listed in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS; see docs/auth_middleware.md for the
design ("secure-by-default via middleware; new endpoints must be added to
AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS to be public").

Re-probed live against the running instance just now (read-only GET, no
credentials, no cookie, no API key):

  GET /api/settings   -> HTTP 401  {"detail":"Not authenticated"}
  GET /api/channels   -> HTTP 401  {"detail":"Not authenticated"}
  GET /api/streams    -> HTTP 401  {"detail":"Not authenticated"}
  GET /api/journal    -> HTTP 401  {"detail":"Not authenticated"}

All four carried a `www-authenticate: Bearer` header, which is the
middleware's own response shape (backend/main.py's 401 branch sets
`headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"}`), not a route-level dependency's.
The middleware is doing its job on this instance today.

The drill stack that produced the original 200s had require_auth or
setup_complete false at request time -- see enhancedchannelmanager-qg14z for
why setup_complete in particular ends up false on a fresh install even
though require_auth defaults true (POST /api/auth/setup never persists
setup_complete). That is the actual mechanism behind this bead's original
four 200s, not an absent dependency on these four routers.

ORIGINAL OBSERVATION (preserved, still accurate for the conditions under
which it was captured)

Found incidentally during backup/restore drill run 2026-08-04-run1 (bead
a429n), outside that drill's scope. FOUND ON A DISPOSABLE DRILL STACK, NOT
production. ECM build v0.18.1-0022.

With NO credentials, no cookie and no API key -- plain curl from the host
against a drill ECM that HAD completed its first-run wizard and had an admin
account:

  /api/settings   HTTP 200
  /api/channels   HTTP 200
  /api/streams    HTTP 200
  /api/journal    HTTP 200
  /api/logs       HTTP 404
  /api/backups    HTTP 404
  /api/users      HTTP 404

GET /api/settings returned all 97 setting keys, including instance-identity
and integration data (Dispatcharr URL and username, SMTP host/user,
Discord/Telegram fields, media-server base URLs, SSRF/log-level/cap
settings). Most credentials were correctly reduced to *_configured booleans.

NOW-ANSWERED SCOPE -- pointers, do not re-investigate here

- "The single most important thing to determine" (whether a POPULATED
  Discord webhook URL and Telegram bot token are returned in cleartext to an
  unauthenticated caller): answered YES, by code inspection, in
  enhancedchannelmanager-9ej7f. backend/routers/settings.py:744
  (discord_webhook_url=settings.discord_webhook_url), :747
  (telegram_bot_token=settings.telegram_bot_token) and :748
  (telegram_chat_id=settings.telegram_chat_id) return these three fields raw
  on every read, with no admin gate on read and no serializer redaction,
  while their six sibling secrets (password, dispatcharr_api_key,
  emby_api_key, plex_token, jellyfin_api_key, smtp_password) are correctly
  reduced to *_configured booleans. The disposable-stack experiment this
  bead originally proposed (configure a dummy webhook/token and curl) is no
  longer needed to answer that question -- 9ej7f owns the fix.
- Step 3's proposed regression test ("assert an unauthenticated request to
  each [router] is rejected") survives as
  enhancedchannelmanager-ne2yy, scoped as a snapshot test pinning the exact
  contents of AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS, since the actual gate is the exempt-list
  membership check in the shared middleware, not a per-router dependency.
- Step 1 ("determine whether this is intentional... or a missing dependency
  on the auth middleware") is answered above: not intentional, not a missing
  dependency -- a state-persistence bug in the setup flow (qg14z) that lets
  the existing middleware's own bypass condition (`not setup_complete`)
  apply when it shouldn't.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE EPIC (not filed separately, recorded here per a
security reviewer's note during this correction pass)

ECM explicitly supports running with auth disabled (require_auth: false is a
real, intentional operating mode, not just a bug state). That mode's
documented/expected blast radius has never been written down. A security
reviewer flagged specifically that "auth disabled is supported" should not
silently mean that any anonymous LAN caller can replace the user table,
plant a persistent mcp_api_key, or install their own TLS private key via the
same API surface this bead's probes hit. That is an operator-facing warning
and documentation gap in its own right (what require_auth: false actually
permits, and whether any of it should be gated even in that mode) and
belongs to the parent epic enhancedchannelmanager-9kwzp to scope, not to
this bead.

Do NOT test any of the above against the PO's production instance on port
6100/6101 beyond read-only, non-destructive GET probes (the four re-probes
above were read-only GETs against already-401-gated endpoints and changed no
state).
notes:
RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. The stated mechanism is FIXED (the setup_complete window closed via bead qg14z), and none of the four paths is in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS. DO NOT CLOSE THIS ID: backend/routers/backup.py:2280-2291 cites bead jy006 from production code for the unresolved question. Rescope to that question only: what the supported require_auth:false mode actually permits, specifically anonymous restore-initial over an existing operator identity, mcp_api_key plant via settings write, and TLS private key install. Decide what to gate and document the rest.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 on branch fix/9kwzp-auth-posture, commit 351f40bd. NOT closed: the epic PR is opened by the orchestrator and work is not complete until it merges.

PO decision implemented as written: three identity primitives require an authenticated human admin even when require_auth is false, on any instance holding an operator identity.

  * POST /api/backup/restore-initial -- routers/backup.py::_guard_initial_restore, early return on require_auth removed. The inline citation of jy006 as an OPEN question is replaced with the resolved decision.
  * POST/DELETE /api/settings/mcp-api-key -- RequireHumanAdminForServiceCredential now carries enforce_when_auth_disabled=True.
  * The ten RequireHumanAdminForTLSMaterial routes -- same flag. Applied WHOLESALE to that gate (GET /settings, DELETE /certificate and the https trio included), not to the key-install subset. title: Dead code: channels importer reads archive_channel['profile_memberships'], a key no producer ever writes
description:
Found while fixing enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn (drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n).

backend/dbas/importers/channels.py::_reattach_profiles reads archive_channel['profile_memberships']. Nothing in the codebase writes that key. The only things that feed it are three unit tests, which therefore test a path that can never execute against a real artifact.

Verified against Dispatcharr 0.28.2 source (read from the pinned image, not inferred): ChannelSerializer carries no membership data at all. ChannelProfileSerializer.channels - the list of enabled channel ids on the profile - is the only place channel-profile membership exists on the wire. So the data _reattach_profiles wants has never been available from the channel side and could not have been.

The dfkbn fix therefore drove membership restoration from the PROFILE rows instead (backend/dbas/channel_reattach.py) and left the dormant path intact rather than deleting live-looking code as a rider on a P0.

DECISION NEEDED, then act
Either:
(a) RETIRE it - delete _reattach_profiles and its three unit tests. The membership concern is now owned by channel_reattach.py, so this is pure removal. Preferred unless there is a plan for (b).
(b) WIRE IT UP - have the artifact builder emit profile_memberships per channel and make it the canonical path, retiring the profile-row approach instead. Only worth it if per-channel membership is wanted for some reason the profile-row list cannot serve.

Whichever is chosen, the three tests currently give false confidence: they are green, and they guard nothing.

title: logo_misses counts successfully-uploaded logos, so the restore red banner fires on a restore that lost nothing
description:
Found while fixing enhancedchannelmanager-dfkbn (drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n). Filed separately because it is pinned by roughly 12 sibling assertions across 5 test files and drives shipped UI, so it cannot ride along on a P0.

logo_misses has always incremented for a logo that was SUCCESSFULLY uploaded - it means 'miss' in the MATCH sense (no channel matched this logo), not in the LOSS sense (a channel lost the logo it had). The D9 red banner is wired to the aggregate, so it can fire on a restore where nothing was lost at all.

The dfkbn fix added a second, semantically different producer: the channel-reattach pass now increments the same counter via record_logo_miss when a channel's archived logo could not be reinstated. That is the loss sense, and it is what makes the drill scenario report 12 instead of the wrong 0. So the counter now has TWO producers with two different meanings feeding one operator-visible banner.

That is an improvement over silently reporting 0, but it is not the end state. An operator cannot tell from the banner whether they lost artwork or whether some archived logo simply matched no channel.

SUGGESTED FIX
Split the aggregate: keep a match-sense counter for unmatched archived logos, and add a distinct loss-sense counter for channels whose archived logo could not be reinstated. Wire the red banner to the loss counter only; surface the match counter as informational. Update the ~12 sibling assertions and docs/dbas_restore_contracts.md, which now documents both producers of the single field.

Do NOT do this without also updating the frontend - RestoreCompleteSummary and its tests assert on the current single field.

title: DBAS Restore task never resets self.passphrase, leaving an operator passphrase resident in process memory
description:
Found while fixing enhancedchannelmanager-cytzj (drill run 2026-08-04-run1, bead a429n). Same class of defect as cytzj, different task, lower severity - filed separately rather than widening that fix unasked.

backend/tasks/dbas_restore.py holds self.passphrase, set by update_config and deliberately excluded from get_config so it is never persisted. But nothing ever resets it. execute()'s finally block cleans up artifact files only. The value therefore stays on the live task singleton for the lifetime of the process, exactly as cytzj's encryption transients did on the backup task.

WHY IT IS LOWER SEVERITY THAN cytzj
- The task sets persist_config = False, so nothing rehydrates it on restart.
- The blast radius is a confusing failure rather than a bad artifact: restoring a DIFFERENT encrypted artifact without supplying a passphrase would attempt decryption with the stale one and fail with the sanitized 'wrong passphrase or corrupted artifact' message. A plain (unencrypted) artifact ignores it entirely.
- No incorrect data is written and no credential leaves the process.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING
An operator-supplied passphrase for an encrypted, credential-bearing artifact sits in process memory indefinitely after the restore completes. That is the passphrase that protects the one artifact carrying live provider credentials.

SUGGESTED FIX
Add self.passphrase = None to the existing finally block in execute(). One line. Pair it with a test asserting a second restore of a different artifact does not reuse a stale passphrase, mirroring the tests added for cytzj.

SWEEP ALREADY DONE
Every task's update_config-only keys were checked programmatically while fixing cytzj. tasks/m3u_digest.py also flags on that heuristic but is a FALSE POSITIVE - its get_config/update_config read and write the DB, so nothing is held on the instance. dbas_restore.py is the only remaining real instance.

title: Sweep test hard-pins an owning class and reds on a refactor ADR-014 declares legal
description: From the PR #773 final review (Warn; filed under the last-round ceiling, 2026-08-04). backend/tests/unit/test_dispatcharr_client_contract_sweep.py:1030 asserts 'DispatcharrClient.get_channels' in owners. Same exposure, more defensibly, at :1010-1017 where five specific templates are hard-pinned as convention canaries. This is structurally the same defect class the PR itself fixed elsewhere (a legitimate refactor turning the suite red with a message that misdiagnoses it) — the sweep's own tests should tolerate the refactors the sweep tolerates. Fix: assert on the (method, template) set or on owner SUFFIX rather than the fully-qualified name, or give the assertion a message explaining that owning class is convention rather than contract. title: ADR-014's restore-exercise trigger is keyed to MAJOR while the codebase is MINOR-keyed
description: From the PR #773 final review (Warn; filed rather than fixed under the declared last-round ceiling, 2026-08-04). docs/adr/ADR-014-dispatcharr-api-drift-strategy.md:90 states: 'A Dispatcharr MAJOR-version bump the operator adopts triggers a restore exercise before trust.' But ADR-014:65 states the opposite basis in the same document — 'Dispatcharr is 0.x, so the MINOR is its breaking-change axis' — and the implementation agrees: TESTED_DISPATCHARR_SERIES = ('0.28',) is MINOR-keyed, and the version advisory warns on a MINOR change. Failure scenario: operator upgrades 0.28 -> 0.29, the advisory correctly warns, but the operational rule that should force a backup->restore round-trip before trusting DBAS does not apply because 0.29 is not a MAJOR bump. The rule sits dormant until a 1.0 that may never arrive. Fix: reword the trigger to the MINOR/series axis so it matches both the document's own reasoning and the shipped constant. Note this claim SURVIVED round 3's invariant pass — worth understanding why (the pass checked coverage/behavior claims; this is an operational-rule claim, a category the pass did not enumerate). Owner: it-architect or technical-writer. Size: Small.

title: Verify the '27 DBAS-restore-critical templates' figure or stop citing it as measured
description: From the ax0kf invariant pass (round 3, 2026-08-03; orchestrator filed on the engineer's behalf). title: Contract sweep: close the reverse path-parameter direction (str against upstream integer)
description: From the ax0kf invariant pass (round 3, 2026-08-03; engineer was denied bd create — orchestrator filed). The sweep's path_parameter_conflict check inspects int-annotated interpolations only: a str-annotated or unannotated client interpolation against an upstream parameter declared type: integer yields NO signal. That is exactly the shape of q6xjl root cause B — the settings PATCH sent a key STRING into a route whose parameter the manifest records as integer — so closing this direction would make the sweep catch a real, already-experienced defect class rather than only the existence/method class. The manifest already carries the upstream types needed; what's required first is a false-positive survey of the client's legitimate string interpolations (the earlier asymmetric-rule work found 12 bare-string params on custom action/converter routes, so expect noise and design the rule around it). Documented as a boundary in ADR-014 and in the check's own docstring as of round 3, so this bead is closing a KNOWN gap, not discovering one. Owner: project-engineer. Size: Small-to-Medium (survey then rule).

title: _request passes timeout=None to httpx, disabling the client default timeout on every call
description: Pre-existing, found during the PR #773 delta review (2026-08-03; confirmed present at origin/dev:279, so NOT introduced by ax0kf). backend/dispatcharr_client.py:372 does request_timeout = kwargs.pop('timeout', None) then self._client.request(..., timeout=request_timeout). In httpx, explicitly passing timeout=None means NO TIMEOUT — it does not mean 'fall back to the client default'. So every _request call that doesn't pass an explicit timeout runs unbounded rather than at the client's configured 30s. Consequence: a hung or black-holed Dispatcharr can stall an ECM request indefinitely instead of failing at 30s; task-engine operations that assume a bounded upstream call could hang. Fix: only pass timeout when a caller supplied one (e.g. use httpx.USE_CLIENT_DEFAULT as the sentinel, or build kwargs conditionally). Note: ax0kf's get_version() docstring ('timeout overrides the client's default per-request timeout') is only accurate today because its single caller always passes 5.0 — that docstring should be revisited with this fix. Owner: project-engineer. Size: Small.

title: Small polish on the Dispatcharr version advisory (latency note, constant shadowing, frontend test)
description: From the PR #773 review (N1/N3/N4; PO backlogged 2026-08-03). Three cheap items on the ax0kf version advisory: (1) N1 — the version probe adds up to 5s (timeout=5.0) to every SUCCESSFUL Test Connection, inside the outer AsyncClient(timeout=10.0); no client-side abort risk (fetchJson sets no AbortSignal) so the cost is perceived wait on a slow Dispatcharr — worth a comment naming the worst case, or a shorter probe timeout. (2) N3 — in _resolve_path_expression (the sweep's extractor), the f-string branch tests 'inner.id in constants' BEFORE falling through to the {} wildcard, so a function parameter sharing a name with a module-level str constant would be substituted with the constant's value. No collision exists today (module-level str constants are exactly _USER_AGENTS_PATH, _CORE_SETTINGS_PATH, _DVR_RECURRING_RULES_PATH; zero overlap with any parameter or local in the class). Fix: consult local annotations first, or have client_module_constants() return only _*_PATH names. (3) N4 — no SettingsModal.test.tsx exists at all (pre-existing), so the advisory's frontend contract ('warning shown, connectionVerified untouched, Save stays enabled') rests on reading 6 lines; add a focused test. title: Manifest recording script has no self-test

Two benign sub-notes to fold in: _path_parameters silently drops $ref-style parameters (drf-spectacular inlines, so it doesn't bite today, and it fails safe — a dropped param surfaces as a PATH PARAMETER COUNT red); and the collision guard's 'and existing[openapi_path] != path' is always True (dict keys unique) — dead sub-condition, harmless. title: Contract sweep scope boundary: 6 hand-written Dispatcharr URLs live outside it
description: From the PR #773 review (W3; PO backlogged 2026-08-03). ax0kf's sweep walks backend/dispatcharr_client.py only. Six f-string Dispatcharr URLs live in non-test backend code outside it: backend/auth/providers/dispatcharr.py:121 (POST /api/accounts/token/), :213 (GET /api/accounts/users/me/), :218 (GET /api/accounts/me/), and backend/routers/settings.py:1329/1366/1385. title: Dual-failure alert names only the cloud error, hiding degraded categories from the pushed notification
description: From the PR #770 review (Nit escalated by PO decision 2026-08-03: file to change, not accept). When a DBAS backup BOTH fails cloud upload AND has degraded Dispatcharr categories, success=False routes to task_engine's error branch whose notification body is result.error (CLOUD_UPLOAD_*) only. The degraded-category names survive in result.message and details['degraded_categories'] (visible in Task History) but never reach the pushed alert. An operator paged for the cloud failure fixes the upload, re-runs, and never learns a category was missing from the artifact. Fix: surface both signals in the dual-failure notification body (e.g. append 'also: N category(ies) degraded — <names>' to the error message, or compose a combined message), keeping the cloud failure as the primary/severity driver. Check task_engine's error-branch message composition is not shared in a way that changes other tasks' alerts. Size: Small.

title: Journal audit line contradicts itself for a degraded-but-successful task ('0 ok, 1 failed' beside success:true)
description: From the PR #770 review (Warn; PO ordered filed 2026-08-03). task_engine's log_entry writes description=f'Completed {task_name}: {success_count} ok, {failed_count} failed' alongside after_value {'success': True, ...}. With zt3kf's binary counts model for dbas_backup (total_items=1, success/failed in {0,1}), a degraded-but-real backup writes 'Completed DBAS Backup: 0 ok, 1 failed' next to success:true in the same Journal row. An operator scanning the Journal (rather than the completion notification, which does explain the degraded category) sees a self-contradictory line for a run that DID produce a usable artifact. Same 'reads clean/confusing at a glance' failure mode zt3kf exists to fix, one surface over. Options: (a) make the Journal description severity-aware (e.g. 'Completed with warnings: N category(ies) degraded'), (b) give dbas_backup per-category counts like dbas_restore's RestoreCounts so the numbers mean items not a boolean (the zt3kf engineer flagged this as the parity candidate), (c) both. Note task_engine's log_entry is shared by every task — verify no other task's Journal text changes. Size: Small.
notes: 2026-08-06, PR #790 (build 0.18.1-0038): option (b) DONE. dbas_backup's counts now mean ITEMS, the item being a CATEGORY. BackupArtifact.gathered_categories (set from len(categories) at the single construction site) is the denominator; DbasBackupTask._counts_from_artifact derives total/success/failed from it, mirroring dbas_restore's RestoreCounts. 15-of-16 now reports '15 ok, 1 failed' instead of '0 ok, 1 failed'; total Dispatcharr unavailability counts the local categories that DID archive rather than writing off the artifact. Severity deliberately unmoved and pinned both ways (clean=success, degraded=warning, upload-failure=error) - the ladder keys on failed_count>0 which still holds exactly when degraded_categories is non-empty. One consequential copy change: _success_task_completion_message gains a task_id-guarded dbas_backup branch so the clean-run line names the unit ('All 16 categories archived') instead of '1 items processed'. Consumer audit: log_entry and its call sites untouched, so NO other task's Journal text changes; build_backup_artifact has one non-test caller and BackupArtifact one construction site. Red-first proof: reverted tasks/dbas_backup.py to origin/dev, 4 of the 10 new tests went red, restored, green. WITH OPTION (a) IN PR #788, THIS BEAD'S FULL SCOPE IS NOW ADDRESSED - PO to close.
close_reason:
Both options resolved and verified. Option (a) landed in 0.18.1-0036 (PR #788): task_scheduler.TaskOutcome + task_outcome() are the one severity derivation, the Journal row leads with the severity, and a new terminal history status completed_with_warnings (migration 0042) makes the history row agree with the alert - that was P-2b, the second surface this bead's notes recorded. Option (b) landed in 0.18.1-0038 (PR #790): dbas_backup now derives per-category item counts from the artifact (gathered_categories / degraded_categories) instead of zt3kf's binary model, so a backup that archived 15 of 16 categories reports '15 ok, 1 failed' rather than '0 ok, 1 failed' - a real artifact no longer described as a total loss. Severity deliberately unmoved and test-pinned: the ladder keys on failed_count > 0, which still holds exactly when a category degraded, so clean=success / degraded=warning / upload-failed=error are all unchanged.

VERIFIED LIVE on the published :dev at 0.18.1-0038 (digest sha256:09e25dc2f5c7277348c64b66543b7e1fbbc07f5fe5a8f6fd53ba23532f955f5a), drill run 2026-08-07-run11-published: a degraded restore's history row read completed_with_warnings / success:true beside a type=warning alert (was 'failed' / success:false beside the alert), and a clean restore still read status 'completed' with a type=success alert - the severity work did not turn every run into a warning.

Deliberately unchanged and pinned by tests: the ecm_task_schedule_last_success_timestamp gauge trigger (still result.success, so a run that degrades every time cannot keep resetting the staleness clock), metadata.progress.status (a new member would break asf3n's notification collapsing), TaskResult.success itself, and TaskHistoryPanel's count-based fallback for rows written by earlier builds.

title: DVR recording instances are not backed up at all — evaluate an upcoming-recordings category
description: Finding from the lsa0s implementation (PR #768; PO ordered filed 2026-08-03). The remapped dvr_rules category now carries recurring recording RULES (/api/channels/recurring-rules/), and recordings themselves (/api/channels/recordings/ — per-instance rows with absolute DateTimeField timestamps, confirmed against Dispatcharr model source) were deliberately excluded from it as instance-state. Consequence: no backup category covers recordings at all. UPCOMING (scheduled, not-yet-recorded) recordings are arguably worth restoring in a same-instance disaster-recovery scenario — losing them means silently missed recordings after a restore; COMPLETED recordings reference media files on the source instance's disk and are not portable. Design questions for a new category (or a documented won't-do): upcoming-only filter semantics, channel/stream FK remapping (DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED pattern), absolute-timestamp staleness on restore (skip past-dated?), cross-instance vs same-instance applicability, dry-run parity from day one. Depends on nothing; informs docs (backup-overview's category list should state the exclusion either way). Size: Medium (design + implement) or Small (document the exclusion). Decision-gated: build vs document.

title: comskip backup category is always empty on Dispatcharr 0.28.2 — claims coverage it doesn't have
description: Finding from the lsa0s implementation (PR #768; PO ordered filed 2026-08-03). The comskip artifact category is populated by splitting core-settings rows on a 'comskip' KEY PREFIX (backend/routers/backup.py, key-prefix split near the corrected comment at ~:1972), but 0.28.2's core-settings rows are grouped blobs (network_access, dvr_settings, backup_settings, user_limit_settings, stream_settings, system_settings, proxy_settings — literal key capture in backend/tests/fixtures/dispatcharr_core_settings_recorded.json). No key starts with 'comskip'; comskip config actually lives INSIDE the dvr_settings blob, which the core_settings category already carries. Net: nothing is lost today, but the comskip category is a silent no-op every backup — no warning stub, always empty — and its presence in artifacts/UI claims coverage it doesn't provide. Also note /api/channels/dvr/comskip-config/ exists upstream but GET returns only {path, exists} (never the .ini content) and POST is a multipart upload — not a backup source. Fix options to evaluate: (a) drop the category (artifact-format consideration: tolerant read of old artifacts that contain it), (b) keep but derive its report from dvr_settings presence so it reflects reality, (c) document-only. Decision-shaped; coordinate with zt3kf's severity work. Size: Small, decision-gated.

title: Dry-run failed counts invisible in task summary and completion notification
description:
From PR #766 code review (Warn, pre-existing; PO ordered fix-now 2026-08-03, riding the y6zg6 PR as a second commit). Two gaps: (1) backend/tasks/dbas_restore.py:382-392 _summary_message dry-run branch says 'Dry-run complete: would create N, update N, skip N across N categories' with no failed/conflict count — unlike tasks/dbas_sync.py:649-661 which sums c.failed into a 'N conflict(s)' phrase for the same convention. (2) dbas_restore.py TaskResult (~:320) never sets failed_count/skipped_count, so task_engine.py:1062's 'elif result.failed_count > 0' can never route a DBAS restore into 'Completed with Warnings' — toast/notification stays on the generic success message even when categories failed. Net: a WOULD-FAIL dry-run (now surfaced correctly by y6zg6 in the rich report UI) is still invisible in Task History one-liners and notifications — a narrower cousin of the q6xjl 'confident but wrong summary' UX. Fix: mirror dbas_sync's summary pattern for the dry-run branch (and apply branch if it has the same gap), wire failed_count/skipped_count into TaskResult. Size: Small.

---
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (2026-08-03):
Verified apply branch of _summary_message already reported failed count (no gap there) — only the dry-run branch needed the "N conflict(s)" phrase, added mirroring dbas_sync.py's dry-run branch verbatim in wording style.

For gap (2), also found total_items/success_count were hardcoded to _TOTAL_STAGES (the 13-stage progress-bar count), not real item counts — same "flattened count" anti-pattern dbas_sync.py had already fixed via its SyncCounts/_counts_from_report helper. Wiring only failed_count/skipped_count while leaving total_items/success_count as stage counts would have produced a self-contradictory "Completed with Warnings" message (e.g. numbers not summing to total_items), so all four TaskResult count fields were sourced from a new RestoreCounts NamedTuple + _counts_from_report static method, mirroring dbas_sync.py's SyncCounts pattern exactly (including the note that cat.failed is populated on dry-run too, per EntityCategoryReport's docstring, so failed_count sums identically on both branches).

Red-first tests added in tests/tasks/test_dbas_restore_task.py (TestSummaryMessageFailedVisibility, TestTaskResultCountsWiring) — 5 of 6 new tests failed pre-fix (the no-failures case already passed, confirming no regression on the happy path), all pass post-fix.

Gates: full backend suite 8142 passed, 4 skipped; scripts/check_fake_tests.py clean; scripts/check_version_consistency.py clean (0.18.1-0015, no version bump).

Committed as 50d04776 on fix/y6zg6-dryrun-would-fail (second commit on top of 0d9d8418, not pushed). CHANGELOG entry added under [Unreleased] Fixed, separate bullet from the existing y6zg6 entry.

title: Design: recorded-schema contract sweep for Dispatcharr client paths + ADR on API-drift strategy
description:
Design bead (architect report delivered 2026-08-03; PO APPROVED same day). Systemic answer to the guessed-endpoint bug class: ECM's Dispatcharr REST client was written against a guessed surface (a comment at backend/dispatcharr_client.py ~1711 deferred verification that never happened), producing three shipped bugs — q6xjl root causes A and B (PR #765) and lsa0s (PR #768).

## PO DECISIONS (2026-08-03)
1. **Strategy: option (a) + (b) combined — APPROVED.** Keep recorded-fixture-per-touched-path as the deep pin for high-risk paths (the only mechanism that catches semantic/format drift like q6xjl's A and B), AND add a contract-test sweep for the existence/method class (which catches lsa0s). Option (c) runtime version gate: advisory only, and per PO decision it RIDES THIS SWEEP IMPLEMENTATION (not a separate bead). Option (d) schema-driven client generation: rejected for now — the client's value is its hand-written credential-hygiene/translation layer; revisit only if the upstream surface grows an order of magnitude.
2. **Version-advisory scope: IN THIS BEAD.** Implement `GET /api/core/version/` (present in the schema, currently uncalled) + a NON-BLOCKING "untested Dispatcharr version" notice wired into the existing connection-test path (backend/routers/settings.py ~:1282, POST /api/settings/test). Home-lab tier: warn, never lock the operator out. This closes the silent-upgrade gap where a re-recorded manifest would otherwise keep validating against an old version.

## Measured baseline (architect, live-verified against the 0.28.2 OpenAPI document, 224 paths)
- 92 call sites in backend/dispatcharr_client.py → 58 distinct URL templates; 27 DBAS-critical.
- 3 templates pinned by recorded fixtures today.
- Exactly 3 templates failed to match the live document — all /api/dvr/rules/* — now fixed by lsa0s (PR #768). Every other template matches method-for-method. Re-measure at implementation time; the sweep should be green on its first commit.

## Sweep design (approved as specified)
- **Extraction derived from source, never hand-copied**: AST walk over DispatcharrClient for `self._request("METHOD", <path-expr>)` plus the two raw `self._client.post(...)` calls in _login/_refresh_access_token. Normalize f-string interpolations to a wildcard token; resolve the module-level path constants by importing the module. **Any path expression the extractor cannot statically resolve MUST fail the test loudly, never be silently skipped** — that discipline is the whole point; a silently-partial sweep would recreate the original "comment claiming coverage that wasn't real" failure in miniature.
- **Manifest fixture**: new backend/tests/fixtures/dispatcharr_openapi_paths_manifest.json — {path: {method: {parameters:[{name,in,type}]}}} for all live paths, body schemas stripped. Deliberately SEPARATE from dispatcharr_openapi_recorded.json (different purpose, different churn profile — a body-schema edit upstream must not spuriously fail the sweep). No redaction needed (paths/methods/param types carry no operator data) — a genuine simplicity win over the deep fixtures.
- **Recording script**: scripts/record_dispatcharr_openapi_manifest.py — takes a raw GET /api/schema/?format=json response (fetched by hand or piped from a saved copy; NO live dependency baked in), emits the stripped manifest with the provenance-metadata block the existing fixtures established (source, fixture_kind, captured_at, dispatcharr_version, why). CI stays hermetic — never fetches at test time.
- **Scope: sweep ALL 58 templates, not just the 27 DBAS-critical.** Extraction is automatic so breadth is free; DBAS-critical classification is instead used to prioritize which paths ALSO earn a hand-written deep fixture.
- **Assert**: path exists + method allowed + path-parameter TYPE matches (free once the manifest exists; guards a future int→UUID pk migration). Query params and request/response body shape explicitly OUT of scope — that is option (a)'s job; generalizing body assertions into the sweep rebuilds option (d) in miniature.
- **Location**: backend/tests/unit/test_dispatcharr_client_contract_sweep.py, house fixture-loading pattern, inside the normal pytest gate — no new CI job.
- **Canary**: assert the extractor found a non-trivial call count (e.g. >= 50) so a broken extractor cannot pass by finding nothing.
- **Failure message** names each (method, path, owning-method) tuple, the manifest's dispatcharr_version/captured_at, and states BOTH causes without presuming one: stale manifest (re-record) vs real client bug (fix the client, cite lsa0s as prior art). Explicitly instruct: do not xfail/skip to force CI green.
- **Recording cadence**: deliberate, not scheduled — on adopting a new Dispatcharr version, or when a PR adds client methods.

## Operational rule (from the team review, to land in the ADR)
A Dispatcharr MAJOR-version bump the operator adopts triggers a restore exercise before trust: re-record the manifest against that version and run a real backup→restore round-trip. Event-triggered, not calendar-based (contrast ADR-005's calendar cadence). Complements the monthly dry-run habit that nvhg7 added to docs/runbooks/disaster-recovery-restore.md.

## Deliverables
1. ADR (full draft exists in the architect's design report — land as docs/adr/ADR-014-dispatcharr-api-drift-strategy.md, Status: Accepted, dated, citing PO approval 2026-08-03 and beads q6xjl/lsa0s as the evidence).
2. The sweep (script + manifest fixture + test) per the design above.
3. The version-advisory gate (GET /api/core/version/ + non-blocking notice on the connection test).
4. Cross-link docs/dispatcharr_api.md's new "verify a path against the live schema" note (landed in PR #772, bead r9oqx) to the manifest + recording script.

Size: Medium; decomposes cleanly (ADR / sweep / advisory can be separate commits or PRs). Sequencing note: lsa0s already merged, so the sweep should be green from its first commit — no allowlist machinery needed.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED on branch feat/ax0kf-contract-sweep-adr (3 commits, not pushed). abaf51e1 ADR-014; 85eec1ac sweep (script + manifest + test + docs cross-link); 4314dd6b version advisory + bump 0.18.1-0022.

MEASUREMENTS (re-measured at implementation time, vs a freshly-fetched live 0.28.2 schema that was byte-identical to the design-time capture, 224 paths):
- extractor resolves 97 call sites / 92 distinct (method,template) pairs / 58 distinct URL templates -- exactly matching the architect's baseline of 58.
- 58 path interpolations, all int-annotated; 46 land on schema type=integer, 12 on bare untyped string.
- SWEEP IS GREEN ON FIRST COMMIT. Zero path/method mismatches, zero arity mismatches, zero unresolvable expressions.

DESIGN DECISIONS made during implementation (all documented in ADR-014 + code):
1. Manifest keys are NORMALIZED templates ({param} -> {}), with the literal upstream path kept as 'openapi_path'. Means the test needs no shared normalizer with the recording script. Recorder fails loudly if two upstream paths collide after normalization (none do on 0.28.2).
2. ONE exemption: (GET, /api/schema/) -- drf-spectacular does not document its own schema route inside the document it generates. It SELF-INVALIDATES: a test asserts the exemption set is exactly that one entry AND that /api/schema/ is absent from the manifest, so it fails (demanding deletion) the day upstream documents it.
3. Path-parameter TYPE check is deliberately ASYMMETRIC. int-annotated vs a declared format (uuid) = failure (the int->UUID pk migration this was asked to guard; the 0.28.2 document already carries 5 uuid path params, so the check is not vacuous and the negative test is built from a real one). int-annotated vs bare untyped 'string' = NOT a failure: drf-spectacular emits untyped string for path converters with no declared type, and 12 of ECM's interpolations are like that -- flagging them would be 12 permanent false positives. Rationale in ADR-014 Consequences + the docstring.
4. Extraction covers THREE conventions plus a registry guard: self._request(LITERAL, path), self._get_json_bounded(path) (the bounded-stream helper, treated as a path-forwarding helper so its forwarded paths stay swept), and self._client.<verb>(...) (the two raw login/refresh posts, self.base_url prefix stripped). Any OTHER raw httpx call site fails test_no_unreviewed_raw_http_call_sites until a human classifies it -- three reviewed plumbing sites are registered.
5. Module constants resolved by IMPORTING dispatcharr_client (per the design), not re-derived from the AST.

VERSION ADVISORY design choice: TESTED_DISPATCHARR_SERIES = ('0.28',) -- a single module-level constant of MAJOR.MINOR SERIES, not full versions (Dispatcharr is 0.x, so minor is the breaking-change axis; a patch release must never nag). Edited in the same change that re-records the manifest; docs/dispatcharr_api.md's re-record recipe says so explicitly. Undeterminable version (no /api/core/version/ route, timeout, unparseable body) => silence, never a nag the operator cannot act on. POST /api/settings/test returns an optional 'warning' alongside success:true; SettingsModal shows it as a warning notification without touching verified state.

LIVE VERIFICATION (read-only, ecm-doctest against the real Dispatcharr 0.28.2 at 172.16.0.20; GETs only, no writes, no restart): the real router coroutine returned {success:true, message:'Connection successful'} with NO warning under the shipped constant, and {success:true, ..., warning:'Connected to Dispatcharr 0.28.2 ... not been tested'} plus the server-side WARNING log line when the constant was temporarily pointed at ('9.9',). Container /app restored to origin/dev afterwards.

GATES: full backend suite 8214 passed / 13 skipped (pre-existing skips); new tests re-run under .venv; check_fake_tests clean; both version scripts OK (0021 -> 0022); mkdocs build --strict clean; npm run docs:check clean; frontend tsc --noEmit + eslint clean. TDD: advisory helper, client method and router wiring were all written test-first and observed red (ImportError, then 2 failing router tests) before implementation; the sweep ships with 10 negative tests proving each check can fail.

NOT DONE (deliberately): no push, no PR (stop-at-commit brief).
close_reason: Shipped by PR #773 (merged 7694271b, build 0.18.1-0022). PO-approved strategy (a)+(b): ADR-014 Accepted (docs/adr/ADR-014-dispatcharr-api-drift-strategy.md); AST-derived contract sweep checking every (method, URL template) DispatcharrClient issues against a recorded 224-path OpenAPI manifest (98 calls / 93 pairs / 59 templates, 0 unresolved, 5 reviewed raw seams, 1 self-invalidating exemption); scripts/record_dispatcharr_openapi_manifest.py; and the non-blocking untested-version advisory (GET /api/core/version/ via the swept client, clamped version string, MINOR-series keyed, silent when undeterminable, cannot re-login). Three review rounds, each proving findings by construction: R1 Block (22 tests written but never committed), R2 Block (the R1 remedy introduced a second-login regression against a 3/min rate limit), R3 closed all seven items plus a written invariant pass that found three more false ADR claims. Final ceilinged verification: wire-traced 1 login under 401 (2 without the fix), cross-module refactor proven RED, 6 prior + 13 reviewer-invented seam shapes all correctly classified, ADR claims independently measured. Full suite 8265 passed; CI green. Follow-ons filed: 0cpld, yducf, qfejq, 6imr3, 3tdgu, tyzmh, and two from the final round (restore-exercise trigger keyed to MAJOR while the codebase is MINOR-keyed; a sweep test hard-pinning an owning class that reds on a legal refactor).

title: Hardening sweep from PR #765 reviews: pagination guard, PATCH-failure test, log exception type, test-helper eq
description: Disposition bead from the q6xjl review rounds (PO approved 2026-08-03). title: DBAS backup reports SUCCESS when a Dispatcharr category fetch fails
description:
Follow-on D from q6xjl investigation (PO authorized 2026-08-03). _gather_dispatcharr_sections (backend/routers/backup.py:2044-2113) wraps upstream fetches in one try and on any exception returns a {'_warning': 'Dispatcharr not connected — ...'} stub as a normal value (:2111-2113); caller gathers per-section so blast radius is one category, but nothing downstream inspects _warning and the task has no degraded-severity concept, so a backup missing a whole category reports clean SUCCESS (observed in doc-test run 4: dvr_rules.yaml was a stub on every run). Fix: propagate the stub into the backup result/notification so a degraded artifact is visibly degraded (warning-level completion, category named). Size: Small.

PO DECISION (2026-08-03, rollback policy — resolves parked note 1): (a) keep current behavior — any failed settings key aborts the restore and triggers full rollback, including benign DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED missing-key cases. Do NOT implement per-key skip-with-warning. The work here is to DOCUMENT the policy clearly: module/orchestrator docstrings state the abort-on-any-failed-key rule and its rationale, and the operator-facing report/messaging should make clear after a rollback that a missing-key failure means the artifact carries a key the destination doesn't have (retry won't help; edit selection or upgrade destination). Parked note 2 (duplicate-key LWW comment, enum-reuse annotation) remains: one-line code comment acknowledging the unique-key assumption; no new enum value needed now that the severity ladder stays single-rung.

ROUTED FINDING from lsa0s implementation (2026-08-03): the single try/except in _gather_dispatcharr_sections means any one failing endpoint degrades the whole gather CALL to a _warning stub — blast radius is per-category today only because the artifact builder happens to invoke it once per category. When fixing severity propagation here, make that per-category isolation an explicit contract (or per-fetch granularity), not an accident of call pattern. NOTE: lsa0s (merged PR #768) fixed the only known always-failing fetch, so post-768 the stub path fires only on genuine connectivity/upstream errors — the severity fix is still needed for exactly those.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (2026-08-03):

Branch fix/zt3kf-degraded-backup-severity, commit d7111c2b (main checkout, no worktree, NOT pushed).

Isolation contract: refactored _gather_dispatcharr_sections (backend/routers/backup.py)
so each requested Dispatcharr section's upstream fetch has its OWN try/except -
a failing endpoint stubs only that section, never siblings requested in the
same call. The one exception is total client unavailability (get_client()
falsy/raises before any per-section fetch): that still degrades the whole
blob under one top-level {"_warning": ...} (unchanged pre-existing shape,
since there is nothing section-specific to isolate there). This closes the
routed finding from lsa0s: isolation is now explicit per-fetch, not an
accident of the artifact builder calling the gather once per category.

Severity propagation: _gather_redacted_categories now returns
(categories, degraded_keys); build_backup_artifact threads degraded_keys onto
a new BackupArtifact.degraded_categories field (default [], backward
compatible - only kwarg construction sites exist). DbasBackupTask.execute()
reports TaskResult(success=True, failed_count=1, success_count=0) when
degraded_categories is non-empty (uploads healthy/not configured), naming the
categories in message + details["degraded_categories"] - reaches
task_engine's existing "Completed with Warnings" branch. Cloud-upload failure
still takes precedence (success=False) when both are unhealthy - unchanged
existing behavior, degraded_categories still recorded in details for
visibility.

Notification naming: extracted task_engine._warning_task_completion_message
(mirrors the existing _success_task_completion_message pattern) and added a
task_id=="dbas_backup" branch alongside the existing stream_probe branch -
reuses the SAME "Completed with Warnings" notification path, no new
notification type or emit call. Directly unit-tested
(tests/unit/test_task_notification_formatting.py) plus one engine-level
seam test (test_dbas_backup_task.py) driving the REAL registered
DbasBackupTask through TaskEngine._execute_task end-to-end.

Rollback-policy docs (PO decision (a)): dbas/restore_orchestrator.py module
docstring gained an "ABORT-ON-ANY-FAILED-KEY" section stating the policy and
rejecting per-key skip-with-warning explicitly, with rationale. run_restore
now appends an operator-facing note when the aborting category is SETTINGS
with a DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED failure: retrying the same restore against the
same destination cannot succeed; edit category selection or change
destination. Proven with two new orchestrator tests (the settings case gets
the note; an unrelated category's DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED does NOT).

Parked note 2: one-line comment on the duplicate-settings-key
last-write-wins assumption at the id_map[setting_name] = row_id line in
dispatcharr_client.get_core_setting_id_map; enum-reuse annotation on
FailureReason.DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED in restore_contracts.py noting the
settings_agents.py key-absent reuse. No new enum value added.

Design choice on TaskResult counts: chose a binary total_items=1 /
success_count in {0,1} / failed_count in {0,1} model for the gather-degraded
signal (mirrors the file's OWN existing cloud-upload tri-state pattern:
success_count = 1 if run_result=="success" else 0) rather than modeling
total_items as all 16 RESTORABLE_SECTIONS categories (which dbas_restore does
via RestoreCounts). Chose the smaller model to keep this a Small-scoped fix
and avoid touching the cloud-upload count semantics in the same TaskResult;
noting this as a deliberate scope call in case a future bead wants
per-category counts for backup parity with restore.

(task_engine helper) or direct pre-fix run (backup.py isolation, dbas_backup
severity, restore_orchestrator note) - see test files for the red evidence

title: Remap dvr_rules backup category to Dispatcharr /api/channels/recordings/
description: Follow-on C from q6xjl investigation (PO decision 2026-08-03: REMAP, not drop). ECM's _DVR_RULES_PATH=/api/dvr/rules/ (backend/dispatcharr_client.py:124) does not exist on Dispatcharr 0.28.2 — requests fall through to the SPA index.html catch-all (200 text/html), so get_dvr_rules JSON-parse fails and the category is silently exported as a _warning stub. Real 0.28.2 surface: /api/channels/recordings/ (+/{id}/) and /api/channels/dvr/comskip-config/ (note: contradicts comment at backend/routers/backup.py:1972-1975 claiming no separate comskip endpoint). Semantics differ (recordings vs rules) — importer/exporter mapping needs design, not just a path swap. Also POST to the old path would return 405 not 404. Depends on nothing; independent of the A+B fix.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION (branch fix/lsa0s-dvr-recordings-remap, commit f1d20d86, v0.18.1-0017 — committed, NOT pushed)

PREMISE CORRECTION — the remap target in this bead's description was wrong.
The "real 0.28.2 surface is recordings + comskip-config" finding came from a path
survey that missed the two actual rule resources ('recurring'/'series' contain
neither "record" nor "dvr"). Live-verified against Dispatcharr 0.28.2:
  * /api/channels/recurring-rules/  -> RecurringRecordingRule ModelViewSet
    (id, optional name, integer channel FK, days_of_week, start_time, end_time,
    enabled, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at). GET/POST on the
    collection, DELETE on {id}/.
  * /api/channels/series-rules/     -> APIView backed by
    CoreSettings.get_dvr_series_rules(), i.e. stored INSIDE the dvr_settings
    core-settings row.
  * /api/dvr/rules/                 -> absent from the live OpenAPI document;
    200 text/html (SPA catch-all).
The PO's "REMAP, don't drop" decision therefore holds and was honoured with a
strictly better target: dvr_rules -> /api/channels/recurring-rules/. That target
matches the category's existing contract exactly (name identity + one channel FK
+ create/delete CRUD), so EntityType.DVR_RULE, the dvr_rules artifact key and the
frontend label are UNCHANGED — no artifact migration, no frontend change.

NOT included in the category, deliberately:
  * series rules — already carried and applied by the core_settings category via
    the dvr_settings row; routing them here too would apply the same state twice.
    They also have no id namespace (identity is title+tvg_id) so they do not fit
    the entity/remap/ledger shape.
  * recordings (/api/channels/recordings/) — per-instance state (channel FK +
    absolute start/end timestamps + task_id + custom_properties), and once
    complete they reference a media file on the SOURCE instance's disk.

ALSO IN THIS CHANGE
  * Unnamed-rule identity: `name` is optional upstream, so identity is name-first
    with a schedule fallback (destination channel + days_of_week + clock window +
    date range). Without it, a repeat restore duplicated every unnamed rule.
  * Dry-run/apply parity: an unresolvable channel FK now reports the SAME
    FailureReason.DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED and the SAME message in both modes
    (previously would_skip on preview vs failed on apply — the y6zg6 class).
    Safe because the channels importer registers provisional remaps on dry-run.
  * get_dvr_rules() normalizes a DRF paginated envelope to a list (a raw dict
    would empty the collision index and duplicate every rule).
  * Corrected the false comment at routers/backup.py claiming Dispatcharr has no
    separate comskip endpoint: /api/channels/dvr/comskip-config/ exists, but GET
    returns only {path, exists} (never the .ini CONTENT) and POST takes a
    multipart upload — not a backup source, so the core-settings prefix split is
    unchanged.

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY — pre-fix artifacts carry `dispatcharr: {_warning: ...}`
in categories/dvr_rules.yaml with no rule list. _extract_section_entities already
returns [] for that shape; now pinned by a test (empty category, neighbouring
categories unaffected, no traceback).

FIXTURE — backend/tests/fixtures/dispatcharr_dvr_recurring_rules_recorded.json
(literal live captures + OpenAPI slice; operator-data-free by construction).

GATES (all green, run from backend/ with the repo .venv):
  ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ --tb=short --no-header -p no:warnings
    -> 8157 passed, 4 skipped (pre-existing documented skips) in 319.69s
  scripts/check_fake_tests.py -> 0
  scripts/check_version_consistency.py -> 0 (all 3 touchpoints 0.18.1-0017)
  scripts/check_version_advances.py -> 0 (17 > baseline 16)
LIVE PROOF (read-only) — fixed client inside ecm-doctest against the real
Dispatcharr: get_dvr_rules() -> list [] (no exception; instance has no rules).

FINDINGS FOR THE PO (not filed — reported to the orchestrator):
  1. The `comskip` artifact category is ALWAYS EMPTY on 0.28.2. The split is by
     the "comskip" KEY PREFIX, but 0.28.2's core-settings rows are grouped blobs
     (network_access, dvr_settings, backup_settings, user_limit_settings,
     stream_settings, system_settings, proxy_settings — literal key capture in
     dispatcharr_core_settings_recorded.json). No key starts with "comskip";
     comskip config lives inside dvr_settings, which core_settings already
     carries. Nothing is lost today, but the category claims coverage it does not
     have. Silent no-op, no warning stub — hence not folded into this bead.
  2. Recording INSTANCES are not backed up at all. Upcoming (future) recordings
     are arguably worth a same-instance DR restore; completed ones are not.
     Would need its own category, not this one.
  3. _gather_dispatcharr_sections wraps ALL selected sections in ONE try/except,
     so any single failing endpoint degrades that whole gather call to a
     `_warning` stub. Blast radius is per-category today only because the
     artifact builder calls it once per category. The generic defect (one bad
     endpoint poisons a multi-section gather) remains.

Series-rules excluded (double-apply via dvr_settings), recordings excluded (instance state). Unnamed-rule identity = channel+schedule+enabled (would-be-state normalization); dry-run/apply parity via provisional remaps; paginated-envelope normalization; comskip comment corrected. Backward-compat pinned for _warning-stub artifacts. Two review rounds, red-proven at the routing seam, CI green, full suite 8159 passed.
