title: DBAS restore apply fails on same-instance round-trip: Dispatcharr PATCH 404 on all core_settings, restore rolled back
description:
Found in doc-test run 4 (fresh install, ecm-doctest at port 6200, following the user guide only — symptom report, not a diagnosis; source not read). Steps: took a DBAS backup via Scheduled Tasks -> DBAS Backup -> Run Now on a freshly set-up instance (1 M3U account, 1 EPG source, 3 channels); downloaded the artifact from Saved Backups; uploaded it in the Restore DBAS Backup card; Preview (dry run) reported 8 categories incl Settings 7 WILL UPDATE, 0 FAILED; clicked Apply these changes. Expected (verify-a-backup.md): confirmation dialog, then apply succeeds. Actual: NO confirmation dialog appeared — apply executed immediately — and the restore FAILED: Settings 7/7 'Upstream API error — Upstream rejected applying setting X' (network_access, dvr_settings, backup_settings, user_limit_settings, stream_settings, system_settings, proxy_settings), banner 'Restore failed — your configuration was rolled back'. Container log: repeated '[DISPATCHARR] API request failed: PATCH - status: 404' then '[DBAS-RESTORE] Importer step settings reported 7 failure(s); triggering rollback'. Also logged just before: '[DBAS-USERS] Could not read User schema for capability check: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' with a UsersCapabilityError rollback, and every dbas_backup run logs '[BACKUP] Failed to fetch Dispatcharr data: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' yet reports success. Dispatcharr is 0.28.2, auth via API key. Reproduced once (did not retry apply). Preview passing while apply 404s also means the dry run does not catch this class of failure. Screenshots: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-03-run4/shots/060-062. Uncertain whether the missing confirmation dialog is doc overstatement or a product regression — noted in run-4 DEFECTS.md either way.

---
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (Project Engineer, 2026-08-03) — branch fix/q6xjl-dbas-settings-contract, commit fdb0c1e6. Scope: fixes A and B only.

ROOT CAUSE A (settings 7/7 PATCH 404). Dispatcharr 0.28.2's CoreSettingsViewSet is a plain DRF ModelViewSet with the default pk lookup, so the detail route is /api/core/settings/{integer id}/. ECM PATCHed /api/core/settings/{key}/ (dispatcharr_client.update_core_setting), which matches no route. Live read-only proof on ecm-doctest: GET /api/core/settings/network_access/ -> 404, GET /api/core/settings/6/ -> 200. Backup artifacts carry key->value only (routers/backup.py flattens; ids are per-instance), so ids must be resolved against the destination at apply time.

FIX A. New DispatcharrClient.get_core_setting_id_map() builds key->row-id in ONE GET (accepts a bare list or a DRF-paginated envelope; drops rows it cannot key rather than guessing an id). update_core_setting() now takes the integer row id. New settings_agents.CoreSettingIdResolver is run-scoped and lazy — core_settings and comskip share Dispatcharr's single settings namespace, so one apply run costs one GET, a dry-run or opted-out category costs none, and a failed fetch is memoized so a dead destination cannot become a per-key fetch storm. A key absent on the destination now fails THAT key with FailureReason.DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED and a by-name message ("Setting key 'X' is not present on the destination Dispatcharr"), not an opaque upstream 404. The credential/auth denylist is unchanged: a denylisted key is never even resolved. Log hygiene unchanged (key name still never reaches a log sink; the PATCH path is now built from an int, not a caller-supplied string).

ROOT CAUSE B (users capability check). /api/schema/ is served by drf-spectacular, whose default renderer is YAML (content-type application/vnd.oai.openapi), so .json() raised "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" -> UsersCapabilityError -> category failed closed on every restore.

FIX B. get_user_schema_write_fields() now requests ?format=json (live-verified: no param -> YAML, ?format=json -> parseable JSON). The fail-closed check itself is unchanged; it can now actually run. Live: _assert_capability passes with 14 write fields, no password_hash.

FIELD-VALUE SURVEY (live GET /api/core/settings/, Dispatcharr 0.28.2, ecm-doctest): bare JSON list of 7 rows {id,key,name,value}; ids NON-CONTIGUOUS and uncorrelated with list position — network_access=6, dvr_settings=18, backup_settings=19, user_limit_settings=21, stream_settings=17, system_settings=20, proxy_settings=7. All 7 pass is_safe_setting_key. Recorded into repo fixtures: backend/tests/fixtures/dispatcharr_core_settings_recorded.json (shape capture, values replaced) and backend/tests/fixtures/dispatcharr_openapi_recorded.json (literal slice of the real /api/schema/?format=json document).

TESTS (TDD; 11 red before the fix). Client: recorded-schema parse yields a non-empty write-field set with readOnly id/api_key excluded; ?format=json asserted; key->id map from the recorded list; paginated envelope; unusable rows dropped; PATCH at the integer-id path. Importer: key->id happy path (asserts exact id->value pairs), missing-key explicit failure, one-GET-per-apply-run across core_settings+comskip, lazy no-fetch on dry-run/opt-out, memoized fetch failure. Roundtrip test extended to assert the resolver is called once and the denylisted key's row id is never PATCHed.

GATES. backend: python -m pytest tests/ --tb=short --no-header -p no:warnings -> 8131 passed, 4 skipped, coverage 76.39% (threshold 56%). scripts/check_fake_tests.py clean. scripts/check_version_consistency.py clean at 0.18.1-0014 (build bumped 0013->0014 across the 3 touchpoints; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry added). No Python lint tool is configured in this repo (CI backend gate is pytest + fake-test guard + version consistency).

OUT OF SCOPE, CONFIRMED DURING VERIFICATION: client.get_dvr_rules() still raises JSONDecodeError against 0.28.2 — that is the sole cause of the "[BACKUP] Failed to fetch Dispatcharr data: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" line on every dbas_backup run (every other gather call returns a list). Belongs to enhancedchannelmanager-lsa0s. Also untouched per brief: backup severity (zt3kf), dry-run preview not catching this class (y6zg6), missing confirm dialog (d20jf).

NOT YET PROVEN: no live restore apply was run (PO-gated). The end-to-end proof is a real DBAS restore against ecm-doctest after review.

title: No CI enforcement of the PII bar on screenshots added under docs/images/
description:
Raised by the security-engineer PII audit on 2026-08-02 and directed to be filed by the PO. Risk rating from that audit: Medium (High severity, Low-Medium likelihood).

BACKGROUND. .gitignore previously excluded docs/images/ entirely, commented '# User guide screenshots (may contain PII)'. To let the operator user guide render, that rule was narrowed to 'docs/images/*' plus '!docs/images/user_guide/', and 65 screenshots were committed after an individual, enumerative PII audit (a further 24 were audited and cleared but deliberately left uncommitted, as they pair with articles not yet landed).

THE GAP. docs/images/user_guide/ is now a tracked directory that any 'git add' can write to, and the standard that governs what may go in it exists only as a comment in .gitignore. Nothing mechanically checks a newly added screenshot.

WHY SEVERITY IS HIGH. MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager is a PUBLIC repository and git history is permanent. This product's UI renders Xtream Codes stream URLs as https://<provider-host>/live/<username>/<password>/<id>.ts, so a single careless stream-list screenshot publishes a working subscription credential irreversibly. Other values that must never appear: the Dispatcharr and SMTP host addresses, the instance's public IP (Dispatcharr renders one in its own sidebar), real email addresses, Schedules Direct and other account usernames, and API keys or tokens.

WHY LIKELIHOOD IS ONLY LOW-MEDIUM. The sanctioned documentation-capture harness already obfuscates PII at capture time behind a leak-assertion gate that fails the capture rather than writing a leaking file. That is a real compensating control. The exposure is the ad-hoc screenshot taken outside that harness.

PROPOSED FIX, reusing what exists rather than building new: run the capture harness's existing leak-assertion pattern list as a CI check over PNGs added under docs/images/ in a PR diff. Per this repo's 'Enforcement Code Tests Itself' rule the check would need a fixture-based self-test proving it actually catches a seeded leak.

Note for whoever picks this up: a raw-byte or OCR scan will not catch everything. In the audited set, provider text was destructively blurred into the raster, and conversely a leak could be rendered as pixels with no matching bytes. Decide honestly what the check can and cannot detect, and make the comment in .gitignore state the residual gap rather than implying full coverage.

Also worth knowing: nine tracked images outside user_guide/ (docs/images/event_sync/ 7, docs/images/normalization/ 2) were already published and had never been audited by anyone. They were checked during this work and all nine pass, so no action is needed on them, but they were unexamined until 2026-08-02.

title: frontend/package-lock.json version skew: 0.18.0 while guarded touchpoints are 0.18.1-00NN
description:
Found 2026-08-02 during the version bumps for PR #761 (build 0009) and PR #760 (build 0010). Pre-existing skew, not introduced by either bump.

frontend/package-lock.json carries version 0.18.0, while the three touchpoints guarded by scripts/check_version_consistency.py are at 0.18.1-0010:
- frontend/package.json ('version')
- backend/routers/backup.py (APP_VERSION)
- backend/main.py (FastAPI(version=...))

package-lock.json is not listed in that script's TOUCHPOINTS constant, so nothing in CI notices the drift and it will keep widening on every build bump. npm itself writes the version into the lockfile's top-level 'version' field and the '' root package entry, so the two are expected to agree with package.json.

Not urgent and not user-visible. The decision worth making is whether the lockfile should join TOUCHPOINTS and be bumped in lockstep like the other three, or whether it is deliberately excluded and the skew is acceptable. Whoever picks this up should check whether any tooling reads that field before changing the guard, since adding a fourth touchpoint makes every future bump slightly heavier.

Related context: a separate stale-node_modules gap surfaced in the same session — this checkout's node_modules predated a dependency added in commit 300bcb1d (2026-07-27), so 'npm run build' failed until npm install was run. That may or may not share a root cause with lockfile hygiene; worth a glance while in the area. PO directed this bead be filed.

title: PII-audit and commit the 65 user-guide screenshots so the operator guide renders, narrowing the docs/images gitignore
description:
PO decision 2026-08-02, option (b): narrow the ignore rule, audit the screenshots for PII, and commit the clean ones before PR #760 merges.

CONTEXT. PR #760 lands the operator user guide (81 files under docs/user_guide/, up from 37). Its 'Operator Docs' CI gate fails with 65 'missing local target' errors: the articles reference screenshots that git refuses to track. .gitignore line 65 ignores docs/images/ outright, commented '# User guide screenshots (may contain PII)'. Only 16 images were ever force-added, which is why the guide rendered correctly during local testing (the mkdocs site serves a worktree where 105 PNGs sit on disk) while CI sees them missing.

THE RISK. MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager is a PUBLIC repository. Committing an image with credentials in it publishes them permanently; git history cannot be quietly un-published. The source screenshots were captured against a live instance whose UI renders Xtream Codes stream URLs in the form https://<provider-host>/live/<username>/<password>/<id>.ts, so a single stream-list screenshot can leak a working subscription credential. Other live values in that environment include the Dispatcharr host IP, an SMTP host IP, the operator's real email address, a Schedules Direct username, and the instance's public IP (Dispatcharr renders it in its own sidebar).

SCOPE.
1. Narrow the .gitignore rule so docs/images/user_guide/ can be tracked while the PII intent of the rule is preserved for everything else.
2. Enumerate all 65 referenced-but-missing images. Audit EVERY one individually. No sampling: this is a one-way public action.
3. Commit only the images that pass. For any that fail, do not commit and do not redact in place; report them so they can be re-shot.
4. Bump the build number to 0.18.1-0010 on the same branch (PR #761 takes 0009; merging out of order breaks the version-advance check).

The 2026-08-02 documentation test produced 152 screenshots that were PII-obfuscated at capture time behind a leak-assertion gate, under ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/shots/. They were built to be promotable into documentation and may cover part of the surface, though filenames and framing will not match the articles' expectations.

Branch: docs/operator-user-guide, in worktree /home/lecaptainc/ecm/wt-docland. Source images are on disk (gitignored) at /home/lecaptainc/ecm/wt-newui/docs/images/user_guide/ — that worktree belongs to a live session and is READ-ONLY for this work.
close_reason: Merged as PR #760. 65 screenshots individually PII-audited and committed; gitignore narrowed to docs/images/* plus !docs/images/user_guide/. A follow-up pass audited the remaining 24 (all clean) which landed in #763. Enforcement gap for FUTURE images tracked separately as fu6yd.

title: Bump build to 0.18.1-0009 so the beads JSONL export refresh can ship
description:
The beads export refresh on branch chore/beads-export-refresh (commit 845ead93) cannot open a PR: the version-advance-guard hook blocks it with 'build number does not advance. Current 0.18.1-0008 (build 8) equals baseline 0.18.1-0008 (build 8). Bump frontend/package.json (and the two other touchpoints in lockstep) to 0.18.1-0009 or higher.'

That branch carries a single commit refreshing .beads/issues.jsonl, which .beads/.gitignore designates as the git source of truth. The tracked export had fallen 475 issues behind the live Dolt store (2509 vs 2984) and had not been touched in the last 117 commits on dev, so beads from several prior sessions — including pui76, ys384 and gk4d0 — were absent from git entirely, along with six filed by the 2026-08-02 documentation test.

Scope: bump the build number to 0.18.1-0009 across all version touchpoints in lockstep, on the existing chore/beads-export-refresh branch, so the export can ship. Nothing else. Do not modify .beads/issues.jsonl — it is generated by bd export and is already correct.

PO decision 2026-08-02: land the export as its own PR rather than having it ride along with a later code PR.

Note for whoever picks this up: the underlying workflow problem is worth thinking about separately. A tracker-data-only change cannot satisfy a guard designed for source changes, which is a plausible reason 475 beads of drift accumulated — if exports can only ship attached to a code PR, and nobody attaches them, they never ship.
close_reason: Merged as PR #761 (build 0.18.1-0009), carrying the beads JSONL export refresh.

description:

The working path today is Settings -> Scheduled Tasks -> DBAS Backup -> Run Now, plus the Encrypted Backup (Migration) card; neither is mentioned. title: Journal shows a Batch id but gives no way to filter by it; the guide sends operators to the raw API
description:
Raised from the 2026-08-02 documentation test (fresh install, container ecm-doctest, port 6200, image :dev). Symptom/gap report — no source read.

user_guide/channels-streams/the-journal.md, section 'Find the rest of a batch', tells the operator to expand a journal row to see 'Batch:' followed by an identifier, then says: 'Every change applied together shares that identifier. The Journal page displays it but does not let you click it to filter, so to pull the whole batch you either search for something the rows have in common, or query the API directly with GET /api/journal?batch_id=<id>. That is the reliable way to reconstruct a large Channel Pipeline run or a big Apply All.'

Confirmed in the UI: expanding a Bulk Commit row does display 'Batch: da27d02a', and it is inert — not a link, not clickable, and there is no batch filter in the Journal's filter row (which offers Category, Action, Source and a free-text search only). So the guide is accurate about the limitation, but the net effect is that the documented 'reliable way' to reconstruct a batch is a raw HTTP request an operator cannot make from the browser.

The obvious fix is to make the displayed Batch id clickable, or add a batch filter — the identifier is already on screen and already the correct key. But that is a product decision for whoever picks this up.

Worth noting this compounds a separate, more serious journal finding filed during the same run (enhancedchannelmanager-r9py9: no per-channel rows are written for Edit Mode changes at all). If that one is resolved such that per-channel rows exist, batch reconstruction becomes considerably more valuable than it is today — the two are worth looking at together.

Filed at the PO's direction after triage of the documentation test findings.

Evidence: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/DEFECTS.md DEF-018; screenshot shots/133-journal-row-expanded.png.

title: Duplicate-EPG-link audit has no UI: the operator guide tells operators to call an MCP tool or raw API endpoint
description:
Raised from the 2026-08-02 documentation test (fresh install, container ecm-doctest, port 6200, image :dev). Symptom/gap report — no source read.

user_guide/epg/channel-to-epg-matching.md, section 'Checking your fleet', tells the operator: 'Run the duplicate-EPG-link audit (audit_epg_duplicates MCP tool / GET /api/epg/audit-duplicates) to find channels still mis-linked: either left over from before this fix, or a region combination the matcher doesn't have enough signal to disambiguate automatically.'

The capability itself sounds genuinely useful — the same article explains at length that mis-linked regional feeds (a West-coast channel silently matched to the East-coast guide row, three hours off) were a real field bug. But there is no way to run this audit from the ECM UI. The only documented routes are an MCP tool and a raw HTTP request, neither of which is available to an operator working in the browser.

The result is an operator guide instructing operators to do something operators cannot do. Either the audit needs a UI surface (most naturally on EPG Manager, or alongside the bulk EPG assignment flow where mis-links originate), or the guide should stop presenting it as an operator task and route it to support/developer documentation instead. That call is for whoever picks this up; I am reporting the gap, not choosing the fix.

Filed at the PO's direction after triage of the documentation test findings. Companion gap for the Journal's batch lookup is filed separately.

Evidence: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/DEFECTS.md DEF-015.

title: Stream list takes ~25 minutes to reflect a group-selection change, with no progress indication anywhere
description:
PO-directed investigation, raised from the 2026-08-02 documentation test. Found on a fresh install (container ecm-doctest, port 6200, image :dev v0.18.1-0008). Symptom report only — I did not read source and did not investigate the cause.

WHAT WAS DONE (all documented steps, from user_guide/getting-started/your-first-channels.md step 3):
1. M3U Manager -> the account's Manage Groups (folder) icon.
2. Disable All (readback confirmed: '0 / 375 enabled').
3. Enabled exactly two groups, 'USA | Local ABC' and 'USA | Local NBC'; each checkbox read back as checked, and the modal header confirmed '2 / 375 enabled'.
4. Save & Refresh.

EXPECTED, quoted from the article: 'The modal closes and ECM immediately re-pulls streams for only the groups you enabled. You don't need a separate manual refresh right after this step.'

WHAT HAPPENED: the modal closed and the toast 'Group settings saved — M3U refresh started for Infinity' appeared, both correct. The M3U row went PROCESSING... then back to READY within about a minute, and the GROUPS column correctly showed '2 / 375 groups'. But the Streams panel in Channel Manager continued to show all 36,468 streams from the initial full-playlist import for roughly 25 minutes afterwards. During that window the row said READY and there was no progress indicator, banner, spinner, count-down or any other signal anywhere in the UI that work was still outstanding. It looked exactly like the group selection had silently done nothing.

After the wait the state converged correctly and completely: the Streams panel settled at 430 streams, matching the two enabled groups (216 + 214), and has been stable since.

SECOND SYMPTOM IN THE SAME WINDOW, possibly the same root cause: during those ~25 minutes the Create Channel dialog's Channel Group dropdown listed every provider stream group (Default Group, '4K / UHD Channels', 'USA | Sports', and so on) as selectable channel groups. Once the system settled, the same dropdown correctly showed only the operator-created group — which is the documented behaviour, since ECM is supposed to exclude groups whose names match provider stream groups. So the exclusion logic is right; it just appears to operate on stale data during the convergence window.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE DELAY: this is a known false-positive generator. The previous documentation test run filed a product bead against this exact behaviour, believing group selection was broken, and that bead had to be retracted. Two consecutive testers have read this as a broken feature. A real operator has strictly less information than either of them.

REPRODUCED: observed once in full on this run, and independently by the prior run's tester on a separate instance.

SELF-CHECKS RUN BEFORE FILING: (1) input took — every group toggle read back from the DOM and the modal's own counter confirmed 2/375; (2) waited — this bead IS the waiting finding, and the end state is correct; (3) container log agrees with the UI rather than contradicting it, showing no error during the window.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE THIS, in the reporter's terms: either the stream list converges promptly after Save & Refresh, or the UI tells the operator that work is still in flight and roughly how much. Either one removes the 'it did nothing' reading. Which of those is the right fix is for whoever picks this up.

Evidence: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/DEFECTS.md DEF-007; screenshots shots/043-streams-usa-expanded.png (36,468 streams after Save & Refresh) and shots/058-channels-recreated.png (settled at 430).

title: Journal records no per-channel rows for Edit Mode changes, so a channel's history cannot be traced by name
description:
Found on a fresh install (container ecm-doctest, port 6200, image :dev v0.18.1-0008) while following docs/user_guide/channels-streams/the-journal.md literally. Symptom report only — I did not read source or investigate the cause.

DOCUMENTED STEPS FOLLOWED, in order:
1. Channel Manager: created two channels (Doctest ABC #100, Doctest NBC #101) in Edit Mode, assigned one stream to each, created channel group 'Doctest Locals', moved a channel into it, applied via Done -> Apply All. Later, bulk-assigned EPG to both channels and applied again.
2. Opened Journal (Insights -> Journal).
3. Set the category dropdown to 'Channel' (readback verified: dropdown reads 'Channel'; backend request was GET /api/journal?page=1&page_size=50&category=channel).
4. Typed 'Doctest ABC' into 'Search entries...'.

EXPECTED, quoted from the article: 'Result: You get that channel's rows newest-first, with the Entity column showing the channel name and the Description column summarising what changed, for example "Updated channel: cleared EPG mapping". Click a row to expand it into Before and After blocks with the exact field values.' The same article also states: 'One Edit Mode session produces one Bulk Commit row plus the individual rows. Applying a batch writes a summary row ... alongside the per-channel rows for what was in it.'

WHAT HAPPENED INSTEAD: the search returns 'No journal entries'. Clearing the search shows the Channel category contains exactly 3 rows in total, every one of them ENTITY='Bulk Commit', ACTION='Bulk Commit', DESCRIPTION='Applied N operations in bulk commit'. There are no per-channel rows at all, so no row anywhere carries a channel name, and a channel's history cannot be traced by name as the article's headline task requires. Expanding a Bulk Commit row shows only an AFTER block of counters ({operations_applied: 2, operations_failed: 0, channels_created: 0, groups_created: 0, validation_issues: 0, continue_on_error: true}), 'User initiated', and 'Batch: da27d02a' — no channel names, no per-field before/after values.

Note channels_created reads 0 in that payload even though the commit created channels, which may or may not be related.

REPRODUCED: yes — observed identically across three separate Apply All commits (two channel/stream commits and one EPG-assignment commit), and confirmed at the backend, whose log for the filtered request reads '[JOURNAL] Retrieved 3 journal entries (total: 3, page 1/1)' for category=channel and 'Retrieved 0' for category=channel&search=Doctest+ABC.

SELF-CHECKS RUN BEFORE FILING: (1) input took — category and search values read back from the DOM and confirmed in the backend request URLs; (2) waited — entries were 11-26 minutes old and displayed; (3) container log agrees with what the UI showed rather than contradicting it.

FILED AS PRODUCT DEFECT because the documentation was clear and correct about what to do and the feature did not do what it says. If the intended behavior is in fact 'bulk commits are summarised only', then this is a documentation defect instead and should be closed as such — I could not tell from the UI alone.

Screenshots: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/shots/128-journal-channel-filtered.png, 130-journal-channel-rows.png, 131-journal-search-doctest.png, 133-journal-row-expanded.png
notes:
DIAGNOSTIC EVIDENCE added 2026-08-02 — narrows this considerably. Still a symptom report; no source was read.

The repository's own documentation screenshot, docs/images/user_guide/channels-streams/1-journal-channel-entries.png (tracked on dev), shows the Journal filtered to the Channel category containing exactly the per-channel rows this bead says are missing: 'ZZ Demo News 24 HD' / Stream Add / "Added stream to channel...", 'ZZZ Docs Demo Impor...' / Delete, 'Flo Racing 03: NO EVE...' / Update / "Updated channel: cleared EPG mapping", each with the channel name in the ENTITY column.

The discriminator is the SOURCE column. Every per-channel row in that screenshot is sourced **AI** (an MCP agent). The only **UI**-sourced row in the frame is a single 'Bulk Commit' summary reading 'Applied 3 operations in bulk...'.

That matches the original finding exactly. Every change in the 2026-08-02 test was made through the UI in Edit Mode, and the Channel category contained only Bulk Commit rows — three of them, all Source UI, with no per-channel rows at all.

So the likely shape of this bug is NOT 'per-channel journal rows are never written'. It is that the **UI Edit Mode commit path writes only a Bulk Commit summary row, while the MCP/AI path writes per-channel rows**. The journalling capability exists and demonstrably works; one write path appears not to use it.

This also means the original bead title understates the scope of what works and overstates what is broken. Whoever picks this up should start by comparing the two write paths rather than looking for missing journal-write code in general.

Consequence for documentation: the guide cannot simply say 'per-channel tracing is not possible', because it is possible for MCP-sourced changes. That nuance is being carried into the article under bead mtkw1.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits f37c794b, b7dbb1ff, 98ed692e.

THE NOTES' DIAGNOSIS WAS CORRECT AND SAVED THE INVESTIGATION. This was never 'per-channel journal rows are never written' - the MCP path wrote them all along and the UI Edit Mode commit path wrote only a Bulk Commit summary. Starting from a comparison of the two write paths, as the NOTES instructed, was the right first move.

The UI bulk-commit path now writes per-channel rows in the same shape, correlated by a new X-ECM-Batch-Id header across all requests of one Apply All, flushed in one transaction.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: 'channels_created reads 0 even though the commit created channels' is NOT the bug it appears. One Apply All is 2+ bulk-commit requests - a create phase, then batches of 200 - each with its own summary row. The reporter expanded a non-create row, where 0 is accurate. groups_created WAS genuinely wrong: it counted len(groupIdMap), which also collects pre-existing groups resolved by name. Both are explicit counters now.

CORRECTION TO THE DOCS the bead quotes: 'One Edit Mode session produces one Bulk Commit row' is wrong in both directions, and the user guide now says one batch containing one or more summary rows plus the individual rows.

Hardened well beyond the bead across three reviewer rounds: journal.log_entries signals failure by RETURNING FALSE and its return was discarded, so a failed batch write silently lost every row; row construction happened after the risky work so any path that mutated then failed lost the row; and recording a landed write now REQUIRES its journal row as a defaultless keyword, with nothing_to_journal(reason) the only way to say otherwise.

Left open as enhancedchannelmanager-ftidn: 75 of 80 journal call sites across 22 modules still discard the return value. And jd3kn: the immediate delete-group path writes no row at all.

title: No one-click 'Back Up Now' control on Settings, Backup and Restore
description:
Symptom report, not a diagnosis — found during documentation test on a fresh install at port 6200 (container ecm-doctest, image :dev) following user_guide/backup-restore/take-a-backup.md, which next-steps.md tells a brand-new operator to do before they need it.

Documented steps followed, in order (Option A, manual backup):
1. Settings -> Backup & Restore.
2. 'Find the Backup card.'
3. 'Click Back Up Now.'

Expected, quoted from take-a-backup.md: 'ECM builds the artifact in the background via the dbas_backup task. A notification appears when the backup completes. The artifact is saved to /config/backups/ on the ECM host.'

What happened: there is no card called 'Backup' and no button called 'Back Up Now' anywhere on Settings -> Backup & Restore. The page's action buttons are: Export YAML, Restore from YAML..., Download Full Backup, Create Encrypted Backup, Add sync target, New Target, Add Cloud Target, Restore from artifact..., Restore. The cards are: Where backups can be sent / Export Configuration (YAML) / Restore from YAML Export / Saved Backups / Full System Backup / Encrypted Backup (Migration) / Cross-Instance Sync. Nothing produces the DBAS .zip snapshot the article (and the page's own 'Which one do I need?' helper) describes as 'what scheduled backups produce'.

Documented steps followed, in order (Option B, scheduled backup):
1. 'Settings -> Task Schedules' — no such item; the sidebar entry is 'Scheduled Tasks'.
2. 'Find the dbas_backup task, or create a new schedule for it.' — the Scheduled Tasks page lists 13 tasks (EPG Refresh, M3U Refresh, M3U Change Monitor, Database Cleanup, Journal Noise Purge, Stream Probe, Re-probe Failed Streams, Struck Stream Cleanup, Popularity Calculation, Dummy EPG Refresh, Black Screen Scan, Stats v2 Rollup & Prune, M3U Change Digest). There is no dbas_backup task and no visible way to create a new schedule for one.

Corroborating in-product signal: Settings -> Backup & Restore shows its own banner 'Backups are not scheduled yet — ECM does not run automatic backups until you schedule them. Set one up.' Clicking 'Set one up' navigates to #settings/scheduled-tasks, the same list that contains no backup task. So the product's own guidance also dead-ends.

Also observed while there: the 'Saved Backups' card says 'No saved backups. Enable the YAML Backup scheduled task to create automatic backups' — naming a 'YAML Backup' task that likewise is not in the task list.

notes:
CORRECTION from the 2026-08-02 documentation re-test (container ecm-doctest, port 6200, image :dev v0.18.1-0008). The second half of this bead's title and description is WRONG and should not be actioned as written.

WHAT THIS BEAD GOT RIGHT (re-confirmed): Settings -> Backup & Restore has no card called 'Backup' and no button called 'Back Up Now'. take-a-backup.md Option A still cannot be followed as written. The card list observed matches this bead's description exactly.

WHAT IS WRONG: the claim that there is 'no dbas_backup task in Scheduled Tasks'. On :dev the task EXISTS. Settings -> Scheduled Tasks lists 16 tasks, not the 13 recorded here; the prior run's list stops at 'M3U Change Digest' and misses three entries further down the page: 'YAML Backup', 'DBAS Backup', and 'DBAS Restore'.

DBAS Backup is present, Disabled, schedule 'Manual only', described as 'Build a redacted, sealed DBAS backup artifact (ZIP + SHA-256 sidecar) in /config/backups/. Scheduled or manual.' The Encrypted Backup (Migration) card also works end to end and produced ecm-backup-2026-08-02_182558.zip + sidecar, with the 12-character passphrase minimum enforced (Create button disabled at 11 characters) and the acknowledgement checkbox required.

NET EFFECT ON SCOPE: this is not 'no way to take or schedule a DBAS backup'. The capability exists and works; what is missing is (a) the 'Back Up Now' control the documentation points at, and (b) any UI surface that LISTS the resulting DBAS artifacts. The 'Saved Backups' card is YAML-only by its own caption ('YAML backups saved on the server by the scheduled backup task') and displayed 'No saved backups' while two real DBAS artifacts sat in /config/backups/. So an operator can produce a backup but cannot confirm from the UI that it exists, nor download or delete it. That listing gap is the more serious half and is not currently captured in this bead's title.

Symptom report only, no source read. Evidence: ~/ecm/doc-test-runs/2026-08-02/DEFECTS.md DEF-010 and DEF-012, screenshots 076-backup-restore-page.png, 077/078 (encrypted backup), 081-scheduled-tasks.png, 082-dbas-run-now.png.

Remaining scope is only: Settings > Backup and Restore has no one-click 'Back Up Now' control, so operators must go via Scheduled Tasks > DBAS Backup > Run Now.
RETITLED 2026-08-16. The old title ended '...and no dbas_backup task in Scheduled Tasks', a clause this bead's own notes had already retracted TWICE. dbas_backup IS registered and IS runnable from the UI. Anyone triaging by title would have mis-scoped this as 'build a backup feature'. Board hygiene only; the body and its history are untouched.

INVESTIGATED 2026-08-16, read-only. THE GAP IS ABOUT 95 PERCENT WIRING.

WHAT IS MISSING: one button that calls api.runTask('dbas_backup') with no parameters. No backend change, no new endpoint, no authorization work - PRIVILEGED_TASK_IDS already covers the task and the page is already admin-gated. The API call, the toast pattern and the invalidateServerData('saved-backups') refresh all already exist ONE CARD AWAY in EncryptedBackupCard.tsx:43.

WHY IT LOOKS BIGGER THAN IT IS: of the seven action buttons on that page, exactly ONE writes a DBAS artifact - 'Create Encrypted Backup'. 'Download Full Backup' hits GET /backup/create, whose docstring says it persists nothing. POST /backup/save has no frontend caller at all. So the only DBAS producer on the page is labelled 'Migration' and demands a 12-character passphrase plus an unrecoverable-loss acknowledgement. The page's 'Which one do I need?' helper is literally truthful and still strands the operator: it recommends DBAS for disaster recovery, then offers no control that produces the plain redacted artifact.

SIZE: Small. Frontend only - a new card modelled on EncryptedBackupCard placed above it, plus two stale strings at :344 and :353 ('Enable the YAML Backup scheduled task'), a component test, docs and CHANGELOG. Fixing those two strings also closes bead e4iok.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS NOW INVERTED, and this must not be missed: THE DOCUMENTATION IS ALREADY FIXED. take-a-backup.md:17 currently reads 'The Backup and Restore page does not have a Backup card or a Back Up Now button' and routes the operator to Scheduled Tasks then Run Now, with an explicit does-not-exist-yet note. That landed in f741fc6f, and Option B's 'Task Schedules' was corrected too. The guide does NOT walk anyone into a dead end today. So if this button ships, the guide has to be rewritten BACK, or it becomes wrong in the other direction.

TWO OPEN BEADS THAT MAY GATE THIS, and the PO should rule on both before it ships:
- gi4zn (P1, open, same epic): the standard REDACTED backup leaves the XC/M3U username in cleartext. A one-click button makes that exact artifact trivially easy to produce and share. Today the passphrase ceremony is an accidental brake.
- sj32h (P2, open): the backup's logo fetch has no wall-clock bound. The ceremony partly shields the encrypted card; a bare button will not. Expect 'I clicked Back Up Now and it hung' unless sj32h ships first or the button carries background-run copy.
PO DECISIONS 2026-08-17, all five, taken after the read-only investigation.

D1 - GATED BY gi4zn. The standard artifact must be fully redacted BEFORE this button ships. Reason: today the only UI path to a DBAS artifact is the encrypted card, so the cleartext XC/M3U username sits inside an encrypted envelope. A plain one-click button would produce the first easily-obtainable artifact carrying that username in the clear - and those are the files operators attach to support tickets and carry between machines. The button does not just remove friction, it removes encryption from an artifact with a known credential leak. Sequence: gi4zn, then this.

D2 - dbas_backup STAYS DISABLED by default. The prior decision stands; ECM does not write to an operator's disk on a schedule nobody chose. What was wrong was never the decision, it was its enforcement - see bead iij6s. Consequence: bead 1vm5r (retention UI) stays P3 and is NOT a prerequisite, because there are no unattended writes accumulating beside journal.db.

D3 - A NEW CARD, NAMED FOR WHAT IT PRODUCES, not for the action. Not 'Back Up Now' on a card called 'Backup'. The reason emerged from D1: once gi4zn lands, the standard artifact is FULLY redacted and cannot restore credentials, while the encrypted one can. An operator restoring from the plain artifact must re-enter every M3U and EPG credential by hand. Naming the card after the action would let them believe a redacted artifact is a complete backup, and they would discover otherwise at the worst possible moment. Something like 'Configuration Backup', with the button stating credentials are not included and pointing at the encrypted card for a complete one. Exact wording is the technical-writer's to choose within that constraint.

D4 - THE GUIDE LEADS WITH THE MANUAL BUTTON, then the schedule. take-a-backup.md gets rewritten back from its current 'the button does not exist' wording, but NOT to its original text, because the card is now named for its contents. The orchestrator flagged the risk and the PO accepted it: an operator may stop after step one holding exactly one stale backup and believe they are covered. That risk is why iij6s matters MORE under this decision, not less.

D5 - xdjbs is CLOSED as established-not-a-defect, with a separate bead filed for the operational step of actually enabling a schedule on the production instance.

SIZE UNCHANGED: Small, frontend only, once gi4zn has landed.

title: SMTP test email fails with generic 'Unexpected error during SMTP test' instead of the documented verbatim SMTP error
description:
Symptom report, not a diagnosis — found during documentation test on a fresh install at port 6200 (container ecm-doctest, image :dev) following user_guide/notifications/index.md, section 'Settings -> Notification Settings -> SMTP'.

Documented steps followed, in order:
1. Settings -> Notification Settings.
2. Filled the documented required fields: SMTP Host 172.16.0.246, SMTP Port 25, Security 'None' (the doc lists 25 (unencrypted) as a valid port and None as a valid Security choice), From Email, From Name. Username/Password left empty (doc marks both Optional).
3. Save Settings -> toast 'Settings saved successfully', SMTP badge flipped Unconfigured -> Configured (matches doc).
4. Test Connection -> entered recipient (the instance operator's own email address) -> 'Send Test Email'.

Expected, quoted from the article: 'A successful test produces a toast that reads Test email sent to <the address you entered>... A failed test surfaces the SMTP error verbatim (auth failure, connection refused, TLS handshake error, etc.). Read the error before changing settings.'

What happened: an error toast reading exactly 'SMTP Test / Unexpected error during SMTP test'. No SMTP-level detail of any kind — no host, no port, no connection-refused/timeout/TLS text. The article explicitly promises the verbatim SMTP error, and the operator is told to read that error before changing settings; there is nothing to read.

Reproduced: yes, identical toast on a second attempt.

Two possibilities I could not separate without leaving the UI (and this test forbids source reading and shell probing): either the send genuinely failed for an environmental reason and the error surface is swallowing the underlying exception, or the send path itself errored. Either way the reportable symptom is the same: the documented diagnostic output does not appear. Note the PO-provided SMTP target is 172.16.0.246:25 with no authentication and was expected to accept mail; I did not verify inbox delivery (no mailbox access), so I cannot say whether mail was sent despite the error.

Screenshots: scratchpad doctest shots/190-smtp-filled.png, 191-smtp-test-result.png, 192-smtp-test-retry.png. Found on a fresh install at port 6200 following the user guide. I did not read source; this is what I saw.
close_reason: Retracted by the reporter — self-inflicted, not a product defect. The failing test ran with Security still set to TLS (STARTTLS) against a plaintext-only server on port 25; my automation's click on the 'None' choice never changed the underlying native <select>, so the setting I believed I had made was never applied. Container logs (read via the documented troubleshooting path) showed 'SMTPNotSupportedError: STARTTLS extension not supported by server', i.e. ECM correctly attempted STARTTLS as configured. After genuinely selecting Security=None and saving, 'Send Test Email' succeeded and produced exactly the documented toast: 'Test email sent to <address>'. The doc's claim that a failed test 'surfaces the SMTP error verbatim' is still not accurate — the UI toast read only 'Unexpected error during SMTP test' while the real reason was in the container log — but that is a documentation-accuracy point, recorded in the doc-test report (DEF-025 area), not a product bug worth holding a bead open for.

title: Stream dedup prompt did not appear when creating a channel whose name matches an existing channel in the target group
description:
Symptom report, not a diagnosis — found during documentation test on a fresh install at port 6200 (container ecm-doctest, image :dev) following user_guide/channels-streams/stream-dedup.md.

Documented steps followed, in order:
1. Channel Manager -> Edit Mode.
2. In the Streams panel, ticked the row checkbox for stream 'US: CNN' (plus 'US: Al Jazeera').
3. Selection strip -> 'Create in...' -> chose channel group 'News Channels'. That group already contained a channel named 'CNN' (created earlier in the run, EPG-linked to 'CNN HD').
4. In the Create Channels dialog set Starting Channel Number 200, clicked 'Create 2 Channels'.

Expected, quoted from stream-dedup.md ('Create in... menu' trigger path): 'If ECM finds a candidate channel in the target group, the StreamDedupModal appears.' The article lists Create in... as one of three trigger paths and says the default confidence threshold is 80%.

What happened: no StreamDedupModal appeared. Two new channels were staged directly (#200 'US: Al Jazeera', #201 'US: CNN') alongside the existing #100 'CNN' in the same group. No error, no toast.

Uncertainty, stated plainly: I could not confirm what confidence score ECM computed for 'US: CNN' vs the existing 'CNN' channel, so I cannot rule out that it scored below the 80% threshold, in which case silence is documented behavior ('If no candidate meets the threshold, the dedup check is silent'). Filing per the guidance to file when it's genuinely unclear whether this is a product defect or a documentation gap. If the score was legitimately under threshold, the doc problem is that the article gives an operator no way to tell 'no candidate' from 'feature not working'. Note also 'Normalization Rules: Disabled' was shown in the Create Channels dialog; the doc does not say whether dedup matching depends on normalization.

Reproduced: the same non-appearance occurred on an earlier attempt via the plain 'Create' button with the same stream.

Also observed while testing this article: stream-dedup.md says the Channel Manager 'subnav bar shows a Pending Merges item with a count badge'. There is no subnav bar and no Pending Merges item anywhere in Channel Manager on this build (no pending merges existed, so this may be conditional rendering the doc does not mention).

Screenshots: scratchpad doctest shots/142-create-in-modal-open.png, 143-create-2-result.png, 144-created-channels-state.png, 145-channel-manager-subnav.png. Found on a fresh install at port 6200 following the user guide. I did not read source.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commits 941d9087, 546e0afe.

THE ANSWER THE BEAD WAS FILED TO GET: 'US: CNN' vs 'CNN' scores 1.00, not below threshold. Obtained by running the production matcher directly - _normalize in CONSERVATIVE mode lowercases and strips, and token_set_ratio scores the subset match at 100. find_candidate returns a match even at threshold 0.99.

So this was NEVER the documented below-threshold silence. The bead's own uncertainty ('I cannot rule out that it scored below the 80% threshold') is resolved: it did not.

THE REAL CAUSE: only a SINGLE-stream selection routes through the dedup hook, and the reporter had two streams selected. Multi-stream goes straight to the bulk modal by design.

Per the PO's decision not to touch the matcher, the fix makes the outcome legible rather than building bulk dedup: 'No duplicate found', 'Duplicate check unavailable', 'Duplicate check skipped'. Applied to the Create in... path and then to the drag-drop sibling, where five branches ended a drop and only one said anything.

ALSO ESTABLISHED, closing the bead's open question: dedup does NOT depend on normalization. The candidates lookup uses the raw stream.name and fires before the Create Channels dialog exists, and the matcher applies its own cleaner. An operator turning normalization off does not lose dedup protection. Held by a pin.

The bead's secondary observation about the missing 'Pending Merges' subnav was verified as correct behaviour, not a defect: ChannelManagerTab gates the whole nav on pendingMergesCount > 0. Documented rather than changed.

Enumeration found two channel-creation surfaces dedup never covers - manual Run Pipeline/Run Rule (the hook is gated off entirely) and CSV import - both now documented as such.

title: The published user guide contains 151 dead links into deliberately-excluded developer docs
description:
Found while removing ADR references at PO request. Removing those fixed 18; a full count shows 151 more of the same defect.

mkdocs.yml excludes all top-level docs/*.md plus /adr/, /commands/, /design/, /runbooks/, /security/, /sre/, /testing/ from the built site. That exclusion is deliberate and documented (COMPONENTS.md docs-tier note): internal docs are kept off the public site on purpose.

But docs/user_guide/ links into that excluded content 151 times, overwhelmingly from 'Going deeper' sections. Every one is a 404 for a reader of the published site. Verified live: an excluded target returns HTTP 404 while a sibling user_guide page returns 200.

Top targets: api.md (51), event_sync.md (16), normalization.md (15), architecture.md (12), template_engine.md (6), runbooks/README.md (6), sre/slos.md (5), versioning.md (4).

Both gates pass. mkdocs reports each as INFO ('contains a link to X which is excluded from the built site'), and --strict only fails on WARNING and above. check-operator-docs.mjs does not catch them either, because the target file exists on disk; it is only absent from the site. See the companion bead on that gate gap.

Three options:

A. Rewrite the links as absolute GitHub URLs, e.g. https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/blob/dev/docs/api.md. Verified these resolve (HTTP 200; the repo is public). Preserves every reference, respects the decision to keep internal docs off the site, and the reader gets the document instead of a 404. Recommended.
B. Delete the links. Loses genuinely useful pointers; several 'Going deeper' bullets exist only to carry one.
C. Publish the developer docs on the site. Reverses a deliberate documented decision and would put threat models and ADRs on a public docs site.

Option A is mechanical and scriptable. Pin to a branch or tag rather than a commit SHA so the links do not rot.

Note the site is already public-repo-backed, so option A discloses nothing that is not already readable on GitHub.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. title: mkdocs --strict passes on links to excluded files, so the user guide shipped 18 dead links
description:
Found when the PO asked whether the user guide referenced ADRs. It did: 18 references across 12 articles, 10 of them as markdown links to docs/adr/*.md.

docs/adr/ is in the mkdocs exclude list, so no ADR page exists on the built site. Verified against the live preview: an ADR URL returns HTTP 404 while a sibling real page returns 200.

The gate gap: mkdocs reports these as

  INFO - Doc file 'user_guide/x.md' contains a link to 'adr/ADR-00N-....md' which is excluded from the built site.

at INFO level. --strict only fails on WARNING and above, so it passed cleanly the entire time. scripts/check-operator-docs.mjs did not catch them either, because the target file genuinely exists on disk; it is only absent from the *site*. Both gates were green and the published guide still had dead links.

This generalises beyond ADRs: any user_guide link into an excluded tree (adr/, runbooks/, security/, sre/, design/, testing/, commands/, validation/) is a 404 for a reader and is invisible to both gates. There are legitimate cross-links of this kind elsewhere in the tree, so the fix should be scoped rather than blanket.

Suggested fix: fail the docs gate when a file under docs/user_guide/ links to a path excluded from the built site. Either parse the mkdocs INFO stream for that message and treat it as an error for user_guide sources, or add the check to check-operator-docs.mjs, which already resolves internal links and would only need to additionally test membership in the built nav.

The 18 references themselves are being removed under the meta-commentary pass; this bead is about the gate that let them ship.

Related: enhancedchannelmanager-pb2s4 (the docs build never runs on a PR at all).

title: EPG, M3U and probe alerts can only ever reach email, and the UI gives no way to discover this
description:
Found while writing the Notifications user guide section. Two coupled gaps in the same area.

GAP 1: the UI cannot create Discord or Telegram alert methods.
ECM has two dispatch paths. Scheduled-task alerts go through _dispatch_to_alert_channels and reach Discord and Telegram directly from shared settings (services/notification_service.py:282-399). But per-source EPG refresh, per-account M3U refresh, and stream probe call alert_methods.send_alert directly (routers/epg.py:413, routers/m3u.py:283, stream_prober.py:787), which dispatches only through AlertMethod rows.

frontend createAlertMethod has exactly one caller and it hardcodes method_type: 'smtp' (SettingsTab.tsx:1213-1222). No code path in the repo creates a Discord or Telegram alert method. So on any instance configured through the UI, EPG/M3U/probe alerts can reach email and nothing else, no matter what the operator configured for Discord or Telegram. Nothing in the UI says so.

GAP 2: the auto-created Email method has notify_info=false and no UI to change it.
So a task with Info severity ticked silently sends no email. The operator ticked a box that does nothing.

Both are discoverability failures rather than crashes, which is what makes them expensive: the operator believes alerting is configured and finds out it is not when an alert they needed does not arrive.

Options: allow the UI to create Discord/Telegram alert methods; or route the three direct callers through _dispatch_to_alert_channels; or, cheapest, state the limitation in the UI. The new user guide documents the current behaviour accurately either way.

title: Telegram alerts from scheduled tasks are sent as unescaped HTML and can be silently dropped
description:
Found while writing the Notifications user guide section.

backend/services/notification_service.py:315-320 interpolates the alert title and message straight into a Telegram HTML-parse-mode payload without escaping. The parallel alert-method path escapes correctly (backend/alert_methods_telegram.py:102-117), so this is an inconsistency between two dispatch paths rather than a missing feature.

Impact: any scheduled-task alert whose title or body contains <, > or & produces invalid HTML. Telegram rejects the sendMessage call and the alert is lost. This is silent: the operator sees no error, and the alert simply never arrives. Channel names and stream names routinely contain & (for example 'Sports & Entertainment'), so this is reachable in normal use, not a contrived input.

Worse, it fails precisely when something has gone wrong enough to fire an alert.

Fix: reuse the escaping helper the alert-method path already uses, or drop parse_mode for this payload. Prefer reusing the helper so the two paths converge.

title: ECM revokes active sessions roughly 30 minutes in, while the refresh token is still valid for days
description:
Hit twice in one session by documentation agents driving Playwright against ecm-ecm-1.

Symptom: POST /api/auth/refresh returns 401 {"detail":"Session not found or revoked"} (backend/auth/routes.py:746) about 30 minutes into a run. The refresh_token cookie in the stored state is nominally valid for another week (issued with a ~7 day expiry), so this is not token expiry. The UserSession row is being revoked or deleted server-side.

Impact seen: a long-running browser automation loses auth mid-run with no client-side recovery path, because the refresh endpoint is the only non-interactive way back and it is what fails. One agent lost a full run to it. For a human operator the equivalent symptom is being logged out mid-task well before any documented session lifetime.

Not reproduced deliberately, so the trigger is unknown. Worth checking: whether a concurrent login for the same user revokes sibling sessions, whether a cleanup task prunes UserSession rows on an aggressive schedule, and whether container restart is the only other revoker.

Filed from observation, not diagnosis. The 30-minute figure is approximate and from two data points.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5). Closing because THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS DISPROVEN and its residual is fully carried by enhancedchannelmanager-upkp1, which I opened and verified covers it.

THE TITLE IS WRONG. Nothing revokes anything at 30 minutes. 30 minutes is access_token_expire_minutes, i.e. the first moment a refresh is exercised at all (the frontend's proactive timer fires at 80%, around minute 24, with the reactive 401 path at 30). The 401 requires the client to present a refresh token that is no longer its session's current one, and by minute 30 that token is already stale for a reason that happened earlier.

RULED OUT, with the checks that ruled them out, addressing all three leads the bead named:
- No scheduled task touches sessions. grep over task_registry.py and tasks/ for UserSession returns zero; the only non-route references repo-wide are main.py:980 (startup purge) and a database.py import.
- No sibling-session revocation on login. routes.py:688-707 only inserts. Two independent cookie jars for the same user both refreshed 200 after the other logged in.
- Container restart purges EXPIRED sessions only. RestartCount=0 on the live instance, one startup purge line, 2 expired rows.
- Live read-only SQL: 0 rows where expires_at != created_at + 7 days among never-rotated sessions, so neither cleanup path can touch a fresh session.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED HERE, both on the TTL surface:
- auth/tokens.py create_access_token/create_refresh_token baked in module constants and ignored the configured jwt.access_token_expire_minutes / refresh_token_expire_days, while the cookie max_age, UserSession.expires_at and the access_token_expires_in metadata all read the configured values. A configured refresh lifetime SHORTER than 7 days reproduces this bead's exact 401: expires_at lands before the JWT exp and _cleanup_expired_sessions deletes the row while the cookie still decodes. Longer logs the operator out early, which is this bead's 'logged out well before any documented session lifetime' verbatim. Not the cause on ecm-ecm-1, which runs the 30/7 defaults, but a live footgun on any instance where those were edited.
- rotate_refresh_token minted post-refresh access tokens with a fabricated username claim of user_<id>, which main.py:614 logs verbatim as the acting operator.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM is rotate-on-every-refresh with a 10-second wall-clock grace, and it is a POLICY question the PO asked not to have decided unattended. Moved to enhancedchannelmanager-upkp1 (P1), where QA's 15-second reproduction is recorded along with three options and a recommendation. Also filed from this investigation: enhancedchannelmanager-yhk3r (refresh 401s are logged nowhere, which is why this took 12 days to diagnose), enhancedchannelmanager-67onh (e2e captureStorageState shared across contexts), enhancedchannelmanager-8bqv3 (dead session config), enhancedchannelmanager-1x3yu (the same username fabrication in the uncalled sibling function).

Suggested successor title, recorded in upkp1: a long-running client's refresh token goes stale and the first refresh attempt, at ~24-30 min, 401s.

title: docs/normalization.md documents condition types, action types, error codes and a journal query that do not exist
description:
Found while writing the Normalization user guide section, which deliberately inherited none of it. Six defects, three spot-verified against source by the orchestrator:

1. Condition types wrong (docs/normalization.md:119-125): documents 'equals', which does not exist in backend/normalization_engine.py. Omits 'tag_group' and 'always', which do.
2. Action types wrong (:127-134): documents 'set', which does not exist. Omits the five real ones: strip_prefix, strip_suffix, regex_replace, normalize_prefix, capitalize.
3. 'Flagged' badge documented (:159, :266) but does not exist in the frontend.
4. 422 detail codes are fictional (:151-157): claims regex:nested_quantifier, regex:oversize_bounded_repetition, regex:oversize_pattern, regex:invalid_pattern, regex:runtime_timeout. Real codes are REGEX_TOO_LONG, REGEX_COMPILE_ERROR, REGEX_NESTED_QUANTIFIER. There is no bounded-repetition check at all.
5. VERIFIED: journal category wrong (:200). Doc gives GET /api/journal?category=normalization. Code writes category="channel" at routers/normalization.py:1330, 1389, 1442, so the documented query returns nothing. An operator following this doc concludes normalization wrote no journal entries.
6. Navigation label wrong (:9, :32, :177): says 'Settings -> Normalization Rules'. The real label is 'Channel Normalization' (settingsSections.ts:102-103).

Related, higher-severity, and already covered by enhancedchannelmanager-gk4d0: docs/images/normalization/normalization-test-rules.png is a v0.16.0 capture showing the retired top tab bar (Auto-Creation, Lookup Tables, FFMPEG Builder). Referenced from docs/normalization.md:38.

Note the new user guide section at docs/user_guide/normalization/ is code-verified and does not carry these errors, so this bead is about repairing the older developer-facing reference, not the operator guide.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Drop item 6, the nav label. docs/normalization.md now reads 'Settings > Channel Normalization' at lines 9, 32 and 177, matching settingsSections.ts:102-103, fixed by commit 35031a54c. Items 1 to 5 all still reproduce: doc still lists condition type 'equals' which does not exist and omits tag_group and always; still lists action type 'set' which does not exist and omits strip_prefix, strip_suffix, regex_replace, normalize_prefix, capitalize; the 'Flagged' badge has zero UI hits; the 422 codes are wrong (real ones are REGEX_TOO_LONG, REGEX_COMPILE_ERROR, REGEX_NESTED_QUANTIFIER per backend/regex_lint.py:92-94); and the journal category is 'channel' not 'normalization' (routers/normalization.py:1330, :1389, :1442).

title: Remove em-dashes from all documentation prose and codify the rule in style_guide.md
description:
PO directive: em-dashes are poor sentence structure and should not appear in documentation prose. Swept ~3600 em-dashes across docs/ (user_guide, runbooks, security, sre, design, testing, commands, validation, and top-level docs/*.md), rewriting each sentence rather than substituting another dash. Survivors are limited to verified exceptions: literal app strings an operator would grep for, quoted UI text checked against source, and content inside code fences.

docs/adr/ is deliberately EXCLUDED (932 em-dashes across 12 files). ADRs are dated decision records; rewriting their prose is editing history. PO decision: leave them.

Durability: added a 'Prose Style (Docs and Comments)' section to docs/style_guide.md stating the rule and the four rewrite patterns, so the convention does not regrow. Without that, style_guide.md itself demonstrated 78 em-dashes.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. Follow-up to update those assertions rides with hmr0e.

title: A pipeline dry run reports 'created' in the same words a live run does
description:
Found while writing the pipeline testing tutorial (bead gsnw0.4).

A completed DRY RUN reports its result as, for example:

  126 matched, 124 created, 2 skipped

That is the same vocabulary a LIVE run uses for work it actually performed. Nothing in the result copy marks it as hypothetical — no "would create", no simulated/preview label on the numbers themselves.

The writer verified via list_channels that ZERO channels were actually created, so the behaviour is correct; it is only the wording that is wrong. But an operator reading "124 created" has been told, in plain language, that 124 channels now exist. The natural next action is to go looking for them — or worse, to believe a destructive rule already ran and start undoing it.

The tutorial documents the distinction explicitly, but a doc explaining that the UI means the opposite of what it says is a workaround, not a fix.

SCOPE: give dry-run results their own vocabulary. "124 would be created" is the minimal change; a labelled preview result region is better, since the numbers are the thing people screenshot and share. Whatever is chosen, apply it to every count in the result, not just the headline.

CHECK THE SAME WORDING ELSEWHERE. The rule analyzer, the Dry Run toolbar action and the per-rule Test button all produce simulated results, and Auto-Creation has its own preview path. One ambiguous result string usually means the summary formatter is shared.

Related and worth knowing: this sits next to a real destructive-action surface. The pipeline can create, merge and renumber channels at scale, and the rollback path is a snapshot restore rather than an undo. A result message that reads as "already done" when it is not is a bad thing to have in that neighbourhood.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Partly done. The TOAST is already mode-aware (ChannelPipelineTab.tsx:627 'Dry run complete - Would create N channels') and so is the Event Sync branch (:1355 'would attach' vs 'attached'). Remaining scope is the two surfaces the bead actually cites: the Execution History row's standard non-event-sync branch (:1363-1371, renders 'N matched, N created, N skipped' identically for dry_run and execute) and the Execution Details modal (:1956-1968, 'Streams Matched:' / 'Channels Created:' with no mode awareness while its sibling EventSyncSummaryDetails already takes an isDryRun prop). Reuse the COUNT_LABELS pattern from RestoreCompleteSummary.tsx:104-106.

title: All 7 event_sync screenshots predate the workspace rework and show four removed UI elements
description:
Found while writing the Event Sync quick start (bead gsnw0.5), and confirmed by viewing the image directly.

docs/images/event_sync/*.png (7 images, referenced from docs/event_sync.md) were captured at v0.17.6-0067 and show a UI that no longer exists. Verified in 1-kind-chooser.png:

  - HORIZONTAL TOP NAV across the width (M3U Manager, EPG Manager, Channel Manager, Guide, ...). The app now has a LEFT SIDEBAR; that row is gone entirely.
  - The full "Enhanced Channel Manager" wordmark, shortened to ECM by bead 2896r.20.
  - A FOOTER bar ("Healthy | Service: Enhanced Channel Manager" plus a version), removed during the workspace rework.
  - An "Update available" pill, removed on 2026-07-31 by bead nhkd4 — that notice now arrives in the notification centre.

Plus outdated copy the agent flagged: the Event Sync rule description reads "Preview-only in this phase", where the current wording is "Preview first; manual runs attach".

So an operator following docs/event_sync.md sees screenshots of an application that differs from theirs in navigation, branding, chrome and copy. The instructions may still be broadly followable, but the images actively mislead about where things are.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THESE SEVEN FILES: docs/user_guide/README.md cites docs/images/event_sync/ as the CANONICAL EXAMPLE of the screenshot convention — numbered kebab-case filenames, interleaved between steps. It is the pattern every new tutorial was told to follow. The convention is fine; the images illustrating it are stale. Anyone checking the exemplar sees an old UI.

SCOPE: recapture all 7 against the current UI at 1280x720 dark, per the documented convention, and update any copy quoted in docs/event_sync.md that changed with them. Note docs/images/ is gitignored ("may contain PII") so replacements need git add -f, and the Event Sync screens can expose provider and team-alias data worth checking before capture.

Consider also whether other pre-rework images exist: docs/images/normalization/ is explicitly grandfathered as non-conforming to the convention, but that says nothing about whether it is CURRENT — worth a look while someone is in there.

title: M3U Manager silently renders 5 of 6 accounts — one with a null URL never appears
description:
Found while writing the M3U Manager tutorials (bead gsnw0.6), verified live against the running instance.

The ECM API returns SIX M3U accounts (list_m3u_accounts / get_m3u_account). The M3U Manager UI renders FIVE, consistently, across multiple page loads. The missing one is id=1, name "custom", type Standard, server URL "N/A", status error.

Likely a render skip on a null or unusable URL.

IMPORTANT FRAMING CORRECTION, established after the report: M3U accounts are NOT stored in ECMs journal.db — there is no m3u_accounts table. They live in Dispatcharr and ECM proxies them. So this is not an ECM-owned orphan record; it is ECM dropping an upstream record from a list without saying so.

That makes it a DISPLAY-INTEGRITY problem rather than a data problem, and arguably worse for it: the operator is looking at what they believe is the list of their accounts, and it is quietly incomplete. Nothing on screen indicates a row was withheld. If the account is misconfigured — which "URL: N/A, status error" suggests — the UI has hidden precisely the record the operator most needs to see in order to fix or remove it.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST:
  - Is the skip deliberate (a guard against rendering a row that would crash) or incidental (a map that throws on a null URL and silently drops the item)? Those want different fixes.
  - Does the same skip apply anywhere else that lists accounts — pickers, dropdowns, the Links or Profiles modals? A filter applied in one render path is usually applied inconsistently.
  - Can the operator delete or repair it from ECM at all, or must they go to Dispatcharr? If ECM cannot act on it, saying so on screen is the fix.

DO NOT simply render the row without checking what breaks. If it was skipped because a null URL crashes a downstream component, un-skipping it moves the failure rather than removing it. Render it in an explicit error state, or surface a count mismatch, but establish the original reason first.

Not reproduced independently by me — the account is upstream, and the evidence is the agents live API-versus-UI comparison. Reproduce before fixing.
notes:
RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Both of the bead's open questions are now ANSWERED, which makes this a UX decision rather than an investigation. The filter is DELIBERATE and long-standing: commit 784f08ac (2026-01-02) hid the internal 'custom' account, seven months before this bead was filed, so it is not a regression. It is applied CONSISTENTLY at five sites: M3UManagerTab.tsx:793 and :805, TaskEditorModal.tsx:142, M3ULinkedAccountsModal.tsx:57, StatsTab.tsx:752 and :815. Remaining scope is a single PO call: either surface an explicit '1 internal account hidden' indicator wherever the filter applies, or close as working-as-designed for Dispatcharr's internal custom-streams bucket.
INVESTIGATION 2026-08-13 (read-only). Findings independently re-verified by the orchestrator against source and the live instance.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS WRONG. The skip is not 'a render skip on a null or unusable URL'. It is a deliberate, NAME-keyed guard: M3UManagerTab.tsx:793 '.filter(a => a.name.toLowerCase() !== "custom")'. Introduced 784f08ac (2026-01-02, 'The custom M3U account is used internally but should not be visible'), with four subsequent repair commits (a87aa478, fc0e1c60, 0f0a0584, e58f1bc6). Predates this bead by seven months; not a regression. Nothing in the component gates visibility on server_url; the only server_url reference is presentational masking at :221 behind hideM3uUrls.

WHAT THE ACCOUNT IS: Dispatcharr's built-in bucket for manually-added streams (backend/config.py:246-250). Absent server_url and status=error are its normal steady state, since it has no upstream to fetch. It is NOT misconfigured, which removes the bead's 'hiding precisely the record the operator needs to fix' framing.

RENDERING IT CRASHES NOTHING. M3UAccountRow null-guards every field this account lacks (:221, :190, :174, :227). The bead's warning against un-skipping is not supported by the code.

ESCALATION, and this now outranks the bead as filed. visibleAccountCount (:804-806) applies the SAME name predicate, so it is computed from the already-filtered set and cannot distinguish 'genuinely empty' from 'everything was hidden'. The live instance today returns exactly ONE account and it is the filtered one, so filteredAccounts.length === 0 AND visibleAccountCount === 0, and :969-971 renders the heading 'No M3U Accounts' with body 'Add an M3U account to start importing streams.' The UI asserts an absolute that the API contradicts. Verified directly: dispatcharr_client.get_m3u_accounts() returns COUNT=1, id=1 name=custom status=error max_streams=0.

INCONSISTENCY IS WIDER THAN THE EARLIER NOTE SAID. Seven filtering sites: M3UManagerTab.tsx:583, :608, :793, :805; TaskEditorModal.tsx:142; M3ULinkedAccountsModal.tsx:57; StatsTab.tsx:752. Five list/select surfaces do NOT filter and will offer 'custom': ConditionEditor.tsx:484 (Channel Pipeline provider condition, the sharpest one, a rule can target it), M3UChangesTab.tsx:316, SettingsTab.tsx:1729 (digest multiselect at :4537), StreamsPane.tsx:1806/:1835/:1794. SettingsTab.tsx:918-919 excludes it only incidentally via 'max_streams > 0'; custom has max_streams 0 today, so that exclusion leaks the moment the value changes.

ZERO TEST COVERAGE. Grep for 'custom' across M3UManagerTab.test.tsx, M3ULinkedAccountsModal.test.tsx, StatsTab.test.tsx yields one hit, an unrelated custom_properties fixture. A seven-site load-bearing predicate with four historical repair commits is pinned by nothing.

BACKEND CAN ACT, UI OFFERS NO AFFORDANCE. m3u.py:748 DELETE, :661 PUT, :701 PATCH all take a plain account_id with no name or id guard. The UI cannot reach them only because the row is never mounted.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether Dispatcharr permits deleting its built-in id=1 (needs a mutating call); whether the unfiltered surfaces cause observed misbehavior (custom is offered there, but selecting it was not exercised); why the instance went from six accounts at filing time to one now.

RECOMMENDED SCOPE: (1) fix the empty-state copy, which is a correctness bug rather than a UX preference, and must not say 'No M3U Accounts' when accounts.length > 0 and everything was filtered; (2) extract the duplicated predicate to one shared helper, since seven copies with four repair commits is the mechanism that produced the drift, and StatsTab.tsx:748-752 already extracted it locally for that reason; (3) decide the hidden-account indicator separately and drive it from the shared helper; (4) decide the unfiltered surfaces separately, flagging ConditionEditor.tsx:484 hardest.

title: First-run password hint contradicts the deliberate NIST-based policy the backend enforces
description:
Found while writing the first-run onboarding docs (bead gsnw0.15), and verified in source.

SetupPage.tsx:134 tells a brand-new operator:
  "At least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and number"

backend/auth/password.py enforces something different, and says so in its own module docstring at line 10:
  "No composition rules (uppercase/lowercase/number)"

What is ACTUALLY enforced: 8+ characters, not on the common/breached list (loaded from common_passwords.txt, cited as NIST 800-63B), and not containing the username.

SO THE HINT IS NOT MERELY STALE -- IT CONTRADICTS A DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISION. NIST 800-63B specifically recommends AGAINST composition rules, because they push users toward predictable substitutions (Password1!) while adding little entropy. The backend followed that guidance on purpose. The UI is telling operators to do the thing the policy deliberately stopped requiring.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO: this is the FIRST SCREEN a new operator sees. It is the only password guidance they get, and it is wrong in a direction that makes their password worse rather than better -- and it withholds the two rules that actually protect them (breached-list and username-substring), which they cannot discover any other way until a submission is rejected for a reason the hint never mentioned.

FIX IS NOT JUST DELETING THE COMPOSITION CLAIM. State what is enforced, in a way that helps: minimum length, that common and previously-breached passwords are rejected, and that the password cannot contain the username. That turns a misleading hint into useful guidance.
