Check whether the same wording appears anywhere else -- the password-change form and any account-creation surface in Settings are the obvious candidates, and one wrong hint usually means it was copied.

The docs written under gsnw0.15 state the ACTUAL enforced rule and flag the UI hint as stale, so the documentation and the UI currently disagree until this lands.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. TWO sites, not one: frontend/src/components/SetupPage.tsx:134 AND frontend/src/components/ResetPasswordPage.tsx:186 carry the identical wrong hint string. Also record, do not fix here: backend/auth/settings.py:55-59 declares min_password_length, require_uppercase, require_lowercase, require_number and require_special, and only min_password_length is ever read (auth/routes.py:1475, :1507-1508), and even that is not wired into validate_password(). Those composition flags are operator-toggleable dead config. Do not let the hint fix imply they work. Bead 034dn closed as a duplicate of this one; its empirical repro was a lowercase-only password accepted on a fresh install.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5). Verified against backend/auth/password.py:113-153 directly rather than trusting the bead's summary.

All sites now read: 'At least 8 characters. Common and previously breached passwords are rejected, and it cannot contain your username.'

THREE sites, not the two the NOTES listed: SetupPage.tsx:134, ResetPasswordPage.tsx:186, and UserMenu.tsx:308 (the change-password modal), which said only 'Minimum 8 characters' and so withheld both protective rules. The bead predicted a third copy existed without naming it.

VERIFIED LIVE by QA against POST /api/auth/setup on a disposable stack: a lowercase-only 13-character password not on the breached list is ACCEPTED (201), which is the NIST 800-63B policy working as designed; 'password' is rejected 422 as too common; a 7-character password is rejected for length; a password containing the username is rejected. So the UI hint and the enforced policy now agree in both directions.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED, as the NOTES instructed, and now filed:
- enhancedchannelmanager-8bqv3: the composition flags in auth/settings.py are operator-toggleable dead config, persisted to auth_settings.json and read by nothing.
- enhancedchannelmanager-xztoc: backend/reset_password.py, a standalone CLI, enforces the uppercase/lowercase/number rules the rest of ECM deliberately dropped. Same defect class as this bead in a second implementation, which mkocf's description never mentioned.

title: POST /api/settings/test has no admin gate and is reachable by the MCP API key
description:
Found while fixing GitHub #754 (commit 9d0220a0). NOT changed in that commit, deliberately.

POST /api/settings/test carries NO route dependency. The Emby, Plex and Jellyfin test-connection endpoints all carry RequireAdminIfEnabled; this one does not. So it is reachable by any authenticated caller, INCLUDING the static MCP API key, which auth_middleware accepts directly (backend/main.py:548).

That matters because bead kgz3k specifically gated the MCP key OUT of changing outbound URLs on save. The save path is gated; this endpoint reaches the network with operator credentials and is not.

WHAT IT DOES: POSTs the operator-supplied username and password, or GETs with X-API-Key, to the host named in the request, and echoes the upstream status back to the caller.

RESIDUAL RISK AFTER 9d0220a0 IS LOWER BUT NOT ZERO. That commit routed this endpoint through the shared SSRF chokepoint, so it can no longer be pointed at cloud metadata or outside the permitted band. What remains is internal port scanning WITHIN the permitted band under lan_friendly, plus a status-code oracle, driven by a principal the codebase already treats as untrusted for this class of change. Assessed Medium (~5.3) before the chokepoint landed; Low-Medium now.

DO NOT JUST ADD RequireAdminIfEnabled WITHOUT CHECKING THE FIRST-RUN PATH. The setup wizard may legitimately call this endpoint before any admin account exists — that is why it was left alone rather than gated in the same commit. Establish whether first-run needs it, and if so whether the gate should be conditional on setup being complete, the way RequireAdminIfEnabled already is for other routes.

Also worth checking as part of the same pass: whether any OTHER route reachable by the MCP key performs outbound requests with stored credentials. One ungated sink usually means the pattern was not applied uniformly rather than that this one endpoint was special.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Widen to all FOUR ungated sinks, not one: POST /test (settings.py:1289), test-smtp (:1474), test-discord (:1574), test-telegram (:1627). All reach the network with operator-supplied or stored credentials and all are reachable via the MCP API key path (main.py:565-571). The correct pattern is already in the same file at :1802-1806 (RequireAdminIfEnabled). The bead's stated first-run blocker is RESOLVED: post-qg14z the wizard hands off to login, and the only caller is SettingsModal.tsx:112, reached after authentication. The SSRF half is already fixed by bead 0yh70 / GH #754, do not redo it.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #849, merged to dev as 97d59a3f, published and verified: check_publish.py confirms ghcr.io/motwakorb/enhancedchannelmanager:dev carries 0.18.1-0089 built from a successful run of that commit.

9ej7f: GET /api/settings now depends on _resolve_settings_admin, the same predicate that already gated WRITE on these fields, and returns an empty value for discord_webhook_url, telegram_bot_token and telegram_chat_id to a non-admin or the MCP service principal. Empty redaction was chosen over a masked tail because SettingsTab round-trips these values and update_settings writes the webhook literally with no preserve-on-omit, so a placeholder would have overwritten a live webhook on a non-admin's next save.

i4qrp: the four settings test endpoints (/test, /test-smtp, /test-discord, /test-telegram) now carry RequireHumanAdminForOutboundTest.

9kwzp.6: four more sinks gated (alert-methods/{id}/test, m3u/digest/test, cloud-targets/{id}/test, cloud-targets/test). POST /api/settings/restart-services gained the ordinary admin tier and deliberately still admits the MCP key, pinned by a test.

9kwzp.7: emby, plex and jellyfin test-connection moved off RequireAdminIfEnabled, which does NOT refuse the MCP key because _build_mcp_service_principal sets is_admin=True. Full per-site audit recorded in backend/tests/test_admin_gate_inventory.py, which walks the live FastAPI dependency tree and asserts both the 14-route MCP-denied set and the 79-route admitted set exactly.

Follow-ups filed and NOT fixed here: 9kwzp.8 (P1, mcp-api-key endpoints carry no auth at all), 9kwzp.9 (backup read path leaks two of the three redacted fields), 9kwzp.10 (four remaining gate inconsistencies), nkwh0.1 (the secrets-ratchet fixture trap hit while shipping this).

title: IntersectionObserver test mocks drop the options argument, so rootMargin and threshold are never exercised
description:
Surfaced by CodeQL js/superfluous-trailing-arguments (#1826) on PR 756, pointing at StickySectionNav.tsx:103. The production call is CORRECT -- new IntersectionObserver(callback, options) is the spec signature. What CodeQL actually resolved is the test double:

  frontend/src/test/setup.ts:83   constructor(_callback: IntersectionObserverCallback) {}
  frontend/src/components/StickySectionNav.test.tsx:7  class IntersectionObserverMock { observe() {} ... }

Both accept ONE parameter. The options object is silently discarded.

WHY IT MATTERS. StickySectionNav passes { root, rootMargin: -72px 0px -65% 0px, threshold: 0 }. That rootMargin is not decoration -- it is what makes the section rail highlight the right entry, by shrinking the observation band to the top of the viewport so a section counts as active when it reaches the header rather than when it merely enters the page. The mock throws it away, so every unit test of the rail active-state runs against an observer with default margins.

The setup.ts mock also declares root, rootMargin and thresholds as readonly fields with empty defaults, which means a test reading them back gets the defaults rather than what the component asked for. A test asserting on those today would pass while proving nothing.

NOT A PRODUCTION BUG, and not a merge blocker -- it is a test-fidelity gap. Worth fixing because the rail active-state behaviour is exactly the kind of thing that looks fine in unit tests and wrong in the browser, which is the failure mode this project spent a whole session correcting.

FIX: have both mocks accept and record (callback, options), expose the recorded options, and let tests assert what the component requested. Consider whether the two mocks should be one shared double -- having a second, weaker copy inside a single spec file is how they drift.

Then check whether any existing rail test would change meaning once the options are honoured. If a test passes only because the margins were defaulted, that is the finding, not a chore.

title: Worktrees have no .venv, so backend pytest silently uses the wrong interpreter
description:
Found during bead work on PR 756. /home/lecaptainc/ecm/wt-newui has no .venv, while docs/testing.md mandates the project venv because the system interpreter has a cryptography version that skips TLS tests.

An agent running "cd backend && python -m pytest" inside a worktree therefore gets the system interpreter and a suite that SKIPS tests rather than failing -- 13 skips that read as normal. The agent on this task noticed and used the main checkout .venv explicitly, but only because it read the testing doc first.

FIX: either have scripts/worktree-bootstrap.sh create or symlink the venv, or make the test invocation resolve the interpreter itself and fail loudly when it is the wrong one. The second is stronger -- a missing venv should be an error, not a quieter test run.

Related trap in the same area, worth documenting alongside: a single-file pytest run trips --cov-fail-under=56 from pytest.ini, so targeted runs need --no-cov. Not a defect, but it costs everyone the first time.

docs/shipping.md has a "Worktree quirks" section that is the natural home for both.

title: Frozen sidebar geometry constants are duplicated across 11 sites in three files
description:
Backlog candidate identified while fixing the release-matrix failure on PR 756 (commit 65a3d16a). Not done, deliberately.

The frozen rail widths 68 (collapsed) and 244 (expanded) are hard-coded in at least eleven places:
  e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts -- nine sites (around lines 26, 888, 898, 901, 1693, 1806, 1873, 2137, 2210)
  e2e/frozen-chrome.spec.ts -- the pinned expected width
  scripts/verify-operator-workspace-release-artifacts.mjs -- expectedBoundingWidth

THE COST OF THE DUPLICATION IS ALREADY PROVEN. The verifier drifted from the CSS and nobody noticed, because it derived a client width by subtracting 1 for a border that does not exist. That job had never run against this branch, so the drift sat undetected until the first PR. A single source of truth would have made the drift impossible rather than merely detectable.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THE SAME PASS, and the reasoning should survive: it is a cross-cutting edit to a GREEN frozen-constants guard, made to fix a RED job, by someone who cannot execute either e2e job full matrix locally. Editing nine assertions in a passing suite on faith to fix a different suite is how a one-line fix becomes an outage.

There is also a real mechanical obstacle: the verifier is bare-node .mjs and the specs are .ts under Playwright transform, so a shared module cannot simply be imported by both. Options are a .mjs module the .ts side imports, a generated JSON constant, or reading the value from the CSS at test time -- the last being the only one that cannot drift from what renders, and therefore worth considering first.

Whoever takes this should treat "the constant matches the CSS" as the invariant, not "the three files agree with each other" -- three files agreeing on a wrong number is the failure mode that was just fixed.

title: Event-loop-blocking test asserts a 50ms budget and fails on loaded CI runners
description:
FAILED IN CI on PR 756: tests/unit/test_dispatcharr_client_epg_bounds.py::test_large_json_decode_does_not_block_event_loop, "assert 0.7936384010000097 < 0.05". One failure against 8006 passed.

NOT INTRODUCED BY THAT BRANCH. The file is present on origin/dev unchanged, and the branch touches neither the test nor dispatcharr_client.py. Verified by git ls-tree and git diff.

PASSES CONSISTENTLY LOCALLY: 5 of 5 clean runs on the dev host.

THE SHAPE. The test patches json.loads with a slow implementation, starts the decode as a task, then does:

    started = time.perf_counter()
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
    assert elapsed < 0.05

The intent is sound and worth keeping -- it proves a slow decode runs off the event loop rather than blocking it, which is a real property users feel as a frozen UI. But the MEASUREMENT is wall-clock scheduling latency of a 10ms sleep, with a 50ms budget, on a shared GitHub runner. 794ms means the runner was saturated, not that the event loop was blocked. The test cannot distinguish "the decode blocked the loop" from "the whole machine stalled", and those have opposite meanings.

DO NOT fix by raising the budget to some larger number -- that weakens the assertion without making it able to tell the two cases apart, and a big enough number stops proving anything. docs/testing.md also prohibits retry plugins as a fix.

BETTER SHAPES TO CONSIDER:
- Assert the RATIO rather than the absolute: measure a control sleep of the same duration with no decode in flight, and assert the in-flight sleep is not materially worse. A saturated runner slows both, so the ratio stays honest while the absolute does not.
- Or assert the property directly rather than by timing: that json.loads was invoked on a worker thread rather than the loop thread, which is what the code change being guarded actually did.

The second is stronger -- it tests the mechanism instead of a symptom, and cannot be defeated by machine load at all.

IMMEDIATE UNBLOCK for the PR is a job re-run; that is legitimate under the docs/testing.md re-run-twice rule, but it should not be the resolution.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. Follow-up to update those assertions rides with hmr0e.

title: Remove the Channel default settings link from Channel Manager's header
description:
PO request 2026-07-30: get rid of "Channel default settings" in Channel Managers heading area.

It is one entry in ROUTE_HIERARCHY settingsLinks (frontend/src/components/routeHierarchy.ts), rendered by App.tsx:2670 through PageHeader relatedLinks.

SAME REASONING AS BEAD hmr0e, which removed M3U Managers #settings/linked-accounts link and left its rationale inline two entries above this one: Channel Defaults is a standing Settings destination with its own navigation entry (settingsSections.ts:97, id channel-defaults, label "Channel Defaults"), so the header link was a second path to a page that was never at risk of being orphaned. Verified reachable independently before removing.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING, and it is pinned by an existing test. PageHeader.css collapses .page-header-meta when the row has no occupant. Channel Manager was the NEGATIVE case in that rules test (PageHeader.test.tsx, it.each with [m3u-manager, true] and [channel-manager, false]) precisely because it still carried a link. With the link gone its meta row collapses too, so that case flips to true and Channel Manager becomes a second positive rather than the negative control. Whoever changes it should keep a negative case if one still exists, or note in the test that none remains -- a rule with only positive cases stops proving the condition matters.

routeHierarchy.test.ts also pins the full href list and, following hmr0e, pins the REMOVED route by name so a re-add has to argue with a named expectation rather than quietly extending an array. Add the same style of pinned expectation for channel-manager.

After this, the surviving settingsLinks are #settings/channel-pipeline and #settings/m3u-digest.

title: cross-route-css-leak logs in per spec and eats the 5/minute budget the other guards avoid
description:
Observed 2026-07-30 during bead nhkd4. In the seven-guard aggregate run at workers=2, e2e/cross-route-css-leak.spec.ts failed BOTH attempt and retry with "Login failed: Too Many Requests". backend/auth/routes.py rate-limits login at 5/minute per IP.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS IN THE FILE NEXT DOOR. e2e/fixtures/css-guard.ts documents this exact failure class and solves it with captureStorageState() -- capture once in beforeAll, reuse for every test. Three guards are on that plumbing and are immune. cross-route-css-leak logs in itself at :189 and is not, so when it runs in parallel with the others they eat its budget.

Re-run alone 90 seconds later it failed attempt 1 with a DIFFERENT symptom -- a 60s waitForSelector timeout at goToRoute :167 -- and passed on retry, so Playwright reported "1 flaky", exit 0. Two different failure modes in two runs is a spec that cannot be trusted to mean anything when it does fail.

NOT caused by nhkd4: .header-update-available is not in that spec SHARED_SELECTORS.

CANDIDATE FIX: move it onto captureStorageState(), and consider serialising the login-performing guards so the aggregate cannot exceed the limit even if a future spec logs in again. Related to bead enhancedchannelmanager-lpvh0, which is the same rate limit hitting the appPage fixture -- worth fixing together, since both are "a spec logs in more often than the backend allows" and the answer in both cases is capture-once.

Do not raise the rate limit as the fix. It is a real protection and the specs are what is wrong.

title: App.css shadows NotificationCenter's own chrome declarations, two of which were lying
description:
Found during bead 9bpkk. App.css carries three `.header .notification-*` rules at (0,3,0) that fully shadow NotificationCenter.css own declarations at (0,2,0):

  .header .notification-bell .material-icons   -> 20px, shadowing the component 24px
  .header .notification-badge                  -> 10px plus a full pill re-geometry, shadowing the component 11px
  (a third .header .notification-* override)

TWO OF THE THREE WERE FLAT-OUT WRONG about the rendered size. Anyone reading NotificationCenter.css to learn what the bell renders at got 24px; it has always drawn 20px. Bead 9bpkk aligned the dead declarations to what actually draws and recorded why, but the shadowing structure is untouched.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT TRAP FROM BEAD 3vjk2, and the difference is the point. 3vjk2 is a base rule winning a TIE on source order, which wrapping the base in :where() fixes. This is a more specific rule winning outright. No :where() restructuring helps -- a reader has to know App.css exists and out-specifies the component.

WHY IT MATTERS: a component stylesheet that does not describe what its component renders is a trap for every future change to that component, and this session has repeatedly been burned by exactly that gap between declared and rendered.

SCOPE: decide where notification chrome should be OWNED. Either App.css keeps it and NotificationCenter.css carries no chrome declarations at all (with a pointer comment), or the component owns it and App.css drops the overrides. Do not leave both declaring the same properties at different values.

Check whether other components have the same shape -- App.css out-specifying a component stylesheet is unlikely to be unique to notifications.

Any change here moves frozen header chrome, which e2e/frozen-chrome.spec.ts pins at a 45px band. Measure rendered before and after; render-neutrality is the goal unless a value is deliberately being changed.

title: Replace the header Update Available pill with a notification-center entry
description:
PO decision 2026-07-30: remove the "Update available" pill from the header and surface the same information as a notification instead.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY.
- App.tsx:2566-2577 renders an anchor .header-update-available inside .header-actions, gated on updateInfo?.updateAvailable, linking to updateInfo.releaseUrl with a system_update_alt glyph.
- App.css:392-420 styles it, including a max-width media query at :418.
- index.css:361 references it in a comment about #1a1a1a text on accent fills.
- services/api.ts:1068-1173 computes updateAvailable CLIENT-SIDE by comparing currentVersion against a fetched latest version, returning { updateAvailable, latestVersion, releaseUrl }.

THE NOTIFICATION MODEL ALREADY FITS, no schema change needed (backend/models.py:529, api.ts:3168):
  type: info | success | warning | error   -> info
  title / message                          -> "Update available" / version detail
  action_label / action_url                -> "View release" / releaseUrl
  source / source_id                       -> the dedup key, see below
  read / read_at, expires_at               -> dismissal and ageing for free

THE HARD PART IS IDEMPOTENCY, and it is the thing to design first. The version check currently runs on the client and re-evaluates on load. A notification is a persisted row. Naively creating one whenever updateAvailable is true produces a new notification on every page load, every poll, forever -- turning a quiet pill into a spammer. Use source + source_id as an idempotency key (e.g. source="version_check", source_id=<latest version string>) so exactly one notification exists per released version, and creating it again is a no-op. VERIFY the create path actually enforces that rather than assuming it -- read backend/routers/notifications.py:85 and check whether it dedupes, and if it does not, decide deliberately whether to add it there or guard at the call site.

DECIDE AND STATE, do not guess:
- Does the check stay client-side and POST a notification, or move server-side? A client-side check means every open browser races to create the same row; a server-side check means one writer. Read how other notifications in this app are created before choosing -- follow the existing pattern rather than inventing one.
- What happens to an old notification when a NEWER version appears? Superseded, or left as history?
- Should it be type info, or warning when the running version is far behind?

REMOVAL is the easy half: delete the anchor, the App.css block including its media query, and update the index.css comment. Check whether .header-actions still lays out correctly with one fewer child -- bead 57pp3 settled that rows reading order ("what changed" -> "what is running" -> controls) and removing the first element changes it.

Guard both halves: the pill is gone from the header, and a notification is created exactly once for a given version across repeated checks. Prove the idempotency guard red first -- a test that only asserts one notification after ONE check would pass against the buggy version.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

title: Notification center typography is off the P1 scale (16 distinct sizes in one file)
description:
PO observation 2026-07-30: notification center text reads large against the rest of the UI, which moved to the P1 scale this session.

NotificationCenter.css declares SIXTEEN distinct font-size values, mixing units:
  px:  24, 11, 20, 48, 22, 16, 18, 12, 14, 11, 18
  rem: 1rem, 0.9rem, 0.85rem, 0.75rem, 0.8rem

Body text elsewhere is now 13px (bead ul2tp), modal titles 16px (bead 99o0x), and section headings 15px. A panel declaring 1rem (16px) body text and 22px headings sits visibly above all of it.

This is the same defect class as the modal passes and the fix follows their pattern: map each declaration to a P1 role by what the text IS, take the role token, and delete the literal. Roles are in frontend/src/index.css under "Typography Roles": metric 20/600, section 15/600, body 13/400, item-title 13/600, label 13/500, meta 11/400, micro 10/700 uppercase, badge 10/500, modal-title 16/600. Icons: --icon-status 18, --icon-action 16, --icon-badge 14, --icon-empty 64.

WATCH FOR, based on what the modal passes hit:
- 48px is almost certainly an empty-state illustration -> --icon-empty, not a text role.
- 24px on a .material-icons is the base-rule specificity tie documented in bead 3vjk2: a single-class override ties index.css .material-icons at 0-1-0 and LOSES, so a naive fix measures as a no-op. Scope through an ancestor, two classes deep.
- rem values are relative to the root, not the parent, so they do not compound -- but converting one still changes the render and must be measured.
- The notification badge on the bell is separate chrome; e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts FORCE_RENDERs .notification-badge and records its ratio. Do not move it without re-measuring that entry.

MEASURE RENDERED, not declared. The panel is reachable from every route, so cover the ten routes; it is not in the 82-dialog harness. Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 in all three themes.

Guard: e2e/route-typography-scale.spec.ts is the precedent and already walks route text with a ratcheted allowlist. The panel needs to be OPEN to be measured, which the current guard does not do -- decide whether to extend it or add a sibling, and justify.

title: Channel Manager split defaults to 58/42, leaving the streams pane 137px narrower
description:
PO observation 2026-07-30: on Channel Manager the channels pane is visibly larger than the streams pane. Pre-existing, not a regression from this session work.

ROOT CAUSE: SplitPane.tsx:19 declares defaultLeftWidth = 58, and ChannelManagerTab never passes the prop. MEASURED LIVE at 1920x1080 against the deployed build: the grid resolves to 972.078px / 6px divider / 697.922px -- 58.2% against 41.8%. Clamps are minLeftWidth 35, maxLeftWidth 70.

Channel Manager is SplitPane ONLY consumer (grep across frontend/src: one JSX usage, one barrel re-export, the rest are its own files and comments). So the 58 default was never a shared decision -- it was this page ratio, expressed as a component default.

PO DECISION: even 50/50, passed explicitly at the call site rather than by changing SplitPane default. The panes hold comparable amounts of information and neither earns the extra 137px. Drag range unchanged at 35-70%.

SECOND FINDING, reported to the PO and DECLINED for now: the divider position does not persist. SplitPane.tsx:23-27 states defaultLeftWidth is "intentionally an uncontrolled, mount-time default" and holds the width in plain useState with no storage. So dragging the divider is lost on reload or tab switch, which is likely why this has felt wrong for a while rather than being adjusted once and forgotten. The PO chose the ratio fix alone; persistence would need a storage key and a per-route-versus-global decision, and is a separate piece of work if it is ever wanted.

GUARD: ChannelManagerTab.test.tsx mocks SplitPane, so a rendered-width assertion there would only be asserting against the stub. The mock now surfaces defaultLeftWidth and the test pins that the call site passes 50 -- an accidental removal of the prop silently restores the lopsided split. SplitPane own tests already cover that the value is honoured and clamped.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TOUCHES SplitPane NEXT: with the call site now explicit, the 58 default is unreached by any consumer. Either retune it to 50 so the component default matches the only real usage, or leave it and document that it is deliberately not what the app renders. Do not leave it silently divergent.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9); all verified in code, not just in CHANGELOG. 2896r.16: TabNavigation.tsx:125-130 renders the Settings drill-in nav with a 'Back to main navigation' control, regression-tested in TabNavigation.test.tsx (commit 73a02a22). 2896r.17: App.tsx:2601-2617 builds routeHeading from settingsSectionHeading() into PageHeader; in-pane headings removed. 2896r.21: StatsTab.tsx:875 wraps the summary counts in RouteHeaderSlot name='status', portalled into the shared route header (commit 661031f6). cujyo: StickySectionNav.tsx:38 scrollWithinContainer() replaces scrollIntoView so the shell no longer scrolls, with a regression test asserting scrollIntoView is never called. vh6hh: ChannelManagerTab.tsx:552 passes defaultLeftWidth={50} explicitly at the call site. 1bpl8: root-caused — detect-secrets drops VERIFIED_FALSE results via is_ignored_due_to_verification_policies, and the Telegram plugin's verify() is a live network call; 9 of 27 plugins behave this way. ECM's own gate is immune because check_secrets.py:149 and :332 both pass --no-verify. Residual: comment that --no-verify is load-bearing for confidentiality.

title: Checkbox and radio sizes are inconsistent across the app and now oversized against 13px labels
description:
PO observation 2026-07-30: Settings checkboxes read large against their item titles. Confirmed and it is estate-wide, not one page.

MEASURED from the CSS: 70 selector occurrences of input[type=checkbox] / input[type=radio] across the frontend, resolving to SEVEN distinct rendered box sizes:

  16px x 16px    18 rule blocks
  18px x 18px     8
  14px x 14px     7
  1rem            2   (= 16px)
  15px x 15px     1
  0.875rem        1   (= 14px)
  no size        21 blocks  -> user-agent default, ~13px in Chromium

Range is 13px to 18px for the same control. shared/common.css declares 14px; SettingsTab.css declares 18px, which is the page the PO noticed. TaskEditorModal.css alone declares 18px, 16px and 16px in three different blocks.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW. Body text moved to 13px this session -- form controls were put on the body role (bead ul2tp, commit 21a0a584) and modal titles went 18 -> 16 (bead 99o0x). Nothing touched checkbox box sizes, so an 18px box now sits beside a 13px label: the control is 38% taller than the text it labels. The inconsistency pre-existed; the text shrink made it visible.

THE TENSION THAT MAKES THIS NON-TRIVIAL, and it must not be resolved by shrinking alone: WCAG 2.5.8 sets a 24x24 CSS px minimum target size. A 14px checkbox is already well under it. Whether that is a violation depends on whether the label is associated so that clicking the TEXT toggles the control -- if it is, the target is the whole row and the visible box size is a purely visual question; if it is not, the box IS the target and shrinking it makes a real accessibility problem worse. CHECK THIS PER SITE before choosing a number. The answer may be a small visible box with a padded or label-extended hit area.

SCOPE: decide one token (or a small justified set) for the control box, relate it to the body role deliberately rather than by eye, apply it, and delete the seven-way spread. Radios get the same treatment as checkboxes -- the PO named both.

Measure rendered sizes, not declarations: 21 blocks declare nothing and inherit a UA default, and this project has repeatedly been burned by reading CSS instead of the compositor. Cover the ten routes AND the 82 dialogs in the harness -- checkboxes appear in both.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, all three themes (accent-color renders differently per theme and the box is a non-text component under WCAG 1.4.11).

Guard it the way the other typography work was guarded: a rendered-CSS spec with a ratcheted allowlist, proven red first. e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts is the closest precedent -- it already walks every control on every route and measures rendered results rather than declarations.

title: StickySectionNav's MutationObserver never sees a renamed section
description:
Found during bead de6u1, reproduced in a jsdom harness against UNMODIFIED StickySectionNav.

The observer is { childList: true, subtree: true } -- no attributes, no characterData. discover() reads dataset.sectionLabel and heading text, and BOTH change without a childList mutation: React updates a lone text child via nodeValue, and an attribute change is not a childList change. So a renamed section keeps its OLD rail label indefinitely, until some unrelated node happens to be added or removed in the container.

REPRODUCED: data-section-label verified as "Renamed" in the DOM while the rail still showed "Alpha" 300ms later.

REAL CASE: renaming a cross-instance sync target. Its task_name embeds the target name (backend/tasks/dbas_sync.py:736), so the rail entry for that task shows the old name until something else mutates the DOM.

SEVERITY REDUCED BY de6u1, not eliminated. Before that bead the same rename ALSO moved the anchor id, so a shared link broke. Now the id is pinned to task_id and only the visible label goes stale. That is a display bug rather than a link bug -- worth fixing, no longer urgent.

LIKELY FIX: attributes: true with attributeFilter [data-section-label, data-section-id], plus characterData: true. BUT discover() itself writes section.id and adds a class, so re-entrancy needs checking before this lands -- an observer that fires on attribute changes will fire on discover() own writes. Work out the guard before widening the observer, or this trades a stale label for an infinite loop.

The de6u1 rename test asserts the id survives a rename and carries a comment explaining why it deliberately does NOT assert the label.

title: Modal title bars are too tall and the title text is oversized
description:
PO request 2026-07-30: shrink BOTH the modal header band and the title text.

MEASURED across all 82 catalogued dialogs (81 rendered) on 2026-07-30. Header band heights fall into three clusters:

  ~64.8px  x58   the dominant case
  ~56.2px  x9    confirm-style dialogs
  78-80px  x7    task-schedule-add/edit, task-editor, find-duplicates, m3u-filters, auto-sync-settings, m3u-groups

THE BAND IS SIZED BY THE CLOSE BUTTON, NOT THE TITLE. The arithmetic closes exactly:
  --modal-header-padding is 1rem 1.25rem, so 16px top + 16px bottom = 32px
  .modal-close-btn is 32x32
  32 + 32 + 1px border = 65px  -> the dominant cluster
  and where there is no close button: 32 + (18px title x 1.3 line-height = 23.4) + 1 = 56.4px -> the short cluster

CONSEQUENCE THAT SHAPES THE WORK: shrinking the title alone does nothing for 58 of 72 measured headers, because 23.4px of title sits inside a 32px-tall row set by the button. The two requests need different levers:
  BAND  -> vertical padding in --modal-header-padding, and/or the 32x32 close button
  TITLE -> --type-modal-title-size (currently var(--text-2xl) = 18px, weight 600, line-height 1.3)

The 7 tall outliers carry a header subtitle (.modal-subtitle, body role) and want checking separately -- they may be correct at 78-80px rather than defective.

DESIGN QUESTION TO ANSWER, not to assume: 73 h3 elements already render at 15px/600, which is exactly --type-section-size. If modal titles move to 15px they become indistinguishable from the section role, and --type-modal-title-* stops earning its existence as a separate role. Either keep a distinct step (e.g. 16px) and justify it, or collapse the role into --type-section-* deliberately and delete it. Do not silently leave a redundant role behind.

.modal-close-btn is 32x32 with padding 0 and is the canonical .action-btn size in shared/common.css -- check what else depends on that before shrinking it, since it is shared beyond modals.

Do NOT confuse this with the frozen app header band (45px) or the rail, which e2e/frozen-chrome.spec.ts pins. Those are not modal chrome and must not move.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080. Measure with scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs; do not recapture the baseline wholesale (stale, bead j5m9v) and treat its geometry rows as untrustworthy (bead iotbh -- captured mid-animation), so measure geometry animation-free.

title: Pin Scheduled Tasks rail anchors to task_id and close the load-window reflow
description:
PO DECISION 2026-07-30: pin the anchors, accepting the one-time break of links already in circulation. Split out of the ue130 policy analysis; the listing policy itself is settled -- KEEP the per-task rail entries. A 17-entry directory over a 3104px page of homogeneous cards is the only way to reach a given task without scrolling.

TWO PARTS.

1. PIN THE ANCHORS. Today the rail id is slugged from the visible label, so it is settings-scheduled-tasks-section-<slugged-task-name>. Use data-section-id={settings-scheduled-tasks-section-<task.task_id>} instead: human label in the rail, stable id in the URL.

   data-section-id WORKS and is currently unused -- verified at StickySectionNav.tsx:56, where section.dataset.sectionId is checked FIRST and unconditionally. Only the id ATTRIBUTE path discards a settings- prefix. My commit message on 4af8f487 claims Settings cannot pin ids; that claim is wrong and applies only to the attribute path.

   WHY IT MATTERS: task_name is a class constant in backend/tasks/*.py (19 of them), so 17 of the 17 live entries are release constants and portable -- but they break across any rename. The genuinely volatile one is backend/tasks/dbas_sync.py:736, instance.task_name = "Cross-Instance Sync: %s" % target_name: renaming a sync TARGET changes the rail id while task_id stays stable (see the deliberate cached-instance rename at :735).

   ACCEPTED COST: every ...-section-<slugged-name> link already shared stops resolving, once. Those links already break on any rename, so this trades a silent ongoing failure for a single known one.

2. CLOSE THE LOAD-WINDOW REFLOW. This is the plain b32co/mch8j defect, still open here and the worst instance measured. Observed live with /api/tasks delayed 5s: rail 0 -> 17 at t=5.52s, pane height 88px -> 3104px, and the deep link fires late -- container scrolls 77px -> 1993px between t=5.7s and t=6.3s.
   Unlike the other pages there is nothing static to pre-render, because every entry comes from the fetch. So decide deliberately what the loading state should offer: a placeholder set is not obviously right when the count is unknown. Whatever you choose, the rail must not grow from nothing into 17 entries under the readers cursor.

ZERO-TASK CASE NEEDS NO CHANGE, verified: the page renders "No scheduled tasks available", StickySectionNav returns null below two items so no rail renders, and a deep link is a silent no-op at scrollTop 0. That is fine.

GUARD IT the way 22fef24d and 4af8f487 were guarded: fetches left pending for the whole test, rail entries and exact id strings asserted together, proven red first. The pinned ids are a contract now -- assert the exact task_id-derived strings, not a pattern.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

title: isAdmin conflates 'not an admin' with 'auth has not resolved yet'
description:
FLAGGED FROM CODE READING, NOT VERIFIED IN A BROWSER. Treat the defect as unconfirmed until someone reproduces it; the code path is what is being reported.

SettingsTab.tsx:5855-5858 passes isAdmin={user?.is_admin ?? false} to the settings sections. useAuth starts user as null and exposes a SEPARATE isLoading flag which App.tsx never reads. So during the window before auth resolves, user is null, the coalesce yields false, and every isAdmin-gated section takes its !isAdmin branch.

PREDICTED SYMPTOM: a real admin briefly sees "Admin access required" on a cold load, then the page swaps to the admin view once auth settles. On a slow connection or a cold container that window is not small.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FLICKER: the !isAdmin branches are the ones bead enhancedchannelmanager-b32co deliberately left rendering zero section-rail entries, on the reasoning that advertising sections to someone who will never see them would be a lie. That reasoning is correct for a genuine non-admin and wrong for an admin whose auth has not resolved -- the same branch is serving two different situations that want different answers.

FIRST STEP IS REPRODUCTION, not a fix. Delay or slow /api/auth/me (or whichever call useAuth makes) against a private build and watch an admin account load the Settings page at 1280x720. If the flash does not occur, find out what else is gating render and close this. The probe harness from b32co is at <scratchpad>/b32co-settings-nav.mjs and already captures storageState once to dodge the 5/minute login limit (bead enhancedchannelmanager-lpvh0).

IF CONFIRMED: the fix is to distinguish the three states rather than two -- resolving, admin, not-admin -- and render neither branch while resolving. Check every other consumer of user?.is_admin for the same coalesce; one occurrence of this shape usually means it was copied.

title: Decide whether data-gated Settings sections belong in the section rail before their data exists
description:
A POLICY QUESTION, not a defect report. Split out from bead enhancedchannelmanager-b32co so the unambiguous loading-branch bugs could be fixed without waiting on this.

Eight data-gated mounts cover FOURTEEN Settings sections that appear in the rail only once their data arrives:
  the seven m3u-digest sections, plus Last Digest
  Probe History
  MCP Connection and Available Tools
  the per-task cards in ScheduledTasksSection, whose ids are DATA-DERIVED

One goes the other way and is worth deciding first because it is the clearest: Reset Probe State (SettingsTab.tsx:5053) is present at mount and DISAPPEARS while probing. A rail entry that vanishes mid-interaction is harder to defend than one that has not arrived yet.

THE QUESTION. Should a section that genuinely has no data be listed at all? Both answers are defensible and they are not the same answer for all fourteen:
  - LIST IT ALWAYS: the rail is a stable map of the page, positions do not move under the cursor, and every section is deep-linkable. Cost: entries that jump to an empty or absent region.
  - LIST IT ONLY WHEN PRESENT: the rail reflects what is actually on the page. Cost: it reflows as data arrives -- the exact complaint that produced bead mch8j -- and a shared deep link resolves or not depending on the recipient instance data.

The per-task ScheduledTasksSection cards are the sharpest case: their ids are derived from data, so a deep link to one is only meaningful on an instance that has that task. That is arguably correct behaviour rather than a bug, and it may deserve a different answer from the other thirteen.

WHAT THIS BEAD NEEDS FIRST: a recommendation per shape, with the reasoning, put to the PO as a decision -- not an implementation. Do not guess at the policy and start editing. If the answer differs across the fourteen, say so; a single blanket rule is probably wrong here.

Only after the policy is settled does implementation follow, and it should be guarded the same way Stats was: fetches left pending, rail entries and exact id strings asserted together, proven red first.

Context: bead mch8j fixed the Stats analogue (commit 22fef24d), and b32co covers the six Settings sections that are absent during load plus one that is never listed at all. Those are unambiguous. This is the residue that requires a judgement.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Two findings this bead surfaced are DONE and tracked elsewhere: the deep-link scroll re-firing on every items mutation is fixed by the one-shot honouredSection latch at StickySectionNav.tsx:107-121, which names this bead in a comment, and the Reset Probe State P1 spinoff is fixed under bead xg9gp (SettingsTab.tsx:5134, now rendered unconditionally). The bead's actual core ask is UNDECIDED and is the remaining scope: the listing policy for the data-gated mounts, namely Last Digest (SettingsTab.tsx:333), Probe History (:5207), MCP Connection and MCP Available Tools (MCPSettingsSection.tsx:26, :371). Also fold in the MCP tool-count-in-heading id instability, still hardcoded as 'Available Tools (80)'.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
ANALYSIS COMPLETE. Three corrections I verified in source myself: 1. SCOPE WAS 2.3x TOO BIG. The seven m3u-digest sections in this bead are NOT data-gated -- they are loading-gated and were closed by commit 4af8f487. The real residue is SIX mounts, not fourteen: Last Digest, Reset Probe State, Probe History, MCP Connection, MCP Available Tools, and the N scheduled-task cards. 2. MY PREMISE ABOUT THE TASK-CARD IDS WAS WRONG. I wrote that they are data-derived and therefore only meaningful on an instance that has that task. False for 17 of 17 observed: task_name is a CLASS CONSTANT in backend/tasks/*.py (19 of them, e.g. task_name = "EPG Refresh"), so they are release constants identical on every instance of that version. Only backend/tasks/dbas_sync.py:736 -- Cross-Instance Sync: -- is genuinely per-instance, and renaming the target changes the rail id while task_id stays stable. 3. MY COMMIT MESSAGE ON 4af8f487 IS WRONG about Settings not being able to pin ids. Verified at StickySectionNav.tsx:56: section.dataset.sectionId is checked FIRST and unconditionally; only the id ATTRIBUTE path discards a settings- prefix. data-section-id is an unused, working escape hatch. The const-list approach 4af8f487 shipped is one valid solution, not the only one. ALSO FOUND, not previously flagged: MCPSettingsSection.tsx:371 hardcodes

Available Tools (80)

, and the rail slugs the anchor from the heading, so the live id is settings-mcp-settings-section-available-tools-80. Adding an 81st MCP tool silently changes the rail label AND breaks every shared link to that section. Fix by moving the count out of the heading or pinning via data-section-id. TWO THINGS SPLIT OUT: the Reset Probe State case is a P1 of its own (the recovery control is hidden by the condition it recovers from) and is not a listing-policy question at all. And StickySectionNav.tsx:84-92 re-fires the deep-link scroll on EVERY items change, forever -- that mechanism, not the missing sections, is what produces the late yank. 22fef24d removed the cause on Stats; the mechanism is still armed everywhere. RECOMMENDATION ON THE ACTUAL POLICY QUESTION: for the milestone sections (Last Digest, Probe History) neither framed option is right -- make the section unconditional with an empty state, so the rail is stable AND every entry lands on real content. And NO, the rail should not distinguish "exists but empty" from "absent": a greyed entry costs a slot, breaks the rails one invariant that every entry scrolls you somewhere, and adds a state screen-reader users must be taught. That distinction belongs inside the section, where a sentence can carry it.

title: Settings sections vanish from the section rail while loading, and one is never listed at all
description:
Direct analogue of bead enhancedchannelmanager-mch8j, fixed for Stats in commit 22fef24d. Settings is the only other StickySectionNav consumer (SettingsTab.tsx:5892; the enumeration below came from a full repo-wide audit, not a sample).

MECHANISM DIFFERS FROM STATS, and is worse. Stats selects sections by an explicit id allow-list. Settings selects on ".settings-section, [data-settings-section]" with routeKey settings-<activePage>, and generates each id by SLUGGING THE LABEL. So a section with no label has no id at all -- there is nothing for a deep link to name, ever, not merely during a loading window.

SHAPE 1 -- six sections absent entirely during load. Each of these early-return branches contains no element matching the selector, so the section is not merely unlabelled, it is not there. On these pages the rail appears from nothing rather than growing:
  MCPSettingsSection.tsx:124 and :135
  AuthSettingsSection.tsx:89 and :97
  ScheduledTasksSection.tsx:653
  SettingsTab.tsx:4242 (m3u-digest loading and error)

SHAPE 2 -- one permanently label-less section. SettingsTab.tsx:4979, the .settings-section under the probingAll conditional on the maintenance page, has no h2, no h3 and no data-section-label. It is skipped forever and never receives an id. This is not a loading-window bug; it is a section that can never be linked to or jumped to. One-line fix.

FOLLOW THE STATS PATTERN: put both the id and the label on EVERY branch, loading and loaded, not only the loading one. Stats did this deliberately -- with the label only on the loading branch, the loaded branch falls back to its heading text, so renaming that heading silently changes the nav entry when the fetch settles, which is the same defect in a new form. One authority per label.

VERIFIED FALSE POSITIVES, do not re-investigate: TLSSettingsSection (tls-settings-section is a distinct class token and its loaded branch contains no .settings-section either, so that page contributes zero rail entries in every state), NormalizationEngineSection, TagEngineSection, UserManagementSection, LinkedAccountsSection, BackupRestoreSection (its six h3s would qualify if its wrapper carried the class -- worth a separate look, but it is not this bug), AlertMethodsSection, EventSyncTeamAliasesSection. The other 47 .settings-section elements in SettingsTab.tsx are clean: 48 matching elements against 47 in-section headings, with :4979 the single gap.

GUARD IT the way Stats was guarded: a spec that leaves the relevant fetches PENDING for the whole test, asserting both the rail entries and the exact id strings together, since they are one contract. Prove it red first.

NOT IN SCOPE: the fourteen data-gated sections that appear late. That is a policy question with its own bead.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

title: e2e appPage fixture logs in per test and trips the 5/minute rate limit, making most specs unrunnable
description:
e2e/fixtures/base.ts appPage logs in from scratch for EVERY test, and backend/auth/routes.py:520 limits login to 5/minute per IP. So any spec with more than about five tests fails wholesale on HTTP 429 -- not on assertions.

MEASURED, 2026-07-30, on e2e/stats.spec.ts: first run 47 failed / 3 passed; after a four-minute cooldown at --workers=1, 28 failed / 10 passed. Every single failure is an identical "Login failed: Too Many Requests" at base.ts:79. Zero assertion failures in either run.

CONSEQUENCE. Browser-level coverage of most routes is effectively unavailable. An engineer who runs one of these specs sees a wall of red that has nothing to do with their change, which trains people to ignore the result -- and a genuine regression in that spec would be indistinguishable from the rate limit.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPO. The seven rendered-CSS guards are immune because they capture storageState ONCE in test.beforeAll and reuse it across every test in the file -- see e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts:713 and the captureStorageState helper in e2e/fixtures/css-guard.ts. appPage should adopt that pattern rather than the rate limit being raised, which would only move the ceiling.

Consider whether storageState should be captured once per WORKER or once per file, and what that means for tests that deliberately need a fresh session (auth specs). A per-test fresh login is right for a handful of tests and wrong as the default.

Found while trying to get browser-level coverage of the Stats route for bead enhancedchannelmanager-mch8j; the agent fell back to a hand-written probe because of this. Pre-existing and unrelated to that change, and not in the current gate list -- which is part of why it went unnoticed.

title: 101 bare-tag elements in modals render at the 16px root with no font-size declaration
description:
The last population off the 2026-07-30 modal measurement. Passes 1-3 (beads ul2tp, 7bsxj, haf9e) are done; this is what is left.

101 elements across the 82 catalogued dialogs render at the bare 16px root because NO font-size declaration governs them at all: span 42, strong 17, p 16, summary 11, label 5, li 5, dt 3, legend 2. Re-measured after pass 3; an earlier count of ~151 also counted single-class variants that the passes have since resolved.

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT FIX IN KIND, and why pass 3 deliberately excluded it. The other three passes corrected declarations that existed and were wrong -- a control taking the UA default, an icon losing a specificity tie, a rem literal off the scale. Here there is nothing to correct. Someone has to CHOOSE a role for each element, and in many cases add a selector to hang it on, since a bare tag inside a dialog is not addressable without one. Every one of the 101 moves the render. Folding them into pass 3 would have made that pass histogram delta uninterpretable.

APPROACH. Do not blanket-declare a size on the dialog body and call it done -- that would set a size for every descendant including ones the passes just placed deliberately, and it would be invisible to review. Work element by element, decide the role from what the text IS (running text -> body, a label -> label, a definition term -> item-title or label, an inline emphasis -> inherit from its container rather than declare), and prefer giving the container a role over addressing bare tags where the container is the real owner.

Watch for elements that are bare on purpose: a strong inside a paragraph should inherit the paragraph, not take its own size.

Measure before and after with scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs. Do NOT recapture the baseline wholesale -- stale by 30 unreviewed signature changes, bead enhancedchannelmanager-j5m9v. Harness geometry rows are untrustworthy, bead enhancedchannelmanager-iotbh; measure animation-free if you need geometry. Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #827 (merge 06f82a47): targeted semantic modal typography tokens, exact 101-element ownership ledger, and live 82-dialog inventory in required Frontend Tests.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
RESIDUAL FROM THE haf9e SWEEP, recorded here because haf9e is closed and this is the nearest open owner.

frontend/src/components/StreamCreateMenu.css:179 still declares '.stream-create-menu-empty { font-size: 0.8rem; }' un-converted, while its siblings in the same file (.stream-create-menu-item, .stream-create-menu-filter-input) were converted to the type scale in commit 5dda3e44.

Likely invisible to the modal harness because it is an empty-list state the stub-prop harness never triggers, and haf9e's population was a rendered-DOM count. Worth folding into this bead's sweep rather than carrying its own.

title: Second load-dependent vitest flake: PendingMergesPage cancel-51-row-action times out under parallel load
description:
PendingMergesPage.test.tsx > "restores the original paginated view when a 51-row all action is cancelled" timed out at 5s during a full parallel run, then passed 40/40 in isolation and was green on a full re-run. Observed by the 7bsxj icon pass; NOT caused by that change, which is CSS-only.

Same shape as bead enhancedchannelmanager-ur9we (StatsTab section jump nav): load-dependent, passes in isolation, surfaces when the machine is saturated. That one turned out to be a genuine product-adjacent race -- the test asserted synchronously on a DOM that completes over several macrotasks -- and its fix was to await the settled state, not to raise a timeout. Check for the same pattern here before reaching for the timeout.

DO NOT normalise it and do not add a retry; docs/testing.md prohibits retry plugins as a fix.

METHOD THAT WORKED FOR ur9we, reuse it: full-suite runs caught nothing in eight attempts; running the single file in a loop while a full-suite run saturated the machine caught it 2-in-30. Then build a DETERMINISTIC red by deferring the relevant mock resolution past the RTL asyncWrapper macrotask, so before/after is provable rather than statistical.

Never pipe vitest through tail -- the exit code returned is the pipe stage, and the FAIL line scrolls past. That cost this session three times.

Note two flakes of the same shape now suggests a systemic pattern rather than two isolated bugs: assertions taken synchronously after an await that resolves earlier than the DOM settles. Worth a sweep for that idiom once this one is understood.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. Follow-up to update those assertions rides with hmr0e.

title: ScheduledTasksSection is entirely inline-styled, including hardcoded hex colours
description:
ScheduledTasksSection renders with 100% inline styles -- hardcoded #3498db / #2ecc71 and scattered fontSize literals such as 16px -- rather than classes and tokens.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.

1. The hardcoded hex colours bypass the theme entirely. They do not respond to light / dark / high-contrast, and they are invisible to e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts reasoning about tokens. #3498db and #2ecc71 were never contrast-measured against any of the three theme surfaces.

2. The fontSize literals are the author fighting a bug rather than choosing a size. An inline style is the ONE thing that beats the .material-icons base rule without touching specificity, so these literals are very likely a workaround for the 0-1-0 tie documented in bead enhancedchannelmanager-3vjk2 -- someone found that a class rule did nothing and reached for the style attribute. Read them as evidence of that defect, not as deliberate design.

SCOPE: migrate to a stylesheet with P1 role tokens and theme-aware colour tokens. Measure the rendered result in all three themes at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 -- the colours in particular must be measured, not converted by eye, since the current values have never been checked against a contrast floor.

Sequencing note: doing this AFTER 3vjk2 means the icon sizes can be expressed as ordinary class rules. Doing it before means reproducing the inline workaround in CSS, which will then be dormant. Prefer after, or coordinate.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Narrower than filed. Text sizing is ALREADY token-driven: ScheduledTasksSection.tsx lines 133, 167, 186, 207, 226, 240, 253, 264, 347, 355, 386, 387 already reference var(--type-body-size), var(--type-meta-size), var(--type-item-title-size), inline rather than classed but on-scale. Remaining scope: migrate the hardcoded hex colours #3498db and #2ecc71 (lines 76, 86, 286, 288) to contrast-measured theme tokens, and move the residual inline icon-size literals (lines 170, 189, 210, 229, 694, 707) into CSS. A ScheduledTasksSection.css now exists but scopes only .task-status-icon.

title: PendingMergesPage bulk dialog spells its close button .modal-close, so it misses all of ModalBase chrome
description:
The bulk-action dialog in PendingMergesPage uses class .modal-close where every other dialog uses ModalBase .modal-close-btn. It therefore misses ALL of ModalBase close-button styling -- padding, hover, colour -- not merely the icon size.

Found during the 7bsxj icon pass, which sized the icon and deliberately did NOT rename the class: renaming would change chrome that pass never measured, on a dialog it was not scoped to.

FIX: rename to .modal-close-btn and delete whatever local rules were compensating for the divergence. Then MEASURE the dialog before and after -- the point is that the button gains styling it has never had, so "it now matches the others" is the outcome to verify visually and by measurement, not to assume.

Check whether any other dialog in the tree has the same typo-shaped divergence from ModalBase class names; one occurrence of a near-miss class name usually means the pattern was copied.

The dev harness renders this dialog with no backend and no login, so before/after is cheap: scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs --only. Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

title: span.stat-value declares 24px against the 20px metric role, and the two stat strips disagree by 4px
description:
Found by the 7bsxj icon measurement, deliberately kept OUT of that pass because it is a different defect class.

:where(.channel-pipeline-stats) .stat-value { font-size: 24px } WINS and says 24px on purpose. That is a literal disagreeing with the P1 metric role (20px) -- not a declaration failing to render, which is what 7bsxj was about. The fix is a value change, not a selector change, so it needed its own decision.

27 elements across the measured dialogs.

.norm-engine-stat-value already measures 20px, so the two stat strips in the app currently disagree by 4px on what a headline metric looks like. That inconsistency is the user-visible part.

BEFORE CHANGING THE VALUE: .stat-value is a bare class in a page stylesheet, so check for other consumers -- a bare class name in a non-scoped file is exactly the shape that turns a local change into a cross-route one. The cross-route-css-leak guard exists for this and should be consulted rather than assumed.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

title: Restructure the .material-icons base rule so icon overrides can win normally (33 dormant rules)
description:
THE HONEST FIX for the class of defect bead 7bsxj worked around, deliberately deferred by that pass because its blast radius is unmeasured.

index.css sets .material-icons { font-size: 24px } at 0-1-0. Any single-class override on an icon co-class ties it and loses on source order, so the declaration renders as a no-op while looking correct in the stylesheet. Wrapping the base in :where(.material-icons) drops it to 0-0-0 and lets ordinary single-class rules win.

WHY 7bsxj DID NOT DO IT, measured rather than assumed: 33 single-class font-size rules on icon co-classes exist app-wide, ALL currently dormant. Only 11 were in that pass measured scope. Restructuring the base would silently activate the other 22 on routes that pass never measured, at values authored blind and never observed once -- .drop-icon 36px, .error-boundary-icon 40px, three banner icons at 1.625rem. That converts a measured 146-element change into an unmeasured 22-rule one.

PREREQUISITE: a route-wide before/after measurement covering all ten routes, not just the modal harness, so every one of the 33 is observed in both states. Then restructure, and treat any newly-rendering value as a decision rather than an accident -- several were written by authors who never saw them take effect.

RELATED FINDING, now documented in docs/css_guidelines.md: a :where()-scoped rule is (0,1,0) and therefore ALSO loses to the base rule. That had silently defeated :where(.tag-engine-section) .expand-icon, whose color worked while its font-size did not. Anyone attempting this restructure needs to know that :where() on the CONSUMER side does not help; it is the BASE that must be wrapped.

Also fold in on pickup: .norm-engine-btn-icon.small .material-icons is now redundant with .norm-engine-btn-icon .material-icons (both 16px) after 7bsxj.

title: docs/testing.md flake baseline is stale by ~1400 tests and now known-wrong
description:
docs/testing.md section "Known baseline flakes (as of 2026-04-20)" records "Frontend (vitest): zero flakes. 1118/1118".

The suite is now 2481 tests across 179 files, and a genuine flake existed in it -- StatsTab section jump nav, filed as bead enhancedchannelmanager-ur9we and fixed. So the line is wrong on both the count and the claim, and it is the line an engineer reads when deciding whether an intermittent failure is known or new. A stale "zero flakes" makes every real flake look like a fresh regression, which is the opposite of what the section is for.

Scope: refresh the counts, record the ur9we flake and its resolution, and state the date the baseline was actually re-measured rather than carrying 2026-04-20 forward. Consider whether the section should record RESOLVED flakes at all -- a list of "things that used to flake and why" is more useful to the next person than a bare zero, and it is how ur9we got diagnosed quickly once observation 1 had a name.

Not actioned during the ur9we fix because another agent held docs/testing.md at the time (bead enhancedchannelmanager-ae3ms, since committed as 52f20944).

title: Stats section-nav pops in as panels load, and a deep link to the bandwidth section cannot resolve
description:
USER-FACING, found while diagnosing the StatsTab flake (bead enhancedchannelmanager-ur9we). The flake was a test problem and is fixed; this is the product behaviour underneath it, which is not.

StickySectionNav discovers a section only once it exposes an h2/h3 or a data-section-label. Of the seven always-mounted Stats panels:

  EnhancedStatsPanel.tsx:96   loading branch HAS data-section-label
  Providers / User Watch Time / Provider Stream Usage   render their h3 on first paint
  BandwidthPanel.tsx:63       loading branch has NEITHER id NOR heading
  PopularityPanel.tsx:100     id, no heading
  WatchHistoryPanel.tsx:96    id, no heading

CONSEQUENCE 1: in a real browser the "On this page" list is incomplete on first paint and entries pop in one at a time as each panel finishes fetching. On a slow instance that is a nav that visibly reflows under the cursor.

CONSEQUENCE 2, the sharper one: BandwidthPanel drops its id entirely while loading, so a deep link to ?section=stats-section-bandwidth-panel cannot resolve during the load window. The anchor the URL names does not exist yet. Anyone sharing that link hands the recipient a scroll target that silently does nothing.

FIX: give all four loading branches both id and data-section-label, so the nav is complete and stable from first paint and every section anchor exists for the whole lifetime of the page. EnhancedStatsPanel already shows the pattern.

This also deletes the race class the test fix worked around -- with a stable nav from first paint there is no window in which the nav exists but is incomplete.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080. Worth checking whether any other route uses StickySectionNav with the same loading-branch shape; Settings does use it.

title: Dialog-side control regression is unguarded by control-typeface.spec.ts
description:
e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts (wired into test:css-guards by bead enhancedchannelmanager-ae3ms) walks PRIMARY_ROUTES with no modal open -- both its face arm and its UA-default-size arm. The ul2tp pass fixed 516 dialog-side elements across 77 of 81 catalogued dialogs that were rendering at the Chromium UA default control size; none of that population has an automated regression guard. A future dialog-scoped rule such as .modal-container button { font-size: initial } would slip past every guard in this set and only be caught by luck.

FEASIBILITY. frontend/modal-harness.html (built via vite.harness.config.ts, gitignored .modal-harness-dist/) force-renders every catalogued dialog with stubbed data -- no backend, no login. scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs already drives it to walk all 82 dialogs and supports --diff. The dialog list is derived from source (src/devHarness/dialogCatalog.ts), and src/devHarness/harnessCoverage.test.ts fails the build if a new dialog is not catalogued -- so a new dialog cannot be silently missed.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. A Playwright spec, or a script reusing the harness the way measure-modal-typography.mjs does, that opens each catalogued dialog via modal-harness.html and reapplies control-typeface.spec.ts two measurement methods -- advance-width face comparison, UA-default-size comparison -- to elements inside the dialog root, with the same ratcheted-allowlist discipline (ALLOWED_DIFFERENT_FACE / ALLOWED_UA_DEFAULT_SIZE) so an allowlist cannot rot. Decide at pickup whether this joins test:css-guards: it needs no backend, unlike most of that aggregate, so it may deserve its own no-backend script family. Add its docs/testing.md row when it lands.

DO NOT build this against a real ECM instance to reach the dialogs. The harness is the whole point -- most dialogs are unreachable on a live instance without the right data (no pending merges, empty review queues, no probe results), which is why the harness exists.

Owning bead: enhancedchannelmanager-ae3ms item 3.

title: control-typeface.spec.ts is in no npm script and no doc, and two guard docs cite a file that does not exist

title: Modal harness geometry rows are captured mid-animation and cannot be trusted
description:
scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs captures each dialog while ModalBase.css modal-container-slide-in is still running -- 0.2s, scale(0.98) -> scale(1). Every box in a capture is therefore multiplied by a run-dependent scale factor, so the geometry arm reports phantom movement in BOTH directions on any change.

THE TELL, from the ul2tp pass: a 32px close button reads 31.80 in one dialog and 31.94 in another IN THE SAME RUN. The raw geometry diff for a change that can only shrink type by 0.33px showed 214 of 281 boxes changing by plus or minus 1-11px, in both directions.

This makes the geometry arm actively misleading, not merely noisy: an engineer reading it would see dozens of layout regressions that do not exist, and a real one-off regression would be indistinguishable from the noise.

TYPOGRAPHY ROWS ARE UNAFFECTED -- font-size/weight/family are not scaled by a transform. The before/after typography comparisons this instrument has produced remain valid.

FIX: finish document.getAnimations() before COLLECT, or add a --no-animation flag that sets a reduced-motion / animation-none override before measuring. The e2e guards already have a FREEZE_ANIMATION helper worth reusing rather than reinventing.

The ul2tp pass worked around this by re-measuring animation-free with both states in one page load; that workaround lives only in that agent scratchpad and should be replaced by a fix in the instrument.

Bead enhancedchannelmanager-xhldy owns the harness.

title: Intermittent vitest failure observed twice on newui, not yet identified
description:

Recording that honestly rather than assuming it was the StatsTab one.

WHAT TO DO: run the suite repeatedly capturing full output to a file (never pipe vitest through tail, which discards the FAIL line -- and note that piping also makes the shell report the pipe stage exit code rather than the runner exit code, which bit this session on pytest as well). Identify the test, then find the actual race rather than adding a wait. Do NOT reach for vitest --retry or equivalent; docs/testing.md prohibits retry plugins as a fix.

A plausible starting point from the run output: the StatsTab-family tests emit repeated warnings of the form "No getStreams / getProbeHistory / getProbeProgress export is defined on the ../../services/api mock", plus two "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading status)" stack traces. comments.text:
OBSERVATION 3 (orchestrator, 2026-08-10, CI on PR #813 / branch fix/ux-batch-0058). This one IS captured, unlike observation 2.

  FAIL src/components/StickySectionNav.test.tsx
    > StickySectionNav - the deep link fires once per navigation (bead ue130)
    > re-arms when the URL names a different section
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times

Run: github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/actions/runs/31418715553/job/93554019711, job 'Frontend Tests', step 'Unit tests with coverage (blocking)'. Result: 197 files passed / 1 failed, 2690 tests passed / 1 failed.

DOES NOT REPRODUCE LOCALLY on the same tree:
  - 5 consecutive isolated runs of StickySectionNav.test.tsx: 5 passed, 0 failed
  - full suite with coverage, matching CI's test:ci command: 198 files / 2691 tests, ALL PASSED, including this exact test

So it is environment-dependent rather than order-dependent-and-local. CI runners are slower and more contended than this host, which fits the timing-sensitive shape.

WHY THIS SHARPENS THE PATTERN. Observation 1 was StatsTab.test.tsx > section jump nav > always lists the always-mounted panels. This is StickySectionNav.test.tsx > the deep-link re-arm. Different files, SAME DOMAIN: section-nav discovery and deep-link firing. The bead's standing hypothesis that observations 1 and 2 are the same test is probably too narrow; the better framing is that the section-nav test family is timing-sensitive as a group.

Both failing assertions are about a callback firing an expected number of times, which is the classic shape of a test racing an effect rather than awaiting it. StickySectionNav uses a MutationObserver plus scroll effects, and its tests assert call counts on vi.fn() spies.

RULED OUT as the cause: the branch under test renames .section-title to .panel-caption in StatsTab, which looked like a plausible culprit given bead 0y596 ('StickySectionNav's MutationObserver never sees a renamed section'). It is not implicated. StickySectionNav discovers sections via section.querySelector('h2, h3') - element tags, not that class - and fix/ux-batch-0058 does not touch StickySectionNav.tsx or its test at all.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: run the section-nav family under artificial CPU contention rather than on an idle host. All three observations are consistent with an effect not having flushed before the assertion, and none reproduce on an unloaded machine.
