title: Un-tokenised em-relative font sizes across the modal estate (~254 elements)
description:
MEASURED over all 82 catalogued dialogs on 2026-07-30. Every off-scale fractional size resolves to an em multiple of the 16px root, which is what identifies them as relative-unit declarations the P1 sweep never converted:

  14.4px = 0.9em    44 elements, 17 dialogs
  13.6px = 0.85em  108 elements,  6 dialogs
  12.8px = 0.8em    54 elements,  9 dialogs
  12px   = 0.75em   26 elements,  7 dialogs
  11.2px = 0.7em    10 elements,  4 dialogs
  9.6px  = 0.6em     3 elements,  3 dialogs
  19.2px = 1.2em     6 elements,  1 dialog
  15.2px = 0.95em    3 elements,  3 dialogs
  48px               1 element  (preview-stream)

Concentrated in: dummy-epg-profile, selection-action-bar, stream-create-menu, channels-pane-renumber-all, history-checkpoint-name, group-multi-select-dropdown, dummy-epg-channel-picker, and the Channel Pipeline dialogs (cp-rule-builder-modal, cp-import-dialog, cp-export-dialog, cp-delete-confirm).

Named signatures include input.search-input, span.collapsible-title, span.collapsible-summary, span.event-sync-pattern-label, button.type-button, button.selection-bar-btn, button.selection-bar-menu-item, button.stream-create-menu-item, span.channel-picker-name, p.user-modal-hint, button.filter-dropdown-action, input.time-input, plus a number of bare h3/span/div/button rules.

SEPARATE FINDING IN THE SAME MEASUREMENT, decide whether it belongs here or in its own bead: ~151 elements render at the bare 16px root with no font-size declaration at all -- bare span (42), strong (17), p (16), summary (11), label/section-label (11), li (5), dt (3). These are untokenised text inheriting the root, not em declarations, so the fix is different in kind.

CAUTION: an em value is relative to its own parent, so converting one to a token changes what any nested em resolves against. Check for nesting before converting, and convert outermost-first.

PO decision 2026-07-30: SEPARATE pass from the control font-size reset (bead enhancedchannelmanager-ul2tp) and the icon-token pass (bead enhancedchannelmanager-7bsxj).

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080. Do not recapture the modal-typography baseline wholesale -- already stale by 30 unreviewed signature changes (bead enhancedchannelmanager-j5m9v).

title: Modal icons render at the 24px base, not the icon tokens (146 elements, 30 dialogs)
description:
MEASURED over all 82 catalogued dialogs on 2026-07-30: 146 elements render at 24px across 30 dialogs. Carried by span.material-icons (73) plus six variants -- span.circuit-breaker-icon.material-icons (10), span.material-icons.norm-engine-expand (9), span.event-sync-exclusion-icon.material-icons (9), span.material-icons.norm-engine-icon (5), and others. Also in this bucket: span.stat-value (27), which is text rather than an icon and is off the metric role (20px).

24px is the base .material-icons rule in index.css. The icon tokens --icon-status (18), --icon-action (16) and --icon-badge (14) never reach these elements.

THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY DIAGNOSED and is the reason this is not a simple find-and-replace: a single-class override such as .norm-engine-icon ties the base .material-icons rule at 0-1-0 specificity and LOSES on source order. Anyone "fixing" this by adding single-class rules will produce declarations that measure as no-ops. The fix has to either raise specificity deliberately, scope through a real ancestor, or restructure the base rule -- pick one and write down why.

Do NOT reach for !important as the mechanism.

Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080. Icon size changes move row heights; the harness records per-dialog geometry including rowHeights per selector -- diff it and report anything that newly clips or wraps.

PO decision 2026-07-30: this is a SEPARATE pass from the control font-size reset (bead enhancedchannelmanager-ul2tp) and from the em-unit pass, because each moves layout differently and should be eyeballed on its own.

Do not recapture the modal-typography baseline wholesale -- it is already stale by 30 unreviewed signature changes (bead enhancedchannelmanager-j5m9v).

title: Form controls render at the UA default font-size (13.3333px) in 77 of 81 dialogs
description:
MEASURED, not inferred: scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs over all 82 catalogued dialogs (81 rendered) on 2026-07-30. 516 elements render at 13.3333px, in 77 of the 81 dialogs. That value is the user-agent default for form controls, 0.8333 x 16px root. Carried by: bare input (152), button.action-btn (139), button.modal-close-btn (65), button.action-btn.danger (27), option (12), button.action-btn.delete (9), across 48 distinct selector signatures.

THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE TYPEFACE ONE, ONE PROPERTY OVER. index.css gained

  button, input, select, textarea { font-family: inherit; }

because browsers do not inherit font-family into form controls. They do not inherit font-size either, and that half was never done. So every control in the app renders at a size nobody chose, and the P1 type scale stops at the control boundary.

THE GUARD IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO IT. e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts measures the RENDERED face by canvas advance width and compares a control against its nearest text-bearing ancestor. It deliberately holds size and weight FIXED at 16px/400 while measuring, precisely so only the family can move the number. That makes it correct for what it asserts and incapable of ever seeing this. It is green today with 516 mis-sized controls on screen.

SCOPE.
1. Add  to the existing reset in frontend/src/index.css. Consider  in the same breath and decide deliberately -- do not add it by reflex, controls and text have different vertical rhythm needs.
2. Extend e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts (or add a sibling) to assert the rendered SIZE against the surrounding text as well as the face. Keep the existing ratcheted-allowlist discipline: fail on a NEW violation and on a STALE entry. Guard first, then land the change, per the PO's standing rule.
3. Re-measure with scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs and report the before/after histogram.

EXPECT GEOMETRY MOVEMENT. Control text growing from 13.3333px to the inherited value changes button and input intrinsic widths and heights in ~77 dialogs. The harness records per-dialog geometry (container/header/body/footer, rowHeights per selector) -- diff it and report anything that newly clips or wraps. Validate at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 per the PO's standing requirement.

The modal-typography baseline is ALREADY STALE by 30 unreviewed signature changes (bead enhancedchannelmanager-j5m9v). Do not recapture it wholesale as part of this work -- that would silently ratify them.

Scope item 1 should read: "Add font-size: inherit to the existing reset in frontend/src/index.css. Consider line-height in the same breath and decide deliberately -- do not add it by reflex, controls and text have different vertical rhythm needs."

comments.text:
Landed in wt-newui (uncommitted; parent verifies/commits).

RESET (frontend/src/index.css, beside the font-family reset):
  button, input, select, textarea { font-family: inherit; font-size: var(--type-body-size); }

  RED before (and again with the final spec, reset reverted): 274 controls / 46 signatures.

included -- the rail and header band did not move.

title: operator-shell.spec.ts: 4 failures from the e2e_test account's missing M3U-changes permission, plus one assertion below the supported viewport floor
description:
Four failures in e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts, all pre-existing. The 70u0r.1 agent controlled every one against the DEPLOYED container build (which lacks its change) and all four fail identically there, so none is caused by the Lookup Tables removal.

Cause 1 (three failures): the e2e_test account lacks the M3U-changes permission on this instance, so the route renders 'You don't have permission to view M3U changes' and the Refresh button the spec looks for never exists. Affects 'all primary route consumers' at both viewports, 'collapsed navigation recovers width', and '200% equivalent'.
This is an environment/fixture defect, not a product defect -- but it means three assertions have been passing vacuously or failing noisily for as long as the account has been short that permission, and the spec cannot tell the two apart. Fix by granting the permission in the e2e fixture setup, and make the spec fail loudly if the permission is missing rather than reporting a UI defect it cannot see.

Cause 2 (one failure): a sticky-overlap assertion at 640x360. Both 1280x720 and 1920x1080 pass. 640x360 is far below the PO's stated 1280x720 minimum supported viewport and mobile is explicitly not a target -- but note browser zoom shrinks the CSS viewport, so a 1280px screen at 200% (WCAG 1.4.4) is a 640px CSS viewport. Decide deliberately whether 640x360 is out of scope or is the 200%-zoom case in disguise; do not simply delete the assertion. See beads 79uf8 and hw8e3 for the same trap already hit once this session.

title: Modal typography baseline is stale relative to the committed tree (30 unreviewed signature changes)

title: Record the opacity-as-de-emphasis rule in css_guidelines.md and fix the error-text instance
description:
Three confirmed contrast failures this session trace to one idiom, and ~160 non-state opacity declarations exist across the frontend CSS, so the pattern will keep producing them until it is written down.

The rule (proposed by the dlavh follow-up): opacity de-emphasises the whole composited group, so it lowers contrast against the PAGE, not against the element's own surface. Use it only where the floor does not apply -- decorative illustrations, :disabled. Where the de-emphasised thing is text, or is a control's only glyph, express the de-emphasis with an ink token instead and record the measured ratio.

The three instances, and why they resolved differently -- the guidance should carry this distinction, because it is what WCAG 1.4.11 turns on:
• .probe-group-btn -- icon-only control, no adjacent label, glyph IS the affordance. FIXED by raising opacity (bead dlavh).
• Stats .no-streams .material-icons -- 64px illustration with 'No active streams' set directly beneath it, identifies nothing the words do not. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED; raising it would undo an intentional de-emphasis to satisfy a floor that does not apply.
• PreviewStreamModal -- .preview-stream-error p at opacity .9 and .error-details at .7. UNFIXED and the sharper case: this is a foreground de-emphasis applied to error text the operator must read. Fix this one as part of the bead.

Cross-reference bead 0zq1p: the measurement core mis-composites exactly this idiom, so anyone reading a recorded ratio for an opacity site needs to know which core measured it.

                                   -> no opacity  4.74 / 5.01 / 4.70  passes

The dlavh agent left it alone for the right reason: it needs an expanded channel with streams to render, and this instance has none, so it could not be measured live and fixing blind is the exact declared-vs-rendered failure this project has been correcting all session.

BUT the guard already has the facility. FORCE_RENDER (contrast-aa.spec.ts:209) mounts data-dependent markup into a host element, and deliberately skips injection when the real thing is already present, so it cannot double up. It currently carries one entry (.notification-badge). Add .probe-stream-btn's markup so the site becomes measurable, THEN measure, THEN set the value -- guard first, then land the change, per the PO's standing rule.

Do NOT copy 0.75 across on the assumption it transfers. The backdrop differs (stream row vs group row), and it must be measured in all three themes at both viewports. Note the sweep that produced 0.75 was run under the buggy measurement core (bead 0zq1p) -- 0.75 clears 3:1 under both the current and the corrected core, but this site's value must be chosen under the corrected one.

title: contrast-aa measurement core accumulates opacity in the wrong direction
description:
e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts chainOf() walks upward from the measured element to documentElement, multiplying a running cumulative by each node's opacity and stamping that running value onto EACH layer as it goes. So an ancestor's background layer is painted at the product of all opacities BETWEEN it and the measured element, including the measured element's own. That is inverted: the opacity that applies to node n's background paint is the product of n and n's ANCESTORS, never its descendants. An element with opacity 0.5 therefore has its page background faded toward the canvas's white, making the guard PESSIMISTIC on every dark/high-contrast site where opacity < 1.

Proof, from the dlavh follow-up: for .probe-group-btn in dark the real backdrop is #1e1e23 (only .channels-pane and html paint, both rgb(30,30,35)) but the guard resolved #56565a -- exactly #1e1e23 painted twice at alpha=0.5 over white. True ratios at opacity .5 were 2.33 dark / 2.82 high-contrast, not the 1.56 / 2.25 the guard reported and which are now quoted as fact in ChannelsPane.css and contrast-aa.spec.ts comments.

Never caught because in the light theme the leak is a near-no-op (white into near-white) and the author validated against the Stats light case.

selfOpacity is CORRECT as-is and must not change: the measured element's text IS inside every one of those groups.

Scope: fix the direction (resolve the chain to the root first, then accumulate downward), re-measure the numbers wrongly recorded in ChannelsPane.css and contrast-aa.spec.ts, and confirm no surviving allowlist entry changes pass/fail state. Expected: Stats illustration ~2.70 dark / ~2.11 light (still failing, entry stays) and ~4.30 high-contrast (still passing, correctly absent).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
FIXED and demonstrated. chainOf now collects the chain upward (the only direction the DOM offers) and accumulates the group alphas DOWNWARD from the root, so a node's background carries its own opacity and its ancestors', never its descendants'. selfOpacity is unchanged — it is still the full product, because the measured element's text really is inside every group.

PROOF THAT IT READS WHAT THE DOM PAINTS — three independent readings of the same pixel, .probe-group-btn .material-icons at the historical opacity .5, dark theme:
  OLD core   backdrop #56565a, ink #73737d, ratio 1.56 (reproduces the recorded figure exactly)
  NEW core   backdrop #1e1e23, ink #575761, ratio 2.32
  SCREENSHOT of the rendered page, sampled inside the glyph's own box:
             mode #1e1e23 (52% of 256px), ink pixel #575761
The old core's backdrop and ink appear NOWHERE on screen. All three themes:
  dark  OLD 1.56 / NEW 2.32 / real bg #1e1e23 ink #575761
  light OLD 2.10 / NEW 2.10 / real bg #ffffff ink #b2b2b2   (the leak is a no-op in light — why it survived)
  hc    OLD 2.25 / NEW 2.82 / real bg #000000 ink #555555
Same three-way agreement on the Stats illustration (64px, ink covers ~25% of the box so both readings are unambiguous): real #252530/#676774 dark, #f5f5f5/#aaaaaa light, #0a0a0a/#757575 hc — NEW matches all six, OLD matches none. Independent cross-check with no screenshot involved: the sibling text inside the same .no-streams block has opacity 1 and must share the surface; the corrected core gives glyph and text the same backdrop, the old core did not.

RED WITHOUT THE FIX: with only the accumulation direction reverted and the corrected numbers in place, the guard's own REGRESSED arm fails the run — 'stats / dark / 1280x720 .no-streams .material-icons GOT WORSE: 1.78, but the entry records 2.68' at both viewports.

FULL A/B SWEEP, both cores over the same walk, 11 routes x 3 themes x 2 viewports: 8277 measurements, 74 moved by more than 0.05, 0 flipped pass/fail. Only three signatures move at all — the two known opacity sites and the sidebar wordmark SVG (opacity .85, passing either way: light 9.92 -> 9.65, dark 9.38 -> 9.77, hc 13.42 -> 13.64; note light moves DOWN, the old core was not uniformly pessimistic). Every other recorded ratio in the file is bit-identical under both cores and needed no correction: dashboard glyphs (1.75/1.92/2.01/2.07/2.81/3.19 light, 3.36-5.26 dark, 4.06-7.28 hc), rail 4.51/10.73/14.31, settings nav 4.79/9.76/14.04, sticky nav 5.41/10.47/15.31, notification badge 4.83/6.21/5.13.

RATIOS CORRECTED (old -> new):
  ALLOWLIST .no-streams .material-icons   dark 1.78 -> 2.68, light 2.13 -> 2.11; hc 3.13 -> 4.30 (passes either way, stays absent)
  header comment, .probe-group-btn at .50  1.56/2.10/2.25 -> 2.32/2.10/2.82
  header comment, .probe-group-btn at .75  3.15/3.28/5.02 -> 3.55/3.28/5.24
  header comment, .probe-group-btn at .70  2.76 dark      -> 3.30/3.00/4.69
  header note 3, Stats illustration        2.13 -> 2.11
  ChannelsPane.css comment: all of the above, plus the retracted claim that 0.75 was the smallest 0.05 step clearing the floor. Under the corrected core 0.70 clears too (light sits exactly ON 3.00). 0.75 stands as shipped; nothing re-opens the PO decision.
No surviving allowlist entry changed pass/fail state.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, documented in the spec and deliberately not fixed: paint() composites one fillRect per layer, which is exact unless a translucent group paints an OPAQUE background over another opaque one (true nesting would flatten to a buffer first). Instrumented across all 8277 sites: zero such chains today.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint 0 warnings, vitest 179 files / 2479 tests, CSS chunk-leak audit TIER 1/2/3 green, all six rendered-CSS guards green (20/20) against a frozen build of this tree served on a private port.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CONFIRMED SHIPPED. Independent re-verification against origin/dev at ad0e0c6d,
reading the committed tree rather than trusting the earlier close comment.

1. DIRECTION. e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts chainOf() (lines 505-529) collects the
   chain upward, then accumulates in a second pass
   `for (let i = chain.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1)`, stamping the running
   cumulative onto layers[i] as it descends from the root. A node's background
   therefore carries its own opacity and its ancestors', never its descendants'.
   selfOpacity is the full product and is unchanged, correctly, because the
   measured element's text really is inside every group. Header note 3a
   documents the whole thing.

2. RE-MEASURED FIGURES, both files. Every number the bead lists as wrong is
   gone from the tree and the corrected one is in place, with the retraction
   written down rather than silently swapped:
   ChannelsPane.css above .probe-group-btn now records 2.32/2.10/2.82 at
   opacity 0.50, 3.30/3.00/4.69 at 0.70 and 3.55/3.28/5.24 at 0.75, and says
   explicitly that it previously recorded 1.56/2.10/2.25 and 3.15/3.28/5.02,
   that those came from a core accumulating in the wrong direction, and that
   0.70 does clear 3:1 so the "smallest 0.05 step" claim is retracted while
   0.75 stands as shipped. contrast-aa.spec.ts carries the same table in its
   header (lines 305-317) with the same retraction.

3. ALLOWLIST PASS/FAIL STATE. The allowlist has exactly two surviving entries
   and neither flipped:
   - .dashboard-card-icon .material-icons, worst {light: 1.75}. Bit-identical
     under both cores per the A/B sweep; still failing, still present, still
     the ratchet on the PO's decorative ratification.
   - .no-streams .material-icons, worst {dark: 2.68, light: 2.11}, re-measured
     from the old core's 1.78/2.13, with high-contrast 3.13 -> 4.30. Still
     failing in dark and light so it stays; high-contrast passes either way so
     it stays correctly absent from `worst`.
   The four entries recorded as deliberately absent are still absent and their
   comments carry the corrected figures.

No re-run of the guard itself was attempted for this confirmation. It needs a
live backend and roughly 10 minutes for 66 route walks, and the close comment
already records a full 8277-measurement A/B over both cores with 74 readings
moving by more than 0.05 and 0 pass/fail flips. Nothing in the committed tree
contradicts it. Confirmation here is of the code and the recorded numbers.

Reported by the Wave 1 measurement-layer pass (branch
guards/wave1-measurement-layer). Bead state deliberately not changed.

title: Wire the modal typography baseline diff into CI
description:
The harness baseline is now accurate and reads zero, which makes it a real ratchet — but nothing runs it.

'node scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs --diff' compares 1,792 selector-signature rows across 82 dialogs and needs no backend and no login, which makes it unusually cheap to gate. It caught a 42-row drift on arrival this session (the baseline predated commit 810d21ea) purely because the agent was told to check first — a check nobody would run by habit.

The executing agent deliberately did NOT add a fourth browser-tier Playwright guard for modal typography, reasoning that the harness plus the refreshed baseline already detect regression and an unwired guard adds cost without adding a gate. That reasoning is right, and it makes wiring THIS the higher-value move.

A guard rail is already in place: --diff refuses any viewport other than the baseline's 1440x900, so the staleness trap cannot recur silently.

Context on the wider gap: of six rendered-CSS Playwright guards added today, only sr-only-hidden is CI-wired. The other five need a live backend, which a preview build cannot provide for every route — that limit is measured, not assumed. The modal harness is the exception precisely because it stubs at the network boundary.

Sizing: Small.

title: computedTextContrast in operator-shell.spec.ts mis-parses color(srgb ...) - reads 0-1 floats as 0-255
description:
A latent measurement bug in a CHECKED-IN spec, and it is the same bug that produced wrong ratios in this epic's own bead descriptions.

Chrome serialises color-mix(in srgb, ...) as 'color(srgb 0.96 0.96 0.96 / 0.94)'. computedTextContrast in e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts greps all numbers out of the string, so it would read those 0-1 floats as 0-255 channels — turning a near-WHITE surface into a near-BLACK one. Any assertion it makes over a color-mix surface is meaningless, in either direction.

This is exactly how the 3.96/3.96/3.27 figures in bead dlavh came to be wrong (true values 3.68/3.68/3.25): an rgba()-only resolver returned null for the color-mix layer and silently treated it as transparent.

The fix pattern already exists in the tree. e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts, added under dlavh, NEVER PARSES A COLOUR — it paints each value to a 1x1 canvas and reads the pixel back, so the engine that painted the page resolves the syntax and does the alpha maths. Reuse that helper rather than repairing the regex, which will keep losing to the next colour syntax CSS adds.

Also worth doing while in there: operator-shell's two contrast tests walk hand-written selector lists of 9-11 selectors on two routes. That narrowness is why five failing .dashboard-card-icon glyphs survived on a route one of them covers. contrast-aa now walks 11 routes x 3 themes x 2 viewports, so the older tests are arguably redundant — consider retiring them rather than fixing them.

Sizing: Small.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
FIXED on branch guards/wave1-measurement-layer, commit 35627284.

computedTextContrast no longer parses a colour. It paints the whole ancestor
chain into a 1x1 canvas and reads the pixel back, the same technique as
e2e/contrast-aa.spec.ts, including the two-sentinel accepts() and root-down
group opacity from bead 0zq1p. The core is duplicated rather than imported
because a page.evaluate body is serialised into the browser and cannot reach a
module import, and contrast-aa runs its copy inside ONE whole-page evaluate over
thousands of nodes; both copies now cite each other and say a model change
belongs in both. contrast-aa's header note claiming the bug is "still latent in
operator-shell" is corrected.

A/B ON THE SAME DOM, not an assumption. Both resolvers ran in the same page:
132 measurements over both tests, both viewports, three themes, both states.
42 moved, all by 0.01 to 0.15, and NONE because of color-mix. Every computed
background in every ancestor chain these selectors walk is plain rgb()/rgba()
today, so the mis-parse really was latent HERE, exactly as contrast-aa said.
What moved is precision: the canvas composites at the compositor's 8-bit depth,
so rgba(16,185,129,.12) over #252530 reads the #263a3e that is painted rather
than the fractional rgb(39,59,62) a float blend carries. No verdict changed;
every listed selector still clears 4.5 with margin.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE IN THERE, both fixed in the same commit:

1. A detached node measured as black on black. getComputedStyle on a node
   outside the document returns an EMPTY declaration and the old parser fed ''
   straight into the blend as transparent. Caught on the first full-file run at
   --workers=2, Channel Manager 1920x1080: React re-committed the group list
   between the locator resolving and the evaluate running. The reading now
   reports itself detached and the caller re-reads (bounded, 10 attempts,
   100ms apart), which works because the locator re-resolves each attempt and
   measures the element that replaced it.
2. No animation freeze. Both tests flip data-theme and measure immediately.
   That is precisely the mistake that put a wrong .failed-streams-alert entry
   into contrast-aa's allowlist (4.40 inside a transition against 4.75 at rest).
   FREEZE_ANIMATION is now applied before any theme flip and re-applied after
   the partial-failure reload, which discards the previous tag.

The evidence object gained declaredColor, backgroundGradient and opacity and
reports painted hex, so a failure says what was on screen rather than what was
declared. A gradient in the chain is surfaced rather than silently averaged
away; there are none on these selectors today.

RECOMMENDATION ON RETIRING THE TWO TESTS: DO NOT RETIRE THEM. Retire the
premise instead, which is that they are contrast tests.

  * On SELECTORS, contrast-aa strictly supersets them. It walks every text node
    on 11 routes x 3 themes x 2 viewports with a per-route element-count floor
    and a bidirectional allowlist ratchet. These two walk 9 to 11 hand-written
    selectors on 2 routes. The bead is right that this narrowness is why five
    failing .dashboard-card-icon glyphs survived on a route one of them covers.
  * On STATES, contrast-aa cannot reach what they reach, and this is the part
    that would be lost. contrast-aa logs into the live container and measures
    whatever that instance happens to render. These are fixture-driven: a
    forced 500 on /api/journal/stats produces .dashboard-card-error p and
    .dashboard-card-error button, and a seeded empty group produces
    .group-subtext and .group-empty-badge. Neither state exists on a healthy
    instance. Note that .dashboard-card-error p and both .service-status-*
    selectors are among the 42 readings that moved in the A/B, so these are
    live measurement surfaces, not decoration.
  * They carry an axe arm the walk does not: AxeBuilder over
    wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa per state, asserting zero serious or critical
    violations, plus release artefacts under
    test-results/operator-workspace-final-validation/.
  * They run BACKEND-LESS (E2E_START_SERVER=true E2E_EXACT_BUILD=true, all
    fixtures mocked via page.route), which contrast-aa structurally cannot:
    docs/testing.md records that contrast-aa and the other four route-walking
    guards are manual-only because Channel Manager never mounts without an API
    (bead 2lw25). So contrast-aa cannot replace them in anything automatable.

Concrete proposal, cheap and low risk: keep both tests, and trim their selector
lists to the elements only a fixture can produce (.dashboard-card-error p,
.dashboard-card-error button, .group-subtext, .group-empty-badge, the
.service-status-* pair). The always-present selectors on the populated states
duplicate contrast-aa exactly and could go. The whole run is 7.9s at
--workers=2, so the overlap costs nothing today and the trim is a tidiness call
rather than a correctness one. Retiring the tests entirely would take the axe
arm, the fixture-only states and the release artefacts with them.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING, not by reading. Both contrast tests pass at --workers=1 and
--workers=2 (4 passed, 7.9s). Full e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts: 62 passed, 3
failed. Those 3 are pre-existing (see below). frontend lint 0 warnings, tsc
clean, vitest 197 files / 2684 tests.

PRE-EXISTING FAILURES OBSERVED, not caused by this change and not swallowed:
e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts "contextual settings links use stable current
hashes", "staged contextual navigation keeps editing or discards before landing
on the exact settings page", and "contextual settings navigation cleanly exits
an edit session with no staged changes" all fail on UNMODIFIED origin/dev at
ad0e0c6d (verified by stashing this change and re-running), both backend-less
and with E2E_BASE_URL pointed at the live container on :6100. First one:
getByRole('link', {name: 'Channel default settings'}) is never found against the
expected href '#settings/channel-defaults'. The other two time out on a click.
All three use the appPage fixture, which performs a real login.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW FINDING N1 FIXED, commit bc962002 on guards/wave1-measurement-layer
(branch rebased onto origin/dev at 18d3c98f, PR #809 / 0.18.1-0054).

The hole: `backgroundGradient` was captured and never asserted on. It reached a
human only inside `JSON.stringify(evidence)` in the assertion message, which
prints only once the ratio assertion has ALREADY failed. In the case that
actually matters, a wrong surface that happens to measure well, nothing ever
read it. Meanwhile a `background-image` cannot be reduced to one colour, so only
the `backgroundColor` layers reached the canvas and the ratio described a
surface that is not on screen.

Implemented as a throw, as directed, and it is the self-consistent choice: the
function already throws on `!accepts(colour)`, `contrast-aa` refuses to measure
such sites outright, there is no allowlist here to route one to, and the caller
has already asserted the selector must be measured. The message names the
selector, the ancestor element and the gradient. The always-null field is
dropped rather than left implying it carries information.

PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL FAILURE, not just compiled. `background-image:
linear-gradient(#111111, #111111)` injected onto `.operator-dashboard-card`, an
ancestor of four measured selectors, then the Dashboard contrast test run BOTH
WAYS over that same page:

  WITHOUT the fix, the test PASSES. It reported .dashboard-card-value at 15.96
  against a #f5f5f5 backdrop in the light theme, while the surface actually
  painted was #111111. True ratio of that #1a1a1a text on the #111111 it sits
  on is 1.08 against a 4.5 floor. The guard certified a catastrophic contrast
  failure as good and was wrong by roughly 15x. That is the hole, demonstrated
  rather than argued.

  WITH the fix, the same page fails at BOTH viewports:
  ".operator-dashboard-card h3: a background-image in the ancestor chain cannot
  be reduced to one colour, so no contrast measurement was taken. Found on
  article: linear-gradient(rgb(17, 17, 17), rgb(17, 17, 17)"

  NO FALSE POSITIVE: injection removed, all four contrast tests pass at
  --workers=2 in 8.0s.

Still latent on the real tree, as the review said: every gradient in the
codebase is on a leaf element, never an ancestor of measured text. Guarded
before that stops being true.

Also on this branch: build bumped to 0.18.1-0055 across all three touchpoints
(commit 9852a06f), which the first pass missed. Worth recording that the missing
bump would NOT have merged green after all: the version-consistency job runs
`scripts/check_version_advances.py --baseline-ref origin/dev` as a second step
on pull_request events with base `dev` (bead w9irb), and that gate fails a PR
whose build does not strictly advance. The consistency check alone is the part
that only proves agreement. Both were run here and both pass.

Reviewer notes N2, N3 and N4 deliberately untouched; they are bead
enhancedchannelmanager-23skw by PO decision.

title: ChannelPipelineTab declares a bare .modal-body textarea - restyles every modal after one visit
description:
Cross-chunk leak of exactly the shape the three guard tiers were built for, and it is still open because scoping it is not obvious.

frontend/src/components/channelPipeline/ChannelPipelineTab.css declares a bare '.modal-body textarea'. ChannelPipelineTab is a lazy chunk appended on first visit and never removed, so once an operator opens Channel Pipeline that rule restyles the textarea in EVERY modal in the app for the rest of the session.

The modal sweep tokenised it (render-neutral) but did NOT scope it, and the reason is real: the modal portals outside .channel-pipeline-tab, so the obvious ancestor scope would stop it matching its own dialog. It needs either the dialog's own root class as the scope, or the rule moved to whichever stylesheet owns that dialog.

Sizing: Small, once the right scope is chosen.

title: Four dead 0-1-0 icon rules remain outside modal scope - tokens applied, rules never win
description:
Same defect class the modal sweep fixed four instances of, still present elsewhere.

A single-class .material-icons override ties at 0-1-0 with index.css's base .material-icons (24px) and loses, so the authored size never renders. The insidious part: .norm-engine-icon and .norm-engine-expand are ALREADY TOKENISED to --icon-status and still measure 24px. The token was applied; the rule never won. So a reader sees correct-looking CSS and a grep for off-scale literals finds nothing.

Fix is two classes of depth, as documented in docs/css_guidelines.md and applied to .catchup-badge__icon (bead sccol) and the four modal cases (bead xhldy).

Detection: this cannot be found by reading CSS — it needs the rendered size compared against the authored one. Worth considering whether the route-typography-scale guard can be extended to flag 'element renders 24px while its own rule declares something else', which would catch the whole class rather than instances.

Sizing: Small to fix the two known, Medium to sweep for the rest.

title: e2e/ is neither typechecked nor linted by any gate - and it already has a real type error
description:
The project's verification layer is the one layer with no verification.

There is no root tsconfig.json, and the frontend's tsc/eslint only cover frontend/src. Playwright's esbuild strips types without checking them, so an e2e spec can ship with a type error and simply fail at runtime — or worse, pass for the wrong reason.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL: e2e/ffmpeg-builder-input.spec.ts:129 has a real 'Cannot find name pathLabel'. Found by an agent running tsc --strict manually because no gate does.

This matters more now than it did this morning. Six rendered-CSS guards were added today (sr-only-hidden, frozen-chrome, route-typography-scale, control-typeface, contrast-aa, settings-nav-groups) and they are the mechanism the PO asked for so that claims about rendered behaviour do not rest on anyone's report. An unchecked guard is a guard that can rot silently.

Work: a root tsconfig covering e2e/, wired into a gate, plus an eslint config that reaches it. Note the pre-existing noise an agent hit: ~65 errors from no root @types/node, which need resolving before the gate can be blocking.

Sizing: Small for the config, Medium if the 65 pre-existing errors need triage.

title: Modal type-scale sweep: execution record
description:
COMPLETE, committed as 078c2075. Filed after the fact — bd create is orchestrator territory, so the executing agent could not create its own bead.

~1,500 typography declarations across ModalBase.css, 34 dedicated *Modal.css/*Dialog.css, 7 modal-only Channel Pipeline stylesheets, and the modal ranges in 7 page stylesheets. 67 files.

PO-APPROVED DEVIATION: the modal title role is 18px, not the 'roughly 17.6px' the PO specified. 17.6px was never chosen — it is what 1.1rem computes to. 18px is var(--text-2xl), a primitive the scale already carries, so the role points at a primitive like every other role. Rendered delta +0.4px. PO reviewed and accepted.
PO-APPROVED: .modal-btn dot-variants (.primary/.cancel/.danger) deleted and 25 markup sites migrated to the hyphenated spelling. Deliberately not render-neutral — 22 buttons converge on the treatment the other 108 already used.

FOUR DEFECT CLASSES FIXED, all measured not inferred: 27 buttons wore a modal-btn VARIANT with no base class (UA default 13.3333px, no padding); 3 wore 'modal-btn btn-secondary' where common.css is emitted last so .btn-* won the geometry; 2 Cancel buttons had a bare modal-btn with no variant (transparent on transparent); four single-class icon overrides lost the 0-1-0 tie with index.css's base .material-icons and rendered 24px instead of their authored 40/48/16/14px.
Plus six var(--error-color, ...) sites in ModalBase.css — the token is defined nowhere, so .modal-btn-danger's fill was a hardcoded literal bypassing bead 4l51b's retone (3.76:1 under white instead of 4.83).

MEASURED at 1280x720 / 1440x900 / 1920x1080 against a HEAD copy: .modal-header 65.93 -> 65.17, .modal-footer 65.06 -> 64.70, .modal-btn 34.34 -> 33.91, .modal-close-btn 31.87 -> 31.87 (padding compensated so the target box stays exactly 32x32), .modal-container 446.15 -> 442.36, horizontal overflow 0 -> 0 at every viewport. Off-scale collapse: 17.6px 101 -> 0, 14.4px 398 -> 44, 14px 251 -> 91, 12.8px 163 -> 54; 13px 817 -> 1447. Harness 82/82 dialogs, no crashes, 1,167 signature rows moved.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG IN FOUR WAYS: --diff read 42 not zero (the committed baseline predated 810d21ea) and was refreshed; every line range was stale, and ChannelsPane's in particular started mid-rule and swallowed a 567-line NON-modal island that was correctly excluded; '32 files / 392 declarations' undercounted the estate at 34 files / 499 declarations plus ~250 in-page.

TOOLING ADDED: --viewport WxH and per-dialog geometry capture in scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs. That geometry is what made the before/after table possible; it did not exist before, which is why no earlier round could report modal heights. --diff now refuses any viewport other than the baseline's, so the staleness trap cannot recur silently.

title: Settings rail overflows at 1280x720 with 18 destinations - is scrolling the right answer?
description:
PRODUCT DECISION, surfaced by the render gate 70u0r.4 and not resolvable in CSS.

The Settings drill-in rail now scrolls, with Back pinned sticky so it can never leave the viewport. That is a legitimate answer. The question is whether it is the RIGHT answer.

Measured: 1099px of content in a 675px rail at the PO's stated 1280x720 minimum (424px over), and 64px over even at 1920x1080. Critically, 1280x720 ALREADY overflowed before grouping — 947px against 675px with only two groups. Eighteen destinations at 45px each do not fit a 720px viewport under any grouping scheme.

So grouping did not cause this; it made an existing problem visible and added ~155px to it.

OPTIONS THE PO MAY WANT INSTEAD OF, OR AS WELL AS, SCROLLING:
- Reduce the destination count. Bead 70u0r.1 already removes one (Lookup Tables). The proposal's rejected relocations would remove more, but the PO declined them on evidence.
- Collapsible groups, so only the active group is expanded. Cheap in the existing markup, but adds a click to reach anything outside the current group and the drill-in already costs a Back press.
- Accept scrolling as shipped, and treat the sticky Back as the mitigation it is.

Worth noting the drill-in's own cost structure: reaching another Settings destination already takes a Back press, which the approved IA calls 'the accepted cost of the drill-in'. Adding a scroll on top compounds it.

Not urgent — nothing is broken and Back is always reachable. But it is the kind of thing that reads as an oversight to an operator, and the PO's minimum viewport is the one where it is worst.
close_reason: PO DECISION 2026-08-12 (backlog validity audit bd bewu9): ACCEPT SCROLLING. The Settings drill-in rail may scroll internally at 1280x720 with 17 destinations; collapsible-by-default groups are explicitly NOT wanted. The status quo already implements this: TabNavigation.css:183-203 makes .navigation-back position:sticky precisely because .primary-navigation is overflow-y:auto and the rail genuinely scrolls at that viewport. No code change required; the bead existed to force this decision and the decision is now made.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-07-31, which turns this from a judgement call into a decision with numbers behind it.

A documentation writer verified the Settings drill-in navigation live at 1280x720 — the PO stated minimum supported viewport — and measured the grouped destination list at 1054px of content inside a 675px sidebar box. So the list is roughly 1.56x the available height and scrolls internally, with the Back control pinned at the top.

That is the concrete form of the question this bead asks. It is no longer "will 18 destinations overflow" — they do, by about 379px, and the current answer is an internal scroll.

WHAT THE GROUPING ALREADY BOUGHT: the destinations are now under six headings — Connections, Channel Processing, Notifications and Reports, Upkeep, Workspace, Administration — and the Administration group is hidden entirely for non-admins rather than rendered empty. So a non-admin sees materially less than 1054px. Whoever picks this up should measure the NON-ADMIN case too before deciding; if the overflow only affects admins, the answer may be different.

OPTIONS, with the measurement in mind:
  - accept the internal scroll (status quo) -- Back stays pinned, so the escape route is never scrolled off
  - collapse groups by default, expanding the one containing the current page -- removes the overflow without removing destinations, at the cost of one click to reach a sibling group
  - reduce row height -- but note control and row sizing was just settled deliberately across the app, and shrinking rows here would diverge from it

DO NOT resolve this by shrinking the type or the rows to fit. That trades a scroll nobody complains about for an inconsistency with the scale the rest of the app just adopted.

Also verified and worth knowing when judging this: the Back control reverts the sidebar to the primary destination list but does NOT change the route -- the settings page you were on stays rendered until you pick a different primary destination. That is unusual enough that it is now documented, and it bears on the question, since Back is not an exit from Settings so much as a sidebar toggle.

title: Form controls do not inherit the app font-family; land the reset once a Playwright guard exists
description:
STRUCTURAL DEFECT, pre-existing, measured. BLOCKED BY PO DECISION on e2e/control-typeface.spec.ts existing first — the PO's standing rule is that every change must be validatable from Playwright, not from a report.

THE DEFECT: frontend/src/index.css:2 sets font-family on the root, but there is NO 'button, input, select, textarea { font-family: inherit }' reset anywhere. Browsers do not inherit fonts into form controls, so every button, input, select and textarea takes the UA default family. Controls therefore render in a DIFFERENT TYPEFACE from the text beside them, on any machine. Measured here: ~9% difference in advance width per pixel.

I FIRST REPORTED THIS WRONG, and the correction is the useful part. I said 'controls render in Arial, not Inter'. Both halves are false. getComputedStyle().fontFamily returns the DECLARED stack, not the face actually used — I read a declaration and reported it as a rendering, which is the same error shape as every other mistake in this epic. Measured by canvas advance width at 13px/400 on this host:
  Inter alone            136.97
  nonexistent-font-xyz   136.97   <- identical, so Inter is NOT available
  Arial alone            148.87
  sans-serif alone       148.87   <- identical, so Arial is NOT available either
  app stack              163.45
  system-ui alone        163.45   <- app text actually renders in SYSTEM-UI
So on this host it is system-ui vs generic sans-serif, not Inter vs Arial.

ALSO: Inter is NOT BUNDLED. No @font-face, no webfont link, no font files under frontend/src or frontend/public. It is a hopeful first entry in a fallback stack, which means the app has probably never rendered in Inter for anyone who did not already have it installed. That is arguably a bigger finding than the reset and is its own decision: ship the font, or stop naming it.

IMPACT MEASUREMENT (the PO asked to measure before deciding). Injected the reset into a live session and re-measured the same elements across all ten routes. Ran twice — once with this host's fallbacks, once forcing a deliberately larger metric gap as a stand-in for a machine where the app font IS installed:

  reset, host fallbacks:      416 controls, 110 changed width, 84 wider, 0 newly clipping, 0 height changes
  reset, forced worst case:   416 controls, 137 changed width, 98 wider, 0 newly clipping, 0 height changes

Typical growth 14-34px on content-sized buttons (Stats toggles, EPG 'Import from...', Settings select triggers), all in flexible containers, which is why nothing breaks. TWO OUTLIERS worth a human look: channel-manager input.search-input +351px (a width:100% field reflowing, not text growth) and journal input -186px (narrower, the opposite of the expected direction).

CONCLUSION: the layout risk does not materialise, even in the forced worst case. Recommend landing the one-line reset. Caveat that survives: font resolution is client-dependent, so any delta measured on one host is not the delta everywhere — which is exactly why the guard must assert the RENDERED face, not the declared family. Comparing getComputedStyle().fontFamily strings would encode my original error in executable form.

title: P1 completion pass: StickySectionNav and the remaining off-scale route text
description: Finishing pass after an adversarial audit refuted the claim that all ten route pages were on the P1 scale. Eight of ten still carried off-scale text. COMPLETE, uncommitted. THE LARGEST MISS AND WHY IT WAS MISSED: .sticky-section-nav button had NO AUTHOR RULE AT ALL — verified live by dumping every matching document.styleSheets rule per element, not inferred from source — so it fell to the UA button default at 13.3333px: 9 elements on Stats, 3 on Settings. It escaped the entire sweep because StickySectionNav.css was UNTRACKED and therefore invisible to every audit. It became fixable only when commit 62432aa4 tracked it, and I did not notice the scope had changed. Also fixed: the On this page was 12px/700/uppercase with letter-spacing silently left at normal — a textbook partial-redeclaration hybrid; now carries .micro-label with the local declarations deleted, which is the only way the shared rule can win. .dense-toolbar .unused-only-toggle 0.85rem -> body role (it sits in the route-header band, but that band is NOT frozen for type — the frozen chrome is the rail and the 45px application bar; .btn-primary beside it in the same DenseToolbar already measured 13px/500). .drag-handle .material-icons fixed once in common.css section 10 rather than per page, covering EPG Manager AND Channel Pipeline. .filter-dropdown-button and .enter-edit-mode-btn -> body role. RESULT: 78 -> 69 off-scale sites, ~29 rendered elements moved. EPG Manager and Channel Pipeline now clean. Before/after computed-style diff over 30 probed selectors shows only intended rows changed; no layout shift, row heights unchanged. FIVE ERRORS IN MY BRIEF, one material: I said .drag-handle .material-icons was EPG-only. It is on Channel Pipeline too, and fixing one would have left the half-finished state the guidelines warn about. I also called four Channel Manager sites em-relative when they are rem literals, so the 'inherits from a parent whose size changed' framing did not apply to any of them. DELIBERATE NON-FIXES, now carrying WHY comments so a future sweep does not read them as oversights: two decorative disclosure carets (.dropdown-arrow 0.6rem, .group-toggle 0.7rem) — no P1 role fits a caret glyph, and the icon tokens start at 14px (+46%). The app's canonical disclosure indicator is .custom-select-arrow, an 18px Material Icons glyph; retiring the caret-character idiom across its five sites is its own change. STILL OFF-SCALE, for other owners: Dashboard (38 sites, entirely the PO's uncommitted OperatorDashboard work); .custom-select-trigger 0.875rem — the single largest remaining source, spanning Guide/Settings/Journal/M3U Changes, shared component with app-wide blast radius; .search-box input and .search-input in common.css, same shape. DOC DEFECT FOUND: docs/css_guidelines.md section Rollout status lists .search-input, .search-box input and .filter-dropdown-button as moved onto the roles. Only the third is true, and only because this pass did it. A doc overstating completion is how the next person stops looking too early.

title: Render-verify the grouped drill-in at 1280x720 and 1920x1080
description:
MEASUREMENT GATE, not a formality. The proposal could not measure this: the drill-in is not deployed, so the rail height under grouping is unknown.

The risk: five group headings add roughly 120px to a 244px rail that may already be near the viewport bound at the PO's minimum supported size. 1280x720 is the floor — the PO has stated mobile is explicitly not a target, so nothing below 1280 matters.

Verify expanded AND collapsed, at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, in all three themes. If the rail overflows at 720px height, that is a real finding and the grouping needs a scroll treatment or fewer groups — report it rather than shipping it.

Blocked on 70u0r.3.

Sizing: Small.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
GATE FAILED — and the failure is the finding. Committed as 9b09b213.

MEASURED, all three themes identical (no theme moves the rail):
  expanded  1280x720   1099px content / 675px rail  = 424px OVER
  expanded  1920x1080  1099px / 1035px              =  64px OVER
  collapsed 1280x720   896px / 675px                = 221px OVER
  collapsed 1920x1080  1035px / 1035px              = fits

Per-group cost is 38.7px (30.7 heading + 8 separation), so 2 -> 6 groups added ~155px, not the ~120px the proposal estimated.

THREE FINDINGS, and the ordering matters:
1. 1280x720 ALREADY OVERFLOWED BEFORE GROUPING. I independently confirmed this against the deployed pre-grouping build: 947px of content in a 675px rail, 272px over, with only 2 groups. Eighteen destinations at 45px do not fit a 720px viewport whatever the headings do. Grouping worsened an existing overflow rather than creating one. The collapsed 1280x720 overflow is ENTIRELY pre-existing — headings are display:none at 68px width, so grouping contributes zero there.
2. At 1920x1080 the overflow IS new. Ungrouped 947px fit the 1035px budget; grouping pushes it to 1099px. The spacious viewport no longer shows the whole list either.
3. THE REAL DEFECT THIS EXPOSED, which no heading-counting test could have found: .primary-navigation is a scroll container and .navigation-back was position:static. An operator scrolling down to Administration took THE ONLY EXIT FROM SETTINGS off screen. Confirmed static on the deployed build.

REMEDY IMPLEMENTED — the one the proposal nominated in advance for exactly this outcome: sidebar-internal scrolling with Back kept in view. .navigation-back is now position:sticky with an opaque --bg-tertiary background, pinned flush to the scroll box top using negative top/margin-top so it neither jumps nor consumes vertical budget — the rail measured 1102 -> 1099px, i.e. it got slightly shorter. Chosen over 'fewer groups' because that would contradict binding decision D1. Verified visually in all three themes at top, mid and bottom scroll: rows pass cleanly behind Back with no bleed-through.

FLAGGED FOR PO REVIEW: this is a CSS change beyond the literal grouping scope. The agent flagged it rather than burying it, which is the right call. TabNavigation.css was unclaimed and clean.

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS: the rail overflows at both viewports and now scrolls. Scrolling is a legitimate answer for 18 destinations, but the PO should decide whether it is the RIGHT answer at their stated 1280x720 minimum, or whether the destination count itself is the problem. That is a product decision, not a CSS one.

title: Apply the approved Settings group assignment, names and order

PO decision D1, with the amendment the PO made during review.

Lands after 70u0r.1, so the list is 17 destinations — Lookup Tables is gone by then.
