title: Add a group field to SettingsSection and derive the drill-in groups from it
description:
The grouping mechanism ALREADY SHIPS — verified. TabNavigation.tsx:77 builds settingsGroups and renders each as <section className='navigation-group'><h2>, the identical markup the primary nav uses. It is hardcoded to a two-way adminOnly split:
  { label: 'Settings', sections: sections.filter(s => !s.adminOnly) },
  { label: 'Administration', sections: sections.filter(s => s.adminOnly) }

So this is a data-and-derivation change, not new UI: add a group field to the SettingsSection interface in settingsSections.ts, and generalise that two-way filter into an N-way grouping driven by the field, preserving group order. Administration stays derived from adminOnly.

Blocked on beads 2896r.16/.17 landing — they own settingsSections.ts (untracked) and TabNavigation.tsx uncommitted.

Sizing: Small.

title: Remove Lookup Tables entirely: UI, router, model, table and the |lookup: pipe
description:
PO decision D2: full removal (option R2-D), chosen over the recommended keep-the-pipe option. FIRST in the epic per D5.

WHY THE FULLER OPTION IS RIGHT. The pipe cannot affect real EPG output today. Verified: _resolve_lookups is called from exactly two places, /preview and /preview/batch (backend/routers/dummy_epg.py). generate_xmltv(profiles, channel_data) neither accepts nor passes a lookups argument, and calls generate_channel_xml with six positional args, omitting the seventh which defaults to None. So a template using {x|lookup:y} resolves in PREVIEW and silently does not in the generated XMLTV — a preview/production divergence. Removal eliminates the trap instead of documenting it.

Supporting evidence: zero lookup tables configured on this instance (/api/lookup-tables returns []); no Dummy EPG profile references the pipe; a profile structurally CANNOT bind a table (dummy_epg_profiles has 33 columns, none stores a lookup id); the only UI that could bind one was DummyEPGSourceModal, the legacy source path deprecated by 09x38.4.

SCOPE:
- frontend: remove from SETTINGS_SECTIONS, delete LookupTableSection.tsx/.css, its devHarness catalog entry and renderer, the four API client functions, and the |lookup: pipe from frontend/src/utils/templateEngine.ts
- backend: delete routers/lookup_tables.py and its registration in routers/__init__.py, the LookupTable model, _resolve_lookups and the inline_lookups/global_lookup_ids request fields in dummy_epg.py, and the pipe from the backend template engine
- migration: destructive, dropping lookup_tables. Follow docs/database_migrations.md.
- docs: template_engine.md documents the pipe and the source-binding; user guide references; a BLOCKING upgrade note, since any instance with rows loses them

MUST CHECK BEFORE THE MIGRATION: whether any instance other than this one has rows. Zero here is not zero everywhere. The upgrade note must say what is lost and offer an export path if that is cheap.

The modal harness (frontend/src/devHarness/) covers the dialogs; its coverage test will go red when LookupTableSection's dialog disappears — update the catalog deliberately, do not silence it.

Sizing: Medium.

title: The --error token serves two incompatible jobs in dark and high-contrast themes
description:
Surfaced by the contrast pass and deliberately not forced, because it is a token-architecture problem rather than a colour choice.

--error is used both as STATUS TEXT on the page background and as a SOLID FILL under white text. In dark and high contrast those pull in opposite directions: as text it needs to be lighter (4.03:1 today, short of AA), as a fill under white it needs to be darker (3.76 dark, 3.41 HC). One token cannot satisfy both. In the LIGHT theme both jobs wanted darker, so light was fixed in that pass (--error #ef4444 -> #c21111, text 3.45 -> 5.70, white-on-fill 3.76 -> 6.21).

Affected: .notification-badge (renders on all 11 routes), .btn-danger, .failed-count, .summary-value, .failed-streams-alert.

PROPOSAL from the agent, endorsed: let --error be the SOLID FILL, and migrate the 97 'color: var(--error)' text sites to the existing --danger-text, which already measures 5.48 dark and 5.81 HC. Many of those 97 are in modal CSS, so this should either precede or ride with the modal pass (bead xhldy).

Explicitly a single atomic change: doing it partially is worse than not at all, for the same reason a partial hoist is worse than none — the diff looks done and half the surfaces render the old way. Same rule as docs/css_guidelines.md section Load order.

Sizing: Medium.

title: Settings IA: group the 18-destination flat list and relocate what does not belong
description:
PO: 'the settings navigation is just one giant blob of things.' Wants categories plus relocations, a proposal document reviewed before any code, and the whole thing checked against the approved operator-workspace IA.

MEASURED STATE
18 destinations, flat. The approved IA (docs/design/operator-workspace-information-architecture.md) already splits the drill-in into Settings (14) and Administration (4: Authentication, User Management, TLS Certificates, MCP Integration), so the blob is specifically the 14.

Two structural facts that matter as much as the naming:
- EIGHT of the 18 pages are rendered INLINE inside SettingsTab.tsx, which is 6,314 lines (general, appearance, channel-defaults, channel-pipeline, email, integrations, m3u-digest, maintenance). The other ten are proper components under settings/. That inconsistency is why Settings is hard to reason about.
- NormalizationEngineSection.tsx is 2,579 lines on its own — larger than most whole routes.

PO DECISIONS
a. Grouping PLUS relocations, with a plan and beads under this epic.
b. Check against the approved IA doc's commitments — Back-control semantics, aria-current, the SYSTEM / SETTINGS / <SECTION> crumb, routeHierarchy.test.ts enforcing a non-empty crumb per section, StickySectionNav placement='rail'.
c. Proposal document first, reviewed before code.

CONSTRAINT: beads 2896r.16/.17 are IN FLIGHT and UNCOMMITTED in exactly these files — the Settings drill-in nav and the hoisting of section headings into the breadcrumb, including the new untracked settingsSections.ts registry. Any proposal must build on that work, not contradict or duplicate it.

LOOKUP TABLES — PO's premise corrected by measurement. The PO believed this could be eliminated because 'we killed off the enhanced Dummy EPGs'. Verified against the running instance: ZERO lookup tables are configured ([] from /api/lookup-tables), but Dummy EPG is ALIVE AND IN USE — an enabled profile named 'B1G Advanced EPG' with live regex patterns. No profile references the {name|lookup:tablename} pipe.

So the lookup-table SUB-FEATURE has zero adoption while the rest of Dummy EPG works. Removing it is a deprecation of a live, fully wired feature — lookup_tables DB table and model, a registered CRUD router (backend/routers/lookup_tables.py), _resolve_lookups in dummy_epg.py, the pipe in frontend/src/utils/templateEngine.ts, and the LookupTableSection UI — not a dead-code deletion. It needs a migration answer for instances that DO have tables, and a decision on whether the template pipe survives without its UI.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECISIONS D1-D5, taken one at a time.

D1 GROUP NAMES — as proposed, WITH ONE AMENDMENT. PO: 'Not a fan of Scheduled tasks being in Notifications and Reports. That seems more like Upkeep.' Correct — Scheduled Tasks is EPG refresh, M3U refresh and database cleanup, which is upkeep not reporting. Final assignment:
  Connections            General, Integrations
  Channel Processing     Channel Defaults, Channel Normalization, Tags, Channel Pipeline
  Notifications & Reports  Notifications, M3U Digest
  Upkeep                 Backup & Restore, Maintenance, Scheduled Tasks
  Workspace              Appearance, Linked Accounts
  Administration         Authentication, User Management, TLS Certificates, MCP Integration
Also better balanced at 2 and 3 rather than 3 and 2. 'Upkeep' over 'System' (the primary nav already uses SYSTEM for the group containing Settings) and over 'Maintenance' (a destination inside the group carries that name).

D2 LOOKUP TABLES — FULL REMOVAL INCLUDING THE PIPE (option R2-D, not the recommended R2-B). Drop the pipe from both template engines, the CRUD router, the LookupTable model, and the lookup_tables table via a destructive migration, plus a blocking upgrade note. Medium, not Small.
The PO chose the fuller option over my recommendation, and the evidence supports it: the pipe cannot affect real output today. Verified — _resolve_lookups is called only from /preview and /preview/batch, while generate_xmltv neither accepts nor passes a lookups argument, so {x|lookup:y} resolves in PREVIEW and silently does not in the generated XMLTV. Removal eliminates that preview/production divergence rather than documenting it. Zero tables exist on this instance and no profile references the pipe; a profile structurally cannot bind one (33 columns, none stores a lookup id).

D3 FOURTH BREADCRUMB CRUMB — NO. Three crumbs stay (SYSTEM / SETTINGS / SECTION). The group is already visible in the sidebar with aria-current, and four parts compete for width at 1280x720. App.tsx needs no change and routeHierarchy.test.ts keeps its contract.

D4 LINKED ACCOUNTS — NOT NOW. Stays in Settings under Workspace. Revisit once the header account menu has a settings surface. Note the proposal disproved my premise that Appearance was per-viewer: every field including theme writes the global settings blob, so Appearance is not a candidate for relocation either.

D5 SEQUENCING — REMOVAL FIRST, then grouping, then refactor. Gets the destructive migration and its upgrade note out while the reasoning is fresh, and the grouping then lands against 17 destinations rather than 18.

STILL BLOCKING EVERYTHING: beads 2896r.16/.17 own SettingsTab.tsx and the untracked settingsSections.ts uncommitted. No child of this epic can start until they land.

title: Guard has no tier for declaration-site / render-site chunk mismatch
description:
The three existing guard tiers all model DUPLICATE DECLARATIONS: tiers 1 and 2 fire when one selector is declared in two different chunks, tier 3 when two files in one chunk declare it. They are blind to the opposite and more dangerous shape — a class declared in ONE chunk and RENDERED from another.

The .sr-only defect (bead zncyv) was exactly this and all three tiers were green for its entire lifetime, correctly: .sr-only had exactly one declaration in the whole tree, so nothing ever collided. It shipped in the ChannelPipelineTab chunk while OperatorDashboard (eager) and SettingsTab rendered it, so two aria-live regions displayed as ordinary visible text until an operator happened to open Channel Pipeline.

Why this half is worse than the collision half: a collision at least renders SOMETHING in both orders, so it tends to be noticed. A missing declaration renders nothing until an unrelated navigation happens — and here it silently disabled an accessibility affordance, which is the category least likely to be reported by a user.

Sketch of a TIER 4, from the agent that fixed zncyv: extract className literals from every TSX, map each to its chunk via the existing deriveChunks(), and assert that every class token a component renders is declared in a chunk that component's chunk is guaranteed to have loaded. Non-trivial — dynamic classNames (template literals, clsx-style conditionals) and legitimately-never-declared utility class names both generate noise — so it needs a measured false-positive budget before the gate shape is chosen, exactly as tiers 2 and 3 did. Both of those found the noise fear did not survive measurement.

Sizing: Medium.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION to a supporting fact, plus a second live instance found.

WRONG — I wrote that '.sr-only had exactly one declaration in the whole tree, so nothing ever collided'. Two declarations existed until commit 108ff499: ActionEditor.css:486 and ConditionEditor.css:262, verified at 108ff499^ and 266356ff^. Tiers 1 and 2 stayed green correctly, but the reason was SAME-CHUNK (both in ChannelPipelineTab), not single-declaration. And tier 3 did not catch it only because tier 3 was born in 108ff499 — the very commit that deleted the duplicate.

The bead's CONCLUSION is unaffected: the guard models duplicate declarations and is blind to declaration-site/render-site mismatch. But the supporting fact I used to argue it was wrong, and a reader checking it would have found the contradiction.

SECOND LIVE INSTANCE, found during the audit: .filters-bar. Declared bare in JournalTab.css:91 and M3UChangesTab.css:148; the only render site is WatchHistoryPanel.tsx:141, whose sole importer is StatsTab.tsx:22 — a THIRD chunk. The scoped .watch-history-panel .filters-bar wins every overlapping property except flex-shrink:0, which the bare rules supply cross-chunk. The existing guard classifies this as a Journal/M3U collision, which is not what it is. Good evidence for the tier-4 design: the current model names the wrong two chunks.

Possible third: .detail-section — Journal declares it bare, M3U Changes also renders it.

CONFIRMED: tiers 1/2 fire on cross-chunk duplicates and tier 3 on same-chunk (test titles at sharedClassChunkLeak.audit.test.ts:714, 732, 806); .sr-only shipped in the ChannelPipelineTab chunk while OperatorDashboard (eager, App.tsx:18) and SettingsTab rendered it; five call sites total; the tier-4 sketch needs a measured false-positive budget, with UNTRIAGED_BUDGET and SAME_CHUNK_UNTRIAGED_BUDGET as the precedent.

title: Modal chrome no longer shrinks below 600px: ModalBase's responsive block was dead and is now deleted
description:
Surfaced and deliberately NOT fixed by bead 87o0c, because fixing it is a design change rather than a render-neutral reconciliation.

ModalBase.css carried an @media (max-width: 600px) block overriding .modal-header / .modal-body / .modal-footer padding to 0.875rem 1rem / 1rem. It NEVER RENDERED. A media query adds no specificity, and StreamsPane.css declared the same three selectors bare and unconditionally, emitted after the whole of ModalBase in the eager bundle. Confirmed live: modal header padding measures 16px 20px at a 500px viewport, exactly as at 1600px.

87o0c made ModalBase the sole owner of the modal chassis. Had the dead block been left in place it would have COME ALIVE and shrunk every modal's chrome below 600px — a change nobody asked for, arriving as a side effect of a consolidation. So it was deleted, preserving what renders today.

The open question is whether the original intent was right: should modal chrome tighten on narrow viewports? The authored values were 0.875rem 1rem for header/footer and 1rem for body, against today's 16px 20px and 20px. Restoring them is a one-block change to ModalBase.css and affects every modal in the product at <=600px.

Note .modal-overlay { padding: .5rem } and .modal-footer { flex-wrap: wrap } from the same media block DID render and were kept.
close_reason: Shipped with hw8e3 in PR #829 (merge 567f0ef2): accessible 700px modal chrome/reflow tier.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CLOSED AS NOT APPLICABLE. PO states the minimum supported viewport is 1280x720; mobile is explicitly not a target.

The deleted block was @media (max-width: 600px). At a 1280 floor it can never fire, so restoring it would change nothing any supported user sees. Measured a real dialog (M3U account editor) at 1280x720 against the live app: header padding 16px 20px, body 20px, footer 16px 20px — the unconditional values, exactly as at 1600px.

The vertical budget is already behaving correctly at that size: container 638px against a 648px (90vh) cap with 82px free, body 504px against a 504px (70vh) cap, and 797px of form content scrolling inside the body while header and footer stay pinned.

If dialog chrome should tighten, the question is height-driven, not width-driven — the frame costs 132px (65 header + 67 footer) before any content, 18% of a 720px viewport, taken out of the 504px the form gets. That belongs to the spacing decisions in the look refactor, not to a one-off media query.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REOPENED. I CLOSED THIS ON WRONG REASONING AND NEARLY CAUSED AN ACCESSIBILITY REGRESSION.

I closed this as 'not applicable' because the PO's minimum supported viewport is 1280x720 and the block is @media (max-width: 600px), so I concluded it 'can never fire for a supported user'. That is false.

BROWSER ZOOM SHRINKS THE CSS VIEWPORT. At 1280 physical px:
  150% zoom -> ~853 CSS px  (nothing fires)
  160%      -> 800 CSS px   (the 820px block fires)
  180%      -> ~711         (+ the 700px block)
  200%      -> 640          (+ all six 600px blocks, including ModalBase's two)
  220%      -> ~582         (+ the 500px block)

WCAG 1.4.4 requires 200% resize support. At 200% zoom on the PO's own minimum screen, every 600px block fires. So these are not dead — they are the ONLY responsive modal behaviour the app has at accessible zoom levels.

'Minimum supported viewport 1280x720' governs physical windows. It says nothing about CSS px, which is what a media query measures.

THIS IS THE SAME ERROR SHAPE AS EVERY OTHER ONE I HAVE MADE THIS SESSION: I took a property of the DECLARATION (a max-width number) and asserted it as a property of the RENDER (unreachability). Identical to calling .header-actions dead because StatsTab.tsx renders no such element, when PageHeader.tsx renders the class on that very route.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ORIGINAL QUESTION. Bead 87o0c deleted ModalBase's @media (max-width:600px) header/body/footer padding block, correctly, because it was dead for a DIFFERENT and real reason: a media query adds no specificity and StreamsPane declared the same selectors bare and unconditionally, so it never rendered even at 600px. That deletion stands. But the question this bead asks — should modal chrome tighten on narrow viewports — is LIVE again, because 'narrow viewport' includes a zoomed 1280px screen, which is a supported configuration.

So the real question is: at 200% zoom the modal frame currently costs 16px 20px of header and footer padding on a 640 CSS px viewport. Should it tighten? The authored intent was 0.875rem 1rem. That intent now looks correct rather than moot.

Reopening. Related: bead hw8e3 instructs deleting nine media-query blocks on the same false premise and must be corrected before anyone acts on it.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: 2026-08-11 refreshed exact-build spike: 1280 physical px at 200% is 640 CSS px, so max-width:600 does NOT fire at the required 200% point. Current header padding is already 8px 20px; restoring old 14px vertical padding would enlarge it. At 640x360 current dialogs have 49px headers, 66px footers, 90vh/323px max containers, scrollable bodies, and no document horizontal overflow. Implement jointly with hw8e3 as a 700px zoom/reflow tier: overlay 8px, max-height 95vh, header 8px 16px, body 16px, footer 14px 16px/wrap, single-column form rows. Preserve 820 complex rail collapse and 500 compact component behavior.

title: Reconcile 31 same-chunk cascade collisions (17 partial-merge, 14 shadow)
description:
GAP FOUND BY THE PO. The P1 sweep left these deliberately, and mklhu covers BUILDING A GUARD to detect them, but nothing owned the actual reconciliation. This bead does.

Distinct from the cross-chunk defect the sweep fixed. All 23 have both copies in the EAGER bundle, so the winner is deterministic per build rather than dependent on tab-visit order. But deterministic only means it breaks the same way every time — in every case below the later rule does NOT fully shadow the earlier one, so the element renders a MERGE of two authors' intentions that neither wrote. That is the same partial-redeclaration hybrid documented in docs/css_guidelines.md, one level up.

Measured against HEAD (266356ff), 23 classes, three clusters:

STREAMSPANE vs COMMON.CSS — 9 classes, an extraction that was never finished:
.checkbox-option, .collapsible-content, .collapsible-title, .filter-dropdown-menu, .filter-dropdown-options, .preview-item, .preview-list, .radio-option — plus .pane-content and .pane-header-actions from ChannelsPane. common.css is emitted LAST in the eager bundle so it wins on shared properties, and the pane copies contribute only the properties common.css never declares. Likely resolution: delete the pane copies, as Wave 0 did for .pane-header h2 and the Channel Manager wave did for .search-input.

MODAL CHASSIS carried by the panes — 6 classes:
.modal-overlay (ChannelsPane + ModalBase + StreamsPane), .modal-header, .modal-body, .modal-footer, .modal-btn, .logo-option-none. ModalBase.css should own the modal chassis outright; the panes' copies predate it. Note bead 6z299.2 hit the same shape in TagEngineSection and chose to SCOPE rather than convert, because that modal's geometry genuinely differed — check each of these before assuming deletion is safe.

TWO PANES RENDERED SIDE BY SIDE — 3 classes:
.group-drag-handle, .inline-stream-actions, .preview-name in ChannelsPane vs StreamsPane. Highest visibility of the three clusters: the panes sit next to each other in the Channel Manager split view, so any divergence is directly comparable on screen rather than latent.

Plus .operator-dashboard (App.css vs OperatorDashboard.css) and .setup-hint (SettingsModal.css vs SetupPage.css).

WHY THIS IS NOT MECHANICAL. Unlike the sweep's deletions, there is no already-correct answer to restore. Where neither copy shadows the other, reconciling means deciding which appearance is right and accepting that the other changes. Each needs a before/after look, and .preview-list is the only one where one copy fully shadows the other and can simply be deleted.

Sequencing: mklhu (the same-chunk guard tier) should land FIRST or alongside, so the fixes are verified by a check rather than by eye, and so the count cannot silently regrow. mktnb is the cross-chunk sibling of this work and is independent.

Reproduce the list with the script recorded on this bead's session, or re-derive: parse every frontend/src CSS file, keep single-class bare selectors declared in 2+ files where all files are in the eager chunk, and flag those whose property sets differ.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTED by the TIER 3 guard (bead mklhu), which measures cascade contention rather than the cruder 'property sets differ' heuristic I used when filing this.

Accurate count is 31, not 23, split three ways:
- 17 PARTIAL — the element renders a MERGE of two or more files that no single author wrote. This is the dangerous shape and the reason this bead exists.
- 14 SHADOW — the last file wins every contended slot. Harmless TODAY, but 6 of the 14 already discard one author's value silently (e.g. .preview-list: StreamsPane authors max-height:180px, common.css wins with 300px). The guard tracks these deliberately, because the commit that ADDS a duplicate and the commit that makes it render wrong are usually different commits — track only PARTIAL and the failure lands on an innocent later commit.
- 5 DISJOINT — no contention at all, both authors' rules apply as written. Deliberately OUTSIDE the gate: .collapsible-content, .collapsible-header .expand-icon, .filter-dropdown-options, .inline-stream-actions, .pane-header h2. Two of these appear in my original cluster list and should NOT be treated as work.

Also corrected: .operator-dashboard (App.css vs OperatorDashboard.css), which I listed, is already resolved in the tree. And the true set is not limited to single-class selectors — .modal-btn:disabled, .rule-active-window legend and an @media variant are in scope and were missing from my list.

The PO's acceptance bar is RENDER-NEUTRAL BY DEFAULT: fold the losing copy's unique properties into the surviving rule so zero pixels move. For the 6 SHADOW cases that silently discard an authored value, render-neutral means preserving what RENDERS today, not what was authored — the discarded value stays discarded, and the fix is to stop two files claiming the class, not to resurrect a value nobody has seen.

Modal chassis (6 of the set): PO decision is INVESTIGATE FIRST — measure each pane modal against ModalBase and convert only where conversion is provably render-neutral; scope otherwise. Anything where conversion would be an improvement but changes geometry is to be reported as a recommendation, not done.

TIER 3 is now in the tree and green, so this work can be verified by a check rather than by eye, and the count cannot silently regrow.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
All 31 resolved. TIER 3 PARTIAL 17->0, SHADOW 14->0, KNOWN_SAME_CHUNK_MERGES emptied. The 5 DISJOINT are untouched and remain deliberately out of gate. Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 177 files / 2481 tests passing.

THE MODAL-CHASSIS PREMISE IN MY BRIEF WAS INVERTED, and this is the finding that mattered. The bead said the pane copies 'predate ModalBase' and warned conversion might change geometry. In fact ChannelsPane.css and StreamsPane.css are eager and emitted AFTER ModalBase.css, so their bare copies were the LIVE chassis for every modal in the app (~70 components render .modal-header/.modal-body/.modal-footer/.modal-btn) and ModalBase's own tokens were dead:
  .modal-header padding  token 0.5rem   -> actually rendering 16px 20px
  .modal-body padding    token 1rem     -> actually 20px
  .modal-overlay bg      token rgba(0,0,0,0.6) -> actually 0.7
  .modal-btn             token 0.625rem 1rem / radius-lg / 3-prop transition -> actually 0.5rem 1rem / 4px / background-color only
  border colour          var(--border-color) -- DEFINED NOWHERE, so ModalBase would have painted a fixed hex in every theme where the live rule was theme-aware var(--border-primary)
So deleting the pane copies alone would have moved geometry across the whole product. The render-neutral conversion was to delete them AND re-point ModalBase's five stale token defaults plus three .modal-btn values to what was rendering. Each token has exactly one consumer inside ModalBase, so the change is provably local. ModalBase now owns the chassis outright and zero pixels move. No scoping was needed; the TagEngineSection precedent did not apply because that modal is already correctly scoped.

DEAD RESPONSIVE BLOCK: ModalBase's @media (max-width:600px) header/body/footer paddings never rendered — a media query adds no specificity and the pane rules were unconditional. Once ModalBase owned the chassis they would have COME ALIVE and shrunk every modal's chrome below 600px as a side effect of the consolidation. Deleted, preserving what renders. Spun out as bead 79uf8. The overlay padding and footer flex-wrap from the same block DID render and were kept.

THREE RULES WITH NO RENDER SITE AT ALL: .conflict-options and .logo-option-none in ChannelsPane.css (both rendered by StreamsPane/BulkEPGAssignModal and EditChannelModal/AutoSyncSettingsModal respectively, with ChannelsPane silently setting their gap and adding a margin), and .norm-group-disabled, which no TSX in the tree emits — two dead copies deleted.

EVIDENCE: pre/post builds served side by side with all ten route chunks installed. 66 computed-style measurements at 1600x1000 and 500x900 — 64 identical, the 2 differences both on .norm-group-disabled, the class nothing renders. 26 pseudo-class rules byte-identical via CSSOM dump. Duplicate bare selectors inside one built stylesheet 22 -> 1. Screenshots of six surfaces, with a same-build control run reproducing identical pixel counts in identical cells, proving the residual diffs are animation noise. Negative control: re-adding .preview-list{max-height:180px} makes TIER 3 fail, removing it restores green — the guard is live, not vacuous.

Also read properties the guard cannot see (transition, box-sizing, user-select, font-style, font:inherit, clip) and found several of them live — worth remembering when reading any tier's 'contended' list.

SPUN OUT, not fixed, because each changes what renders: bead d3ubm (.sr-only aria-live regions render as VISIBLE TEXT on Dashboard and Settings until Channel Pipeline is visited — P1 accessibility), bead 79uf8 (modal chrome below 600px), bead 4nn2o (checkbox/radio asymmetry inherited from the deleted duplicate).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: CORRECTION: my earlier comment on this bead cited 'bead d3ubm' for the .sr-only accessibility defect. That ID does not exist — I fabricated it after a truncated bd create output, rather than looking it up. The real bead is enhancedchannelmanager-zncyv. No other ID in that comment is affected (79uf8 and 4nn2o are both real and verified).

title: Guard blind spot: same-chunk (eager-vs-eager) collisions are invisible by construction
description:
The Wave 3 guard keys collisions on CHUNK identity: it fails when one bare selector carrying typography or layout properties is declared in two DIFFERENT bundle chunks. That is correct for the defect class it was built for — the lazy-chunk visit-order leak, four historical instances.

But it is blind by construction to collisions where both files are in the SAME chunk, and the eager bundle is one chunk containing index.css, common.css, App.css, ChannelsPane.css, StreamsPane.css, ChannelManagerTab.css, ModalBase.css, PendingMergesPage.css, EditMode.css and ~30 modals.

This is not theoretical. The cleanup pass fixed a live user-visible P1 that the guard could not see: ChannelProfilesListModal.css and ChannelsPane.css BOTH declare .channel-item, both eager, and ChannelsPane is emitted later — so its display:grid destroyed the modal's flex row and the Manage Channels list rendered channel names in a 32px track. The guard was green throughout.

Same-chunk collisions are deterministic per build rather than visit-order dependent, so they are a different defect class — but 'deterministic' only means it breaks the same way every time, not that it is correct. Rollup's emission order is an implementation detail nobody is asserting on.

Proposal: a third tier keyed on BYTE ORDER within a chunk rather than chunk identity. It should report same-chunk bare duplicates where the later declaration does not fully shadow the earlier one, since that is the shape that produces surprise. Spec section 5 already lists several with genuinely conflicting values that Wave 1 left alone for exactly this reason: .logo-option-none, .modal-btn, .preview-more, .setup-hint, .pane-header, .search-input, .edit-mode-*.

Expect noise; the existing tier-2 work showed the fear of noise did not survive measurement, so measure before deciding the shape.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
TIER 3 landed, green, proven against the real defect. Suite is 177 files / 2481 tests, 2481 passing (+13: TIER 3, its config guard, and 11 classifier unit tests).

EMISSION ORDER WAS DERIVED AND THEN MEASURED, not assumed. The agent read Vite's actual vite:css-post renderChunk source (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:20714) rather than working from memory, reimplemented bundler execution order, then validated it: for every source CSS file it found class tokens unique to that file, located them in the built stylesheet, and ordered files by median byte offset. 108 adjacent comparisons across 15 built stylesheets, ZERO inversions — run twice, on newui HEAD and on a rebuilt 266356ff^.

Two corrections to the existing file's assumptions surfaced by that validation: Vite 8 bundles with ROLLDOWN, not Rollup, so the header's 'Rollup default code-splitting' wording is dated; and deriveChunks() collapses Toast.css/ToastContainer.css into EAGER when the build actually emits them as a separately-linked stylesheet. Neither changes a verdict today; both are documented in the file. The second is a real (currently zero-instance) false-negative in TIER 1/2 — backlog.

CLASSIFICATION, which is better than the heuristic I filed 87o0c with: 17 PARTIAL (element renders a merge no author wrote), 14 SHADOW (last file wins every contended slot), 5 DISJOINT (no contention — excluded from the gate). SHADOW is deliberately INCLUDED despite being harmless today, on the reasoning that the commit which adds a duplicate and the commit which makes it render wrong are usually different commits; tracking only PARTIAL would land the failure on an innocent later commit. Six of the 14 already discard an authored value silently.

SHORTHAND/LONGHAND CLOSED AT MEASURED ZERO COST — the largest named gap in TIER 1/2. Expanding shorthands adds zero reported selectors on both HEAD and 266356ff^, because every group containing a shorthand/longhand pair was already reported via a literal property. So no false-positive budget is spent, and a page can no longer evade the tier by writing padding-left against a shared padding. border-radius deliberately not treated as part of border.

PROOF: at 266356ff^ TIER 3 reports the .channel-item collision verbatim — 'NEW PARTIAL EAGER :: .channel-item, contended: align-items, column-gap, cursor, display, gap, padding, DIVERGENT VALUES: display, padding', naming ChannelProfilesListModal.css:226 and ChannelsPane.css:1042 with their emission positions. That is the live user-visible P1 fixed in 266356ff, which TIER 1 and TIER 2 were green through.

Eight failure drills, each reverted with the file byte-identical afterwards, including a SHAPE CHANGED branch and both !important cases — !important appears 47 times in the tree but never inside a same-chunk multi-file group, so that branch would otherwise have shipped untested.

TIER 2 reported no NEW LEAK on any run while the concurrent mktnb agent was working.

title: StreamsPane's bare .filter-select is eager and live in three chunks, two of them frozen chrome
description:
Found during the Channel Manager remap, and deliberately NOT fixed there.

StreamsPane.css declares .filter-select bare. StreamsPane is in the EAGER bundle, and the class is consumed by three chunks: Channel Manager's own stream filter, plus Journal's and M3U Changes' filter triggers — and BOTH of those toolbars are portaled into the FROZEN route-header band via RouteHeaderSlot.

So the bare eager rule is what actually draws the box those frozen-band triggers sit in. Scoping it to .streams-pane would silently restyle frozen chrome on two routes that the Channel Manager wave does not own. The agent remapped its font-size only and verified live that both tabs' filter boxes stay pixel-identical at 218x48.

Fixing this properly means deciding what the frozen band's filter trigger should look like and changing it deliberately, with the band's geometry re-verified against beads 57pp3, eupzi, sccol and sl7dx. That is frozen-band work, not content-pane work.

Related, same shape: Wave 1 already had to invent a per-page journal-filter-select class because .filter-select .custom-select-trigger was colliding across Journal and M3U Changes. This bead is the remaining half of that problem.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #828 (merge 140d3d10): private filter ownership and exact-build route-order/responsive guard.

title: Stats route-header band: the whole .header-left subtree is portaled and still off-scale
description:
Found during the Stats remap. The P1 spec's exclusion list under-covers Stats: RouteHeaderSlot name='status' wraps the ENTIRE .header-left subtree (StatsTab.tsx:889), not just the .summary-stat family at 87-118 and the :has(.header-summary) block at 1071-1173 that the spec lists.

So .header-left, the whole .provider-live-table* family, .refresh-indicator and .refresh-select are ALL portaled into the frozen route-header band. The Wave 2 agent correctly left every one of them alone.

They still carry four --text-muted text sites (the 2.61:1 light-theme AA failure) and six off-scale sizes: 15px, 14px, 0.8125rem, 0.6875rem x2, 0.8rem.

This needs its own bead because it is frozen-band work: the band's geometry was settled by beads 57pp3, eupzi, sccol and sl7dx, so any change here has to be verified against that frozen chrome rather than treated as content-pane remapping. Do not fold it back into the P1 sweep.

Related, same area: .header-actions at StatsTab.css:196 is DEAD in StatsTab.tsx (no element renders it) but is bare in a lazy chunk, so once Stats has been visited it overrides PageHeader's .header-actions in the frozen band on every page. It sits in the guard's TIER 2 baseline under 6z299.1. Deleting it is layout-only and needs frozen-band verification, which is why it was not done inline.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Complete. Contrast fixed, geometry held, and the bead's own claims corrected on every count.

WHAT I CLAIMED vs WHAT IS TRUE:
- 'Four --text-muted sites' — actually FIVE, and only TWO were in scope. The other three sit inside the PO's uncommitted 2896r.21 hunks, one of them a rule the PO added. Left alone.
- 'Six off-scale sizes: 15px, 14px, 0.8125rem, 0.6875rem x2, 0.8rem' — actually 13 declarations across 12 rules, 8 of them in the PO's hunks. My list was also half-derived from the WORKING TREE rather than HEAD: 15px exists only in the PO's uncommitted work and never in the committed file. It omitted .refresh-indicator's 0.75rem, both 14px icon sizes, and five literals in the PO's tail block.
- '.header-actions is dead' — TRUE that StatsTab.tsx renders no such element, but MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE and I nearly caused a bad deletion. The CLASS is rendered on the Stats route by PageHeader.tsx:73, which emits <div className='header-actions' data-page-header-slot='primary-action'> and Stats fills it with Refresh. StatsTab.css's bare copy was therefore LIVE on Stats and on every route visited after Stats. It was harmless only by coincidence: it declared common.css's five properties with byte-identical values and omitted flex-shrink:0, which still applied from common.css by per-property cascade. Deletion is render-neutral, verified on six routes.

CHANGED (StatsTab.css only): .provider-live-table thead th -> micro role + --text-secondary; .refresh-indicator -> meta size + --text-secondary; .provider-live-table -> --type-body-size (identical 13px); two 14px icon sizes -> --icon-badge (identical); .refresh-select -> --type-body-size; .header-actions deleted with a pointer comment.

THIRD UNDEFINED VARIABLE FOUND: .provider-live-table tr.unknown-bucket td used var(--accent-warning, ...), and --accent-warning is defined NOWHERE in the tree — verified, zero definitions, one reference. So the high-contrast theme's --warning never reached it and the hardcoded fallback always won. Same defect class as --error-color (PrintGuideModal, bead 6z299.3) and --border-color (ModalBase, bead 87o0c). Corrected to var(--warning).

CONTRAST, measured in all three themes at 1600x1000:
  .provider-live-table thead th   dark 4.82->6.46   light 2.61->5.27   HC 8.52->15.00
  .refresh-indicator              dark 4.82->6.46   light 2.61->5.27   HC 8.52->15.00
  unknown-bucket row              HC 9.22->10.37 (dark and light unchanged)

GEOMETRY HELD: header.header exactly 45.00px in all three themes on Stats AND on M3U Manager / Journal / M3U Changes / Channel Pipeline / EPG Manager / Dashboard visited after Stats. .route-page-header 107.28, .page-header-status 24.78, .header-left 24.78, the summary strip 24.19, .refresh-indicator 24.78, route .header-actions 30.00 — all identical before and after. The condensed provider table does not render live (5 providers against a >6 threshold), so its exact markup was injected and measured at 7, 8 and 9 rows in all three themes: identical. The micro remap shrinks the th row 29 -> 27.5px, but .provider-live-table-wrapper caps at max-height 220px and the table exceeds that at the smallest count that renders at all, so the wrapper is pinned and the band never sees it. That measurement is what justified taking the th onto its role rather than leaving it off-scale.

FAR WORSE CONTRAST BUG FOUND, deliberately not fixed here and handed to bead dlavh: .refresh-indicator.active uses color: var(--success-text), the token for text drawn ON a success fill. As a foreground on the page background it measures 1.09:1 in light (#fff on #f5f5f5 — the glyph is invisible) and 1.06:1 in high contrast. The obvious fix does not work either: --success is 5.97 dark / 14.43 HC but only 2.09 light. .status-success in common.css has the identical problem app-wide, which is the same 2.09:1 this bead already names via .status-label. One root cause, several surfaces, and a token decision rather than a frozen-band CSS change.

PO-DESIGN INTERACTION TO FLAG: above 6 providers .header-left is 300.97px tall and lands in the PO's grid-column 2 / grid-row 1 beside the h1, making the route header 383px. The 2896r.21 compact strip is one-line by construction (flex-wrap:nowrap, overflow-x); the condensed-table branch is not. Pre-existing, not introduced here, but the PO should know that branch exists.

JUSTIFIED DEVIATION: edited one data line in cssAudits/sharedClassChunkLeak.audit.test.ts, which the brief forbade. Deleting .header-actions moves its TIER 2 baseline chunk set from [EAGER, JournalTab, M3UChangesTab, StatsTab] to [EAGER, JournalTab, M3UChangesTab], and TIER 2 fails on CHUNKS MOVED — the guard's own message says to update the chunks deliberately. The deletion is not shippable without it. Only that line plus a comment and a stale line reference; no tier structure touched.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 179 files / 2488 tests passing, guard 16/16 with TIER 1 = 0.

title: Scope 15 bare cross-chunk layout collisions found by the extended guard
description:
Surfaced by the tier-2 (layout/paint) extension of the cross-chunk guard, which covers width/height/padding/margin/display/position/flex/grid/colour/background/border/cursor in addition to typography. These 15 belong to no wave of the P1 consolidation — same class of work as Wave 1, just found by a wider net. Filed separately rather than bolted onto 6z299.2, which is already dispatched and scoped.

NINE render differently TODAY depending on tab-visit order:
.form-row (display AND gap, across three chunks), .drag-handle + :hover + :active (colour), .checkbox-group (gap), .radio-group (gap), .group-item (align-items), .profile-card (border-radius), .profile-actions (gap), .details-grid + its @media variant (grid-template-columns), .current-logo-preview (margin-bottom).

The rest are identical-value duplicates — latent, one edit away from diverging.

They are held in the guard's KNOWN_CROSS_CHUNK_LAYOUT baseline under bead: 'NEEDS-TRIAGE', with an UNTRIAGED_BUDGET of 15 that may only be lowered. Retiring this bead means scoping each one and deleting its baseline entry; the guard fails loudly on a stale entry, so the baseline cannot silently rot.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
All 15 resolved. TIER 2 baseline 30 -> 15 entries (all remaining owned by 6z299.x); UNTRIAGED_BUDGET 15 -> 0. Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 177 files / 2481 tests all passing, TIER 1 = 0.

METHOD: 11 scoped with :where() so each site keeps its own authored value and stops donating; 4 deleted as provably redundant; 2 hoisted to a single owner (.updated-label/.updated-time were byte-identical in two lazy chunks -> new common.css section 29 plus a guidelines catalogue entry).

MEASURED, NOT REASONED: pre-fix and post-fix builds served side by side on private ports with /api proxied, all ten route chunks installed by walking every route in one context, 31 cascade probes each built under a TSX-verified ancestor chain. 14 owner-surface probes byte-identical across every property — including the three riskiest calls (the .drag-handle reduction, the .radio-group deletion, and both carry-overs). 17 probes changed, every one a VICTIM page restored to its own author's value: .form-row at the M3U account modal grid->flex, .drag-handle justify-content center->normal on Pipeline and Streams, .checkbox-group padding 8px 0->0 off Settings/ScheduleEditor/bulk-create, .profile-card at cloud targets flex->block, .current-logo-preview at Edit Channel 16px->12px. :hover/:active compared by dumping live CSSOM rules, since computed style cannot reach them.

SIX ERRORS IN MY BRIEF, two of which would have caused regressions:
1. .form-row at RuleBuilder has NO CONSUMER — Channel Pipeline never renders the class. The rule existed purely to donate display:flex to Settings' Email grid. Deleted, not scoped.
2. .current-logo-preview in LogoModal declares ONLY margin-bottom; the whole box comes from ChannelsPane. The symmetric scope-both-sides move I specified would have stripped LogoModal's box. Scoped one side only.
3. .checkbox-group cannot be scoped to .rule-builder — EventSyncRuleEditor and BulkRuleSettingsModal ride the same chunk and take their padding/wrap from RuleBuilder's bare rule. Route root used instead.
4. .profiles-list cannot be scoped on both sides — StreamsPane's bulk-create picker takes its scrollability from ChannelProfilesListModal's eager rule and sits under no shared ancestor. Left bare with a comment.
5. .drag-handle's 'divergent color' is a GUARD ARTEFACT. Both cross-chunk copies use var(--drag-handle-color); the divergence came from a THIRD copy (StreamsPane, color:inherit) in the same EAGER chunk, because the guard stores one value per chunk. The real divergence was justify-content. Worth knowing when reading any TIER 2 'divergent' annotation.
6. The test baseline I quoted (2468) was stale — the concurrent TIER 3 agent had added 13 tests.

FLAGGED FOR PO VETO: .group-item input[type=checkbox] in DeleteOrphanedGroupsModal was donating a 0.75rem right / 0.25rem top margin to PRINT GUIDE's checkbox whenever the Settings chunk was loaded. Scoped with the rest of its family, so Print Guide's checkbox now sits on its own 0.75rem flex gap alone. Same-family scoping also applied to .group-item:last-child/:hover/.selected and .profile-card:hover/.inactive/.default. Any of these can be unscoped on request.

BACKLOG FOUND: StreamsPane.css .radio-group{gap:0.75rem} is dead code — common.css is emitted last in eager (byte 268,131 of 273,289 vs StreamsPane at 173,984), so every StreamsPane radio group renders at common's 0.5rem. Fixing it would change render, so it was left. Also corrected a stale in-file comment in DeleteOrphanedGroupsModal.css that claimed both files were in the eager bundle — they are the Settings and Guide chunks.

title: Modals join the P1 type scale
description:
The P1 sweep is content-pane only by PO decision, so ~40 modals keep their pre-P1 sizes while every page behind them moves to the P1 scale. Consistent (all modals lag together) but it is a visible seam that will invite piecemeal drift.

Nine Channel Pipeline stylesheets are modal-only and untouched: RuleBuilder, ActionEditor, ConditionEditor, BulkRuleSettingsModal, EventSyncRuleEditor, EventSyncPreviewPanel, EventSyncTestPatternsPanel, EventSyncAutoSyncFixDialog, ProviderScopedGroupPicker. Plus the modal ranges inside otherwise-swept files: ChannelsPane 2148-4971, StreamsPane 768-1728, NormalizationEngineSection 647-1337, and the Probe Results / Plex token modals living inside SettingsTab.css.

Wave 0 already moved a few shared classes across the modal line by PO decision (.group-name/.group-count, .file-name/.file-size, .badge, .btn-*), so the modals are already partially on the scale — which strengthens the argument for finishing rather than leaving them half-migrated.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. Follow-up to update those assertions rides with hmr0e.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
PO DECIDED — four decisions, taken one at a time.

1. SCOPE. Finish the type scale into modals NOW as a bounded project; the broader look refactor is a SEPARATE project. Rationale surfaced during the decision: the sweep delivered a typography system (27 --type-* tokens, 636 references, one owner per shared class, three guard tiers) but NOT a design system. The real content of a look refactor is spacing — --space-* tokens exist and have THREE uses against 2,312 hardcoded paddings and margins. That is why components look inconsistent, and it needs its own preset decision rather than being folded in here.

2. MODAL TITLE takes a DISTINCT role, formalised at roughly its current 17.6px/600, not the 15px section role. A dialog's title is the primary heading of its own surface, closer to a route title than to a panel heading inside a page. ModalBase already carries --modal-title-size: 1.1rem as a bespoke token; that becomes a real role in the scale. Route title stays 20px/700, section stays 15px/600.

3. BUTTONS: tokenise .modal-btn onto the scale and normalise its own contradictory variant naming (it has BOTH .modal-btn-primary and .modal-btn.primary, BOTH .modal-btn-danger and .modal-btn.danger). Do NOT unify it with .btn-* this pass. The two languages genuinely differ — .modal-btn is 0.5rem 1rem / 14.4px / --radius-md against .btn-primary's 0.625rem 1.25rem / 13px / --radius-lg — and unifying changes 168 buttons. That is a vocabulary decision belonging to the look refactor.

4. VERIFICATION: build a dev-only MODAL HARNESS that force-renders every dialog with stub props, and verify all 62 before and after. Every previous round hit the same wall — agents measured what they could reach and reasoned about the rest, honestly but with the risk concentrated in rarely-opened dialogs, which is exactly where a regression goes unnoticed longest. The harness is a repo artefact that stays, and it will be needed again for the look refactor, which touches the same dialogs.

ORCHESTRATOR DECISION (stated, not asked): scope covers the 32 dedicated *Modal.css/*Dialog.css files AND the modal ranges inside page stylesheets — ChannelsPane 2148-4971, StreamsPane 768-1728, NormalizationEngineSection 653+, TagEngineSection 425-534, LookupTableSection 59+, SettingsTab's probe-results and Plex-token blocks, ChannelPipelineTab's four modal blocks. Excluding them would just move the seam inside those files.

ESTATE, measured: 62 TSX render a dialog. 32 dedicated modal/dialog CSS files = 6,858 lines, 319 font-size declarations, 8 tokenised. ModalBase.css = 1,955 lines, 73 font-size, 0 tokenised. 392 font-size declarations total, 12 tokenised (3%), spread across 18+ distinct values. Roughly 21% of the CSS estate.

Good news from bead 87o0c: only 3 modals still redeclare the chassis, and ModalBase genuinely owns .modal-overlay/-header/-body/-footer/-btn with its token defaults re-pointed to what actually renders. The structural problem is already solved; what remains is typography and vocabulary.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION to this epic's stated estate, and new measured data for the remap.

MY DIALOG COUNT WAS WRONG THROUGHOUT. Every brief and bead I wrote said 62 dialogs. 62 is the FILE count. The real dialog count is 83 — see bead xhldy.1. The 392 font-size figure was derived from the CSS files and is unaffected, but any plan sized against '62 dialogs' undercounts the verification surface by about a quarter.

VERIFICATION SUBSTRATE IS NOW IN PLACE (xhldy.1, closed): a dev-only harness force-renders 82 of the 83 dialogs with no backend and no login, and a baseline of 1,792 selector-signature rows is captured. The 83rd is ModalOverlay.tsx, the shared wrapper, which is not a dialog and is measured indirectly by all the others. Re-run with node scripts/measure-modal-typography.mjs --diff.

MODAL CONTRAST, measured across all 83 dialogs by the contrast pass (bead dlavh) and handed here: light 64 failures across 27 dialogs, dark 40 across 24, high-contrast 17 across 16. JSON in the scratchpad as modal-audit.json.
IMPORTANT: dlavh's token-level fix already resolved every modal --text-muted site, so that does NOT need carrying into this pass. What remains has different causes: --warning used as a foreground (17 sites), hardcoded rgb(46,204,113) / rgb(231,76,60) / rgb(52,152,219) in probe-results and task pills, .modal-required on --error, .modal-btn-danger, and .filter-mode-badge.include.

DEPENDENCY ADDED: bead 4l51b (the --error dual-role migration) touches many modal CSS files, since a large share of the 97 'color: var(--error)' sites are in modals. It is in flight now. This pass must land AFTER it, or the two will collide in the same files.

Also relevant: bead lw04j records 48 custom properties referenced but never defined, several of which are in modal CSS and one of which (--text-on-accent) produced a literally invisible element. Worth resolving before or with this pass rather than remapping type on rules whose colours resolve to nothing.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
EPIC SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETE. Modal estate is on the P1 type scale, committed 078c2075, deployed, all six rendered-CSS guards green (20 tests).

PO reviewed and accepted all three flagged judgement calls: the 18px title role (vs the 'roughly 17.6px' specified), the sticky Back control, and deleting the .modal-btn dot-variants with 25 markup migrations.

Execution record is bead xhldy.2 (closed). Spun out and filed: ica5t (P1 — login page inputs render in Arial, and the typeface guard structurally cannot see it because it only runs authenticated), dlcl2 (bare .modal-body textarea leaking across chunks), 4axyl (532 modal controls at the UA default), 7su2h (wire the harness --diff into CI), w8u1e (dead 0-1-0 icon rules outside modal scope).

REMAINING IN SCOPE, not done: modal contrast — --warning used as a foreground (17 sites), .filter-mode-badge.include, .modal-required. Outside a type pass by design; bead dlavh's token-level work already resolved every modal --text-muted site.

title: Light-theme contrast failures: --text-muted, status colours, and provider type chips
description:
All pre-existing, none introduced by the type-scale work, all measured.

- --text-muted measures 2.61:1 on --bg-secondary in the light theme — below the AA floor. The P1 sweep moves meta/micro text off it, but it remains on non-meta text, on icon fills, and throughout the modals the sweep does not touch. Highest remaining concentrations by file: ChannelsPane.css 51 uses, ChannelPipelineTab.css 20, StatsTab.css 19, NormalizationEngineSection.css 19, StreamsPane.css 17, ModalBase.css 15, TagEngineSection.css 13, ActionEditor.css 10.
- .status-label green measures 2.09:1 on the row background in the light theme (noted by the f4yc7 pilot).
- .account-type.xc measures 2.70:1 in light and .std 3.28:1 in dark (noted by bead sccol).
- ::placeholder rules (common.css 247, 276, 645, 676, 783) were deliberately exempted from the sweep — placeholder contrast is a separate question and should be decided on its own.
- Recharts tick fills in EnhancedStatsPanel/ProvidersPanel/UserStatsPanel/StatsTab pass var(--text-muted) as a JS prop, so they carry the same failure and are unreachable from CSS.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION + OUTCOME. This bead's DESCRIPTION contains figures I asserted without verifying. Three are wrong. Trust this comment over the description.

WRONG — '.account-type.std 3.28:1 in dark'. Measured: .std is 4.59 in dark and PASSES; it is 1.87 in LIGHT, the worst chip in the app. The 3.28 figure is .xc in dark. I misread an existing code comment about .hdhr and propagated it. .xc actually fails in ALL THREE themes: 2.70 light / 3.27 dark / 4.34 high-contrast.

WRONG — the --text-muted file counts. I wrote 'ChannelsPane 51, ChannelPipelineTab 20, ModalBase 15'. Actual: 35, 14, 2. And it is in SIXTY files with 251 uses, not the seven I listed.

CORRECT — --text-muted 2.61:1 on --bg-secondary in light; .status-label green 2.09:1; .account-type.xc 2.70 light.

OUTCOME — WORK IS COMPLETE. Live contrast failures 140 -> 34 across all 11 routes x 3 themes. Light 101 -> 8, dark 24 -> 15, high-contrast 15 -> 11. Zero regressions, confirmed by signature diff. Four of the original 140 were :disabled controls that WCAG 1.4.3 exempts and the refined audit correctly drops.

METHOD worth reusing: a DOM contrast auditor was built that walks every rendered element on all 11 routes in all 3 themes and resolves each text node's TRUE COMPOSITED foreground and background through alpha, element opacity and ancestor stacking, applying the right AA floor per element (4.5 normal, 3 large/icon). Two bugs in the auditor itself were found and fixed before its numbers were trusted: it was taking background from the parent (reporting every primary button as white-on-page) and counting disabled controls.

ROOT CAUSE, one sentence: light-theme semantic colours were dark-theme values that were never re-toned. So the fix was at TOKEN level, per theme, each value darkened along its own HSL lightness ray so no hue moved — which honoured the PO's 'happy with the look' constraint and fixed 251 --text-muted sites at once INCLUDING every modal file, without editing a single excluded file.

--text-muted was deliberately NOT retired: the step is real and passing in dark (4.82 vs 6.46) and high-contrast (8.52 vs 15.00), so retiring it would flatten two themes the PO likes. In light there is no legal step below --text-secondary, so the two converge there. Documented in index.css and css_guidelines.md as 'muted is a dark-theme distinction'.

title: PreToolUse bead-guard resolves the wrong prefix inside git worktrees
description:
Reported independently by three engineer agents this session.

The PreToolUse bead-guard hook derives the expected bead prefix from the working directory BASENAME. Inside /home/lecaptainc/ecm/wt-newui it therefore demands ids matching 'wt-newui-*', while the repo's real ids are 'enhancedchannelmanager-*'. Any VCS message check performed with cwd inside the worktree is denied.

Workaround agents have been using: run the VCS operation with -C pointing at the worktree while cwd stays in the main checkout. This works but is a trap for every future worktree-based agent, and it is the 'resolve the actual target tree' hook failure mode called out in the shared engineering-discipline notes.

Suggested fix (one line): uncomment the issue-prefix setting in .beads/config.yaml, or have the guard read the prefix from .beads/ rather than the directory basename.

Related: the same guard also pattern-matches VCS keywords inside bd descriptions, so writing a bead ABOUT this bug trips it. Second-order symptom of the same over-broad matching.

Implemented as an opt-in StickySectionNav placement prop: Settings passes 'rail', Stats keeps the default 'top' bar.

Rail is a sticky right-hand column inside the .settings-content grid. Below 1100px it reverts to the original horizontal bar - every rail-only declaration is undone, not just grid placement, since overriding placement alone left a stacked vertical list matching neither layout (PO-reported).

Bug found and fixed during PO review: keepFocusedControlVisible decided whether the nav bounds a control from above using the placement prop, but the rail reverts to a top bar via a CSS media query, so prop and rendered layout disagreed below 1100px. It now decides from geometry - the nav bounds from above only when it overlaps the focused control's horizontal band. This fixed the audited sticky-controls e2e at all three viewports.

The e2e assertion was itself wrong for a rail: 'focused.top >= nav.bottom' only holds for a horizontal bar. Replaced with a rectangle-intersection check, which is the honest invariant in both placements.

- Removed two page headers the class-based sweep missed. LookupTableSection had the class but grep -m1 matched a modal h2 above it; ScheduledTasksSection used an inline-styled header with no class. Scheduled Tasks needed the text block removed while keeping the sibling Refresh button.

title: Operator workspace PO review round 1: nav IA, logo collapse, header status pill, dashboard visual identity, remove footer
description:
PO review of the newui operator workspace (epic enhancedchannelmanager-2896r) raised seven items:
1. Left nav must collapse by clicking the logo (keep the explicit Collapse button too - PO decision).
2. Dashboard cards have no per-card icons, images, or semantic color.
3. Service status moves from the footer to the top bar as a status dot + 'Online'.
4. 'New update available' moves to the top bar.
5. The footer/bottom bar is removed once 3 and 4 land. Version folds into the status pill as 'Online - vX.Y.Z' (PO decision).
6. Operations group reorders to M3U Manager, EPG Manager, Logo Manager, Channel Manager.
7. Guide and M3U Changes both move to the Insights group.

Must also update TabNavigation.test.tsx, e2e/operator-shell.spec.ts, the IA design doc, operator user-guide docs, and scripts/check-operator-docs.mjs expectations. Must not regress the WCAG contrast work closed in rv84z or the axe/release gates from 2896r.9.
notes:
All seven PO items implemented on the newui branch working tree.

1. Logo collapse - the ECM logo is a button wrapping the mark, first in sidebar focus order.
2. Dashboard visual identity - per-card icon chip, per-card accent top rule, semantic tone icon on the status line (check/warning/error/info).
3. Service status pill in the header - role=status, dot + state + version, states Online/Connecting/Offline/verbatim-unhealthy.
4. Update-available link moved to the header, pulse disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
5. Footer removed; shell grid is now header + work area, bottom bound is the viewport.
6. Operations reordered to M3U/EPG/Logo/Channel Manager; Automation keeps only Channel Pipeline.
7. Guide and M3U Changes moved to Insights (order Guide, Stats, M3U Changes, Journal - agent judgment, membership was PO-specified).

PO reversed the initial keep-both decision: the separate Collapse button is removed, logo is the sole collapse control. It takes the canonical Collapse navigation / Expand navigation name so all existing e2e selectors resolve to it.

Two defects found and fixed during the work:
- Logo aria-label originally contained the phrase 'collapse navigation', and Playwright getByRole name matching is substring-based, so every query for the Collapse button resolved to two elements (15 e2e failures). Guarded by a new unit test asserting exactly one control carries that phrase.
- Header status version measured 4.34:1, under the 4.5:1 floor, because the tinted pill background raised background luminance behind muted text. Now recedes by weight/size at 10.2 dark / 12.8 light / 11.9 high-contrast.

Also fixed pre-existing enhancedchannelmanager-eo7er (P1): dashboard freshness text at 2.61:1 in the light theme.

e2e updates: footer landmark assertion inverted to expect no contentinfo; two geometry helpers rebased from the removed footer onto the viewport bottom; keyboard traversal helper rebased from the old bottom Collapse button onto the last navigation destination, plus a new assertion that the logo toggle precedes the destinations.

Gates: typecheck, lint, docs:check clean; 2394 frontend unit tests pass; contrast verified across dark/light/high-contrast. Full operator-shell e2e re-run in progress. NOT yet committed - working tree only.
