title: Operator-message polish: condense the persistence warning, operator-voice the interpreter diagnostics, surface mount status outside the log
description:
PR #753 review, UX designer (findings 1-2 + discoverability), with SRE concurring on alert fatigue. All P3 polish - the messages are honest and correctly ordered today.

(1) The DATA IS NOT PERSISTENT block (entrypoint.sh:198-209) is 12 separate print_warning calls, so it renders as 12 stacked '!' glyphs - and that repetition survives color-stripping in piped docker logs, saved log files, and Portainer's log pane. Content ordering is right (danger -> stakes -> fix -> backup caveat) and the severity channel is correct (yellow print_warning, not red print_error, matching the advisory intent). The issue is cadence: this 12-line wall prints on EVERY startup for as long as the container stays unmounted, which for a legitimate throwaway container is indefinite. Scenario: operator runs a test container without a volume, sees the wall, ignores it (container works fine), accumulates real config over weeks, does a routine Portainer Recreate, and the same wall gets the same 'yeah yeah' dismissal it earned on day one. Suggested condensation to ~6 lines is in the review thread.

(2) print_python_diagnostics (entrypoint.sh:83-102) uses print_info (blue, the routine-status channel) for BOTH the raw diagnostic dump and the actionable fix, always directly under a red print_error. In a Portainer log pane that is a wall of blue FYI lines after the one red line that matters. Two specifics: sys.prefix is emitted with zero explanation (a non-Python operator cannot know what a good vs bad value looks like), and the fix text is developer-voice - 'Remove the override' never says WHERE the override lives. The CHANGELOG for this very PR diagnoses it precisely (a stray PATH entry sitting in that container's Environment Variables tab, carried over by the update flow) and none of that concreteness reached the message the operator actually reads. Suggested replacement copy is in the review thread.

(3) DISCOVERABILITY (follow-up, explicitly not a merge condition): unmounted CONFIG_DIR is silent data loss whose only surface is a startup log line. An operator sees it only if they open container logs at the moment of recreate - the moment they are least likely to look, since a successful-looking Portainer Recreate gives no in-UI signal. Worth surfacing persistence status in the ECM web UI (dismissible banner) or on /api/health so it reaches a surface operators actually check.

Verified correct and NOT to be changed: severity is carried by both color AND glyph shape (✓/✗/!/→), so it degrades correctly for a colorblind operator or a saved log read without color.

title: Docs: ECM_PYTHON/ECM_UVICORN/CONFIG_DIR env-var reference + preflight-failure runbook + unmounted-config recovery procedure
description:
PR #753 review, technical writer (findings 1-3) with IT architect and project engineer concurring (3/10 personas independently).

(1) UNDOCUMENTED OPERATOR-FACING ENV VARS. README.md:80-92 is the canonical operator env-var reference (PUID/PGID, ECM_PORT/ECM_HTTPS_PORT, Volumes). ECM_PYTHON, ECM_UVICORN and CONFIG_DIR appear nowhere in it or in docs/ (grep: zero hits). This is not academic: PR #753's own print_python_diagnostics prints, in the operator's terminal, 'point ECM_PYTHON/ECM_UVICORN at the interpreter that has ECM's deps'. An operator who hits exactly the failure this PR targets sees those two names and finds no documentation of what they do, how to set them, or the PATH-fallback behavior. CONFIG_DIR is a pre-existing backend var (backend/config.py:20) that this PR makes the entrypoint read and names directly in the new warning text, while README still documents /config as a fixed path. A changelog entry is a record of a change, not a contract - nothing currently says these are supported, so nothing stops a future refactor removing them.
Fix: add all three to the README env-var list in the existing style; mark ECM_PYTHON/ECM_UVICORN as advanced escape hatches for custom images. Do NOT document ECM_MOUNTINFO - see bead nz8q4, it should be removed from the runtime surface entirely.

(2) NO RUNBOOK FOR THE FAILURE MODE THIS PR EXISTS TO FIX. docs/runbooks/ has no entry for a failed preflight/startup (confirmed against docs/runbooks/README.md:15-30 and on disk). docs/user_guide/troubleshooting/index.md lists common-issues.md and ui-banners-and-warnings.md as Planned stubs only. The PR body documents a round-trip diagnosis that happened BECAUSE no such artifact existed - textbook trigger per docs/runbooks/README.md's own line ('an alert without a runbook is a fire alarm without an exit map'). The remedy text currently lives only in CHANGELOG [Unreleased], which the next release will bury.
Fix: docs/runbooks/container-preflight-failure.md per docs/runbooks/template.md - reading the interpreter-diagnostics block, the pre-0.16.0 PATH-inheritance trigger, the ECM_PYTHON/ECM_UVICORN override path.

(3) NO RECOVERY PROCEDURE FOR THE DATA-LOSS SCENARIO THE NEW WARNING ANNOUNCES. docs/user_guide/troubleshooting/recovery-patterns.md is Planned, not written; nothing in docs/user_guide/backup-restore/ covers 'container has no mount, back up before recreating'. An operator who sees DATA IS NOT PERSISTENT understands they need a backup but has no page walking unmounted-container -> take backup -> add mount -> recreate -> restore as one sequence.
Fix: a short section in docs/user_guide/backup-restore/ titled 'My container isn't persisting data' with that exact sequence.

Verified by the database engineer and NOT a concern: the warning's 'Back up first (Settings -> Backup & Restore)' advice is SAFE, not a trap. The UI button (BackupRestoreSection.tsx:93-110) calls GET /backup/create, which streams the zip straight to the HTTP response and lands it in the operator's own Downloads folder - never written to the doomed writable layer. The separate POST /backup/save does write to CONFIG_DIR/backups, but it is not wired to any frontend button or scheduled task.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Items 1 and 2 fully open: README.md still has zero mentions of ECM_PYTHON, ECM_UVICORN or CONFIG_DIR despite all three being live and load-bearing (entrypoint.sh:76-115, config.py:25), and no container-preflight-failure runbook exists. Narrow item 3: prevention-side guidance now EXISTS at installation.md:58-79 and first-run.md:9-73, which cover mounting config and taking a backup before recreate. What is still missing is the dedicated 'I already have an unmounted container, here is the recovery sequence' walkthrough.

title: Stale-inherited-container-environment: ECM_VERSION is wrong in the field today; detect divergence from image defaults
description:
PR #753 review, IT architect (finding 4) + project engineer (finding 2). Explicitly NOT for PR #753 - this is the generalization.

PR #753's own evidence: the reporting operator's container had ECM_VERSION=0.8.4-0007 on a current image filesystem, because Portainer/Unraid/Watchtower 'update/recreate' copies the OLD container's environment onto the NEW image. The PR fixes the Python case. The class is untouched.

ECM_VERSION is live: backend/routers/health.py:213,249 and backend/observability.py:1295 read it. So every affected container is RIGHT NOW reporting 0.8.4-0007 from /api/version, /api/health and the observability build-info metric. That population is precisely the one most likely to file the next bug report, and the version string in that report will be a lie. PUID/PGID, CONFIG_DIR, ECM_PORT and RELEASE_CHANNEL are inherit-copied by the same mechanism with no detection.

Tractable fix: the Dockerfile already bakes the defaults (ENV lines 39-43, 74-78), so preflight can compare the live environment against the image's baked values and warn on divergence for vars the operator has no reason to override (ECM_VERSION, GIT_COMMIT, RELEASE_CHANNEL). That converts a whole class of 'recreate copied my 2024 environment' incidents into one preflight line.

Related, from the project engineer: the root cause is a clobbered PATH (Dockerfile:57 ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH is exactly what the recreate flow overwrites), and PATH is never repaired. A single line at the top of entrypoint.sh - PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"; export PATH - covers every current call site, every future one, gosu's own PATH resolution on the exec line, and the PATH the uvicorn process inherits. That last one is what the PR leaves stale: sys.executable rescues the Python side, but the app still resolves external binaries through the operator's PATH - shutil.which(ffprobe) at backend/routers/health.py:154 and backend/stream_prober.py:59, and bare ffmpeg argv at backend/routers/stream_preview.py:107,153,277,325. In the reported field case those still resolve (/usr/bin is in the stale PATH), so this is NOT a live bug - it is the next variant waiting to happen.

Note the architect and engineer agree on layering: do NOT set ENV ECM_PYTHON in the Dockerfile (it would fix today's cohort while manufacturing the identical bug for the next venv move, since Portainer would then copy a stale ECM_PYTHON forward). Pinning inside the entrypoint with a literal non-inheritable default is the durable layer. The PATH export belongs in the entrypoint too, alongside the pin - not in the Dockerfile.

Also add PYTHONHOME, PYTHONPATH and VIRTUAL_ENV to print_python_diagnostics: a stale inherited PYTHONHOME breaks /opt/venv/bin/python regardless of the pin, so the next report in this family would produce a log paste that looks clean.

title: entrypoint: honor CONFIG_DIR end-to-end and demote ECM_MOUNTINFO from public env var to a function parameter
description:
PR #753 review, IT architect. Two container-contract issues.

(1) CONFIG_DIR is honored in exactly ONE of four places, and the new check now ADVERTISES a configuration the rest of the entrypoint does not support. entrypoint.sh:11 reads CONFIG_DIR=${CONFIG_DIR:-/config} and only check_config_persistence uses it. check_filesystem still hardcodes /config at :216, :220, :228 (mkdir -p /config/tls /config/uploads/logos), :231 (chown -R appuser:appuser /config), :232 (chmod 700 /config/tls) and the write probe at :235. check_tls_config still reads /config/tls_settings.json at :304-306. backend/config.py:20 confirms the APP honors the env var, and the Dockerfile ships ENV CONFIG_DIR=/config, so this is a live operator-settable variable.

Consequence for CONFIG_DIR=/data -v ecm-data:/data: preflight prints '✓ Config directory /data is on a mounted volume (data persists across recreates)' - an explicit endorsement - then never chowns /data. A fresh named volume mounts root-owned at a path absent from the image, so appuser cannot write it post-gosu and the app fails on settings.json AFTER preflight said everything was fine. Meanwhile chmod 700 /config/tls silently builds a decoy tree in the writable layer and check_tls_config reports TLS unconfigured while the app serves HTTPS from /data/tls_settings.json.

The gap predates the PR; the PR is what starts advertising CONFIG_DIR as working.
Fix: use ${CONFIG_DIR} throughout check_filesystem and check_tls_config. The existing test harness truncates at 'check_filesystem() {' so it is untouched. Cheaper alternative if appetite is low: suppress the persistence endorsement whenever CONFIG_DIR != /config.

(2) ECM_MOUNTINFO (entrypoint.sh:161) is a TEST SEAM promoted to permanent public API on a :latest rolling image with unknown external consumers. It has no operator use case, and it is subject to the very inheritance mechanism this PR exists to fix - an operator who sets it once, or a container that acquires it from a copied environment, permanently disables real mount detection. Because the check fails OPEN by design ([ -r "$ECM_MOUNTINFO" ] || return 0), that disablement is silent.
Fix: config_dir_is_persistent() already takes the directory as $1; make the mountinfo path $2 with the /proc/self/mountinfo default in the function body. Tests then call config_dir_is_persistent "/config" "$FIXTURE" directly - a SMALLER harness, and zero runtime configuration surface.

title: entrypoint tests: behavioral coverage for check_application/check_tls_config interpreter sites + widen the anti-regression guard
description:
PR #753 review. QA engineer PROVED a silent regression by injection; code reviewer and project engineer independently flagged the guard's narrowness.

(1) COVERAGE HOLE, confirmed by injection. entrypoint.sh:287,293 (check_application) and :309-310 (check_tls_config) sit OUTSIDE the 'check_filesystem() {' cut point both new test files use as their harness boundary, and no test invokes either function. The only thing covering those lines is test_no_bare_interpreter_invocations_remain, a pure text regex. QA changed $ECM_PYTHON to $ECM_PYTON (a typo expanding to empty) at the check_tls_config site in a disposable worktree and reran ALL 46 tests: all 46 still passed. A regression at one of the '7 former bare-python3 sites' the commit message enumerates would ship silently today. Worse, the surrounding '2>/dev/null || echo False' swallows the resulting command-not-found, so the runtime symptom is TLS silently reported as disabled.
Fix: one behavioral test each for check_application and check_tls_config using the existing extract-and-execute pattern - swap $ECM_PYTHON for a capturing shim (as test_event_loop_selection.py already does for $ECM_UVICORN) and assert the pinned path appears in the captured invocation.

(2) GUARD NARROWER THAN ITS OWN PROMISE. test_entrypoint_interpreter.py:188 -
invocation = re.compile(r"(?<![\\w/$\"-])python3?\\s+(-c|--version)\\b")
The assertion message promises 'must invoke $ECM_PYTHON, never a PATH-resolved interpreter'. It actually catches only '-c' and '--version'. It passes a future 'python3 -m uvicorn', 'python3 -m alembic upgrade head', 'python -V', or a heredoc 'python3 <<EOF'. The '/' in the lookbehind also exempts absolute paths, so a hardcoded '/usr/local/bin/python3 -c' - the bug itself - passes clean. Nothing guards a new bare 'uvicorn' or 'pip' either.
Fix: widen to python3?\\s+[-\\w] and add uvicorn|pip to the alternation.

(3) Wiring is asserted textually only. TestPreflightWiring slices run_preflight_checks and greps; it never executes it. A runtime defect in ordering or FAILED chaining would not be caught.

(4) Environmental coupling: test_falls_back_to_path_when_pinned_interpreter_is_absent depends on /opt/venv being ABSENT from the test host. True on CI runners, but the test fails for anyone running the suite inside the ECM image. Making VENV_BIN=${ECM_VENV_BIN:-/opt/venv/bin} would let the test control it.

Verified non-issue, do not re-raise: shell parity is fine - host /bin/sh and container /bin/sh are both dash (base python:3.12-slim). The test_event_loop_selection.py harness edit is a faithful accommodation, not a weakening: 29 tests pass on both branch and dev.

title: config_dir_is_persistent: exclude tmpfs/ramfs and handle kernel octal-escaped mount points
description:
PR #753 review. Two demonstrated defects in the ebl4n mount check (entrypoint.sh:180-186), both reproduced by the orchestrator and independently by SRE, security, code reviewer, QA and project engineer.

(1) FALSE REASSURANCE - tmpfs. The awk matches on mountinfo field 5 only and never inspects filesystem type. A '--tmpfs /config' (or read_only:true + tmpfs:/config, a real hardening pattern) yields the reassuring line '✓ Config directory /config is on a mounted volume (data persists across recreates)'. That statement is false - tmpfs does not survive a recreate or even a restart. This is the SAME failure shape ebl4n exists to close (preflight said fine while data was ephemeral), reintroduced via a different mount type. It is the actively-dangerous direction: the author's documented bias at :165-167 ('a false your-data-is-ephemeral would be worse than saying nothing') reasons about false NEGATIVES only; fail-open does not cover a false POSITIVE that reassures an operator right before they lose data.
Fix: skip lines whose fstype (first field after the ' - ' separator) is tmpfs/ramfs.

(2) FALSE ALARM - escaped paths. The kernel octal-escapes whitespace in mountinfo field 5 (\\040 for space); the comparison is against the raw unescaped shell value of CONFIG_DIR. Reproduced: mountinfo '/my\\040config' vs CONFIG_DIR='/my config' does not match, so a genuinely-mounted directory gets the full DATA IS NOT PERSISTENT block. The code comment at :161-163 NAMES this hazard and then draws an unrelated conclusion ('so the field-5 comparison below is exact') - the escaping is never handled and no fixture covers it.
Fix: gsub(/ /, "\\\\040", dir) in the awk (plus \\011/\\134 for completeness), or honestly document it as a known false-positive rather than a solved case. Add a 5th mountinfo fixture with an escaped path.

Verified-correct in the same function and NOT to be changed: trailing slash works via the ancestor rule; /config-backup correctly does not match /config; unreadable mountinfo correctly stays silent; advisory-never-fatal wiring is right and the security engineer explicitly defends fail-open as correct.

title: Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK: interpreter fallback/override parity with entrypoint + container-level verification
description:
PR #753 review. Flagged independently by SRE, security engineer, code reviewer, project engineer and IT architect (5/10 personas).

Dockerfile:98 is now 'CMD /opt/venv/bin/python -c ...' - a build-time literal with NO fallback and NO ECM_PYTHON honoring. entrypoint.sh:69-77 goes to deliberate trouble to do both, explicitly promising 'an image without /opt/venv behaves as it did before'. The healthcheck breaks that promise.

Failure scenario with a concrete in-repo consumer: an operator relocates the venv and sets ECM_PYTHON - the exact escape hatch the new diagnostics block instructs them to use. The app starts and serves correctly; the container is reported unhealthy forever. docker-compose.mcp.yml:16-18 already has 'depends_on: ecm: condition: service_healthy', so the MCP sidecar would never start, with nothing in the logs pointing at the healthcheck (Docker reports only the CMD exit code). Swarm/Portainer/autoheal act on the unhealthy status too.

The Dockerfile's own comment concedes the pin buys nothing today ('urllib is stdlib, so this happens to survive that today'), and the PR body states the change was not verified at container level. CI builds the image but never runs the healthcheck, so that caveat still stands.

Fix (either): CMD sh -c '${ECM_PYTHON:-/opt/venv/bin/python} -c "..."' || exit 1, or revert to the PATH lookup and drop test_dockerfile_healthcheck_pins_the_interpreter. Whichever is chosen, verify once at container level: docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}'.

Note: the project engineer confirmed /opt/venv/bin/python DOES exist in the shipped image, so the default path is correct and ECM's own published image is unaffected. Blast radius is custom/derived images and ECM_PYTHON users.

title: entrypoint: assert ECM_UVICORN is executable + warn when an explicit interpreter override is discarded
description:
PR #753 review. Two linked gaps in the 0oi96 interpreter pin.

(1) check_python probes $ECM_PYTHON --version and 'import fastapi, uvicorn' (the MODULE) but never asserts [ -x "$ECM_UVICORN" ]. Preflight prints all-green, then 'exec gosu appuser "$ECM_UVICORN"' dies with a bare not-found and zero diagnostics. Reproduced independently by the orchestrator, the security engineer and the code reviewer: ECM_PYTHON=<good> ECM_UVICORN=/opt/venv/bin/uvicorn on a host without the venv -> PREFLIGHT_RC=0, exec would fail. This is exactly the failure class the PR body says it exists to eliminate ('fixing preflight alone would have moved the same failure one line down'). print_python_diagnostics already computes the answer ('NOT EXECUTABLE - the app launch would fail here too') but is reachable only from failure branches, so the one string describing this case can never fire in it.

Fix: in check_python before 'return 0': if [ ! -x "$ECM_UVICORN" ]; then print_error "Uvicorn launcher not executable: ${ECM_UVICORN}"; print_python_diagnostics; return 1; fi

(2) The [ ! -x ] fallback at entrypoint.sh:69-77 cannot distinguish 'the default pin is absent' (fallback correct) from 'the operator set ECM_PYTHON explicitly and typo'd it' (fallback wrong). Proven live in ecm-ecm-1 by the project engineer: ECM_PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/pyhton silently resolves /opt/venv/bin/python3 with no log line. Self-inflicted loop: the diagnostics tell the operator to set ECM_PYTHON, they fat-finger it, and get back the identical message that sent them there.

Fix: capture _was_set=${ECM_PYTHON:+1} before the default expansion; print_warning in the fallback branch when the override is being discarded. Same for ECM_UVICORN.

title: Team review of PR #753 (entrypoint interpreter pinning + config-persistence warning)
description: Run /team-review over PR 753 at small-team effective tier (ecm-core home-lab x ci-release small-team, strictest-wins). Post consolidated verdict to the PR.

title: Preflight: warn when CONFIG_DIR is not a mount (data lives in the container's writable layer)
description: Field case 2026-07-27 (see 0oi96): an operator's container had docker inspect Mounts == [], meaning /config — settings + journal.db — lived only in the container's writable layer. Preflight reported '✓ Config directory exists' and '✓ Config directory is writable', which is technically true and dangerously reassuring: any container delete/recreate (including the Portainer/Unraid/Watchtower 'update' flow that caused their actual failure) silently destroys all ECM data. Work: in backend/entrypoint.sh preflight, detect whether CONFIG_DIR is a mount point (e.g. compare device ids of $CONFIG_DIR and /, or grep /proc/self/mountinfo) and emit a loud non-fatal warning when it is not — wording should tell the operator their data is ephemeral and how to fix it (bind mount or named volume). Non-fatal: a first-run/test container without a mount is legitimate. Add a fixture test for both branches. Pairs with 0oi96 (same file, same field case) — consider shipping together if 0oi96 has not merged yet.

title: GHCR publishes no version-pinned tags above 0.8.3 — operators cannot pin or roll back by version
description: Support-ergonomics finding from the 2026-07-27 field case: GHCR carries only latest/dev/main/main-<sha>/dev-<sha>. An operator on 'the 0.18.0 image' actually pulled :latest and cannot roll back to a known-good release by version — only by opaque main-<sha>. This directly hampers 'revert to the previous release while we debug' during an incident, and makes 'what version are you running' unanswerable from the tag. Work: publish semver tags on release cuts (0.18.0, 0.18, plus latest) — note the release workflow ALREADY tags 0.18.0/0.18/latest on the main push per the v0.18.0 cut, so verify whether this is a gap only for pre-0.18 releases or an ongoing one, and backfill/document accordingly. Check docs/shipping.md + build.yml before assuming.

title: Docs: container-wont-start troubleshooting article keyed to preflight output
description: Gap found during the 2026-07-27 field support case (see 0oi96, ebl4n): docs/user_guide/troubleshooting/index.md is an explicit stub, installation.md and first-run.md are unwritten, and there is no upgrade/migration note anywhere for the 0.15.x->0.16.0 system-wide-pip -> /opt/venv transition. Grep confirms ZERO mentions of QNAP or Container Station anywhere in docs/ or README — yet the field case was a QNAP user, and QNAP has two device-specific traps that generic Docker docs miss. Write docs/user_guide/troubleshooting/container-wont-start.md keyed to the exact preflight failure lines, covering: (1) 'Required Python packages missing' / ModuleNotFoundError — caused by a container whose config predates 0.16.0 being 'updated' in place rather than recreated, so the inherited PATH lacks /opt/venv/bin; the fix is DELETE + recreate, not update; (2) no /config mount -> data lives in the container writable layer and dies on recreate (pairs with ebl4n's warning); (3) port conflicts and config-dir permission failures. Include the four diagnostic commands from the field case. ADD A QNAP SECTION: Container Station's Update/Recreate preserves the old container's environment (this is the actual mechanism that broke the field user); QNAP's / and /root are a RAM disk wiped on reboot, so backups and bind mounts MUST live under /share/<ShareName> (verify with ls /share/) — a docker cp backup written to /root is lost on the next reboot; Container Station GUI-created containers need the shared-folder volume added explicitly. Coordinate with the tutorials epic (gsnw0) troubleshooting/installation children so this doesn't duplicate them.
notes: FIELD-VALIDATED 2026-07-27: the QNAP resolution procedure below was confirmed working by the reporting operator. Write the article from these exact steps. (1) Back up first — docker cp <container>:/config to a path under /share/<ShareName>, NEVER to ~ or /root (QNAP's root fs is a RAM disk, wiped on reboot); verify journal.db is present in the copy. (2) Diagnose — docker inspect <container> --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -E '^(PATH|ECM_VERSION)=' ; a PATH lacking /opt/venv/bin plus a stale ECM_VERSION (field case showed 0.8.4-0007 against a current image) proves an in-place Container Station update carried the old container's env forward. Confirm the image itself is healthy with: docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh <image> -c 'echo $PATH; python3 -c "import fastapi; print(1)"'. (3) Fix — STOP and REMOVE the container, then create it fresh from the image; do NOT use Container Station's Update/Recreate, which is the mechanism that preserves the stale env. (4) Add the missing /config volume during recreate (field case had Mounts == [], so all data sat in the container's writable layer), restoring the backup into the host folder before first start. (5) Verify PATH now starts with /opt/venv/bin and ECM_VERSION reads the current build.

title: Pin the approved Channel Manager responsive and accessibility standard
description:
## User value
Operators receive the same readable, operable Channel Manager at common desktop sizes without clipped labels, content behind navigation, or regressions in dense rows.

## Work
Add the rendered regression matrix that makes the approved mockup behavior a release standard for Channel Manager and the new shell. Cover both navigation states, normal/Edit Mode, representative health states, menus, artwork, and stream row edge cases.

## Success signal
CI produces reproducible evidence that future UI changes preserve the approved layout and interactions at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.

## Required Skills
qa-engineer,ux-designer
acceptance_criteria:
• Run Playwright at exactly 1920x1080 and 1280x720 for expanded and collapsed navigation, normal and Edit Mode, and populated plus applicable empty/error states.
• Expanded sidebar is 244px and shows complete grouped labels; collapsed sidebar is 68px and genuinely icon-only—OPERATIONS/AUTOMATION headings have zero visual footprint, while every icon retains an accessible name/title/tooltip.
• Sidebar client width equals scroll width; main content clears the rail; no document-level horizontal overflow, pane overlap, text beneath navigation, or clipped required controls.
• Verify one semantic h1, logical landmarks/focus order, visible focus, keyboard navigation, menu Escape/focus return, and non-color-only status names.
• Verify channel number/name columns, channel artwork fallback, each compact status icon/count, channel-only badges/probe detail, assigned timeout layout, inventory artwork/text/actions order, and Edit Mode-only handles.
• Assert surrounding typography and icon density match current ECM at both widths; do not shrink fonts through a 1280-only media rule.
• Capture named screenshots for all core states and file blocking defects for any visual/geometry/accessibility failure.
• Treat this matrix as a release gate for the operator-workspace epic.
notes:
## Canonical reference
Use the PO-approved Channel Manager mockup Sites v16 / commit `48353d703b9c1b6ba2e33ea2b9f9bce05cf6412c` together with this bead’s acceptance criteria. Preserve current ECM APIs and existing functions; the mockup establishes layout, hierarchy, visibility, density, and interaction standards.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified the Channel Manager responsive/accessibility release gate: exact two-viewport state matrix, 26 deterministic named screenshots plus icon/geometry metadata, real keyboard focus/menu coverage, settled 68/244px navigation, self-hosted icons, and CI artifact reporting. Dedicated 6/6 and full exact 56/56 no-retry Playwright pass at 0b56033d.

title: Implement Channel Manager Edit Mode interactions and bulk action bar
description:
## User value

## Work

## Success signal

acceptance_criteria:

• Streams inventory row and supported group-header handles remain Edit Mode only. Use the approved ⋮⋮ row affordance and Material drag_indicator group affordance with accessible drag instructions.
• Entering/leaving Edit Mode preserves layout alignment and does not introduce horizontal overflow in expanded or collapsed navigation.
• The bottom selection bar renders only in Edit Mode with at least one selected channel.

title: Standardize assigned-stream and source-inventory rows
description:
## User value
Operators can read assigned stream health without losing the stream identity and can scan the source inventory without unrelated probe noise or misordered controls.

## Work
Implement the approved assigned-stream row and Streams inventory row contracts, including artwork semantics, metadata density, warning allocation, action icons, and grid ordering. Preserve current stream actions such as copy URL, probe, preview/edit/remove/reset where supported.

## Success signal
Stream identity, URL/provider metadata, warnings, and actions remain legible and non-overlapping in both panes at both audited viewport sizes.

## Required Skills
project-engineer,ux-designer
acceptance_criteria:
• Assigned stream rows stay inline beneath their channel and render stream logo_url only when present; broken images hide and no fallback placeholder is invented.
• Assigned rows may show their existing probe/quality details, including quality badges and stale/failed/timeout/strike information, without crushing name, URL, provider, or actions.
• Probe-timeout rows reserve usable identity and warning width, use compact visible wording (for example Probe timeout • 3/3), retain full detail in accessible text/title, and do not overlap fixed action controls.
• Streams inventory rows render in strict visual/DOM order: optional stable artwork slot, flexible stream identity/URL/provider text, then fixed right-side actions. No text may render after or beneath the action buttons.
• Inventory artwork is the stream’s own logo_url, never channel/provider artwork; when absent, preserve grid alignment without displaying a fallback image icon.
• Streams inventory shows no probe counts, probe warning text, quality/status badges, or channel-level health indicators.
• Stream-side icon buttons use ECM sizing and existing Material icons; row and pane kebab menus contain iconized current actions and are pointer/keyboard operable.
• Long identity text ellipsizes in the flexible middle column; tests assert DOM order, minimum usable widths, non-overlap, and action placement at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
notes:
## Canonical reference
Use the PO-approved Channel Manager mockup Sites v16 / commit `48353d703b9c1b6ba2e33ea2b9f9bce05cf6412c` together with this bead’s acceptance criteria. Preserve current ECM APIs and existing functions; the mockup establishes layout, hierarchy, visibility, density, and interaction standards.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified assigned-stream and source-inventory row standards, exact timeout geometry, inventory health-noise removal, keyboard-visible actions, and complete accessible pane menu/focus behavior. Full gates and 29/29 no-retry Playwright pass at 504ba6b1.

title: Standardize Channel Manager channel-row identity and health indicators
description:
## User value
Operators can identify a channel, distinguish its number from its name, and recognize the most important stream-health condition at a glance without reading duplicate status text.

## Work
Implement the approved channel-row hierarchy, artwork behavior, EPG line, compact stream count/status indicator, resolution badges, and existing channel actions. Use current channel and probe data already available to Channel Manager.

## Success signal
A channel row communicates identity and its highest-priority health state consistently and compactly at both audited desktop sizes.

## Required Skills
project-engineer,ux-designer
acceptance_criteria:
• Render channel number in its own fixed/aligned column without a # prefix and channel name in a separate adjacent identity field. The guide subtitle is stacked beneath the channel name at the same left edge. Header and rows share one alignment contract: `Number | Channel / Guide | Streams`; normal and Edit Mode preserve the same column geometry.
• Render channel artwork from staged logo URL first in Edit Mode, otherwise logo_id resolved through the logo map cache_url then url; show the Material image placeholder only when a channel has no logo; hide broken artwork.
• Render the guide subtitle as the EPG Provider value, an en dash, then the tvg-name value (for example `Schedules Direct – ESPN`); do not repeat `TVG Name`/`tvg-name` labels; keep additional identifiers in tooltip/detail where current behavior requires them.
• Render one compact stream indicator: status icon plus total stream count. Healthy uses neutral lan. Deterministic priority is no streams (warning + 0), failed probe (red error), stale (history/warning), black screen (videocam_off/purple), low FPS (slow_motion_video/amber), then healthy.
• Do not render duplicate channel-summary text such as No streams, N stale, Low FPS, or failed probe beneath the compact indicator.
• Resolution capability badges appear only in the Channels pane and remain highest-first using current tiers/colors; Streams inventory has none.
• Channel kebab uses existing iconized actions, correct sizing, tooltips, keyboard navigation, Escape, and focus return.
• Add unit and rendered tests for number/name separation, shared header/row geometry, artwork/fallback, every status/precedence state, stream totals, badges, menus, and non-color-only accessible naming.
notes:
## Canonical reference
Use the PO-approved Channel Manager mockup Sites v16 / commit `48353d703b9c1b6ba2e33ea2b9f9bce05cf6412c` together with this bead’s acceptance criteria. Preserve current ECM APIs and existing functions; the mockup establishes layout, hierarchy, visibility, density, and interaction standards.
close_reason: Implemented and verified source-accurate Channel Manager channel rows: shared Number | Channel / Guide | Streams geometry, artwork resolution, compact health precedence/counts, channel-only badges, accessible iconized actions, and viewport coverage. Full gates, code review, and QA pass at 509ee1fd.

title: Implement the approved Channel Manager two-pane workspace
description:
## User value

## Work

## Success signal

acceptance_criteria:
• Render exactly one h1: OPERATIONS / CHANNEL MANAGER; remove any duplicate Channel Manager title.
• Preserve the current Channel Manager route, API calls, filters, menus, actions, deep links, and permission behavior.
• Keep Channels and assigned streams together in the left pane; keep the all-provider source inventory in the right pane.

• At 1920x1080 and 1280x720, expanded and collapsed navigation retain usable two-pane content with no document horizontal overflow.

notes:
## Canonical reference
Use the PO-approved Channel Manager mockup Sites v16 / commit `48353d703b9c1b6ba2e33ea2b9f9bce05cf6412c` together with this bead’s acceptance criteria. Preserve current ECM APIs and existing functions; the mockup establishes layout, hierarchy, visibility, density, and interaction standards.

Docs/MkDocs/frontend gates pass at a48e2ce6.

title: Prioritize ECM shell and page actions for 1280x720
description:
## User value
Operators using the audited smaller desktop can see navigation, the primary action, and meaningful task content without competing chrome.

## Work
Apply the approved layout budget after navigation, page hierarchy, long-page, toolbar, and dashboard work; preserve the spacious 1920x1080 experience.

## Success signal
Every core route passes the 1280x720 layout budget without hiding required actions or introducing page overflow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define and test horizontal and vertical layout budgets for every primary route at 1280x720 while preserving 1920x1080.
- Collapse navigation, secondary descriptions, and secondary actions according to the specification.
- Never hide a required task action without a clearly labeled recovery path.
- Retain primary actions, freshness, and meaningful above-fold task content.
- Avoid document horizontal overflow and unjustified nested scrolling; support 200% zoom and browser text scaling.
- Keyboard focus is never obscured by shell or sticky elements.
- Playwright covers every primary route at both viewports with populated and relevant empty/error states.
notes:
## Channel Manager layout budget
The implementation must satisfy enhancedchannelmanager-2896r.10 through .13 at both widths without responsive font shrinking. At 1280x720, preserve two panes; let minmax(0) identity columns ellipsize while artwork/status/warning/action columns retain their specified space.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified compact layout budgets for all 11 primary routes at 1280x720 while preserving 1920x1080, with real populated/alternate-state content, focus/freshness, action recovery, nested-scroll ownership, zoom, and deterministic boot coverage. Full gates and exact 52/52 no-retry Playwright pass at a1523980.

title: Standardize dense table and list toolbars across ECM
description:
## User value
Operators find search, filters, sorting, views, selection counts, and bulk actions in predictable locations across M3U, EPG, Logos, Changes, and Journal.

## Work
Adopt one toolbar composition using the existing overflow policy and menu primitives while preserving each route’s API/query behavior.

## Success signal
Representative search/filter/sort/select workflows use consistent placement and terminology across dense screens.
acceptance_criteria:
- Use the approved order: search, filters, sort/view, selection count, then bulk actions; document justified deviations.
- Use URL state for shareable filter/sort/page values where routing supports it and document limitations otherwise.
- Preserve query parameters, API contracts, pagination, and safe page reset after filter changes.
- Define populated, loading, empty, error, permission, and disabled-selection states.
- Provide semantic labels/grouping, visual-order keyboard traversal, accessible menus, Escape/focus return, and non-color-only selection.
- Verify populated/empty/error states at both viewports with primary controls visible and secondary controls recoverable.
- Add shared-component and rendered E2E coverage with no clipped controls or document overflow.
notes:
## Approved Channel Manager toolbar exception
Channel Manager uses the selection-dependent Edit Mode bottom bar specified by enhancedchannelmanager-2896r.13. Its icon order, 2+ Merge rule, upward More menu, and Clear action are the approved dense-workspace exception to the generic toolbar order.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified shared dense toolbars across M3U, EPG, Logos, Changes, and Journal with approved order, accessible sorting/menus, truthful loading/empty/error/permission/stale states, request concurrency protection, and two-viewport containment. Full gates and exact 46/46 no-retry Playwright pass at 353569b0.

title: Improve orientation and save safety on long ECM pages
description:
## User value
Operators can move through long Settings and Stats surfaces and confidently apply or abandon edits without losing location or silently losing work.

## Work
Apply sticky section navigation, selective disclosure, and persistent pending-change actions only to audit-confirmed long pages. Preserve existing write API semantics and avoid silent autosave conversion.

## Success signal
Direct section entry, edit/save/cancel/error, and navigation-away journeys retain context and prevent accidental loss.
acceptance_criteria:
- Apply behavior only to pages identified as long in the approved specification.
- Sticky section navigation tracks the current section and supports deep-linkable direct entry.
- Low-frequency content may collapse, but critical warnings and current values remain visible by default.
- Pending edits expose Save/Apply, Cancel/Revert, unsaved state, success/error feedback, and navigation-away protection.
- Inventory write APIs and preserve payload/partial-update semantics; do not introduce silent autosave.
- Keyboard controls work with Enter/Space, focus is not obscured by sticky UI, and 200% zoom/reduced motion remain usable.
- Sticky elements cover no content and introduce no nested-scroll trap or document overflow at either viewport.
- Test dirty/pristine, direct section entry, save success/failure, cancel, and navigation-away paths.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified audited long-page section navigation, payload-baseline dirty tracking, save/cancel/error and history protection, reduced-motion behavior, and persistent sticky focus clearance. Full gates and exact 40/40 no-retry Playwright pass at 749436d2.

title: Standardize page hierarchy and contextual configuration links
description:
## User value
Operators can predict where titles, purpose, primary actions, freshness, filters, and related settings links appear without recalling hidden configuration locations.

## Work
Extend the existing PageHeader rather than creating a competing primitive, migrate primary routes, and add contextual Settings links only where directly task-related.

## Success signal
Every primary page follows one recognizable hierarchy and related configuration is reachable in context.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migrate every primary route to the approved order: title/purpose, primary action, freshness/status, then filters/view controls.
- Allow one primary action unless the specification records a justified exception.
- Contextual configuration links use stable Settings routes/deep links and preserve return context where supported.
- Keep existing API behavior and define loading/error/permission handling for status and freshness sources.
- Each page has one semantic h1, accessible action/link names, logical DOM/focus order, and visible focus.
- Render every consumer at both viewports with no wrapped/clipped required action or document overflow.
- Add shared-component tests and representative rendered route-link tests.
notes:
## Approved Channel Manager hierarchy
Use one semantic h1, `OPERATIONS / CHANNEL MANAGER`, with the purpose description beneath it. Do not repeat `Channel Manager` as a second title or eyebrow. The two pane headers are subordinate headings.
close_reason: Standardized all 11 primary routes through explicit title/purpose, primary action, source status, controls, and related-link slots on newui through commit 9f9177ab. Preserved guarded staged navigation and exact Settings subpages; added truthful loading/error/permission/success-zero/stale lifecycle with scoped Retry and concise live semantics. Full 2,307-test frontend suite, typecheck, ESLint, build, exact-build Playwright 21/21 no retries across target viewports/all routes/200%, code review PASS and QA PASS.

title: Add a compact operator dashboard with actionable system summary
description:
## User value
Operators can identify source health, freshness, pending work, and recent automation failures from one landing surface and drill directly into the relevant filtered screen.

## Work
Implement only the approved minimal card inventory. Reuse existing APIs and client caching; do not duplicate management controls or introduce an aggregate endpoint without documenting why current APIs are insufficient.

## Success signal
Each card has a verified data source, honest state, and working task-oriented deep link.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each approved card exposes label, value, freshness/status, loading skeleton, honest empty state, actionable error/retry, permission-safe state, and relevant filtered deep link.
- Filter state appears in the destination URL where supported.
- Inventory and reuse existing APIs/cache; avoid fan-out storms and ambiguous stale data.
- Status is not color-only; headings/landmarks, card links, focus, and announcements are accessible.
- Primary status remains above the fold at 1280x720 and cards do not crowd or overflow either audited viewport.
- Component, API-contract, error-state, and rendered E2E tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified the compact six-card operator dashboard with authoritative unfiltered totals, App snapshot reuse, StrictMode-safe deduplication, honest states/freshness, permission-safe deep links, and responsive accessible layout. Full gates and exact 34/34 no-retry Playwright pass at 0ba9f191.

title: Implement grouped collapsible left navigation and application shell
description:
## User value
Operators can reach any destination predictably while Channel Manager, Guide, and other dense workspaces retain horizontal room.

## Work
Implement the approved grouped, collapsible navigation by extending existing responsive-navigation primitives. Preserve all route contracts and make expanded/collapsed states fully accessible.

## Success signal
Every route is reachable by pointer and keyboard at both audited sizes, with no destination hidden behind an unlabeled icon.
acceptance_criteria:
• Implement approved groups, current-route indication, expanded/collapsed modes, and a safe default at both viewports.
• Preserve URLs, direct links, browser history, permissions, and existing route behavior.
• Persist the preference locally or explicitly document session-only behavior.
• Use semantic navigation/list/buttons with accessible names, aria-expanded/aria-current, logical keyboard behavior, visible focus, skip-to-content, Escape and focus return where overlays exist.
• Expanded mode is 244px with complete group/destination labels. Collapsed mode is a 68px icon-only rail: section headings and visible destination text occupy zero space, while every icon has an accessible name, title/tooltip, current-state indication, and practical target.
• Sidebar client width equals scroll width; main content clears the rail and never renders beneath it.
• Verify Channel Manager and Guide usability with no clipping or document overflow at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
• Add component and rendered-browser tests for routing, keyboard operation, collapse, persistence, label visibility, icon alignment, and sidebar/page overflow.
close_reason: Implemented grouped 244px/68px accessible operator sidebar and application shell on newui through commit 17f6d532. Preserved routes/history/permissions, canonicalized channel-pipeline aliases, added route-safe skip/focus/title behavior and native/guarded link semantics. Full 2,270-test frontend suite, typecheck, ESLint, production build, exact-build Playwright 10/10 across both viewports/nav states/pages/zoom, code review PASS, and QA PASS.

title: Specify and validate ECM operator-workspace information architecture
description:
## User value
Operators receive route grouping, labels, and page hierarchy aligned to their real tasks rather than an implementation-led list of equally weighted tabs.

## Work
Inventory routes, user types, top tasks, dashboard cards, shell behavior, page-header/toolbar patterns, long-page navigation, responsive priorities, and old-to-new route mapping. Define UI states, accessibility behavior, and the data/API source for every dashboard card and contextual link.

## Success signal
An approved specification maps every route exactly once and prototypes the complete shell at both audited desktop sizes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inventory every primary and Settings route, single-operator user type, and top operator tasks.
- Define and validate group labels/order, collapsed and expanded shell behavior, dashboard card inventory, page hierarchy, toolbar order, long-page behavior, and 1280x720 priorities.
- Map old to new destinations while preserving route URLs, deep links, browser history, and permission behavior.
- Document loading, empty, error, stale, and permission states plus API source for each dashboard card/context link.
- Specify landmarks, skip link, focus order, collapse semantics, keyboard behavior, visible focus, and reduced-motion behavior.

It inventories all primary and 18 Settings routes, pins the approved shell/Channel Manager standards and viewport/accessibility contracts, maps APIs without invented capabilities, preserves legacy URLs, and records only non-blocking Dashboard decisions.

title: Reorganize ECM into a cohesive operator workspace
description:
## User value
Single self-hosted operators can locate routine operations, understand page purpose and status, and retain usable work area at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 instead of navigating an equally weighted collection of tabs.

## Scope

Extend completed PageHeader, overflow-menu, responsive-navigation, and Settings primitives rather than replacing them. No backend feature expansion unless the dashboard inventory proves current APIs cannot provide required state.

title: Label the Full Backup ZIP file chooser for assistive technology
description:
## Problem
The visible .zip file input under Settings > Backup & Restore > Restore Full Backup has no associated label or accessible name. Confirmed by rendered DOM inspection at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 on 2026-07-26.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in and navigate to Settings > Backup & Restore.
2. Scroll to Restore Full Backup.
3. Inspect the visible .zip file input or attempt to locate it with Playwright getByLabel.
4. Observe that it has no associated label or accessible name.

## UX impact
Assistive-technology users cannot identify a high-consequence restore control or its expected file type. Violates WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, and 4.1.2 and weakens error prevention for restore.
acceptance_criteria:
- The file control exposes a unique accessible name such as “Choose ECM full-backup ZIP”.
- Visible text is programmatically associated.
- Accepted .zip format is announced or described.
- Playwright getByLabel locates the control uniquely.
- Rendered verification passes at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
close_reason: Shipped PR #747 (merge 9b5b79a8, v0.17.6-0174) after team review (label work confirmed correct round 1; changelog blocker fixed round 2): Full Backup ZIP file input has visible htmlFor-associated label announcing name + accepted format; red-first tests + live getByLabel verification. Deployed to container from final dev.

title: Give Authentication minimum-password-length control an accessible label
description:
## Problem
The visible number input for minimum password length in Settings > Authentication has no id, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or associated label. Confirmed by rendered DOM and keyboard inspection at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 on 2026-07-26.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in and navigate to Settings > Authentication.
2. Inspect the visible minimum-password-length number input.
3. Query its accessible name or attempt to locate it with Playwright getByLabel.
4. Observe that it has no associated label or accessible name.

## UX impact
Assistive technology exposes a number input without its purpose. Violates WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, and 4.1.2 and Nielsen consistency standards.
acceptance_criteria:
- The control exposes “Minimum password length” as its accessible name.
- Its visible label is programmatically associated.
- Constraint guidance remains available to assistive technology.
- Playwright getByLabel locates the input uniquely.
- Rendered verification passes at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
close_reason: Shipped PR #747 (merge 9b5b79a8, v0.17.6-0174): Minimum Password Length control label-associated with (6-32) hint via aria-describedby; red-first tests incl. labeled-input-drives-save-payload; live-verified. Deployed to container from final dev.

title: Backup artifact producers: user_agents + core_settings + comskip + dvr_rules sections
description: Discovered during kxcjf verification (2026-07-26): build_backup_artifact() in backend/routers/backup.py emits no user_agents/core_settings/comskip/dvr_rules sections (zero references), so the restore-side importers for those categories — fully wired into both registries by kxcjf/PR #742 — receive absent plan slices and degrade to selected=False no-ops. The epic's 13-category round-trip promise needs the producer side: add the four section producers to the artifact builder (SETTINGS plan-slice contract documented in backend/dbas/importers/settings_agents.py: entities are {section: 'core_settings'|'comskip', values: {...}}), extend the artifact tests (test_0i2vt_backup_artifact.py TestCategories), and extend the real-apply round-trip test to consume a genuinely-produced artifact for these categories instead of an augmented plan. Client getters already exist (get_user_agents, get_dvr_rules, get_core_settings in dispatcharr_client.py). Plugins stay excluded per ADR-012 D10.
notes: Producer-side finding (lc6zu): Dispatcharr has NO separate comskip endpoint — dispatcharr_client has only get_core_settings (/api/core/settings/), and the settings_agents importer applies BOTH core_settings and comskip via per-key PATCH update_core_setting on that same namespace. Producer therefore fetches core settings once, normalizes the list-of-{key,value} shape to a mapping, and splits comskip*-prefixed keys into the comskip section (disjoint split, no double-apply). Redaction: dangerous-marked setting VALUES (importer's is_safe_setting_key denylist, imported so the lists cannot drift) are replaced with the REDACTED sentinel at the gather chokepoint, ALWAYS (even include_credentials) since the importer unconditionally skips those keys by name. NOTE: /api/core/useragents/, /api/dvr/rules/, per-name settings PATCH paths remain live-unverified (0i2vt.13 deferred verification flag still stands).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #743; 12-category v0.18 producer scope complete (plugins excluded per ADR-012 D10), drift-proof redaction, genuine round-trip tests

title: Extend builtin Quality Tags seed with 3840P/2160P/4320P/8K

Live instance was fixed via tag-group API (3840P + 2160P added to group 1); fresh installs still get the stale 12-tag seed. Extend the seed with 3840P, 2160P, 4320P, 8K (dedupe against existing entries). Seed runs on fresh DB init only, so verify via unit test / fresh-DB path, not container deploy.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Seed semantics correction: _populate_builtin_tags is NOT fresh-init-only. It runs from init_db() (main.py:902) on EVERY startup and tops up missing builtin tags into existing installs (database.py:1566-1567 comment confirms intent). Live DB verified read-only: 3840P/2160P exist as is_builtin=0, case_sensitive=0 -> seed will SKIP both (no duplicate, no mutation). 4320P/8K will be ADDED to the live DB as builtin tags on first restart after this ships (by design of the sync). title: GH #726: rule editor action-card remove X has full-height hit area — blank-space click deletes the action
description: Field report (langtd19, GH #726, on v0.17.6-0152, reporter-rated P3-Medium): in the Channel Pipeline rule editor's Actions section, the close/remove X button 'extends the length of the section' — its clickable area stretches to the card's full height, so clicking into the blank space below the visible X accidentally removes the action (silent destructive click, no confirm). Repro: create rule → add a create-channel action → click anywhere in the blank space below the X. Screenshot on the issue. Likely cause: the remove button is a direct child of a flex row/column with default align-items:stretch, so the button (or its wrapper) fills the cross axis — same CSS class as the CatchupBadge stretch bug (fixed with align-self:flex-start). Likely site: ActionEditor.tsx / RuleBuilder.tsx action-card header + its CSS. FIX: constrain the button's hit area to its visual glyph (align-self:flex-start or move it into a fixed-height header row), verify the same pattern isn't present on sibling remove buttons (conditions section, other card types) and fix those in the same pass if identical. Frontend-only, Small. Reply to the reporter on GH #726 when shipped.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #735 (merged to dev, v0.17.6-0162). GH #726 (langtd19): the rule editor action-card remove X had an invisible full-height hit area (measured live: 26x423px for an 18x18 glyph — .action-remove-btn was a direct child of the .action-editor flex row with default align-items:stretch), so clicking blank space below the glyph silently deleted the action. CSS-only fix: align-self:flex-start + margin-top:4px, padding-top removed, mirroring the already-correct .condition-remove-btn byte-for-byte. Hit box now 26x26px, live-verified before/after with elementFromPoint + click behavior (blank-space clicks retained the action; the X still removes). Sibling audit of every remove/close button in the editor family: only this one affected. CSS-source regression test pins the fix. Reporter reply + GH #726 close pending PO approval of the draft.

title: ChannelsPane: row + group-header selection not keyboard operable (bare spans) — mirror the zwhw4 semantic-checkbox fix
description: Follow-on surfaced during PR #734 review (zwhw4, StreamsPane). ChannelsPane has the SAME bare-span selection flaw that the review flagged as a must-fix in StreamsPane: the per-channel row selector (ChannelListItem.tsx ~L341, .channel-select-indicator) and the group-header select-all (ChannelsPane.tsx ~L769, .group-checkbox) are clickable spans with no native control semantics — not focusable, no aria-checked, no keyboard handler. A keyboard-only user cannot select channels, which gates every selection-dependent action (the 09x38.17 floating SelectionActionBar, bulk ops, Move-to-group, etc.) exactly the way the StreamsPane gap gated Create-in. FIX (mirror zwhw4's shipped pattern in StreamsPane.tsx ~L2016, v0.17.6-0161): real <button type=button role=checkbox aria-checked aria-label="Select channel <name>"> keeping the material-icons glyph aria-hidden; CSS button reset + :focus-visible accent outline (see .selection-checkbox in StreamsPane.css); same for the group header (note StreamsPane's group header uses a button with aria-pressed — decide checkbox-vs-toggle consistency across panes and note the choice). TESTS (mirror zwhw4's): full keyboard-only flow regression — Tab to a row selector (real tab-order), Space selects (aria-checked asserted), then reach + activate a SelectionActionBar action entirely by keyboard, zero pointer events; plus a semantic-checkbox state test; upgrade existing test helpers to role-based queries. Frontend-only, Small-Medium.

title: Fix flaky CI timeout in formModalCancelButton UX-audit test (walks 245 tsx files, default 5s timeout)
description: Frontend Tests intermittently fails in CI on src/uxAudits/formModalCancelButton.audit.test.ts with 'Test timed out in 5000ms' at line 204 (walkTsxFiles). The audit AST-parses ALL ~245 src/components/*.tsx files with no explicit it() timeout, so it uses vitest's default 5000ms. Locally ~484ms; in CI (coverage instrumentation + loaded runner) ~5061ms -> exceeds 5s -> timeout FAIL (not a real modal-footer violation — it times out before finishing). Downstream: the Docker 'Wait for Test Suite' gate then fails too. It's a creeping flake — was just under the line on recent PRs (dev/sy1sz/4dpiz passed), tipped over as the component count grew; will keep failing every PR until fixed. FIX: give the audit an explicit generous timeout (~30000ms, it legitimately parses 245 files) AND optionally a correctness-preserving speedup (skip the heavy TS AST parse for files whose raw text doesn't even contain 'modal-footer' — such a file cannot have a violation). Check sibling src/uxAudits/*.audit.test.ts for the same full-tree-walk + default-timeout pattern (same latent flake). Test-only change.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #731 (merged to dev, v0.17.6-0157). Fixed the flaky CI timeout in formModalCancelButton.audit.test.ts: the audit AST-parsed all ~245 src/components/*.tsx files under vitest's default 5000ms timeout — fine locally (~0.5s) but ~5.06s under CI coverage, intermittently timing out (and cascading to the Docker Wait-for-Test-Suite gate). Fix: explicit 30s timeout + a behavior-preserving prefilter (skip the TS AST parse for files whose text lacks the 'modal-footer' substring — such a file cannot contain a .modal-footer violation; stale-allowlist assertion still passes, proving detection preserved), cutting runtime to ~334ms. Sibling iconOnlyButtons.a11y.test.ts already had a 60s timeout. Test-only + forced version bump (repo guard requires every PR to advance the build).

title: Provider catch-up badge in M3U manager (aggregate is_catchup across a provider's streams)
description: PO request (follow-on to sy1sz / catch-up badges): show a catch-up badge on an M3U provider/account row in the M3U manager when ECM detects that ANY stream belonging to that provider supports catch-up. Unlike sy1sz (frontend-only, per-stream/per-channel), this needs a BACKEND per-provider aggregation: for each M3U account, does any stream with m3u_account==account_id have is_catchup==true. EFFICIENCY: is_catchup is db_index=True in Dispatcharr (rezg0), so FIRST investigate whether Dispatcharr's streams endpoint supports filtering by is_catchup (e.g. GET /api/channels/streams/?m3u_account=X&is_catchup=true&page_size=1 -> count>0) for a cheap O(providers) indexed query, rather than fetching/scanning all streams per provider. If filtering isn't supported, consider reusing an existing streams-by-provider aggregation (see backend/routers/stream_stats.py / provider paths) or a bounded scan. Deliverable: (1) backend — expose a per-M3U-account has_catchup flag (and optionally max catchup_days) via the M3U accounts payload or a small dedicated endpoint, computed cheaply; (2) frontend — render a catch-up badge (Material 'history' icon, consistent with sy1sz) on the provider/account row in M3UManagerTab, tooltip e.g. 'Provider supports catch-up'; (3) tests. Depends on the sy1sz badge component/pattern for visual consistency. Contract for is_catchup/catchup_days is pinned in rezg0 (closed).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #729 (merged to dev, merge commit a09b575b, v0.17.6-0156). Provider catch-up badge in the M3U manager: new read-only GET /api/providers/catchup-status endpoint aggregates per-M3U-account catch-up via a cheap indexed query (Dispatcharr honors ?m3u_account=X&is_catchup=true; is_catchup is db_index=True -> O(providers) count query, concurrent via asyncio.gather; verified live). Per-account probe failure degrades to has_catchup=false (never 500s the manager); only account-list fetch failure 500s. Frontend renders the shared CatchupBadge (sy1sz) on provider rows in M3UManagerTab when has_catchup===true, best-effort fetch. catchup_days is SAMPLED from one row (not guaranteed max — Dispatcharr won't cheaply give a max; provider depth uniform in practice; named catchup_days not _max to avoid overclaiming). title: Part B follow-up: multi-process/durable concurrency hardening for group-profile reconcile
description: DEFERRED from PR #724 (y3m6o.3) per PO 'right-size + re-baseline' decision (round 8). These are the distributed-systems findings the round-8 team review raised that are NOT warranted at the current single-operator/single-process home-lab tier, to be designed UPFRONT (threat-model first, per the contract-first retro) IF the tool ever moves to genuine multi-process/multi-operator use: (1) CROSS-PROCESS coordination — the per-effective-group asyncio.Lock registry is module-local, so TLS mode (which spawns a second 'uvicorn main:app' subprocess, https_server.py) does not serialize mutations across the two processes; full fix = single-writer + TLS proxy, or a cross-process lock. (2) DURABLE global desired-state — a versioned group-level desired selection incl. explicit-empty (tombstone) so a partially-failed clear auto-heals across sweeps/restarts without silent resurrection (PR #724 ships the HONEST interim: surface incomplete clear, no false success). (3) Deep normalize-vs-save and save-vs-save TOCTOU (compute winner/targets inside the lock critical section). Precondition to pick this up: a decision that the tier has changed. Do NOT build this for single-operator home-lab use.
notes: Also noted (round-9 audit): routers/backup.py DBAS-restore calls engine.run_task(DBAS_RESTORE_TASK_ID) directly via its own admin-gated endpoint (not /api/tasks/{id}/run), so it's a pre-existing 'tasks should only execute in main' candidate NOT covered by the TLS proxy allowlist. Orthogonal to profile reconcile; left out of PR #724. Fold into any future 'all background work is main-only' hardening.
close_reason: WON'T FIX AT CURRENT TIER (PO decision). ECM is single-operator/single-process home-lab; the distributed-systems hardening here only pays off under genuine concurrency (multi-user or multi-process-with-concurrent-mutation), which is not the current or planned tier. The main item — cross-process coordination for the profile RECONCILE — is ALREADY shipped: PR #724 round-9 made main the sole writer via the TLS subprocess proxy (profile-mutating/reconcile routes forward to main, so the in-process per-effective-group lock is authoritative). RESIDUALS documented here, to be REOPENED + designed upfront (threat-model first, per the contract-first retro) IF/WHEN the tier changes to genuine multi-process/multi-operator use — do NOT build for single-operator: (1) DURABLE tombstone/versioned desired-state so a partially-failed CLEAR auto-heals across sweeps/restarts (PR #724 ships the honest interim: incomplete clear surfaces truthfully, operator re-saves — sufficient at tier). (2) DEEP normalize-vs-save + save-vs-save TOCTOU (compute winner/targets inside the lock critical section) — only reachable under concurrent saves a single operator doesn't generate. (3) Pre-existing UNLOCKED direct-membership endpoints (PATCH /api/channel-profiles/{id}/channels[/bulk-update]) — never used the reconcile lock even in main; orthogonal to auto-sync reconcile. (4) DBAS-restore (routers/backup.py) runs engine.run_task directly and could execute in the TLS subprocess — a rare admin op, 'background-work-should-be-main-only' candidate, also low-value at tier. Reopen precondition: an explicit decision that the deployment tier has changed.

title: Determine Dispatcharr 0.28.0 catch-up API path/fields
description: Discovery for the catch-up badge feature. Dispatcharr 0.28.0 adds catch-up (timeshift) support. Inspect the Dispatcharr source on GitHub (github.com/Dispatcharr/Dispatcharr, 0.28.0 tag) to determine: (1) which API endpoint/serializer exposes catch-up capability for a channel and/or its streams (likely the channel or stream detail — fields such as catchup / catchup-source / tvg-rec / catchup_days or similar, mirroring XMLTV/M3U catchup attributes), (2) the exact field name(s) carrying the catch-up flag AND the number of days supported, (3) whether the info lives on the stream, the channel, or both, and how ECM's dispatcharr_client would fetch it. Record findings in the bead / docs so the feature bead can implement against a known contract. Reference: M3U catchup attrs are typically catchup="append|default|shift|flussonic" + catchup-days="N"; XMLTV EPG may carry per-programme catchup too.
close_reason: DISCOVERY COMPLETE (verified against Dispatcharr v0.28.0 source AND ECM's own code). CONTRACT: catch-up is exposed as two scalar fields with identical JSON keys on BOTH stream and channel objects: is_catchup (boolean) + catchup_days (int, days). Channel-level is a denormalized rollup (is_catchup = ANY member stream true; catchup_days = MAX across streams). JSON keys == model field names (serializers list them explicitly). Present in BOTH list AND detail of GET /api/channels/streams/ and GET /api/channels/channels/ (no query param, no extra fetch). Parser derives them from Xtream tv_archive / tv_archive_duration (the IPTV catchup MODE string is NOT modeled — only the bool flag + day count). SUPPORTED TEST = is_catchup === true (authoritative; NEVER infer from catchup_days). TOOLTIP = catchup_days; edge case is_catchup=true & catchup_days=0 => 'catch-up available' (do NOT render '0 days'); is_catchup=false & catchup_days>0 => not supported (flag wins). ECM INTEGRATION: NO backend change needed — get_channels() (raw passthrough, routers/channels.py) and get_streams() (passthrough + channel_group_name enrichment, routers/streams.py) ALREADY carry both fields to the frontend. ECM already reads stream is_catchup internally (GH #652, channel_pipeline_evaluator) but reads catchup_days NOWHERE, and the frontend Channel/Stream types do NOT yet declare either field (only 'catchup' as a SortMode). => sy1sz is a FRONTEND-ONLY feature. Sources: github.com/Dispatcharr/Dispatcharr@v0.28.0 apps/channels/models.py + serializers.py + api_urls.py + api_views.py, apps/m3u/tasks.py.

title: [bug] Channel profile edit errors masked as generic 500 in profiles.py — real Dispatcharr status/body discarded (GH #720 comment)
description: GH #720 follow-up (langtd19): editing Channel Profiles in the Channel Manager throws a red toast titled 'Profiles' with only 'Internal server error' as detail. Root cause (investigation): backend/routers/profiles.py blanket-maps almost every upstream failure to HTTPException(500, 'Internal server error'), discarding the real Dispatcharr status/body. 6 handlers mask (list/create/get/rename/delete/single-membership); only bulk_update_profile_channels correctly surfaces upstream 4xx via upstream_http_exception (bead lq38l.4). close_reason: Shipped in PR #727 (merged to dev, merge commit 76543df0, v0.17.6-0154). GH #720 follow-up: 6 channel-profile handlers in backend/routers/profiles.py (list/create/get/rename/delete/single-membership) no longer mask upstream Dispatcharr failures as an opaque HTTPException(500, 'Internal server error') — they now surface the real status/body via the upstream_http_exception idiom (the same one bulk_update_profile_channels already used), so a Dispatcharr 4xx reaches the operator with its true detail. Diagnosability fix — makes the reporter's environment-specific failure visible (the surfaced detail is the log info we'd have asked them for). 6 per-handler upstream-4xx tests + genuine-non-HTTP-error-still-500 contract retained; stream-profile handlers out of scope. Code-review green.

title: [bug] GH#720: Channel Pipeline / Event Sync rules ignore channel-profile selection — new channels added to ALL profiles
description:
GH issue #720 (langtd19). Standard and event-sync Channel Pipeline rules with a channel-profile selection added created channels to ALL channel profiles instead of only the selected one(s). Root cause: assign_channel_profile applied the selection enable-only, but Dispatcharr auto-joins every new channel to all profiles, so honoring a selection is subtractive (enable selected + disable the channel in every other known profile). Two parts:

PART A (rule-action path) — IMPLEMENTED, code-reviewed (APPROVE-WITH-NITS, all closed), shipping in build 0.17.6-0150 (PR to dev). Added shared _apply_exclusive_profile_membership helper in channel_pipeline_executor.py; refactored _execute_assign_channel_profile and _assign_default_profiles onto it; lifted the engine profile-fetch gate in channel_pipeline_engine.py to fetch the full profile universe whenever any standard OR event-sync rule uses an assign_channel_profile action (not only when a global default is set). Degrades to enable-selected-only when the universe is unavailable. Full backend suite green (7639 passed); new executor + engine regression tests including the #720 gate coverage.

PART B (M3U AutoSync-modal reconciliation path) — STILL OPEN. Covers the AutoSyncSettingsModal.tsx / custom_properties.channel_profile_ids path per PO decisions 1a/2b/3a. Not addressed in 0150.

#720 tracks both parts and stays OPEN until Part B ships.
close_reason: All children shipped and GH #720 closed. y3m6o.1 (truthful run-level status, PR #723, v0.17.6-0152), y3m6o.3 (Part B — M3U Auto-Sync channel-profile reconciliation, PR #724, v0.17.6-0153), y3m6o.2 (make exclusive-membership semantics visible in dry-run + rule copy, PR #730, v0.17.6-0158). Original issue (channels added to ALL profiles) fixed by Part A (PR #721, v0.17.6-0150) + Part B; the separately-reported edit-profiles error was fixed under lsctv (PR #727, v0.17.6-0154). title: POST /api/client-errors returns 500 on stack URLs with out-of-range port
description: Pre-existing bug surfaced during uliyr verification (not caused by that work): POST /api/client-errors returns 500 when a reported stack trace contains a URL with an out-of-range port number — obfuscate.py line 36 calls parsed.port, which raises ValueError for ports outside 0-65535, and the exception is uncaught. Impact: the client-error reporting endpoint itself crashes on exactly the kind of malformed input error reports contain, so those reports are lost. Fix: wrap the parsed.port access in a try/except (treat unparseable port as no port) and add a regression test with a hostile URL. Small.

title: commit-msg guard hook: bead-id regex cannot match this repo's alphanumeric bead ids
description: Surfaced twice while shipping PRs #709 and #710: the commit-msg guard hook rejects git commit -m messages that lack a name-123 style token, but this repo's bead ids are alphanumeric (uliyr, vkktd.4, 09x38.17) and can never match that regex. Both ship engineers had to work around it with git commit -F, which passes with the bead id in the body — meaning the hook currently gates on message-delivery mechanism, not on actual bead reference presence. Fix: widen the regex to match this repo's id format (enhancedchannelmanager-[a-z0-9.]+ or the bare suffix form) so -m works and the check actually validates what it intends to. Locate the hook (likely repo-level git hook or the shared pretooluse hook config) and add a test case with a real bead id. Small.
notes: Guard located: /home/lecaptainc/claude-agent-dev-team/hooks/pretooluse.py (PreToolUse hook, Rule 3), registered directly in ~/.claude/settings.json. Finding: own-prefix alphanumeric ids (enhancedchannelmanager-zfp2z, -0i2vt.4, -09x38.17) already matched at HEAD via -m; the real gap was the -F/--file bypass (message files were never validated — gate was on delivery mechanism). Fix (uncommitted working-copy change in claude-agent-dev-team repo): hook now reads the -F/--file message file at hook time and validates bead-reference presence there too; fails open for unreadable messages (-F -, shell substitutions, absent file). Bare-suffix form (zfp2z alone) intentionally NOT accepted: [a-z0-9]+ without prefix would match every English word and gut the check. Self-test extended (-F block + 09x38.17 case), --check passes. Needs a commit in the claude-agent-dev-team repo when PO says ship — nothing to commit in enhancedchannelmanager.

title: Journal noise policy: decide retention for run_on_refresh_skipped and task start/complete buckets
description: PO DECISION 2026-07-19: auto-purge BOTH remaining noise buckets — auto_creation/run_on_refresh_skipped (approx 8,044 rows) and task start/complete (approx 8,500 rows, approx 285/day) — and make the policy configurable in settings rather than hardcoded. Implementation: extend the existing JournalNoisePurgeTask (backend/tasks/journal_noise_purge.py, shipped in bead uliyr v0.17.6-0140) which already carries retention_days plus per-category toggles surfaced in TaskEditorModal. Add both buckets as toggleable categories on the same settings surface, defaulting to enabled at the established 3-day retention. Engineer to evaluate whether per-category retention overrides (falling back to the task default) are warranted — task start/complete carries more operational forensic value than run_on_refresh_skipped, so a single shared retention may over- or under-purge one of them. Predicates must stay narrowly scoped the way uliyr's did: category plus action_type allowlists verified against actual write call sites, with survival tests proving neighboring categories and action types are untouched. Related minor fix noted during uliyr work: the rule duplicate endpoint journals no create entry (delete-only pairs observed), an audit-trail asymmetry that can be fixed in the same pass.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #733 (merged to dev, v0.17.6-0160). Implements the PO decision: auto-purge auto_creation/run_on_refresh_skipped (~8k rows) + scheduled task start/complete (~8.5k rows, ~285/day) via the existing JournalNoisePurgeTask, both toggleable on the TaskEditorModal surface, default-on at 3-day retention. Forensic rows protected STRUCTURALLY by the predicate (cancel/fail/error + manually-triggered runs never purge, any age) so no per-category retention knobs needed; routine scheduled rows are redundant with task_executions (30-day retention). Also: rule-duplicate endpoint now journals a create entry (audit-trail asymmetry fixed). Review cycle hardened shared task-registry infra with 4 real pre-merge catches: (1) task config now persists to ScheduledTask.config + rehydrates on startup (was silently reverting for ALL tasks incl. CleanupTask retention — pre-existing latent data loss); (2) persistence is intent-driven — stored config is ONLY accumulated operator PATCH keys, never a read of the mutable live instance, so schedule-run parameter overlays structurally cannot become global defaults (incl. via enabled-only or partial PATCHes); (3) hydration strips field-level nulls (shared helper with write side) — fixes a probe-all→probe-nothing flip hazard; (4) three tasks opted out via persist_config=False with rationale (dbas_restore/dbas_sync destructive-arm flags re-disarm on restart, m3u_digest settings-table-backed). 18-test persistence suite incl. the reviews' exact repro sequences; final review APPROVED with zero findings.
