title: Channel logos broken when Dispatcharr is reached via docker-internal hostname (GH #662)
description: GitHub issue #662 (FractalBoy, v0.17.5, reporter priority P4, screenshot attached to issue). When ECM connects to Dispatcharr via a docker-network hostname (localhost behind gluetun, or a container name), channel icons never render: logo URLs served to the browser are built from the Dispatcharr base URL that only the ECM *server* can resolve, so the client's image fetches fail. Repro: same docker network, point ECM at Dispatcharr by internal hostname, open channel list -> no icons. Reporter's suggested fix: ECM should serve an image URL built from the hostname the client used to reach ECM and proxy the image through to Dispatcharr. Triage to confirm where logo URLs originate (backend passthrough vs frontend construction), whether ECM's existing logo cache/proxy machinery (logo manager, /cache endpoints) can be reused, and any auth implications of proxying. SHIPPED (v0.17.6-0131): backend/routers/channels.py. - New GET /api/channels/logos/{logo_id}/image — authenticated same-origin proxy. Fetches bytes server-side from Dispatcharr's /api/channels/logos/{id}/cache/ (live-observed: 200+bytes for both local-file and external-URL logos, 404 JSON for unknown ids, upstream Cache-Control 3600s remote / 14400s local, no ETag, no redirects). Forwards If-None-Match upstream (304 short-circuit passthrough); falls back to a default Cache-Control (public, max-age=86400) when upstream sends none; maps upstream 404 -> 404, other >=400 / transport failures -> 502. Intentionally NOT in main.py's AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS — same-origin tags send the httpOnly access_token cookie, so the global auth middleware admits real browser sessions with no frontend change needed. - _ecm_origin(request): browser-facing scheme://host, honoring X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host (first value of a comma list) for reverse-proxied deployments, falling back to the request's own scheme + Host header (always browser-reachable by construction). - _rewrite_logo_cache_url(logo, origin): rewrites a logo dict's cache_url to {origin}/api/channels/logos/{id}/image, preserving Dispatcharr's ?v= cache-buster so browser caching stays correct across logo replacements. Leaves a falsy cache_url untouched (frontend falls back to logo.url) and never touches url itself. - Wired into all logo response paths so a logo renders immediately everywhere it's returned: GET /logos (list, both the passthrough and aggregate-and-sort branches), GET /logos/{id}, POST /logos (create, incl. the find-existing-by-url fallback), POST /logos/upload, PATCH /logos/{id}. Tests: 15 new tests in backend/tests/routers/test_logos.py covering the proxy endpoint (200/304/404/502 mapping, If-None-Match forwarding, Cache-Control fallback, ETag passthrough) and the cache_url rewrite across get/create/upload/update responses (?v= preserved, falsy cache_url left alone, url field untouched). 156 router tests green (test_logos.py + test_channels.py). Live-verified: 401 on unauthenticated image fetch, successful proxy fetch through the authenticated session, cache_url rewritten in real API responses.

title: Merge Streams action: Exclude target groups renders full group list — needs dropdown (GH #677)

placeholder?, emptyMessage?, disabled?, itemLabelSingular?, itemLabelPlural?,
className? }. Collapsed "N selected" button, search, Select All/Clear All
(search-scoped), checkbox list in a role="group" container, outside-click

classes from shared/common.css (documented shared idiom) rather than new
CSS, per the CSS golden rule.

Two portal-specific bugs found and fixed during live verification (not
caught by unit tests — jsdom doesn't lay out real stacking contexts):
1. Menu renders via createPortal to document.body at position:fixed (like

   Escape closed the dropdown AND simultaneously triggered the parent

   unwanted "Unsaved Changes" discard dialog.

Tests: new GroupMultiSelectDropdown.test.tsx (17 tests: open/close, search
filter, select/clear all, onChange payloads, outside click, Escape, inactive
option styling, empty state, disabled state) + updated ActionEditor.test.tsx
(existing checkbox tests now open the dropdown first) + new coverage in
RuleBuilder.test.tsx and BulkRuleSettingsModal.test.tsx for the
normalization-group picker. 160 frontend tests green across the 4 files,
1965 total suite green, tsc clean, eslint --max-warnings 0 clean.

Live-verified at localhost:6100 against real production-scale data (~2900
channel groups — the exact "unwieldy for large group counts" scenario):
collapsed -> open -> search -> select -> collapse, Save + reopen round-trip
persistence, Escape isolation, and a StreamsPane regression check (existing

zi85o-9.png (not committed — local verification artifacts only).

Deferred (not in this scope): StreamsPane/ChannelsPane's own filter

of the shared common.css classes — worth a follow-up cleanup bead, not
converted to GroupMultiSelectDropdown here (different interaction shape,
lower priority, avoids blast radius on working code).

title: User report: {date+3d} template token rejected in stream-name-match regex condition
description: User report via PO 2026-07-17. In a Channel Pipeline rule's stream-name-match (regex) condition, the user entered {date+3d} and got REGEX_VALIDATION_ERROR ('expected } at position 2', conditions[2].value) — the validator correctly rejects it as raw regex ({...} = quantifier). Open question driving triage: does {date+Nd}-style dynamic date tokenization exist ANYWHERE in ECM (dummy-EPG template engine? event sync date handling?) such that the user's expectation is reasonable, and is there/should there be token expansion in rule-condition regex fields? Likely dispositions: (a) feature request — date-token expansion in conditions (relates to backlog bead 6lhmb 'Auto Sync and Auto Creation by date'); (b) docs/UX gap — clarify the field is raw regex and point to whatever the right mechanism is; (c) user guidance only. Triage first; PO decides.
notes:
TRIAGE COMPLETE (2026-07-17, read-only): VERDICT = BUG, not feature request. {date+3d} is a first-class, DOCUMENTED feature (USER_GUIDE.md:742, 'Date Expansion in Regex', contributed by @lpukatch): channel_pipeline_evaluator._expand_date_placeholders (evaluator.py:189-279) expands {date}/{today}/{date+N[d|w]}/{date-N}/{date:FORMAT} (90-day cap) into a date-alternation regex BEFORE compile at runtime (evaluator.py:508 for stream_name_matches; also 539/674/686). But the WRITE-TIME gate — regex_lint.lint_conditions_json → lint_pattern → safe_regex.compile (regex_lint.py:620→413) — compiles the RAW value with no expansion, and the strict 'regex' library rejects {date+3d} (and even the documented bare {date}) as an invalid quantifier → REGEX_COMPILE_ERROR/REGEX_VALIDATION_ERROR 422. Runtime and docs are right; the gate is wrong. No workaround exists (save is blocked). FIX SHAPE: run the same date-placeholder expansion (or equivalent pre-pass) in the lint path before safe_regex.compile so validation exercises the same string the evaluator will; include the error-message docs pointer check. Also note: docs/style_guide.md#regex anchor confirmed valid; stdlib re would accept the literal but ECM deliberately uses the stricter safe_regex — the fix is expansion, not loosening the engine.
MERGED via PR #697 (v0.17.6-0128, dev 9224eb17). Fix verified live pre-merge (422→200 on {date+3d}, broken patterns still rejected). Bead stays OPEN awaiting reporter confirmation per user-reported-bug DoD: (1) merged ✓; (2) deploy to where the user is — their instance picks it up on next :dev image pull; (3) reporter notified — reply drafted, PO relaying; (4) close on reporter confirmation.

title: Channel Pipeline Rollback button 409s on snapshot-backed runs — frontend never sends confirm=true
description: Found during bead 09x38.9's backend trace (PR #687, which changed copy only and deliberately left this alone). Backend rollback_execution delegates to restore_snapshot when a snapshot exists AND confirm=true is passed; the frontend's Rollback button never sends confirm, so on has_snapshot=true executions the call 409s instead of performing (or offering) the restore — Rollback effectively only works on legacy no-snapshot runs. Decide the intended UX: (a) frontend catches the 409 and re-prompts with the snapshot-restore warning then retries with confirm=true, (b) Rollback is hidden/disabled on snapshot-backed rows (Undo this run is the correct action there), or (c) backend stops requiring confirm for this path. Note the new PR-687 tooltip copy already tells users to prefer 'Undo this run' for full restores — option (b) may be the cleanest. Evidence: channel_pipeline_engine.py rollback_execution/restore_snapshot; ADR-010 §D5.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #732 (merged to dev, v0.17.6-0159). Channel Pipeline 'Rollback' button 409'd on snapshot-backed runs because the frontend never sent confirm=true (backend rollback_execution requires confirm to delegate to restore_snapshot). PO decision (option b): hide Rollback on has_snapshot=true rows — the existing 'Undo this run' button (restore-snapshot?confirm=true) is the correct full-restore action there and the tooltip already steers users to it. Fix: AND !execution.has_snapshot into the Rollback button render condition; Rollback still shows on legacy no-snapshot runs. Also tidied the now-misdirecting Rollback tooltip + confirm-dialog copy (they pointed to Undo/snapshot which don't apply on the no-snapshot rows Rollback now appears on). Frontend-only + tests (snapshot -> no Rollback + Undo shown; legacy -> Rollback shown). ADR-010 D5 confirm gate preserved.

title: Pending Merges: surface candidate channel name, not bare ID (API contract gap)
description: UX pass 3 Major (more useful; SOURCE-CONFIRMED ONLY — live queue was empty and the subnav link is hidden at zero pending, so verify live once the queue has rows). The 'candidate channel' a row would merge into renders as a bare candidate_channel_id; PendingMergeRecord in frontend/src/services/api.ts has no name field, so this is an API-contract gap, not a frontend-only fix. An operator deciding Merge-vs-Create-New for a non-exact match must leave the page to identify the target of a data-merge decision. Fix: include candidate channel name (and ideally group/number) in the pending-merges payload + render it. Backend change — engineer to assess join cost; open question from pass 3: is the missing name a known deferred trade-off or an oversight?
notes:
Implemented in PR #694 (branch feat/09x38.14-pending-merge-names, build 0126).

Join-cost finding: resolved via ONE batched Dispatcharr call per list-page
request (client.get_channels(page=1, page_size=1000)), mirroring the
existing "candidate pool" convention already used by GET /candidates and
the enqueue endpoint in backend/routers/channel_merges.py. Rejected
per-row get_channel(id) resolution as an N+1 explosion (up to
MAX_PAGE_SIZE=200 Dispatcharr round-trips per page). Answer to the pass-3
open question: this was an oversight, not a deliberate deferred
trade-off — PendingMergeRecord simply never carried a name field since
BD-E shipped it.

Payload additions (additive, backward-compatible): candidate_channel_name,
candidate_channel_number, candidate_channel_group_name — all null when
the candidate can't be resolved (deleted since queuing, or a Dispatcharr
fetch failure; both degrade to the same UI fallback rather than a 500).

Frontend: PendingMergesPage renders name (+ #number, group) as the
primary label, id kept as secondary/tooltip text; unresolved candidates
render "Channel no longer exists (id N)".

MCP: list_pending_channel_merges is a pure passthrough of this endpoint's
JSON — it gains the new fields automatically, no code change; only its
docstring was updated for accuracy.

Gates: backend 7231 passed/4 skipped; frontend 1913 passed (133 files);
tsc/eslint/vite build clean. Live: deployed both sides to ecm-ecm-1;
mcp__ecm__list_pending_channel_merges confirmed the live (still-empty)
queue returns the same {merges: [], total: 0, ...} shape; Playwright
confirmed the Channel Manager subnav Pending Merges entry stays hidden at
zero pending (no regression), no console errors. Did not create
pending-merge rows on the live instance per instruction.

title: Logo Manager: sortable columns + unused-logo filter at 2,946-logo scale
description: UX pass 3 Major (more useful). 2,946 logos; visible rows show '0 channels' used-by; no column sort and no orphan/unused filter (DOM-confirmed: headers are plain text, not buttons). Bulk-identifying unused logos is impractical at this scale — while M3U Changes' comparable table IS sortable, so this is feature-age variance, not a design tier. Fix: sortable columns (at minimum used-by count, name) + an 'unused only' filter; pairs naturally with existing delete flows for cleanup. Evidence: cross-check clear against the held ChannelsPane/Streams tooling theme when implementing.
notes:
Implemented (bead status left in_progress per instructions — not closing).

PR #686: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/pull/686 (feat/09x38.13-logo-sort-filter -> dev), build v0.17.6-0119.

Key finding (Real Fixtures First): read Dispatcharr's live LogoViewSet source in the dispatcharr container. It has NO ordering support at all (get_queryset() hardcodes .order_by('name'), only DjangoFilterBackend configured with no filterset_fields — no 'ordering' param exists to forward). Its 'search' param was ALSO already a silent no-op — the view only reads name/used/ids, never search. So ECM's own /api/channels/logos search passthrough had never actually worked upstream; it only appeared to work because LogoManagerTab loaded all 2946 logos client-side and filtered in the browser.

Implementation: GET /api/channels/logos gains sort_by (name|channel_count), sort_order (asc|desc), unused_only (bool). When any is set, ECM fetches the complete logo list from Dispatcharr in ONE call (client.get_all_logos_raw(), via Dispatcharr's no_pagination=true escape hatch) and sorts/filters/paginates locally in Python -- this is what makes sort and the filter truthful across pages. When none are set, the original zero-overhead single-Dispatcharr-page passthrough is preserved byte-for-byte (locked by test_uses_passthrough_when_no_sort_filter_or_search), so LogoModal's picker / AutoSyncSettingsModal / GuideTab / getAllLogos() are unaffected.

LogoManagerTab.tsx rewritten from load-all-2946-then-slice-client-side to true per-page server fetch, with M3UChangesTab's sortable-header idiom (click header -> toggle asc/desc, arrow icon) plus an 'Unused only' toggle.

Gates: backend 7226 passed/4 skipped (pre-existing skips, unrelated) via ../.venv/bin/python from backend dir. Frontend: 1861 passed/128 files, eslint --max-warnings 0 clean, tsc --noEmit clean, vite build clean.

Live verification against the real 2946-logo dataset: default load '2946 total'; Unused only toggle -> '2945 matching' (exactly one logo has channels); Used By descending surfaces that one logo (Flo Racing, 50 channels) at the top; search 'flo racing' while sorted -> '1 matching' (search composes with sort); Name sorts alphabetically both directions.

Backlog candidate (not filed as a bead, noting per 'Findings Are Backlog Candidates'): the new sort/filter path re-fetches the full 2946-row Dispatcharr catalog on every page-turn (no caching) since Dispatcharr itself can't paginate a sorted/filtered result. Fine at current scale (single fast annotated query), but worth a short-TTL cache if the catalog grows much larger.

title: Settings 'Security' page: scope/name mismatch + instant-persist with no Save button

title: Rule editors: identical stepper component, opposite interaction models — align on the Event Sync wizard pattern
description: UX pass 2 Major (cleanup). Standard-rule and Event-Sync-rule editors share the same visual stepper pill nav but behave oppositely: Event Sync is a true wizard (one step rendered at a time); Standard Rule's stepper scroll-jumps within one continuous form (DOM-confirmed: all step regions are rendered siblings). Learning one gives the wrong mental model for the other. Pass 2 rated the Event Sync editor best-in-class (live plain-language preview, adaptive footer, progressive disclosure) — align the Standard editor to it, or visually differentiate the two navigation idioms. Evidence: ux09x38-p2-standard-rule-editor.png, ux09x38-p2-rule-editor-open.png family.
notes: PO DECISION (2026-07-17): Option (b) — TRUE WIZARD CONVERSION. PR #692 (visual differentiation) closed unmerged and superseded. Standard Rule editor becomes step-at-a-time like the Event Sync wizard: per-step render gating, per-step vs on-save validation display routing, ~68-test rewrite accepted. Round-trip invariant remains mandatory (open existing full-config rule → step through → save yields unchanged payload). The whole-rule synthesis rail (live intent sentence / analyzer / save hint) should REMAIN visible across steps if feasible — it reads from full state, which exists regardless of which step renders. Reuse the Event Sync editor's stepper/footer components where practical.

title: Channel Pipeline: disambiguate 'Rollback' vs 'Undo this run' in Execution History
description: UX pass 2 Major (cleanup). Two adjacent icon-only, destructive-sounding actions on every Execution History row are asymmetrically explained: title='Rollback' has zero elaboration while the other reads 'Undo this run — restores pre-run channel state from snapshot' (DOM-confirmed). A user cannot tell what distinguishes them before clicking. Fix: distinct names + explanatory tooltips for both (and consider a confirm dialog stating exactly what each will restore). Evidence: ux09x38-p2-execution-history-actions.png (repo-root scratch, do not commit).
notes:
Implemented in PR #687 (branch fix/09x38.9-rollback-undo-labels, build 0120).

TRUE SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE (traced handlers -> engine):
- Rollback (rollbackChannelPipelineExecution -> POST /rollback -> rollback_execution
  in channel_pipeline_engine.py, no-snapshot/legacy path): the LEGACY PER-RUN UNDO.
  Deletes channel(s) this run created and reverts channel(s) it modified using this
  run's own recorded changes (created/modified entity lists, or a surgical
  journal-driven un-merge when the journal fully covers the run). Does NOT touch the
  pre-run snapshot.
- Undo this run (restoreChannelPipelineSnapshot -> POST /restore-snapshot?confirm=true
  -> restore_snapshot): a FULL WHOLE-RUN RESTORE from the pre-run ChannelPipelineSnapshot
  (ADR-010 SS D8). Intentional optimistic overwrite (SS D5): overwrites every affected
  channel's current stream assignments with the exact pre-run state, discarding ANY
  edits made since (manual edits, later merges, Dispatcharr drift), including edits
  made after the run finished.

PRE-EXISTING BEHAVIOR NOTE (out of scope, flagged not fixed): rollback_execution
itself delegates to restore_snapshot when a snapshot exists AND confirm=true is
passed, but the frontend Rollback button's API call never sends confirm — so on a
has_snapshot=true execution (where BOTH buttons render), clicking Rollback currently
409s ("has a pre-run snapshot... re-send with confirm=true") rather than doing
anything. Tooltip/confirm copy describes the intended/legacy semantics (accurate for
the no-snapshot case, which is when Rollback is actually the only action shown).
Backlog candidate, not fixed here per the scope guard (UI text only, no behavior
change).

COPY CHANGES: row tooltips on both actions rewritten to state what each restores and
cross-reference each other by name; Confirm Rollback dialog body rewritten from a
bare count to name the legacy-undo mechanism and point at "Undo this run"; Undo This
Run dialog gained one contrast sentence. Rollback button also got the shared
.action-btn.danger class (red hover) to differentiate from Undo's existing amber
hover -- the two Material Icons glyphs (undo vs settings_backup_restore) were already
visually distinct so no icon swap was needed. aria-labels left unchanged (Rollback /
Undo this run) to avoid churning ~15 existing accessible-name-based tests; only
title attributes and dialog body text changed.

TESTS: 3 new + 1 extended in ChannelPipelineTab.test.tsx (tooltip content x2, decline
Confirm Rollback -> API not called, Undo This Run dialog contrast sentence).

GATES: npx vitest run 1864/1864 pass; eslint --max-warnings 0 clean; tsc --noEmit
clean; npm run build clean.

LIVE VERIFICATION (Playwright MCP @ localhost:6100): hovered both actions on a real
completed execution row, tooltips read the new copy; clicked Rollback -> Confirm
Rollback dialog showed new copy -> Cancel (declined); clicked Undo this run -> Undo
This Run dialog showed warning banner + new contrast sentence -> Cancel (declined).
Execution status confirmed unchanged (still completed, not rolled_back) after both
declines -- nothing executed against live pipeline history.

PR #687 pushed, gh pr checks --watch in progress.

title: Auto-Sync Settings modal: de-duplicate overlap fields + surface a discoverable Auto-Sync Rules view
description: UX pass-1 consolidation finding, re-verified valid on the post-#678 build (#678 changed save semantics, not modal composition). The 3rd-level modal (M3U Manager → Manage Groups → per-group gear) has 7 sections; three duplicate concepts that already have dedicated shallower UI one level up: Channel Profile Assignment ↔ per-account 'Manage Profiles', Stream Profile Assignment ↔ top-level 'Stream Profiles' screen, Channel Name Filter (Regex) ↔ per-account 'Manage Filters'. Same concept configurable in two unrelated-looking places = Nielsen #4 consistency + #6 discoverability violation. Force EPG Source / Override Channel Group are defensible as sync-time per-group overrides (persisted on the M3U group's own settings row) — not asserted misplaced. Scope: (a) de-duplicate or explicitly cross-reference the three overlap fields ('overrides Manage Profiles for auto-synced channels only'); (b) improve discoverability — today reaching a configured override means per-account → up-to-919-group modal → 'Auto-sync only' filter → gear that is disabled until BOTH Enabled and Auto-Sync toggles are on. Consider a dedicated 'Auto-Sync Rules' list view mirroring the Channel Pipeline tab's list pattern. Related polish: the disabled gear tooltip mentions only auto-sync, not the Enabled prerequisite. Evidence: ux09x38-p1recheck-07..12.png at repo root (untracked scratch — do not commit).
notes:
PO DECISION (2026-07-17): DROP the 3 duplicate fields (Channel Profile Assignment, Stream Profile Assignment, Channel Name Filter) from the Auto-Sync Settings modal, relying on the dedicated shallower screens — engineer must FIRST verify the per-group override semantics are genuinely redundant (i.e. the dedicated screens cover the same effect for auto-synced channels; if a group-scoped override has distinct behavior the dedicated screen cannot express, STOP and report before deleting). Auto-Sync Rules list view DEFERRED — out of scope for this bead.

ENGINEER FINDING (2026-07-17) — STOP TRIPWIRE HIT, NO CODE CHANGES MADE:

Verified all 3 candidate-duplicate fields against the dedicated screens the PO
decision named. All 3 have DISTINCT semantics the dedicated screen cannot
replicate — deletion would be a real regression, not a dedup. No branch, no
PR. Bead status left untouched pending PO re-scoping.

1. Channel Profile Assignment (custom_properties.channel_profile_ids) vs
   "per-account Manage Profiles" (M3UProfileModal, onManageProfiles):
   NOT THE SAME ENTITY. M3UProfileModal edits M3UAccountProfile — a stream
   connection/failover profile (max_streams, search/replace regex on stream
   URLs), type M3UAccountProfile in types/index.ts:224. The auto-sync field
   assigns Dispatcharr ChannelProfile (client-facing channel visibility,
   type ChannelProfile:154, channels:number[]) to channels AS Dispatcharr
   auto-creates them from this one group. Same English word "profile," two
   unrelated domain objects. A real Channel-Profile-assignment surface DOES
   exist elsewhere (ChannelProfilesListModal + bulk assign in Channel
   Manager, and default_channel_profile_ids global default in Settings) but
   neither is group-scoped-at-sync-time: Channel Manager's bulk action is a
   manual one-off on already-existing channels; the Settings default applies
   globally to every auto-created channel account-wide. Neither can say
   "channels synced from THIS group get profile X" without affecting every
   other auto-synced group.

2. Stream Profile Assignment (custom_properties.stream_profile_id) vs
   "top-level Stream Profiles screen" (StreamProfilesListModal):
   Read the file's own header comment: "Read-only list — no edit/delete
   here... unlike channel profiles, ECM has no PATCH/DELETE stream-profile
   endpoints wired at all yet." It is a CATALOG CRUD screen (list + create
   only) for StreamProfile entities (ffmpeg command definitions) — it has
   ZERO assignment capability, to a channel or a group. The only other place
   ECM sets target_stream_profile_id is MergeChannelsModal (a one-off
   channel-merge action), unrelated to auto-sync. Dropping this field removes
   100% of ECM's ability to assign a stream profile to auto-synced channels
   per-group; there is no fallback UI path at all.

3. Channel Name Filter/Regex (custom_properties.name_match_regex) vs
   per-account "Manage Filters" (M3UFiltersModal):
   M3UFiltersModal's M3UFilter type (types/index.ts:321) is scoped to
   `m3u_account` only — no channel_group field — and operates at M3U
   parse/import time (decides which streams Dispatcharr imports AT ALL,
   account-wide). The auto-sync field is GROUP-scoped and operates at
   Dispatcharr's auto_channel_sync time (decides which of one group's
   already-imported streams get promoted to channels). If an account has
   multiple auto-sync-enabled groups, an account-level name filter cannot
   isolate one group without side-effecting the others. Different scope,
   different pipeline stage, different capability shape (single include
   pattern vs. ordered list of include/exclude filters).

EXISTING-STORED-VALUES DISPOSITION (live check, read-only, Playwright MCP
against localhost:6100, Infinity account, 'USA | Flo Racing' group — the
system's one currently-configured live auto-sync group):
  - Channel Profile Assignment: "LiveTV" — LIVE NON-DEFAULT VALUE
  - Stream Profile Assignment: "Proxy" — LIVE NON-DEFAULT VALUE
  - Channel Name Filter (Regex): empty — at default in this group
  - (for context) Force EPG Source: None: Override Channel Group: "Flo
    Racing Live" (self-referential/no-op); Channel Sort Order: "Name";
    Custom Logo: None.
Modal was opened read-only and closed via Cancel — nothing saved, nothing
mutated. Two of the three fields slated for deletion carry real operator
configuration RIGHT NOW. Per the #678 clobber-fix architecture
(merge_group_settings_row / handleSave spreads ...customProperties before
overlaying managed keys), simply deleting the JSX sections without touching
handleSave's per-field if/delete lines would likely leave the raw values
technically alive in custom_properties (passed through like any
Dispatcharr-added unknown key) but with ZERO UI to see, edit, or discover
them — exactly the "invisible config" worst-case the PO decision warned
against, and it would land squarely on this account's real Flo Racing
config on day one.

RECOMMENDATION: the mapping in the original bead description (UX audit)
appears to have been driven by name/word similarity ("profile", "filter")
rather than actual entity/scope identity. Recommend the PO revisit scope:
either (a) keep the 3 fields and instead add cross-reference language/
tooltips pointing at the dedicated screens for the DIFFERENT things they
manage, or (b) if consolidation is still wanted, it requires building the
group-scoped capability into the dedicated screens first (a larger feature,
not a deletion) rather than dropping the only place these settings can be
configured.

Tooltip fix (bead's small/independent item) NOT done — held pending PO
scope decision since it ships in the same PR path as the deletion work per
the original task framing; trivial to do separately once scope is
confirmed. Location for future reference:
frontend/src/components/M3UGroupsModal.tsx lines 456-473 (title/aria-label
ternary) — currently "Enable auto-sync to configure settings" for the
disabled case, doesn't mention the Enabled prerequisite.

No branch created, no commits, no PR. Bead status/priority left unchanged.
PO RESCOPE (2026-07-17, after STOP-tripwire findings): drop-the-fields is OFF — all 3 fields verified functionally unique, 2 carry live config (LiveTV / Proxy on USA | Flo Racing). New scope: disambiguation-in-place — retitle/cross-reference the 3 modal sections so they cannot be mistaken for the similarly-named screens (account profiles / stream-profile catalog / account filters), plus the disabled-gear tooltip fix (M3UGroupsModal.tsx:456-473 — name BOTH prerequisites: Enabled + Auto-Sync). No field removal, no behavior change. Auto-Sync Rules list view remains deferred.
IMPLEMENTATION (2026-07-17) — disambiguation-in-place, per PO rescope note.

Changes (branch fix/09x38.8-autosync-disambiguation, build 0123):

   for the 3 collision-prone sections (titles unchanged, no field/behavior

Tests: 4 new AutoSyncSettingsModal tests (titles unchanged + each section's

title: Manage Groups modal discards unsaved toggles on X-close/Escape with no dirty-guard prompt
description: CONFIRMED live 2026-07-17 (UX pass-1 re-check, real UI clicks, backend v0.17.6-0110-era container). When one or more group Enabled/Auto-Sync toggles have been changed in M3U Manager → Manage Groups, dirty state IS tracked (it enables the 'Save & Refresh' button), yet closing via the X button OR the Escape key discards all pending changes instantly with zero confirmation. The modal has no Cancel button — only X and 'Save & Refresh'. Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status) + #5 (error prevention). Stakes raised by #678: 'Save & Refresh' is now a real multi-field write, so operators plausibly batch many toggles before saving; one stray Escape/X wipes the batch invisibly. Outside-click path untested but likely same code path — cover it in the fix. Repro evidence: ux09x38-p1recheck-01..06.png at repo root (untracked scratch — do not commit).
acceptance_criteria: Closing Manage Groups (X, Escape, and outside-click if applicable) with unsaved toggle changes prompts 'Discard unsaved changes?' before discarding; clean close with no dirty state remains instant; no change to Save & Refresh behavior.

title: EPG Manager: reconcile dual Dummy EPG sections — legacy is the SUPPORTED path, ECM Dummy EPG Profiles is dead
description: UX pass 1 Major (consolidation). Two adjacent sections with near-identical descriptions: 'Dummy EPG Sources' (legacy source_type=dummy) and 'ECM Dummy EPG Profiles'. Operator can't tell which to use. PO DECISION 2026-07-17: legacy source_type=dummy is a supported thing; the enhanced 'ECM Dummy EPG Profiles' path is DEAD — the opposite of the pass-1 assumption. Scope: deprecate/fold away the ECM Dummy EPG Profiles section, keep legacy. CAUTION: live instance has real data under the dead path ('B1G Advanced EPG' profile) and 0 entries under legacy — needs a migration/disposition plan for existing profiles, and reconciliation against docs/template_engine.md (which documents the dead path's engine).
notes:
PO DECISION (2026-07-17): MIGRATE. Convert existing ECM Dummy EPG Profiles (incl. live 'B1G Advanced EPG') to legacy source_type=dummy sources — engineer must first verify functional feasibility of the conversion; then remove the ECM Dummy EPG Profiles section and deprecate docs/template_engine.md accordingly. If migration proves infeasible, STOP and report back before any removal — do not fall back to hard-kill without PO sign-off.
PHASE 1 FINDINGS (2026-07-17, project-engineer) — TRIPWIRE FIRED: STOP, no code changed.

VERDICT: MIGRATE is NOT feasible as a config-migration + section-removal. The named Event Sync dependency is real, live, and deep. Per bead tripwire + PO note, stopping before any removal; awaiting PO decision.

WHY (blast radius — ECM Dummy EPG Profiles engine is load-bearing for Event Sync):
- channel_pipeline_schema.py (~L796,L1315-1339): event_sync config carries dummy_epg_profile_id, validated against the DummyEPGProfile table.
- channel_pipeline_engine.py (_assign_event_sync_dummy_epg L3683+, _refresh_dummy_epg_and_retry L3917+): resolves DummyEPGProfile rows, AUTO-ADDS the event master group to the profile's channel_group_ids, regenerates /api/dummy-epg/xmltv/<profile_id>, refreshes the Dispatcharr source, retries assignment. Shipped feature ti939.3.3.
- channel_pipeline_executor.py (assign_event_sync_dummy_epg L3861+): assigns event channels to the Dispatcharr EPG source whose URL is /api/dummy-epg/xmltv/<profile_id>.
- EventSyncRuleEditor.tsx: 'Dummy EPG profile (optional)' dropdown populated by getDummyEPGProfiles(); config field dummy_epg_profile_id (eventSync.ts L100).
- Tests: test_event_sync_dummy_epg.py, test_event_sync_config_schema.py, test_event_loop_responsiveness.py.
Removing the ECM Profiles engine breaks Event Sync guide-data auto-assignment. Migrating to a legacy source would require REWIRING Event Sync to reference legacy dummy sources by id and re-implementing the group-coverage auto-management + XMLTV regeneration — a redesign of a shipped feature, not a migration.

FEASIBILITY OF OUTPUT EQUIVALENCE (separate axis): the two paths share the SAME template engine and an IDENTICAL field set. DummyEPGSourceModal (legacy source_type=dummy) writes title/time/date patterns + all templates + timezones/tags/lookups into custom_properties; DummyEPGProfile stores the same in the dummy_epg_profiles table. So per-event templated richness is expressible on BOTH sides. HOWEVER: ECM's XMLTV endpoints (/api/dummy-epg/xmltv, /xmltv/{id}, /generate) generate ONLY from the DummyEPGProfile table — there is NO ECM code path that renders XMLTV from a legacy dummy source's custom_properties (that generation is Dispatcharr-native). Not fully closed read-only; does not change the STOP.

LIVE STATE: 1 profile 'B1G Advanced EPG' (id=1, enabled, group 359). Parses sports stream names -> channel/sport/team1/team2 + event times; title_template '{channel} | {sport} | {team1} vs. {team2}'; program_duration 180m. This IS the event-sync guide-data use case. 0 legacy source_type=dummy sources exist on the instance (5 EPG sources are external: epg.guru x3, Teamarr, Schedules Direct). 1 pipeline rule 'Test Sync' (id=1, enabled).

FULL SURFACE OF THE ECM-PROFILES PATH:
- DB: models.py DummyEPGProfile (dummy_epg_profiles) + DummyEPGChannelAssignment (dummy_epg_channel_assignments); alembic baseline.
- Backend engine: dummy_epg_engine.py, dummy_epg.py router (CRUD /profiles, /preview, /preview/batch, /xmltv, /xmltv/{id}, /generate, /profiles/export|import/yaml, /lint-findings), template_engine.py (shared with legacy path).
- Task: tasks/dummy_epg_refresh.py (task_id dummy_epg_refresh).
- MCP: mcp-server/tools/epg.py (list/create/get/update/delete_dummy_epg_profile, generate_dummy_epg, preview_dummy_epg).
- Backup/DBAS: routers/backup.py exports+restores dummy_epg_profiles section (L1777, L2054, _restore_dummy_epg_profiles L2604).
- Frontend: EPGManagerTab.tsx (mounts <DummyEPGManagerSection> at L1228), DummyEPGManagerSection.tsx, DummyEPGProfileModal.tsx/.css, ImportDummyEPGModal.tsx, PatternBuilder.tsx, BackupRestoreModal.tsx, api.ts, types/index.ts.

OPTIONS FOR PO:
A) Keep both, just DISAMBIGUATE (rename/relabel + docs) — cheapest, no removal, resolves the operator-confusion root cause without touching Event Sync.
B) Reverse the PO ruling: ECM Profiles is the SUPPORTED path (it is the one Event Sync integrates with and the one the live B1G data lives in); deprecate/fold the LEGACY 'Dummy EPG Sources' section instead. Inverts the bead premise.
C) Full migration INCLUDING an Event Sync rewire (reference legacy sources by id, re-implement group auto-coverage + regeneration) — Large/Epic, redesigns a shipped ti939 feature; needs its own decomposition + QA.
Recommend A or B. Not proceeding to Phase 2.
PO DECISION #2 (2026-07-17, supersedes MIGRATE): Option B — REVERSE the original ruling. ECM Dummy EPG Profiles is the SUPPORTED path (Event Sync dependency, live B1G profile, shared template engine); the legacy 'Dummy EPG Sources' section (source_type=dummy, zero live usage, no ECM-side XMLTV generation) is the one to deprecate/fold away. Scope care: this ships fleet-wide — other deployments MAY have legacy dummy sources; grandfather any existing ones (render + manage, deprecation notice) and stop offering new-creation; zero data deletion anywhere. Retitle/clarify the ECM section as the one Dummy EPG feature. docs/template_engine.md stays authoritative (drop the planned deprecation); user_guide EPG pages updated accordingly.

title: Full-pass verify: ECM auto-sync group setup vs Dispatcharr-native (newer Dispatcharr changed auto-sync UI; field report: ECM setup doesn't take)
description: PO request 2026-07-16. Field report: setting up auto-sync for groups in ECM does not set it up properly in Dispatcharr; newer Dispatcharr versions changed the auto-sync groups UI (and possibly the API shape underneath). Task: full-pass test both directions — (1) configure group auto-sync via ECM (API/MCP + UI path) and verify the resulting state inside Dispatcharr (API + UI); (2) configure the same natively in Dispatcharr and diff the two states; (3) map ECM's write path (group settings -> Dispatcharr client) against the current Dispatcharr API schema to find renamed/moved/ignored fields. Record ECM + Dispatcharr versions in the dev environment; if our Dispatcharr predates the UI change, flag the version gap explicitly rather than declaring no-repro.
notes: FULL-PASS COMPLETE 2026-07-16 (qa-engineer, live vs Dispatcharr v0.27.2 = latest; NOT version-gated). Simple repro FAILED: plain ECM toggle DOES land and displays checked in the new Dispatcharr UI. Field report explained by 3 adjacent real defects: (1) CLOBBER — Dispatcharr update_group_settings (api_views.py:495-585) is a FULL-ROW UPSERT with defaults for omitted fields; ECM's partial payloads reset them. Proven live: enabled-only write silently wiped auto_channel_sync true->false and start 1.0->null. ECM never sends auto_sync_channel_end (new v0.25.0) — M3UGroupsModal.tsx:218-234, routers/m3u.py:1230-1236 — so any ECM group save erases natively-configured end ranges; AutoSyncSettingsModal.tsx:279-293 rebuilds custom_properties from {} losing post-v0.24 keys (channel_numbering_mode etc.). (2) MCP group tools 100% broken: mcp-server/tools/m3u.py:375-412 resolves names via a channel_groups[].name field the serializer stopped providing (v0.24.0+) — every call returns 'group not found'. (3) Expectation gap: native Dispatcharr save = Save-and-Refresh (channels appear immediately); ECM save never refreshes -> looks inert until next scheduled refresh. Fix scope MEDIUM: read-modify-write full field set in all 4 writers + MCP name resolution via /api/channels/groups/ join + 'takes effect on next refresh' UI copy + recorded v0.27.2 fixture regression test. Side finding: routers/m3u.py:1117-1118 masks Dispatcharr 400 bodies as generic 500s. Both systems verified restored to snapshot; no refresh triggered; evidence screenshots sync478fe-*.png + JSONs in scratchpad.

title: Event sync review fingerprint includes event date — recurring daily events need re-accept every day
description:
Found in jqwfq spike: master_event_key (services/event_sync_review.py ~L157-174) includes the full UTC start timestamp, so a recurring same-name daily event produces a different fingerprint each day and an operator ACCEPT does not carry forward — daily review churn. Honest behavior (same-name-across-days is the undecidable case) but heavy operator cost once the jqwfq stale-dateless demote rail lands. Related: jqwfq, ti939.3.

SHIPPED (v0.17.6-0132, PR feat/event-sync-phase2-closeout): PO-approved design option (b) — drop the date from the fingerprint ONLY when the parser SYNTHESIZED it (the three assume_current_date dateless patterns, tracked via new SYNTHESIZED_DATE_PATTERN_NAMES constant in event_sync_matcher.py). Such parses key on <cleaned title>|dateless|<local clock HH:MM><STANDARD tz offset> (utcoffset - dst, so keys survive DST transitions). Dated parses byte-identical to prior keys — no migration; pre-upgrade dateless accepts re-ask once. Accepts/rejects on recurring dateless slots now carry forward across midnight; jqwfq rail no longer re-demotes daily. 15 new tests in tests/services/test_event_sync_review.py incl. DB-backed day-boundary accept/reject carry-forward with already_answered exercised.

title: M3U change digest is blind to pure renames (stream diffs only computed on group count change)

A pure rename (old event name out, new event name in, count stable — exactly how PPV slot providers behave) records nothing in M3UChangeLog. Affects change-log fidelity and anything downstream that assumes renames are visible. Related: jqwfq.

title: Event sync: stale dateless stream matches today's master at 1.0 under assume_current_date
description: User report (Zedan, GH bundle 20260716 follow-up): a secondary stream still carrying YESTERDAY's event name matched today's master perfectly. Mechanism: rule has assume_current_date=true; provider left yesterday's dateless slot name in the M3U; parse synthesizes TODAY's date at the same clock time so dt is small and the title is identical, score 1.0, attach. Undecidable from the name alone. Investigate freshness signals: Dispatcharr stream last_seen/updated_at metadata, ECM m3u_change_monitor change history (when did this stream name last change), or provider-day heuristics. Possible shapes: (a) only assume current date for streams whose name changed since the last provider day; (b) demote assume_current_date matches to review when the stream name predates the current M3U refresh day; (c) operator-facing staleness warning in preview. Needs design before code. Related: yjchp (venue rail batch), dvgri.
notes:
DESIGN SPIKE COMPLETE. Key facts: (1) Dispatcharr per-stream timestamps are USELESS for this — live survey of 2500 streams shows updated_at and last_seen bumped for every stream on every M3U refresh (refresh-liveness, not name-freshness); is_stale is the inverse signal; no created_at exposed. (2) M3UChangeLog diffs CANNOT answer it — stream-name diffs only computed when a group's stream COUNT changes, pure renames record nothing (backlog candidate: digest rename blindness). (3) M3USnapshot.groups_data CAN answer it cheaply — full per-group stream-name lists captured ~2x daily, 90-day retention; question becomes 'was this exact name present in a snapshot before local midnight today (America/New_York, same anchor parse_event_name uses)'. Binding constraint: MAX_STREAM_NAMES=500 per group and enabled-groups-only — absence is inconclusive so the rail must FAIL OPEN (positive membership definitive, cap can only cause missed detections never false demotes). RECOMMENDED: design (b), staged, size MEDIUM — Stage 1 compute+surface staleness signal (observability, validate heuristic live), Stage 2 demote stale-dateless attach-band matches to AMBIGUOUS review queue with new reason stale_dateless_stream_name, mirroring the venue-conflict rail precedent; operator review-queue ACCEPT outranks the heuristic (accept-upgrade path already exists). Gate demote on the counterfactual 'assume_current_date was load-bearing' re-parse so dated streams are never touched. Per-rule knob demote_stale_dateless default TRUE as recurring-event escape hatch. Designs (a) hard-block and (c) age knob rejected (silent false negatives / no age signal exists); (d) observability-only rejected as endpoint but shipped as Stage 1. WART flagged: master_event_key includes full UTC start so recurring daily events need a review accept EVERY day (date-agnostic fingerprint = separate risky follow-up). Full touch points, backward compat (validate_event_sync_config default-fill pattern), and test plan incl. real 500-cap fixture in spike report. Backlog candidates: digest rename blindness; date-in-fingerprint daily re-accept churn; preflight warning when change monitor disabled (staleness rail silently inert).

ENGINEER START (worktree agent-abd63876b4497e4d3, branch fix/jqwfq-stale-dateless-guard from origin/dev @1ce1b381): implementing staged design (b) per spike. Stage 1 observability (staleness signal via M3USnapshot membership, surfaced in preview/debug-bundle), Stage 2 demote rail (AMBIGUOUS_REASON_STALE_DATELESS_NAME, knob demote_stale_dateless default true).

IMPLEMENTATION + LIVE VALIDATION (engineer, worktree branch fix/jqwfq-stale-dateless-guard): Both stages implemented. Stage 1: services/event_sync_staleness.py (previous_day_names + name_seen_before_today tri-state, fail-open incl. 500-cap detection); SecondaryStream.name_seen_before_today; router+engine compute lookup via run_in_threadpool; preview/debug-bundle expose per-row flag + stale_suspect_streams/freshness_unknown_streams counts. title: Investigate user debug bundle: merge-into-existing skips 'ESPN' as not found, merge+create makes duplicate
description: External user's debug bundle: auto-creation merge reported "Channel 'ESPN' not found, skipped (merge only)" though the channel exists; merge (create-if-new) created a duplicate ESPN. ROOT CAUSE: every ActionExecutor lookup index holds ONE channel per name key, so with the same name in several groups (supported GH-92 layout — the bundle had five channels named 'ESPN' in five groups) a group-scoped lookup could only test one arbitrary survivor; when it sat in another group the lookup returned 'not found'. FIX (PR #670, build 0103): multi-candidate companion indices; each _find_channel_by_name stage keeps its legacy single-slot pick (unchanged winner semantics when it passes scope/manual gates) and scans all same-key candidates when it fails. Manual-channel gate + wy6l5 breadcrumb apply to scanned candidates; rename/create/dry-run keep indices in sync. 12 regression tests in test_g0uuf_duplicate_name_scoped_lookup.py. Follow-up noted: debug bundle channels.json omits auto_created, so manual-vs-auto is not diagnosable from a bundle.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (reproduced in unit repro): ActionExecutor lookup indices are single-candidate dicts keyed by lowercase name (_channel_by_name last-seen-wins, fallback maps setdefault first-seen-wins). User bundle has FIVE channels literally named 'ESPN' in five groups (ids 166902, 218340, 218758, 236818, 248009). Dispatcharr load order leaves id 248009 (group US SPORTS) as the only 'espn' index entry. The ESPN rule's create_channel lookup is scoped to group 5210 (GH-92 match_scope_target_group) → _in_scope rejects the sole candidate and NEVER considers the in-scope ESPN 236818 → returns None. merge_only → 'not found, skipped (merge only)'; merge → creates duplicate ESPN in group 5210. Repro: _find_channel_by_name('ESPN', scope_group_id=5210) returns None with 236818 present. Normalization fallbacks can't save it because normalize('ESPN')=='ESPN' (norm_lower==name_lower short-circuits). Fix direction: name→list-of-candidates indices (or scope-aware scan fallback) at channel_pipeline_executor.py:255 + _find_channel_by_name. Secondary suspect ruled less likely but worth surfacing in UX: manual-channel gate (orzck) produces identical symptom; bundle can't distinguish (channels.json omits auto_created — diagnosability gap worth fixing in bundle export).

title: Evaluate and fix uvloop 0.22.1 risk — switch event loop or upgrade
description: Follow-up from P1 crash investigation (enhancedchannelmanager-xzdx9 / GH #546). uvloop 0.22.1 has open upstream issues: segfault in FastAPI-in-container (uvloop #706) and responses leaking to the wrong request under load (uvloop #645 — data-exposure risk). PO approved fixing overall, not just evaluating. Candidate fixes: run uvicorn with --loop asyncio, or upgrade uvloop if a fixed release exists. Must include: load-test comparison to quantify any throughput cost of asyncio loop, verification that response-leak scenario is covered, and confirmation the P1 containment middleware still behaves identically on the chosen loop.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED (container-first, not committed):

FACTS: uvicorn was launched with no --loop flag at all 3 launch points (backend/entrypoint.sh production path, tls/https_server.py HTTPS subprocess, main.py __main__ dev run) -> uvicorn 'auto' policy selected uvloop 0.22.1 (installed via uvicorn[standard] extra in requirements.in). UPSTREAM STATUS (checked 2026-07-16 via gh api): latest uvloop release is STILL 0.22.1 (2025-10-16) — no fixed release exists. #706 (segfault, FastAPI-in-container) OPEN. #645 (response leaked to WRONG request under load — data exposure; multiple independent production reports incl. fd-reuse RuntimeErrors) closed 2026-05-01 via PR #740 merged to master but UNRELEASED. Upgrade path therefore unavailable.

DECISION: pin stdlib asyncio loop everywhere (--loop asyncio / loop=), with ECM_UVICORN_LOOP env escape hatch (whitelisted to auto|asyncio|uvloop; invalid values fall back to asyncio with a warning — value lands in subprocess argv). Rationale: eliminates the uvloop-only data-exposure + segfault class entirely; measured throughput cost is ZERO at ECM's scale (see numbers).

FILES: backend/entrypoint.sh (--loop ${ECM_UVICORN_LOOP:-asyncio} + rationale comment); backend/tls/https_server.py (resolve_loop_choice() + --loop in _get_uvicorn_command); backend/main.py (startup log of active loop implementation for auditability from docker logs; __main__ dev run passes loop=resolve_loop_choice()); NEW backend/tests/unit/test_event_loop_selection.py (8 tests: resolver whitelist/default/override, HTTPS subprocess cmd pins loop, text guards on entrypoint.sh + main.py __main__).

VERIFIED LIVE in ecm-ecm-1 (host-network, port 6100): loop proof via new startup log — 'Event loop implementation: asyncio.unix_events._UnixSelectorEventLoop' on BOTH HTTP main process (cmdline shows --loop asyncio) and HTTPS subprocess (6143); uvloop baseline phase logged 'uvloop.Loop'. P1 CONTAINMENT (GH #546) re-proven on BOTH loops with temp /api/wadu3-boom probe raising SystemExit: 3x 500 + [EXIT-DIAG] BaseException-contained log each time, process alive, health 200 after (probe removed from container afterwards). AUTH: valid cookie 200 / invalid 401 / missing 401 / MCP key 200.

LOAD TEST (60-way concurrent cookie-auth bursts, 600 req/round x 3 rounds x 2 runs per config, mixed endpoints auto-creation/rules + normalization/rules + executions + health, per-response shape-integrity check in the spirit of uvloop#645): uvloop mean 215.8 & 243.1 rps, p50 218/200ms, p95 673/474ms; asyncio mean 230.7 & 220.6 rps, p50 203/224ms, p95 551/632ms. Delta ~1.7% within run-to-run noise (uvloop itself varied 12% run-to-run) -> NO measurable throughput cost; handlers/SQLite dominate, not the loop. 0 errors, 0 shape mismatches in 7,200 measured requests.

GATES: full backend suite 7053 passed / 4 documented skips (venv interpreter) on dev@96d24cbd + change; py_compile clean; sh -n entrypoint.sh clean. NOTE: mid-task the GH#645 fold_match_key merge (PR #666) landed on origin/dev; container DB was already at migration 0034 from that branch's verification overlay, which made pre-merge dev code 500 on rule create (NOT NULL fold_match_key) — resolved by fast-forwarding local dev to 96d24cbd and redeploying; event_sync e2e 6/6 green after. Unrelated to loop change.

SHIP RECOMMENDATION: ship. Data-exposure class eliminated, zero measured cost, single env var rolls back to uvloop without rebuild.
REVIEW ROUND 1 (REQUEST CHANGES) ADDRESSED:

BLOCKER 1 (unquoted --loop expansion, argv injection via field-splitting): entrypoint.sh now uses --loop "${ECM_UVICORN_LOOP}" (quoted).
BLOCKER 2 (no whitelist on production path + asymmetric failure vs HTTPS subprocess): entrypoint.sh now has a case-block whitelist mirroring resolve_loop_choice() — auto|asyncio|uvloop pass through; anything else (incl. empty) falls back to asyncio, non-empty invalid values emit a print_warning. Fails CLOSED instead of crash-looping (uvicorn click.Choice rejection + set -e + exec would have restart-looped the container).

LOCKSTEP: tests upgraded from text-regex to BEHAVIORAL — test_event_loop_selection.py now executes the real launch tail of entrypoint.sh (defaults + case whitelist + exec line) in a POSIX shell with the exec swapped for an argv dumper, asserting the exact word-split argv uvicorn receives: default->asyncio, uvloop/auto overrides honored, notaloop->asyncio+warning, crafted 'asyncio --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=*'->asyncio+warning with NO extra flags in argv; plus a text assertion the expansion stays quoted. 13 tests in file. Docs: docs/runbooks/request-timeout.md env-var table gained ECM_UVICORN_LOOP row (whitelist, asyncio default, uvloop #645/#706 rationale, env-var rollback); docs/runbooks/dep-bump-backend-asgi-regression.md 'exact uvicorn invocation' line updated to include --loop.

VERIFIED LIVE in ecm-ecm-1 with the fixed entrypoint deployed: (a) normal restart boots on asyncio — cmdline '--loop asyncio', startup log 'Event loop implementation: asyncio.unix_events._UnixSelectorEventLoop' on HTTP + HTTPS subprocess, health 200; (b) fail-closed proven via docker exec running the DEPLOYED /app/entrypoint.sh launch logic in the container's own shell with ECM_UVICORN_LOOP=notaloop -> WARN + argv '--loop asyncio' (uvicorn never sees the invalid value); (c) injection attempt 'asyncio --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=*' -> WARN + '--loop asyncio', no injected flags in argv; (d) ECM_UVICORN_LOOP=uvloop -> '--loop uvloop' (escape hatch intact).

GATES: sh -n clean; test_event_loop_selection 13 passed; containment + tls suites 38 passed combined. Files now in working tree: backend/entrypoint.sh, backend/main.py, backend/tls/https_server.py, backend/tests/unit/test_event_loop_selection.py (new), docs/runbooks/request-timeout.md, docs/runbooks/dep-bump-backend-asgi-regression.md. Non-blocking reviewer items (quoting sibling ECM_PORT/CONCURRENCY/KEEP_ALIVE expansions, style-guide shell-quoting section) deliberately NOT done per coordinator — backlog candidates.

title: Sort by name in AutoCreation
description:
Imported from GitHub issue #644: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/644

### ECM Version

v0.17.5

### Priority

Priority 3: Medium, needs looking at soon but not immediate

### What is the bug?

hi,

After all channels are created (using the two pipelines, one for the US and one for PL), is it possible to automatically sort the channels by name after the first pipeline finishes (for us or pl)?

Right now for PL number starts from 1 for US 400.
For PL I would like to sort it via name same for US


### Steps to Reproduce

version: 1
exported_at: '2026-07-13T18:07:27.713038Z'
rules:
- name: all
  description: null
  enabled: true
  priority: 0
  m3u_account_id: null
  m3u_account_name: null
  target_group_id: null
  target_group_name: null
  conditions:
  - type: always
    connector: and
  actions:
  - type: create_channel
    if_exists: merge
    name_template: '{stream_name}'
    group_id: 1
    group_name: Default Group
  - type: assign_epg
    epg_id: 1
  - type: assign_logo
    value: from_epg
    epg_id: 1
  run_on_refresh: true
  stop_on_first_match: true
  sort_field: stream_name
  sort_order: asc
  sort_regex: ''
  stream_sort_field: smart_sort
  stream_sort_order: asc
  normalize_names: true
  skip_struck_streams: false
  probe_on_sort: false
  orphan_action: delete

_No response_
notes:
QA triage (2026-07-15): Already supported, undiscoverable. sort_group pipeline action (channel_pipeline_schema.py:248, Pass 3.6 _sort_channel_groups) does exactly what reporter wants. Root cause of confusion: sort_field controls stream processing order, not numbering; with channel_number:auto the rule-level renumber pass is silently skipped (_get_rule_starting_number returns None → continue at channel_pipeline_engine.py:2537,4318). Nothing documented. PO DECISION: docs fix (sort_field vs sort_group + auto-numbering gotcha in docs/user_guide/channel-pipeline/) PLUS UI hint in rule builder when sort_field set with channel_number:auto. Also add regression test asserting the skip behavior. Reporter's immediate answer: add sort_group action per group with starting_number 1 (PL) / 400 (US). Size: Small + Small.
Engineer (2026-07-16): Implemented docs + UI hint scope.

Docs: new docs/user_guide/channel-pipeline/sort-vs-numbering.md covering
sort_field (stream processing order) vs sort_group (post-run alphabetical
sort+renumber), the channel_number:auto gotcha (rule-level renumber pass
silently skipped), and a worked example matching the reporter's PL(1)/US(400)
case. Wired into docs/user_guide/channel-pipeline/index.md (Planned articles
table + Going deeper section).

UI hint: frontend/src/components/channelPipeline/RuleBuilder.tsx — Channel
Sort field in Output & Run phase now shows an informational hint (reuses the
existing .norm-hint pattern) when a create_channel action's Channel Number is
Auto/unset AND a Channel Sort is selected. New isAutoChannelNumber() helper
mirrors backend _get_rule_starting_number semantics (undefined or literal
"auto" = auto; numeric or "N-M" range = not auto).

Tests: 6 new unit tests in RuleBuilder.test.tsx (sort/numbering hint describe
block) covering show/hide across auto-unset, literal "auto", fixed range, no
sort_field, and no create_channel action cases. Full frontend gates green:

title: BUG/FR -> handle  duplicate channel (same channels but with space/big/small letters) in AutoCreation
description:
Imported from GitHub issue #645: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/645

### ECM Version

v0.17.5

### Priority

Priority 3: Medium, needs looking at soon but not immediate

### What is the bug?

Hi, right now I have six providers. 😉

Because there are so many channels, I'm running into issues with duplicate channel creation. For example, I have channels named "eurosport 2", "Eurosport 2", "Eurosport2", and "eurosport2". The system creates four separate channels instead of recognizing them as the same one. Is there a way to automatically merge or normalize these channel names during creation to prevent duplicates? ofc there are much more examples like this so I'm looking on general solution 😉 with one provider I can manage manually but with more is just to much time consuming ;)

### Steps to Reproduce

version: 1
exported_at: '2026-07-13T18:07:27.713038Z'
rules:
- name: all
  description: null
  enabled: true
  priority: 0
  m3u_account_id: null
  m3u_account_name: null
  target_group_id: null
  target_group_name: null
  conditions:
  - type: always
    connector: and
  actions:
  - type: create_channel
    if_exists: merge
    name_template: '{stream_name}'
    group_id: 1
    group_name: Default Group
  - type: assign_epg
    epg_id: 1
  - type: assign_logo
    value: from_epg
    epg_id: 1
  run_on_refresh: true
  stop_on_first_match: true
  sort_field: stream_name
  sort_order: asc
  sort_regex: ''
  stream_sort_field: smart_sort
  stream_sort_order: asc
  normalize_names: true
  skip_struck_streams: false
  probe_on_sort: false
  orphan_action: delete


### Screenshots / Logs / Artifacts

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_
notes:

Case-insensitive merge already works (test_find_channel_by_name_case_insensitive); gap is whitespace-only variants. normalize_names only runs user-authored rules; no built-in whitespace collapse on merge-lookup path (channel_pipeline_executor.py:3966 _find_channel_by_name lowercases only). Same gap in find_duplicate_channels (routers/channels.py:2787). PO DECISION: implement as OPT-IN rule flag — new per-rule toggle that folds case + collapses whitespace on the if_exists merge comparison key only (never the stored/visible name). Mirror in Find Duplicates for parity where the flag is on. Size: Medium. Engineer must first reproduce with a scoped dry run — reporter's example implies case-only pairs also failed, contradicting passing test; read [AUTO-CREATE-EXEC] lookup trace before fixing.
Engineer findings (GH #645 fold_match_key implementation, worktree wt-gh645-dedup):

EVIDENCE GAP RESOLVED (repro via unit-level probes feeding the exact 4 reported strings through create/merge in 6 topologies): case-only merging WORKS in every topology (single run, second run, dry-run, with/without normalization engine) — the passing test at test_channel_pipeline_executor.py:271 is telling the truth. The whitespace pair ('Eurosport 2' vs 'Eurosport2') never merges — confirmed root gap. The reporter's 4 distinct spellings therefore require a cross-run divergence on top of the whitespace gap; the two documented paths that reproduce it are (a) manual-channel gate: existing channels whose auto_created flag is falsy are treated as not-found (orzck W1 design) so each run re-creates, and stream-order changes across runs produce different first-seen spellings; (b) per-rule group scoping (match_scope_target_group default True) when spellings land under rules/groups that differ. No second in-executor bug found; no fix needed beyond the approved flag.

title: Bug: _consolidate_operations drops only the create when deleteChannel precedes createChannel for same temp id (dangling delete)
description: Surfaced by u8qr6.7 reverse-order test. routers/channels.py _consolidate_operations (~L1081-1091): the create+delete-of-same-temp-channel cancellation is ORDER-DEPENDENT. Forward order (create before delete) cancels both. REVERSE order (deleteChannel before createChannel for the same negative temp id) appends the deleteChannel to ordered_ops BEFORE temp_ids_created is populated (create processed later in the same loop), so only the create is dropped and a dangling deleteChannel(<neg temp id>) survives — it targets a channel that was never created and would ERROR at execution. The module docstring states the contract order-INDEPENDENTLY ('Create + delete of same temp channel cancel out'). FIX: first pass to compute a channels_to_create set (symmetric to channels_to_delete), then cancel in either order. A reverse-order test exists as xfail(strict=True) on branch feat/u8qr6-assertions-coverage — remove the xfail when fixed (it will flip to a real pass).

title: Host provisioning: local python cryptography 41.0.7 lags the repo pin (49.0.0)
description:
Discovered during u8qr6.1 (CertificateStorage tests). The dev host's system python has cryptography 41.0.7, but the repo/container/CI pin is 49.0.0 (backend/requirements.txt). Production tls/storage.py::parse_certificate uses cert.not_valid_before_utc, which requires cryptography >=42 — so on the stale local interpreter that method FAILS for any real cert, and any local gate run of TLS/cert-touching tests false-fails. CI is unaffected (uses the pin). ACTION: bring the local interpreter in line with the pin (or standardize on a venv from backend/requirements.txt for local gates) so local verification matches CI. Interim: gate crypto-touching tests in a venv with cryptography==49.0.0. Note: prior local gate runs for non-crypto work (EPG matcher, scheduler) were unaffected since they don't touch not_valid_before_utc.

=== RESOLVED 2026-07-14 ===: system python is Debian externally-managed (PEP 668) — pip install (even --user) refuses, and --break-system-packages would risk the OS python, so it was NOT modified. Instead built a canonical pin-aligned virtualenv at repo ./.venv (gitignored) from backend/requirements.txt: cryptography 49.0.0, pytest 9.0.3 — matches CI exactly. Local gates should run via ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest. TLS tests verified green in it. (If bare 'python3 -m pytest' must work, that requires --break-system-packages with OS risk — deferred to operator.)

title: MCP surface: list_tasks must show effective_enabled (not just parent enabled)
description:
GAP found post-merge (build 0091): vkktd surfaced effective_enabled on GET /api/tasks + the debug bundle + (deferred) frontend, but NOT on the MCP surface. mcp-server/tools/tasks.py:31 list_tasks still formats 'enabled' from t.get('enabled') (the PARENT gate) and ignores effective_enabled — which the API now returns in each task dict. So an AI agent calling list_tasks over MCP sees 'auto_creation — enabled' even when it's gated off and will never fire: the exact 'reads Enabled but won't run' trap vkktd exists to eliminate, still live on the agent-facing surface (arguably the MOST important one, since the field report was diagnosed via agent tooling).

FIX: list_tasks should surface effective_enabled — e.g. show 'enabled' only when effective_enabled is true, and an explicit 'enabled but WON'T RUN (no active schedule)' when enabled && !effective_enabled (mirror the frontend wontRun signal from vkktd.4). Also confirm the debug-bundle MCP tools (get_auto_creation_debug_bundle / get_channel_pipeline_debug_bundle) pass through the new effective_enabled fields. Sibling to vkktd.4 (frontend) — both surface the same field.

PROCESS NOTE: engineer brief scoped REST API + frontend and did not check the MCP surface; add 'MCP surface' to the ship checklist for backend changes that alter task/entity status shape.

title: m3u_digest tests exercise a hand-copied reimplementation, not the real execute() path
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091). The M3U digest exclude-filter + adversarial safe_regex tests run against a hand-copied mirror of the filter block, NOT the production M3UDigestTask.execute() code path, so production divergence would go uncaught (the 'guard' only substring-checks source). Refactor the production filter into a testable unit and point the tests at it:
  - [medium] backend/tests/unit/test_m3u_digest_exclude.py:129 (TestExcludeFilterLogic._apply_exclude_filters (and all its callers, e.g. test_group_exclude_drops_matching_group, test_stream_exclude_partial_keeps_remaining, etc.)) — The exclude-pattern filtering tests run against a hand-copied reimplementation of the filter block, not the real production code inside M3UDigestTask.execute().
  - [medium] backend/tests/unit/test_m3u_digest_safe_regex.py:33 (TestAdversarialPatterns (all methods)) — The adversarial safe_regex fallback tests (ReDoS, oversize pattern, invalid pattern) run against `_apply_exclude_filters`, a hand-copied mirror of the exclude-filter block in tasks/m3u_digest.py::execute(), not the real production function.
  - [low] backend/tests/unit/test_m3u_digest_exclude.py:306 (TestProductionFilterShape.test_production_filter_uses_safe_regex) — The 'guard' meant to catch divergence between the test's reimplemented filter and the real production filter only checks that the literal substrings 'safe_regex.compile' and 'safe_regex.search' appear somewhere in M3UDigestTask's source via inspect.getsource — it does not exercise the real filtering behavior at all.

title: Tighten weak/smoke test assertions that accept failure as a pass
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091). A cluster of tests assert loose status-code sets that admit a real regression as a PASS (e.g. accept 500 or validation-failure alongside success), or are smoke tests that only assert 200 without inspecting the body. Tighten each to assert the intended outcome (and body shape where relevant):
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_api_alert_methods.py:267 (TestTestAlertMethod.test_test_method_sends_test_message) — Test mocks create_method to always return a working test_connection() (True, "OK"), which deterministically produces a 200 — but the assertion accepts (200, 500), so a real regression that turns the success path into a 500 would still pass.
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_api_alert_methods.py:289 (TestTestAlertMethod.test_test_method_returns_result) — The only assertion on response content is wrapped in `if response.status_code == 200:` — under the given mocked setup the branch is always taken, but the test can silently assert nothing if a future change makes the status non-200, defeating the test's stated purpose ('returns test result').
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_api_settings.py:166 (test_restart_services_reinitializes) — Assertion accepts either success (200) or failure (500) as a passing result, so a real regression that makes /api/settings/restart-services always fail would not be caught.
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_api_stream_preview.py:266 (test_update_settings_accepts_valid_stream_preview_modes) — The test claims valid stream_preview_mode values 'should be accepted' but asserts status_code in (200, 400, 422) — a set that covers both success AND validation-failure responses.
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_normalize_channel_create.py:132 (test_create_channel_accepts_normalize_flag / test_create_channel_accepts_normalize_false) — Both single-channel-create tests assert `response.status_code in (200, 201, 500)`, so a 500 error (e.g. a broken normalize code path, an exception in the router) is treated as a PASS.
  - [medium] backend/tests/integration/test_normalize_channel_create.py:189 (test_bulk_commit_accepts_normalize_flag_on_create_channel) — Asserts `response.status_code in (202, 500)` — a 500 (e.g. an exception raised anywhere in the bulk-commit dispatch) passes the test just as a correct 202 would.
  - [low] backend/tests/e2e/test_channels.py:12 () — Every test in this e2e smoke file asserts only `status_code == 200`; there is no coverage of error/edge paths for the routes it touches (e.g. invalid `page`/`page_size` values, a channel-group id that doesn't exist, empty vs populated CSV template).
  - [low] backend/tests/e2e/test_health_settings.py:32 (test_cache_stats) — Test is named/documented as verifying GET /api/cache/stats "returns cache statistics" but only asserts status_code == 200; the response body/shape is never inspected.
  - [low] backend/tests/e2e/test_preview.py:21 (test_stream_preview_nonexistent / test_channel_preview_nonexistent) — Assertion accepts any of (400, 404, 500) for a nonexistent-ID preview request, so the test cannot distinguish a correct 404 from an accidental 500 crash path.
  - [low] backend/tests/integration/test_api_alert_methods.py:100 (TestCreateAlertMethod.test_create_discord_method) — No mocking of method registration state; assertion accepts (200, 201, 400), so the test cannot distinguish a working create-Discord-method flow from a broken one as long as the status code isn't something else entirely — it never verifies the created method's fields.
  - [low] backend/tests/integration/test_api_auth_setup.py:51 (test_protected_endpoints_indicate_setup_needed) — The core assertion `response.status_code in (200, 401, 403, 503)` accepts almost any outcome, so the test cannot fail on a real regression (e.g. a protected endpoint that returns 200 with no auth/setup gate at all still passes).

title: UX: task must not read 'Enabled' while parent gate is off / never fires
description:
UX: a task can read "Enabled" in the UI while its parent gate is off and never run (parent vkktd). task_registry.py:384-387 explicitly warns of this trap. The API GET /api/tasks returns the EFFECTIVE enabled (parent) — good — but confirm the UI surfaces THAT (not the child/schedule enabled), and that toggling "Enabled" flips the parent (verified working via the real-toggle test on ecm-ecm-1). 

INVESTIGATE + HARDEN:
- Confirm the task list/detail UI binds to the effective/parent enabled, so a user can never see "Enabled" on a task that won't fire.
- Consider surfacing "enabled but has never run / next_run in the past" as a warning state in the UI (the exact signature users hit).
- If any path lets the child schedule be enabled while the parent stays off without a visible indicator, close that gap.

ACCEPTANCE:
- With parent disabled, the UI does NOT present auto_creation as running/enabled-and-fine.
- Toggling Enabled in the UI sets the parent and the task begins firing on the next tick.
=== NEW EVIDENCE (real-toggle test on ecm-ecm-1, 2026-07-14) ===
CONFIRMED A SECOND, SHARPER BUG: the task-level "Enabled" toggle (PATCH /api/tasks/{id} -> instance.enable() -> _save_task_to_db, task_registry.py:214) sets ONLY the parent scheduled_tasks.enabled. It NEVER touches the child task_schedules.enabled (managed separately by the per-schedule endpoint, routers/tasks.py:889-890). enable()/disable() (task_scheduler.py:624/631) only flip _enabled (the parent).

CONSEQUENCE (reproduced): with child=0, PATCH enabled=True returned HTTP 200, set parent=1, and GET /api/tasks reported enabled=TRUE with next_run=NULL — yet the task did NOT fire over a full tick (firing needs BOTH; child=0 excludes it from the due query, task_engine.py:607). So the operator sees "Enabled", the toggle 'succeeds', and the task is structurally unable to run with ZERO feedback. (When BOTH were set =1 via the earlier repro, it fired immediately — proving the gates.)

The parent/child enabled states are independent and can silently diverge; nothing reconciles them or warns. next_run=NULL while enabled=True is a reliable 'will never fire' tell the UI/bundle should surface.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) task "Enabled" toggle should reconcile the child (enable the default child schedule when enabling the task), or (b) the UI must compute effective_enabled = parent AND (>=1 enabled child schedule) and never show a bare "Enabled", plus warn on enabled+next_run=null. Coordinate with vkktd.1 (log the child-disabled skip) and vkktd.2 (bundle effective-enabled).
=== UX DESIGN PASS (ux-designer, 2026-07-14) — DECISION: AUTO-RECONCILE ===
RESOLVED FORK: enabling a task should AUTO-RECONCILE — ensure >=1 child schedule is enabled (auto-enable the default/single child when none enabled). Disabling leaves children as-is (inert, no data loss). Rationale: the UI already presents one toggle as the whole story; the "parent on / all children off" state has no legitimate user workflow (it's only a migration/seed artifact); two independent toggles is power-user flexibility nobody here needs (home-lab solo operator) — it's a footgun, not a shortcut. Error PREVENTION > recovery.

BACKEND edge-handling (for the enable-reconcile impl):
- Common case (single child schedule): enable it. 
- Multiple children, none enabled: enable most-recently-created/disabled; if truly ambiguous, fall back to the warning+one-click-fix for that case (don't block the 95%).
- MANUAL-only tasks (schedule_type=manual): do NOT reconcile / not "wontRun" by design.
- Make reconciliation VISIBLE (toast: "Enabled the existing schedule too, so this task will actually run") — silent reconcile is a different trust problem.

FRONTEND follow-up spec (defer to frontend agent):
- Copy fix (SHIP IMMEDIATELY, 1 line, TaskEditorModal ~L398-411): replace "When disabled, no schedules will run for this task." with "The task and at least one schedule below must both be enabled for this to run automatically."
- New TaskStatusPill component, 4 variants: Running / Enabled(green) / "Enabled, won't run"(amber, when enabled && !next_run && status!=running) / Disabled. List UI already binds task.enabled (effective/parent) — good.
- "Fix it" one-click affordance on the wontRun state → PATCH the disabled child schedule; if zero schedules exist, open editor at Add-Schedule.
- Opt-in discoverability: reuse BackupScheduleBanner pattern on the Channel Pipeline tab — show when >=1 run_on_refresh rule exists AND auto_creation effective-enabled is false. Re-arm dismissal when rule-set changes.
- A11y: aria-live on pill state transitions; aria-label "Enable schedule for {task}" on Fix-it.
- BACKEND must tell frontend which task_ids are manual-only (avoid wontRun false-positives). Full design in session UX agent output.

=== BACKEND DELIVERED (build 0091, PR #656): read-side effective_enabled on GET /api/tasks + bundle, and enable-time AUTO-RECONCILE of the child schedule (MANUAL excluded, newest-of-many, observable, safe-wrapped). Frontend implementation split to the new frontend follow-up bead (see epic). Closing this bead's backend scope.

title: Debug bundle: export effective (parent AND child) task-enabled, not just child schedule
description:
Debug bundle must export EFFECTIVE task-enabled state, not just the child schedule (parent vkktd). The bundle exports task_schedules.json = the CHILD table, whose `enabled` is always seeded True; it omits the PARENT scheduled_tasks.enabled that actually gates firing. Result: a gated-OFF task reads "enabled: true" in the bundle, actively misleading diagnosis (it did — cost a multi-hour investigation).

FIX: in the debug-bundle generator, for each task include the PARENT scheduled_tasks.enabled AND an explicit `effective_enabled = parent.enabled AND child.enabled`, plus child next_run_at / last_run_at. Ideally rename/annotate so it's unambiguous which "enabled" is the firing gate.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A bundle taken while auto_creation parent=disabled, child=enabled shows effective_enabled=false (not a bare enabled=true).
- The frozen next_run_at + null last_run_at remain visible as corroborating signal.
- Related: enhancedchannelmanager-0la8g (bundle/analyzer shape reconciliation) — check for overlap.
