title: SPIKE: choose timezone-aware EPG scoring approach (A global suffix / B matcher synonym map / C tie-break restructure)
description:
PO-approved design spike (2026-07-14) to de-risk vznut.2. Personas: project-engineer + code-reviewer (invoke via /spike).

QUESTION: Which approach best fixes West->Pacific EPG matching without regressing the heavily-tuned matcher?
- A: add PACIFIC/MOUNTAIN/CENTRAL to global TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES (stream_normalization.py:34). Check every other caller that relies on these NOT being stripped.
- B: West<->Pacific synonym map scoped to the EPG matcher only.
- C: restructure sort_key tie-breaks to reward region-CONSISTENCY (channel region == EPG region) without changing key generation; note has_regional (epg_matching.py:893-895) is currently backwards.

METHOD: prototype each against (1) the KNM fixture from the debug bundle channels.csv (real (Pacific) tvg_ids), and (2) the existing epg_matching regression suite. Also decide: region ENCODING/detection source (tvg_id paren vs name vs streams), scoring SEMANTICS (new term vs band-level tiebreak vs gate), Mountain==West or own region, and the edge guard for 'Eastern' as a name-word.

DELIVERABLE: a recommendation with evidence (which option, how many existing tests move, regression surface), feeding vznut.2's build. Does NOT modify production code.

Runs after vznut.1 confirms the mismatch class (per PO gate); can be prepared in parallel since it needs only code + fixture, not live audit data.
============================================================
SPIKE COMPLETE (2026-07-14) — RECOMMENDATION
============================================================
RESULT: **Hybrid A+C, scoped inside epg_matching.py's epg_match_key** (three coordinated changes: candidate-gen collapse of PACIFIC/CENTRAL/MOUNTAIN, region-word token/acronym neutralization, region-consistency tie-break replacing the backwards has_regional). Proven on KNM fixture: 0/24 -> 24/24, 0 test movement across 2,132 tests.
Rejected: Option A-alone (0/24), C-alone (0/24), Option B (higher regression risk).
KEY CORRECTION: TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES (stream_normalization.py:34) is the DEPRECATED path; production strips via the 'Timezone Tags' DB group — do the region strip in epg_match_key (match-only), NOT the tag group (which also renames display names).
Full detail + resolved sub-decisions + characterization-test list recorded on vznut.2.
NEW SCOPE FLAG raised to PO: auto-creation uses a SEPARATE matcher (channel_pipeline_executor._match_epg_data) — the field report is match_channels_epg only; auto-creation is a distinct change. PO to decide narrow-vs-follow-up before vznut.2 build.
Throwaway prototype artifacts left in agent scratchpad (not for merge).

title: Timezone-aware EPG scoring: treat West==Pacific, region-consistent ranking
description:
GROOMED 2026-07-14 (10-persona batch, home-lab tier, component ecm-core). Prevention half of parent vznut. NOT READY TO BUILD — needs a design decision + characterization tests first (see below). Sequenced AFTER vznut.1.

USER VALUE: regional feeds auto-match the correct guide on auto-creation and match_channels_epg, eliminating manual per-channel correction.

SIZE: Large. Not because the logic is big, but because it modifies a heavily-tuned, load-bearing matcher (epg_matching.py; prior tunings cited by beads bd-xxzxe, m4hp1, a6445, bd-6rz70, s5vyz, o97n). HIGH regression risk — unanimous across engineer/code-review/architect/QA.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): epg_match_key strips TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES=[EAST,WEST,ET,PT,CT,MT] (stream_normalization.py:34) so West/East/default collapse to one key; 'PACIFIC' is NOT in that list, so the correct (Pacific) entry gets a different key and loses (lower confidence) to the exact East key match. Separately, sort_key tie-break #9 has_regional (epg_matching.py:893-895) is LATENTLY BACKWARDS — it prefers the NON-regional entry. Fixing it will intentionally FLIP existing rankings.

DESIGN DECISION REQUIRED BEFORE BUILD (three options, engineer/architect/SRE/QA all raised):
- Option A: add PACIFIC/MOUNTAIN/CENTRAL to global TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES. Simplest; but affects ALL stream normalization, not just EPG matching. Must verify no other caller depends on these NOT being stripped.
- Option B: West<->Pacific synonym map scoped to the EPG matcher only. Lower blast radius; more code paths.
- Option C: restructure tie-breaks to reward region-CONSISTENCY (channel region == EPG region) without changing key generation. Preserves back-compat; adds 1-2 new sort_key positions; most complex.
Also to decide: region ENCODING/detection source (tvg_id paren e.g. USANetwork(Pacific)(USAP).us vs channel name vs streams), scoring SEMANTICS (new term vs band-level tiebreak vs gate), and whether Mountain==West or its own region.

HARD PRECONDITION (code-review, non-negotiable): characterization tests locking CURRENT matcher behavior for regional variants MUST land before any change — current coverage in tests/unit/test_epg_matching.py + test_epg_match_key.py is thin on regional cases. This documents that the has_regional flip is deliberate and catches unintended re-rankings.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] User outcome: '...West' channels prefer the '(Pacific)' EPG row; re-running vznut.1 audit after shows the West/East duplicate class resolved.
- [ ] Characterization tests lock pre-change behavior FIRST (code-review precondition).
- [ ] West channel -> Pacific/West entry preferred; East channel -> East entry (QA T1/T2).
- [ ] Untagged/non-regional networks (ESPN, CNN, Fox News) match IDENTICALLY to pre-fix — no regression (QA T4; architect/engineer top concern).
- [ ] Region term does not violate existing invariants: source-priority stays band-level only; country(+40)/exact(+25) still outrank region-only; token-overlap still discriminates same-region candidates (QA T5).
- [ ] Full existing epg_matching regression suite passes (QA T6).
- [ ] KNM 37-channel fixture (debug bundle channels.csv, real (Pacific) tvg_ids) as integration regression: >=90% match Pacific, audit shows no duplicate cluster (QA T7).
- [ ] Edge guard: 'Eastern' as a name-word (not a region tag) not mis-detected (QA concern d).
- [ ] Docs: document the regional equivalences pulled from code + before/after example (tech-writer, M).

CONCERNS: regression on the tuned matcher (all eng personas); scope may expand if vznut.1 evidence shows non-East/West patterns (PM/architect); consider feature-flag for a release cycle (engineer). SECURITY: none — scoring-only change inside the already-trusted match_channels_epg/link_channel_epg path; keep the synonym list a fixed constant (no user-input regex).
>>> PO DECISIONS 2026-07-14:
- GO/NO-GO GATE: proceed with vznut.2 as scoped (West==Pacific) once vznut.1's audit confirms ANY West/East region mis-links exist. (Field report already establishes this; the audit is the standing check + regression oracle.)
- DESIGN APPROACH: resolve Option A vs B vs C via a DESIGN SPIKE first (see spike bead), before committing build effort on the high-risk matcher. Spike tests all three against the KNM fixture + regression suite and recommends one.
- Sequencing: vznut.1 ships -> audit confirms mismatch class -> design spike picks approach -> characterization tests -> vznut.2 build.

============================================================
SPIKE vznut.3 RESULT (2026-07-14) — READ BEFORE BUILDING
============================================================
RECOMMENDED APPROACH: **Hybrid A+C, scoped INSIDE epg_matching.py's epg_match_key** (NOT global TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES, NOT the DB tag group, NOT Option B). Proven on the KNM fixture: 0/24 -> 24/24 West->Pacific, 0 regressions across 2,132 EPG/normalization/pipeline/tag/channel tests.

CORRECTION to this bead's root-cause framing (spike, empirical):
- TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES (stream_normalization.py:34) does NOT drive production matching — it only feeds the DEPRECATED legacy normalize_for_epg_match path. Production strips timezone via the "Timezone Tags" DB group (EAST/WEST only) inside extract_core_name(for_matching=True). So the original 'Option A: add PACIFIC to TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES' would change NOTHING in production.
- Do the region strip in epg_match_key (a match-only artifact, like the existing residual-digit sweep at epg_matching.py:459), NOT in the tag group — the tag group is ALSO consulted by display-name renaming rules (normalization_migration.py:40), so adding PACIFIC there would strip 'Pacific' from displayed channel names (real blast radius). Scoped variant hits 24/24 with the tag group untouched.
- Option B (synonym map keeping region in key) is HIGHER regression risk than assumed — breaks the 'West collapses to base' invariant. Recommend AGAINST B.

THREE COORDINATED CHANGES (all in epg_matching.py):
1. Candidate-gen: collapse PACIFIC/CENTRAL/MOUNTAIN to base key in epg_match_key so the regional entry becomes an exact candidate. REQUIRED for short-name nets (AMC/FX/TBS/E!/FXX) whose Pacific entry is otherwise never a candidate (prefix scan gated at len>=4, epg_matching.py:1020) — no tie-break can reorder a candidate that isn't in the set.
2. Token/acronym neutralization: exclude region words from identity tokens AND from paren-acronym extraction (build_epg_lookup ~664). Else '(Pacific)' scores as an extra token (m4hp1 -4 penalty, pushes East a full band ahead) and mis-indexes into by_acronym['pacific'], shadowing the real (USAP).
3. Region-consistency tie-break: replace latently-backwards has_regional (epg_matching.py:894) with a region-consistency rank (0=match,1=neutral,2=conflict) at the same sort position, via detect_region().

RESOLVED SUB-DECISIONS:
- Encoding/detection: tvg_id parenthetical FIRST (authoritative for JESmann), then last word of display name.
- Scoring semantics: band-preserving TIE-BREAK (not a new confidence term, not a hard gate). Only reorders in-band ties; never outranks country(+40)/exact(+25). Requires step 2 first or the band separates and the tie-break can't fire.
- Mountain = its OWN region (M), NOT ==West. Only West==Pacific(PT). Central its own (C). No in-data evidence to alias MT/CT->PT.
- Eastern edge guard: exclude adjective forms (eastern/western) from map + strip regex; detect region only from trailing-word/paren. Proven: 'PBS Eastern','Western Channel' -> None; 'BBC East' -> E.

CHARACTERIZATION TESTS TO LAND FIRST (code-review precondition, from spike):
1. Lock has_regional currently prefers NON-regional (the flip must be deliberate).
2. Lock short-name net (AMC West) currently produces NO Pacific candidate (why C-alone fails).
3. Lock '(Pacific)' currently mis-extracts to by_acronym['pacific'] + token-extra penalty (33 vs 37).
4. Invariant guards (stay green): non-regional (ESPN/CNN) unaffected; East->East/default not Pacific; West-with-only-base->still matches base; 'Eastern'/'Western' not region; genuine acronym (OWN/FETV) still resolves.
5. KNM 37-channel fixture integration (>=90% Pacific).

>>> NEW SCOPE DECISION FOR PO (spike flag): vznut.2 AC says regional feeds auto-match 'on auto-creation AND match_channels_epg'. These are SEPARATE code paths — match_channels_epg -> epg_matching.py (this Hybrid A+C fix); auto-creation -> channel_pipeline_executor._match_epg_data (a simpler separate mirror with its own hardcoded timezone list, no band/token/region scoring). The field report is about match_channels_epg ONLY. The auto-creation half is a DISTINCT additional change. DECISION: narrow vznut.2 to match_channels_epg only (recommended), or add auto-creation as a follow-up bead.
>>> PO DECISION 2026-07-14 — SCOPE: NARROW vznut.2 to match_channels_epg (epg_matching.py) ONLY. The auto-creation matcher (channel_pipeline_executor._match_epg_data) is OUT of scope here — filed as follow-up vznut.4, gated on vznut.1 audit evidence. This matches the field report and keeps the change to the proven Hybrid A+C surface.

=== CODE REVIEW 2026-07-14 (code-reviewer): APPROVE-WITH-NITS, merge-ready ===
Independently verified the high-risk items: all 7 EPGMatchWithScore sites carry epg_region; band-preserving (region tie-break at tuple pos 9, after confidence/source — cannot outrank country+40/exact+25); inert when channel has no region; channel+EPG both route through epg_match_key so region collapse is symmetric; whole-word + adjective guard real. Test quality good (labelled flips vs invariants).
FINDINGS:
- WARN #1 (detect_region trailing-quality-tag gap): name branch takes strictly words[-1]. 'AMC West HD' -> last word 'HD' -> region None -> falls back to East. Channels being matched usually have NO tvg_id, so channel-side region relies on the name; 'West HD'/'West FHD' is a common IPTV pattern => fix silently doesn't help those (NOT a regression — stays pre-fix East — a coverage gap). Fix: strip quality tokens before trailing-word detection + test. => PO DECISION below.
- MINOR #2: add end-to-end invariant test that 'Comedy Central' channel still links 'Comedy Central' row post-collapse (central noun conflated w/ timezone; self-match holds but untested).
- MINOR #3: extract_paren_acronym gained skip-short-and-continue (un-characterized change to load-bearing bd-6rz70 fn); confirm intentional + lock w/ test.
- NITS #4-6: docstring contract, redundant assert, red-state not reconstructable from git (spike has it).
Reviewer rec: merge as-is (KNM target 24/24, bare names) + fast-follow the detect_region gap.

=== STATUS 2026-07-14: MERGE-READY (verified + fully reviewed) ===
Branch feat/vznut.2-timezone-aware-epg (worktree wt-vznut2), 3 commits: fcf15f9a (core Hybrid A+C + 28 tests) / 2134a5c4 (review nits: detect_region quality-skip, acronym revert, +tests) / bdf9ed9a (detect_region bare-digit skip + 2 tests).
Gates independently re-run by coordinator: 6844 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. KNM fixture 24/24 West->Pacific.
Code review: APPROVE-WITH-NITS -> all findings folded -> 2 focused re-reviews both CLEAR-TO-MERGE.
Follow-ups filed as beads: vznut.5 (docs), vznut.6 (pagination ceiling), vznut.4 (auto-creation matcher). NOT merged — awaiting PO ship go.

title: Duplicate/shared EPG-link audit: surface channels sharing one epg_data_id
description:
GROOMED 2026-07-14 (10-persona batch, home-lab tier, component ecm-core + mcp-server). Ships FIRST — detection + ground-truth generator for the West-shares-East EPG bug (parent vznut). READY TO BUILD.

USER VALUE: operators with multi-region lineups can find channels silently mis-linked to the same EPG row — today there is no way to detect this. KNM's ~37 West channels would surface immediately.

SIZE: Small (engineer ~15-30min; DBA notes M-ish only due to live Dispatcharr pagination). No schema change.

KEY STRUCTURAL FACT (DBA): epg_data_id lives in DISPATCHARR, not ECM journal.db. Audit is a read-only aggregation over the live Dispatcharr channel list (GET /api/channels/channels/), NOT a local DB query.

>>> PO DECISION 2026-07-14 — SURFACE: embed a 'shared EPG links' summary INSIDE the existing match_channels_epg preview (where re-matching already lives) PLUS expose a read-only MCP tool/endpoint (e.g. audit_epg_duplicates / GET /api/epg/audit-duplicates). Resolves the UX actionability concern; keeps scope Small. 'Dedicated report' and 'read-only-only' options declined.

OTHER DEFAULTS chosen in grooming (override if wrong):
- Manual-invoked first (matches the ground-truth-data goal); scheduled-task variant is deferred follow-up, not in scope.
- Exclude NULL/unlinked channels (they are 'unlinked', not 'mis-linked'); optional include_unlinked flag can come later.
- Output JSON, sorted by channel id, deterministic (QA: must be a repeatable test oracle).
- Report ANY sharing (group size >= 2), no threshold.

OPEN (engineer to confirm during build, DBA): is epg_data_id globally unique or per-source? If per-source, GROUP BY (epg_source_id, epg_data_id). Default to the correct-per-source grouping.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] User outcome: running the audit lists every set of channels sharing one epg_data_id; KNM's 37 would be flagged.
- [ ] Surfaced inside the match_channels_epg preview (PO decision) + read-only MCP tool.
- [ ] Read-only — no mutation during audit (security/code-review).
- [ ] Groups by the correct Dispatcharr linkage key; NULL/unlinked excluded (DBA/QA).
- [ ] Output includes channel_id, channel_name, shared epg_data_id, count, and the shared EPG entry's name/tvg_id (QA/DBA).
- [ ] Deterministic JSON output usable as a test oracle (QA).
- [ ] Tests: shared-id detected; singletons ignored; NULL ignored (QA Test 1-4).
- [ ] Pre-ship smoke: audit ~100+ channels well under UI-hang threshold (SRE, <500ms).
- [ ] Docs: short 'finding & fixing mis-linked channels' section under docs/user_guide (tech-writer, S) — acceptance criterion, not a separate bead.

CONCERNS: none blocking. Low risk across all domains.

=== CODE REVIEW 2026-07-14 (code-reviewer): APPROVE-WITH-NITS, merge-ready ===
No blockers. Findings:
#1 (Warn, land pre-merge): the /match embed runs the audit over the FILTERED channel scope (request.channel_ids). If an operator re-matches only West channels, the East counterpart is out of scope and the shared link won't surface in the PREVIEW. title: EPG matcher is timezone-blind: West channels mis-link to East EPG rows; (Pacific) entries penalized
description:
Field report (KNM debug bundle 20260714, ECM 0.17.5). User's West channels (USA Network West, TNT West, Cinemax West, etc.) had epg_data_id pointing at their East counterpart's EPG row, silently showing East's schedule. JESmann source DOES carry genuine (Pacific) guide entries; they just weren't linked. match_channels_epg ranked the wrong East match above the correct Pacific one. User fixed all ~37 West channels manually.

Root cause (backend/epg_matching.py):
1. epg_match_key/normalize_for_epg_match strips TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES=[EAST,WEST,ET,PT,CT,MT] (stream_normalization.py:34) from the match key. 'USA Network West', 'USA Network East', and 'USA Network' all collapse to key 'usanetwork' -> matcher is timezone-blind on its primary (confidence) signal.
2. 'PACIFIC' is NOT in TIMEZONE_SUFFIXES. JESmann entries like USANetwork(Pacific)(USAP).us normalize to 'usanetworkpacific' -> a DIFFERENT key. Correct Pacific entry becomes only a fuzzy/prefix match (lower confidence) while the wrong East entry is an EXACT key match (higher confidence). East wins on confidence -> the ranking inversion the user observed.
3. The lone regional tie-break (sort key #9, has_regional = 1 if EPG name contains a regional word, ascending) PREFERS the non-regional East default over a '...Pacific' entry, compounding it.

Gaps confirmed: (a) no timezone/region-aware EPG matching or west<->pacific synonym; (b) normalization rules only clean display name, cannot drive EPG source selection; (c) no scheduled task re-validates epg_data_id linkage (epg_refresh only pulls program data for already-linked tvg_ids); (d) NO audit tool detects two channels sharing one epg_data_id (the exact signature of this bug).

Possible directions (needs grooming): timezone-aware scoring that treats West==Pacific and rewards region-consistent candidates; add PACIFIC (and MOUNTAIN/CENTRAL synonyms) to region handling; a 'duplicate/shared EPG link' audit surfaced in match_channels_epg preview or as its own report; optional re-validate-links pass.

title: Enforce build-number ADVANCE (not just match) on source PRs — CI + agent hook
description:
PROBLEM: the version-consistency CI check (scripts/check_version_consistency.py, .github/workflows/test.yml:295) only verifies the 3 version touchpoints MATCH, not that the BUILD number ADVANCES. This session shipped ~9 source PRs to dev at 0.17.6-0084 with no bump and no CHANGELOG entry, undetected the whole time (bead 2til0 was the catch-up). versioning.md documents prior skews (PR #277, bd-9rtlc) — this recurs.

GOAL: make a non-advancing build number un-mergeable on any source-touching PR, and ideally caught before push.

MECHANISMS (PO flagged 'setting up hooks'; recon findings):
1. CI (authoritative, recommended primary): extend check_version_consistency.py OR add a job that fails when frontend/package.json BUILD is not strictly greater than origin/dev's BUILD. SCOPE using the EXISTING docs-only classification — .github/workflows/docs-only-pass.yml already fast-passes docs-only PRs, so those are exempt by construction. MUST exempt the release-cut PR (drops the -BUILD suffix; see shipping.md release flow) and handle base=dev.
2. Claude Code hook (agent-side — directly addresses THIS session's failure mode, since the miss was the agent skipping the step): a PreToolUse/guard hook on the ship action (gh pr create / gh pr merge, or git push) that blocks/warns if the version didn't advance. None configured today (.claude/ has no hooks). New.
3. Local git pre-push hook: COMPLICATED — core.hooksPath is already set to .beads/hooks (beads tool owns it), so a project pre-push hook can't use .git/hooks. Would need to coexist with beads' hooksPath or be dropped in favor of (1)+(2).

DESIGN DECISIONS (PO): which layer(s) — CI-only, or CI + agent hook; how to define exempt PRs (reuse docs-only-pass logic + release-cut); whether to also (optionally, secondary) assert a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] touch on source PRs (harder to enforce meaningfully — a diff-touch check at best); whether the check should suggest the next build number in its failure message. Priority P2 — prevents a recurring release-hygiene bug.
notes: PO DECISIONS: build BOTH layers — (1) CI hard-gate on build-number advance, (2) Claude Code agent-side hook on the ship action. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] check = INCLUDED but OPTIONAL/SOFT (warn, do NOT block) in both layers. Exemptions (must not break): docs-only PRs (reuse docs-only-pass.yml classification), the release-cut PR (version drops the -BUILD suffix / base main). Design: a single shared checker script (e.g. scripts/check_version_advances.py) invoked by BOTH the CI job and the agent hook (DRY). Agent hook lives in a CHECKED-IN .claude/settings.json (project-shared), scoped to gh pr create/merge (or git push) only — must not block the agent's normal non-ship git ops. hooksPath is claimed by beads (.beads/hooks) so NO local git pre-push hook.

title: Event Sync: option to refresh the rule's M3U providers before a run
description: PO feature request: a setting so that when an Event Sync rule run happens, ECM first refreshes all 'applied M3Us' (the M3U accounts backing the rule's master + secondary groups), THEN runs the match/attach — so the run always works against fresh data, eliminating the refresh-ordering staleness window (see the refresh-watermark self-heal discussion). Derive the accounts from the rule's master_group + secondary groups -> their M3U account ids -> trigger M3URefreshTask for those, wait, then run. Reuse existing M3URefreshTask (account_ids). DESIGN DECISIONS (pending PO): (A) which runs pre-refresh — live manual Run only (keeps dry-run zero-write, since a refresh WRITES to Dispatcharr's stream list; auto-runs already follow a refresh so excluded) vs also the dry-run Test vs also auto-runs; (B) per-rule Advanced toggle vs global setting. Defaults for the rest: synchronous refresh-then-run with progress feedback; best-effort (a failed provider refresh warns but the run still proceeds against current data, mirroring the watermark partial-success behavior). ALSO document the refresh-ordering/self-healing behavior + this new option in docs/event_sync.md as part of this work (folds in the PO's doc request). Touches the run path (executor/engine) + rule schema + editor UI + M3U refresh wiring.

(B) Per-rule Advanced toggle ('Refresh this rule's M3U providers before running'), refreshing exactly that rule's master+secondary providers. Rest of design (defaults): synchronous refresh-then-run with progress feedback; best-effort (failed provider refresh warns but run proceeds against current data). title: Event Sync execution details are confusing (Evaluated 0 / Matched 0 while log shows 9 already-attached)
description: PO report: an Event Sync dry-run's execution details show Streams Evaluated: 0, Streams Matched: 0, Channels Created: 0 — but the Execution Log shows '9 matched streams' ('Stream already in channel …'). The standard-rule summary counters (evaluated/matched/created) don't map to Event Sync's model (secondary streams evaluated; attached vs ALREADY-attached [idempotent]; ambiguous; unmatched; parse-failed). So a real, working idempotent run reads as 'nothing evaluated, nothing matched.' Two asks from PO: (1) evaluated count should reflect ALL streams evaluated, (2) matches that are already-attached should be surfaced as matches (already attached), not hidden as 0. PO directive: HAVE THE UX DESIGNER RECONSIDER the Event Sync execution-details summary. title: Event Sync editor: 4-step wizard + persistent impacts rail; establish shared modal-layout primitives in common CSS
description:
Convert the as-built Event Sync editor (two-pane + scroll-spy on branch feat/eventsync-editor-redesign) into a 4-STEP WIZARD that keeps the persistent live-impacts rail. Continue on that same branch (do NOT branch again). Presentation/UX only — do NOT change buildConfig, save semantics, config fields, provider-scoped pickers, or preview wiring.

FILES: frontend/src/components/channelPipeline/EventSyncRuleEditor.tsx (+ .css), ChannelPipelineTab.tsx (mount ~L1114), EventSyncPreviewPanel.tsx, ModalBase.css / a new shared modals stylesheet.

STEP MODEL: 1 Scope · 2 Matching · 3 Behavior · 4 Review & Preview. Full-width step pills under the header drive the LEFT column only. Free non-linear nav (any pill clickable). Keep all four step sections MOUNTED, toggle visibility with hidden (preserves picker/test-panel state + refs). Focus the step heading (tabIndex=-1) on step change; aria-current on the active pill. DELETE the IntersectionObserver + scrollToSection (this removes the step-3-never-highlights bug by construction; root cause was rootMargin '0 0 -55% 0' + a short last section).

LEFT COLUMN per step: Scope = Basic Info (name*/description/enabled) + Show-all-groups + Master picker + Secondary picker + 'use master's own streams' anchor. Matching = Parse patterns + Custom shared pattern + Test patterns (collapsed, auto-expand on failure) + Time tuning / Score threshold / Date handling / Per-group overrides subgroups (keep the collapsible subgroups + 'N changed' badges). Behavior = Automation / Scope-extension / Guide-data subgroups. Review = read-only settings summary with per-row jump-back links ([back-arrow] -> setCurrentStep).

RIGHT RAIL (persistent, sticky, aside aria-label, all steps): (a) INTENT SENTENCE at top always (reuse existing intent useMemo). (b) STEP-REACTIVE IMPACT BLOCK keyed on currentStep, all client-side/instant: Scope -> master name+provider+auto-sync chip, secondary count, auto-sync roll-up; Matching -> pattern coverage count + last Test-patterns result summary if run; Behavior -> risk chips (Auto-run / Title-only / Assumes-date / Guide-data) via badge/badge-warning classes, fed by the existing *Changed flags. (c) SINGLE EventSyncPreviewPanel instance: compact on steps 1-3, expanded on Review. MANUAL trigger only (no auto-run — it is a live server dry-run). STALE-MARKING: snapshot buildConfig() when a preview runs; if current buildConfig() diverges, dim results + show 'Settings changed — re-run' (do NOT auto-clear). Keep disabledReason=validationError on the Preview button.

FOOTER: Cancel (far left, routes through attemptClose dirty-guard) · Back (hidden on step 1) · Next (steps 1-3) which becomes Save on step 4. NEW rules: Save only on step 4. EDIT existing rule (rule prop present): Save also available every step. Save-from-Review must navigate to the offending field's step then focus it (stepForField map). Back/Next MUST call setCurrentStep only — never attemptClose/onCancel — so the dirty-guard fires only on Cancel/Escape/×.

SHARED MODAL-LAYOUT PRIMITIVES (epic mandate): author the two-pane grid, stepper, rail, intent card, subgroup, and why-details styles as GENERIC reusable classes in the COMMON modal CSS (ModalBase.css or a new shared modals.css) with generic names (e.g. .modal-twopane/-main/-rail, .modal-stepper/-item/-num, .modal-intent, .modal-subgroup, .modal-why) so future modals + the standard rule builder reuse them. REUSE: intent useMemo, EventSyncPreviewPanel, validationError, junctions auto-sync data, *Changed counts, badge classes, dirty/attemptClose/onRegisterClose (S4), modal-sm alertdialog confirm. Keep modal-xxl width (scoped so the kind chooser stays modal-lg). Keep 820px single-column collapse (rail drops below main).

ACCEPTANCE: step nav switches left column + updates rail reactively; rail shows correct per-step impacts; preview compact/expanded by step, manual, stale-marks on config change; Back/Next never trigger discard confirm; Cancel/Escape/× do (when dirty); Save routes to offending field's step; new-vs-edit Save availability correct; shared .modal-* classes live in common CSS and Event Sync consumes them; scroll-spy code removed. SEQUENCING: Child 1 ships first (lands the shared primitives on dev). Child 2 (backend) can run anytime in parallel on its own branch. Child 3 branches off dev once child 1's shared primitives are available and child 2's endpoint exists. Engineers run sequentially in the main checkout (this repo's worktree mechanism is unreliable). S2 (Medium): regroup the 8 Advanced flags by purpose (Matching: Time tuning + Score; Behavior: Automation + Scope-extension + Guide-data) with labeled subgroups + 'N changed' badge on collapsed subgroups; move risk prose into <details>.
S3 (Medium): two-pane grid (form ~62% / sticky validation rail ~38%), rule-intent plain-language sentence in rail, Preview promoted into rail (always visible), scroll-spy 3-phase spine (Scope/Matching/Behavior). Single-column fallback < ~820px.
S4 (Small, NOT in current scope): dirty-state discard guard (Escape+Cancel) + secondary-empty inline anchor.
S5 (Small, BACKEND-BLOCKED, NOT in current scope): preview provenance chip 'matched_via' — needs a backend field; file dependent bead when picked up.

CURRENT ENGINEERING SCOPE = S1+S2+S3. Reuse shared classes (modal-xxl, .form-group/.form-hint, .checkbox-option, .event-sync-details/<summary>, .badge/.badge-sm, modal-sm confirm). New component-local classes justified: .event-sync-editor-grid, .event-sync-rail, .event-sync-intent, .event-sync-subgroup, .event-sync-scrollspy (IntersectionObserver). Must NOT break existing provider-scoped pickers, preview wiring, or save-config assembly.

title: Event Sync parse: dateless time-first-after-colon-slot ('PPV 06: 4:15pm Title') and '@ <time>' dateless leave title polluted / unmatched
description: Reporter's live PPV feeds: 'PPV 06: 4:15pm Zenith Racing Series Road America', 'PPV 08: 6pm DIRTcar...' fail even with assume_current_date — the dateless-time-first pattern requires a '-'/'|' before the time, not a colon/space slot. FIX (gated behind assume_current_date): add a time-first pattern for '<slot>: <time> <title>' (colon/space slot, no dash) and treat '@ <time>' (dateless) so '@' is consumed not left in the title. PO approved.

title: Event Sync 6xxmp gap: include_master_group_streams still requires a non-empty secondary — allow empty secondary so the pure same-named-group case is usable
description: Dispatcharr source confirms ChannelGroup.name is unique=True (apps/channels/models.py) — two providers' same-named group is ONE ChannelGroup with per-provider ChannelGroupM3UAccount junction rows (auto_channel_sync/enabled/custom_properties). So there is exactly one 'MLB PPV'; the operator cannot pick two. include_master_group_streams (bead 6xxmp) is the correct mechanism BUT channel_pipeline_schema.validate_event_sync_config:958-964 still requires secondary_group_ids non-empty, and the editor buildConfig blocks save when secondaryGroupIds is empty — so the pure same-group case (only the OTHER provider's streams, in the same group as master) cannot be saved. FIX: allow empty secondary_group_ids when include_master_group_streams=true (master group is the scoped source; anti-unscoped rail intact). Relax editor buildConfig likewise + UI copy. Fetch/resolve/preflight already handle empty secondary + master self-source. PO approved: relax schema for the flag.

title: Event Sync: opt-in parse_master_from_stream — read master identity from attached stream so channels can be named freely
description: PO-approved (per-rule flag). Default OFF. When on, each master channel's event title+time are read from its FIRST attached stream's name (fetched via get_streams_by_ids) instead of the channel name. Design: shared async helper services.event_sync_resolver.build_master_name_to_id builds identity-name->channel-id; matcher/resolver unchanged (they score whatever identity strings the map's keys carry; attach maps the winning key back to channel id). Wired: preview (channel_pipeline.py uses helper), run (executor.execute_event_sync_rule builds map async before run_cpu_bound, passes master_name_to_id to _resolve_event_sync; composes with Channel Group Override effective id). Schema flag + frontend checkbox + docs + MCP docstring. Tests: build_master_name_to_id (2), schema (3), executor run-path (2 incl flag-off-doesnt-match). Composes with all other flags. NOT yet shipped. Parent ti939.

title: Event Sync BUG: Channel Group Override splits channels vs streams across two groups; no master_group_id satisfies both fetch + preflight
description: FIXED (fetch-follows-override). resolve_effective_master_group_id (event_sync_preflight.py) maps an auto-synced override SOURCE group -> its TARGET so master channels are fetched where they actually live. Wired into preview (channel_pipeline.py: fetch settings once, resolve, use effective id for get_channels + filter), run (engine fetches settings once, resolves per rule, passes effective_master_group_id to executor.execute_event_sync_rule -> _resolve_event_sync channel filter). Preflight now accepts an override TARGET as master (reads auto-sync via source) + accepts a pre-fetched all_settings to avoid double fetch. Operator can point master at EITHER the auto-synced source group (natural pick) OR the target; both work. Live-verified: resolve_effective(95->override 420)=420 on the real instance. Tests: 7 new preflight/override unit tests; updated manual-run test (settings now read for override resolution, not a gate). Docs: event_sync.md override + master-naming subsections. NOTE: include_master_group_streams composes correctly when master=source (streams fetched from source, channels from target). NOT yet shipped.

title: Event Sync: opt-in per-rule assume_current_date for dateless live groups (Boxing '6PM', LIVE EVENT '4:15pm')
description: Bucket 2 of the second parse-failure report. Providers list live 'today' schedules with a TIME but NO date: 'Boxing 05 : FURY vs HALL 6PM', 'Fury v Makhmudov 19:00', 'LIVE EVENT 05 - 4:15pm Zenith Racing Series Road America' (time-FIRST). The never-guess-date rail rejects these by design. PO approved an OFF-by-default per-rule flag assume_current_date that fills the current date (event_timezone) so time-only listings match. Requires: bare-time capture incl. hour-only 'H PM'/'H:MM am' forms, title+time patterns for BOTH orders (time-first '- <time> <title>' and time-last), thread flag through resolver->parse_event_name without changing default never-guess behavior. RISK: cross-day same-time-of-day false matches (window still guards). Note LIVE EVENT group times are unreliable (4:15pm vs 9:15am for same event) so parsing alone won't pair that group. Parent ti939.

title: Event Sync: parse parenthesized numeric dot/slash dates, e.g. 'PPV EVENT 01: Title (7.12 9:15 AM ET)'
description: Bucket 1 of the second parse-failure report. Provider shape wraps a US month-first NUMERIC date in parens: '(7.12 9:15 AM ET)' / '(7/12 12:00 PM ET)'. Current built-ins only accept @/| delimiters and month-NAME dates. Fix: add '(' to the shared delimiter and a numeric-date built-in pattern (month-first, M.D or M/D). Prototyped clean, 0 corpus regressions. These carry a real date and pair with the Flo/other listings. Parent ti939. PO approved add-only.

title: Event Sync group picker: same-named provider groups collapse to one entry, blocking master+secondary selection across providers
description: OPTION B IMPLEMENTED (PO decision). New config flag include_master_group_streams (default false). When on, the MASTER group's own streams are also fetched as a secondary source and matched to master channels; resolver drops those already attached to a master channel (attached_stream_ids param) so preview/run parity holds and the auto-synced provider's own streams are never re-offered. Executor attach was ALREADY idempotent (channel_pipeline_executor.py:3629 already_attached no-op) so the spike's duplicate-attach risk is a non-issue; the resolver filter is for dry-run parity + noise. Master NEVER added to secondary_group_ids (anti-1341 rail intact). Files: channel_pipeline_schema.py (allowed key + bool validate), services/event_sync_resolver.py (attached_stream_ids filter), routers/channel_pipeline.py (preview fetch + attached_stream_ids), channel_pipeline_engine.py (run fetch), channel_pipeline_executor.py (attached_stream_ids from master channel .streams), frontend types/eventSync.ts + EventSyncRuleEditor.tsx (checkbox), docs/event_sync.md. Tests: resolver filter (4), schema (4), editor (3), roundtrip fixture updated. Deployed to container + smoke-verified. NOT yet shipped (awaiting PO 'ship the fix').

title: Event Sync parse failures: default patterns reject trailing suffixes, pipe-delimited names, weekday prefixes, region markers
description: FIXED + deployed. Broadened the 2 built-in DEFAULT_EVENT_PATTERNS in services/event_sync_matcher.py: (1) folded captured time into the date pattern so trailing suffixes after the time are ignored (was end-anchored -> parse failure); (2) accept | as well as @ delimiter; (3) optional weekday prefix. Synced eventSyncShippedPatterns.json builtins byte-for-byte (parity gate green). 0 regressions across 60 corpus parses; both reported names parse on live backend. Regression tests added. Docs cookbook updated. NOT yet shipped.

title: Event Sync editor: master + secondary group selectors should default to enabled groups only (with show-all escape hatch)
description: User feedback on the early Phase 1/2 build: the master-group select and secondary-group multi-select in EventSyncRuleEditor display ALL channel groups (hundreds on a real instance), which is noisy. They should limit to ENABLED groups. 'Enabled' = the group is enabled on its M3U/provider account (M3UGroupSetting.enabled === true) — the editor already fetches this into groupSettings via getProviderGroupSettings(), so this is a CLIENT-ONLY change: no backend, no new endpoint. Design: default both selectors to show only groups where groupSettings[g.id]?.enabled === true; add a 'Show all groups' toggle (default off) that reveals the full list for edge cases (temporarily-disabled group, or a group with no provider settings). The existing name-filter box stays. Master pre-flight (auto-sync ON) and secondary guidance (auto-sync OFF) are unchanged — this only affects which groups are LISTED. Groups with no groupSettings entry are treated as not-enabled (hidden unless show-all). Preserve the z4y4a round-trip: a rule that already references a now-disabled/hidden group must still display and round-trip that selection (don't drop an already-chosen group just because it's filtered out of the list). Size: Small, frontend-only. vitest for: default hides disabled groups, show-all reveals them, already-selected out-of-filter group still renders.

title: Event Sync rules-list badge tooltip wrongly says 'never on unattended refresh' for auto-run rules
description: Found during Phase 2 live verification. ChannelPipelineTab.tsx:890 hardcodes the event_sync kind-badge tooltip: 'attaches streams on MANUAL pipeline runs only (never on unattended refresh); attaches are journaled and reversible via rollback'. Since ti939.3.1 shipped opt-in auto-run, that 'never on unattended refresh' clause is FALSE for a rule with event_sync_config.auto_run=true — an operator who enabled auto-run and hovers the badge is misinformed about why overnight attaches occur. Fix: make the tooltip conditional on rule.event_sync_config?.auto_run (e.g. auto-run ON → 'runs on manual pipeline runs AND automatically after each M3U refresh; journaled and reversible'; OFF → keep current). Low severity (tooltip, default off), safety-relevant clarity. Same copy-consistency class as the ti939.2.4 stale-copy rider.

title: Event Sync review queue: add direct test that tripped-breaker / pre-flight-fail unattended run enqueues nothing
description: From PR #622 review nit 3: enqueue-nothing under a tripped circuit breaker / failed pre-flight on an unattended run is structurally guaranteed (enqueue sits downstream of the PR #620 breaker return + per-rule pre-flight continue, both tested) but has no dedicated one-assertion pin. Add the pin to harden the 'doesn't enqueue garbage' claim. Small, test-only.

title: Event Sync review queue: UI copy should warn that rejecting one contested pairing may auto-attach the sibling
description: From PR #622 review nit 2: rejecting one contested pairing can cause the sibling to auto-attach at threshold (test_reject_collapses_a_contest_to_the_survivor — correct/intended since the survivor was always attach-band). Queue UI/dialog copy should make clear that 'reject B' may yield 'A attaches' so the operator isn't surprised. UI-copy only.

title: Event Sync review queue: DBAS config-restore silently wipes pending + answered review decisions (FK CASCADE)
description: From PR #622 review nit 1: _restore_auto_creation_rules does query(ChannelPipelineRule).delete(), and the event_sync_reviews FK CASCADE (test_rule_delete_cascades_to_review_rows) drops every review row — pending questions AND operator accept/reject decisions — on a DBAS config restore, with no warning. Operational state self-rebuilds on the next run (pending re-enqueue) but ANSWERED decisions are lost, so previously-accepted pairings re-ask and previously-rejected pairings re-surface. No security rail affected (fingerprint keying intact). PO DECISION NEEDED: accept as-is (mirrors pending_merges), or re-key/re-import review decisions by rule NAME across restore (fingerprints already survive; only the rule_id FK breaks). Small if re-keying.

title: Event Sync Phase 2 prerequisite: circuit breaker must gate the event_sync auto-run chain
description: From PR #616 review (ti939.2.3): today a tripped channel-pipeline circuit breaker gates only the unattended chain, and manual runs bypass it — correct in Phase 1B because manual is the ONLY event_sync trigger. When Phase 2's opt-in auto-run flag lands (epic ti939.3), the breaker must explicitly gate the event_sync auto-run path too, or a crashed event_sync run will not stop subsequent automated event_sync runs. This bead is a design prerequisite for the ti939.3 auto-run bead — link/block accordingly during Phase 2 grooming.

title: Event Sync rule editor: preserve API-authored multi-pattern configs on resave
description: From PR #614 review nit: EventSyncRuleEditor's initialCustomShared keeps only the first non-shipped shared pattern, initialGroupOverrides keeps patterns[0] per group, and an all-custom saved selection gets the built-ins re-added on resave — silently modifying hand-/API-authored configs when edited in the UI. UI-authored configs are unaffected. Fix: round-trip the full patterns/group_patterns arrays through the editor state (render extras read-only if the editor UI can't express them, but never drop them on save).

title: Event Sync Test Patterns panel: surface matcher-level validity, not just group presence
description: From PR #614 review nit: the panel's completeness check is group-presence only (title + day/month + hour/minute captured), while the matcher additionally requires a valid month name, hour <= 23, and a real calendar date — so 'A vs B @ 45 Jul 06:00 PM ET' or a custom pattern capturing a garbage month shows 'Parsed' in the panel yet is unmatchable at preview/run time (operator-facing false confidence). Fix: compute a matcher-level validity flag on the backend (reuse _groups_have_complete_time + _build_start semantics from services/event_sync_matcher.py — cheapest is a small endpoint addition or extending the dummy-epg batch preview response) and render it in EventSyncTestPatternsPanel with the same honest never-guess wording.

title: Event Sync: prefer journal-driven surgical unmerge over snapshot full-replace for event_sync rollbacks
description: From PR #616/#617 review (ti939.2.3 gap): rollback_execution with a snapshot delegates to restore_snapshot, which full-replaces each channel's stream list with the pre-run set — reverting Dispatcharr's own master-stream churn between run and rollback. Dispatcharr never resets stream lists, so a stale stream id written by full-replace will NOT self-heal. Fix: when the journal fully covers the run's attaches (category=event_sync, batch_id=execution id), prefer the surgical _journal_driven_unmerge (remove only the run's added ids) and fall back to snapshot restore otherwise. Keep confirm gating. Standard-rule path unchanged.

title: Pre-existing e2e failures: tests/e2e/test_channel_pipeline_tags.py TestFFmpegProfiles hits removed /api/ffmpeg router
description: Observed 2026-07-11 while shipping ti939.1.1/.1.2 (unrelated add-only change). TestFFmpegProfiles::test_list_profiles and ::test_capabilities fail with 404 {'detail': 'Not Found'} because the FFMPEG Builder feature (router /api/ffmpeg) was removed in build 0062 (beads vrrxv/1w428) but the e2e tests were not updated. CI is unaffected (workflows ignore tests/e2e), so this only bites local full-suite runs. Fix: delete or rewrite the TestFFmpegProfiles class in backend/tests/e2e/test_channel_pipeline_tags.py. Repro: cd backend && python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_channel_pipeline_tags.py::TestFFmpegProfiles

title: Guided setup: one-click confirmed auto_channel_sync toggle for master/secondary groups (journaled, never a side effect)
description:
Guided setup: when the rule editor detects a misconfigured group — master with auto_channel_sync OFF, or a secondary with it ON — offer a one-click fix that toggles the Dispatcharr setting via the existing update_m3u_group_settings write path.

**Hard constraint (security, locked at planning)**: this is an EXPLICIT, separately confirmed operator action with its own confirmation dialog stating exactly what will change and why ("Turn OFF auto-sync for 'FIFA | World Cup' (Provider 2)? Dispatcharr will stop creating duplicate channels from this group; existing auto-created channels from it may be removed by Dispatcharr."). NEVER a side effect of saving a rule or running the pipeline. Every toggle is journaled (the existing allow_multi_provider_auto_sync guard-change journaling at routers/settings.py ~L1194 is the precedent).

Also note in the confirm dialog and docs: snapshot restore does NOT revert Dispatcharr group settings — the journal entry is the recovery breadcrumb.

Acceptance: toggle only reachable through the confirm dialog; journal entry per toggle; pre-flight warnings clear after fix; test coverage for both directions (enable master / disable secondary).

Size: Small.

title: Dummy EPG auto-assignment for master event channels (rides existing Pass 5 retry)
description:
Wire the optional dummy_epg_profile reference in event_sync_config so master event channels get guide data automatically. The master group's channels are ordinary Dispatcharr channels, so this rides existing machinery: dummy EPG profile assignment + the existing Pass 5 deferred assign_epg retry (regenerate XMLTV then retry) already handle the hard parts.

Scope: config field + validation (profile must exist); assignment applied to master-group channels within the rule's scope on each run (idempotent — already-assigned channels are no-ops); operator docs section showing an event profile whose title/time patterns match the master provider's naming (patterns may be shared with the rule's parse patterns — call that out to avoid double authoring).

Acceptance: run assigns the profile to new event channels; Pass 5 retry path exercised in a test; docs updated.

Size: Small.

title: Ambiguous-band review queue keyed on event identity (content fingerprints, never channel/stream IDs)
description:
Route ambiguous-band matches (score below attach threshold but above reject) into a review workflow instead of silently skipping them, so borderline events consolidate with one operator click instead of a threshold gamble.

Reuse the pending-merges review pattern (ADR-008) but with the event-specific requirements from the team review:
- **Keying (HARD CONSTRAINT, security)**: pending decisions and accepted/rejected outcomes key on content fingerprints — (rule_id, provider_id, normalized_stream_name_hash, normalized_event_key) — never channel/stream IDs. A decision must survive refreshes and re-apply when the same provider string + event identity recurs; the queue must NOT refill with already-answered questions.
- **UI (security + UX)**: the existing pending-merges UI was built for 1:1 decisions with a single score. Event candidates must show per-candidate evidence: both raw names side by side, parsed titles/times, time delta, team-token verdict — not just an aggregate number. An opaque score is the human-factors condition that let the original 1,341-merge incident scale.
- Accepting an ambiguous match attaches the stream and records the decision so future runs auto-attach that pairing; rejecting suppresses it.

Acceptance: decisions persist across simulated refreshes; queue does not duplicate answered items; journal records queue-driven attaches distinctly from threshold attaches.

Size: Medium.

title: Opt-in auto-run on refresh watermark (per-rule flag, default off) + unattended notifications
description:
Allow event_sync rules to run unattended on the existing refresh watermark task (ADR-011 model) — as an EXPLICIT per-rule opt-in flag, default false. No silent enablement: the operator flips it per rule after they trust manual runs.

Scope: the flag in event_sync_config + validation; watermark task includes opted-in event_sync rules; unattended runs produce the same journal provenance + summary line as manual runs (the summary line is the 3 AM safety net); notification on cap overage or pre-flight failure (master auto-sync OFF) so unattended misconfigurations surface via the existing notification channel rather than silence.

Timing note (documented, not engineered around): Dispatcharr's sync_auto_channels is a Celery task after M3U refresh; ECM's watermark run may occasionally precede master-channel materialization for brand-new events — convergence on the next run is the accepted behavior (tested in the 1B lifecycle scenarios).

Acceptance: flag default-off verified by test; unattended run journals identically to manual; notification paths exercised in tests.

Size: Small.

title: Playwright E2E happy path: configure → test patterns → preview → manual run → multi-provider streams on master channels
description:
One Playwright E2E happy path — deliberately single-path; matcher rigor lives in the frozen corpus gate, not in E2E.

**Flow**: configure an event_sync rule with shipped default patterns -> Test Patterns shows parsed fields -> Preview shows match cards and summary -> trigger a manual run -> the master group's channels show streams from >= 2 providers -> journal shows event_sync provenance entries for the run.

**Acceptance criteria**: test stable in the E2E suite (or, if flaky against the harness, demoted to a documented pre-release manual script with the flake reason recorded); screenshots captured for release notes.

Size: Small. Depends on: 1B resolver bead + 1A frontend bead.

title: docs/event_sync.md Phase 1: operator walkthrough, pattern cookbook, auto-sync gotcha, dev rationale
description:
Write `docs/event_sync.md` — one document, dual-audience (normalization.md pattern), shipping in the same window as the preview endpoint/UI.

**Operator section**:
1. Task walkthrough: "Consolidate event groups across providers" — pick the broadest/most reliable provider's group as MASTER (leave/turn its Dispatcharr auto_channel_sync ON), set every secondary provider's event group auto-sync OFF (manual steps this phase; screenshots), create the event_sync rule with a shipped default pattern, use Test Patterns, read the Preview.
2. Pattern cookbook: at least 3 provider name shapes -> working pattern, using the real observed formats ("Fubo Sports Network 07 : Chelsea vs. Brentford @ Jan 17 10:00 AM ET", "Peacock 14: Mercury vs. Aces @ 11 Jul 06:00 PM ET").
3. Troubleshooting, headlined by the auto-sync gotcha: "Still seeing duplicate channels? A secondary group still has auto_channel_sync ON." Also: nothing matches -> check parse failures panel / master auto-sync ON pre-flight; events missing entirely -> master-as-ceiling limitation explained (secondary-only events get no channel; see the unmatched list).
4. Threshold and bands: what attach/ambiguous/reject mean; threshold minimum 0.80 and why. Include VERBATIM: "Wrong attachments are reversible and non-compounding, but not self-healing — the matcher is deterministic, so a bad match repeats every run until you adjust a pattern or threshold, or the provider renames the stream."

**Developer section**: matcher layering (parse -> time-block -> parsed-title fuzzy -> team-token) and why each layer exists; the event admission policy as a structurally separate branch from the callsign policy, with the history stated ACCURATELY: the prior incident was 1,341 false-POSITIVE merges (an unscoped fuzzy rule), which is why scoping is schema-mandatory and team-token conflict hard-rejects; why there is no durable cluster state (verified Dispatcharr UUID preservation + in-place updates; stateless recompute; never key on channel IDs); the Pass 4 orphan bypass; the future-state constraint that any refresh-surviving state keys on content fingerprints.

**Explicitly NOT written** (home-lab tier): no ADR file, no versioned API reference, no performance guide.

**Acceptance criteria**: every rule config field documented; cookbook patterns copy-paste tested against the Test Patterns panel; doc linked from the reference-guides table in CLAUDE.md/docs index if applicable.

Size: Small. Depends on: preview endpoint bead (documents real behavior). Owner: technical-writer persona; Sonnet-class agent appropriate.

title: Frontend: event_sync rule editor, shipped default patterns, Test Patterns panel, match preview UI (no apply control)
description:
Frontend for the event_sync rule kind: editor, pattern testing, and match preview. Preview-only — there is NO apply/attach control anywhere in this phase.

**Rule editor**:
- Master group select. Show live auto-sync status; if OFF, show guidance (this phase does NOT toggle Dispatcharr settings — explicit instructions instead; a guided one-click confirmed toggle is a Phase 2 bead).
- Secondary groups multi-select with the inverse validation (should be auto-sync OFF) and the same guidance-not-mutation stance.
- Parse pattern selection: ship 3-4 DEFAULT patterns covering the observed shapes ("Title @ Date Time", "Slot N : Title @ Date Time", generic "Title Date Time") so ~80% of operators never write a regex. Custom-regex fallback per group.
- Advanced (collapsed) section: time_window_minutes, attach_threshold (input clamped >= 0.80), shared-vs-per-group patterns. Defaults hidden by default — quick path is: pick master, pick secondaries, pick pattern, preview.

**Test Patterns panel** (reuse the normalization Test Rules / dummy-EPG preview affordances): paste sample names or fetch live samples from the selected groups -> table of raw name -> extracted title / date / time per pattern. Native table semantics.

**Preview screen** (renders the preview endpoint response): match cards showing each provider's RAW name side by side with parsed title/time, score, band as text label + icon (never color alone), team-token verdict, time delta, disparity flags; a distinct unmatched-secondary-streams list; parse-failure panel; summary line ("42 would attach, 8 ambiguous (skipped), 3 unmatched, 1 parse failure").

**Accessibility baseline**: labels + text with icons, keyboard-navigable cards, focus states, ARIA on band labels, no modal-only flows.

**Acceptance criteria**: operator path from zero to previewed rule with shipped defaults and no regex authoring; vitest coverage for pattern-test rendering, band rendering, and clamp behavior; screenshots of the preview for the PR.

Size: Medium. Depends on: preview endpoint bead.

title: Event Sync Phase 2: automation + operator conveniences (opt-in auto-run, review queue, dummy EPG, guided toggles)
description:
Automation and operator conveniences, gated on Phase 1B being shipped and trusted (operator has run manual attaches without false positives). Each child is independently shippable; none is required for the core feature to be usable.

**Standing design constraint for every child** (security, locked at planning): any state that must survive a Dispatcharr refresh — review-queue decisions, exclusions — keys on content fingerprints / event identity (rule_id, provider_id, normalized_stream_name_hash, normalized_event_key), NEVER on channel or stream IDs. Channel IDs are stable only while an event lives; stream IDs can churn on provider refresh. A review queue keyed on channel IDs would refill with duplicates of already-answered questions.

Size: Medium across children.

title: GH #600: MCP create/update_auto_creation_rule drops bool/float/list[int] nested in actions
description: GH #600 triage + fix. TRIAGE: live repro proved ECM's MCP server/backend handle correctly-typed nested bool/float/list[int] fine; the reported 400 reproduces byte-for-byte only when the MCP CLIENT stringifies nested values ('true','0.75','[912, 913]') — some LLM clients do. Top-level typed params get Pydantic lax coercion; nested list[dict] values rode through verbatim into the backend's strict isinstance checks. Bonus finding: condition negate/case_sensitive are NOT validated — a stringified 'false' was truthy and silently inverted the condition. FIX (v0.17.6-0056, PR #601): field-aware lenient coercion at the MCP tool boundary in mcp-server/tools/channel_pipeline.py (_coerce_actions/_coerce_conditions) for create/update_channel_pipeline_rule + deprecated aliases: known bool fields, numeric fields, int-list fields (incl. string elements), condition-type-aware value coercion, recursion into nested condition groups. String params never touched; unparseable values pass through so backend errors surface. 21 new tests (test_gh600_nested_value_coercion.py); 434 mcp-server tests pass. Verified live end-to-end pre/post deploy to ecm-ecm-mcp-1. GH comment with full analysis posted on #600.
notes:
TRIAGED via live repro against dev instance (v0.17.6-0055) through the session's own MCP connection.

FINDING: NOT an ECM serialization bug. Two live calls prove it:
1. Exact issue payload with real JSON types (bool true, float 0.75, list [912,913]) -> rule created successfully (id=4, verified via get, then deleted).
2. Same payload with nested values as STRINGS ('true', '0.75', '[912, 913]') -> reproduces the issue's 400 byte-for-byte, all 5 errors in the same order.

ROOT CAUSE: reporter's MCP client/LLM emitted nested scalars as JSON strings inside actions[i]. Explains their pass/fail table exactly:
- Top-level bool (match_scope_target_group) 'works' because it is a typed param (bool|None) -> FastMCP/Pydantic lax-coerces 'true'->True at the tool boundary.
- Nested values are Any inside list[dict] (additionalProperties:true) -> no coercion, forwarded verbatim, backend isinstance checks fail.
- Nested str 'works' trivially; nested int (max_streams) 'works' only because merge_streams never type-validates it (no isinstance check in channel_pipeline_schema.py).
Reporter's default=str/httpx hypotheses disproven: ecm_client uses httpx json= (strict), and correctly-typed values pass end-to-end. Reporter's claimed version 0.18.0 does not exist (latest tag v0.17.5).

POSSIBLE HARDENING (PO decision): lenient type coercion at MCP tool boundary for known action/condition fields ('true'/'false'->bool, numeric strings->float/int, JSON-string lists->list) since LLM clients demonstrably stringify nested values. Alternative: reply on GH #600 asking for client details / wire capture.

title: MCP↔backend contract enforcement (Plan B): endpoint-contract registry + ECMClient wrapper + OpenAPI contract test
description:
MCP-tool <-> backend-API contract enforcement ("Plan B" from the post-#229 retro). Kills the drift class that was the root cause of 4 of @Koalamanx's 5 bugs (#221 group_id vs channel_group_id; #222 {"rules":[...]} envelope; #223 no real bulk endpoint; #224 swallowed 422 detail). The registry becomes the single source of truth that the tools USE (so a tool physically cannot drift from it), validated against the backend's OpenAPI spec. Plan C (codegen a typed client from OpenAPI) is the heavier alternative — parked; revisit only if B does not hold.

== DESIGN ==

1. mcp-server/_endpoint_contracts.py — the registry
   - frozen dataclass Endpoint: name, method, path (FastAPI-style {param}), request_fields frozenset[str], query_params frozenset[str], response_fields frozenset[str], plus response_is_list bool and an optional "contract-exempt reason" escape hatch.
   - ENDPOINTS dict keyed by a stable id (~tool name; dedupe where multiple tools hit one endpoint).
   - Only names are stored (not full schemas) — that is all the subset checks need. Pure stdlib + dataclasses (must import fine in the backend test env).

2. mcp-server/ecm_client.py — call_endpoint(ep, *, path_args=None, body=None, query=None, timeout=None)
   - formats ep.path from path_args (clear error if a placeholder is missing)
   - asserts set(body or {}) <= ep.request_fields and set(query or {}) <= ep.query_params; raises a developer-facing ContractError on violation — ALWAYS ON (cheap subset check). A tool that sends "group_id" when the registry says "channel_group_id" fails loudly at call time.
   - dispatches to the right httpx verb from ep.method
   - on 4xx/5xx surfaces the response body's "detail" (generalizes the #224 fix; keep the RuntimeError-with-detail behavior the #233 batch added)
   - keep the existing get/post/patch/delete methods (for /health and incremental migration)
   - response-shape validation is left to the contract test (schema-level), not runtime (backend may omit optional fields).

3. Migrate ~112 tools (mcp-server/tools/{channels,channel_groups,streams,m3u,epg,auto_creation,export,tasks,stats,system,notifications,profiles,normalization}.py + resources/overview.py) from hand-rolled client.post("/api/...", json_data={...}) to client.call_endpoint(ENDPOINTS["..."], path_args=..., body=...). Building each ENDPOINTS entry from BOTH the tool code AND the backend route + Pydantic model surfaces any CURRENT drift beyond #221-225 — expect a handful to fix.

4. backend/tests/integration/test_mcp_tool_contracts.py (backend-side: needs FastAPI app importable; adds mcp-server/ to sys.path to import ENDPOINTS). Builds app.openapi(). For each Endpoint asserts: (a) (method, path) in spec["paths"]; (b) request_fields ⊆ the request-body schema's properties (resolving $ref/anyOf/allOf) — the #221 catcher; (c) query_params ⊆ declared query params; (d) response_fields ⊆ the 2xx response schema's properties (resolving $ref) — the #222 catcher. Plus a tool-source guard: regex/AST-scan mcp-server/tools/*.py for client.call_endpoint(ENDPOINTS[...]) refs and any remaining client.<verb>("/api/...") literals; assert every referenced endpoint id is in ENDPOINTS; any unmigrated raw path is a warn (phase 1) / fail (phase 2) unless marked "# contract-exempt: <reason>". Fiddly bits: $ref/anyOf/allOf resolution; the bulk-commit discriminated union (special-case or list the union's superset); GET/DELETE with no body; bare-list responses (response_is_list).

== PHASING (two PRs) ==
Phase 1 (Medium): _endpoint_contracts.py + ECMClient.call_endpoint + the contract test + the tool-source guard in WARN mode + migrate the channels/* and auto_creation/* tool domains (~36 tools — the ones that bit us). Lands the immediate value, proves the design, contract test goes live for the migrated domains. Version bump + CHANGELOG Changed.
Phase 2 (Medium-Large): migrate the remaining ~11 domains; flip the tool-source guard to FAIL on any unmigrated raw /api/ literal; add the "verify the effect" hardening for mutating tools (return the backend's response object in the tool reply / read-back-and-confirm so a 200-with-no-effect like #221 can't fool the calling agent). CHANGELOG entries per the hardening.

== RISKS ==
- OpenAPI $ref/anyOf/discriminated-union resolution in the contract test is the fiddliest part (bulk-commit is the worst case) — may special-case.
- 112-tool migration is mechanical but voluminous — phase 1 de-risks the design first.
- Multi-call / dynamic-path tools (e.g. build_channel_lineup) may not fit one Endpoint — keep them on raw client.<verb> with a "# contract-exempt: <reason>" marker (intentional, not drift).
- sys.path import of mcp-server/_endpoint_contracts.py in the backend CI test env must work (pure stdlib — fine).

Relates to ~/retros/2026-05-11-19_standup-bug-sweep.md §5. P2.
notes: Phase 1 shipped in PR #235 (v0.16.0-0081): _endpoint_contracts.py + ECMClient.call_endpoint + the OpenAPI contract test + the channels/auto_creation domains migrated (28 endpoints; 3 current-drift bugs fixed — group_id→channel_group query param, merge_channels re-routed to /bulk-merge, bulk_commit idMappings→tempIdMap/groupIdMap). Phase 2 remains: migrate the other 11 domains (78 raw client.<verb> calls — channel_groups 9, epg 11, export 6, m3u 7, normalization 2, notifications 5, profiles 2, stats 9, streams 16, system 6, tasks 5) onto call_endpoint; flip the tool-source guard to FAIL on any unmigrated raw /api/ literal; add the verify-the-effect hardening for mutating tools.
close_reason: Complete. Phase 1 (PR #235, v0.16.0-0081): _endpoint_contracts.py + ECMClient.call_endpoint + the OpenAPI contract test + channels/auto_creation migrated. Phase 2 (PR #236, v0.16.0-0082): remaining 11 domains migrated, tool-source guard flipped to FAIL-mode, verify-the-effect hardening for mutating tools. ~99 endpoints in the registry; zero un-exempt raw client.<verb> calls left. Across both phases the registry surfaced 8 silent-drift bugs the test suite never caught (filters ignored: GET /api/streams group/provider_id, GET /api/channels group_id, GET /api/journal limit, GET /api/epg/grid channel_id/limit; tools that 422'd on every call: merge_channels, create_task_schedule; bulk_commit reading idMappings; list_export_profiles/list_task_schedules reading nonexistent response fields) — all fixed. Plan C (codegen typed client) remains parked.

title: Bug: ecm-mcp SSE server rejects mcp-remote OAuth discovery → Claude Desktop can't connect (gh #218)
description:
GH #218 (reporter swarthyplacebo, against v0.16.0-0056, ecm-mcp 0.16.0-0075-dev). Claude Desktop via mcp-remote can't connect to ecm-mcp:6101. mcp-remote unconditionally runs OAuth Dynamic Client Registration discovery before connecting; the probe it sends to /sse is rejected by the MCP Python SDK 1.27.0 SSE handler (mcp/server/sse.py:132 connect_sse → ValueError 'Request validation failed' → 421 → disconnect). Direct curl with Authorization: Bearer (or ?api_key=) works — auth is correct; the MCP server itself is fully functional. ecm-mcp uses the DEPRECATED FastMCP.sse_app() transport (mcp-server/server.py:96) on /sse + /messages/, behind an APIKeyAuthMiddleware, SDK pinned at mcp==1.27.0.

Scope/severity: affects ONLY the Claude-Desktop-via-mcp-remote ingress; Claude Code (direct SSE via .mcp.json) works; channel-management core unaffected — P2 'severely degraded' overstated, suggest P3. Reporter found a working workaround (Claude Desktop → mcp-remote → supergateway:6202 (streamableHttp) → mcp-proxy → ecm-mcp:6101/sse?api_key=...) and offered to share their systemd/supergateway config; also noted Authorization:Bearer fails silently through mcp-proxy, must use ?api_key= query param.

Fix options:
1. Modernize transport: migrate ecm-mcp from FastMCP.sse_app() (deprecated) to Streamable HTTP (mcp.streamable_http_app(), endpoint /mcp) + bump mcp SDK. Streamable HTTP is the current standard and mcp-remote handles it cleanly (the reporter's workaround literally translates SSE→streamableHttp). Requires: new endpoint path, update docker-compose.mcp.yml + README + .mcp.json + docs/architecture.md, adapt APIKeyAuthMiddleware path checks, keep SSE as a deprecated alias if backward-compat matters. Medium. ← recommended proper fix.
2. Discovery-fallback route: add /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server + /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returning a clean 404 / explicit 'no-OAuth, API-key only' so mcp-remote's discovery short-circuits and falls through to direct connect without probing /sse in the 421-ing way. Small — but verify mcp-remote actually falls through after a clean 404 (reporter's analysis suggests the /sse probe is the killer, so this may not be sufficient alone).
3. Investigate the exact 'Request validation failed' (is it the SDK's TransportSecurity Origin/Host DNS-rebinding check at connect_sse?); if so, allow mcp-remote's origin (the server is API-key-gated anyway). Small but security-adjacent.
4. Docs (do regardless): document the working Claude Desktop config (the supergateway/mcp-proxy chain, with the ?api_key= gotcha) OR steer Claude Desktop users to a known-good path; the README currently shows a bare {url:'...:6101/sse?api_key=...'} which doesn't work for mcp-remote-based setups. Small.

Same reporter as gh #217 — credit in the resolution.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.16.0-0078 (PR #232) — migrated ecm-mcp from deprecated FastMCP.sse_app() to Streamable HTTP (/mcp); disabled DNS-rebinding Host allowlist (localhost-only default would 421 remote clients; API key remains the gate); rewrote test_server.py (28 tests); updated .mcp.json/README/architecture/docker-compose/MCPSettingsSection. GH #218 commented & closed. Follow-ups: SDK bump (separate, ADR-001 gate), committed .mcp.json key scrub, '124 tools' wording.

title: Bug: compound OR normalization rule strips entire channel name (gh #217)
description: GH issue #217 (reporter swarthyplacebo, against v0.16.0-0056, P2 'severely degraded'). NormalizationEngine: when a rule uses Compound (OR) logic, primary_match (the match_end position used by strip actions) is only captured if Condition 1 matches (the code pins it to i==0). If Condition 1 mismatches but Condition 2 matches, the strip-action metadata is never set, the engine falls back to match_end=len(text), and the ENTIRE channel name is stripped → blank name. Repro: rule Logic=OR, Cond1='Starts With: VariantA' (mismatch), Cond2='Starts With: VariantB' (match), Action='Strip Prefix' → channels matching VariantB become empty strings. Reporter's proposed fix in backend/normalization_engine.py (~_match_compound_conditions): change 'if i == 0 and match.matched and not cond_negate: primary_match = match' to 'if primary_match is None and match.matched and not cond_negate: primary_match = match'. Needs: confirm root cause, assess the fix, add a regression test, check the AND-logic / negated-condition paths aren't affected.
close_reason: Duplicate of enhancedchannelmanager-hssif (same gh #217 compound-OR-strips-whole-name bug). Detail captured here merged into hssif context.
