title: Fix scheduled task enabled not persisting to database
description: TaskRegistry._save_task_to_db overwrote instance._enabled from the stale DB row and never wrote enabled back, so PATCH enable/disable had no effect after save/reload. YAML Backup (default_enabled=False) made this especially visible. Fix: set db_task.enabled = instance._enabled. Unit test: test_sync_to_database_persists_enabled_for_existing_task.

title: Fix compound OR logic stripping entire channel name in normalization rules
description:
Bug reported in GH issue #217 by swarthyplacebo (ECM 0.16.0-0056, P2).

Symptom: A normalization rule with Logic=OR + cond1=Starts With VariantA (mismatch on the channel) + cond2=Starts With VariantB (match) + action=Strip Prefix produces an empty channel name. The strip applies to the entire string instead of just the matching prefix.

Root cause confirmed in backend/normalization_engine.py:1033-1034 (_match_compound_conditions):

  if i == 0 and match.matched and not cond_negate:
      primary_match = match

When OR logic short-circuits past a non-matching cond1, the i==0 guard prevents primary_match from being captured even though cond2 matched. final_matched=True (via any()), primary_match=None → falls through to RuleMatch(matched=True, match_start=0, match_end=len(text)) on line 1046 → action strips the entire text.

Proposed fix (one-line, from reporter, verified correct):

  if primary_match is None and match.matched and not cond_negate:
      primary_match = match

This captures the first matching, non-negated condition's metadata regardless of index. Also corrects a latent identical bug for AND logic when condition 1 is negated and a later condition isn't.

Plan when resumed:
1. Branch from origin/dev
2. Write a failing pytest that reproduces the OR-cond2-only-matching empty-string symptom (likely in backend/tests/unit/test_normalization_engine.py or similar — check existing _match_compound_conditions coverage)
3. Apply the one-line fix
4. Verify test passes + full backend suite (cd backend && python -m pytest tests/ --tb=short --no-header -p no:warnings 2>&1 | tail -1)
5. Add CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] Fixed referencing GH #217
6. Open PR to dev, drive through to merge
7. Comment on GH #217 thanking the reporter, confirming their diagnosis, and linking the fix
8. Close this bead after PR merges

Reporter context: first-time submitter, drafted diagnosis with Gemini + Sonnet 4.6 confirm. Acknowledge that in the resolution comment.

GH issue: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/217
close_reason: Fixed in v0.16.0-0076 (PR #230). One-line fix to _match_compound_conditions per the reporter's diagnosis + 3 regression tests + CHANGELOG. GH #217 commented & closed.

title: Fix flaky clientErrorReporter withImportTelemetry chunk_load test
description: The test 'reports a chunk_load error and re-rejects on failure' in frontend/src/services/clientErrorReporter.test.ts uses a brittle 'await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))' to settle a fire-and-forget telemetry chain. The chain has ~4 microtask hops including crypto.subtle.digest in hashUserAgent. On CI runners with v8 coverage instrumentation, those hops can spill past the macrotask boundary, causing the assertion 'expected fetch to be called at least once' to fail. Locally on npm run test:ci with PR 211 frontend tree applied, the test passes. CI failed twice on PR 211 (run 25254967624). Fix: replace the setTimeout(0) settle with vi.waitFor() polling. Discovered while merging PR 211 (#211).

title: Auto-creation rule analyzer: lint + structural findings (Phase 1)
description:
## Why

Users build broken auto-creation rules and have no way to find out short of
running them and reading the dry-run logs. The 2026-04-28 debug bundle
review surfaced four real-world bugs in one user's rules.yaml that the
existing regex_lint catches none of:

  - `UK|`, `US|` saved under "Matches (Regex)" — valid regex, matches every
    group because of the trailing empty alternation.
  - `^4K` saved under "Contains" — looks like regex but is being substring-
    matched, so it matches nothing.
  - `^\^4k` saved under "Matches (Regex)" — typo from double-escaping.
  - OR-connector precedence: ungrouped ORs after a `normalized_name_in_group`
    constraint silently drop the guard for the OR'd conditions.

## What shipped

1. **Three new advisory lint codes** in `backend/regex_lint.py`:
   - `REGEX_TRIVIALLY_MATCHES_ALL` — empty alternation in a top-level `|`.
   - `OPERATOR_VALUE_LOOKS_LIKE_REGEX` — Contains-operator value with regex-
     like substrings (`^foo`, `foo$`, `.*`, `\b`, etc.). Bare `|` not flagged
     (legitimate for M3U group substrings).
   - `REGEX_REDUNDANT_ESCAPE_CARET` — `^\^` prefix.
   New `severity` field on `LintViolation` (default `error` for back-compat).
   New `lint_pattern_advisory` and `lint_conditions_json_advisory` so the
   advisory codes never come back from the strict save-time path that
   raises 422.

2. **New module** `backend/auto_creation_rule_analyzer.py`:
   - Reuses the AND/OR grouping algorithm from
     `auto_creation_evaluator.evaluate_conditions` (duplicated, not
     imported, to keep the analyzer off the runtime hot path —
     `split_or_groups` + `test_users_sports_rule_grouping` lock the
     contract).
   - Emits structural findings: `ANDOR_DROPS_GUARD`,
     `MERGE_STREAMS_NO_TARGET_CHANNELS`,
     `RULE_HAS_NO_HOPE_OF_MATCHING`. All severity `warning`; saves never
     blocked.

3. **Two new endpoints** in `backend/routers/auto_creation.py` (declared
   before `/rules/{rule_id}` so the static segment isn't captured by the
   path parameter):
   - `POST /api/auto-creation/rules/analyze` — analyze rules currently
     in the DB.
   - `POST /api/auto-creation/rules/analyze/from-bundle` — multipart
     upload of a debug bundle tar.gz; parses `rules.yaml` and (when
     present) `channel_groups_diagnostic.json` for the structural
     checks. Never touches the DB — safe to point at any user's bundle.

4. **New MCP tool** `analyze_auto_creation_rules(bundle_path=None)` in
   `mcp-server/tools/auto_creation.py`. Calls live endpoint when
   `bundle_path` is None; otherwise streams the bundle to `/from-bundle`.
   Returns a markdown report with one section per rule. New
   `post_multipart` helper added to `ecm_client.py`.

## Acceptance

- 25 new unit tests in `test_regex_lint.py` covering each new code,
  severity plumbing, and the advisory-doesn't-block-strict path.
- 30 new unit tests in `test_auto_creation_rule_analyzer.py` covering
  every finding code (positive + negative).
- 9 new router tests in `test_auto_creation.py` covering live-mode
  happy path, bundle-mode happy path, bundle missing rules.yaml → 400,
  non-tar.gz → 400, invalid YAML → 400.
- 4 new MCP tests in `test_tools.py` covering live mode, clean-result
  message, multipart upload, and missing bundle file.
- 10 acceptance tests in `test_bd_0gntx_user_bundle.py` against the
  saved 2026-04-28 user fixture — every finding called out in the
  diagnosis reproduces.
- Backend full-suite: 3294 pass. MCP full-suite: 26 pass. Coverage
  61.5% (gate is 56%).

## Docs

- New `docs/auto_creation_rule_analyzer.md` documents each finding
  code with example, why-it-matters, and remediation. Linked from
  `CLAUDE.md` reference table.

## Note on MERGE_STREAMS_NO_TARGET_CHANNELS

The bead originally listed an execution-history-based path for this
finding. The shipped Phase 1 only implements the simpler path: explicit
`target_group_id` on the rule + the bundle's `channel_groups_diagnostic.json`
showing 0 channels in that group. The execution-history path is deferred
to Phase 2 along with live group-corpus matching and per-rule dry-run
replay.

title: Include normalization rules in debug bundle (follow-up to bd-cns7j)
description: Bundle's rules.yaml only carries auto-creation rules; normalization rule groups (referenced by auto-creation rules via normalization_group_ids) are absent. Reports of 'normalization isn't stripping X' (e.g. user's bd-cns7j-followup regionals issue) cannot be diagnosed from the bundle alone — we have to ask the user for their rules separately. Add normalization_rules.yaml capturing all groups with nested rule definitions.

title: Auto-creation: country prefixes (DE:/AT:) and quality suffixes (3840P) no longer stripped from channel names
description: User reports that auto-creation rules that previously normalized 'DE: RTL 3840P' down to 'RTL' have stopped working. Channels are landing with full prefix+suffix. Same family as a fix shipped last week. Need to inspect the debug bundle in ~/ecm to determine whether it's a rule misconfiguration or a logic regression.
notes: DIAGNOSED (config, not code — no PR needed): (1) At bundle time (7/16, ~/ecm/ecm-debug-bundle-20260716-164406.tar.gz) ALL 8 normalization groups were disabled — that's why nothing stripped; they've since been re-enabled and DE:-prefix + standard quality suffixes strip correctly. (2) Residual: '3840P'/'2160P' are not members of the builtin Quality Tags group (12-tag seed in database.py:1574 never included them) — add them via the tag-group UI to get 'DE: RTL 3840P' -> 'RTL'. (3) Reminder: auto-creation applies normalization per-rule via normalization_group_ids — production create rules must include groups 1+2. Optional enhancement candidate (separate bead if PO wants): extend the builtin seed with 2160P/8K/4320P. Awaiting PO: apply config change + confirm with reporter, then close.

title: Debug bundle generation fails with generic 'Failed to generate debug bundle'
description: Debug bundle generation timed out for large catalogs (~15K channels). Root cause: GET /api/auto-creation/debug-bundle ran sequentially inside the request — 150 page fetches + 150 stream-detail batches blew the 30s ECM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS budget. Fix: replaced GET with POST/{job_id} 202+poll pattern (matches bd-enfsy), parallelized page + stream-batch fetches via asyncio.gather (concurrency cap 8), in-memory job dict with 30-min TTL pruning. Frontend uses new startDebugBundle/pollDebugBundle helpers; both Settings and Auto-Creation tabs updated. 7 new backend tests + 6 new frontend tests; container smoke test confirmed enqueue in 1.8ms, 571-channel bundle delivered in 531ms.

title: Investigate frontend memory leak on Settings page navigation (gh #207)
description:
Frontend memory leak on Settings page navigation (gh #207). Two leak families, two fixes.

LEAK FAMILY 1 — render loop (shipped in PR #209, v0.16.0-0070, merge f9cfc96a):
- SettingsTab.tsx:319-324 useEffect was missing dep array → ran every render
- useHashRoute.setHash always allocated fresh HashRoute + called pushState even when route unchanged
- Cross-component loop armed when ecm:open-task-editor sessionStorage key was set (NotificationCenter writes it on Edit-Schedule clicks; ScheduledTasksSection only clears it after the matching task loads, so a stale taskId stranded the key)
- Latent under React 18 batching, runaway under React 19.2.5 concurrent rendering
- Fix: add `[]` deps to the consuming useEffect; setHash bails when tab+settingsPage match current route
- Browser-verified: 7 nav clicks → 7 history entries (was tens of thousands), heap stable

LEAK FAMILY 2 — @dnd-kit MutationObserver leak (this PR, v0.16.0-0071):
- Reporter retest on confirmed 0070 build still showed +2,400 KB/s heap growth on #settings/normalization with 20 active "Export Publish" notifications.
- Heap snapshot diff: top grower was MutationRecord — millions of instances, +234 MB Size Delta in 30s.
- Root cause: @dnd-kit/core's useRect() hook, called for every mounted sortable element, attaches a MutationObserver to document.body with subtree:true. With ~30 sortable rows mounted on Channel Normalization plus a heavy notification toast stream (2s poll tier), every toast mount/unmount fired childList records to all 30+ observers — millions of MutationRecord instances retained.
- Fix: sweep all 9 <DndContext> mount sites across 8 files (SubstitutionPairsEditor, ChannelDetail, ChannelsPane ×2, NormalizationEngineSection ×2, EPGManagerTab, SettingsTab ×2 in Channel Defaults) and gate <DndContext> mount on a local isReorderMode/isEditMode toggle. Drag handles only render after user clicks a "Reorder" button; "Done" exits.
- Local Chromium-Playwright verification: 0 MutationObservers on #settings/normalization idle (was 19 pre-fix), 60s heap slope -453 KB/s post-fix (was +2,400 KB/s on reporter Edge 147), all 1231 frontend tests pass, lint + typecheck clean.
- Reporter reverification on Edge 147 / Win 11 is the authoritative signal — Chromium-Playwright cannot reproduce the absolute leak rate due to scheduler differences.

title: Re-dismiss CodeQL alerts #233, #1242, #1243 under 'false positive' category (ADR-005 §Dismiss-With-Comment Policy item 3 compliance)
description:
## Context
Finding A1 from the 2026-04-25 ADR-005 Phase 5 first monthly dismissal-log audit (`docs/security/audit-2026-04-codeql-dismissal-log.md`).

Three CodeQL alerts were dismissed under the GitHub UI `won't fix` category, which ADR-005 §Dismiss-With-Comment Policy item 3 explicitly forbids in Phase 1. The substantive justifications are correct (these are textbook `false positive (with evidence)` dismissals — CodeQL doesn't model `@register_method` side-effect-at-import); only the UI-category selection is wrong.

## Affected alerts (all `py/unused-import` in `backend/main.py`, dismissed 2026-04-24 under PR #161 / bd-kdsn3)
- Alert #233
- Alert #1242
- Alert #1243

## Action
1. In GitHub Security tab → Code scanning, find each alert.
2. Reopen and immediately re-dismiss under reason `false positive`.
3. Retain the existing comment verbatim:
   "Side-effect import: registers @register_method decorator at module load time. Marked with # noqa: F401. Removing breaks alert dispatch (bd-kdsn3)."
4. Verify by re-running the audit query:
   `gh api 'repos/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/code-scanning/alerts?state=dismissed&per_page=100' --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.dismissed_reason=="won'\''t fix")'`
   Must return zero rows.

## Acceptance
- [ ] All three alerts re-dismissed under `false positive`.
- [ ] Audit query returns zero `won't fix` dismissals.
- [ ] Bead closed before next monthly audit (end of May 2026).

## Refs
- bd-o8t26 (parent — this audit)
- bd-kdsn3 (originating cleanup pass that introduced the miscategorization)
- ADR-005 §Dismiss-With-Comment Policy item 3 (`docs/adr/ADR-005-code-security-gating-strategy.md`)
- Audit report: `docs/security/audit-2026-04-codeql-dismissal-log.md` Finding A1
close_reason: Already satisfied before this session: all three alerts (233/1242/1243, py/unused-import in main.py) were re-dismissed as 'false positive' on 2026-05-16 with ADR-005 §3-compliant comments citing this bead + kdsn3; verified 2026-07-26 via API (zero won't-fix dismissals remain repo-wide). No state changed. Prior pass fixed it but never closed the bead.

title: Open /api/session-start to unauthenticated POSTs (SLO-6 denominator coverage, follow-up to arp3o)
description:
PO chose option B from the post-arp3o follow-up: open ONLY /api/session-start to unauthenticated POSTs (NOT /api/client-errors).

Context: PR #196 (bd-arp3o) shipped /api/session-start as JWT-required, which means the SLO-6 denominator only counts authenticated sessions. Pre-auth bootstrap activity (login-page errors, login-page sessions) cannot be observed in /metrics. This is the SLO-6 substrate gap the spike (docs/sre/spike-slo-6-session-semantics.md) flagged.

PO decision: option B. Move /api/session-start into AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS so pre-auth sessions ARE counted in the denominator. Keep /api/client-errors JWT-required (do NOT open it). Accept the resulting measurement bias: pre-auth errors are NOT counted in the numerator, but pre-auth sessions ARE counted in the denominator -> error rate is biased LOW. Document the bias in ADR-006 §1 and SLO-6.

Follow-on to: bd-arp3o (PR #196).
Related: bd-bong9 (ADR-006), bd-i6a1m (SLO-6 phase 1 implementation).
close_reason: Shipped via PR #197 (merge sha a2b57c52). /api/session-start now in AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS so pre-auth sessions count toward SLO-6 denominator. Asymmetry with JWT-required /api/client-errors documented in ADR-006 §1 (amendment) and SLO-6 (Known measurement bias note). Smoke verified: unauthenticated POST returns 200 {deduplicated:false} and ecm_session_starts_total bumps; dedup + schema validation intact. Skipped optional authenticated label (would require ADR-006 §9 addendum, out of follow-up scope).

title: Update ADR-001: remove per-week dep-bump cadence limit
description:
ADR-001 currently caps major dependency bumps to one-per-7-day-window merged to dev. The cadence rule was anchored in human review/observation time — operators needed days to spot latent regressions before the next bump landed.

PO call (2026-04-25): the rule is structurally wrong for AI-era work. The actual bottleneck is CI verification cycles (minutes), not human attention (days). Six parallel agents can verify and ship six bumps in less time than the cadence rule permits one.

## Required updates to ADR-001

1. Excise the "one major bump per 7-day window" cadence rule.
2. Preserve the rest of ADR-001 (whatever other rules it codifies).

title: Spike: session semantics for SLO-6 denominator (ecm_session_starts_total)
description:
Decide how ECM defines a "session" before implementing the ecm_session_starts_total counter. The SLO-6 SLI denominator needs a well-defined session boundary; getting this wrong once and then changing it later invalidates 28 days of SLI history.

## Candidates (all proposed during i6a1m extension work)

**A. One per page load (SPA boot)**
- Pros: simplest to implement; frontend emits once on initial mount; no auth dependency; captures pre-login bootstrap errors.
- Cons: multi-tab inflation — 3 tabs of the same user = 3 "sessions". Also every hard-refresh resets. SLO-6 denominator becomes noisier than actual unique user-sessions.

**B. One per JWT issuance (auth-tied)**
- Pros: aligned with existing auth flow; natural session boundary; single counter bump per login event.
- Cons: excludes anonymous/pre-login bootstrap errors from the SLI denominator — the "bootstrap" error kind in clientErrorReporter.ts can't match against this denominator. Also undercounts: long-lived JWTs mean one "session" can span days of activity.

**C. One per session-cookie lifetime**
- Pros: closest to a true "unique user-session" — SubtleCrypto-generated UUID stored in sessionStorage, counter emitted once on first page load with that session_id. Survives same-tab navigation, resets on tab close. No auth dependency.
- Cons: requires a new frontend bookkeeping surface (session cookie/sessionStorage write); need to decide scope (sessionStorage vs localStorage vs httpOnly cookie); slight privacy surface (though scoped to same-origin SLI use).

## Out of scope for this spike

- Implementation of the counter itself — that's the follow-up bead (see DEPENDS_ON below, blocked on this spike).
- SLO target revision — 99.0% lands with i6a1m; revise only if the spike surfaces that the chosen semantic meaningfully changes the measurable baseline.

## Who to consult

- **SRE** — recommended C during standup for measurement accuracy. Owns SLO evolution.
- **UX Designer** — weigh in on multi-tab semantics and whether sessionStorage write is visible/degrading for users.
- **Security Engineer** — review the session_id surface: is it PII? Does it need rotation? Any LGPD/GDPR implication of adding a per-session identifier?
- **Project Engineer** — sizing + implementation complexity of each candidate.

## Deliverable

One-page decision doc (committed as a retro/spike artifact, OR embedded in a new ADR if the consensus is this needs an architectural decision record). Decision must name the chosen semantic with one-line justification per persona, plus enumerate the implementation steps for the follow-up bead.

Run /spike when ready.

LABELS: spike, sre, slo, observability
close_reason: Spike complete. Decision: candidate C (cookie/sessionStorage lifetime). All three personas (SRE, Security, UX) converged on C from independent rationales. Decision doc merged to dev: docs/sre/spike-slo-6-session-semantics.md (PR #192, merge SHA b4e033b87682aace36bb57a1143d1e76ccd304b1). Implementation steps for arp3o documented in §6 of the doc; arp3o is now actionable.

title: Bug: POST /api/settings drops mcp_api_key when omitted from request body
description:
Surfaced by the i6a1m extension agent (PR #173) while wiring telemetry_client_errors_enabled into SettingsTab. Out of scope for that work — filing here.

Symptom: when a caller POSTs to /api/settings with a partial body (e.g., only telemetry_client_errors_enabled), mcp_api_key is not preserved — it gets overwritten with null/empty instead of keeping the existing stored value. This affects any settings update flow that doesn't resend every field.

Expected: partial update semantics. Fields absent from the request body should retain their current stored value, not be cleared.

Suspected location: backend/routers/settings.py::update_settings. The handler probably does a full overwrite with the Pydantic model's defaults rather than an explicit merge against the existing settings.

Investigation steps:
1. Reproduce: GET /api/settings (record mcp_api_key), POST with just {telemetry_client_errors_enabled: true}, GET again — confirm mcp_api_key is cleared
2. Check if the Pydantic model makes mcp_api_key Optional with a default of None — if so, any partial POST will nuke it
3. Confirm whether this affects other sensitive fields (dispatcharr credentials, Fernet keys, etc.) — if so, this is higher priority than P2

Fix patterns to consider:
- Pydantic model_exclude_unset on incoming body, merge into existing settings dict
- Separate partial-update endpoint (PATCH /api/settings)
- Require full body on POST, deprecate partial updates

Acceptance:
- Reproduction test in backend/tests/routers/test_settings.py demonstrating the bug
- Fix preserves all sensitive fields across partial POSTs
- Test covers at least: mcp_api_key, and one other sensitive field (e.g., dispatcharr password)

title: Write ASGI rollback runbook (docs/runbooks/dep-bump-backend-asgi-regression.md) — PR #170 merge gate
description:
Merge gate for PR #170 (ASGI triplet: starlette 1.0 + fastapi 0.136.1 + uvicorn 0.46).

SRE identified gap during standup 2026-04-24: existing docs/runbooks/dep-bump-smoke-test.md is generic; does NOT cover ASGI-triplet regression modes. PR #170 is a major starlette bump touching the middleware chain that emits all four ecm_http_* / ecm_health_ready_* SLI families. Silent SLI degradation is the real risk — container boots, serves 200s, and emits 3 of 4 metric families while SLOs burn undetected.

Runbook must document:

1. Pre-merge walkthrough (dry-run the rollback):
   - git revert <#170 merge SHA> → docker build → docker restart ecm-ecm-1
   - Confirm previous image tag is pinned before merge
   - Verify /metrics emits all four ecm_* families under synthetic traffic BEFORE merge baseline capture

2. Post-deploy verification (non-negotiable):
   curl /metrics | grep -E '^ecm_(http_requests_total|http_request_duration_seconds|health_ready_ok|health_ready_check_duration_seconds)'
   Must return non-zero samples for ALL four families, not just container-up.

3. Regression modes specific to starlette 1.0:
   - Middleware ordering / BaseHTTPMiddleware semantics changes
   - ASGI scope mutation changes
   - Exception propagation / handler contract changes
   - uvicorn 0.46 event-loop behavior

4. Rollback triggers:
   - Any ecm_* family stops emitting post-deploy
   - p95 latency delta > 10% from pre-merge baseline
   - 5xx rate delta > baseline + 0.1%
   - vjlzf/pvq6s test count regresses post-merge (should be stable or improving)

Acceptance: runbook exists, rollback dry-run logged in PR #170, reverse link added from dep-bump-smoke-test.md.

title: ADR-006: Frontend error telemetry (Phase 1 local-sink architecture, OTel migration target)
description:
Prereq for enhancedchannelmanager-i6a1m (Phase 1 frontend error telemetry implementation).

Surfaced by spike on 2026-04-24 with SRE + security-engineer + it-architect reporting concurrently. PO accepted the Phase 1 shape; IT-architect's guidance: write ADR before implementation, keep i6a1m open until ADR lands.

The ADR must codify:

**Decision**: Ship local-sink frontend error telemetry at `POST /api/client-errors` for Phase 1. OTel-log-record-schema for payload. No external egress by default. Defer SaaS opt-in, SQLite admin view, and OTel collector export to Phase 2.

**Scope**:
- Endpoint: `POST /api/client-errors`, JWT-required (same auth as other /api/* routes).
- Rate limit: token bucket per session, 10 events/minute + 8 KB/request cap; 429 on overflow.
- Payload schema (OTel-log-record compatible):
  ```
  { kind: 'boundary'|'unhandled_rejection'|'chunk_load'|'resource',
    message: str (<=512, scrubbed),
    stack: str (<=4096, basename-stripped),
    release: str (Vite build env),
    route: str (pathname only, no query string),
    user_agent_hash: str (sha256),
    ts: iso8601 }
  ```
- Field allowlist (security-engineer): YES stack/message/pathname/viewport/UA-major-version; NO query strings/referrer/cookies/localStorage/user-typed input.
- Scrubber: extend backend/obfuscate.py regexes (IP/hostname/credential redaction) to the frontend payload path, applied both client-side before send and server-side before log write (belt-and-suspenders).
- Server-side landing: structlog line with `logger: 'ecm.client_error'` + Prometheus counter `ecm_client_errors_total{kind,release}` + histogram `ecm_client_error_reports_bytes` on existing /metrics.
- Label cardinality: `kind` fixed enum; `release` capped to current + prior 2 builds.
- Capture sites: React ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch (exists) + window.onerror + window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection') + Vite vite:preloadError + dynamic-import .catch + pre-bundle inline script in index.html (~20 lines via navigator.sendBeacon for pre-mount crashes).
- Transport: navigator.sendBeacon with fetch fallback; reporter MUST swallow its own errors (never break UX).
- Opt-out: telemetry.client_errors_enabled setting, default ON. Data never leaves the container; privacy-neutral by default. Any future external sink is opt-IN with operator-owned DSN.
- SLO-6 (in docs/sre/slos.md): error-free session rate >= 99% on 7d window; gated at `sessions >= 50/day` for evaluation. Target marked 'to-be-calibrated after 30d of data' (insufficient-data handling consistent with other uncalibrated SLOs per 5uxwh posture).
- Alerting rule added to docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml. Operator-provisioned per 5uxwh.

**Phase 2 (out of scope for ADR-006; note as migration target)**:
- OTel migration path: OTLP-compatible payload means future collector swap is drop-in.
- Opt-in external SaaS sink (operator-owned DSN).
- SQLite-backed admin 'recent errors' view (only if operator demand surfaces).

**Risks codified in ADR**:
- Crash-loop error storms (mitigated by rate limit + circuit breaker).
- Label cardinality blow-up (mitigated by bounded vocab).
- PII/credential leakage (mitigated by scrubber + allowlist).
- Sink unreachable must not break UX (mitigated by try/catch + sendBeacon).
- Base-rate blindness on low-traffic LAN instances (mitigated by insufficient-data gate).

Acceptance:
- docs/adr/ADR-006-frontend-error-telemetry.md exists, follows existing ADR format (ADR-001, ADR-004, ADR-005).
- Status: accepted.
- Links: i6a1m, 5uxwh (alerting posture), SRE/security-engineer/it-architect spike findings.
- PR merged to dev.

Size: Small (doc-only, encodes a decision already made).
close_reason: Merged via PR #168 — docs/adr/ADR-006-frontend-error-telemetry.md landed, encoding PO-accepted Phase 1 architecture. Unblocks i6a1m implementation.

title: BE test drift (SPA fallback): 9 tests in event_loop_responsiveness + backup path-injection fail in container
description:
Surfaced while clearing enhancedchannelmanager-0gcu9. Root cause is the same as 0gcu9 item #2 (SPA fallback "/{full_path:path}" registers only when backend/static/ exists — present in ecm-ecm-1 container, absent in CI), but it affects 9 additional tests across 2 files that the original bead did not cover.

Failures (all deterministic in ecm-ecm-1, green in CI):

tests/integration/test_event_loop_responsiveness.py::TestRequestTimeoutMiddleware::test_slow_handler_returns_504
- Test dynamically registers /api/_test_stall_for_timeout after app startup. The SPA catch-all registered at import time is earlier in the route table, so it wins the match and returns 200 instead of letting the stalling handler trigger the 504 timeout middleware.

tests/routers/test_backup.py::TestSavedBackupsPathInjection (8 params across test_download_rejects_traversal_payloads + test_delete_rejects_traversal_payloads):
- URL-encoded slash payloads (%2Fetc%2Fpasswd, ..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd, ...) decode to multi-segment paths that can never match {filename}, so they fall through to the SPA catch-all. Test expects 400/404/422 (router-level rejection) but gets 405 (GET-only catch-all rejects DELETE, and the SPA-path winning the route match blocks the backup router from rejecting at all).
- Security note: the traversal payload IS rejected at the routing layer — never reaches the backup handler. This is not a bypass, just a test expectation mismatch vs. container behavior.

Suggested fixes (all Small):
1. test_event_loop_responsiveness: register the stall route BEFORE the SPA fallback, or register it via monkeypatch.setattr on app.router.routes at index 0 (prepend).
2. test_backup TestSavedBackupsPathInjection: add 405 to the accepted reject codes, or (better) design the backup route so it handles URL-encoded slashes explicitly before the SPA catch-all. The test assertion list should document that 405 is an acceptable rejection.

Acceptance:
- All 9 failures either pass in ecm-ecm-1 container or are restructured to be robust against SPA-fallback presence.
- pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e is fully green in ecm-ecm-1 without --deselect.
- This combined with 0gcu9 closure is the prerequisite QA was asking for to unblock the v0.16.0 dep-bump epic.
close_reason: Implemented and merged via PR #174. Pre-fix: 25 failed / 2934 passed. Post-fix: 11 failed / 2971 passed (-14 targeted failures cleared — 8 backup path-injection, 6 export path-injection variants from same SPA root cause, plus 2 stall-route tests from event_loop_responsiveness). Remaining 11 failures are pre-existing test drift unrelated to SPA — will file separate bead for journal/auto_creation/mcp_status/tags metadata drift.

title: mcp-server tools __init__.py imports nonexistent ffmpeg/tasks modules
description:
## Context
Discovered during bd-kdsn3 (CodeQL note-level cleanup) when verifying mcp-server module imports after touching tools/{channels,channel_groups,epg,m3u,notifications,profiles,stats}.py.

## Symptom
\`\`\`
$ python -c "from tools import register_all_tools"
ImportError: cannot import name 'ffmpeg' from partially initialized module 'tools'
\`\`\`

## Root Cause
mcp-server/tools/__init__.py lines 4-19 imports modules \`ffmpeg\` and \`tasks\` that do not exist in \`mcp-server/tools/\`:
\`\`\`
$ ls mcp-server/tools/
auto_creation.py  channel_groups.py  channels.py  epg.py  export.py  __init__.py  m3u.py  normalization.py  notifications.py  profiles.py  __pycache__  stats.py  streams.py  system.py  tasks.py
\`\`\`
Wait — \`tasks.py\` exists. \`ffmpeg.py\` does NOT. The error message says ffmpeg.

## Fix Options
1. Create the missing \`tools/ffmpeg.py\` with a stub \`register(mcp)\` function (and remove from __init__.py if no FFmpeg MCP tools are planned).
2. Remove \`ffmpeg\` from both the import and \`_MODULES\` lists in __init__.py.

## Why P2
This means \`register_all_tools()\` is currently broken — the MCP server would fail to start when the registration function runs. Either:
- The MCP server has been broken at startup since this __init__.py was added, OR
- There's another entry point that registers tools individually that I haven't found.

Needs investigation before choosing fix #1 vs #2. Verify whether MCP server is actually starting in production.

Found-via: bd-kdsn3
close_reason: Merged via PR #165 (rolled in alongside 0gcu9) — mcp-server/tools/__init__.py orphan ffmpeg import removed; python -c 'from tools import register_all_tools' now succeeds.

title: Refactor cyclic-import topology: extract shared Base module + cloud_storage factory split
description:
## Context
Deferred from bd-kdsn3 (CodeQL note-level cleanup). 15 py/cyclic-import findings exist that require non-mechanical refactoring to resolve. Per orchestration discipline, mechanical-only cleanup deferred architectural refactor here.

## Findings (15 total)
### Cluster A: cloud_storage factory pattern (8)
- backend/cloud_storage/base.py:90,93,96,99 — get_adapter() factory imports concrete adapters lazily
- backend/cloud_storage/{s3,gdrive,onedrive,dropbox}_adapter.py — each imports cloud_storage.base for ABC + dataclasses

This is a classic factory cycle: base defines the abstract class + factory; concrete adapters inherit from base. The factory's lazy `from cloud_storage.X import` inside the function body breaks runtime cycle but CodeQL still flags it.

**Fix options:**
1. Extract factory into `cloud_storage/factory.py` so base.py has no cyclic deps.
2. Extract data types (UploadResult, ConnectionTestResult, CloudStorageAdapter ABC) into `cloud_storage/types.py`; let base.py be just the factory.

### Cluster B: database.py <-> models.py / export_models.py / normalization_migration.py (7)
- backend/database.py:129 imports models
- backend/database.py:130 imports export_models
- backend/database.py:315 imports normalization_migration
- backend/models.py:9 imports database (circular)
- backend/export_models.py:9 imports database (circular)
- backend/normalization_migration.py:15,285 imports models (circular)

Models import `Base` from database; database imports models for table registration on init. Standard SQLAlchemy footgun.

**Fix:** Extract the SQLAlchemy `Base = declarative_base()` into `backend/db_base.py`. Both database.py and models.py import from db_base; models no longer needs database, breaking the cycle. Same for export_models.py and normalization_migration.py.

## Out of Scope
- Mechanical CodeQL cleanups (bd-kdsn3, in progress)

## Acceptance
- [ ] All 15 py/cyclic-import findings resolved (verified by next CodeQL run on the affected files)
- [ ] No runtime regression (full backend test suite passes)
- [ ] Consultation with IT Architect before merging — import topology change touches every model
close_reason: Landed via PR #172 (merge commit dabbb65c) on dev. Cluster A: cloud_storage/base.py split into types.py (ABC + dataclasses) and factory.py (get_adapter); external callers import from cloud_storage package root. Cluster B: declarative_base() extracted to backend/db_base.py; database.py re-exports for BC, models.py + export_models.py import from db_base directly. All 15 py/cyclic-import CodeQL findings resolved. CI green: Backend Tests, Frontend Tests, CodeQL Python, CodeQL JS, Semgrep. Rebased twice onto origin/dev (dead-import cleanup conflicts in publish_pipeline.py + 2 test files, resolved by taking dev's cleanup + refactor's new import path). Unblocks 0i2vt.4 and skqln.2.

title: PO decision: 6rrl5 dep-bump epic ~9-week cadence vs v0.16.0 release window
description:
Surfaced by bd-6rrl5.4 spike (PR #151). At ADR-001's 7-day-per-major cadence × 9 majors (6 frontend + 3 backend = TS6, React 19, Vite 8, eslint 10, jsdom 29, @dnd-kit 10, fastapi 0.137+, uvicorn, starlette 1.0), the full 6rrl5 epic is a ~9-week minimum.

Three options for the PO:

(a) Fit into current v0.16.0 release window — delay v0.16.0 cut by ~9 weeks until epic completes. Single coherent release; integrators see all dep updates together. Cost: long delay before next user-facing release.

(b) Cut v0.16.0 first on current scope (everything shipped through v0.16.0-0056) — run dep-bump epic in v0.17.x window. Faster user value delivery; dep bumps are an internal/operational release. Cost: two release cycles in close succession.

(c) Mixed: ship safe + lower-risk bumps (jsdom canary per ADR-001, possibly the backend triplet) in v0.16.0; defer larger frontend ecosystem bumps (React 19 + Vite 8 + plugin-react 6 + TS 6 + eslint 10) to v0.17.x. Cost: epic scope split; bookkeeping overhead.

This is a scope/sequencing decision — no engineering work, just PO determination. Once decided, the chosen path becomes the operating plan for the epic.

Related beads: 6rrl5 (epic), 6rrl5.4 (compat spike that surfaced this), 6rrl5.3 (baseline that any decision still needs).

title: Phase 2 automation: mechanical G1a + G1b + G5 + G6 + G7 verification on release-cut PRs (depends on bd in CI for G1a)
description:
Automate the manually-verified pre-cut gate items from ADR-004 §3 via a GitHub Action that runs on release-cut PRs (PRs whose title matches the regex ^Release v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ AND whose head branch matches ^release/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$).

## Mechanically-verifiable gates

| Gate | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| G1a | Run 'bd list --status open --priority 0' and 'bd list --status open --priority 1' against the cut SHA — both must be empty, OR every open item must be cited by ID in the PR description's 'G1a Justifications' section | **Requires 'bd' available in CI** — the dependency. Either a 'bd' container image, a Go binary fetched in the action step, or the beads project's published action if one exists. |
| G1b | 'gh api repos/:owner/:repo/code-scanning/alerts --paginate | jq …' — must return 0 OR every open alert is cited by alert number + dismissal category in the PR description's 'G1b Waivers' section per docs/shipping.md G1b 'formally waived' semantics | Easier than G1a; 'gh' is already available in actions. The PR-description parsing is the harder half. |
| G5 | Diff CHANGELOG.md between the PR head and 'main'; assert (a) a [Unreleased] section is present + empty, (b) a [X.Y.Z] section (matching the PR title's version) is present with today's date | Pure file diff + regex; no external state. |
| G6 | Parse 'frontend/package.json' on the PR head; assert version == X.Y.Z (extracted from PR title / branch name) | Trivial. |
| G7 | 'gh pr list --base main --state open --json number,title' — must return only the PR being checked (or that PR + a hotfix PR with the hotfix-priority tiebreaker handled) | Trivial; runs at merge-time, not PR-open-time, to avoid race windows. |

G2, G3, G4 are already mechanically enforced via branch protection required checks + Code Scanning merge protection rule (per ADR-005). No new automation needed for those.

## Implementation sketch

- New workflow: '.github/workflows/release-cut-gate.yml'
- Trigger: 'pull_request' (opened, synchronize, edited) AND 'pull_request_review' if needed for the merge-time G7 re-check.
- Job: 'release-cut-gate' — only runs when 'github.event.pull_request.title' matches the release-cut regex.
- Steps: install 'bd' (G1a), run each gate check, post a check-run with per-gate pass/fail, optionally post a sticky PR comment summarizing which gates pass and which require justification.
- Block merge: register the 'release-cut-gate' check as a required status check on 'main' branch protection (additive to ADR-005's CodeQL checks). Hotfix PRs are exempt because their branch name does not match 'release/v…'.

## Out of scope

- Hotfix-PR gate automation (different scope subset; if needed, file a separate follow-on).
- CHANGELOG content quality lint (ADR-004 §Implementation Sketch §3 lists this as 'separate docs-tooling bead if desired'; not bundled here).
- Auto-creating the release-cut PR or auto-promoting CHANGELOG (still PO-authored).

## Dependencies

- BLOCKED ON: 'bd' available in CI runner. If beads doesn't yet ship a GitHub Action or installable binary suitable for CI, file a sub-bead to address that first.
- Soft dependency on bd-tvlxz item 5 (G1b 'formally waived' semantics) — already landed in docs/shipping.md; the automation needs to parse PR description per that semantics.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Release-cut-gate workflow lives at '.github/workflows/release-cut-gate.yml'.
- [ ] All five gates (G1a, G1b, G5, G6, G7) report individual pass/fail status in the PR check-runs.
- [ ] At least one synthetic-PR test demonstrates each gate failing and then passing.
- [ ] 'release-cut-gate' added to 'main' branch protection required checks (in addition to ADR-005's existing CodeQL + tests checks).
- [ ] docs/shipping.md updated to note that Phase 2 enforcement is now active and the manual checklist is now a redundant safety net (kept for the cut-authorizer to read, no longer the primary gate).

## References

- ADR-004 §4 ("Implementation Sketch" / "Out of scope" — Phase 2 automation explicitly punted to follow-on bead)
- ADR-004 §Sequencing & Rollout item 5 ("Month 2+ — Phase 2 automation (separate bead)")
- bd-tvlxz item 6 (this bead's parent task)
- docs/shipping.md §Pre-Cut Gate Checklist (semantics being automated)

title: ADR-005 audit cadence: extend to PO-downgrade detection + allow_force_pushes flip events
description:
Extend ADR-005's monthly/quarterly dismissal-log audit cadence (per ADR-005 Dismiss-With-Comment Policy item 6) to absorb two new audit scopes surfaced by ADR-004 §Interaction with ADR-005:

## Scope 1: PO-downgrade detection (G1a escape-hatch surveillance)

Surface any release-cut PR where a P1 bug was downgraded to P2 (or lower) by the PO within the 30 days prior to the cut SHA. Catches the authorized-but-risky G1a bypass pattern that ADR-004's 'or each justified in PR' escape-hatch permits — a downgrade IS authorized, but a recurring pattern of downgrade-immediately-before-cut is a signal that the gate is being culturally weakened.

Implementation hint: query 'bd' history for status/priority transitions on each P1-bound bug, cross-reference with the cut SHA timestamp on the release-cut PR. May require a small bd-history shell helper if the audit becomes more than ad-hoc.

## Scope 2: allow_force_pushes flip-event audit

Periodically review the GitHub repo audit log for 'allow_force_pushes' flip events on the 'main' branch protection rule (per ADR-004 §Interaction with ADR-005 item 3). Every legitimate flip corresponds to an authorized rollback bead (e.g., the v0.16.0 rollback, bd-vgm4l); anything else is investigated. Cadence: fold into the existing monthly-then-quarterly dismissal audit so we don't add a separate cadence to maintain.

Implementation hint: 'gh api /repos/:owner/:repo/audit-log' or the GitHub Settings → Audit log UI. Filter on action='protected_branch.update' and inspect the diff for allow_force_pushes toggling. Cross-reference each true → false (and false → true) flip with an authorized rollback bead; flag any flips lacking a corresponding bead.

## Rationale

ADR-004 created two new operational surfaces that ADR-005's existing audit cadence does not currently cover. Rather than file a separate audit cadence, extend the existing one — same persona (Security Engineer per ADR-005, with SRE coordination per ADR-004), same cadence (monthly for the first quarter post-Phase-3, then quarterly), same artifact (audit bead per cycle).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Monthly audit checklist (per ADR-005 item 6) extended to include both new scopes.
- [ ] First audit cycle after this bead lands includes both scopes; findings filed as separate beads if any.
- [ ] If 'gh api' audit log access requires an org-admin PAT not currently provisioned, file a sub-bead to obtain it before the next audit cycle.

## References

- ADR-004 §Interaction with ADR-005 (items 3 and 4)
- ADR-005 §Dismiss-With-Comment Policy item 6 (existing audit cadence)
- bd-tvlxz item 4 (this bead's parent task)
- bd-kgjci (ADR-005 implementation; Phase 5 calls for first monthly audit bead)

title: CI: doc-only PRs blocked by required CodeQL checks (paths-ignore + branch protection chicken-and-egg)
description:
Surfaced by PR #139 (bd-pf82j). .github/workflows/build.yml and test.yml use paths-ignore: '**.md', so doc-only PRs trigger zero CI. But dev branch protection requires 5 checks (Backend Tests, Frontend Tests, CodeQL Analysis (python), CodeQL Analysis (javascript-typescript), Semgrep Lint). Result: doc-only PRs are unmergeable without admin override or hacky code-touch.

Approaches (engineer picks based on what's smallest + safest):
(a) Remove '**.md' from paths-ignore — full CI on every doc PR; correct but slow
(b) Add a sentinel 'docs-only-pass' workflow that triggers on paths: '**.md' and emits check-runs matching the required names with success — preserves CI economy; requires careful name matching across multiple jobs (RECOMMENDED)
(c) dorny/paths-filter inside existing workflows to no-op the heavy steps for doc-only PRs

Constraint: must not silently mask real CI failures on mixed PRs (any non-docs path in a PR must trigger real CI). Approach (b) needs paths/paths-ignore to be mutually exclusive between the sentinel workflow and the main workflows.

Verification: open a test PR with only a CHANGELOG.md edit and confirm it merges cleanly with all 5 required checks satisfied. Then verify a mixed PR (docs + .py) still gets the real checks, not the sentinel.

Directly blocks PR #139 today; affects every future doc-only PR (api.md updates, runbook additions, CHANGELOG ceremony, ADR drafts).

Effort: ~1-2 hours including verification on real test PRs.

User value (DX): doc improvements ship without ceremony or workarounds.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #141. New .github/workflows/docs-only-pass.yml emits the 5 required check-runs (Backend Tests, Frontend Tests, Semgrep Lint, CodeQL Analysis (python+javascript-typescript) via matrix) for doc-only PRs matching paths: ['**.md', '.beads/**']. Path filter is the strict complement of build.yml/test.yml's paths-ignore. Mixed-PR safety verified live: PR #141 itself triggered real CI (workflow file is not a doc path), confirming sentinel does not mask real failures. Unblocks PR #139 (api.md backfill from bd-pf82j) once its branch updates pick up the sentinel.

title: GH-59: Providers panel (6th panel in Stats tab, 4 visualizations)
description:
Ship the GH-59 "Providers" panel as the 6th panel in the Stats tab, delivering all 4 visualizations the reporter asked for.

## User outcome

Operator opens Stats tab → scrolls to Providers section → sees 4 charts answering "which upstream providers are performing well vs poorly" → makes data-driven keep/drop decision at renewal.

## Panel contents (4 visualizations per GH-59)

1. **Buffering events by provider** — multi-series time-series (one line per provider). Data: `/api/stats/providers/buffering` (skqln.15).
2. **Time spent watching each provider** — stacked area chart showing cumulative watch time per provider, with total at top. Data: `/api/stats/providers/watch-time`.
3. **Channels-by-provider heat map** — 2D grid: rows=providers, cols=top-N channels, cell=watch time. Data: `/api/stats/providers/channel-heatmap`. Uses heatmap primitive from skqln.16.
4. **Bitrate by provider over time** — multi-series time-series of computed bitrate (bytes/sec). Data: `/api/stats/providers/bitrate`.

## UI details

- Window selector: 7d / 30d / 90d (shared across all 4 charts in the panel).
- NULL provider_id rows surface as "Unknown" bucket with a tooltip explaining pre-cutover attribution gap.
- Panel placement: 6th stacked section in `frontend/src/components/tabs/StatsTab.tsx`, after the Users panel (skqln.6).
- Stats tab IA stays flat (no sub-nav) — UX flagged this as pressure toward the deferred sub-nav refactor; accept for v0.17.0 and revisit in v0.18.0.

## Blocks / blocked by

- Blocked by: skqln.15 (all 4 APIs), skqln.16 (heatmap + palette primitives)
- Blocks: 39ao6 (user-facing tracker closes when this ships + skqln.15 ships)

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 4 charts render against live session_telemetry data
- [ ] Window selector switches all 4 charts in sync
- [ ] "Unknown" provider bucket is visible and tooltipped
- [ ] Accessibility: all charts meet WCAG 1.4.1 (color not sole channel) — tooltips, patterns, or value overlays carry meaning
- [ ] Responsive: panel degrades gracefully at <1024px (charts stack or scroll, heatmap uses skqln.16's responsive fallback)
- [ ] Vitest component tests: data-mapping correctness for each chart from API payload → rendered series
- [ ] No regression on Users panel (skqln.6) rendering or perf

title: Chart primitives: heatmap component + colorblind-safe categorical palette for provider series (GH-59)
description:
Build the chart primitives that GH-59 needs but the rest of ECM doesn't have yet. Recharts 3.8.1 (`frontend/package.json`) has no first-class heatmap, and ECM has no categorical color scale for multi-series charts.

## Scope (UX flagged as "chart primitives sub-initiative in disguise")

1. **Heatmap component** — 2D grid visualization for Channels-by-Provider. 2. **Categorical color scale** — colorblind-safe palette tokens for up to ~15 providers. Adopt Okabe-Ito or Paul Tol's "bright" qualitative palette; define tokens in frontend design-system stylesheet.
3. **Multi-series legend** — reusable legend component that handles N categorical series with truncation and hover emphasis.
4. **Numeric overlay for heatmap cells** — per UX's WCAG 1.4.1 requirement: color must not be the sole channel carrying meaning. Cells render their numeric value on hover + high-contrast label overlay when color contrast is insufficient.

## What this is NOT (explicit de-scoping)

- NOT a Stats-tab IA redesign. Primitives must work inside the existing flat-stack Stats tab (see UX finding: 8+ sibling sections already).

title: GH-59: 4 provider-stats read API endpoints (buffering, watch-time, heatmap, bitrate)
description:
Ship 4 read-API endpoints backing the GH-59 Providers panel. All aggregate from `session_telemetry` with `provider_id` grouping.

## Endpoints

1. **`GET /api/stats/providers/buffering`** — time-series of buffer_event_count grouped by (provider_id, time_bucket). Query params: `window` (7d/30d/90d), `bucket` (hour/day).
2. **`GET /api/stats/providers/watch-time`** — total watch time per provider over window. Aggregates `SUM(poll_interval_ms)` grouped by provider_id.
3. **`GET /api/stats/providers/channel-heatmap`** — 2D grid: rows=providers, cols=channels, cell=SUM(bytes_delta). Caps at top-N channels to keep payload bounded (config: N=50 default).
4. **`GET /api/stats/providers/bitrate`** — derived bitrate time-series per provider. Computes `SUM(bytes_delta) / SUM(poll_interval_ms) * 8` per (provider_id, time_bucket).

## Indexes used

Per skqln.2 (amended by this epic): `(provider_id, observed_at)` for queries 1/2/4; `(provider_id, channel_id, observed_at) INCLUDE (bytes_delta)` covering index for heatmap (query 3). DBA flagged ~10–15% write-overhead cost for the additional index on the hot write path — accepted for GH-59.

## Handling NULL provider_id

Rows with NULL provider_id (pre-cutover data, resolver gaps) surface as a synthesized "Unknown" provider bucket. Do not exclude — operators need to see the attribution gap.

## Blocks / blocked by

- Blocked by: skqln.2, skqln.3, skqln.13, skqln.14
- Blocks: skqln.17 (frontend panel)

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 4 endpoints return correct aggregates against a 5M-row seeded fixture with 3 providers
- [ ] Response payloads match frontend contract (documented inline with skqln.17)
- [ ] pytest-benchmark gate (skqln.10, amended) shows p95 < 800ms for each endpoint against seeded fixture
- [ ] Property-based test: SUM of per-provider watch-time = SUM of per-user watch-time (same universe)
- [ ] NULL-provider bucket surfaces as "Unknown" and is not silently excluded
- [ ] Auth: endpoints require authenticated user (follow existing `/api/stats/*` middleware)

title: Buffer-event ingestion: wire Dispatcharr system events into session_telemetry.buffer_event_count (GH-59)
description:
Wire Dispatcharr buffering/system events into `session_telemetry.buffer_event_count` so GH-59's "buffering events by provider" chart has real data.

## Why net-new (Engineer's finding)

`backend/dispatcharr_client.py:984-991` (`get_channel_stats_detail`) returns "buffer status" per-client, and `get_system_events` at line 993-1012 emits buffering events. **Neither is called from `BandwidthTracker._collect_stats` today** — it only polls `get_channel_stats`. The `buffer_event_count` column in skqln.2's schema exists but has no writer.

## Scope

1. Decide: fold buffer-event polling into `_collect_stats` (single poll path, keeps skqln.3's single-write invariant) OR add a sibling poller (separate cadence for system-events stream). Default to folding into `_collect_stats` to minimize moving parts.
2. Idempotency / dedup: system events stream may re-deliver events. De-duplicate by event_id or (channel_id, client_id, event_ts) within a poll window.
3. Attribute each buffer event to the correct `provider_id` using skqln.13's resolver.
4. Increment `session_telemetry.buffer_event_count` per (session_id, observed_at) bucket.

## Blocks / blocked by

- Blocked by: skqln.2, skqln.3, skqln.13 (uses the resolver)
- Blocks: skqln.15 (buffering-by-provider endpoint needs populated column)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Buffer events flow from Dispatcharr → session_telemetry within one poll cycle of occurrence
- [ ] Dedup test: same event delivered twice → count increments once
- [ ] Unit test: buffer event on failover stream attributes to the active provider at event time, not poll time
- [ ] No p95 latency regression on poll cycle

title: BandwidthTracker: active-stream → provider resolver for per-poll provider tagging (GH-59)
description:
Add active-stream → provider resolver inside BandwidthTracker so every per-poll `session_telemetry` row gets a non-NULL `provider_id`. This is the write-side companion to the forward-compat column in skqln.2 and the "schedule-killer" the grooming team identified.

## Why this is non-trivial (Engineer's finding)

`backend/bandwidth_tracker.py:272-394` (`_collect_stats`) currently keys only on `channel_id` / `channel_number` / `client_ip`. Dispatcharr exposes `m3u_account` per-stream (`backend/dispatcharr_client.py:282-321`), but **channels have failover across multiple streams across multiple providers**. Per-poll provider attribution requires resolving: "active stream for channel N at time T → that stream's `m3u_account_id`." That resolver does not exist today.

## Scope

1. Extract or extend a resolver: given a channel in `_collect_stats`, determine the currently active stream and return its `m3u_account_id` (→ `provider_id` via M3U-to-provider mapping).
2. Handle NULL resolution gracefully: log a counter when provider cannot be resolved (falls back to `provider_id = NULL` on write, surfaces as "Unknown" in provider panel).
3. Cache resolution results within a single poll cycle to avoid N Dispatcharr round-trips per poll.
4. Emit a `data_consistency_sli` metric: % of rows with non-NULL provider_id per poll (for skqln.12 observability scope).

## Blocks / blocked by

- Blocked by: skqln.2 (schema migration), skqln.3 (BandwidthTracker single-write refactor — this rides on the refactor, not a separate write path)
- Blocks: skqln.14 (buffer-event ingest shares resolver pattern), skqln.15 (read APIs assume provider_id populated)

## Hidden work (pre-flagged)

- Dispatcharr `/proxy/ts/status` payload may not name the active stream directly; may require cross-referencing `/channels/<id>/streams` + client-session correlation.
- Backfill of historical `channel_watch_stats` rows into `session_telemetry` with NULL `provider_id` is acceptable (can't recover history) — provider panel will show "Unknown" bucket for pre-cutover data. Document this in skqln.11 runbook.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Resolver returns `provider_id` (or NULL) for every channel in every poll
- [ ] ≥95% of polls successfully resolve provider_id under steady state (SLI target; tune post-deploy)
- [ ] Unit tests: resolver correctness for single-stream, failover, stream-not-yet-resolved, and no-active-stream cases
- [ ] Integration test: 5-minute poll cycle against seeded fixture with 3 providers produces expected provider_id distribution
- [ ] No p95 latency regression on `_collect_stats` (pytest-benchmark gate from skqln.10 passes)

title: Auto-creation /run endpoints → background-task pattern (202 + poll)
description:
Current state: POST /api/auto-creation/run and POST /api/auto-creation/rules/{id}/run execute the pipeline synchronously inside the request coroutine. On large catalogs this can take minutes, which is why we just exempted /api/auto-creation/ from the 30s request-timeout middleware (bd-zv6pi hotfix). That exemption removes defense-in-depth on all auto-creation endpoints.

Move fetchExecutions() to a finally so the UI always refetches post-attempt. That cleanup pairs well with the polling change but can be shipped standalone too.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
# bd-eio04.11 — ReDoS Detector Spike Report

**Decision:** Use the hand-rolled AST walker. Do not adopt `redos-detector` (npm-only)
or `regexploit` (PyPI, stale).

## 1. Corpus

**Sources:** `/config/journal.db` in `ecm-ecm-1` (8 normalization rules, 3 auto-creation
rules, 1 dummy-EPG profile) + regex-literal patterns harvested from `backend/tests/**`.

**Size:** 32 unique patterns (user-input syntax, i.e. pre `(?<name>...)` → `(?P<name>...)`
conversion). The real production rule DB is sparse — the meaningful regex surface area
today is almost entirely the dummy-EPG `title_pattern` / `time_pattern` / `date_pattern`
fields.

**Example real-production patterns:**
- `(?<channel>.+?):\s+(?<event>(?:(?<sport>.+?)\s+\|\s+(?<team1>.+?)\s+vs\s+(?<team2>.+?))|(?:.+?))\s+@\s+`
- `(?<hour>\d{1,2})(?:\s*:\s*(?<minute>\d{2}))?\s*(?<ampm>[AaPp][Mm])(?:\s+(?<timezone>[A-Z]{1,5}))?`
- `(?<month>Jan|Feb|...|\d{1,2})[/\s]\s*(?<day>\d{1,2})(?:[/,\s]+(?<year>\d{2,4}))?`

Full list: `/tmp/bd-eio04.11-rule-corpus.txt`

## 2. Library landscape

| Candidate | PyPI? | Last release | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| `redos-detector` | **No — npm only** | 2026-02-14 (npm) | Not usable from Python without shelling out to Node. Brief assumed a Python pkg; there isn't one with that name. |
| `regexploit` (doyensec) | Yes | **2021-03-11** (5 years stale) | Only maintained Python ReDoS AST-analyzer on PyPI. Models `re.sre` but with limitations noted below. |
| Hand-rolled on `re._parser` | n/a | Stdlib (always current) | ~60 LoC, zero deps, already matches how our engine actually parses. |

Given `redos-detector` is npm-only, the binary choice in the brief is effectively
`regexploit` vs hand-rolled.

## 3. Results

### Run setup
- Both detectors receive the user-syntax pattern and apply our own
  `_js_to_python_named_groups` conversion (same helper used at runtime in
  `backend/dummy_epg_engine.py`).
- `regexploit` was run at its **most-sensitive** setting (any finding = flag; default
  CLI uses `starriness > 2`). This gives it every chance.
- Hand-rolled walker only flags **nested unbounded quantifier with a trailing
  killer** — this precisely matches the shape Python's `re` engine is actually
  vulnerable to. Bare `(a*)*` and similar are not flagged because Python's engine
  optimizes them away (verified empirically below).

### Numbers

| Set | n | Hand-rolled flagged | `regexploit` flagged | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| **Real corpus (benign — must not flag)** | 32 | **0 (0 FP)** | **1 (1 FP)** | `regexploit` flagged the B1G production `title_pattern`. |
| **Known-evil with killer (must flag)** | 7 | **7/7** | 7/7 | Both detectors equal. |
| **Ambiguous no-killer (Python optimizes — should not flag)** | 3 | 0 | 0 | Both detectors equal. |
| **Total time for 42 patterns** | | 0.97 ms | 4.05 ms | Hand-rolled ~4× faster. |

### The one `regexploit` false positive

```
(?<channel>.+?):\s+(?<event>(?:(?<sport>.+?)\s+\|\s+(?<team1>.+?)\s+vs\s+(?<team2>.+?))|(?:.+?))\s+@\s+
```
(Dummy-EPG profile #1, `B1G Advanced EPG` — currently in production.)

`regexploit` reports `starriness=3`. Empirical verification on stdlib `re`:

| Input | Length | Match time |
|-|-|-|
| `ESPN: Football \| Lions vs Tigers @ 10pm` | 39 ch | 0.1 ms |
| 200× `a` (no `@` terminator) | 200 ch | 0.1 ms |
| Adversarial `x`s with spurious `: vs vs vs …` | 393 ch | 2.6 ms |

Not exploitable. `regexploit` misses that the inner `.+?` repeats are **lazy**; it
over-counts their contribution to `starriness`. This is the specific false positive
shape the bead brief called out as a "one-way door" — rejecting a pattern that has
worked in production.

### Known-evil patterns both detectors flag (TPs at parity)

All of these are **confirmed exploitable** in stdlib `re` — verified with 5 s timeouts:

| Pattern | Observed on 22–30 chars |
|-|-|
| `(a+)+b` | 195 ms |
| `(a*)*b` | HANG (> 5 s) |
| `(.*)*X` | HANG |
| `(a+)*b` | 1553 ms |
| `(.+)+X` | 3099 ms |
| `^(\w+\s?)*$` | HANG at 25 ch |
| `(\w+)+$` | HANG |

Both detectors catch all seven. Hand-rolled reports `nested-unbounded-repeat-with-killer`;
`regexploit` reports `starriness=11` on each.

### Patterns intentionally NOT flagged (shared correct behavior)

Verified with Python's `re` engine — these do **not** ReDoS in production because
Python's engine either optimizes or factors them:

| Pattern | Python behavior |
|-|-|
| `(a*)*` | No backtracking; optimized to O(n). |
| `(.*)*` | Same. |
| `(a\|a)+$` | Python `re._parser` factors `(a\|a)` to `a(\|)` — not ReDoS. |

Both detectors correctly pass these. Any detector that flagged them would produce
spurious FPs.

## 4. Recommendation

### Winner: Hand-rolled AST walker

**Why:**
1. **Zero false positives on the real corpus.** `regexploit` produced one — on a
   production-in-use pattern. For a save-time linter, that's the ticket-escalation
   scenario the bead called out as the critical failure mode.
2. **Identical true-positive coverage.** 7/7 on known-evil-with-killer controls,
   matched by regexploit.
3. **No external dependency.** `regexploit` hasn't had a release since 2021; adding
   a 5-year-stale dependency for ~60 LoC of logic is not a trade we'd justify to the
   code reviewer.
4. **~4× faster per pattern** (marginal at this scale, but relevant if the linter
   runs on every pattern write).
5. **Model matches our engine.** The hand-rolled walker uses `re._parser.parse` —
   exactly what `re.compile` calls. Any behavior it models IS how our engine behaves.
   `regexploit` ships its own parser that can drift.
6. **Maintenance locus.** We own it. If the model ever over- or under-flags, we edit
   the file; we don't file an issue on a dormant GitHub project.

**Caveats:**
- **Uses `re._parser`, which is a private stdlib module.** CPython has been stable on
  this API for years but it is technically private. Python 3.11 renamed the module
  from `sre_parse` to `re._parser`; the import should `try: import re._parser` then
  `except ImportError: import sre_parse`. The eval harness does exactly this.
- **Depends on `re._constants` for opcodes.** Same private-but-stable caveat. If
  this becomes a concern, the codes are small enums we could inline by name.
- **Does not detect ambiguous alternation** (e.g. `(aa|ab)+X`) as a distinct shape.
  However, Python's `re` engine's common-prefix factoring makes most realistic
  ambiguous-alternation patterns non-ReDoS in our engine; and regexploit at default
  threshold also misses them. If we need this coverage, it's ~15 extra LoC.
- **Does not detect exponential patterns that don't involve nested repeats** (rare
  in real life — e.g. `.*.*.*`-style in some engines). Python's `re` handles these
  fine via its NFA-with-memoization in 3.11+ so it's moot for us.

### Reference implementation (for bd-eio04.7 to lift)

The working reference is `/tmp/bd-eio04.11-eval.py`. The essential routine is:

```python
import re
try:
    import re._parser as sre_parse
    from re._constants import (
        MAX_REPEAT, MIN_REPEAT, SUBPATTERN, BRANCH, IN,
        LITERAL, NOT_LITERAL, CATEGORY, AT, ASSERT, ASSERT_NOT, MAXREPEAT,
    )
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover  (Python < 3.11)
    import sre_parse
    from sre_constants import (
        MAX_REPEAT, MIN_REPEAT, SUBPATTERN, BRANCH, IN,
        LITERAL, NOT_LITERAL, CATEGORY, AT, ASSERT, ASSERT_NOT, MAXREPEAT,
    )

_REPEAT_OPS = {MAX_REPEAT, MIN_REPEAT}


def _js_to_python_named_groups(pattern: str) -> str:
    """Match backend/dummy_epg_engine.py — handle (?<name>…) → (?P<name>…)."""
    if not pattern:
        return pattern
    return re.sub(r"\(\?<(?!\=|\!)", "(?P<", pattern)


def _is_unbounded(repeat_args) -> bool:
    _min, _max, _body = repeat_args
    return _max == MAXREPEAT


def _contains_unbounded_repeat(parsed) -> bool:
    for op, args in parsed:
        if op in _REPEAT_OPS and _is_unbounded(args):
            return True
        if op is SUBPATTERN:
            _gid, _a, _b, subp = args
            if _contains_unbounded_repeat(subp):
                return True
        elif op is BRANCH:
            _none, branches = args
            if any(_contains_unbounded_repeat(b) for b in branches):
                return True
        elif op in (ASSERT, ASSERT_NOT):
            _dir, subp = args
            if _contains_unbounded_repeat(subp):
                return True
    return False


def _has_post_killer(subp_tail) -> bool:
    """Anything after an unbounded repeat that can fail the match."""
    for op, args in subp_tail:
        if op in (LITERAL, NOT_LITERAL, IN, CATEGORY, AT):
            return True
        if op is SUBPATTERN:
            _gid, _a, _b, inner = args
            if _has_post_killer(inner):
                return True
        if op in _REPEAT_OPS:
            _min, _max, body = args
            if _min >= 1 and _has_post_killer(body):
                return True
    return False


def detect_redos(pattern: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (is_vulnerable, reason). False + "" means safe to accept.

    Flags ONLY nested unbounded quantifiers followed by a killer element
    that forces backtracking — the shape Python's re engine is actually
    vulnerable to.
    """
    try:
        converted = _js_to_python_named_groups(pattern)
        parsed = sre_parse.parse(converted)
    except re.error as e:
        return (False, f"syntax-error:{e}")  # let the caller handle syntax separately

    def walk(subp, outer_suffix_has_killer: bool) -> str | None:
        for idx, (op, args) in enumerate(subp):
            remainder = subp[idx + 1 :]
            local_killer = _has_post_killer(remainder) or outer_suffix_has_killer

            if op in _REPEAT_OPS:
                _min, _max, body = args
                if _is_unbounded((_min, _max, body)) \
                   and _contains_unbounded_repeat(body) \
                   and local_killer:
                    return "nested-unbounded-repeat-with-killer"
                r = walk(body, local_killer)
                if r:
                    return r
            elif op is SUBPATTERN:
                _gid, _a, _b, subp2 = args
                r = walk(subp2, local_killer)
                if r:
                    return r
            elif op is BRANCH:
                _none, branches = args
                for b in branches:
                    r = walk(b, local_killer)
                    if r:
                        return r
            elif op in (ASSERT, ASSERT_NOT):
                _dir, subp2 = args
                r = walk(subp2, False)  # lookarounds don't propagate outer killer
                if r:
                    return r
        return None

    reason = walk(parsed, outer_suffix_has_killer=False)
    return (reason is not None, reason or "")
```

**Integration note for bd-eio04.7:** Call `detect_redos` from the router save handler
for dummy-EPG profiles, normalization rules (when `condition_type == "regex"`), and
auto-creation `sort_regex`. Reject with HTTP 400 and a message pointing to the
documentation when `is_vulnerable` is `True`. Syntax errors are handled separately
by the existing `re.compile` path.

**Tests to include in bd-eio04.7:**
- All 7 known-evil-with-killer patterns → must reject.
- All 32 real-corpus patterns → must accept.
- All 3 ambiguous-no-killer patterns → must accept (Python optimizes).
- Empty / whitespace / None → accept.
- Malformed syntax → returns `syntax-error:` reason (caller decides handling — the
  existing compile step will catch these anyway).

## 5. One-liner

Hand-rolled: 0 FPs, 7/7 TPs, 60 LoC, zero deps.
`regexploit`: 1 FP (on a production pattern), 7/7 TPs, 5-year-stale dependency.
`redos-detector` (npm): not applicable to a Python backend.

title: Semgrep CI rule + style guide: prohibit bare re.* on user input
description:
Prevent regression of the ReDoS bug class by blocking dynamic-pattern re.* calls at review time.

Deliverables:
1. .semgrep.yml with rule 'no-bare-re-on-dynamic-pattern' that flags re.search/match/sub/compile when the first arg is not a raw string literal. Excludes tests/ and safe_regex.py itself.
2. Wire Semgrep into .github/workflows/test.yml as a required job.
3. Create docs/style_guide.md with a 'Regex' section:
   'User-supplied regex must use safe_regex, not re. Any regex where the pattern originates from the database, request body, settings, template, or any user-editable source must be evaluated through safe_regex. The re module is reserved for module-level constants compiled from hard-coded literals (convention: _UPPER_SNAKE_RE = re.compile(r"...")). safe_regex enforces a 500-character pattern cap and a 100ms evaluation timeout to defeat ReDoS. On timeout or invalid pattern it logs [SAFE_REGEX] at WARNING and returns the no-match sentinel — callers should treat this as did not match and continue.'
4. Rename the kwarg preserve_superscripts → preserve_numeric_superscripts (if any remains post-policy refactor) in same PR as the style guide lands.

title: Write-time pattern linting at persistence boundaries
description:
Reject pathological regex patterns at save time — cheaper than runtime timeout and catches issues at authoring.

Persistence boundaries:
- POST/PUT /api/normalization/rules — normalization rule condition_value and action value
- POST/PUT /api/auto-creation/rules — condition value, action pattern, sort_regex, name_transform_pattern
- POST/PUT /api/dummy-epg/rules — title_pattern, time_pattern, date_pattern, substitution find pairs

Validation:
- Reject if pattern length > 500 chars.
- Reject if static analyzer detects nested quantifier (e.g., (a+)+, (a*)*, (a|a)+). Use redos-detector library or small AST check.
- Reject if pattern fails to compile via safe_regex.compile.

One-time migration: scan existing rows in normalization_rules, auto_creation_rules, dummy_epg_rules for pre-lint rows that would now fail validation; flag in UI for user review. Do not auto-delete user data.

title: backend/safe_regex.py — shared safe-regex utility with ReDoS timeout
description:
New module backend/safe_regex.py providing search/match/sub/compile wrapping the 'regex' library (not stdlib 're') with per-call ReDoS protection.

API:
  safe_regex.search(pattern, text, *, flags=0, timeout_ms=100, max_pattern_len=500)
  safe_regex.match(pattern, text, *, flags=0, timeout_ms=100, max_pattern_len=500)
  safe_regex.sub(pattern, repl, text, *, flags=0, timeout_ms=100, max_pattern_len=500)
  safe_regex.compile(pattern, *, flags=0, max_pattern_len=500)
  class RegexTimeoutError(Exception)

Behavior:
- 100ms default timeout via regex library's timeout kwarg (best-effort in worker threads, which is acceptable given task-level budgets above).
- 500-char pattern length cap, matching existing template_engine.py MAX_REGEX_LEN precedent.
- On timeout or compilation error: log at WARNING with [SAFE_REGEX] prefix and return no-match sentinel (None for search/match, original text for sub). This matches the existing try/except re.error fallthrough in NormalizationEngine.
- Expose RegexTimeoutError for callers wanting strict mode.

Add 'regex' to backend dependencies. Follows existing shared-utility convention from backend/log_utils.py and backend/obfuscate.py.

Supersedes bd-tcegl.

title: Auto-creation: letter-superscripts (RAW/HD) not stripped; preserve_superscripts too coarse
description: Reporter: GH-104 thread. Symptom: Settings > Normalization 'Test' strips letter-superscripts (RAW, HD) correctly, but auto-creation rules leave them in created channel names. title: security: add RequireAdminIfEnabled to all normalization router endpoints
description:
Code Reviewer flagged during PR #107 review (GH-104 fix, bd-u9odj): backend/routers/normalization.py has **zero** endpoints with RequireAdminIfEnabled, despite several being destructive:

- POST /api/normalization/groups — creates new rule groups
- DELETE /api/normalization/rules/{id} — deletes rules
- POST /api/normalization/migration/run — runs migrations
- POST /api/normalization/import — imports rule config (arbitrary data ingest)
- POST /api/normalization/apply-to-channels — **rename + delete channels** (NEW in PR #107)

Pre-existing systemic gap; not PR-introduced. CR chose not to block PR #107 on this since adding auth to the whole router is scope creep on a bug-fix PR.

## Scope
Add RequireAdminIfEnabled to every mutating endpoint in backend/routers/normalization.py. Audit read endpoints (GET /groups, GET /rules) — likely OK without, but confirm.

## Acceptance
- All POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoints in normalization.py carry RequireAdminIfEnabled
- Tests added for 401/403 on non-admin caller for each endpoint
- No regression on admin flow

## Priority rationale
P2 (not P1) because:
- Auth is enforced at the router middleware level typically anyway
- Destructive endpoints are unlikely to be discovered + exploited by unauthenticated users
- Pre-existing, not urgent
- Should land soon after PR #107 but doesn't block it

## Source of finding
Code Reviewer subagent first-pass review of PR #107, 2026-04-22.

title: Phase 2: Restore-complete UX — overall summary + per-entity counts
description:
Render the aggregate-count response from the dry-run engine + real restore. For each entity show: created, updated, skipped (with reasons), failed (with reasons). For rollback scenarios, clearly label the state as 'restore failed — state rolled back' not 'success'.

Size: 1 day.

Source: ADR-008 D9 three-tier surfacing + Sequencing Phase 2.

User value: user sees exactly what changed and what did not at the end of a restore, not a generic 'restore complete' toast. Mirrors the dry-run preview so apply-vs-preview discrepancies are visible.

Success signal: UI renders the full per-entity breakdown on restore complete; rollback state is labeled correctly; mirrors the dry-run preview shape so users recognize it.
close_reason: Verified done: tri-state summary + per-entity counts mirroring dry-run shape, wired e2e via DbasRestoreModal; 15 tests green

title: Phase 2: Restore-complete UX — logo-miss red banner
description:
On the restore-complete screen, when channels_without_logo > 0, display a prominent RED banner (PO-specified UX treatment, 2026-04-21). Banner text names the count and links to a detail view listing the affected channels so the user can fix them one-off.

Source: ADR-008 D9 updated + Open Question 5 resolution.

User value: a restored channel with a missing logo looks identical to a correctly-restored channel at the API level (DBAS's silent-DEBUG pattern hides this). The red banner makes the problem unmissable at the moment the user sees the restore complete, when they can act on it. Closes the silent-data-quality bug DBAS ships today.

Success signal: banner fires on a test restore with 1+ logo miss; banner does NOT fire when all logos attached; detail view lists the correct affected channels with edit links that land on Dispatcharr's channel page.

title: Phase 2: Pre-flight validation + compensating-delete rollback
description:
Dispatcharr has no database transactions. Best-effort consistency is:
1. Pre-flight validation — validate the entire import plan (FK references resolvable, names unique where required, counts within reasonable bounds) BEFORE applying any changes.
2. Compensating-delete rollback — if an entity's apply step fails mid-run, track everything created up to that point and issue compensating DELETEs to restore the pre-restore state.

The restore-summary response surfaces partial state explicitly (which entities succeeded, which failed, which were rolled back) rather than reporting success when the state is actually mixed.

Size: 1-2 days.

Source: ADR-008 per-entity transactional safety row + Risks: 'Post-restore state drift on partial failure'.

User value: a restore that hits a Dispatcharr API error mid-run does not leave the user with a half-applied archive; either the restore completes or the rollback returns them to the starting state. Partial failures are visible, not silent.

Success signal: fault-injection test (simulated 500 from Dispatcharr at the midpoint of Channels import) triggers full compensating-delete rollback; restore summary correctly reports 'failed — rolled back' not 'success'.
close_reason: Verified done: unconditional preflight + reverse-order compensating-delete rollback, tri-state outcome never mislabeled success; 13 tests green

title: Phase 2: Schema version validation on restore
description:
Validate the schema_version field in the restore archive's manifest. Refuse unknown versions with user-facing message 'Unsupported backup version'; full version detail is logged server-side only (no schema-internals leakage in UI or HTTP error body — per D1 + S4).

ECM already has ecm_export.version infrastructure; extend to the DBAS-absorbed path.

Size: 0.5-1 day.

Source: ADR-008 D1 + S4.

User value: a user restoring a v0.19 archive on a v0.18 ECM sees 'Unsupported backup version' immediately instead of a silent partial restore that corrupts data. Closes the silent-drift failure mode that DBAS's current format has (no schema_version today).

Success signal: restore of a crafted archive with a higher schema_version than the running build is refused with the correct user-facing message; server log contains the actual version detail for operator troubleshooting.
close_reason: Verified done: version gate at restore-ingest chokepoint before any mutation, shared with preflight; 13 tests green

title: Phase 2: Dry-run engine (counts-only, default-ON for Dispatcharr restores)
description:
Aggregate per-entity, per-action counts: would-create, would-update, would-skip. Scope is counts-only; full entity-level diff tree deferred to v0.19.x per D7.

Default-ON for Dispatcharr restores — destructive-on-live-data risk is real; counts-only dry-run is a cheap guardrail. User can opt in to apply (not opt out of dry-run).

Size: 1-2 days.

Source: ADR-008 D7 + Alternative A-rejection (full diff tree too expensive for v0.18.0).

User value: before applying a restore, user sees 'would create 14 channels, update 203, skip 2 orphans, attach 187 logos (12 missing)' — answers the 'am I about to wreck my setup?' question with almost zero engineering cost vs. a full diff tree.

Success signal: dry-run produces correct counts on a known test archive; apply-after-dry-run result matches the counts dry-run predicted; toggle defaults to ON every time the restore UI opens.
