title: Phase 2: Logos importer — 3-tier match + bulk-delete + streaming upload + validation
description:
Logos has the largest memory/bandwidth profile in the restore. Implement per ADR-008 D8:
- Streaming upload pattern: read each logo file -> decode base64 -> pass bytes to upload_logo_file -> release before reading the next file. NOT a CumulativeMemoryTracker port (D8 leans streaming; re-evaluable at kickoff per implementation-time decisions).
- 3-tier match per logoMap contract: src:{source_id} (primary) -> name:{lowercased_original_name} (fallback 1) -> file:{sanitized_filename} (fallback 2).
- Bulk-delete pre-step to clear existing logos before upload.

Missing Dispatcharr client methods (must be added): bulk_delete_logos, get_all_logos_paginated.

Security validation (part of the 17-item STRIDE checklist + new addenda):
- 50MB per-logo cap.
- MIME magic-byte validation (reject mismatched-extension / disguised binaries).
- Path-traversal guard on ZIP extract (reject ../ or absolute paths in archive entries).
- Filename-basename validation (strip directory components).

Math: 50MB cap x 2000 logos = 100GB policy ceiling; streaming design must survive this without OOM.

Size: 4-6 days.

Source: ADR-008 D8 + Logos contract + Security Mandatory/STRIDE items.

User value: logos restore correctly at large archive sizes without OOMing the container; disguised binaries or path-traversal-crafted archives are rejected before extraction.

Success signal: 2000-logo archive restore completes under the streaming pattern without OOM; MIME + path-traversal attack corpus rejected; 3-tier match rate >95% on real backup data.
close_reason: Module-complete (40 tests green: 3-tier match, streaming upload, 50MB cap, MIME+traversal validation); apply-registry wiring moved to enhancedchannelmanager-kxcjf (PO decision 2026-07-25)

title: Phase 2: Channels importer with 4-tier stream matching + custom-stream fallback
description:
Channels is the most complex restore entity. Streams are embedded (not standalone). Implement the 4-tier stream-matching fallback chain (documented in sub-spike output) + custom-stream fallback (synthesizes a custom-stream M3U account for orphaned streams, with a WARN log on fallback path so operators see when the heuristic fires).

Missing Dispatcharr client method: create_stream (must be added). Verified present: update_profile_channel at dispatcharr_client.py:950.

Size: 4-5.5 days (Channels) + 1.5-2.5 days (embedded Streams) = ~5.5-8 days.

Source: ADR-008 Channels row + per-entity sizing.

User value: channels restore end-to-end with their correct stream attachments; orphaned streams do not vanish — they land in a custom-stream account where the user can triage them.

Success signal: 4-tier match rate >99% on a test archive with mixed stream states; custom-stream fallback fires with a WARN log and correctly attributes the orphans; update_profile_channel correctly reattaches channels to profiles post-create.
close_reason: Verified done: 4-tier stream match + custom-stream fallback, wired into real apply registry; 69 tests green. Production FK remaps depend on kxcjf wiring of groups/profiles

title: Phase 2: Bulk importer — user agents + core settings + plugins + DVR rules + comskip + users
description:
Restore the 6 net-new entity types (not previously in ECM's backup scope):
- User agents: ~4 missing Dispatcharr client methods (get/create/update/delete), 1-2 days.
- Core settings: ~2 missing methods (get/update), 1-2 days; consumes remap tables from upstream entities.
- Plugins: ~2 missing methods (get/create), 0.5-1 day; straight POST.
- DVR rules: ~3 missing methods (list/get/create), 0.5-1 day; requires channel ID remap.
- Comskip config: ~2 missing methods, 1 day; YAML/JSON format quirks.
- Users: ~1 missing method (create_user), 1-2 days; username uniqueness + password hash handling.

Size: ~5-7 days combined. All net-new in ECM.

Source: ADR-008 per-entity sizing table.

User value: users do not have to manually re-create user agents, adjust core settings, reinstall plugin configs, recreate DVR rules, or recreate admin users after a restore.

Success signal: each entity round-trips via backup/restore; core settings correctly consume remap tables so FK references point at the restored IDs, not the source-export IDs.
close_reason: Module-complete (29 tests green); plugins excluded per ADR-012 D10 (sanctioned), users split to closed bead l1p4p; apply+dry-run registry wiring moved to enhancedchannelmanager-kxcjf (PO decision 2026-07-25)

title: Phase 2: Bulk importer for channel groups + channel profiles + stream profiles
description:
Restore three related entities that feed Channels. ECM already has partial equivalents:
- backup.py:1051-1076 (channel groups)
- backup.py:1079-1097 (channel profiles)
- backup.py:1100-1122 (stream profiles)

Extend each to match ADR-008 scope and produce an ID-remap table (source-export ID -> destination ID) for downstream consumers (Channels, DVR Rules, Core Settings).

Size: ~3 days combined (Channel Groups: 1 day, Channel Profiles: 1 day, Stream Profiles: 1 day per ADR-008 per-entity table).

Source: ADR-008 per-entity sizing + ID-remap tables contract.

User value: Channel groups, profiles, and stream profiles restore before Channels import so foreign keys resolve on the first pass.

Success signal: remap tables correctly rewrite FKs when Channels importer runs; ECM's existing upsert-by-name logic for channel groups continues to work.
close_reason: Module-complete (29 tests green, remap-table producer verified); apply-registry wiring moved to enhancedchannelmanager-kxcjf (PO decision 2026-07-25)

title: Phase 2: EPG sources importer
description:
Restore EPG sources after M3U completes. Waits for Dispatcharr's EPG-data download to finish before reporting success (otherwise downstream Channels importer matches against an empty EPG).

Size: 1-2 days. Verify existing Dispatcharr client methods cover create/update/delete EPG source.

Source: ADR-008 per-entity sizing + sequencing-hard requirement (M3U BEFORE EPG).

User value: EPG sources restore with their URLs and refresh schedules; users do not manually re-add each source.

Success signal: EPG sources restore successfully; EPG-data download completes before Channels import begins (verified by polling or synchronous wait).
close_reason: Module-complete (14 tests green); apply-registry wiring + EPG-download-wait moved to enhancedchannelmanager-kxcjf (PO decision 2026-07-25)

title: Phase 2: M3U accounts importer (4-way group matching + deferred auto-sync)
description:
Restore M3U accounts with the patterns proven by DBAS:
- 4-way group matching (by ID, by name, by URL, by export-key).
- Deferred auto-sync pattern (extract settings on import; apply AFTER Channels + Logos finish — protects logo import from an auto-sync race on the Dispatcharr side).
- 2-stage refresh polling: status endpoint + stream-count-stable heuristic.
- is_active toggle workaround for the Dispatcharr quirk where newly-imported M3Us do not always trigger stream fetch.

Shape of the deferred settings return: deferredAutoSyncSettings: list[{m3u_account_id: int, settings: dict}] (per ADR-008 deferred M3U auto-sync settings contract).

Size: 4-6 days. First entity to restore (blocks EPG, Channel Groups, User Agents, Channels). No missing Dispatcharr client methods.

Source: ADR-008 per-entity sizing + sequencing-hard requirement (M3U BEFORE EPG BEFORE Channels BEFORE Logos).

User value: Dispatcharr M3U accounts restore cleanly with their upstream refresh settings intact; no manual per-account fix-up after restore.

Success signal: restore of 20 M3U accounts with mixed group states (new, existing, renamed) hits 100% match via the 4-way logic; deferred settings apply correctly after Channels + Logos finish; refresh polling terminates when stream count stabilizes.
close_reason: Verified done: 4-way group matching + deferred auto-sync, wired into real apply registry; 23 tests green

title: Phase 1: Backup retention policy (last-N + time-based)
description:
Retention policy for backup artifacts (local + cloud): configurable last-N (keep last N successful backups) and time-based (keep backups newer than X days). Deletion runs after a successful new backup completes, never before — never leave a user with zero backups.

Aligns with ADR-007 precedent (retention/rollup policy) once filed by Stats v2 initiative.

Source: ADR-008 Sequencing Phase 1.

User value: cloud storage bills stay bounded; old backups aged out automatically so users do not manually prune.

Success signal: after N+1 backups, the oldest is gone; time-based pruning honors the threshold; audit log records each deletion with the reason (last-N or age-based).

title: Phase 1: Cloud upload wiring (S3 / OneDrive / Dropbox / GDrive / WebDAV)

Backend adapters exist for all five providers and S3/GDrive/WebDAV are SSRF-hardened + upload-wired (factory.py SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS), but only S3 and GDrive are operator-reachable end-to-end. title: Phase 1: Backup ZIP artifact builder with schema_version + SHA256 + manifest
description:
Build the ZIP container: YAML settings file + binary subtree (per-image logo files + metadata.json + url-mappings.json) + SHA256 checksum file alongside the ZIP + manifest entry carrying schema_version.

schema_version is MANDATORY from the first release (ADR-008 D1 + Alternative A7 rejection). Restore on an unknown version refuses with user-facing message 'Unsupported backup version' (full detail server-side logs only, per D1 / S4).

Source: ADR-008 D1 + Sequencing Phase 1.

User value: a v0.18.0 backup is forward-compatible — future ECM versions can detect an older artifact and route to a migrator rather than silently misapplying it. The checksum protects against transport corruption on cloud-storage round-trips.

Success signal: manifest round-trips correctly on local restore; SHA256 validates; unknown schema_version is rejected with the correct user-facing message.

title: Phase 1: Scheduled + manual backup invocation via task_scheduler
description:
Register DBAS backup task in backend/task_scheduler.py / task_registry.py. Support cron and interval schedules. Expose a manual-trigger endpoint for on-demand backups. Each scheduled task carries an owning user_id; at fire time, verify owner is still admin + active AND owning target credentials have not been rotated (Security Mandatory #5).

Source: ADR-008 D5 + Sequencing Phase 1.

User value: users can schedule recurring backups (nightly, weekly) without cron on the host; manual trigger supports 'before-upgrade' safety snapshots.

Success signal: scheduled backup fires at the configured time, produces a valid ZIP artifact with schema_version, emits progress via the polling endpoint; orphaned schedule with deactivated owner does NOT fire and logs the skip.

title: Phase 1: First-run SSRF wizard + always-on denylist + DNS rebinding mitigations
description:
First-run wizard choice: LAN-friendly (RFC1918 private IPs allowed; DEFAULT) vs. public-only (private IPs blocked). Always-on denylist regardless of choice: link-local 169.254.0.0/16, IMDS 169.254.169.254, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, IPv6 loopback ::1, IPv6 ULA fc00::/7, IPv6 link-local fe80::/10, IPv6 site-local fec0::/10, IPv4-mapped IPv6 ::ffff:0:0/96, wildcard 0.0.0.0/8, non-http(s) schemes. TLS verify=True default; per-target insecure=true flag requires audit-log entry on every outbound request.

DNS rebinding mitigations (mandatory):
- Resolve-then-connect-by-IP: resolve hostname once, validate returned IP against denylist, connect by IP with hostname as SNI/Host header.
- Block HTTP redirects (3xx) to previously-unvalidated hosts OR re-run full denylist check on every redirect target before following.

Extends bead zbt74 validator pattern with IPv6 / CGNAT / DNS-rebinding coverage if not already present.

Source: ADR-008 D4 + Security Mandatory #2, #3.

User value: ECM cannot be tricked into hitting cloud metadata endpoints, internal infrastructure, or unicast-scanning via user-configurable destinations — protects the deployment environment from an authenticated-admin-induced SSRF.

Success signal: regression test corpus covers unicode, IPv6-mapped, redirect chains, and DNS-rebinding (two-IP response) cases; wizard appears on first run and records the choice; per-request audit log fires on insecure=true targets.

title: Phase 1: SyncTarget + CloudTarget models with Fernet-encrypted credentials
description:
New SQLAlchemy models:
- SyncTarget — Dispatcharr-B URL + encrypted credentials (reserved for v0.18.1 sync; defined in v0.18.0 so the schema lands once).
- CloudTarget — cloud destination tokens (S3, WebDAV, OneDrive, Dropbox, GDrive).

Reuse backend/cloud_storage/crypto.py Fernet primitive (no new crypto surface). Add credential_version + token_revoked_at columns for scheduled-op credential-freshness binding (Security Mandatory #5).

Source: ADR-008 D3 + Security Mandatory #1, #5.

User value: users can configure cloud backup destinations with credentials encrypted at rest; schedules that fire after credentials are rotated or revoked no longer silently use stale tokens.

Success signal: CRUD for both models round-trips encrypted credentials correctly; Alembic migration runs cleanly; freshness-check blocks a scheduled op when credential_version increments.
close_reason: Verified done (board reconciliation 2026-07-25): models + Fernet encryption at every credential read/write, migration 0023, fire-time freshness gate; 18+ tests independently re-run green

title: Phase 0: STRIDE addenda — export artifact redaction + outbound destinations
description:
Extend docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md with two addenda sections:
1. Export artifact redaction — documents the ZIP-path redaction requirement that matches the existing YAML-path redaction (closes Security Mandatory #4 + #6).
2. Outbound destinations — documents SyncTarget + cloud-destination credentials + SSRF validators on all outbound URLs (feeds Phase 1 SSRF wizard design).

Source: ADR-008 Sequencing Phase 0 + Two STRIDE addenda required as Phase 1 prerequisites.

User value: the shipped STRIDE model stays the authoritative security reference for DBAS-absorbed code; future reviewers have one document, not a stale model plus a scattered ADR.

Success signal: threat_model_dbas_import.md contains both addenda with threat rows, mitigations, and residual-risk assessments; the 17-item hardening checklist is extended to cover the new items.

title: Phase 0: Fernet key bootstrap integrity check (mode 0600 + ownership)
description:
On container boot, verify /config/.export_key is mode 0600 and owned by the app user. If either constraint is violated, regenerate rather than proceed with a weakened key.

Source: ADR-008 Security Mandatory #1.

User value: credential encryption key cannot be silently degraded by a filesystem permission regression — the container either boots with a correct key or bootstraps a fresh one, never runs with a world-readable or wrong-owned key.

Success signal: bootstrap logs show 'key integrity verified' or 'key regenerated due to <reason>' on every container start; unit test confirms bad-mode and bad-owner scenarios both trigger regeneration.
close_reason: Verified done with sanctioned deviations (board reconciliation 2026-07-25): mode-0600 repair + fail-closed-on-foreign-ownership REPLACES the bead's 'regenerate on violation' (regeneration would orphan live credential ciphertext and allow chmod-forced key rotation — security improvement, PO decision cited in crypto.py docstring); check runs lazily at first crypto use rather than container boot — boot-time probe tracked as follow-up enhancedchannelmanager-m40pn. Evidence: crypto.py _verify_key_integrity/_atomic_write_key, TestKeyIntegrity suite (7 tests), independently re-run green.

title: v0.18.0 DBAS absorption: Backup + Restore (full round-trip, 13 categories)
description:
Absorb DBAS (Dispatcharr Backup And Sync) into ECM as a first-class backup/restore subsystem. Source of truth: docs/adr/ADR-008-dbas-absorption-approach.md (Accepted 2026-04-21). Supersedes stale 42-bead plan gb5r5 (retired 2026-04-21).

Scope: Phase 0 (security prerequisites) + Phase 1 (backup + cloud upload) + Phase 2 (restore, all 13 categories). Sync (Phase 3) is v0.18.1, separate epic.

Estimate: 27-46 engineer-days single-engineer.

Nine PO-level decisions captured in ADR-008:
- D1 Artifact format: ZIP-wrapped YAML + binary subtree + SHA256 + schema_version mandatory day one.
- D2 Phase-1 scope: v0.18.0 MUST ship backup AND restore (backup without restore is pointless).
- D3 Credential storage: Fernet symmetric via existing backend/cloud_storage/crypto.py; no KMS for MVP.
- D4 Outbound URL policy: first-run SSRF wizard (LAN-friendly default) + always-on denylist + DNS-rebinding mitigations.
- D5 Progress transport: HTTP polling (reuse task_scheduler + NotificationCenter); WebSocket NOT ported.
- D6 Release sequencing: v0.18.0 then v0.18.1 sequential per ADR-004 ONE-major-thing discipline.
- D7 Dry-run engine: counts-only; full diff tree deferred to v0.19.x.
- D8 Logo memory: streaming upload pattern, not CumulativeMemoryTracker port.
- D9 Logo-miss severity: WARN log + aggregate count + prominent red banner on restore-complete (not silent DEBUG).

Five Open Questions all resolved inline in ADR-008 (scope=full round-trip, 27-46 day estimate accepted, SSRF default=LAN-friendly, dry-run=counts-only, logo-miss=prominent banner).

13 Dispatcharr categories covered: M3U accounts, EPG sources, channel groups, channel profiles, stream profiles, user agents, core settings, plugins, DVR rules, comskip config, users, channels (streams embedded), logos.

User value: enables Dispatcharr operators to back up full configuration + restore end-to-end (cross-instance migration, disaster recovery). Retires standalone DBAS companion product.

Success signal: v0.18.0 ships with full 13-category round-trip; first user-driven full restore on a clean Dispatcharr succeeds without manual cleanup; logo-miss banner fires correctly when logos are absent.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE — v0.18.0 shipped 2026-07-27 (tag v0.18.0, main@ae25ad70, GHCR promoted). Full backup+restore round-trip delivered: all 19 children closed (board-reconciled 2026-07-25 with verified evidence; final gaps closed via kxcjf apply-registry wiring, lc6zu producers, PR #743 closeout batch). Scope per ADR-012: 12 categories, plugins excluded (D10). All nine PO decisions D1-D9 delivered as specified. Phase 3 (cross-instance sync) is v0.18.1 scope, separate epic when groomed.

title: Stats v2: observability instrumentation (metrics, logs, data-consistency SLI)
description:
Instrumentation for Stats v2 — metrics, logs, and the dual-write divergence SLI measurement during the transition window. Implementation counterpart to child .10 (which defines SLOs and alert rules against these metrics).

## Metrics to emit (SRE spec from team-plan, bounded cardinality)

- ecm_stats_query_duration_seconds{endpoint, granularity} — histogram. Labels bounded (~5 endpoints × 3 granularities = ~15 series per bucket)
- ecm_session_telemetry_writes_total{result=success|failure} — counter
- ecm_session_telemetry_write_duration_seconds — histogram
- ecm_bandwidth_tracker_dual_write_divergence — gauge (during transition window; computed by background reconciler)
- ecm_stats_ingest_queue_depth — gauge (if any async ingest path exists)
- ecm_session_telemetry_row_count — gauge (for storage-growth alerts)
- Each rollup table: _last_refresh_seconds_ago gauge (DBA pushback: 'stale refreshes are how GH-59 silently lies to users')

## Logs
- Every session_telemetry write failure: WARN with trace_id, session_id, provider_id
- DO NOT log per-buffering-event — that's metric territory, not log
- Log redaction rules from Privacy 11a apply (no user_id+channel_id pairs leak)

## Data-consistency SLI (transition window)
- Background reconciler runs every N minutes during dual-read feature-flag window
- Compares: SUM(session_telemetry.bytes_delta WHERE channel=X) vs. channel_watch_stats.total_bytes WHERE channel=X for a sample window
- Emits ecm_bandwidth_tracker_dual_write_divergence gauge
- Alert fires if divergence > 0.5% over 1h (per child .10)

## Blocked by
- child .3 (BandwidthTracker refactor) — writer must exist to instrument
- child .5 (GH-62 backend API) — endpoint must exist to time
- child .1 (ADR-007) — indirectly, since rollup tables being monitored depend on retention design

## Blocks
- GH-62 release (SRE: instrumentation ships WITH feature)
- child .10 (SRE SLO/alert config) — alerts need metrics to fire on

## Acceptance
- All metrics above registered with bounded cardinality verified (no user_id/channel_id as labels — Code Reviewer checkpoint)
- Log lines for write-failures emit with correct fields (trace_id, no PII leaks)
- Reconciler implemented and emitting the divergence gauge
- Per-route timing middleware labels don't explode (Code Reviewer checkpoint)

title: Stats v2: SLOs, storage-growth alerts, and deployment-safety runbook
description:
SRE deliverables for Stats v2 operational readiness. Lands WITH the feature, not after (SRE hard ask from team-plan).

## SLOs (SRE starting point from team-plan)
- Stats tab availability: 99.5% (internal admin tool — not 99.9% revenue-path). ~3.6h/month error budget.
- /api/stats/watch-time p95 < 800ms, p99 < 2s
- Stats tab initial render p95 < 1.5s (API + chart paint)
- Dual-consistency SLI: session_telemetry row count vs. BandwidthTracker session count — alert if divergence > 0.5% over 1h during the transition window (when legacy writes are still on)

## Storage-growth alerts
- P3 warning at 60% of projected 12-month capacity (ticket, plan retention)
- P2 alert at 80% (page during business hours, execute ADR-007 retention)
- P1 alert at 95% (page immediately)
- Pages go to on-call SRE rotation (doesn't exist yet; page routes to the instance operator's email address until rotation exists — DOCUMENT this explicitly per SRE)

- Frontend feature flag for Users panel (stats_v2_users_enabled, default off, flip per-env)

## Cardinality veto (SRE block at review)
- user_id and channel_id MUST NOT become Prometheus metric labels — value in response only
- provider label OK (bounded <20 providers expected)
- buffering event counts go in histograms, not as labels

## Blocked by
- child .3 (BandwidthTracker refactor) — writer must exist to set SLO targets
- (parallel with) child .11 (observability instrumentation) — metrics from instrumentation feed the alerts

## Blocks
- GH-62 release (SRE hard ask: instrumentation lands with feature)

## Acceptance
- SLO doc lands (likely at docs/operations/ or as a runbook entry)
- Prometheus alert rules land in config or wherever alert rules live (TBD)
- Runbook entries for the 3 Stats v2 alert classes
- Deployment runbook updated with Stats v2 smoke test

title: Stats v2: performance baseline + CI benchmark gate for hot aggregation query
description:
Performance baseline + automated CI regression gate on the hot watch-time aggregation query. QA + DBA both argued (and won) during team-plan that this is non-negotiable for v0.17.0 — 'cut to 1 day if sprint squeezes, do not cut to zero.'

## Scope
- Seeded 6-month synthetic dataset (deterministic seed) committed as a test fixture — generator script that produces realistic session counts (e.g., ~50 users × 10 sessions/day × 180 days = ~90k rows)
- pytest-benchmark gate in CI on the three hottest aggregation queries (watch_time_by_user_daily, per-user breakdown, date-range filter)
- p95 SLO per query: < 200ms at the 6-month data shape
- Fail CI if p95 regresses by > 20% vs. baseline

## Why not skip this
DBA: 26M-row scale is where aggregation on unindexed columns degrades. Without a CI gate, we discover in prod.
QA: 6-month degradation is a product-trust bug; cheaper to baseline now than chase later.
PM pressure to slip to v0.17.1 should be resisted (surfaced in team-plan).

## Blocked by
- child .5 (GH-62 backend read API) — queries to benchmark must exist
- (implicit) schema + indexes from child .2

## Blocks
- GH-62 release (QA hard ask)

## Acceptance
- Synthetic fixture generator script at backend/tests/fixtures/
- pytest-benchmark config + 3 benchmark tests at backend/tests/performance/
- CI pipeline runs benchmarks and fails on >20% regression
- Baseline numbers documented in test file docstring

title: Privacy 11b: post-implementation privacy sign-off for Stats v2
description:
Security Engineer deliverable: post-implementation verification that what was built matches what was specified in 11a. Blocks GH-62 release.

## Verification scope
- Access control tested — users see only their own watch time (or admin-only aggregate, per 11a decision)
- Retention job runs correctly and prunes per ADR-007
- Logs redacted per 11a requirements (no leakage in app logs, support bundles, release notes, etc.)
- No cross-user leakage in API responses

title: Privacy 11a: pre-implementation threat model + data classification for Stats v2
description:
Security Engineer deliverable: land BEFORE session_telemetry schema merges. Split from the original single privacy bead #11 per Security's team-plan ask (2026-04-21).

## Why pre-impl, not post-impl
'Doing only post-impl review is how you discover the schema needs changing after it's shipped' — Security. Threat model + data classification define retention, access control, and redaction requirements up front so Architect/DBA build to spec, not retrofit.

## Deliverables
- **Data classification** — what fields in session_telemetry are sensitive (user_id, channel viewing habits)? PII-adjacent behavioral data handling.
- **Access control boundary** — can users see only their own watch time, or all users (admin-only)? Shared-household scenario (one Dispatcharr username, multiple viewers)? Default: least-privilege.
- **Retention requirements** — feed into ADR-007 (child .1). Security sets the MINIMUM; DBA/SRE set the operational max.
- **Log redaction requirements** — watch-time data must NOT leak into app logs, support bundles, diagnostic exports, or Discord release-note automation.
- **PII minimization** — do we need raw session rows forever, or only rollups?
- **Consent/visibility UX requirement** — users must be able to see what's recorded about them. Whether opt-out is supported is a PO call; doc the decision.

## Blocks
- child .2 (session_telemetry schema) — schema merge requires 11a sign-off
- child .1 (ADR-007 retention) — informs retention minimum

## Acceptance
- Threat model document (or threat-model section in relevant doc) with DREAD or similar scoring per identified threat
- Data classification table checked into docs/security/
- Retention requirements stated and passed to ADR-007 authors
- Redaction requirements passed to Engineer for implementation
- Security sign-off on the schema + retention policy BEFORE schema bead (.2) ships

title: BandwidthTracker single-write refactor + channel_watch_stats_v compat view
description:
Refactor BandwidthTracker to write telemetry to the new session_telemetry table ONLY (single-write). Ship a SQL VIEW channel_watch_stats_v that presents the old channel_watch_stats shape over session_telemetry for read-compat, so GH-62 and any other existing consumers of channel_watch_stats continue to work without immediate refactoring.

## Why single-write (not dual-write)
Team-plan 2026-04-21: DBA and Engineer both argued (and won, 3-to-1 against Architect) that dual-write creates two write paths that WILL silently diverge. The view approach keeps one source-of-truth while preserving legacy read surface.

## Implementation outline
1. Add append-to-session_telemetry inside BandwidthTracker._collect_stats (or an extracted helper) alongside current writes.
2. Feature-flag the writer (env var or settings flag) so we can disable without reverting code if a latency regression appears — Architect's refinement, accepted.
3. Once the flag is stable on dev for at least one sprint, switch legacy writes (channel_watch_stats) OFF and repoint the read via VIEW channel_watch_stats_v (SELECT ... FROM session_telemetry GROUP BY ...) to preserve the legacy read contract.

## Risk (Engineer flagged as 'hidden work')
- _collect_stats is ~180 lines with 4 dependent tables already. Adding a 5th is measurable correctness risk.
- Hidden work: backfill strategy for historical data, reconciliation job during transition, dual-read feature flag, legacy-write removal plan. Engineer estimated ~2 days of 'nobody scoped' work on top of the core refactor.

## Backfill strategy
Options to discuss with DBA/Architect at impl start:
- (a) Backfill existing channel_watch_stats rows into session_telemetry at migration time (requires synthesizing observed_at and poll_interval_ms — lossy)
- (b) Start session_telemetry at T0; view returns UNION of legacy rows + new rows for a transition window
- (c) Accept a short gap in historical data for GH-62 first ship; backfill only if user complaint arises

## Blocked by
- ADR-007 (retention policy) — informs whether rollup tables exist at refactor time
- session_telemetry schema migration (parent bead child .2)

## Blocks
- GH-62 backend read API (child .4) — depends on stable write path
- Observability instrumentation (child .11) — depends on the writer existing to instrument

## Acceptance
- BandwidthTracker writes session_telemetry per-poll under feature flag
- channel_watch_stats_v view returns data equivalent to channel_watch_stats for GH-62's access patterns
- Dual-read feature flag allows toggle between legacy table and new view for rollback
- QA property-based consistency test (see child .9) green
- No regression on existing stats endpoints during feature-flag-off state

title: Schema + Alembic migration for session_telemetry (Stats v2)
description:
Create the unified session_telemetry table and ship its Alembic migration. This is the foundation for both GH-62 and (future) GH-59.

## Schema (per DBA's refined design during team-plan)

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| session_id | TEXT (UUID) | indexed |
| observed_at | INTEGER (unix epoch ms) | DBA renamed from 'ts'; mandatory index |
| user_id | INTEGER | FK users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL |
| provider_id | INTEGER | FK providers(id) ON DELETE SET NULL — nullable until provider tagging ships for GH-59 |
| channel_id | INTEGER | FK channels(id) ON DELETE SET NULL |
| bytes_delta | INTEGER NOT NULL | per-poll delta, CHECK >= 0 (DBA renamed from 'bytes' — explicit delta semantics) |
| buffer_event_count | INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | DBA renamed from 'buffer_events' |
| poll_interval_ms | INTEGER NOT NULL | avoid future assumption of fixed cadence |

NOTE: bitrate_bps dropped — DBA: derivable from bytes_delta / poll_interval_ms; storing derived values invites disagreement.

## Mandatory indexes
- (observed_at) — retention sweeps, time-range queries
- (user_id, observed_at) — GH-62 watch time by user
- (provider_id, observed_at) — GH-59 provider performance (forward-looking)
- (session_id) — session reconstruction

Covering index (user_id, channel_id, observed_at) INCLUDE (bytes_delta) — only if EXPLAIN shows need; skip speculatively.

## Alembic migration constraints
- Use render_as_batch=True (SQLite table-rebuild pattern)
- Migration tested against a 5M-row seeded db before merge (DBA's hard ask)
- Round-trip up/down test (Code Reviewer block-level ask)

## Blocked by
- ADR-007 (retention policy) must land first — informs whether indexes cover rollup access patterns
- Privacy 11a (pre-impl threat model) must land first — may require additional columns or omissions per data-minimization

## Blocks
- BandwidthTracker single-write refactor
- GH-62 backend read API
- All GH-59 impl (deferred to v0.18.0, not in v0.17.0)

## Acceptance
- Schema matches DBA refined design above
- Alembic migration file lands in backend/alembic/versions/
- Up + down migration pass against empty and seeded dbs
- No regression on existing 2503+ tests

title: ADR-007: Retention & rollup policy for session_telemetry
description:
Architectural decision record defining the retention, rollup, and data-lifecycle policy for the new session_telemetry table.

## Why this must land BEFORE first write
Architect and DBA both asserted this as a hard prerequisite during the 2026-04-21 team-plan. Without a retention policy in place, session_telemetry accumulates unboundedly — DBA projected ~13–26M rows over 3–6 months (~1.5–3GB with indexes) at current load, which is workable for SQLite only with disciplined retention + rollups.

## Decisions the ADR must capture
- Raw retention window (DBA proposed 30 days; SRE wants 30d full + 90d downsampled to 5-min buckets; architect leans 180d)
- Rollup schedule (nightly cron vs. on-demand view)
- Rollup tables vs. views (DBA strong pref for tables — views re-scan 26M rows)
- Per-user watch_time_by_user_daily PK and shape
- Per-provider provider_performance_daily PK and shape
- Pruning job (who runs it, alerting if it falls behind, failure modes)
- When Postgres trigger fires (DBA: >50M rows or multi-writer, not v0.17.0)

## Authorship
SRE owns retention window justification (operational cost + query perf at horizon); Architect owns schema-lifecycle placement; DBA owns enforcement mechanism; Tech Writer owns the ADR write-up consistency and cross-linking to database_migrations.md.

## Blocks
- BandwidthTracker single-write refactor (child bead, TBD) — cannot land before ADR-007

## Acceptance
- ADR file lands at docs/adr/ADR-007-session-telemetry-retention.md
- Format matches ADR-001/004/005 precedent
- PO-accepted with all Open Questions resolved inline

title: Stats v2 initiative (v0.17.0): Users panel + session_telemetry foundation
description:
Parent tracker for Stats v2 (v0.17.0 scope). Consolidates **both** GH-62 (user watch-time stats) and GH-59 (per-provider stream stats) into a single cohesive "Stats v2 upgrade" release, backed by the unified session_telemetry data foundation.

## Scope decision history

- **2026-04-21 team-plan consensus**: unanimous AMBER, "yes but smaller" — GH-59 deferred to v0.18.0+, GH-62 committed to v0.17.0 via skqln.5 + skqln.6.
- **2026-04-23 grooming (bd show for details)**: team unanimously recommended keeping GH-59 deferred (6/6 personas). **PO override: pull GH-59 into v0.17.0.** Reason: "Statistics feature — Stats v2 ships as one cohesive stats upgrade release." Override acknowledged; release scope expanded from 12 beads → 17 beads (+42%).

## v0.17.0 scope (as of PO override 2026-04-23)

Chosen pattern: **Package A + DBA's single-write approach** (not dual-write, not defer). Rationale: honors DBA's data-integrity concern while landing the forward investment the architect wants.

## User-visible outcome

Two new Stats tab panels:
- **Users panel** (5th panel, GH-62): personal/admin view of watch-time-by-user with daily trend chart, channel table (total minutes, last watched), and 7/30/90-day selector.
- **Providers panel** (6th panel, GH-59): operator view of provider performance with 4 visualizations — buffering events by provider (time-series), time spent per provider (stacked area), channels-by-provider heatmap, bitrate by provider (time-series). Operator uses this to make data-driven provider keep/drop decisions at renewal.

No sub-nav refactor — users still land on Stats tab normally; both new panels sit alongside Overview/Channels/Popularity/History as flat stacked sections. Stats tab pressure toward sub-nav IA redesign is acknowledged and deferred to v0.18.0.

## What ships (17 child beads)

**Foundation (shared):**
1. skqln.1 — ADR-007: retention/rollup policy (must land BEFORE first write). Amendment: retention window now considers per-provider quarterly trend analysis per PO override.
2. skqln.2 — Schema + Alembic migration for session_telemetry. Amendment: add `(provider_id, channel_id, observed_at) INCLUDE (bytes_delta)` covering index for GH-59 heatmap query.
3. skqln.3 — BandwidthTracker single-write refactor + channel_watch_stats_v compat view. Now the backbone for skqln.14 (provider resolver) and skqln.15 (buffer-event ingest).
4. skqln.7 — Privacy 11a: pre-implementation threat model. Amendment: extend data classification to cover provider attribution (potential provider-relationship PII surface).
5. skqln.8 — Privacy 11b: post-implementation privacy sign-off.

**GH-62 impl (Users panel):**
6. skqln.5 — GH-62 backend watch-time-by-user read API.
7. skqln.6 — GH-62 frontend Users panel.

**GH-59 impl (Providers panel) — NEW, added 2026-04-23 via PO override:**
8. skqln.14 — Active-stream → provider resolver in BandwidthTracker (the "schedule-killer" the grooming team flagged).
9. skqln.15 — Buffer-event ingestion: wire Dispatcharr system events into session_telemetry.buffer_event_count.
10. skqln.16 — GH-59 backend: 4 provider-stats read API endpoints.
11. skqln.17 — Chart primitives: heatmap component + colorblind-safe categorical palette.
12. skqln.18 — GH-59 frontend Providers panel (6th panel in Stats tab, 4 visualizations).

**Quality gates:**
13. skqln.10 — Perf baseline + CI benchmark gate. Amendment: gate expands from 1 hot query to 5 queries (GH-62 watch-time + 4 GH-59 provider aggregates).
14. skqln.11 — SLOs, storage-growth alerts, deployment-safety runbook. Amendment: runbook entry for NULL provider_id cascading into "Unknown" provider bucket; per-provider SLIs on read latency.
15. skqln.12 — Observability instrumentation. Amendment: `provider_id` confirmed safe as Prometheus label (<20 providers bounded per SRE pre-clearance); add data-consistency SLI for provider resolution rate.
16. skqln.9 — Stats v2 user guide entry + metric glossary. Scope extends to cover both Users and Providers panels.
17. (Reserved — add if scope adjustment needed.)

## What's still NOT in v0.17.0 (kept deferred)

- Sub-nav refactor for Stats tab (IA redesign; pressure is now higher with 6 panels, accept for v0.17.0).
- Cross-feature Stats IA redesign.

## Key design decisions (from team-plan + PO override)

- **Write pattern**: single-write to session_telemetry; legacy channel_watch_stats exposed via VIEW channel_watch_stats_v for GH-62 read compat. (Not dual-write — DBA argued and won: two write paths would silently drift.)
- **Provider tagging**: BandwidthTracker gains active-stream → provider resolver (skqln.14). NULL provider_id surfaces as "Unknown" bucket in Providers panel; not silently excluded.
- **Buffer event ingestion**: new polling path folded into `_collect_stats` (skqln.15), with idempotency/dedup on event_id or (channel_id, client_id, event_ts).
- **Retention**: keep raw 30 days, rollups forever. ADR-007 scope re-examined for quarterly trend suitability.
- **Cardinality discipline**: user_id and channel_id NEVER become Prometheus metric labels (SRE veto). provider_id IS allowed as a label (bounded <20 providers).
- **Testing**: property-based consistency tests between session_telemetry and legacy tables during cutover; pytest-benchmark gate on 5 hot queries; Playwright E2E on Stats tab if and only if sub-nav ships (not in v0.17.0, so not needed).

## User-facing trackers

- hl2fm (GH-62 User stats) — closes when skqln.5 + skqln.6 ship.
- 39ao6 (GH-59 Per-provider stats) — closes when skqln.16 + skqln.18 ship.

## Risk acceptance (PO override 2026-04-23)

The grooming team unanimously recommended deferring GH-59. The PO overrode on release-cohesion grounds. Risks the team identified and the PO has accepted:

1. **Engineer**: skqln.3 BandwidthTracker refactor becomes 1.5×–2× harder with provider resolver + buffer-event ingest piled on.
2. **DBA**: 30-day empty-panel problem — Providers panel will show limited data until session_telemetry has accumulated 30d+ of history post-deploy. Backfill into channel_watch_stats' provider-free history is impossible. Operators should expect "useful in 30d, fully useful in 90d" messaging.
3. **SRE**: ADR-007 retention policy now pressured to commit to longer raw window or explicit rollup-with-provider-dimension before skqln.1 closes.
4. **UX**: Stats tab IA pressure — 6 stacked panels in a single release degrades Users panel discoverability in its own launch release; sub-nav refactor debt grows.
5. **QA**: test matrix expands 2D → 3D (user + provider consistency); 5M-row fixture rewrites for provider cardinality; benchmark gate 1 → 5 queries.
6. **PM**: commitment-stability reputational cost — reopening unanimous team-plan AMBER 48h after it was made. Mitigation: override is documented here so future decisions can reference the trail.

## Reference

- Team-plan session 2026-04-21 (12 personas, unanimous AMBER).
- Grooming session 2026-04-23 (6/6 Stay Deferred).
- PO override 2026-04-23: full pull-in, release-cohesion reason.

title: Auto-creation: separate-not-merge option for channels already in another group (GH-92)
description:
GitHub issue #92 (langtd19), filed 2026-04-21. User impact: High.

## Problem
When two auto-creation rules target different channel groups (e.g., rule A targets SPORTS, rule B targets ESPN), running rule B merges channels into the rule A group if channel names already exist there, rather than creating new channels in the rule B target group.

## User workaround (brittle)
Rename channel groups with unicode suffixes to force differentiation. Works for most cases, breaks for some regex/odd-naming cases.

## Suggested implementation
Add an option to scope the existing-channel check to the target channel group only, so a channel with the same name in a different group triggers a new-channel creation rather than a merge.

## Acceptance direction (TBD by engineer)
- New option on rule (or global) restricting duplicate-check to target group scope
- Test: two rules, same channel name, different target groups → two separate channels each in correct group
- Backwards-compatible default (opt-in)

title: Investigate CodeQL scan configuration: custom vs. Default Setup (clarify single-source-of-truth)
description:
Architect investigation. The PR #82 dispatch context claimed the repo runs TWO CodeQL scans that disagree (custom .github/workflows/build.yml AND GitHub Default Setup), with Default Setup producing the 4 new path-injection errors while custom passes. Evidence on the PR itself contradicts this:

1. All 847 historical CodeQL alerts in the repo (including the 4 new path-injection alerts IDs 1416-1419) have analysis_key = '.github/workflows/build.yml:codeql-analysis' — meaning they come from the CUSTOM workflow.
2. PR #82's individual 'CodeQL Analysis (python)' and 'CodeQL Analysis (javascript-typescript)' jobs both PASS (they exit zero because they successfully UPLOAD SARIF).
3. The failing check named 'CodeQL' is owned by app 'GitHub Advanced Security' (app_slug: github-advanced-security) — it is the AGGREGATE PR check that compares SARIF delta vs. the base branch and fails when new HIGH alerts are introduced. It consumes output from the SAME custom workflow.

In other words: there is almost certainly ONE CodeQL scan (the custom one), and the perceived disagreement is between (a) the individual scan jobs 'pass' because SARIF upload succeeded and (b) the aggregate GHAS PR check 'fail' because new HIGH findings were introduced. That is correct behavior, not config drift.

Task: verify this hypothesis definitively. If confirmed, update the PR #82 dispatch framing. If there genuinely IS a Default Setup also enabled (visible at Settings > Code security > Code scanning > Default setup), recommend disabling it to avoid dual-scan drift and unify on the custom workflow + codeql-config.yml query filters (currently excludes py/log-injection).

Output: short architect note + config change recommendation if needed. Close the bead with evidence.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #156. Drift verdict: NO DRIFT — gh api code-scanning/default-setup returns state=not-configured; last 100 analyses all from .github/workflows/build.yml:codeql-analysis (single source); alerts from one tool entry (CodeQL 2.25.2). Source-of-truth split documented: build.yml (codeql-analysis job) owns WHEN; .github/codeql/codeql-config.yml owns WHAT. New docs/security/codeql-config.md (operational reference: SoT table, add/remove rule procedure, drift verification commands). ADR-005 cross-link added; CLAUDE.md Reference Guides updated.

title: Baseline smoke test: round-trip 0001 up/down on non-empty DB
description:
Why:
Baseline revision 0001 (bd-c5wf5, PR #81) passes the metadata drift test (test_baseline_matches_metadata_no_drift) and runs on fresh installs via _bootstrap_alembic, but no one has exercised a full round-trip against a non-empty DB. A down migration that has never been run is as dangerous as a backup that has never been restored — and right now the DBAS rollback story leans on Alembic's downgrade path being sound.

This bead exercises the baseline revision end-to-end before the next migration lands so we know 0001 is genuinely reversible.

Scope:
- Take a copy of a populated /config/journal.db (dev or DBAS snapshot).
- Run: alembic upgrade head → alembic downgrade base → alembic upgrade head against that copy using ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////tmp/…
- Verify: every table re-created, FK constraints restored, PRAGMA state intact, row data unaffected (compare row counts per table before/after round-trip upgrade).
- If downgrade fails (expected risk on a 36-table baseline with batch_alter semantics), capture the error, add the affected table to a known-non-reversible list in docs/database_migrations.md, and decide whether to patch revision 0001 or document the limit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented result of the round-trip in docs/database_migrations.md (or a follow-up ADR if results warrant).
- If reversible: remove the 'baseline not yet exercised' warning from docs/database_migrations.md.
- If NOT reversible: warning stays and explicitly lists which tables block a clean downgrade.

Out of scope:
- Any new migration (0002+). This is strictly about validating 0001.
- Automating the round-trip in CI. Manual exercise is fine for this bead; a follow-up can wire CI.

title: Design spec: shared DBAS components (progress, category toggles, dry-run preview, WS handler)
description:
## Why

bd-gb5r5.3 (Backup & Restore import) and bd-gb5r5.4 (Backup & Restore sync) share the same interaction primitives: file upload, dry-run preview modal, per-category toggle list, 3-phase progress bar, WebSocket progress handler, cancel-with-confirm. UX flagged during grooming on 2026-04-20 that without a shared spec, these will be built twice and diverge. Spec once, build once.

## Scope — component specs (wireframe + behavior contract)

- `<DryRunPreviewModal>` — per-category table with add/update/skip/conflict counts; expandable rows; Proceed / Cancel actions; focus trap; Esc dismisses.
- `<CategoryToggleList>` — checkbox list with select-all; disabled state with tooltip for categories not present in payload; full keyboard navigation.
- `<PhasedProgressBar>` — ordered phase list with current-step highlight, per-phase progress, overall bar, elapsed time; aria-live phase announcements; role=progressbar.
- `<CancelWithConfirm>` — prominent cancel button; confirm dialog warns about partial state; post-cancel summary of what was applied.
- `<WSProgressHandler>` (hook) — connection lifecycle, reconnect-with-resume, disconnect-does-not-mean-stopped semantics, progress event monotonicity guarantee.
- `<ConflictResolutionRow>` — per-row radio (Keep existing / Overwrite / Rename / Skip) plus "Apply to all in category" bulk action; default is the safest option (Nielsen heuristic #5, error prevention).

## Terminology lock (coordinate with PO)

UI-facing name is "Backup & Restore" — "DBAS" is internal jargon and must not appear in user-visible strings. Define source/destination instance terminology in the spec so import and sync use identical language.

## A11y acceptance (per component)

- Keyboard-only operable (Tab order, Enter/Space activation, Esc dismiss).
- Screen reader announcements defined for phase changes, completion, errors, and cancel confirmation.
- Focus-return on modal dismiss to the trigger element.
- Correct aria roles (progressbar, dialog, alert, status).

## Deliverable

- `docs/ux/dbas_components.md` with wireframes + behavior contracts, plus any supporting Figma/mermaid artifacts.
- Linked from `docs/user_guide/_index.md` once the Technical Writer bead lands.

## Out of scope

Actual component implementation — that lives in the bd-gb5r5.3 and bd-gb5r5.4 epics. This bead is spec-only so both epics can consume a single source of truth.

title: ADR-006: Two-instance sync credential & trust model
description:
bd-gb5r5.4 requires ECM to hold outbound credentials to a second Dispatcharr instance. This is a new trust boundary and credential surface; requires Security sign-off on threat model.

Decisions required:
(a) Credential storage — encrypted at rest (key source: env secret, KMS, sealed secret?). Never plaintext in env vars or DB columns. Masked in all UI surfaces and logs.
(b) TLS enforcement — verify=True default for all outbound calls to the peer instance. No verify=False unless per-instance opt-in flag is set AND the opt-in is audit-logged each use.
(c) Trust model — is the destination assumed to be a trusted peer within the same org, or must we design for arbitrary third-party Dispatcharr endpoints? Affects rate limiting, data minimization, and error-handling assumptions.
(d) Payload scoping — user passwords and API tokens inside the sync payload excluded by default. Explicit allow-list for what syncs, deny-list never overridable.
(e) Threat model — spoofed destination, MITM, credential theft at rest, replay. Paired review with Security.

title: ADR-003: WebSocket introduction & long-running job pattern
description:
bd-gb5r5.4 (two-instance sync) requires WebSocket-based progress. If WS is not already established in ECM, this epic introduces the pattern — and the pattern will calcify fast (CR warning) so schema discipline is required up front.

Decisions required:
(a) Authn/authz for WS connections — session cookie, bearer token, per-message auth?
(b) Reconnect semantics — resume on last-seen sequence, replay buffer size, idempotency.
(c) Backpressure — slow client handling, server-side drop policy, queue bounds.
(d) Progress envelope — versioned schema, e.g. {type, phase, progress, data, meta}. Naming and versioning discipline locked before first consumer ships.
(e) Scope — WS progress as a cross-cutting pattern (reusable by import, black-screen scan, probe, restore) vs. sync-specific. Recommendation: cross-cutting.

Soft-couples to ADR-002 — bd-gb5r5.3's restore progress UI likely wants the same envelope.

title: ADR-002: DBAS restore engine transaction model & downtime contract
description:
bd-gb5r5.3 (restore engine) requires documented architectural decisions before implementation.

Decisions required:
(a) Transaction model — single transaction spanning all categories vs. savepoint-per-category (partial restore on failure).
(b) Acceptable downtime during the restore window — is the API offline, read-only, or fully available?
(c) Concurrent-API behavior during restore — reject with 503, queue, or allow (with what consistency guarantees)?
(d) Pre-restore snapshot protocol — VACUUM INTO before restore for auto-rollback target; retention, location, cleanup.
(e) Rollback-on-error guarantees — what state is guaranteed if restore fails mid-run?

Required inputs:
- DBA: Alembic migration coupling, FK dependency graph for category ordering.
- SRE: observability during restore (progress, duration, failure telemetry).
- Security: endpoint authz, audit logging for destructive ops.

title: [BUG] Auto-create engine _smart_sort_streams has same within-bucket bug as sw883
description:
Follow-up to bd-sw883 / GitHub #73.

The sw883 fix corrects the within-bucket sort in backend/stream_prober.py — the comparator previously appended a tuple of zeros for the primary criteria on deprioritized streams, collapsing the within-bucket order to insertion order.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Test-quality hygiene fix. Independent of any E2E infrastructure work.

Problem: e2e/modals.spec.ts has 21 conditional test.skip() calls (skip-if-no-orphans-found, skip-if-button-not-present, etc.). These silently pass in Playwright output, making the suite report green while ~21 cases exercised nothing.

Scope:
- Convert every conditional test.skip() in e2e/modals.spec.ts to test.fixme() with a descriptive message naming the missing precondition (e.g., 'fixme: requires Dispatcharr-provided orphaned groups', 'fixme: requires linked M3U accounts with profiles').
- Silent green becomes loud red for any run that reaches those branches. Matches the cataloged 21 states from the 2lw25 evaluation report.
- If any of the 21 are NOT conditional (i.e., legitimate hard skips for unimplemented features), leave them as test.skip() with a TODO comment.

Effort: ~30 minutes. One file, no infrastructure changes.

Prerequisite: none. Can be done any time, independent of t8xw3 and 2lw25.

Benefit: kills the silent-green anti-pattern immediately. When 2lw25 eventually delivers E2E-in-CI, the fixmes become red checks that drive the cataloging of what state to seed. When 2lw25 seeds that state, convert fixme() back to the regular test body.

Flagged during engineer evaluation of 2lw25 on 2026-04-19. Kept separate so the hygiene fix isn't blocked behind a 10-14h sidecar/runner investment.

title: E2E in CI: Dispatcharr mock sidecar OR self-hosted runner
description:
Reframed 2026-04-19 after engineer evaluation (Path C chosen).

ORIGINAL SCOPE (obsolete): seed the ECM container for modals.spec.ts conditional skips.

REAL PROBLEM — architectural:
- ECM is a proxy. ~15 of 21 conditional skips in modals.spec.ts require Dispatcharr-owned entities (channels, channel_groups, M3U accounts, profiles, logos, EPG sources). No amount of ECM-side seeding produces them.
- CI currently points DISPATCHARR_URL at localhost:9999 (a black hole). There is no Dispatcharr instance in CI.
- Only ~6 of 21 skips could be covered by ECM-native seeding (dummy EPG, auto-creation rules, orphan-scan state).
- This means the E2E job as originally designed in t8xw3 can never be a real gate on GitHub-hosted runners.

TWO REAL PATHS (pick when scheduled):
1. **Mock Dispatcharr sidecar.** Extend backend/tests/fixtures/mock_dispatcharr.py into a standalone FastAPI container; docker-compose alongside ECM in CI; point DISPATCHARR_URL at it. Effort ~10-14h. Risk: mock drifts from real Dispatcharr contract → false-positive passes.
2. **Self-hosted GitHub runner with real Dispatcharr.** Run CI on a local machine that has the full integration environment (Dispatcharr + Postgres + mock M3U sources). Highest fidelity; biggest infra lift. Requires managing runner uptime, security boundaries, data hygiene.

DECISION POSTPONED:
PO chose Path C from the 2026-04-19 evaluation: pull E2E from t8xw3 entirely and treat E2E-in-CI as a separate future initiative. This bead now tracks THAT initiative.

SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD (when picked up):
- Evaluate mock vs. self-hosted runner vs. a hybrid.
- Implement chosen approach.
- Add e2e job back to .github/workflows/test.yml (gated on PR-to-main + nightly + workflow_dispatch per original t8xw3 design).
- Ensure all 21 modals.spec.ts skips either run cleanly or are explicitly marked fixme with reason.
- Required checks on main include the e2e job (companion bead 8w33i needs updating once this lands).

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Hygiene cleanup of test.skip() → test.fixme() in modals.spec.ts. That's a separate small bead so the silent-green antipattern is killed immediately, not blocked on E2E infrastructure work.

Status: P2, no immediate priority. Sits in backlog until PO chooses to invest.
design:
Evaluation in progress (research phase). See final brief in conversation — do not implement until PO greenlights.

Key architectural finding: Most spec.ts state requirements route via Dispatcharr (external service). In CI today, DISPATCHARR_URL=http://localhost:9999 is a black hole — no Dispatcharr runs. ECM-native data is limited to: auto-creation rules, dummy EPG profiles, FFmpeg profiles, normalization rules, tags, alerts, scheduled tasks, journal, and notifications. The 21 skips' required entities (orphaned groups, channels, M3U accounts/profiles, logos, LCN-capable channels, M3U filters) are ALL Dispatcharr-owned.

Implication: Seeding via ECM's REST API (option 1) is insufficient by itself — those API routes forward to Dispatcharr. Options must be reframed:
- Option 1 as written (API-driven seed via ECM): only works for auto-creation + dummy EPG. Does NOT cover the majority of the 21 skips.
- Option 2 (SQL-direct to /config/ecm.db): also only covers ECM-native entities. The real data is in Dispatcharr's Postgres, unreachable from CI without standing up a Dispatcharr service.
- Option 3 (/api/testing/seed endpoint): same constraint — endpoint lives in ECM, can't write to Dispatcharr.

Missing option (option 4): Mock the Dispatcharr backend. Add a test-mode env flag that makes DispatcharrClient return a deterministic fixture from a JSON file instead of hitting the real service. Already have partial infra: backend/tests/fixtures/mock_dispatcharr.py uses respx for unit tests; that pattern could be extended to an in-process Dispatcharr shim served via docker-compose in the E2E job.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Fixed: black screen scan task silently overwriting is_black_screen=False on every ffmpeg timeout.

Contract change in stream_prober._detect_black_screen:
- Return type: bool → Optional[bool]. True = black, False = clean, None = indeterminate (timeout / no YAVG samples / abnormal exit).
- Added ffmpeg -timeout 15s network stall guard (microseconds) at the input level.
- Bumped asyncio wait_for grace from sample_duration+15s to sample_duration+30s. Cold-start scans on slow-to-buffer IPTV providers were hitting the 20s wall before the first keyframe decoded.

Call sites updated:
- probe_stream() inline black-screen check now keeps is_black at None when detection is disabled or indeterminate.
- _save_probe_result() signature: is_black_screen: Optional[bool] = None. The success path now writes is_black_screen ONLY when it's True or False — None preserves prior state.
- tasks/black_screen_scan.py::scan_one: None is routed into error_count (surfaced in the TaskResult summary as 'N errors') and the DB row's is_black_screen is left untouched. Previously every timeout wrote False and the stream counted as 'clear' in the task report.

Tests:
- Renamed test_returns_false_on_timeout → test_returns_none_on_timeout; asserts None.
- Renamed test_returns_false_when_no_yavg_data → test_returns_none_when_no_yavg_data; asserts None.
- Added test_preserves_black_screen_when_detection_indeterminate: regression guard that pins None → no DB write.
- Full suite: 2425 passed.

User-observable behavior after fix:
- Scan results now report 'N black screen, N clear, N errors' with real numbers in the errors bucket.
- A scan-task timeout on a stream that a manual probe flagged as black no longer wipes that finding.
- Cold-start timeouts drop substantially thanks to the longer grace and ffmpeg -timeout option, but any remaining timeouts are now visible rather than masquerading as clean streams.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
In channel manager edit mode, check streams under search A, change search to B, check more streams, drag all selected onto an existing channel. Staging adds all IDs correctly, but the expanded channel view shows only streams from the current search because loadStreams resolves staged IDs against the current-search result set plus the backend channel-streams response — streams whose objects only appeared in a prior search aren't in either source.

Fix: App.tsx accumulates a seenStreams Map that is populated every time searchStreams/loadStreamGroup returns results and is never cleared on new search. ChannelManagerTab threads it through as seenStreamsMap. ChannelsPane.loadStreams seeds localStreamMap / combinedMap from seenStreamsMap first so previously-seen streams resolve by ID regardless of the current search filter.

Also rolls in the TS-error cleanup that was intentionally left out of v0.16.0-0037 because it overlapped this feature's file diffs: video_codec added to ALL_SORT_CRITERIA / DEFAULT_SORT_ENABLED / SORT_MODE_LABELS, and a fetchChannels() -> onChannelsChange?.() typo fix in ChannelsPane's FindDuplicatesModal onMerged handler.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
After moving Dispatcharr+ECM to a new server and restoring an ECM ZIP backup, Channel Manager showed static groups (e.g. My Teams) as empty/wrong-count while the Guide tab worked. Two independent bugs:

1. backend/routers/channel_groups.py get_channel_groups() filtered hidden groups by numeric ID only. hidden_channel_groups records (carried over in journal.db from the old server) collided with unrelated groups on the new Dispatcharr instance, hiding the user's static groups. Fix: validate stored group_name against current Dispatcharr group at the same ID; auto-prune stale records.

2. backend/routers/backup.py _restore_channel_groups() (YAML restore) deleted all Dispatcharr groups and recreated them by name, orphaning all channel/stream FK references. Fix: upsert by name only.

title: NIST 800-63B password policy alignment
description:
Modernize password validation to follow NIST 800-63B guidelines:

1. **Drop composition rules** — remove uppercase/lowercase/number requirements (they produce predictable patterns like Password1)
2. **Uniform 8-char minimum** — apply to all users including admin-created (currently 6 in admin_routes.py:160)
3. **Replace 33-word common password list** with a proper breached password check — either bundle a top-100k list or integrate haveibeenpwned k-anonymity API (sends only first 5 chars of SHA-1 hash, no plaintext leaves the server)
4. **Remove starts-with-common-word check** — overly broad, catches legitimate passwords while missing actual breaches
5. **Keep**: no max length penalty, no periodic rotation, allow paste in frontend fields

Files: auth/password.py (validate_password, COMMON_PASSWORDS), auth/admin_routes.py:158-160

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
Add an optional provider diversification step to the stream probe's auto-reorder (Smart Sort) pipeline. After streams are sorted by quality (resolution, bitrate, etc.), optionally interleave them across M3U accounts so failback streams alternate providers instead of clustering on one. This improves failover resilience — if one provider goes down, the next stream in line comes from a different provider.

Implementation approach:
- Add a diversification step after the existing Smart Sort in stream_prober.py _smart_sort_streams()
- Two modes: round-robin (alphabetical rotation across accounts) and priority-weighted (user-assigned account priorities determine order)
- Controlled by a new setting (e.g. stream_sort_diversify: disabled/round_robin/priority_weighted) alongside existing sort criteria
- Could reuse the existing m3u_account_priorities setting already in the prober
- Should be per-schedule configurable like other probe parameters

Inspired by PR #37 (closed — broader feature set was undiscussed and duplicated existing functionality, but this specific concept has value).

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: Port DBAS importService.ts to Python. Upload and restore from ZIP. Ordered restore sequence: M3U → EPG sources → profiles → groups → stream profiles → logos → channels → user agents → settings → plugins → DVR → comskip → users → refresh triggers. Name-based conflict resolution with ID remapping. Stream matching fallback chain (tvg_id → station ID → normalized name → hash). Logo matching (source ID → name → sanitized filename). Dry-run/inspect mode. Per-category selective restore.
notes:
Security hardening criteria from bd-qmuij (STRIDE threat model, docs/security/threat_model_dbas_import.md):
(1) Admin-only endpoint + DBAS paths absent from AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS
(2) Per-category opt-in flags for users + plugins (default false)
(3) Current authenticated admin row never overwritten/deleted/demoted by restore
(4) Zip Slip hardening: reject absolute/.. paths, symlink entries, >32-segment paths, >255-byte names
(5) Zip bomb caps: max 256MB upload, 10k entries, 1GB uncompressed, 100x per-entry ratio (PO-tunable)
(6) Streaming upload (shutil.copyfileobj to NamedTemporaryFile) — no await file.read()
(7) SHA-256 manifest per file verified before any extraction outside tempdir
(8) Tempdir isolation + guaranteed cleanup; dry-run must be side-effect free
(9) Secrets-in-logs denylist + _redact() helper (password, token, api_key, smtp_password, M3U creds)
(10) URL scheme re-validation on restore (reuse bd-ppe28.3)
(11) Per-category audit log (journal.log_entry) with request ID; users category logs usernames only, never hashes
(12) Error message sanitisation (no paths/SQL/usernames in HTTPException detail)
(13) Plugin execution gate: written to disk but NOT executed at import; activation via separate admin action
(14) SQLAlchemy transaction per category with rollback on exception
(15) Dispatcharr restore batches capped at 500 items
(16) CSRF: bearer-token required; reject cookie-only requests
(17) Authz denials emit structured WARN logs
Test module layout: backend/tests/security/ (test_dbas_import_{authz,zipbomb,zipslip,manifest,users,secrets,audit,cleanup,url_validation,plugins}.py)
PO decisions required (see threat model §6): A1 plugins code-vs-config; A2 cross-instance restore scope; A3 users-table version compat; A4 ratify DoS caps; A5 journal tamper-evidence; A6 CSRF posture

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description:
User feedback: Two matching gaps in merge_streams logic:

1. 'Bravo East' does not match 'US Bravo (East)' — after country prefix strip we get 'Bravo (East)' but the channel is 'Bravo East'. The parentheses around directional words (East/West) prevent matching.

2. 'Fox News Channel' does not match 'US Fox News' — after country prefix strip we get 'Fox News' but the channel is 'Fox News Channel'. The shorter provider name is a substring of the channel name but not an exact match.

Possible approaches:
- For case 1: normalize parenthetical directions in core-name comparison, e.g. 'Bravo (East)' -> 'Bravo East'
- For case 2: needs careful thought. Cannot just strip 'Channel' since providers may also use it. Could try a 'channel name contains provider name' fallback tier, but risk of false positives. May need scoring/confidence thresholds.

Low priority — user says 'not a big deal' and overall matching is working well.

title: Tests and documentation
description:
Tests + documentation for the dummy EPG template engine.

Backend tests
- New backend/tests/integration/test_dummy_epg.py (16 tests) covering edge cases through the /api/dummy-epg/preview HTTP path:
  - Nested conditionals (3-level, with middle absent) + trace reports each level.
  - Lookup edge cases: missing key passes value through; unknown table falls back to raw template (not 500, because TemplateSyntaxError is soft-caught in render_template); chained lookup after transform.
  - Invalid regex in conditional: unclosed char class → evaluates false, oversized (>500 char) → false, trace records kind_detail='regex'.
  - Backwards compat: legacy {name_normalize} suffix, legacy inside conditional, pipe on missing group renders empty.
  - Trace shape: literal-only template returns single literal entry; include_trace=false omits traces key.
  - Global lookup resolution: created via /api/lookup-tables then referenced by ID; missing global ID ignored silently.

Frontend tests
- 12 new cases in api.test.ts covering listLookupTables (summaries-only, errors), getLookupTable, createLookupTable (body shape), updateLookupTable (rename + partial entries), deleteLookupTable (204 + 404), and previewDummyEPG (basic render, include_trace flag propagation, inline_lookups + global_lookup_ids forwarded).
- MSW handlers in src/test/mocks/handlers.ts for /api/lookup-tables (GET list/detail, POST, PATCH, DELETE) and /api/dummy-epg/preview (respects include_trace, returns shaped payload).

Documentation
- New docs/template_engine.md: syntax reference (placeholders, pipes, conditionals, lookups), limits, worked examples, trace format, and cross-refs to every related file.
- docs/api.md: added Lookup Tables endpoint table and documented the new inline_lookups / global_lookup_ids / include_trace fields on /preview.
- CLAUDE.md: added 'Dummy EPG Template Engine' → docs/template_engine.md in the Reference Guides table.

Totals: backend 2424 tests (+16), frontend 1112 tests (+12). Typecheck clean.

title: Backend processing integration
description:
Backend integration of the template engine + lookup tables.

- backend/dummy_epg_engine.py: render_template now delegates to template_engine.TemplateEngine with an optional lookups dict; TemplateSyntaxError falls back to the raw template so typos in a profile config don't crash an XMLTV refresh. generate_channel_xml accepts lookups and binds it to a local _render helper used by all inner template renders. preview_pipeline and preview_pipeline_batch accept lookups.
- backend/routers/dummy_epg.py: PreviewRequest and BatchPreviewRequest gained inline_lookups (dict[str, dict[str, str]]) and global_lookup_ids (list[int]). New _resolve_lookups helper merges inline tables with globals fetched from lookup_tables by ID; inline tables override same-named globals. Both /api/epg/dummy/preview and /preview/batch now resolve lookups via a DB session and hand them to the engine.
- Updated test_dummy_epg_engine.py test_render_missing_key_renders_empty to reflect the new semantics (missing placeholders render as '' instead of leaving raw {tokens} in output — matches the frontend applyTemplate).
- Added 5 new /preview integration tests covering pipe transforms, conditionals, inline lookups, global lookup IDs, and inline-overrides-global precedence.

Scope notes: the bead called for a separate /api/epg/dummy/process endpoint, but 'process' is effectively /preview/batch with channel-name inputs + lookups — both endpoints now support exactly that. Left as single endpoint to avoid pointless duplication; revisit if .6 preview UI needs a different shape.

Profile-column persistence (inline_lookups / global_lookup_ids on DummyEPGProfile) is deferred to .5 since that bead covers the modal save path that writes them.

title: Enhanced preview UI
description:
Enhanced preview UI for dummy EPG.

Backend
- template_engine.TemplateEngine.render_with_trace(template, groups, lookups) -> (output, trace). Trace entries: literal, placeholder (with initial/final + per-pipe input/output), conditional (condition, kind_detail truthy|equality|regex, taken, nested body). Lookup pipes annotated with {source, matched} so the UI distinguishes hits from misses. _evaluate_condition now returns (taken, detail) for richer trace display. +7 unit tests.
- preview_pipeline accepts include_trace; when true, response includes a 'traces' dict keyed by template field name (title_template, description_template, etc.).
- PreviewRequest adds include_trace: bool. +2 integration tests.

Frontend
- templateEngine.ts: renderWithTrace() mirror with identical trace shape + 6 Vitest tests.
- New TemplateHelp.tsx + .css: collapsible syntax reference (placeholders, pipes with each transform listed, lookups, conditionals, worked example).
- Reworked 'Test Your Configuration' section in DummyEPGSourceModal:
  - Kept the fast in-browser live preview (renamed 'Live Preview (browser)').
  - Added 'Run Server Preview' button that POSTs with include_trace=true.
  - New ServerPreviewView component shows match/fallback badge, matched variant, extracted groups grid, and every rendered field with its resolved output.
  - Each field with a non-empty trace gets a 'Show trace' toggle that renders a step viewer: placeholder rows show initial value → each pipe's output; lookup pipes show hit/miss badges; conditionals show taken/skipped + kind detail + value + nested body.
- DummyEPGPreviewResult extended with optional traces dict; DummyEPGPreviewRequest carries inline_lookups, global_lookup_ids, include_trace.

title: Per-source inline lookups in dummy EPG modal

- types/index.ts: DummyEPGCustomProperties extended with inline_lookups (Record<string, Record<string, string>>) and global_lookup_ids (number[]).
- DummyEPGSourceModal.tsx: new collapsible Lookup Tables section, opened automatically when loaded state already has lookups. Global tables shown as a scrollable checkbox list populated from api.listLookupTables() on modal open (refetched each open so newly-created tables appear). description: Bandwidth tracker treated Dispatcharr total_bytes as already including fan-out to all clients. In reality total_bytes is the source stream bytes only. title: Register TLS Certificate Manager as monitored service
description:
Add TLS Certificate Manager as a monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Check certificate file exists
- Verify certificate is not expired
- Check days until expiration (warn if < 30 days)
- Verify ACME account status if using Let's Encrypt

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Valid cert, > 30 days until expiry
- degraded: Cert expires within 30 days
- unhealthy: Cert expired or missing

Only register if HTTPS is enabled in settings.

title: Register Telegram Bot as external service
description:
Add Telegram Bot as an external monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Call Telegram getMe API with bot token
- Verify bot is active and token valid
- Check chat IDs are accessible

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Bot responding, token valid
- unhealthy: Invalid token or bot blocked

Only register if Telegram alert method is configured.

title: Register Discord Webhook as external service
description:
Add Discord Webhook as an external monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Validate webhook URL format
- Test webhook reachability (HEAD request)
- Optionally send test message

Status Indicators:
- healthy: Webhook reachable
- unhealthy: Webhook URL invalid or unreachable

Only register if Discord alert method is configured.

title: Register SMTP Server as external service
description:
Add SMTP Server as an external monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Test SMTP connection with configured credentials
- Verify TLS/SSL handshake if enabled
- Check authentication success

Status Indicators:
- healthy: SMTP connection successful
- degraded: Connection slow or intermittent
- unhealthy: Cannot connect or auth fails

Only register if SMTP is configured in settings.
Configuration: host, port, username, password, from_address, use_tls

title: Register Alert Methods as monitored service
description:
Add Alert Methods as a unified monitored service.

Health Check Implementation:
- Test connectivity to each enabled alert method
- Discord: Validate webhook URL is reachable
- SMTP: Test connection to mail server
- Telegram: Verify bot token with getMe API

Status Indicators:
- healthy: All configured methods reachable
- degraded: Some methods failing
- unhealthy: All methods failing (alerts won't be delivered)

Only check methods that are configured and enabled.

title: Optional/Notification Services
description:
Register and monitor optional services that depend on user configuration. Only monitor if the service is configured/enabled.

Services:
- Alert Methods Service: Combined health of all configured alert channels
- SMTP Server: Email delivery (if configured)
- Discord Webhook: Discord notifications (if configured)
- Telegram Bot: Telegram notifications (if configured)
- TLS Certificate Manager: HTTPS certs (if HTTPS enabled)

title: v6dxf.2: Local Authentication - User Management CRUD
description:
Local Authentication - User Management CRUD (COMPLETED)

Implemented user management for local authentication:

1. User Registration (POST /api/auth/register)
   - Creates new users with username, email, password
   - Validates unique username/email (409 conflict)
   - Enforces password strength (422 if weak)
   - New users are non-admin by default

2. Admin User CRUD (/api/admin/users)
   - GET: Paginated user list with search
   - POST: Admin creates user (relaxed password rules)
   - PATCH: Update user fields (email, display_name, is_admin, is_active, password)
   - DELETE: Soft delete (deactivate user)
   - GET /{id}: Get single user
   - Non-admin gets 403 Forbidden

3. Password Management
   - POST /api/auth/change-password - Change own password (requires current)
   - POST /api/auth/forgot-password - Request password reset (always 200 for security)
   - POST /api/auth/reset-password - Reset password with token (1-hour expiry)

description:
Apply normalization when normalize flag is set in single channel create endpoint.

## Changes
In create_channel() endpoint (@app.post('/api/channels')):
- Check if request.normalize is True
- If true, get normalization engine and normalize the name
- Use normalized name in channel data

## Code Pattern
@app.post('/api/channels')
async def create_channel(request: CreateChannelRequest):
    data = {'name': request.name, ...}
    if request.normalize:
        from normalization_engine import get_normalization_engine
        session = get_session()
        try:
            engine = get_normalization_engine(session)
            result = engine.normalize(request.name)
            data['name'] = result.normalized
        finally:
            session.close()
    result = await client.create_channel(data)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Single channel creation respects normalize flag
- Normalization only applied when flag is True

description:
v0.8.7: Normalization Engine - Tag/Rules Engine Redesign & Testing

This release completes the normalization engine with a major architectural redesign separating tags from rules, followed by comprehensive testing.

## Part 1: Tag/Rules Engine Redesign (5 child epics, 22 tasks)
Separates the current normalization system into two distinct subsystems:

**Tag Engine** - Vocabulary/data management
- TagGroup and Tag models for organizing strings into groups
- Built-in tag groups: Quality, Country, Timezone, League, Network
- Tag management UI with bulk import

**Rules Engine** - Enhanced logic layer
- New 'tag_group' condition type (match ANY tag from a group)
- Position-aware matching (prefix/suffix/contains)
- If/Then/Else conditional logic
- Enhanced rule editor UI

### Phases:
1. Phase 1: Tag Engine Backend (models, migration, API, built-in tags)
2. Phase 2: Rules Engine Enhancement (tag_group condition, else logic)
3. Phase 3: Tag Engine Frontend (TagEngineSection component)
4. Phase 4: Rules Engine Frontend (enhanced rule editor)
5. Phase 5: Migration & Testing
6. Phase 6: Add Normalization to Channel Creation (optional normalize flag, preview, settings)

## Part 2: Testing (7 tasks)
- Unit tests for compound condition matching
- Integration tests for normalization rules API
- Frontend unit tests for normalization components
- E2E tests for normalization engine
- Documentation updates
