title: Renumber inputs silently truncate a typed fractional value
description:
Found during bead ic884.1 (build 0109). In contract, so nothing breaks, but it is silent normalization of exactly the kind the PO ruled against when choosing reject-over-normalize for ic884.1.

Several renumber inputs parse with parseInt and are guarded >= 1: Sort and Renumber, Renumber All Groups and its per-group overrides, the group reorder custom number, per-group bulk-create starts, and frontend/src/components/moveChannelNumbering.ts.

Typing 1.5 into any of them yields 1, with no warning and no indication anything was changed. The operator asked for one thing and got another.

These are integer-only by design and produce a strict subset of the canonical contract, so they cannot generate an out-of-contract value and ic884.1 deliberately left them alone. That scoping was right. But the PO's decision on ic884.1 was explicitly that out-of-contract input should be REJECTED WITH A CLEAR ERROR rather than silently altered, and these inputs do the opposite for the same class of mistake.

FIX: either reject a fractional value in these inputs with the same operator-facing sentence ic884.1 introduced, or accept and honour it. Do not keep truncating silently. If these fields are genuinely integer-only for a reason (they seed sequential renumbering), rejecting with 'whole numbers only' is the smaller change and matches the reject-not-normalize principle.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). Every renumber-start input now rejects a fractional value with WHOLE_CHANNEL_NUMBER_RULE_MESSAGE instead of truncating it: Sort and Renumber, Renumber All Groups and its per-group overrides, group reorder custom number, cross-group move, mass renumber, and moveChannelNumbering.ts. Each dialog derives one value and one error that the preview, the disabled guard and the handler all read, so they cannot disagree. Two further sites in channelPipeline/ActionEditor.tsx were fixed in the same pass (one of them was hiding ay3iq's new backend rejection). RuleBuilder now refuses to save while any action field is displaying a rejection, via a validity registry, and actions are keyed by stable identity rather than array index.

title: Password-reset success path logs the full account email address
description:
Found during the cb1e1 rebase. PII hygiene, no credential exposure.

backend/auth/routes.py:1452: logger.info('[AUTH] Password reset email sent to: %s', user.email)
backend/auth/routes.py:223:  the same message inside the send helper, for the same event.

Bead cb1e1 moved the FAILURE branch of this flow to a user_id= shape, matching the convention every other [AUTH] line in the file uses. The SUCCESS branch was deliberately left alone in that PR, because changing :1452 while :223 still logged the address would have made the pair more confusing rather than less.

So today a successful reset writes a subscriber's email address into the log twice for one event. That is the same log operators paste into GitHub issues, which is the premise cb1e1 itself was filed on.

Also worth noting: the duplication overstates send counts for anyone reading the log as a metric.

FIX: collapse to one line in the user_id= shape. The helper at :223 only receives to_email, so surfacing a user id there needs either a parameter change or moving the log up into the handler; pick one deliberately rather than adding a second parameter to carry both.

Not covered by any existing child of the nkwh0 'Secrets and PII hygiene' epic; checked. Adjacent to nymj6 but distinct.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #869 (merge e35b03ad, v0.18.1-0110). Collapsed to one line in the user_id= shape. Chose to move the log up into the handler rather than pass a user id down: send_password_reset_email receives only an address, a token and a base URL, so a user id would be a parameter it uses for nothing but a log line, while the handler already holds the user and knows the event. Regression test drives the real handler to smtplib.SMTP.sendmail and asserts the address appears in no log record the request emitted, and that exactly one success line is written.

title: Auth login-failure logs echo an unbounded caller-supplied username
description:
Found during the Codex-review fix pass on bead upkp1 (PR #865). Same log-hygiene class as the X-Forwarded-For / User-Agent finding fixed there, on the half that was left alone.

backend/auth/routes.py:648-670: login_request.username is written into three WARNING lines with no length limit and no charset restriction.

PR #865 fixed the ADDRESS side of auth logging: client addresses are now rendered from ipaddress rather than echoed, and free-form fields have secret-shaped runs redacted and are reduced to printable ASCII before truncation. The username side of the same log lines was not in that scope.

An unauthenticated caller controls this value entirely. It is a smaller target than the header finding, because a username is displayed rather than secret, but the shape is identical: caller-chosen text reaching a log line unbounded and unsanitized. A caller can pad the log, and can put arbitrary text where an operator reads an identity.

FIX: route it through the same _log_safe_agent-style sanitizer PR #865 introduced, rather than writing a second one.

ALSO, lower and recorded here rather than filed separately: the refresh-refusal dedupe map (_refresh_denial_log_state) is caller-keyed, so a caller sending varied VALID addresses can churn it. It is bounded at 256 pairs, so this is log noise rather than a leak or a memory issue.

title: Rule analyzer emits RULE_REFERENCES_DISABLED_NORMALIZATION_GROUP but no operator doc describes it
description:
Found while verifying the docs fix on PR #850 (bead rtst2.1). PRE-EXISTING, not caused by that branch; recorded so the count stops drifting.

THE GAP. The rule analyzer surfaces NINE finding codes. Six are emitted by backend/channel_pipeline_rule_analyzer.py itself (ANDOR_DROPS_GUARD, MERGE_SCOPE_NOT_TARGET_GROUP, MERGE_SCOPE_PINNED_TO_OTHER_GROUP, MERGE_STREAMS_NO_TARGET_CHANNELS, RULE_HAS_NO_HOPE_OF_MATCHING, RULE_REFERENCES_DISABLED_NORMALIZATION_GROUP) and three come from backend/regex_lint.py and are surfaced through the same rail (REGEX_TRIVIALLY_MATCHES_ALL, OPERATOR_VALUE_LOOKS_LIKE_REGEX, REGEX_REDUNDANT_ESCAPE_CARET).

docs/user_guide/channel-pipeline/debugging-rules.md documents EIGHT of the nine. RULE_REFERENCES_DISABLED_NORMALIZATION_GROUP has no section anywhere in the operator guide.

CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING. On origin/dev before PR #850, the analyzer already emitted RULE_REFERENCES_DISABLED_NORMALIZATION_GROUP (2 occurrences in the module) and the operator guide already did not mention it (0 occurrences), while its heading read 'The seven finding codes'. PR #850 added a genuinely new code and correctly moved the documented count from seven to eight. The off-by-one is therefore unchanged in magnitude by that branch; it is older.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING PARAGRAPH. An operator who hits this finding in the rule builder gets a code with no entry in the guide the UI points them at. It is also the reason the documented count and the emitted count disagree, so the next person to add a code inherits an ambiguous baseline and cannot tell whether the prose count is a deliberate subset or simply stale.

SCOPE.
1. Write the missing section in debugging-rules.md following the established four-part shape used by the other eight (What it looks like / Why it is wrong / Worked example / How to fix it), and correct the count prose to nine across the files that state it: conditions-and-actions.md, test-a-rule.md, channel-pipeline/index.md.
2. Decide and record whether the count is meant to include the regex_lint-sourced codes. The docs currently do include them, which is reasonable operator-facing behaviour, but nothing says so and that is what makes the number fragile.
3. Consider a test that pins the documented code set against the emitted set so the two cannot drift again. That is the durable fix; items 1 and 2 are one-off corrections. Note the count appears in prose form ('the eight finding codes') as well as anchor form, and prose is what no linter catches.

Verification commands used: grep -oE 'code="[A-Z_]+"' backend/channel_pipeline_rule_analyzer.py | sort -u, and the same against git show origin/dev:<path>.

title: detect-secrets' TelegramBotTokenDetector matches in isolation but reports zero end-to-end; something in the filter pipeline eats every hit
description:
Found while building the ECM secrets arm under bead h9av3, 2026-08-10. Recorded rather than chased, by PO decision. Our own rule covers the gap meanwhile, so this is an investigation, not an exposure.

THE ANOMALY. detect-secrets 1.5.0's TelegramBotTokenDetector is enabled by default and its regex is \d{8,10}:[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}. Called DIRECTLY the detector fires correctly: 1 finding per call, confirmed in isolation.

But an end-to-end 'detect-secrets scan' returns ZERO findings across three token variants times bare / assignment / API-URL contexts times .py and .md file types. Eighteen combinations, no hits. Reproducible.

Something in the default filter pipeline is dropping every hit before it reaches the report. The engineer did not chase the mechanism, and the behaviour being reproducible is what justified keeping our own telegram-bot-token rule rather than deferring to the library.

WHY IT IS WORTH UNDERSTANDING, beyond this one detector. We adopted detect-secrets as the general layer specifically so our own arm could shrink to ECM-specific shapes. That division of labour assumes the library's detectors actually fire in the configuration we run them in. This is one measured case where a detector that appears enabled contributes nothing. If the cause is general rather than specific to this detector, the same silence could apply to others we are relying on, and we would not know.

Candidate causes worth eliminating in order: a heuristic filter such as is_indirect_reference, is_likely_id_string, or is_templated_secret rejecting the value; a verified-only code path suppressing unverified findings; the plugin being present in the plugin list but filtered out of the run; or a baseline-related exclusion. None of these are confirmed, they are starting points.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: run 'detect-secrets scan --list-all-plugins' and compare against what the scan actually loads, then bisect the filter chain with 'detect-secrets scan --no-filter' style options or by disabling filters individually, on a fixture holding a known-shaped token. If the cause turns out to be general, widen this bead; if it is specific to the Telegram detector, note it and close.

CONTEXT AND SCOPE. Our arm's own telegram-bot-token rule is anchored on the same shape and is tested, so nothing is currently uncovered. This bead is about trusting the general layer, not about a live gap. Related: h9av3 carries the full secrets-audit findings, and the PEM and JWT rules were deliberately CUT from our arm on evidence that detect-secrets' PrivateKeyDetector and JwtTokenDetector do fire on both end-to-end, which is the same class of claim this bead casts doubt on for one detector. Those two were verified working; this one was verified not.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9); all verified in code, not just in CHANGELOG. 2896r.16: TabNavigation.tsx:125-130 renders the Settings drill-in nav with a 'Back to main navigation' control, regression-tested in TabNavigation.test.tsx (commit 73a02a22). 2896r.17: App.tsx:2601-2617 builds routeHeading from settingsSectionHeading() into PageHeader; in-pane headings removed. 2896r.21: StatsTab.tsx:875 wraps the summary counts in RouteHeaderSlot name='status', portalled into the shared route header (commit 661031f6). cujyo: StickySectionNav.tsx:38 scrollWithinContainer() replaces scrollIntoView so the shell no longer scrolls, with a regression test asserting scrollIntoView is never called. vh6hh: ChannelManagerTab.tsx:552 passes defaultLeftWidth={50} explicitly at the call site. 1bpl8: root-caused — detect-secrets drops VERIFIED_FALSE results via is_ignored_due_to_verification_policies, and the Telegram plugin's verify() is a live network call; 9 of 27 plugins behave this way. ECM's own gate is immune because check_secrets.py:149 and :332 both pass --no-verify. Residual: comment that --no-verify is load-bearing for confidentiality.

title: Narrow-viewport @media copies of .filters-bar remain in JournalTab.css and M3UChangesTab.css
description:
Deliberately left out of scope by the engineer working bead albfq on branch fix/ux-batch-0057, and flagged rather than silently taken.

That branch deleted the two BASE '.filters-bar' declarations from JournalTab.css and M3UChangesTab.css, because only WatchHttoryPanel.tsx:145 renders that class anywhere in the tree, and wrote the missing flex-shrink:0 at the real owner (.watch-history-panel .filters-bar in WatchHistoryPanel.css).

The narrow-viewport '@media' copies of the same class in both files are equally dead by the same argument. They were left alone because deleting them changes the panel's sub-600px layout, which is outside what bead albfq scoped. Their audit baseline entries in frontend/src/cssAudits/sharedClassChunkLeak.audit.test.ts still track them.

Two things to settle when picking this up:

1. Confirm they are still dead after the base-rule deletion. The reasoning is the same but should be re-verified rather than inherited.

2. Coordinate with the modal-chrome breakpoint work. Beads 79uf8 and hw8e3 are landing a canonical 650px breakpoint across the modal estate to actually reach the WCAG 1.4.4 200 percent zoom point, on the finding that the existing 600px value only fires beyond 213 percent zoom. If these '.filters-bar' media queries use 600px they are subject to the same argument, so deleting them versus retargeting them is not an obvious call. Do not delete on autopilot.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Drop the 'coordinate with modal-chrome breakpoint work' caveat. Beads 79uf8 and hw8e3 are both CLOSED (shipped PR #829, canonical breakpoint at 700px), and the coordination concern never actually applied: modalResponsiveBreakpoints.audit.test.ts scopes modalStyleFiles() to files imported by components rendering ModalOverlay, and JournalTab.css / M3UChangesTab.css are tab panels, not modals, so they were never in that audit's scope. Core claim intact: the @media copies survive at JournalTab.css:547, :567 and M3UChangesTab.css:555, :583.

title: e2e/m3u-changes.spec.ts:44 asserts .filters-bar is visible on a tab that renders .filters-summary-row
description:
A dead assertion, found during the fix/ux-batch-0057 work and confirmed present in BOTH the before and after trees, so it is not caused by that branch.

e2e/m3u-changes.spec.ts:44 asserts that '.filters-bar' is visible on the M3U Changes tab. That tab renders '.filters-summary-row'. The class '.filters-bar' appears nowhere in M3UChangesTab.tsx's markup.

This connects to bead albfq, which established that '.filters-bar' is rendered by exactly ONE component in the whole tree, WatchHistoryPanel.tsx:145, while JournalTab.css and M3UChangesTab.css both DECLARED it. Those two dead declarations have now been deleted on branch fix/ux-batch-0057, and the missing flex-shrink:0 was written at the real owner.

So the spec was asserting against a class that the tab never rendered, and which was only ever present as a dead CSS declaration in that tab's stylesheet. Either the assertion has been silently passing for the wrong reason, or it has been failing and nobody looked. Determine which, then either repoint it at '.filters-summary-row' or delete it.

Worth checking while in there whether other e2e specs assert on classes their target route does not render. This one surfaced only because someone deleted the dead CSS underneath it.

title: [spike] WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow: is ECM usable at 400% zoom (320px CSS viewport)?
description:
Deferred out of the modal-chrome work (beads 79uf8 and hw8e3) by the UX designer, who recommended it be its own spike rather than folded in.

WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) requires usability at 200% zoom. On the PO's stated 1280x720 minimum that is a 640px CSS viewport, and the 79uf8/hw8e3 work addresses it by canonicalising the modal estate on a 650px breakpoint.

WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow) is stricter and separate: it implies usability at 400% zoom, i.e. a 320px CSS viewport on the same 1280px floor, with no two-dimensional scrolling. Nothing in ECM has ever been tested there. The UX designer measured no narrower than 460-582px and explicitly declined to extrapolate.

QUESTION FOR THE SPIKE: does ECM claim 1.4.10 conformance, should it, and what would it cost? The answer plausibly ranges from 'a handful of breakpoints' to 'the operator workspace shell fundamentally assumes a wide viewport', and the point of a spike is to find out which before anyone commits to it.

Relevant context: mobile is explicitly out of scope per PO decision, and the supported floor is 1280x720. That makes 1.4.10 a deliberate accessibility choice rather than an incidental one, which is exactly why it deserves a decision rather than a silent omission. A self-hosted operator tool has a different obligation profile than a public consumer site; say what that profile is as part of the finding.

Measured baseline to start from, from the 79uf8 work: at 200% zoom fixed modal chrome already consumes 31.9% of viewport height (115px of 360px). At 400% the arithmetic gets considerably worse.

title: restore-initial correctness silently depends on poolclass=StaticPool; document it and add a non-mocked token test
description:
Two informational findings from the security review of branch fix/lf29s-restore-initial-auth-gate, grouped because both are cheap and both are about keeping a verified property verified.

1. STATICPOOL COUPLING. The lf29s fix introduced session: Session = Depends(get_session) at backend/routers/backup.py:2308, so the endpoint now holds an open SQLite read transaction across _restore_from_zip's close_db() then JOURNAL_DB_FILE.write_bytes() then init_db() sequence.

The reviewer hypothesised this would prevent the WAL checkpoint and let a stale journal.db-wal replay over the restored database. Under SQLAlchemy's DEFAULT QueuePool this REPRODUCES EXACTLY: the control with no session restored correctly, the variant holding a session silently reverted to the pre-restore data while reporting integrity_check=ok.

It does NOT reproduce in ECM, because backend/database.py:1232 uses poolclass=StaticPool, whose dispose() closes the single shared connection regardless of checkout state. Confirmed in a faithful StaticPool repro and again in three isolated end-to-end scenarios.

So the endpoint is correct today, but its correctness silently depends on a pooling choice made elsewhere for unrelated reasons. A future concurrency change moving off StaticPool would make restore-initial return 200 while silently discarding the restore — the worst possible failure mode for a restore. Add a comment at backend/database.py:1232 and beside the new dependency recording the coupling.

2. NON-MOCKED TOKEN TEST. The new tests in backend/tests/routers/test_backup.py patch routers.backup.get_current_user and routers.backup.get_token_from_request, so NO test exercises real token validation. A change to decode_token, to signature verification, or to the is_active check would not be caught by this suite. test_rejects_mcp_service_principal patches the very predicate under test, and test_rejects_invalid_token_when_a_user_row_exists patches get_current_user to raise, so both pin wiring rather than behaviour.

The reviewer closed the gap manually and verified the property holds today: a real token minted via auth.tokens.create_access_token for a non-admin row is refused, a forged token is refused, a valid-signature token for a nonexistent uid is refused, and a real static MCP key is refused. Add at least one non-mocked test so the property stays verified rather than being re-proven by hand each time.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5). Both halves, and the reviewer's framing condition on this bead was honored: the property named is 'is_admin is resolved from the DATABASE ROW, not from the token body.'

STATICPOOL COUPLING: recorded at BOTH ends (backend/database.py:1228-1256 and routers/backup.py:2352-2369) and pinned by a test, not left as a comment nobody reads. The thing that regresses is a one-word edit in database.py by someone who never opens backup.py, and nothing else in the suite would catch it because restore-initial's own tests patch close_db/init_db out entirely and cannot see the WAL. The pin runs the real init_db against a temp DB and asserts isinstance(engine.pool, StaticPool) with a failure message naming restore-initial and the remediation. A second test records the divergent dispose() semantics the claim rests on, so it is not folklore.

NON-MOCKED TOKENS: new backend/tests/routers/test_9kwzp5_restore_initial_real_tokens.py, 13 tests minting real tokens via auth.tokens.create_access_token. Proven meaningful by implementing the reviewer's exact named refactor (decode_token_safe(token).get('is_admin')) and watching 4 go red, including test_an_is_admin_claim_in_the_token_body_confers_nothing, the direct privilege-escalation demonstration. Before this file that refactor shipped green through the entire suite.

Codex confirmed these tests would fail if reverted.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEWER CONDITION ON THIS BEAD'S FRAMING (2026-08-10), attached when W2 was accepted as deferrable rather than blocking.

Do not let this bead read as a generic 'add better tests' nicety, or it will be groomed to the bottom and never done. It should name the specific unpinned property:

  'is_admin is resolved from the DATABASE ROW, not from the token body.'

That is the property that matters and the one nothing currently guards. The reviewer traced it manually and confirmed it holds TODAY: _caller_is_human_admin -> get_current_user -> decode_token gives HS256-pinned decode, expiry enforcement, jti revocation, sub to DB lookup, is_active enforcement, is_admin read off the DB row, and MCP-principal rejection.

The gap is that nothing would FAIL if a future refactor swapped get_current_user for something like decode_token_safe(token).get('is_admin'). That change would ship green through the entire existing suite, because every test in TestRestoreInitialIdentityGate patches routers.backup.get_current_user and routers.backup.get_token_from_request, so no test ever presents a real signed token.

To be fair to the existing tests, they DO pin the wiring of every branch, and both reintroduction routes named in the original review brief still go red. The gap is behavioural, not structural.

Minimum to close: one non-mocked test that mints a real token via auth.tokens.create_access_token for a seeded NON-ADMIN row and asserts 403, and one for a seeded ADMIN row asserting 200.

title: Set Logo from M3U and Set Logo from EPG write immediately but sit inside Edit Mode's staged toolbar
description:
Found while writing the Channels & Streams user guide section.

The bulk actions 'Set Logo from M3U' and 'Set Logo from EPG' (selection toolbar, More menu) call api.updateChannel per selected channel with no staging: frontend/src/components/ChannelsPane.tsx:1764 and :1816.

The problem is context, not the write itself. These items live in the Edit Mode selection toolbar alongside actions that ARE staged (Move to group, Normalize Names, Sort Streams). They are not counted in Edit Mode's change count, are not reverted by Cancel or Discard, and are not covered by Undo. An operator who has built a mental model of 'Edit Mode stages everything until I Apply' will reasonably expect these to stage too, and will expect Cancel to undo them.

Applied across a large selection this is not recoverable through the UI.

Related existing behaviour: 'Create new channel group' is also immediate (ChannelsPane.tsx:2848) and already documented as such.

Options: stage them like their toolbar neighbours; or confirm before applying; or mark them visibly as immediate in the menu. The new user guide documents the current behaviour prominently in channels-streams/logos.md and adds a row to bulk-edit.md's staged-vs-immediate table, but the affordance remains inconsistent with its surroundings.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111) as part of enhancedchannelmanager-kz089, per this bead's own NOTES: 'Fold bead i4yk1 in here, same defect class, same toolbar, one fix shape.'

Set Logo from M3U and Set Logo from EPG now stage as updateChannel {logo_id} operations alongside their toolbar neighbours (ChannelsPane.tsx assignLogoToChannel). They are counted in Edit Mode's change count, reverted by Discard, and covered by Undo/Redo - the three things this bead said they were not.

EVIDENCE THIS BEAD'S SPECIFIC COMPLAINT IS CLOSED, not just its parent's: the bead's objection was context, not the write - 'these items live in the Edit Mode selection toolbar alongside actions that ARE staged (Move to group, Normalize Names, Sort Streams)'. Those neighbours are unchanged, and the two logo actions now behave identically to them.

The bead's related note that 'Create new channel group is also immediate' is stale and was struck during kz089's rescope - it stages as of bead vtapf, build 0052.

The bead offered three options (stage / confirm / mark visibly). The PO chose staging for this class, reserving the confirm treatment for the three actions that genuinely cannot stage.

title: Group drag-reorder in Channel Manager looks persistent but is discarded on reload
description:
Found while writing the Channels & Streams user guide section.

In Channel Manager's Edit Mode you can drag channel groups to reorder them. The order is held in component-local React state: 'groupOrder' is a useState in frontend/src/components/ChannelsPane.tsx:1232, and its only setter is at :4266. Nothing reads or writes it to storage or the API.

On reload, groups are re-sorted by lowest channel number (ChannelsPane.tsx:3453-3474) and the operator's arrangement is gone.

Impact: the gesture is indistinguishable from a persistent one. There is no unsaved-changes indicator, the group order is not counted as an Edit Mode change, and Apply does not persist it. An operator who spends time arranging groups loses that work silently on the next page load.

The durable equivalent is the renumber offered by the Reorder Group dialog, which does write. The new user guide documents that distinction, but the affordance itself is still misleading.

Options: persist group order, or remove the drag affordance, or surface that ordering is derived from channel numbers and only renumbering is durable.
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Narrower than the title. The drag ALWAYS opens the Reorder Group dialog (ChannelsPane.tsx:3792-3803), which DEFAULTS to renumbering (:3801 sets 'suggested'), and :4356-4388 stages channel_number updates through onStageUpdateChannel. Since reload sorting derives from lowest channel number, the default path does make the arrangement durable through Apply All. The loss is confined to the operator choosing 'Keep current numbers' (:6481-6493), which sets local groupOrder state and writes nothing, with no unsaved-changes indicator and no Edit Mode change counted. Rescope to: either persist groupOrder, or say in that radio's sublabel that the resulting order is display-only.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #870 (merge f2ad4e9f, build 0.18.1-0111). Commit 9823968c (KEEP_CURRENT_NUMBERS_SUBLABEL in ChannelsPane.tsx).

PO decision: do NOT persist groupOrder. Make the radio's sublabel say the resulting order is display-only.

Closed against the RESCOPED version in the NOTES, not the title. The title says drag-reorder is discarded on reload; that is wrong. The drag always opens the Reorder Group dialog, which DEFAULTS to renumbering and stages channel_number updates through onStageUpdateChannel - and since reload sorting derives from lowest channel number, the default path IS durable through Apply All. The loss was confined to choosing 'Keep current numbers', which set local state and wrote nothing with no unsaved-changes indicator.

So the fix is honest copy on that one radio, not persistence. An operator reading it now understands the arrangement will not survive a reload and that renumbering is the durable option.

TEST HONESTY, recorded because it matters for anyone re-verifying: the test is a copy pin on the exported constant, NOT a DOM test. The dialog opens only via a @dnd-kit group drag, which needs real element rects jsdom does not provide, and no suite in this repo drives that library. The engineer labelled it as such in-file rather than letting it read as rendered proof.

title: MCP tool clear_auto_created says it deletes channels; the endpoint only clears a flag
description:
Found while writing the Troubleshooting user guide section.

The MCP tool description in mcp-server/tools/channels.py:1008 and 1024-1027 tells the model (and therefore the operator) that clear_auto_created DELETES auto-created channels. The endpoint it actually calls, backend/routers/channels.py:2283-2286, only clears the auto_created flag on those channels. Nothing is deleted.

This matters more than a normal docstring error because the consumer is an LLM acting on the operator's behalf. An agent that believes the tool is destructive will either refuse to call it without confirmation it does not need, or will call it expecting cleanup that never happens and then report the library as cleaned when it is not.

Fix is a docstring correction, not a behaviour change, unless the intent really was deletion. Confirm which before editing.

title: Event Sync Review step clips the Best candidate column inside the right-hand rail
description:
Found while recapturing docs/images/event_sync/ against the current UI (bead enhancedchannelmanager-gk4d0).

On the Review step (step 4) of the Event Sync rule editor, the preview detail renders inside the roughly 355px right-hand rail of a 1000px modal-xxl. '.event-sync-table-wrap table { width: 100% }' makes the 5-column 'Unmatched secondary streams' table squeeze to fit rather than scroll horizontally, so the final 'Best candidate' column is clipped at the rail edge.

Best candidate is the column an operator actually needs on that screen: it is what tells them why a secondary stream did not match. It is also the column docs/event_sync.md previously called out by name in its alt text, which had to be reworded because the value is no longer readable.

Suggested fix: give .event-sync-table-wrap an overflow-x: auto and drop the width: 100% on the inner table so the table keeps its natural column widths and scrolls, matching how other wide tables in the app behave. Alternatively widen the rail on the Review step, since step 4 is the only step that renders full detail (compact={currentStep !== 4}).
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Half the suggested fix is already a no-op: .event-sync-table-wrap already has overflow-x: auto (EventSyncPreviewPanel.css:229-231, landed in cd9f474a). The actionable defect is the second half: .event-sync-table-wrap table has width: 100% (:235-236), which pins the table to the rail width so overflow-x never engages and the 5-to-6 column table compresses instead of scrolling. Fix is to drop width:100% or add a min-width. Per geometry-defect discipline, prove with a Playwright check at the 1000px modal-xxl width.

title: MCP settings UI renders an em-dash in a user-facing status string
description:
frontend/src/components/settings/MCPSettingsSection.tsx:188 renders 'MCP server online — N tools available'. Found during the documentation em-dash sweep by a writer working docs/runbooks/mcp-release-verification.md, which quotes the string verbatim.

The PO's no-em-dash directive was scoped to documentation, so this was deliberately NOT changed. Product copy is a separate decision and the change also touches the component's test file, which asserts the string.

If the rule is extended to UI copy: update the component, its test, and the verbatim quote in docs/runbooks/mcp-release-verification.md:111 together, or the runbook's grep-target stops matching.

title: An empty hidden channel group cannot be deleted — ECM reports M3U sync settings that are not there
description:
Found during the Channel Manager tutorial work (bead gsnw0.2). Left on the test instance because it could not be removed.

Channel group "Default Group" (id=1304) was created as a SIDE EFFECT of create_channel without a group argument. It is empty and hidden. It cannot be deleted:

  delete_channel_group          refused, twice, including with delete_channels=True
  delete_orphaned_groups        did not remove it

ECM refuses on the grounds that "M3U sync settings" are attached — for a group that is empty, hidden, and was auto-created moments earlier by a channel-creation call that did not name a group.

TWO SEPARATE THINGS TO ESTABLISH, and they may have different answers:
  1. Why does creating a channel without a group silently create a persistent group? If that is intended, it should be visible and removable. If it is a fallback, it should probably reuse an existing default rather than minting a record.
  2. Why does the delete guard fire? Either the group genuinely has sync settings attached that nothing surfaces — in which case the guard is right and the UI is hiding the reason — or the guard is checking the wrong thing and refuses a group it should allow.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE STRAY RECORD: an operator can reach this state through ordinary use, and once there they have an undeletable object in their lineup with no on-screen explanation of why the delete failed and no path to fix it from the UI. The failure message names a cause the operator cannot see or act on.

REPRODUCTION should be cheap: create a channel via the API without specifying a group, then attempt to delete the group that appears.

The record is still present on the test instance — it is inert, so it was left rather than forced, but it is available to whoever picks this up.

title: link_channel_epg rejects the epg_data_id its own docstring recommends
description:
Observed while verifying the EPG tutorials (bead gsnw0.7). Not root-caused; reproduce before fixing.

Calling link_channel_epg with epg_data_id set to the id displayed on a match candidate in the Bulk EPG Assignment UI returned:

  400 Invalid pk ... object does not exist

The MCP tools own docstring recommends exactly that usage — take the candidates displayed epg_id and pass it as epg_data_id. Linking by tvg_id instead worked correctly.

LIKELY BUT UNCONFIRMED: an id-space mismatch. ECM proxies Dispatcharr, and several entities in this system carry both a Dispatcharr id and an ECM-local primary key. If the match candidate surfaces one and link_channel_epg expects the other, every caller following the docstring hits this. The alternative is a stale-candidate fluke, where the id was valid when the match ran and gone by the time the link was attempted.

WHY IT IS WORTH CHASING DESPITE BEING P3: the docstring is the interface contract for an MCP tool, so an automation author has no way to discover the correct usage except by hitting the 400. And if it IS an id-space mismatch, the same confusion probably exists in other tools that accept a "pk" sourced from a proxied entity — one wrong docstring usually means the pattern was copied.

FIRST STEP: determine which id space the match candidates epg_id belongs to and which one link_channel_epg validates against. If they differ, fix the docstring AND consider accepting both, since callers already in the wild will be passing whichever one the docs told them to.

The tvg_id path works and is what the tutorials document, so no operator-facing guidance depends on this being fixed.

title: shared_epg_links is computed, returned and tested — and no UI ever renders it
description:
Found while writing the EPG tutorials (bead gsnw0.7), and confirmed independently.

backend/epg_matching.py defines find_shared_epg_links(), the /epg/match response carries a shared_epg_links payload, and backend/tests/routers/test_epg.py:2566 asserts its presence and shape. So it is computed, serialised, and guarded by a test.

NOTHING IN THE FRONTEND CONSUMES IT. A repo-wide grep for shared_epg_links / sharedEpgLinks across frontend/src returns zero hits. BulkEPGAssignModal destructures only exact / multiple / none / summary. There is no UI surface for it anywhere.

WHY THIS SURFACED: docs/user_guide/epg/finding-mislinked-channels.md told operators the match preview shows an inline "shared EPG links" summary. It does not, and never has. The doc has been corrected with a dated note rather than the claim being silently deleted — a reader who tried to follow it was hunting for a control that does not exist.

THE TEST IS THE INTERESTING PART. A passing test asserts the field is present, so the backend contract is protected while the feature it exists for is unreachable. That is a guard proving something nobody can use — the same shape as several findings this session, where green meant less than it appeared to.

DECIDE, do not default:
  - if shared-link detection is wanted, the work is a UI surface in the bulk-assign flow, and the backend half is already done and tested
  - if it is not wanted, remove the computation, the response field and the test together, and note it in the changelog since it is a response-shape change that an API consumer could be reading
Either is defensible. What is not defensible is leaving a tested, documented, unreachable feature in place — which is how the doc came to describe it in the first place.

Note the whole-fleet MCP/API audit IS a real way to see shared links today. So the capability exists for an API caller; it is only the UI that never landed.

title: TLS DNS-provider credentials are stored in plaintext while cloud-target credentials are encrypted
description:
FOUND ON A LIVE INSTANCE during GitHub #755 work. Reported to the PO immediately; values were never printed or copied.

/config/tls_settings.json stores DNS-01 ACME provider credentials as plaintext JSON. Confirmed present on the running test instance: aws_access_key_id in AWS AKIA format, aws_secret_access_key as a 40-character secret, and dns_api_token, alongside the ACME and certificate settings.

WHY THIS IS INCONSISTENT RATHER THAN MERELY UNFORTUNATE: this codebase already has a credential encryption facility. Cloud backup targets encrypt their credentials with Fernet, and bead m40pn added a startup probe that checks that keys file mode and ownership and logs loudly at ERROR when they are wrong. TLS DNS credentials get none of that -- same class of secret, same config directory, different treatment.

BLAST RADIUS IS LARGER THAN ECM. A Route53 DNS-01 credential can create and delete records in the hosted zone it is scoped to. If the key is scoped broadly rather than to a single zone, it reaches further. This is not an ECM-internal token that only matters inside the app; it is an external cloud credential whose compromise is a customer problem regardless of what ECM does next.

EXPOSURE PATHS WORTH CHECKING, not just the file itself:
  - is tls_settings.json included in backups or the DBAS export? A plaintext credential inside an archive that gets copied to a cloud target is a second, wider copy.
  - does any API response return these fields, even to an admin? A settings GET that echoes them puts them in browser memory and any proxy log.
  - what are the file mode and ownership, and does anything probe them the way m40pn probes the Fernet key?
  - are they written to logs on a renewal failure?

SCOPE: bring these under the same encryption and the same startup integrity probe as the cloud-target credentials, or state deliberately why DNS credentials are different and document that decision. Do not simply chmod the file and call it done -- the inconsistency with the Fernet path is the finding.

SEPARATE AND IMMEDIATE, for the PO rather than for this bead: the credential currently on the test instance should be treated as exposed and rotated, since it has been sitting in plaintext in a container filesystem.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #864 (merge 449c5bd5). Scoped to the three checks the recalibration COMMENT specified, not the P1 description. Fernet encryption deliberately NOT added, per PO decision 2026-08-13.

CHECK 1, does any API response echo a stored credential: GET /api/tls/settings masks all three fields to *** plus last 4, verified at source and now pinned by a test that also asserts no full value survives anywhere in the payload. No other route and no other router returns a stored TLS credential. CLEAN, as the comment predicted it might be.

CHECK 2, do the values reach logs: TWO REAL PATHS, both reproduced rather than theorised, both now closed.
(a) backend/main.py's 422 validation-error handler logged the raw request body, exc.body and pydantic's per-error input at ERROR, and echoed them in the response. POST /api/tls/configure and /test-dns-provider both carry dns_api_token, aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key in the body, so ANY TLS settings save rejected for an unrelated reason wrote live credentials in clear into the log. Note exc.errors() carries the ENTIRE body as input on a missing-field error, so redacting the body alone would not have sufficed. mask_secrets did not rescue this: its key/value rule needs the key adjacent to the separator and JSON puts a closing quote in between (now filed as enhancedchannelmanager-w9vv0).
(b) A Cloudflare token containing a character illegal in an HTTP header value, a trailing newline being the copy-paste shape, makes h11 raise LocalProtocolError whose str() is 'Illegal header value b\'Bearer <the whole token>\''. Reproduced with a synthetic token. That string was logged verbatim and, on the renewal path, stored into last_renewal_error and served from GET /api/tls/status, the weakest-gated route in the router.
Fixed by a new backend/tls/redaction.py that deletes credential values BY IDENTITY before running the pattern sweep (charset-independent, unlike the regex), applied in both DNS providers, the renewal path, the settings loader and the router. Route53 redacted too as defence in depth, though botocore was checked empirically and does not echo the key.

CHECK 3, startup probe: verify_tls_settings_integrity_at_startup() in backend/tls/settings.py:253-345, called from the same startup block as m40pn's Fernet-key probe. Checks mode and ownership only, never opens the contents (asserted by a test). Repairs mode drift to 0600 at WARNING; ERROR on failed repair and on a foreign owner under a non-root process; never raises, matching m40pn.

SCOPE ESCALATION WORTH KNOWING: the 422 handler fix initially covered only /api/auth and /api/tls. Codex rated the remainder HIGH; walking the live app found SIXTEEN credential-bearing write routes still exposed, not the four Codex named by reading. The prefix allowlist was then deleted entirely: every request body is redacted on every path, so a credential-bearing route added tomorrow fails safe. Field-level diagnostics (loc, msg, type) survive, proven live.

RESIDUAL, filed: enhancedchannelmanager-boltm covers the one remaining carrier, a validator that interpolates its input into a ValueError message. No current validator on a credential field does this; Codex confirmed. Also filed enhancedchannelmanager-9hdfr for the probe duplication this knowingly created with cloud_storage/crypto.py.

No live credential value appears in the diff, tests or any report; verified by SHA-256 comparison of live values against every credential-length substring of the full diff, 802 tokens scanned, 0 hits.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
RECALIBRATED after the PO explained the purpose, and after checking the exposure paths. The original P1 was overstated; downgraded to P3.

WHAT IS NOT A PROBLEM, established rather than assumed:
- The credential PRESENCE is by design. It is a Route53 DNS-01 ACME credential; ECM must hold it and must use it unattended to renew certificates. There is no version of this feature where the key is absent.
- NOT in git. Not tracked, and zero occurrences of the live values across every patch on every ref. The only AKIA strings in the repo are AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, the AWS documentation example, in test fixtures.
- NOT in backups. BACKUP_DIRS is ["uploads/logos", "tls", "m3u_uploads"] and sweeps DIRECTORIES; tls_settings.json sits at the config root, not inside tls/. Nothing in routers/backup.py, dbas/ or tasks/ references it. settings.json goes in redacted and journal.db scrubbed.
- File mode is already 0600, owner-only.

WHY ENCRYPTING AT REST IS WORTH LESS HERE THAN IT FIRST APPEARS, and this is the honest part: ECM has to decrypt this unattended to renew a certificate, so the Fernet key must live in the same config directory. An attacker who can read tls_settings.json can almost always read the key file too. That is the standard limitation of at-rest encryption for an unattended service, and it applies equally to the cloud-target credentials that DO use Fernet. Encrypting this buys consistency and a little defence-in-depth against a PARTIAL disclosure -- one file pasted into a support thread, one stray copy -- not protection against host compromise.

SO THE RESIDUAL VALUE IS MOSTLY IN THE TWO CHECKS THAT WERE NEVER DONE, and they are worth more than the encryption:
  1. Does any API response echo aws_secret_access_key or dns_api_token, even to an admin? That puts a live credential in browser memory and in any proxy log between them and ECM. Cheap to check, genuinely bad if true.
  2. Are these values written to logs on a renewal failure? Logs get pasted into GitHub issues -- this session imported two such issues, both containing log excerpts.

A third, cheap and worth doing regardless: extend the bead m40pn startup probe to cover this file mode and ownership the way it already covers the Fernet key. That catches a real misconfiguration (a 0644 after a manual edit or a restore) rather than defending against a threat the architecture cannot defend against.

Encryption itself: do it for consistency if the other work lands anyway, but it is not the reason to open this bead.

title: test_dedup_matcher find_candidate budget calls itself informational but asserts
description:
Small honesty gap found while reviewing sibling wall-clock budgets during bead ssvvl.

backend/tests/services/test_dedup_matcher.py:387 asserts a 5 ms per-call budget on find_candidate, while its own docstring says "Not a hard gate -- informational".

Both statements cannot be true. It is marked @pytest.mark.slow, and the CI gate runs -m "not slow" (.github/workflows/test.yml), so in CI it is genuinely not a gate. But the documented LOCAL gate is "cd backend && python -m pytest tests/" with no marker filter, which does run it -- and there it is a hard gate that fails the suite.

Measured during ssvvl: 0.49 ms per call against the 5 ms budget, so roughly 10x headroom. Not currently at risk, and materially different from the event-loop budgets fixed in bb4dc67c and 741d524a -- this one measures pure CPU, where contention degrades the number proportionally rather than catastrophically, so its signal band stays above its noise band.

FIX IS A DECISION, NOT A CHANGE OF NUMBER. Either make it genuinely informational -- report the timing without asserting, so it cannot fail a local run -- or drop the docstring claim and treat it as the gate it actually is. Do not simply raise the budget; 10x headroom is not the problem, the contradiction is.

Worth checking whether other tests in that file or its siblings carry the same "informational" wording while asserting, since the phrasing looks copied.

title: 532 controls in modals render at the UA default - 174 of them text-bearing
description:
Measured across the 82 harness-rendered dialogs: 532 form controls have NO author font-size at all, so they render at the UA default 13.3333px.

Most are icon-only buttons where it does not matter. The ones that do: 152 bare <input>, 12 <option>, 10 <select> — all text-bearing, all rendering at a size no rule declares.

Note this is a DIFFERENT defect from the font-family reset landed today. That fixed which typeface controls use; this is about size. A control with no author font-size will sit off the P1 scale forever and no grep finds it, because there is nothing to grep.

Related and already filed separately: off-scale shared classes that render inside dialogs but are owned by content-pane CSS — .custom-select-trigger/.custom-select-value (14px, 12 dialogs), .search-input (14.4px, 12 dialogs), .stat-value (24px, 9 dialogs), .checkbox-option/.radio-option (14.4px in common.css). Changing those touches pages already declared on the scale, so they need their own decision.

Sizing: Medium.
close_reason: Backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. 1z3fr: independently re-measured with mkdocs build --strict plus a link resolver over docs/user_guide/**; 0 actionable dead links remain, not 151 (73 files converted to absolute GitHub links). etrde: answered by commit b639b1d7 (channel-groups-and-tags.md:59-65 now distinguishes multi-select move from single-channel drag); its other target file legacy-task-reference.md was deleted in e58532ab. g4w7r: superseded by bead 3tflw's ratchet decision, where the PO explicitly declined to red-line CI on pre-existing violations; the codification half already landed in style_guide.md, and the sweep half is no longer the agreed target (current backlog is 180 instances if cleanup is ever rescoped). xhldy: epic shipped in commit 078c2075; both children closed; residual scope already tracked as ica5t, dlcl2, 4axyl, 7su2h, w8u1e. 4axyl: systemic cause closed by bead ul2tp, which added a global 'button, input, select, textarea { font-size: var(--type-body-size) }' rule at index.css:186-194 and fixed 516 elements across 77 of 81 dialogs. 7iid7: literal duplicate of 5dckk (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout); 5dckk survives. ur9we: both identified manifestations fixed, Obs.1 by 05bccf77 and Obs.3 by 494c8c6a (bead 7zp6g); Obs.2 never identified and presumed subsumed. kcyiq: wall-clock 'elapsed < 0.05' assertion replaced with a mechanism assertion (off-loop thread ident plus loop advancement) in commit bb4dc67c. rnzu0: diagnosis task complete, and the finding is that the three specs are stale, not the app; routeHierarchy.ts:44-58 deliberately emptied Channel Manager's settingsLinks under bead hmr0e, and the label is now 'Channel Defaults' in the Settings sidebar. Follow-up to update those assertions rides with hmr0e.

title: Modal breakpoints (500/600/700/820px) fire under browser zoom - review them, do not delete
close_reason: Shipped with 79uf8 in PR #829 (merge 567f0ef2): reviewed 820/700/500 modal breakpoint contract and full catalog guard.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
DO NOT ACT ON THIS BEAD AS WRITTEN. Its premise is false and following it would cause an accessibility regression.

The bead says nine @media blocks 'can never fire for a supported user' because all target <=820px and the support floor is 1280x720, and instructs deleting them.

WRONG. Browser zoom shrinks the CSS viewport. At 1280 physical px: 160% zoom = 800 CSS px (the 820 block fires); 180% = ~711 (+700); 200% = 640 (+ all six 600px blocks); 220% = ~582 (+500). WCAG 1.4.4 requires 200% resize support, so on the PO's own minimum screen every 600px block fires at an accessibility-required zoom level.

These nine blocks are the only responsive modal behaviour the app has at accessible zoom. Deleting them removes it.

The error is mine and is the same shape as the rest of this session: a property of the DECLARATION (a max-width number) asserted as a property of the RENDER (unreachability). 'Minimum supported viewport' governs physical windows; a media query measures CSS px.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED: the count and the values, verified exactly — nine blocks, six at 600px (BulkLCNFetchModal:178, M3UFiltersModal:238, VLCProtocolHelperModal:224, PreviewStreamModal:225, ModalBase:490, ModalBase:1649), one at 820 (ModalBase:1943), one at 700 (M3UProfileModal:357), one at 500 (LogoModal:225).

WHAT THE BEAD SHOULD BECOME: not a deletion. The real questions are whether these breakpoints are the right ones for a zoomed 1280 viewport, whether they are internally consistent (500/600/700/820 looks accreted rather than designed), and whether modal chrome should tighten at those sizes — which is bead 79uf8, now REOPENED for the same reason.

Also confirmed and still worth acting on: app-wide there are 61 @media blocks, 40 of them <=900px. The 'check the wider app' note holds — but under the corrected premise, which is that these fire under zoom, not that they are dead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: 2026-08-11 refreshed spike: combine with 79uf8; original delete premise and 200%-zoom arithmetic are false. Preserve three semantic tiers: 820 complex two-pane/rail collapse; 700 zoom/reflow tier covering 640 CSS px; 500 compact content. Keep M3UProfile 700 and Logo 500. Move safe VLC/Preview 600 reflows to 700. Redesign M3UFilters before moving because current rule hides Action/Order; keep values visible in a labelled compact layout. Prefer BulkLCN compact truncation at 500. Add exact harness matrix at 1280x720, 640x360, and 821/820, 701/700, 501/500 plus a closed media-block census.

title: checkbox/radio option asymmetry inherited from a deleted duplicate
description:
Minor, surfaced by 87o0c. .checkbox-option and .radio-option now share one rule in common.css except that checkboxes additionally carry flex-wrap: wrap and padding: 0.5rem 0.

That asymmetry is not a design decision — it is inherited. StreamsPane.css's duplicate .checkbox-option happened to declare two properties its .radio-option twin did not, and 87o0c's acceptance bar was render-neutrality, so the extra two were preserved as a checkbox-only rule rather than folded into the shared group (which would have moved every radio option).

Aligning the two is a visible change and needs a decision on which is right. Low priority; noted so the asymmetry is not later mistaken for intent.

title: .action-btn has no flex-shrink:0, so row action buttons compress below 32px
description:
Pre-existing, NOT introduced by the P1 sweep — confirmed by measuring before and after Wave 0.

common.css section 18 gives .action-btn width:32px; height:32px. But .account-actions (M3U Manager) and .source-actions (EPG Manager) are flex rows about 180px wide holding up to 7 buttons: 7x32 + 6x4 gap = 248px. With the default flex:0 1 auto the buttons shrink to fit — measured 18.4px to 25.4px wide against a declared 32px. Height is correct at 32px.

Logo Manager and Channel Pipeline are unaffected (fewer buttons per row), which is why they measure a clean 32x32.

Fix is a flex-shrink:0 on .action-btn plus a decision about what the row should do when it genuinely runs out of width — wrap, overflow menu, or a narrower column. That is a layout decision, not typography, which is why the sweep left it alone.

Note the sweep DID make this more visible: with the whole app now on a tighter type scale the compressed buttons are more noticeable against their neighbours.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the core claim holds, every number in it is wrong, and one bullet would cause a regression.

CONFIRMED: .action-btn declares no flex-shrink anywhere in the tree (common.css:1486, and no .action-btn rule sets it). The compression is real.

WRONG — the M3U figures. 8 buttons, not 7 (XC accounts add a Refresh VOD action, M3UManagerTab.tsx:250-324). Container 180px is right. So the worst case is (180-28)/8 = 19.0px, not the 18.4-25.4 range I quoted for a 7-button row.

WRONG — the EPG figures, in both directions. 5 buttons, not 7 (4 when EPG URLs are hidden), and the container is 120px, not 180px (EPGManagerTab.css:53,75 last track). Worst case 20.8px at 5 buttons, 27.0px at 4.

So '7x32 + 6x4 = 248px in 180px' describes a configuration that exists in NEITHER tab. Gap 0.25rem/4px is confirmed for both.

WRONG AND DANGEROUS — 'Logo Manager and Channel Pipeline are unaffected ... which is why they measure a clean 32x32'. Logo Manager does NOT. LogoManagerTab.css:419 scopes .card-actions .action-btn to 24x24 with a 14px glyph, and three of its five action buttons are in .card-actions (LogoManagerTab.tsx:440,448,456); only the two at :387,395 are 32x32. Anyone 'fixing' this bead by asserting a uniform 32x32 regresses the logo card grid.

Channel Pipeline unaffected IS confirmed, but not for the reason I gave. It is not 'fewer buttons per row' — Pipeline has SIX, more than EPG. The mechanism is that .col-actions is width:auto (ChannelPipelineTab.css:348), so the row is never constrained.

WHAT THE FIX MUST RESPECT: a flex-shrink:0 on .action-btn is not sufficient and may not be safe. At 8 buttons in 180px the row needs 284px; unshrinkable buttons will overflow or force a layout change. The real decision is what a row does when it runs out of width — wrap, overflow menu, or a wider column — and it has to preserve Logo Manager's deliberate 24x24 card variant.

Every measurement in the original description came from reading one row on one tab and generalising.

title: Generic class names colliding across pages: .detail-*, .stat-*, .section-title
description:
Naming drift found during the type-scale audit. Wave 1 scopes these so they stop leaking, but scoping treats the symptom — the underlying problem is that several pages independently invented the same generic noun.

- .detail-label / .detail-item / .detail-row / .detail-section: four pages (Channel Pipeline rule details, M3U Changes change details, Stats panel details, Journal) each invented 'detail'. Scoped in Wave 1; one of them should adopt a distinct term.
- .stat-value / .stat-label / .stat-item: the same names mean at least six different things across StatsTab (per-channel detail grid AND the header-band summary tiles), ChannelPipelineTab (header band), EnhancedStatsPanel, BandwidthPanel and WatchHistoryPanel. Wave 0 deliberately did NOT hoist these — the two donors are different components, and hoisting would have shrunk the frozen band 24->20px while growing Stats' card values 14->20px.
- .section-title: is simultaneously the section role (Pipeline, Settings, most Stats panels) and a micro/uppercase caption (StatsTab.css bare rule). After Wave 1 scoping, consider renaming the caption to .panel-caption so .section-title means one thing.

Per the style guide's naming discipline, word reuse across distinct concepts is the defect.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the roster is wrong, two 'already scoped' claims are wrong, and one claim is stale. The recommendation survives intact.

WRONG ROSTER — I said .detail-* collides across four pages (Channel Pipeline, M3U Changes, Stats, Journal). Across the four names there are SEVEN owners: those four plus WatchHistoryPanel, PopularityPanel and M3UProfileModal. And no single name is owned by the quartet I named:
  .detail-label   -> Pipeline, M3UChanges, Popularity, WatchHistory
  .detail-item    -> M3UProfileModal (6 rules), M3UChanges, Popularity, WatchHistory — Pipeline and Stats ABSENT
  .detail-row     -> Pipeline, Stats only
  .detail-section -> Journal only

WRONG — 'scoped in Wave 1'. True for .detail-label/.detail-item/.detail-row. NOT true for .detail-section: JournalTab.css:462 .detail-section pre is bare, and common.css:1820,1850 .detail-section h4 is bare AND eager. Both JournalTab.tsx and M3UChangesTab.tsx render .detail-section, so Journal's bare rule reaches M3U Changes' elements cross-chunk. Still open.

WRONG — '.section-title is a section role in Pipeline, Settings, most Stats panels'. SettingsTab.tsx renders ZERO .section-title. The nearest is ScheduleEditor.tsx:429, which renders inside TaskEditorModal — a modal, not the Settings page. Pipeline and the six scoped Stats panels are confirmed.

STALE — 'StatsTab.css bare rule'. No bare .section-title exists anywhere; all 11 rules are scoped, and StatsTab's is :where(.stats-tab) .section-title at StatsTab.css:384. Wave 1 scoped it. The other half of that claim IS confirmed: it is the micro/uppercase caption while the rest are the section role, which is the actual collision.

CONFIRMED — .stat-value/.stat-label mean six different things (StatsTab .summary-stat and .stats-tab, Pipeline .channel-pipeline-stats, EnhancedStatsPanel, BandwidthPanel, WatchHistoryPanel). .stat-item has only four contexts, not six, and is STILL BARE in two chunks (ChannelPipelineTab.css:48, StatsTab.css:640), on the guard baseline under 6z299.1.

The recommendation — rename the Stats caption to .panel-caption so .section-title means one thing — survives all of the above unchanged.

Three .header-left h2 rules and both .pane-header h2 copies were already dead and are deleted in Wave 0.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION — THREE OF THIS BEAD'S CLAIMS ARE WRONG AND ACTING ON THEM BREAKS THINGS. Trust this comment over the description.

WRONG 1 — 'DummyEPGChannelPicker.tsx/.css imported by nothing'. It IS imported: devHarness/dialogRenderers.tsx:31 imports it and :193 renders it; dialogCatalog.ts:58 catalogues it; harnessCoverage.test.ts:49 asserts the catalog covers every dialog-rendering file AND NOTHING ELSE. Deleting the component breaks tsc --noEmit and reds that test. The true, narrower claim is that it is absent from the PRODUCTION module graph, because vite.config.ts has a single entry and the harness builds from vite.harness.config.ts. I over-read the guard's 'absent from every built chunk' into 'imported by nothing'.
  ChannelDetail.tsx/.css IS genuinely unreferenced — confirmed, only self-imports and two doc comments tree-wide.

WRONG 2 — '.pane-header h2 copies were already dead and are deleted'. Only the TYPOGRAPHY declarations were dead. Both selectors survive with live non-typographic declarations: StreamsPane.css:22 has display:flex/align-items/gap/min-width — the row that puts the badge beside the title — and ChannelsPane.css:85 has transition:color, with :89 .pane-header.edit-mode h2 depending on it. An engineer who greps the selector, finds rules this bead says are deleted, and deletes them, breaks the StreamsPane header layout. The three .header-left h2 deletions in the same sentence ARE confirmed.

WRONG 3 — '.stats-summary/.stat-card ... and no className anywhere'. EnhancedStatsPanel.tsx:139-152 renders one .stats-summary and four .stat-card. That is the leak my own deletion comment documents, so the bead contradicts the code comment I wrote.

MISCLASSIFIED — .pending-merges-candidate-id is filed under 'Dead rules (no live surface)' and it HAS a live surface (PendingMergesPage.tsx:762). It was a shadowing question, not a deadness question, and the shadowing claim was also wrong: the later rule redeclares only color and font-size, so font-weight:500 and word-break were still live. Already fixed in the tree; PendingMergesPage.css:177 now records this verbatim. A SHADOWED RULE AND A DEAD CLASS ARE NOT THE SAME FINDING and must never share a heading — that conflation is what nearly caused the regression.

MISCLASSIFIED — .filters-bar. Filed as dead; it is not. The bare declarations at JournalTab.css:91 and M3UChangesTab.css:148 are live and already on the guard baseline. The only render site is WatchHistoryPanel, imported solely by StatsTab.tsx:22 — a THIRD chunk. The scoped .watch-history-panel .filters-bar wins every overlapping property except flex-shrink:0, which the bare rules supply. So deleting it IS a render change. It is also a second live instance of the defect class in bead nraba — declaration site and render site in different chunks — and the guard currently misclassifies it as a Journal/M3U collision.

CONFIRMED: ChannelDetail dead; GuideTab .control-group select and .error-message dead (both already deleted); .stream-name-more never rendered (deleted); .stats-summary/.stat-card are media-query-only with no base selector; .filters-bar's only TSX site is WatchHistoryPanel.tsx:141; the three .header-left h2 rules dead and deleted.

STATUS: every genuine 'dead rule' bullet is already executed in the tree with an explanatory comment at each site. What remains is (a) ChannelDetail deletion, safe; (b) DummyEPGChannelPicker, NOT deletable without also removing its harness catalog entry and renderer; (c) .filters-bar, a scoping decision not a deletion. Those three should be split out and this bead closed.

FLAG: both 'dead' stylesheets (ChannelDetail.css, DummyEPGChannelPicker.css) have one-line edits in the current working diff. Either a sweep is touching them unaware, or they are less dead than claimed. Check before telling anyone they are dead.

title: Stale task_registry row: export_publish in DB but not registered (removed Export tab)
description: Observed on every container start since the Export tab removal (commit f9e6dcca, 'remove FFMPEG Builder and Export tabs; relocate cloud targets'): '[TASK-REGISTRY] Task export_publish in DB but not registered' WARNING. The scheduled_tasks row for the removed task was never cleaned up, so every boot logs a warning for a task that can never run. Work: either purge the orphan row in a small migration (guarded, reversible) or have the registry reconcile/disable rows for tasks that no longer exist, consistent with how register_sync_target_tasks prunes stale per-target rows. Cosmetic but it trains operators to ignore registry warnings, which matters now that sync uses the same warning channel for real problems.

title: PendingMergesPage cancel-restore flake recurs at the raised 5000ms timeout (6wkgm fix insufficient)
description: Recurrence observed 2026-07-27 on CI run 30271655512 (during PR #752, a diff that does not touch PendingMergesPage; green locally 40/40 in 6.8s, passed on re-run). History: bead 6wkgm (PR #744, merged 2026-07-26) diagnosed the same test — 'restores the original paginated view when a 51-row all action is cancelled' (PendingMergesPage.test.tsx, bead ixcf1 / GH #642) — as a cancel-restore race and fixed it by waiting for dialog removal first, coupling the assertions inside one waitFor, AND raising the timeout to 5000ms; it passed 10/10 stability runs. CI has now blown through that 5000ms ceiling, so the structural fix helped but the fixture is simply too heavy for a loaded runner. Do NOT just raise the number again — that is the second bump and it will recur. Prefer shrinking the 51-row fixture while preserving the >50 pagination boundary the test pins (e.g. lower the page-size constant under test rather than the row count), or splitting the pagination-boundary assertion from the cancel-restore assertion so neither needs a heavy render. Related: 681a1 (closed, same waitFor family).
notes: RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. Bead 7iid7 was closed as a literal duplicate of this one (same file, same test, same load-dependent timeout on the 51-row cancel-restore); consolidate any follow-up here. Confirmed unchanged since filing: PendingMergesPage.test.tsx:1340-1365 still has bead 6wkgm's shape, with timeout 5000 at :1362, both assertions coupled in one waitFor, and the 51-row fixture intact. The fix remains structural (shrink the fixture or split the assertions), not another timeout bump. A full vitest run on an idle machine passes 2787/2787, consistent with the bead's own load-dependence note.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #877 (merge 8d7c4ce9, build 0.18.1-0114). This was a PRODUCT bug, not only a test flake. cancelBulkIntent decided whether to restore the operator's paginated view by comparing rowsRef.current (ids joined) against a snapshot string; rowsRef is written by a passive effect and is not guaranteed current when a click is handled. When it lagged, the check concluded the view had moved on when it had not and Cancel closed the dialog WITHOUT restoring, leaving the operator on the whole-queue list instead of their page. The comparison now uses the array identity handed to setRows against the rendered rows from the click's own render closure, both settled at click time. The test now waits for nothing at all, because Cancel closes and restores in one commit. Codex confirmed no writer reconstructs an identical-contents array while the dialog is legitimately cancellable, and no stale closure. Given its own CHANGELOG entry separate from the test work, per Codex. Deliberately NOT done: the 51-row fixture was not shrunk, because it is what pins the >50 pagination boundary this bead says to preserve.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
RECURRENCE 2026-08-13, second flake-induced pipeline block in one day.

Failed on PR #859 (branch test/operator-docs-required-context), a change that touches TWO DOCS FILES AND ONE PYTHON TEST and no frontend code at all:

  FAIL src/components/tabs/PendingMergesPage.test.tsx
    > PendingMergesPage - bulk actions (GH #642 / bead ixcf1)
    > restores the original paginated view when a 51-row all action is cancelled
  Test Files  1 failed | 207 passed (208)

That is this bead's test verbatim, failing at the raised 5000ms timeout exactly as this bead predicted the 6wkgm fix would leave it. Bead 7iid7 was closed earlier the same day as a literal duplicate of this one.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN NOISE, AND THE SECOND DATA POINT. Frontend Tests is a REQUIRED status check, so this flake blocks a merge outright. Earlier the same day the sibling StickySectionNav flake (bead vmk2m.1) failed the post-merge Tests run on dev, which failed 'Wait for Test Suite', which gated every image-build job, so all five skipped and NOTHING published: dev sat at 0.18.1-0091 while the registry carried 0090 until the run was manually re-run. Two different flakes, two different blast radii, one day.

THE COMMON SHAPE, worth acting on rather than re-diagnosing a third time. Both are load-dependent async-settling tests. Both were previously 'fixed' by relaxing a tolerance rather than by removing the race: 6wkgm raised this one's timeout to 5000ms, and 7zp6g added a waitFor to StickySectionNav. Both recurred through that fix. This bead already says the remaining work is structural rather than another tolerance bump, and that judgement now has two independent confirmations.

Consider whether these two want a single piece of work rather than two: an audit of the suite for assertions that wait on a tolerance instead of on an observable the component actually settles. Bead k4bwl (docs/testing.md flake baseline stale by ~1400 tests) is adjacent, since the baseline that would tell anyone how often this happens is itself wrong.

No fix attempted here. The PR was unblocked by re-running the failed job, which proves the test passes sometimes and nothing else.

title: sync_targets.last_source_fingerprint: no writer, no ratified semantics — define or drop
description: Surfaced during 7ipq2.2 live validation (2026-07-27): the last_source_fingerprint column (migration 0024, DBA ruling xp6mp) has never been written by any code path and its semantic was never ratified. Options: (a) define it as the redacted-plan hash feeding ADR-013 S4 delta detection (skip sync cycles when source unchanged) and implement the writer + reader; (b) drop the column via a follow-up migration. Note: 7ipq2.2's fixes DID add writers for its siblings last_outcome/last_full_sync_at — this column is now the only orphan on the table.
notes:
ADR-013 re-read 2026-07-27 clarifies this: S4 explicitly rules 'Full-read + idempotent upsert every cycle. NO delta state in v1', with delta/CDC deferred and 'gated on measured slowness'. So last_source_fingerprint is not an oversight — it is the reserved input for that deferred S4 delta work, shipped as part of the DBA's three-column ruling. Its two siblings (last_full_sync_at, last_outcome) gained writers in 7ipq2.2. Decision is therefore narrower than originally framed: either (a) document the column in-place as reserved-for-S4-delta (code comment + models.py docstring) so the next reader stops re-discovering it, or (b) drop it and re-add when delta work is actually scheduled. Recommend (a) — it is nullable, costless, and ADR-sanctioned.
RESCOPE from backlog validity audit (bd bewu9), PO-approved 2026-08-12. The bead's own recommended option (a) has NOT been done and remains the cheap answer: document the column in place as reserved for ADR-013-S4. The trap the note wanted closed is still open, because export_models.py:153-155 still describes an unimplemented behaviour ('for idempotent skip-if-unchanged on the next run') as though it were live. title: Phase 3: per-target sync concurrency
description: Small follow-up noted in 5gzg5: v1 serializes all sync runs across targets under one task id (safe but slow for multi-target operators). Allow per-target concurrent runs with per-target locking so one slow/unreachable B doesn't starve the others; keep per-target serialization (no two concurrent runs against the same B). Metrics/alerting (k78ja) must stay per-target-accurate.
notes:
ROUND 1 — PR #752 REMEDIATION (head a8a9064c). Commits: 15bfb094 (four review-matrix fixes), d3676564 (merge origin/dev after #750+#751 landed), a8a9064c (PO-authorized per-target counter label, kept separate for delta re-review). BLOCK 1: migration preserves effective enabled state onto the per-target parent (absent legacy parent == non-blocking, matching the engine gate); persisted via sync_to_database after the migration txn commits; regression test_migrated_schedule_fires_on_first_due_tick runs startup-through-first-due-run and timed out pre-fix. BLOCK 2: new apply-only SLI ecm_sync_last_full_success_timestamp (observability.record_sync_full_success), stamped only on APPLY+SUCCESS; ECMSyncStalledTargetDrift re-keyed off the generic gauge (which a dry-run preview advanced); 4 gauge tests + rule-shape test now forbids the generic gauge in the expr. BLOCK 3: live-B recipe on per-target endpoint + bound-target rule + per-target metric labels. WARN: SyncTargetsCard busyId scalar to Set with functional updates; two-target deferred-promise regressions. CodeQL py/import-and-import-from FIXED not dismissed. PO SCOPE: ecm_sync_runs_total gains sync_target_id, keyed on the SyncTarget PK (immutable; a name label would fork the series and break rate()/increase() continuity); 'unknown' catch-all on the no-target path; cardinality 3 x targets (1-3) + 1.

FINDING FOR PO (flake, needs a bead — agent cannot create): frontend/src/components/tabs/PendingMergesPage.test.tsx 'restores the original paginated view when a 51-row all action is cancelled' (bead ixcf1 / GH #642) hit a CI-only 5000ms timeout on run 30271655512; untouched by this PR and green locally (40/40); passed on re-run. Likely default testTimeout too tight for the 51-row fixture on a loaded runner — raise the per-test timeout or shrink the fixture while keeping the >50 pagination boundary.

OPERATOR NOTES FOR MERGE: take the updated docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml (alert SLI metric changed); add a sync_target_id filter to saved ecm_sync_runs_total dashboard queries.

ROUND 2 — DELTA RE-REVIEW P1 REMEDIATED — HELD (no merge). Head 581ddbdd on feat/7ipq2-concurrency, PR #752 updated in place, v0.18.1-0003 (origin/dev unchanged at a1b92361; #752 still the only open PR). P1: register_sync_target_tasks persisted a freshly materialized default_enabled=False instance over the EXISTING enabled per-target ScheduledTask parent before sync_from_database hydrated it, so an enabled sync was silently disabled on the next NORMAL restart (the parent gate then blocked the enabled child). FIX — one invariant, not another migration special case: new backend/tasks/dbas_sync.py::_persist_sync_task_row is the single write path for a per-target parent row and is used by BOTH registration entry points (register_sync_target_tasks and ensure_sync_target_task); an existing row is AUTHORITATIVE (the instance is hydrated FROM the row before saving, so the enabled write is a no-op while name/schedule/bookkeeping still land) and seed_enabled only chooses the value for a row that does not exist yet. Steady-state restart and legacy upgrade are now the same rule; a legacy schedule that was firing onto an already-disabled per-target row is left off with a WARN naming the reason. REGRESSIONS (test_dbas_sync_concurrency.py section 10) each drive a GENUINE second process startup (registry tasks+instances cleared, DB kept, real main.py order register then sync_from_database) plus a real engine due-tick, and assert behaviour first so the RED is the missing FIRE rather than row state: test-enabled-parent-survives-a-normal-restart-and-fires (RED: 'enabled schedule did not fire after a normal restart'); test-disabled-parent-stays-disabled-across-restart (guard direction, green both sides); test-migrated-schedule-still-fires-on-the-second-startup (RED: 'migrated schedule stopped firing after a restart'). NON-GATING DOC CLEANUPS: CHANGELOG.md dropped the stale result-only-counter and generic-gauge alert-expr claims and now states the restart invariant; docs/sre/slos.md fresh-install-guard paragraph qualified (ECMSyncStalledTargetDrift guards on its OWN SLI, ecm_sync_last_full_success_timestamp > 0); docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml responder caveat carried the same stale 'counter stays result-only' claim, now per-target. GATES: backend exit 0 / 76.41% cov, frontend 2266 green (160 files), tsc + eslint --max-warnings 0 clean, vite build clean, version consistency OK at 0.18.1-0003, fake-test guard clean. CI: 24 pass / 0 fail / 8 skipping. Awaiting the PO team delta re-review.
close_reason: Shipped PR #752 (merge 4ba49d48, v0.18.1-0003) after two review rounds. Per-target sync concurrency via ADR-013 S6 (one task per SyncTarget; engine's existing guard becomes the per-target lock), bounded by ECM_SYNC_MAX_CONCURRENT (default 3). Round 1 fixed 4 matrix items (non-fireable migrated schedules, preview-resets-drift via new apply-only SLI ecm_sync_last_full_success_timestamp, stale live-B recipe, scalar UI busy state) + PO-authorized sync_target_id label on ecm_sync_runs_total. Round 2 fixed a P1 the round-1 remediation introduced: registration now never downgrades an existing parent's enabled gate (single write path, row authoritative), pinned by three behaviour-first second-startup regressions. Also found+fixed v1 silently swallowing a second same-tick target's run.

title: shipping.md: document CONFLICTING-release-PR workflow suppression + ours-merge remedy
description: Approved by PO 2026-07-27, from the v0.18.0 cut retro trail: a release PR whose branch conflicts with main (inevitable when main/dev ancestry diverges via squash back-syncs) is CONFLICTING/DIRTY and GitHub silently runs ZERO pull_request workflows — no checks appear at all, which reads as CI being broken (this cost the v0.18.0 cut ~1 hour of diagnosis). Document in docs/shipping.md Release Workflow: (1) the failure signature (no checks reported, check-suites absent, other apps still receive events); (2) the remedy — merge origin/main into the release branch with -s ours to record ancestry while keeping the release tree byte-identical (verify: git diff HEAD~1 empty), precedent v0.17.4 (6f88a261) and v0.18.0 (f0e86f09); (3) consider making it a standard cut step since squash back-syncs guarantee the divergence recurs. Related: mvz5r (G1b dev-ref gap, same cut).
