title: Version-advance PreToolUse hook is worktree-blind
description: During the GH #645 ship (PR #666), the version-advance guard hook validated CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (main checkout, parked at 0099) instead of the worktree branch being PR'd (0100), falsely blocking gh pr create from a worktree. Engineer verified the check manually and created the PR via gh api (documented in the PR body); CI re-enforced the rule server-side. Fix: hook should resolve repo root from the command's cd/git -C target, or accept an env override for worktree shipping.
notes: Fixed on branch fix/yxtuz-version-guard-worktree, commit 8d26e3e8 (not pushed, not merged — PO decides shipping). Approach: PROJECT_DIR resolution from the gh pr create command's leading 'cd <path> &&' or 'git -C <path>', plus ECM_VERSION_GUARD_ROOT env override; falls back to prior CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/script-location default for the plain main-checkout path (unchanged behavior). Verified manually via 4 cases incl. a real throwaway worktree reproducing then fixing the exact PR-666 false-block, plus pre-fix-via-git-stash comparison and an env-override-only case. No pytest harness exists for .claude/hooks/*.sh (only scripts/check_version_advances.py has unit tests, which don't cover the shell wrapper) -- noted as a backlog candidate: add a lightweight fixture-based self-test for the hook per engineering-discipline's 'Enforcement Code Tests Itself' principle, mirroring backend/tests/unit/test_check_version_advances.py's approach but invoking the .sh directly. Also noted: the hook's gh-pr-create matcher does plain substring/regex matching, not real bash parsing -- a Bash command that itself CONTAINS the literal text '&& gh pr create' (e.g. inside a quoted string, as happened during my own verification) can spuriously trigger it. Pre-existing limitation, not touched by this fix; only surfaced during testing.

title: Residual gap: BaseException containment can't cover outer middleware bodies (incl. auth_middleware)
description: Follow-up from P1 fix (enhancedchannelmanager-xzdx9 / GH #546), code-review finding #1. The BaseExceptionContainmentMiddleware is innermost, so it contains SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt raised in route handlers and dependencies. It structurally CANNOT contain a BaseException raised inside the bodies of the outer BaseHTTPMiddleware layers themselves — including auth_middleware (backend/main.py:515-547), where decode_token_safe runs on the exact concurrent-cookie path from the GH #546 repro. Each BaseHTTPMiddleware body runs in a task outside the guard; no user-space registration position can catch it. Since the actual raiser in the reporter's environment was never identified, if it lives in an outer middleware body the shipped fix will classify the death (atexit/[EXIT-DIAG] diagnostics) but not prevent it. Purpose of this bead: (a) document the gap so a field recurrence is not misread as the containment fix failing; (b) if recurrence happens, the [EXIT-DIAG]/atexit output should name the raiser — attach it here; (c) possible hardening avenues if needed later: audit outer middleware bodies for BaseException sources (audited once: none raise), or restructure outer middlewares to pure-ASGI so the guard can wrap them.
close_reason: Closed as documented (PO decision 2026-07-26): the BaseException-containment ceiling is now permanently recorded in docs/auth_middleware.md 'Known limitation' section + pointer comment at auth_middleware in main.py, shipped in PR #745 (merge 634c9101, v0.17.6-0172) after team review corrected the operator diagnostic (atexit [EXIT-DIAG] line WILL appear; the containment CRITICAL traceback is what's absent) and the remediation description (middleware-stack redesign, not just pure-ASGI conversion). No field occurrence observed; reopen only if an [EXIT-DIAG]-absent outer-middleware death ever fires.

title: Stats - Live stats block, use the space condensed for many providers
description:
GH-481. Live Stats provider display on the Stats tab auto-switches from the per-provider tile layout to a condensed table once there are more than 6 active providers, so operators with many M3U accounts don't get an unbounded row of tiles.

Condensed table renders inside a 220px max-height scroll container so the page doesn't grow unbounded with provider count.

A settings-level toggle to let operators force the condensed/tile layout regardless of provider count was considered and deliberately deferred — noted as a follow-up candidate, not implemented in this batch (the >6 auto-switch threshold covers the reported case).

Changes land in StatsTab.tsx/.css with StatsTab.test.tsx + StatsTab.drillDown.test.tsx coverage.

Shipped in the combined v0.17.6-0135 PR alongside GH-482 (bead n5cwp) and GH-496 (bead wwovg).

title: Under stats implement section that shows usage of streams per provider in channels
description:
GH-482. Adds GET /api/stats/providers/stream-usage — per-provider stream usage under the Stats tab, reusing the existing cached channel<->stream assignment index (no new query pass over Dispatcharr data).

Two counting metrics surfaced intentionally: assigned_streams (PRIMARY) — distinct streams from the provider assigned to >=1 channel (a stream in 3 channels counts once); total_assignments (secondary) — sum of channel-memberships across those streams (a stream in 2 channels counts twice), surfacing providers whose streams get heavily reused. total_streams (provider's full catalog size) + utilization_pct (assigned_streams / total_streams) give scale/context. provider_id is null for the synthetic "Unknown" bucket (an assigned stream whose m3u_account didn't resolve to a known/current provider).

Endpoint is NOT admin-gated — Dispatcharr-derived catalog/assignment data, same trust tier as GET /api/stats/channels, not per-user watch history like the ProviderStats family.

New ProviderStreamUsagePanel.tsx (+ .css) renders a sortable table under Stats. Tests: backend/tests/routers/test_stats_provider_stream_usage.py, frontend/src/components/tabs/ProviderStreamUsagePanel.test.tsx.

Shipped in the combined v0.17.6-0135 PR alongside GH-481 (bead 49obj) and GH-496 (bead wwovg).

title: Allow filtering/targeting specific M3U accounts for M3U Change Digest
description:
GH-496. M3U Change Digest notifications can now be scoped to a selected subset of M3U accounts, so an operator with a high-churn FAST provider (10k+ stream URL changes/hour) can exclude it from digest emails/Discord without losing change history — M3UChangeLog logging is never filtered, only what gets built into a notification.

Backend: new M3UDigestSettings.account_ids column (nullable Text/JSON, get_/set_ helpers mirroring the exclude_group_patterns pattern), landed via handwritten Alembic migration 0035 (m3u_digest_settings predates revision 0005's baseline, so the alembic-smoke fast-path test also needed its manual ALTER TABLE simulation updated). Query filter added in tasks/m3u_digest.py:_build_digest_payload — when no explicit single-account filter is active and account_ids is non-empty, the change-log query adds M3UChangeLog.m3u_account_id.in_(account_ids). Empty/unset account_ids = all accounts (unchanged default).

Immediate-digest decision: send_immediate_digest() (fires for exactly one account right after its M3U refresh) SKIPS sending entirely — without calling execute() — when that account isn't in a non-empty selection, logging at INFO. The operator deliberately excluded it; DB logging for that account is untouched by this decision.

Frontend: new "Account Filter" section on Settings > M3U Digest, reusing the shared GroupMultiSelectDropdown component (options/selectedIds/onChange/label API) populated via the existing getM3UAccounts() call.

Tests: backend/tests/unit/test_m3u_digest_account_filter.py (settings round-trip, scoped/unscoped query filtering, explicit-account-overrides-scope, immediate-digest skip/proceed), 5 new cases in tests/routers/test_m3u_digest.py (PUT persistence, empty clears, omitted leaves unchanged), tests/integration/test_alembic_smoke.py updated. Frontend: SettingsTab.digest.test.tsx (6 cases: picker rendering, selection count, load-reflects-saved-state, save payload, empty-selection payload, test-digest payload).

Live-verified against the real container: dropdown populated with real Dispatcharr M3U accounts, selected a subset, saved, confirmed "2 accounts selected" survives a full page reload, confirmed the persisted DB row (account_ids='[18, 19]'), and an in-container probe against real production change-log data (2895 total rows) confirmed the new filter correctly reduces to exactly the 1216 rows belonging to the selected accounts. Settings reset to all-accounts (NULL) after verification.

Shipped in the combined v0.17.6-0135 PR alongside GH-482 (bead n5cwp) and GH-481 (bead 49obj).

title: NGINX support
description:
Imported from GitHub issue #590: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/590

### What would you like this feature to do?

Hi,

I tried using NGINX to forward traffic to the ECM instance. However, the application blocks access when I use my own domain, with traffic being routed through NGINX.

I looked through the ECM settings and integrations to see if there was an option to whitelist custom domains, but I couldn't find one.

I'm creating this feature request to address that limitation. Instead of using the built-in TLS configuration, I would prefer to use my own NGINX configuration and have TLS managed by my NGINX management tool. This would allow me to use my own domain while still accessing the ECM instance through a reverse proxy.


### How would you suggest implementing?

By whitelisting the domain I use in nginx-manager that's already managing the DNS and TLS via cloudflare.

### How critical do you think this is?

Medium - Nice to have, would use it regularly

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Auto Sync and Auto Creation by date
description:
Imported from GitHub issue #646: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/issues/646

### What would you like this feature to do?

Allow Auto Sync and Auto Create rules to be enabled by date.  Example:  I want "football" auto sync rule to assign profile "Primary" during season (start date) and when the season ends (end date) I can have it un-assign the "Primary" profile. 

### How would you suggest implementing?

_No response_

### How critical do you think this is?

Medium - Nice to have, would use it regularly

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Apply pagination bounds validation across all list endpoints (systemic 1a5mf)
description: Code review of 1a5mf flagged that the same unvalidated 'page: int = 1, page_size: int = 100' pattern (→ 500 on page=0/negative, invalid values passed straight to the upstream client) exists in ~7 sibling list endpoints: routers/channels.py get_logos (~L444, same file), streams.py:127, journal.py:20, m3u_digest.py:47/164, notifications.py:34, epg.py:530, stats.py:1246. 1a5mf fixed only get_channels. Apply the same Query(1, ge=1) / Query(100, ge=1, le=<sane>) treatment across these list endpoints (mind real max page_size callers, as get_channels needed le=10000 for App.tsx pageSize=5000). Add per-endpoint 422 tests.
notes: FIX READY, unshipped: branch fix/g4z2h-pagination-bounds @ 63392f48. All 8 endpoints bounded with caller-evidenced ceilings (logos 10000, streams 1000, journal 250, m3u_digest 200/200, notifications 100, epg 1000, watch_history 100); journal+stats silent clamps converted to 422 (behavioral change, changelog-worthy); docs/api.md stale cap corrected. Repo-wide sweep found no further unvalidated endpoints. Gates: 350 router tests + full suite 7100 passed, cov 89.29%. Orchestrator re-verified. Awaiting PO ship decision.

title: Bug: tls/settings.py get_expiry_days/needs_renewal have same naive-local-vs-UTC tz skew as n5zw2
description: Flagged by the n5zw2 fix. tls/settings.py:136 get_expiry_days (and needs_renewal) compute expires - datetime.now() where expires is parsed naive-UTC — the SAME tz-skew bug class fixed in tls/storage.py under n5zw2, but in a different module and not covered by the paths that fix addressed. Make the whole TLS module tz-consistent: use the same naive-UTC-now approach (n5zw2 added _utcnow_naive() in storage.py). Add a tz-sensitive test. Note: the n5zw2 engineer chose naive-UTC (not tz-aware) specifically because an aware cert time would break this L136 subtraction — so keep the module on the naive-UTC convention.
notes: FIX READY, unshipped: branch fix/wccvo-tls-settings-tz @ 215f05f0. _utcnow_naive() mirrored from n5zw2 storage.py idiom into tls/settings.py get_expiry_days; tz-sensitive tests added (verified failing pre-fix). Gates: 49 tls tests + full suite 7060 passed (venv). Orchestrator re-verified targeted gates. Awaiting PO ship decision.

title: Robustness: GET /api/channels?page=0 or negative returns 500 (invalid pagination passed to upstream)
description: Observed during u8qr6.2 e2e edge probing (pre-existing, not encoded as expected). GET /api/channels?page=0 and page=-1 return 500 — invalid pagination is passed straight to the Dispatcharr client which raises. Should be a 422/400 validation error, not a 500. Add pagination bounds validation on the channels list endpoint. Low severity / environment-dependent.

title: Bug: tls/storage.py cert expiry math compares naive-local now() vs naive-UTC cert times (tz skew)
description: Found during u8qr6.1 code review (pre-existing, NOT introduced by that PR). CertificateInfo.days_until_expiry / is_expired / is_not_yet_valid (backend/tls/storage.py:42,47,51) compare datetime.now() (naive LOCAL time) against not_after/not_before stored as naive UTC (not_valid_after_utc.replace(tzinfo=None), ~line 277). Near a nonzero UTC offset this skews expiry/validity math by the offset — a cert could read expired/valid up to (offset) hours early/late. Fix: compare in a single consistent timezone (use datetime.now(timezone.utc) and keep the cert times tz-aware, or convert both to naive UTC consistently). The new u8qr6.1 tests use generous windows so they neither flake nor catch this — add a tz-sensitive assertion when fixing.

title: MCP naming: align audit_epg_duplicates tool name with epg_audit_duplicates contract key
description: Code-review nit #2 from vznut.1 (deferred fix-forward, was not filed — filing now). mcp-server/tools/epg.py:211 defines the tool 'audit_epg_duplicates' while its contract key (mcp-server/_endpoint_contracts.py:527) is 'epg_audit_duplicates' (noun order flipped). Sibling contract keys use the epg_<verb> form (epg_match, epg_link_channel). Align to one consistent order so a future grep doesn't miss it. Purely internal cosmetic; do it before the tool sees wide use.

title: Missing edge-case direction tests (reverse-order / disable direction)
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091). Regression tests that cover only one direction of a bidirectional behavior:
  - [medium] backend/tests/unit/test_consolidate_operations.py:160 (test_create_then_delete_temp_channel_cancels) — The only create+delete cancellation test puts createChannel BEFORE deleteChannel in the ops list; there is no test for the reverse order (deleteChannel before createChannel for the same temp id).
  - [low] backend/tests/unit/test_task_registry_enabled_persist.py:8 (test_sync_to_database_persists_enabled_for_existing_task) — Only the enable-a-disabled-task direction is covered; there is no companion test disabling a previously-enabled task to confirm sync_to_database also persists False correctly (the original regression was about `enabled` being silently reset from the old row, which could manifest in either direction).

title: Flaky-risk: wall-clock timing assertions in the default suite
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091). Hard asserts on real wall-clock timing (sleeps / latency budgets / bcrypt duration) run in the default (non-benchmark) suite and can false-fail under CI contention. Move to a benchmark-marked/informational tier or make them robust:
  - [low] backend/tests/integration/test_event_loop_responsiveness.py:79 (test_health_under_500ms_while_normalize_batch_runs) — Wall-clock timing assertion (health_elapsed < 0.5s against an 0.8s sleeping handler) can false-fail under CI host contention even though the margin is generous; same pattern repeats at line 160 for the xmltv variant.
  - [low] backend/tests/services/test_dedup_matcher.py:366 (test_find_candidate_under_5ms_per_call_for_500_candidates) — Microbenchmark asserts real wall-clock latency (<5ms/call) as a hard `assert` in the default (non-slow, non-benchmark-marked) test suite, contradicting its own class docstring that calls it 'informational... not a hard gate.'
  - [low] backend/tests/unit/test_concurrency.py:105 (test_does_not_block_event_loop) — Uses a real `time.sleep(0.3)` on a worker thread and `asyncio.sleep(0.05)` concurrently, then asserts the fast task completes in under 0.25s — a wall-clock timing assertion that can flake under CI scheduling contention even when the code is correct.
  - [low] backend/tests/unit/test_password_security.py:52 (test_hashing_takes_minimum_time) — Asserts `elapsed > 0.1` (wall-clock timing) on a bcrypt hash call; under CI load, hardware differences, or a lowered bcrypt cost-factor default, this can flake independent of any real regression in the security property it intends to check.

title: Mock-wiring tests don't assert forwarded args / side-effects
description:
Full-suite test audit (build 0091). Tests that mock a collaborator but never assert the meaningful call args or the side-effect that makes the behavior real (so a silently-ignored param or a skipped reload would still pass). Add the missing call-arg / side-effect assertions:
  - [medium] backend/tests/routers/test_m3u_digest.py:201 (test_passes_account_filter) — Test claims to verify the account filter is passed to the detector but never inspects the mock's call args (or asserts anything about the detector at all).
  - [medium] backend/tests/routers/test_m3u_digest.py:189 (test_passes_hours_param) — Test claims to verify the hours=48 query param reaches the detector but only checks assert_called_once() — it never checks the actual `since` datetime argument, so it would still pass if hours were silently ignored.
  - [low] backend/tests/routers/test_alert_methods.py:112 (test_creates_method / test_updates_name / test_updates_enabled / test_deletes_method) — These tests patch get_alert_manager to return a MagicMock (routers/alert_methods.py calls get_alert_manager().reload_method(id) on create/update/delete at lines 218, 333, 367) but never assert reload_method was actually invoked, so the manager-notification side effect that makes alert config changes take effect live is unverified.

title: EPG audit + /match truncate at page_size=10000 — paginate for very large fleets
description:
Code-review nit #4 (vznut.1): GET /api/epg/audit-duplicates and POST
/api/epg/match fetched channels with a single page_size=10000 call, silently
truncating fleets >10000 channels (total_channels then misleading).
Pre-existing pattern (both handlers), NOT a vznut.1 regression.

IMPLEMENTED: extracted a shared _fetch_all_channels(client) helper in
backend/routers/epg.py, used by both handlers. Pages with page_size=1000,
terminating on fetched >= result["count"] or an empty page -- the same paged
scan shape as the stale-ids endpoint (routers/streams.py) and
stream_stats.get_streams. Adds a _CHANNELS_FETCH_MAX_PAGES=1000 hard stop
(precedent: routers/backup.py's _CHANNELS_MAX_PAGES) so a misbehaving
upstream can't loop forever -- a ~1M-channel ceiling with a logged warning if
ever hit, not a silent truncation. Backward-compatible with mocks lacking a
"count" key (defaults to 0, so a single-page response still terminates after
one call -- no extra round-trip for the common small-fleet case).

Tests: backend/tests/routers/test_epg.py, 6 new tests (3 per endpoint) --
multi-page fleet with total_channels correctly reflecting the full,
untruncated count; single-page small-fleet behavior unchanged
(get_channels call_count == 1); empty-fleet handled gracefully.

Verified live on ecm-ecm-1: GET /api/epg/audit-duplicates via MCP returns
identical results to before the fix (50 channels, no shared links), with the
container log confirming the new paged fetch (page=1&page_size=1000, single
page needed for a 50-channel fleet).

title: Docs: document timezone-aware EPG regional equivalences (West==Pacific, Mountain/Central) + before/after examples
description:
Deferred docs AC from vznut.2 (scope was epg_matching.py-only). Documents the
regional-equivalence behavior in the matcher: West==Pacific (region code W),
Mountain (M) and Central (C) as their own regions with no cross-equivalence;
tvg_id-paren-then-trailing-word region detection (quality/digit tokens
skipped, adjective forms like "Eastern"/"Western" deliberately not matched);
region-consistency as the LAST tie-break, after confidence/source
priority/exact-token scoring, and inert for non-regional channels.

IMPLEMENTED: added a "Channel-to-EPG matching" section to
docs/user_guide/epg/index.md -- regional-equivalence table, region-detection
rules, ranking behavior, a before/after example (AMC West -> AMC(Pacific)),
and a dev note pointing at epg_matching.py's detect_region() /
epg_match_key() / _sort_matches(). Updated the "Tip" in
finding-mislinked-channels.md, which previously told operators a
poorly-ranked Pacific entry was a separate untracked matcher-scoring issue --
now stale since vznut.2 shipped region-awareness; the tip now says
re-matching a West channel should rank correctly in most cases post-fix.
Also corrected the dev note's claim that the auto-creation matcher
(_match_epg_data) "is not yet region-aware" -- vznut.4 shipped in the same
batch made it region-aware too, reusing the same detect_region(), so the
note now describes both matchers sharing one source of regional truth.

title: Follow-up: make auto-creation EPG matcher (_match_epg_data) region-aware
description:
SPIN-OUT from vznut.2 grooming/spike (2026-07-14). vznut.2 fixed ONLY
match_channels_epg (epg_matching.py). Auto-creation used a SEPARATE, simpler
matcher -- channel_pipeline_executor._match_epg_data -- with its own
hardcoded timezone list and no band/token/region scoring.

IMPLEMENTED: _match_epg_data is now region-aware, reusing
epg_matching.detect_region() (one shared source of regional truth with the
vznut.2 fix, no duplicated region-detection logic). Added
ActionExecutor._region_rank(channel_region, entry) -- 0 = region matches (or
channel has no detected region), 1 = entry has no region, 2 = conflict.
Within the existing exact-match and prefix-match tiers, candidates now sort
by (region_rank, len_diff) instead of len_diff alone -- region-consistency
tie-break goes AHEAD of the name-length-similarity tie-break, since length
is a coincidental signal while a region tag is deliberate (the KNM wrong-region
failure mode was exactly a shorter/coincidental name winning). Inert (all
candidates rank 0) for channels with no detected region, so non-regional
matching is unchanged.

Tests: backend/tests/unit/test_channel_pipeline_executor_epg_region.py, 19
tests -- characterization guards pinning pre-vznut.4 behavior (exact-tvg_id
short-circuit, exact-over-prefix tiers, length-similarity ordering, call-sign
matching, single-entry fallback) plus new regional coverage (West==Pacific
equivalence, Mountain/Central as their own regions, tvg_id-paren-then-last-word
detection with quality/digit skipping, region-consistency tie-break within
tiers).

title: Reconcile channel-groups diagnostic shape between debug-bundle generator and analyzer
description: Found during m1s38.2. build_channel_groups_diagnostic (debug bundle path) emits channels_by_group_id, but the analyzer's MERGE_STREAMS_NO_TARGET_CHANNELS check reads groups[].{id,channel_count}. So that finding likely never fires on real production bundles via the /rules/analyze/from-bundle route. m1s38.2's new analyze-body endpoint builds the correct {groups:[...]} shape directly and is unaffected. Fix: reconcile the bundle generator's diagnostic shape with what the analyzer reads (or make the analyzer accept both). Pre-existing bug, backend, small.

title: Document frontend static-asset cleanup in shipping.md + add deploy-frontend wrapper
description: SRE flagged during team-plan m1s38: shipping.md §6 does not mention 'rm -rf /app/static/assets/*' before the frontend 'docker cp' step. docker cp only ADDS files, so stale Vite content-hash bundles linger in /app/static/assets/ and can cause intermittent CSS/JS chunk mismatches. CLAUDE.md documents the cleanup but shipping.md (the canonical shipping flow) does not. Fix: add the cleanup step to shipping.md's frontend deploy section, and add scripts/deploy-frontend.sh that does clean+build+copy as one operation to remove operator error. Home-lab hygiene follow-up, outside epic m1s38.
notes: Done (local, not yet shipped). Added scripts/deploy-frontend.sh — atomic build -> clear /app/static/assets/* -> docker cp, with --no-build, --help, ECM_CONTAINER override, and a not-running guard. Wired it into CLAUDE.md's Frontend deploy block (script first, manual sequence kept as the documented equivalent). shipping.md turned out to have NO container-deploy step (it's the PR flow); added a one-line cross-reference under step 1 pointing to the script + CLAUDE.md rather than duplicating deploy content there. Verified: bash -n clean; --help prints header-only; not-running container exits 1; bad arg exits 2. Awaiting 'ship the fix' to PR.

title: Team-alias dictionary for team-token matching (corpus-gated aliases)
description:
Operator-editable team-alias dictionary consulted by the team-token layer of the event matcher: e.g. "Man Utd" == "Manchester United" == "MUFC". Raises recall on abbreviation-heavy providers without loosening the fuzzy threshold (the safe direction: aliases add known-equivalences instead of lowering the evidence bar).

Scope: small CRUD (likely a normalization-rule-group-style table or JSON setting), matcher lookup during team-token comparison (both hard-reject and boost paths), management UI, and corpus additions — every alias added ships with corpus pairs proving it (a wrong alias is a new false-positive vector, so aliases are corpus-gated like code).

Trigger: recurring missed matches in the ambiguous band traceable to team-name variants (visible in preview/journal evidence).

Size: Small-Medium.

--- IMPLEMENTATION (2026-07-18, PR #707, commit fdb766a6, v0.17.6-0138) ---
Shipped to OPEN PR #707 (PO away — not merged). Storage: JSON setting event_sync_team_aliases on DispatcharrSettings (bead-sanctioned option; no models.py change, no migration — deliberately avoids overlap with in-flight PR #705). Matcher: alias index in _team_similarity after the qualifier rail (event_sync_matcher.py) — strictly monotonic (same-group hit = 1.0; different-group/no-group pairs byte-identical to no-alias run; an alias can never CREATE a disagree — pinned by tests), reaching BOTH hard-reject and boost paths through _team_pair_verdict; dictionary loaded from settings at the match_streams/score_pair boundary (team_aliases=None) so attach/preview/debug share one dictionary; frozen corpus gate byte-stable (fixtures inject explicit aliases or ()). CRUD: GET/PUT /api/event-sync/team-aliases (routers/event_sync_aliases.py), validated against the matcher's own normalization, journaled. UI: EventSyncTeamAliasesSection on Settings → Channel Pipeline. MCP: get/update_event_sync_team_aliases (new tools/event_sync_aliases.py + contract entries at registry end). Docs: event_sync.md 'Team aliases (operator dictionary)' + api.md. Dictionary ships EMPTY (corpus-gated policy; no speculative aliases seeded). Gates: backend 7413 passed, frontend 1990 passed + tsc/eslint/build, mcp-server 585 passed, version consistency OK. Live-verified on ecm-ecm-1 via scratch merge with #705 (container parity): UI round-trip + journal row + score_pair default flipping reject/team_token_conflict → attach/agree 1.0 from the persisted dictionary + zero-write preview unchanged for non-aliased data; fixture dictionary cleared after.

title: Opt-in promotion of unmatched secondary-only events to ECM-managed channels (needs own design pass; evidence-gated)
description:
SHIPPED: PR #708 (https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/pull/708), branch feat/ti939.4.1-event-promotion, commit 1de39da2, version 0.17.6-0139. Merge driven by the orchestrator.

BUILT (2026-07-18, project-engineer): opt-in promotion of unmatched secondary-only events to ECM-managed channels — the ONE sanctioned exception to "ECM never creates channels". Implemented per the architect design memo with both PO-locked decisions honored verbatim:

1. LIFECYCLE = reconciliation-driven deletion. A promoted channel is current iff its justifying unmatched stream was observed in the provider playlist THIS run; Pass 4 orphan reconciliation deletes per orphan_action (default delete). No wall-clock arithmetic, no timestamps, no K-run counters anywhere in the delete path. Extra safety: a rule that made no observation this run (fetch failure, invalid config, disabled) is NOT reconciled — a transient provider error can never mass-delete promoted channels (results["event_sync_promotion_reconcile_rule_ids"] gate + dedicated test).
2. CLUSTERING = exact master_event_key only (t6bin dateless semantics inherited verbatim from services/event_sync_review.py). Cross-provider same-key streams share ONE channel; no fuzzy clustering; promoted channels never enter the matcher candidate set (target group is never read by the resolver).

WHAT SHIPPED:
- services/event_sync_promote.py (NEW, pure): build_promotion_plan + promoted_channel_name — the ONE planner both the preview endpoint and the live executor call (dry-run parity by construction). Deterministic key-derived channel names; dateless parses carry NO date in name/identity (midnight re-run adopts). Cap applies to creations only.
- channel_pipeline_schema.py: promote_unmatched / promote_target_group_id / max_promote_per_run (default 25, ceiling 200) in _EVENT_SYNC_ALLOWED_KEYS + validation. Absent keys = feature invisible (never default-filled). Target group required when enabled, refuses master + secondaries (ownership rails).
- channel_pipeline_executor.py: _execute_event_sync_promotion — create-or-adopt via the existing _execute_create_channel if_exists=skip + match_scope_target_group machinery (allow_manual_channel_merge=True: a previously-promoted channel reads as manual next run since Dispatcharr does not persist ECM's auto_created marker; name-adoption in the ECM-owned target group IS the idempotence mechanism). Attaches via _add_stream_to_channel with kind="event_sync_promote" fingerprint provenance (provider_id + stream_name_hash + event_key; IDs display-only), journal category event_sync. assign_event_sync_dummy_epg group filter parameterized to include the target group + same-run-created channels.
- channel_pipeline_engine.py: promotion registered into rule_channel_order (managed set = promoted channels ONLY; register-time ownership assert + Pass 4 last-resort target-group rail, both WARN+refuse). Pass 4 hard bypass now conditional on promote_unmatched; first-run-populate + orphan_action semantics inherited; renumber verified a natural no-op (no create_channel action, no starting number; pinned by test). created_entities/channels_created aggregated from the event_sync phase; event_sync_promote_capped warning mirrors attach cap; summary-line extras ("N promoted, M promoted-adopted").
- Rollback: promotion runs have created entities so _event_sync_journal_covers_run returns False and the standard snapshot restore path applies (deletes run-created channels, restores master stream lists). Round-trip pinned by test.
- routers/channel_pipeline.py preview: promotion plan computed by the same helper over the same resolution; "promotion" block + summary.would_promote(+_streams) + per-unmatched-row annotations (would_promote/promote_action/promote_channel_name/promote_capped) — keys present ONLY when enabled (AC-1 payload parity).
- MCP preview_event_sync renderer: distinct "Would promote"/PROMOTE block + docstring; rule CRUD MCP tools never carried event_sync_config (pre-existing, verified) — inline preview passes the new keys through and the backend rule save API validates them via the one validator.
- Frontend: EventSyncRuleEditor Behavior-step collapsed "Promote unmatched events" subgroup (toggle + dedicated-group CustomSelect filtered of master/secondaries + explicit ECM-will-CREATE-and-DELETE copy + client-side rails mirroring the validator); EventSyncPreviewPanel "Would promote (N)" section between unmatched and parse failures + unmatched-table verdict column + summary-line count; types in types/eventSync.ts.
- Docs: docs/event_sync.md new "Promoting unmatched events (Phase 3 opt-in)" section with honest ownership/deletion semantics, config-table rows, master-as-ceiling section updated (no longer "not built yet"), "What ECM deliberately does NOT do" amended; docs/api.md preview payload table updated. CHANGELOG [Unreleased]/Added entry; version bumped 0.17.6-0138 -> 0.17.6-0139 in all three touchpoints (check_version_consistency.py green).
- AC-11 PINNED: excluded_by_operator streams ARE promotable (exclusions block ATTACH to a specific master, not promotion); ambiguous is NOT (open review question); parse_failed untouchable. Unit + integration tests + docs.

TESTS: backend 7501 passed (25 new in tests/unit/test_event_sync_promotion.py covering AC1-7/9/10/11 + managed-set invariant + renumber no-op + no-observation protection; 4 new preview-parity tests in tests/routers/test_event_sync_preview.py; 11 new schema tests; shared make_promote_client fixture). Frontend 2009 passed (4 new preview-panel + 5 new editor tests), tsc + eslint clean, build OK. MCP 618 passed (2 new renderer tests).

LIVE VERIFICATION (container ecm-ecm-1, dev): zero-write COPY-config preview of the live "Test Sync" rule with promote_unmatched=true + scratch target group 1298 ("Test Group", 0 channels) -> "Would promote: 2 channel(s) (2 new) from 4 unmatched stream(s)" with live cross-provider clustering (Strong + CRX providers sharing each event key). UI screenshots ti939-41-1..3.png (editor subgroup, Would-promote section, unmatched annotations). Editor discarded without saving; stored rule config verified to carry no promote keys afterward. title: Bug: MCP bulk_add_streams_to_channel times out (~4 min) on Raspberry Pi for 9-10 streams (gh #223)
description: GH #223 (reporter Koalamanx, Pi 5 / Docker Compose). bulk_add_streams_to_channel with 9-10 stream IDs times out after ~4 min on a Pi; single add_stream_to_channel calls are reliable. The MCP 'bulk' tool (mcp-server/tools/channels.py:266-296) fakes a bulk op by looping POST /api/channels/{id}/add-stream (one HTTP request per stream); there is no real backend bulk-add-streams endpoint (routes: /add-stream, /remove-stream, /reorder-streams, /bulk-commit). On slow hardware each add-stream Dispatcharr roundtrip is slow; 9-10 sequential × per-call latency exceeds the MCP tool's httpx timeout. Fix candidates: (a) raise the MCP tool's httpx timeout for bulk ops; (b) add a real backend bulk-add-streams endpoint (one Dispatcharr roundtrip / fewer); (c) chunk the batch; (d) document the loop-single workaround. Needs profiling of the add-stream endpoint cost. Severity: P3 — workaround exists; slow-hardware edge case.

The flag was added deliberately as opt-in / default-off / backwards-compatible (bd-r9mtd, GH-92) — so flipping the default is a behavior change for all existing rules and needs PO sign-off + a CHANGELOG breaking note. Options: (a) flip the default to true (PO call); (b) keep default off but add a rule-analyzer finding ('this merge rule with match_scope_target_group=false can merge into channels in other groups') + clearer docs; (c) document the footgun only. Relates to GH-92 ('Create Channel groups separation not only merge'). Severity: P3 / needs-discussion.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.16.0-0080 (PR #234) — Plan A+B: flipped match_scope_target_group code default to True for new rules (no DB migration; Alembic 0002 backfilled false into every existing row so flipping the code default only affects new rules); fixed backend/routers/backup.py restore path to round-trip the field; added MERGE_SCOPE_NOT_TARGET_GROUP analyzer advisory finding (info, fires for existing rules with create_channel + if_exists in (merge, merge_only) + match_scope_target_group=False); 192 tests pass incl. 10 new analyzer cases. title: Add ecm_session_starts_total counter for SLO-6 denominator
description:
Implement the counter that closes out SLO-6's SLI formula. Today the SLO-6 entry in docs/sre/slos.md references this counter but the counter does not exist, so the SLI falls back to log-aggregation (slow, requires log aggregator we don't have) and the two alert rules in docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml fire on absolute error rate (noisier proxy — fires on traffic spikes even when error ratio is flat).

## Blocked by

~~Upstream spike bead decides session semantics (A page-load / B JWT / C cookie-lifetime). This bead is intentionally small-scope implementation once the spike decides.~~

**RESOLVED** by enhancedchannelmanager-1tl01. Spike merged 2026-04-24 (PR #192, merge SHA b4e033b87682aace36bb57a1143d1e76ccd304b1).

## Chosen semantic: C — cookie/sessionStorage lifetime

SRE, Security Engineer, and UX Designer personas converged independently. Frontend generates a SubtleCrypto-backed UUIDv4 `session_id`, persists it in `sessionStorage` (NOT localStorage, NOT a server-set cookie), emits `POST /api/session-start` once with that `session_id`. Backend deduplicates via short-TTL (24h) in-memory set before incrementing `ecm_session_starts_total`.

**Security constraints** (non-negotiable, from spike §3.2):

1. `session_id` MUST be a SubtleCrypto-generated v4 UUID, NOT a hash of UA / IP / user identifiers.
2. Stored in `sessionStorage` ONLY — never `localStorage`, never a persistent cookie.
3. Never logged by the backend, never returned in API responses, never indexed in the database. The dedup set is in-memory only.

**Fail-open contract** (UX, from spike §3.3): if `sessionStorage.setItem` throws (private mode, strict-privacy browser), skip silently — the user is excluded from the SLO denominator, NOT blocked from the app.

Full implementation steps in [docs/sre/spike-slo-6-session-semantics.md](../docs/sre/spike-slo-6-session-semantics.md) §6.

## Acceptance (refined per spike outcome)

1. New counter `ecm_session_starts_total` (no labels) registered in backend/observability.py alongside the existing ecm_* families. Also a gauge `ecm_session_dedup_set_size` so SRE can spot pruner leaks.
2. Frontend: new `installSessionTracker()` (or equivalent in `clientErrorReporter.ts` adjacent module) reads `sessionStorage.getItem('ecm_session_id')`, generates UUIDv4 + persists + POSTs if absent, no-ops if present. Wraps the entire block in try/catch — fail-open if sessionStorage unavailable. Honors `VITE_ECM_ERROR_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` and runtime `telemetry_client_errors_enabled` settings.
3. Backend: new `POST /api/session-start` endpoint with Pydantic schema `{ session_id: str }`. UUID v4 regex validation; reject non-matching with 422. In-memory dedup set with 24h TTL, lazy-prune at request time. Increment counter only on first sighting. Sit behind same auth posture as `/api/client-errors` (defer the pre-auth question to PO during implementation review).
4. SLO-6 SLI expression in docs/sre/slos.md updated to PromQL-native form:
   ```
   1 - (sum(rate(ecm_client_errors_total{kind="boundary"}[28d]))
        / sum(rate(ecm_session_starts_total[28d])))
   ```
5. Alert rules in docs/sre/prometheus_rules.yaml updated from absolute-rate alerts to ratio-based alerts so they match SLO-6 semantics (e.g., ECMClientErrorRatioElevated: fire when ratio > 0.5% sustained 10m).
6. Tests:
   - Unit: `sessionStorage.setItem` failure → no POST, no exception bubbles.
   - Unit: dedup set rejects re-submitted UUID within TTL; accepts after expiry.
   - Integration: full session lifecycle bumps `ecm_session_starts_total` exactly once across N navigations within the same tab.
7. Smoke in ecm-ecm-1: open one browser session, observe `/metrics` shows `ecm_session_starts_total` increased by exactly 1.

## Follow-ups

- docs/runbooks/frontend_error_rate.md (separate bead already filed) will need the ratio-alert language once this lands.
- The pre-auth coverage question (ADR-006 §1 vs UX rationale for C) may warrant an ADR-006 amendment — file as a separate bead during implementation review if the PO chooses to expand coverage.
close_reason: Implemented and merged: PR #196 (merge SHA 5c16c14d95a8862cd523a458e1dd2cc84a305567). Backend counter ecm_session_starts_total + gauge ecm_session_dedup_set_size registered in observability.py, new POST /api/session-start endpoint with UUIDv4 dedup (24h TTL). Frontend installSessionTracker() wired in main.tsx with sessionStorage + crypto.randomUUID + fail-open per spike Option C. SLO-6 SLI in slos.md promoted to PromQL-native; prometheus_rules.yaml ECMClientErrorRate* alerts swapped to ratio-based ECMClientErrorRatio*. 18 backend tests + 8 frontend tests added (3174 + 1185 total green). Smoke verified in ecm-ecm-1: counter goes 0→1 on first POST, dedup returns true on resubmit. Runbook update tracked under follow-up bead enhancedchannelmanager-06jyv per spike §6.7.

title: Ship Cache-Control defaults on /assets (immutable) and index.html (no-cache) in backend/main.py
description:
Surfaced by 11t6c runbook work (PR #167, 2026-04-24). Infra-cache agent verified that ECM's Starlette StaticFiles mount emits only ETag / Last-Modified — no Cache-Control header on /assets/* or /index.html.

Consequence: every operator inherits whatever their reverse proxy defaults to. The infra-cache-invalidation runbook (PR #167) is therefore needed because ECM doesn't ship cache-safe defaults. A tiny backend change would shift the problem from 'per-operator infra discipline' to 'ECM ships safe defaults.'

Scope:
- Inspect backend/main.py around lines 1020-1036 (the StaticFiles mount).
- Add Cache-Control response headers via a middleware or explicit header wiring:
  - /index.html: 'no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate' OR 'no-cache' (must always revalidate — entry point must never serve stale).
  - /assets/*: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' (content-addressed hash paths from Vite — eternal cache safe).
- Verify behavior with curl -I against a fresh container.
- Confirm no regression in normal page loads.

Acceptance:
- curl -I ecm-ecm-1:8000/index.html shows Cache-Control: no-cache (or equivalent).
- curl -I ecm-ecm-1:8000/assets/index-<hash>.js shows Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable.
- Backend test coverage for the header-emit behavior.
- Reference added from docs/runbooks/infra-cache-invalidation.md noting that ECM now ships safe defaults (reduces scope of operator-side work; runbook still covers pathological cases).

Size: Small.

This is P3 — infrastructure-discipline improvement, not a bug. Operators' existing setups keep working; this just makes ECM a better citizen.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #181 (merge commit ddaadd9e). Branch was rebased clean (cherry-picked bfb7877f onto current origin/dev) after a bad merge silently dropped sister-bead changes. Diff verified to be ONLY the 3 hl603 files: backend/main.py +52, backend/tests/integration/test_static_cache_headers.py +126 (new), docs/runbooks/infra-cache-invalidation.md +7. Backend suite: 3065 passed, 0 failed. All 5 required CI checks SUCCESS.

title: Add SLO-3 calibration-risk note to slos.md (aspirational until Prometheus ships)

title: Document infra-side cache invalidation for operators behind nginx/Cloudflare/CDN
description:
Surfaced by SRE runbook spike (2026-04-24, PR #164). docs/runbooks/dep-bump-frontend-regression.md covers browser-cache invalidation (asset hashes, hard reload, service-worker flush) but assumes users hit ECM directly. Operators deploying behind nginx / Cloudflare / Varnish / other CDNs may need infra-side flush steps that the runbook doesn't cover.

Two shapes to consider:
1. Add a section to dep-bump-frontend-regression.md covering common reverse-proxy cache behavior.
2. Create sibling runbook docs/runbooks/infra-cache-invalidation.md that any frontend-touching runbook links.

Option 2 is preferred — the cache concern isn't dep-bump-specific, it applies to any frontend release.

Scope (either option):
- Common reverse-proxy configs: nginx location blocks with proxy_cache, Cloudflare cache rules, Varnish VCL patterns.
- How to flush after a frontend release (purge-by-URL, purge-all, soft-purge).
- How operator verifies cache is flushed (curl + response headers, asset-hash spot-check).
- Link from dep-bump-frontend-regression.md and from any future frontend-release runbook.

Acceptance:
- File or section exists with the three items above.
- Linked from docs/runbooks/README.md index.

title: Validate normalization_group_ids against NormalizationRuleGroup at rule write-time
description:
Surfaced by bd-pf82j docs work. PUT /api/auto-creation/rules/{id} and POST /api/auto-creation/rules/bulk-update both accept normalization_group_ids as a JSON list, but neither verifies the IDs exist in normalization_rule_groups. A typo, deleted group, or copy-paste from the wrong env stores garbage; failure surfaces later as silent 'no normalization happened' with no clear error.

Scope:
- Add a Pydantic validator (or service-layer check) that queries normalization_rule_groups for submitted IDs and returns HTTP 422 with the offending IDs named if any are missing
- Apply to both PUT /rules/{id} and POST /rules/bulk-update paths
- Check for stale IDs in existing data first; if present, validate on write only (not on read) to avoid breaking already-stored rules
- Tests: valid IDs accepted, missing ID returns 422 with offending ID, mixed valid+invalid returns 422 listing all invalid

User value: clear error at write-time vs silent runtime failure. Better UX. Catches frontend bugs and copy-paste mistakes from other environments.

Effort: ~30-45 min plus stale-ID audit.

Related: bd-pf82j (api.md backfill that flagged this gap as 'doc states honestly that no validation occurs').
notes: PR #145 opened: https://github.com/MotWakorb/enhancedchannelmanager/pull/145 — write-time FK validation for normalization_group_ids on PUT /rules/{id} and POST /rules/bulk-update. Delta-on-write semantics chosen (only submitted IDs validated; stored values left alone for backward-compat). Backend tests: 3088 passed. 9 new tests added. Awaiting merge before close.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #145. Stale-data audit confirmed clean (0 stale references in production DB). Helper _validate_normalization_group_ids in backend/routers/auto_creation.py: single IN query, deduped, raises 422 with invalid_normalization_group_ids list. Wired into PUT /rules/{id} (between rule lookup and scalar apply — no partial mutations) and POST /rules/bulk-update (after fetch, before mutation loop — single 422 rolls back batch). Delta-on-write semantics chosen as defense-in-depth. POST /rules (create) explicitly out of scope; symmetric coverage tracked as bd-j5p4k. 9 new tests; 3088 backend tests pass.

title: Add ?batch_id= query parameter to GET /api/journal for bulk-operation forensics
description:
Surfaced by bd-pf82j docs work. The journal API currently filters via 'search' only (ILIKE on entity_name/description). After bd-91mcq, batch_id is the documented correlation primitive — every bulk auto-creation operation writes N rows sharing one 8-char batch_id. Without an API filter, integrators (and the frontend) must hit the DB directly to answer 'what did this batch change?'

Scope:
- Add 'batch_id: str | None = Query(None, description="Filter to a single bulk operation\'s journal rows")' to backend/routers/journal.py GET handler
- Conditionally '.filter(JournalEntry.batch_id == batch_id)' in the query
- Tests: 200 with batch_id present (returns N rows), 200 with batch_id absent (existing behavior unchanged), invalid batch_id format rejected at parameter level
- Update docs/api.md GET /api/journal section to document the new param

Surfaces the idx_journal_batch_id index shipped in bd-dmu8w (currently unreachable via API).

User value: bulk-operation forensics queryable via API; UI can show 'what did this batch change?' without DB shell access.

Effort: ~30 min. Pure additive; no breaking change.

Related: bd-pf82j (api.md backfill that flagged this gap), bd-91mcq (introduced batch_id), bd-dmu8w (added the supporting index).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #143. backend/routers/journal.py + backend/journal.py: added Optional[str] batch_id Query parameter; conditional JournalEntry.batch_id == batch_id filter (hits idx_journal_batch_id from bd-dmu8w). 4 new tests in test_journal.py covering matching/empty/no-param-regression/composes-with-search. docs/api.md updated: bd-pf82j 'future bead' caveat replaced with first-class param documentation. 3083 backend tests pass.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: PR #99 emits a single journal entry for bulk-update with entity_id=0, entity_name='bulk', first-5-rule-names description, and no batch_id. This doesn't match the established pattern in backend/routers/channels.py:914 (bulk channel renumber) which emits one entry per entity with a shared batch_id uuid. For forensics ('what did bulk-update do to rule 47 at 14:32?') we need per-rule entries with before/after diffs. Implement: (1) generate batch_id = uuid4().hex, (2) capture scalar field before-values during _apply_rule_scalar_updates (return the diff), (3) emit one journal entry per mutated rule with entity_id=rule.id, action_type='bulk_update', batch_id, and the diff. Flagged in original R1 review as non-blocking follow-up; tracking here.

title: enhancedchannelmanager
description: PR #99 bulk_update_auto_creation_rules loops session.query(AutoCreationRule).filter(AutoCreationRule.id == rid).first() per id, plus session.refresh(rule) per row post-commit. Replace with one .filter(AutoCreationRule.id.in_(rule_ids)).all() + dict lookup, and drop session.refresh() — attached instances already reflect the committed values for columns written by _apply_rule_scalar_updates. title: Unicode confusables/skeleton normalization (homoglyph handling)
description:
Backlog — not part of epic bd-eio04. Filed as follow-up after grooming session 2026-04-22.

NFC/NFKC do NOT fold Cyrillic 'а' (U+0430) with Latin 'a' (U+0061) — they look identical but remain distinct code points. Users experiencing rule-match failures across alphabets need Unicode TR39 skeleton/confusables treatment.

Defer until a real user scenario surfaces (currently speculative per security persona). If filed:
- Use a confusables library (e.g., unicode-confusables pkg) or Unicode TR39 skeleton mapping.
- Apply after NFC normalization (bd-eio04.4).
- Opt-in via NormalizationPolicy flag, not default-on (it's aggressive).
- Scope fixtures: Cyrillic/Latin, Greek/Latin, Latin digit/letter confusables (O/0, I/1/l).

title: CodeQL note-level cleanup pass: empty-except, unused-*, cyclic-import, unreachable-statement
description:
## Context
32+ low-signal CodeQL findings across the backend, mostly informational. Bulk triage pass to either fix opportunistically or dismiss with justification so the scanner board stays signal-rich.

## Inventory (from current Default Setup scan)
Open alert counts by rule (excluding HIGH-severity errors tracked elsewhere):
- py/unused-import: 34 (mostly DX noise, safe to delete)
- py/unused-local-variable: 16 (usually a latent bug signal — inspect each)
- py/cyclic-import: 15 (architectural — cloud_storage/*, database.py, export_models.py, normalization_migration.py; don't rush, risk of runtime import-order breakage)
- py/empty-except: 11 (routers/auto_creation.py:1294, routers/export.py:604/1110, export_manager.py:195; each swallows silently — CLAUDE.md bans this)
- py/unused-global-variable: 4
- py/import-and-import-from: 1
- py/multiple-definition: 1 (auto_creation_engine.py:1530 — same-name function redefined)
- py/unreachable-statement: 1 (routers/settings.py:1052 — dead 'return {"status": "revoked"}' after try/except that always returns)
- js/unused-local-variable: 2
- js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor: 1

## Approach
1. DELETE (safe): all py/unused-import findings, the unreachable-statement in settings.py:1052 (verified dead code after try/except, confirmed line 1052 is never reached).
2. INSPECT (may be bug): py/unused-local-variable (16) and py/unused-global-variable (4) — each could be a missed assignment or dead branch. Triage line-by-line.
3. FIX BANNED PATTERN: py/empty-except (11) — CLAUDE.md's backend guide says 'Never silently swallow exceptions' and 'Always log before raising'. Each bare except needs either a logger.warning + re-raise/continue OR narrower Exception type.
4. LEAVE OR ARCHITECT-TOUCH: py/cyclic-import (15) — cloud_storage/*, database.py, models.py, export_models.py, normalization_migration.py. These are TYPE_CHECKING-style import cycles that are runtime-safe; either annotate or refactor; consult IT Architect before changing import topology.
5. DISMISS: py/import-and-import-from (1), multiple-definition (1) after review.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every non-error CodeQL finding in the current scan is either fixed in code OR dismissed in the UI with a meaningful reason (not 'won't fix' silently)
- [ ] No new empty-except blocks introduced during the pass
- [ ] Next CodeQL run shows 0 note-level findings in the scrubbed files (or a documented exception list)
- [ ] settings.py:1052 unreachable-statement removed

Out of scope:
- py/path-injection (tracked in -0a1pr and export-related follow-up)
- py/stack-trace-exposure (8 errors — tracked separately in a new bead if prioritized; I recommend filing one)
- py/reflective-xss (1 error — tracked separately if prioritized)
- py/partial-ssrf (2 errors — tracked separately if prioritized)

title: Execution History: show the name of the rule that triggered the run
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #795 by @sultan7swing. Reporter rates it "Medium - nice to
have, would use it regularly".

## The ask

Execution History shows the run outcome but not WHICH rule produced it. Current fields:

    Status / Mode / Started / Completed / Duration /
    Streams Evaluated / Streams Matched / Channels Created

Add a "Rule Name:" field alongside them.

## Why

Operators running several rules in succession cannot tell which rule a given history
entry belongs to, so they cannot match an outcome back to the rule that caused it.

## Scope notes

Likely small -- the execution record is already keyed to a rule (the backend logs
"[AUTO-CREATE] Created rule id=... name=..." on the write path). Check whether the
execution row already carries the rule id and only the UI omits it, in which case this
is frontend-only. Handle the multi-rule / full-pipeline-run case: a run that fires many
rules needs something sensible in the field rather than a blank or an arbitrary pick.
Also decide the display for a rule that was renamed or deleted after the run.
acceptance_criteria: An Execution History entry shows the name of the rule that produced it, alongside the existing fields. A run that fired multiple rules displays something unambiguous rather than a blank or an arbitrary single name. A run whose rule was since renamed or deleted still renders without error. Covered by a frontend test against a history fixture with single-rule, multi-rule and deleted-rule cases.

title: Channel name normalization: operator-defined alias mapping (preferred name -> alternative names)
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #775 by @lavazza2017. Reporter rates it "High - would
significantly improve my experience".

## The ask

Automatically treat channel names that differ only by punctuation, spacing or common
suffixes as the same channel -- e.g. "Stars TV" and "Stars.TV" -- and display them
under a single preferred name.

Proposed shape is an operator-maintained mapping table:

    Preferred Name  ->  Alternative Names
    Polonia         ->  Polonia, Polonia 1, Polonia1, Polonia.1
    Stars TV        ->  Stars TV, Stars.TV, Stars-TV
    TVN             ->  TVN, TVN HD, TVN-HD

Whenever a stream matches any listed alternative, it is assigned to the preferred
channel name. Reporter accepts that this needs up-front setup, and expects the mapping
list to grow into a mostly-automated workflow over time.

## Scope notes

NEEDS GROOMING / possibly a spike before build. ECM already has a normalization engine
(docs/normalization.md) with normalized_name_* conditions, and Event Sync already has a
corpus-gated team-alias dictionary (enhancedchannelmanager-ti939.4.2, closed). The real
question is whether this is:

  a. a new user-facing alias table (net-new CRUD + UI + matching integration), or
  b. a documentation/UX gap where the existing normalization rules already do this and
     operators cannot discover how, or
  c. a smaller extension of the existing normalization engine with an alias-map
     condition/action type.

Resolve that before sizing. Answering (b) may close the issue with docs alone.
acceptance_criteria: First: a spike determines whether the existing normalization engine already satisfies the ask (docs fix), needs an alias-map condition/action (small extension), or requires a net-new alias table (full feature). If build is chosen: an operator can define preferred-name -> alternative-names mappings, streams matching any alternative are assigned to the preferred channel name, the mapping survives pipeline runs, and the reporter's three examples (Polonia, Stars TV, TVN) all resolve correctly including the punctuation and HD-suffix variants.

title: Event Sync: option to detach stale streams that no longer match the sync configuration
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #725 by @mrdynamo against the dev event-sync work.

## The ask

When a provider refreshes and Dispatcharr triggers an auto-sync, the channel name
is correctly updated with the new event, but streams ECM attached on a PREVIOUS
day are left attached to the channel.

Reporter investigated (and discussed on Discord): Dispatcharr native auto-sync does
NOT delete and recreate a channel when only the stream NAME changes -- the channel is
updated and renamed in place. So streams ECM previously attached are never cleaned up
by Dispatcharr, and ECM currently does not clean them up either.

## Suggested implementation (from reporter)

An additional option in the event sync configuration to detach stale streams that no
longer match the sync configuration: if an attached stream is not the parent auto-sync
stream from Dispatcharr, remove it when it no longer satisfies the "Would attach stream"
rules in ECM.

## Scope notes

Distinct from enhancedchannelmanager-sfysz (closed), which covers journal-driven
surgical unmerge on event_sync ROLLBACK. This is about steady-state recurring sync,
not undoing a run.

Needs a design pass on: opt-in vs default (detaching streams is destructive), how to
identify the Dispatcharr parent auto-sync stream so it is never detached, and whether
the detach should be journalled per-channel so it is reversible.
acceptance_criteria: An event sync rule with the new option enabled removes ECM-attached streams that no longer match the rule on a subsequent sync, while never detaching the Dispatcharr parent auto-sync stream. The option is off by default. Detaches are recorded in the journal so the run can be rolled back. A test covers the reporter's scenario: channel renamed in place by Dispatcharr auto-sync, previous day's ECM-attached streams present, sync run -> stale streams gone, current streams intact.

title: Consider encrypting Dispatcharr password
description: The Dispatcharr password is stored in plaintext in /config/settings.json. For deployments where the config directory might be accessible to untrusted users, consider encrypting the password. Low priority since ECM is designed as a local network tool.
close_reason: After analysis: Encryption would provide minimal security benefit. The password must be decryptable to send to Dispatcharr's API for authentication. Storing an encryption key alongside the config would allow anyone with config access to decrypt it anyway - this is security theater. For users who need better security: (1) Use Docker environment variables for sensitive config, (2) Restrict access to the config directory at the OS level. The current approach is appropriate for a local network tool. Won't implement.

title: Add optional basic auth for ECM API
description: ECM's API endpoints have no authentication. This is fine for local network use, but if users want to expose ECM beyond their LAN, they should have the option to enable basic auth or another authentication mechanism. Consider adding an optional AUTH_ENABLED environment variable.
close_reason: Deferred - ECM is designed for local network use only. Users who want to expose ECM beyond their LAN should use a reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik, Caddy) with authentication, which provides more flexibility and security than built-in basic auth. This is the standard pattern for containerized applications. If there's significant user demand for built-in auth, it can be revisited.
